organization: Arc Institute

evidence.tested: Of 285 Evo-designed genomes, 16 were synthesized and gave functional phages in E. coli, and these were tested for fitness, host range and, for three resistant strains, a phage cocktail.
evidence.unknown: The source states host range was limited to E. coli C and W, all 16 phages were based on the phiX174 template, and clinical use is not shown.
evidence.ai_role: Evo, fine-tuned on Microviridae sequences, generated whole phage genomes resembling phiX174.

title: Deep Loop Shaping reduces LIGO control noise
summary: The method, described in Science and tested at the Livingston site, reduced noise 30–100-fold in the observatory's most unstable feedback loop, in collaboration with LIGO, Caltech, and GSSI. The result covers one control loop; extending it to all loops and adding hundreds of events per year are projections.
ai_technology: Deep Loop Shaping (reinforcement-learning control)
organization: Google DeepMind; LIGO, Caltech, and GSSI

evidence.tested: The controller was trained in simulation and then tested on the real LIGO Livingston system, where noise in the most unstable feedback loop fell 30 to 100 times and stayed stable over prolonged periods.
evidence.unknown: The source states gains come from one control loop, applying the method to all loops and extra detections per year are described as potential or projected.
evidence.ai_role: A reinforcement learning controller with frequency-domain rewards replaced linear control design for the mirror feedback loop.

title: New combinations of additives for LNMO batteries found with machine learning
summary: A model trained on data for 28 additives predicted the performance of 125 new combinations and identified formulations that outperformed the initial ones in tests. The study concerns high-voltage LNMO batteries; the Argonne announcement, accessed via Newswise, does not quantify the improvement or describe industrial-scale validation.
ai_technology: Machine learning on molecular features of additives
organization: Argonne National Laboratory

evidence.tested: Electrolyte additive combinations proposed by a model trained on 28 additives were tested in Gr||LNMO cells, and the ML-suggested mixtures outperformed the original set.
evidence.unknown: The source states the model used only 28 additives, gives no quantitative performance figures or top additive names, and does not describe industrial-scale validation.
evidence.ai_role: A machine learning model linked additive descriptors to battery performance and predicted the performance of 125 new combinations.

title: GPT-4b micro: Yamanaka factor variants with over 50-fold higher expression
summary: OpenAI and Retro Biosciences used a specialized model to design Yamanaka factor variants that produced over 50-fold higher expression of reprogramming markers in vitro than controls, with results replicated across multiple donors, cell types, and delivery methods, and pluripotency confirmed. Reported by OpenAI; the model is not publicly available.
ai_technology: GPT-4b micro
organization: OpenAI; and Retro Biosciences

evidence.tested: Designed Yamanaka factor variants were tested in vitro across multiple donors, cell types and delivery methods, with over 50-fold higher expression of reprogramming markers and pluripotency confirmed relative to controls.
evidence.unknown: The page gives no detailed protocol or data, the model is not publicly available, and the results are reported by OpenAI only.
evidence.ai_role: A specialized GPT-4b micro model designed Yamanaka factor variants.

title: Antibiotics designed with generative AI against gonorrhea and MRSA
summary: Over 36 million possible compounds were screened computationally: candidate NG1 killed resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in a dish and in a mouse model, while DN1 cleared a MRSA skin infection in mice. Only 2 of 80 fragment candidates could be synthesized; these are preclinical results.
ai_technology: Generative AI for molecule design
organization: MIT

evidence.tested: Generative models screened more than 10^7 chemical fragments in silico against N. gonorrhoeae or S. aureus, plus unconstrained design. Of 24 synthesized compounds, seven showed selective antibacterial activity; two leads reduced bacterial burden in mouse infection models.
evidence.unknown: Mouse results only; no human testing is stated. The paper's abstract was read, not the full text.
evidence.ai_role: Genetic algorithms and variational autoencoders generated fragment-based and de novo compounds; researchers synthesized and tested selected compounds.

source_review.scope: Original institutional announcement checked for the specific results, AI contribution and limitations cited in the antibiotic dossier or mathematical follow-up pilot. Full-paper reanalysis, external replication and an exhaustive follow-up search were not performed.

relationships.reason: The source names this earlier screening result as program background for moving to de novo generative design. New compounds and experiments; not a clinical follow-up or replication of the earlier candidate.

The source names this earlier screening result as program background for moving to de novo generative design. New compounds and experiments; not a clinical follow-up or replication of the earlier candidate.

title: Decoding inner speech with a brain-computer interface
summary: In four people with severe motor and speech impairments, researchers found imagined-speech signals in the motor cortex and decoded them with machine learning. They also tested filters and a trigger phrase to limit unintended decoding. This is a proof of principle with implanted electrodes: free, rapid inner speech cannot be decoded accurately, and attempted speech remains more accurate.
ai_technology: Brain-computer interface and machine learning
organization: Stanford University; and collaborators

evidence.tested: Imagined-speech signals were recorded from motor cortex in four participants with implanted electrodes and decoded in real time, with filters and a trigger phrase tested to limit unintended decoding.
evidence.unknown: The source states this is a proof of principle, free inner speech cannot yet be decoded accurately, and attempted speech remains more accurate.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning decoded the imagined-speech neural signals.

title: AlphaEarth Foundations: a 10-meter map of Earth
summary: A model combines optical, radar, 3D laser, and climate-simulation data into one representation for 10-meter squares, using 16 times less storage and with 24% lower average error than the compared models. The Google Earth Engine dataset has over 1.4 trillion embeddings per year and has been tried by more than 50 organizations. Benefits with LLM agents remain prospective.
ai_technology: AlphaEarth Foundations
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Compared against traditional methods and other AI mapping systems on land-use identification and surface-property estimation; average error 24% lower than the models tested, storage 16 times lower. Over 50 organizations tested the dataset; no sample sizes given.
evidence.unknown: The page states no limitations; it says the team is still exploring time-based capabilities and that embeddings may be more useful combined with reasoning LLM agents.
evidence.ai_role: The model turns satellite and Earth observation data into compact embeddings; scientists and partners use them to create maps and classify ecosystems.

title: Virtual Lab: AI agents design nanobodies against SARS-CoV-2
summary: A group of AI agents led by a principal agent designed 92 nanobodies: two bound to spike protein from recent variants in lab tests, and humans wrote about 1% of the conversation. Only 2 of 92 bound; the date is the Nature publication date given on the page.
ai_technology: Multiple AI agents (Virtual Lab)
organization: CZ Biohub; and Stanford University

evidence.tested: The Virtual Lab designed 92 nanobodies; experiments (multiplexed ELISA) showed a range of functional binders. Two showed improved binding to JN.1 or KP.3 while keeping strong binding to the ancestral spike protein.
evidence.unknown: The two are called candidates for further investigation. Neutralization and clinical use not reported in the abstract. Full text is paywalled; counts of tested designs beyond 92 and binding values were not read.
evidence.ai_role: An LLM principal investigator agent guided LLM scientist agents through meetings, with human feedback; they built a pipeline using ESM, AlphaFold-Multimer and Rosetta. Humans ran the experiments.

title: An autonomous platform speeds research on polymer mixtures
summary: The platform tests up to 700 mixtures a day (96 at a time), guided by a genetic algorithm: hundreds of mixtures outperformed the individual components, and the best retained 73% enzyme activity, 18% more than the best component. Application is limited to enzyme thermal stability, replenishment is still manual; published in Matter.
ai_technology: Genetic algorithm with robotics
organization: MIT

evidence.tested: An autonomous platform tested up to 700 polymer mixtures a day, and the best mixtures retained 73% enzyme activity, 18% more than the best component, in a retrospective analysis of the results.
evidence.unknown: The source states application is limited to enzyme thermal stability and replenishment is still manual.
evidence.ai_role: A genetic algorithm guided the choice of polymer mixtures tested by the robotic platform.

title: AutoBot: robotic optimization of halide perovskites
summary: A closed loop with robotics and Bayesian optimization explored a four-parameter synthesis space of over 5,000 combinations, and the model made predictions after sampling less than 1%; humidity during deposition was the most influential factor. This is process optimization, not a new material; the page gives no accuracy figure.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization with robotics
organization: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Molecular Foundry)

evidence.tested: A closed loop of robotic synthesis and Bayesian optimization explored over 5,000 combinations, and predictions were validated with manual and in situ photoluminescence measurements.
evidence.unknown: The page gives no model accuracy metrics and no explicit limitations; the wider application to other semiconductors is forward-looking.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian optimization chose which experiments to run and identified humidity as the most influential factor after sampling under 1% of the space.

title: Aeneas: restoration, dating, and provenance of Latin inscriptions
summary: The model restores texts with 73% top-20 accuracy for gaps up to ten characters (58% when length is unknown), attributes provenance with 72% accuracy across 62 Roman provinces, and dates inscriptions within 13 years; it was trained on over 176,000 inscriptions. In a study with 23 historians on 60 inscriptions, results were best when parallels and predictions were used together. Published in Nature.
ai_technology: Aeneas
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Corpus of 176,861 Latin inscriptions. Aeneas: 72% geographical accuracy over 62 provinces; dating within 13 years on average; restoration character error rate 40.5% with known length. 23 historians on 60 inscriptions, solo versus with Aeneas parallels and predictions.
evidence.unknown: The paper notes a small dataset, survival bias, only about 5% of inscriptions with images, and weaker results where data are scarce. Training data include earlier editors' restorations. Other languages are suggested, not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Aeneas restored text, attributed provinces, estimated dates and retrieved parallels; historians evaluated outputs and combined them with their own knowledge.

title: Gemini Deep Think reaches gold-medal level at the 2025 IMO
summary: An advanced version of Gemini Deep Think solved 5 of 6 problems at the 2025 IMO, scoring 35 out of 42 and working in natural language within the 4.5-hour limit. IMO coordinators assessed and certified the score, while clarifying that they do not validate the system.
ai_technology: Gemini Deep Think
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: An advanced Gemini Deep Think version solved the official 2025 IMO problems within the time limit, and IMO coordinators graded and certified the 35 of 42 score with the same criteria as for students.
evidence.unknown: The IMO did not validate the system or model, and this version is not yet public and was first given to trusted testers.
evidence.ai_role: Gemini Deep Think worked end-to-end in natural language, exploring multiple solution paths in parallel.

title: AlphaGenome: predicting the effects of DNA variants
summary: The model reads sequences up to 1 million base pairs and predicts thousands of gene-regulation properties at single-letter resolution. It outperformed the best external models in 22 of 24 sequence evaluations and matched or outperformed the best in 24 of 26 variant evaluations. Stated limits: distant regulatory elements; not validated for personal genomes or clinical use.
ai_technology: AlphaGenome
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: AlphaGenome was evaluated on sequence and variant-effect benchmarks against external models, outperforming in 22 of 24 and matching or exceeding in 24 of 26 evaluations, plus a TAL1 case study.
evidence.unknown: The source states it is not validated for personal genomes or clinical use, distant regulatory elements remain a challenge, and cell-specific patterns need improvement.
evidence.ai_role: A model takes up to 1 million DNA base pairs and predicts thousands of genomic tracks and variant effects.

title: Skala: a deep-learning exchange-correlation functional
summary: It comes close to the 1 kcal/mol threshold on the W4-17 benchmark (0.85 kcal/mol on the single-reference subset) and is competitive with leading hybrid functionals on GMTKN55 at lower cost. It was trained on about 150,000 high-accuracy energy differences, roughly 100 times the previous dataset size. Accuracy is shown only within the training data's chemical space; it was not yet public at the time.
ai_technology: Skala (neural network for DFT)
organization: Microsoft Research

evidence.tested: Skala was evaluated on the W4-17 atomization benchmark, reaching 0.85 kcal/mol on the single-reference subset, and on GMTKN55, where it was competitive with hybrid functionals.
evidence.unknown: Accuracy is claimed only within the training data chemical space, expansion to broader chemistry is at an early stage, and the functional was not yet public.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning exchange-correlation functional learned from about 150,000 high-accuracy energy differences.

title: Dead Sea Scrolls redated with AI and radiocarbon
summary: The Enoch tool dated the writing of 135 manuscripts with about 79% agreement with palaeographers and roughly 30-year precision, following new radiocarbon dating; many scrolls appear older than expected. The 79% measures agreement with palaeographers, not accuracy against known dates; the announcement gives no details on training data.
ai_technology: Enoch (palaeographic dating model)
organization: University of Groningen; Pisa, KU Leuven, and University of Southern Denmark

evidence.tested: The Enoch dates for 135 manuscripts, following new radiocarbon dating, were compared with palaeographers' judgments, with about 79% agreement.
evidence.unknown: The source states the 79% measures agreement with palaeographers rather than accuracy against known dates, that about one in five datings disagreed, and that training-data details are not given.
evidence.ai_role: Enoch, a writing-style model trained on radiocarbon-dated samples, dated the manuscripts.

title: Rentosertib: AI-designed drug reports Phase IIa results in pulmonary fibrosis
summary: In the GENESIS-IPF study of 71 patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis at 22 centers (placebo versus three doses, 12 weeks), the 60 mg/day group had a mean FVC change of +98.4 mL versus −20.3 mL for placebo. Groups were small, so larger studies are needed; biomarker analysis was exploratory.
ai_technology: Pharma.AI (generative AI for targets and molecules)
organization: Insilico Medicine

evidence.tested: Phase 2a, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, 71 patients for 12 weeks. Primary endpoint (patients with at least one treatment-emergent adverse event) was similar across arms: 70.6% to 83.3%. Treatment-related serious adverse events were low and comparable.
evidence.unknown: Efficacy in larger and longer trials is not established by this phase 2a study.
evidence.ai_role: Generative AI was used to discover the TNIK target and the small-molecule inhibitor, per the paper's title and abstract.

title: Robin: ripasudil as a candidate for dry macular degeneration
summary: FutureHouse's multi-agent system generated hypotheses, experiments, and analyses and identified ripasudil, already used for glaucoma, as a candidate against dry macular degeneration. Lab testing of ten candidates found that a ROCK inhibitor increases phagocytosis by retinal pigment epithelial cells; human researchers carried out the experiments. Announced May 20, 2025, and published in Nature May 19, 2026. Preclinical data.
ai_technology: Robin (Crow, Falcon, and Finch agents)
organization: FutureHouse

evidence.tested: Human researchers lab-tested ten candidates proposed by Robin, and a ROCK inhibitor was found to increase phagocytosis by retinal pigment epithelial cells.
evidence.unknown: The source calls ripasudil a candidate, not a proven treatment, and the mechanism proposed by Robin is not stated to have been tested.
evidence.ai_role: A multi-agent system generated hypotheses, chose experiments, analyzed data and drafted main figures.

title: Microsoft Discovery: a PFAS-free refrigerant in about 200 hours
summary: Microsoft researchers used AI models and high-performance simulations to identify a prototype PFAS-free immersion coolant for data centers in about 200 hours, then synthesized it in under four months; initial tests of key properties match predictions. Microsoft describes it as an experiment still under analysis.
ai_technology: Microsoft Discovery (agentic orchestration and high-performance computing)
organization: Microsoft

evidence.tested: A prototype PFAS-free coolant was synthesized, and some of its primary properties were tested and matched the AI predictions.
evidence.unknown: Microsoft calls it only an experiment still under analysis, and only some properties have been tested.
evidence.ai_role: AI models and HPC simulations in Microsoft Discovery identified the candidate in about 200 hours.

title: AlphaEvolve: an agent for designing algorithms
summary: An evolutionary agent based on Gemini and automated evaluators. It recovered an average of 0.7% of Google's computing resources, sped up a Gemini training kernel by 23%, and found an algorithm using 48 multiplications for 4×4 complex matrices. Across more than 50 open math problems, it matched the state of the art in about 75% and improved it in about 20%.
ai_technology: AlphaEvolve (Gemini Flash and Pro)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Results were checked by automated evaluators, and the agent was applied to over 50 open math problems and deployed tasks, matching state of the art in about 75% and improving it in about 20%.
evidence.unknown: The source states the approach applies only to problems whose solutions can be checked automatically, and broader access is not yet available.
evidence.ai_role: An ensemble of Gemini models proposed code in an evolutionary loop with automated evaluators.

title: Aardvark Weather: end-to-end forecasting without a physical model
summary: A single AI model replaces the entire forecasting chain: it starts from satellite and station observations and produces global and local forecasts in minutes on a desktop using about one-tenth of the data; the page says it beats the US GFS on many variables. The announcement gives no metrics; it is not operational and depends on ERA5. Published in Nature.
ai_technology: Aardvark Weather
organization: University of Cambridge; Alan Turing Institute, Microsoft Research, and ECMWF

evidence.tested: Forecasts were compared with the operational NWP baseline (GFS) and with NWS and an end-to-end system; the Nature paper reports the global forecasts beat the baseline for several variables and lead times.
evidence.unknown: The source states it is not operational, depends on ERA5, and that hurricane, air quality and other applications are proposed rather than tested.
evidence.ai_role: A single model ingested satellite and station observations and produced global and local forecasts.

title: Seven organic-solar-cell molecules designed with generative models
summary: Generative and predictive models, refined with experts and experiments, suggested new non-fullerene acceptors for organic solar cells. Seven molecules were synthesized and tested, with efficiencies close to predictions; the news item gives no efficiency values or advantage over the best existing materials.
ai_technology: Generative and predictive molecule models
organization: A*STAR; National University of Singapore, and Elix

evidence.tested: Seven generated non-fullerene acceptor molecules were synthesized and tested, with power conversion efficiencies close to the model predictions.
evidence.unknown: The source gives no efficiency values, no test methods and no advantage over the best existing materials.
evidence.ai_role: A generative model and a predictive model, refined with experiments, proposed the molecules.

title: MICrONS: a map of one cubic millimeter of mouse visual cortex
summary: A map with over half a billion connections and about 75,000 reconstructed neurons from roughly 28,000 sections, produced over nine years by more than 150 researchers. AI traced every neuron outline, and the result requires human checking, much of which is already done. This is about one-thousandth of a mouse connectome, and cell counts vary within the text.
ai_technology: AI neuron segmentation
organization: Princeton University; Allen Institute, and Baylor College of Medicine

evidence.tested: Not reported
evidence.unknown: The source states the map is about one-thousandth of a mouse connectome, the result requires human proofreading (much already done), and the connectome is not necessarily the neural code.
evidence.ai_role: AI traced the outline of every neuron through the electron microscopy slices.

title: Euclid: 500 candidate strong gravitational lenses
summary: The first catalog of 500 candidate galaxy–galaxy lenses, almost all previously unknown, was selected with AI models and then reviewed by citizen scientists and experts. These are candidates, not confirmed lenses; 7,000 by the late-2026 release and about 100,000 by mission end are projections.
ai_technology: Image-classification models
organization: ESA; and Euclid Consortium

evidence.tested: AI candidates were inspected by citizen scientists and then vetted and modelled by experts, system by system, to produce 497 candidate lenses in the first catalogue.
evidence.unknown: The page calls these candidates, not confirmed lenses, gives no error or false-positive rates, and the future counts are projections.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning models performed the initial sweep for candidate lenses.

title: The AI Scientist-v2: a fully generated paper passes a workshop review
summary: A paper produced end to end by the system received a mean score of 6.33 at the ICBINB workshop at ICLR 2025, above the average acceptance threshold. Humans only supplied the topic and selected three papers to submit, and the accepted one was withdrawn. Only one of three cleared the threshold; it was a workshop, not the main conference, and there was no meta-review.
ai_technology: The AI Scientist-v2
organization: Sakana AI

evidence.tested: Three AI-generated papers went through double-blind review at an ICLR 2025 workshop, and one scored 6.33 on average, above the acceptance threshold.
evidence.unknown: The source states it was a workshop rather than the main track, there was no meta-review, and the authors' own review found none of the papers met the main-track bar.
evidence.ai_role: The system generated the papers end to end from a human-supplied topic, and humans chose which three to submit.

title: ECMWF puts AI forecasts (AIFS) into operation
summary: The European center operationalized AIFS Single on February 25, 2025, alongside the physical IFS model. ECMWF reports gains of up to 20% on tropical-cyclone tracks and about 1,000 times lower energy use. It is deterministic, at 28 km versus 9 km for IFS.
ai_technology: AIFS (machine-learning model)
organization: ECMWF

evidence.tested: Not reported
evidence.unknown: The page does not describe the verification methods or datasets, the grid is 28 km versus 9 km for IFS, and ensemble forecasting is a future step.
evidence.ai_role: A machine learning model trained on past weather evolution projects the same initial conditions as the IFS model forward every six hours.

title: CorrDiff: kilometer-scale weather forecasts with generative AI
summary: A diffusion model takes atmospheric data from 25-kilometer to 2-kilometer scale and also predicts variables absent from the inputs, such as radar reflectivity. The paper appeared the same day in Communications Earth and Environment; the initial model was tuned on Taiwan data with the Central Weather Administration, and Taiwan's disaster-reduction center uses it for alerts. NVIDIA claims 500 times faster and 10,000 times more energy-efficient than high-resolution numerical forecasting on CPU: company figures, with no accuracy comparison on the page.
ai_technology: CorrDiff (diffusion model)
organization: NVIDIA

evidence.tested: Not reported
evidence.unknown: The article gives no accuracy metrics or accuracy comparison and does not explicitly list limitations; the speed and energy figures are company claims.
evidence.ai_role: A diffusion model downscales atmospheric data from 25 km to 2 km and predicts variables missing from the input.

title: BioEmu-1: ensembles of protein structures with deep learning
summary: An open-source model that generates thousands of protein structures per hour on a GPU and reproduces the equilibrium distribution of a molecular-dynamics simulation using 10,000 to 100,000 times fewer GPU-hours. Predicted folding free energies correlate well with experimental values. The authors call it ‘a first step.’
ai_technology: BioEmu-1
organization: Microsoft Research

evidence.tested: Generated ensembles were compared with a molecular dynamics simulation of protein G using 10,000 to 100,000 times fewer GPU hours, and predicted folding free energies were correlated with experimental values.
evidence.unknown: The authors state they are aware of limitations but the post does not list them, and it is presented as an early step.
evidence.ai_role: A generative deep learning model produces thousands of protein structures per hour on a GPU.

title: AI co-scientist: a multi-agent system for generating hypotheses
summary: A system based on Gemini 2.0 that generates hypotheses and research proposals. In the lab, three drugs it suggested for repurposing against acute myeloid leukemia reduced cancer-cell viability, and all suggested treatments for liver fibrosis showed activity. Expert assessments covered only 11 targets; fibrosis results awaited a Stanford report.
ai_technology: AI co-scientist (Gemini 2.0, multi-agent)
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: Elo auto-evaluation over 203 research goals; 15 expert-curated goals; blinded experts rated 11 goals (preference rank 2.36). In vitro on four AML cell lines: binimetinib, pacritinib, cerivastatin reduced viability; KIRA6 IC50 10 nM in KG-1a versus 180 nM in TK6. Seven combinations tested.
evidence.unknown: The paper calls validation preliminary and in vitro only. KIRA6 was far less effective in MOLM-13 and HL-60. Expert evaluation was small and subjective; Elo is not ground truth. Liver fibrosis and AMR details are summarized only.
evidence.ai_role: A Gemini-based multi-agent system generated, debated and ranked hypotheses; experts selected candidates and prioritized lab experiments.

title: Evo 2: the largest AI model for biology
summary: Trained on more than 9.3 trillion nucleotides from over 128,000 genomes, it reads sequences up to 1 million nucleotides, flags harmful mutations, and designs genetic elements and genomes as long as those of simple bacteria. In BRCA1 tests it exceeds 90% accuracy in distinguishing benign from potentially pathogenic variants (a result limited to that gene). Preprint; human pathogens were excluded from training.
ai_technology: Evo 2 (genome language model)
organization: Arc Institute

evidence.tested: The model was tested on BRCA1 variants, where it reached over 90% accuracy distinguishing benign from potentially pathogenic mutations, and on identifying genetic changes affecting protein function and fitness.
evidence.unknown: The source reports the BRCA1 result for one gene only and states no other limitations beyond human pathogens being excluded from training.
evidence.ai_role: A genome language model trained on 9.3 trillion nucleotides flags harmful mutations and designs genetic elements.

title: Two molecules against KRAS from a hybrid AI and quantum process
summary: A process combining quantum and classical computing with Chemistry42 selected 15 candidates; two showed activity against mutated KRAS variants in living cells. Published in Nature Biotechnology, this is a proof of principle, with no significant quantum advantage or demonstrated superiority over compounds obtained by classical methods.
ai_technology: Chemistry42 and hybrid quantum-classical models
organization: University of Toronto; and Insilico Medicine

evidence.tested: Fifteen candidates from the hybrid process were tested in the lab, and two strongly targeted mutated KRAS variants in living cells.
evidence.unknown: The source states it is a proof-of-principle study with no significant quantum advantage and no demonstrated superiority over classically designed molecules.
evidence.ai_role: Generative AI (Chemistry42) and a quantum-classical process designed molecules, narrowed to 15 candidates.

title: MaSIF designs binders for protein–drug complexes
summary: MaSIF designed proteins that recognize three complexes containing progesterone, venetoclax, or actinonin, then validated them in the lab. A venetoclax-inducible system activated the antitumor activity of CAR T cells in vitro; this is a proof of concept without clinical validation.
ai_technology: MaSIF (deep learning on molecular surfaces)
organization: EPFL; and AITHYRA

evidence.tested: MaSIF-designed binders were validated in the lab against three drug-bound complexes, and a venetoclax-inducible system switched on CAR-T tumor-killing activity in vitro.
evidence.unknown: The source states the CAR-T work is in vitro only, with no clinical validation, and binding sites are hard to predict.
evidence.ai_role: MaSIF generated surface fingerprints and searched for complementary protein surfaces to design binders.

title: MatterGen: materials design with a generative model
summary: A diffusion model trained on 608,000 stable materials. Compound TaCr2O6, generated with a constraint of 200 GPa bulk modulus, was synthesized and measured at 169 GPa (relative error under 20%), but with Ta–Cr disorder differing from the proposed structure. One experimental example.
ai_technology: MatterGen (diffusion model)
organization: Microsoft Research

evidence.tested: The generated TaCr2O6 structure was synthesized and its bulk modulus measured at 169 GPa against the 200 GPa target, with relative error under 20%.
evidence.unknown: The source reports one experimental example, with Ta-Cr disorder differing from the proposed structure, and cites no separate publication for this compound.
evidence.ai_role: MatterGen, a diffusion model conditioned on a 200 GPa bulk modulus, generated the structure.

title: Computer-designed proteins neutralize snake toxins
summary: Small, stable proteins designed with AI bind and neutralize three-finger toxins from cobras and mambas in the lab; in mice, they yield 80–100% survival against lethal neurotoxin doses, depending on the toxin. Laboratory and animal studies only; traditional antivenoms remain central.
ai_technology: AI protein design (RFdiffusion)
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: Lab tests showed the designed proteins neutralized multiple subtypes of three-finger toxins; in mice they gave complete protection from lethal neurotoxin exposure, with 80-100% survival depending on the toxin and antitoxin.
evidence.unknown: The page does not mention human trials, toxin types other than elapid three-finger toxins, and traditional antivenoms remain central to treatment.
evidence.ai_role: Designed small, stable proteins on the computer that bind key regions of the toxins.

title: PRAIM: AI finds more breast cancers in German screening
summary: In a prospective study of over 460,000 women at twelve German sites, AI-assisted reading detected 6.7 cancers per thousand exams versus 5.7 without AI. Recall rates for further assessment were 37.4 versus 38.3 per thousand. This observational study does not show a survival benefit, and estimates of workload reduction with automated reading come from simulations.
ai_technology: AI support for mammogram reading (Vara)
organization: Universität zu Lübeck; UKSH, and Vara

evidence.tested: A prospective study of over 460,000 women at twelve German sites (2021-2023) compared AI-assisted reading with standard double reading by radiologists: 6.7 vs 5.7 cancers per 1,000 exams.
evidence.unknown: No survival benefit is shown; workload and skipped-review figures come from simulations, and the effect on prognosis is still to be studied.
evidence.ai_role: AI read about half of the mammograms, marking cases as normal or suspicious, with the rest read by double reading.

title: GenCast: ensemble weather forecasts with a diffusion model
summary: A 0.25° model that outperformed ECMWF's ENS ensemble on 97.2% of 1,320 variable-and-lead-time combinations (99.8% beyond 36 hours) and produces a 15-day ensemble in about 8 minutes on a TPU. Physical models remain essential because they provide training data and initial conditions.
ai_technology: GenCast (diffusion model)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Forecasts were compared with ECMWF ENS on held-out 2019 data (trained up to 2018) across 1,320 variable and lead-time combinations; GenCast was more accurate on 97.2% of targets.
evidence.unknown: Forecasts are especially uncertain beyond a few days, the wind-power analysis is only a proof of principle, and physics-based models remain needed for training data and initial conditions.
evidence.ai_role: A diffusion model generates an ensemble of 50 or more 15-day weather trajectories from the current weather state.

title: AlphaQubit: a neural decoder for quantum error correction
summary: A Transformer-based decoder trained on data from a 49-qubit Sycamore processor made 6% fewer errors than tensor-network methods and 30% fewer than correlated matching in the largest experiments. It is too slow for real-time error correction on fast superconducting processors.
ai_technology: AlphaQubit (Transformer)
organization: Google DeepMind; and Google Quantum AI

evidence.tested: On Sycamore data, logical error per round was 2.901e-2 (distance 3) and 2.748e-2 (distance 5), versus 3.028e-2 and 2.915e-2 for a tensor-network decoder. Simulations to distance 11 (241 qubits); correlated matching was 1.25 to 1.4 times worse.
evidence.unknown: Throughput is slower than the 1 microsecond per round target. Training at distance 11 needs more data. Accuracy beyond distance 11 and logical computations remain future work. Larger-distance results are simulated.
evidence.ai_role: A recurrent transformer neural network decodes surface-code syndromes to predict logical errors; it is the method under test.

title: OCx24: experimental catalysts for evaluating prediction models
summary: A dataset from Meta FAIR, the University of Toronto, and VSParticle covers over 600 mixed-metal catalysts made from 13 elements and tested under the same conditions, alongside analysis of over 19,000 materials. Hydrogen-evolution predictions flagged platinum-containing alloys as promising, although platinum was absent from training data. Fewer than 25% of produced catalysts matched the target; this was a pilot.
ai_technology: Catalyst prediction models (Open Catalyst)
organization: Meta AI; University of Toronto, and VSParticle

evidence.tested: Computational predictions were compared with lab results: 441 gas diffusion electrodes tested in zero-gap electrolysis and 572 characterized samples, alongside DFT-verified adsorption energies on about 20,000 materials.
evidence.unknown: Platinum was ranked as a top hydrogen-evolution candidate but was not experimentally tested, and the abstract lists no explicit limitations.
evidence.ai_role: AI-accelerated relaxations (685 million) fed a data-driven Sabatier volcano that flagged platinum-containing alloys as promising.

title: Evo: a foundation model for DNA, from molecules to genomes
summary: Published in Science, Evo (Arc Institute, Stanford, and UC Berkeley) designed EvoCas9-1, a CRISPR system sharing only about 73% of its sequence with CRISPR-Cas9 but with comparable activity after eleven designs, and new IS200/IS605 transposons that cut and paste DNA. The team calls this the beginning and conducted an ethics and safety study.
ai_technology: Evo (DNA foundation model)
organization: Arc Institute; Stanford, and UC Berkeley

evidence.tested: Evo was prompted to generate CRISPR systems; EvoCas9-1 was obtained after testing eleven designs, validated in the lab by an experimental biology subteam.
evidence.unknown: The page gives no success rates or error analysis, and an ethics and safety investigation addressed potential risks rather than efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: Evo, a DNA-trained foundation model, designed the protein and RNA components of EvoCas9-1 and new IS200/IS605 transposons.

title: Seven-day flood forecasts with reliability similar to earlier five-day forecasts
summary: The new model, trained on 15,980 stations (up from 5,680), gives seven-day reliability comparable to the previous model's five-day forecast. Flood Hub covers over 100 countries and about 700 million people (up from 460 million). About 250,000 virtual points are unverified and intended for experts only; flash, urban, and coastal floods remain out of scope. Google Research reports the November performance and coverage update, and the March 2024 Nature paper linked in the relationship documents the earlier model.
ai_technology: Hydrological forecasting model
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: Gauged basins were checked with standard cross-validation, and ungauged locations were checked against Sentinel-1 radar inundation images; reliability was compared using Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency distributions across 3,079 basins.
evidence.unknown: Ungauged validation covers only a fraction of locations, flash, urban and coastal floods are out of scope, and virtual-gauge forecasts are unverified.
evidence.ai_role: An LSTM network takes meteorological time series and static catchment attributes, adds input from DeepMind's medium-range forecast model, and outputs a probabilistic streamflow distribution.

relationships.reason: The November announcement describes a new model and identifies the March paper as its predecessor.

title: Mobile autonomous robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry
summary: Mobile robots move samples between a synthesis platform, a UPLC-MS spectrometer, and a benchtop NMR, while a heuristic decision-maker evaluates data and chooses reactions. Demonstrated on structural diversification, supramolecular chemistry, and photochemical synthesis. The AI is heuristic and there is no speed or accuracy metric; the announcement says robots will not have a ‘Eureka’ moment.
ai_technology: Heuristic decision-making with mobile robots
organization: University of Liverpool

evidence.tested: Mobile robots were demonstrated on three exploratory chemistry problems (structural diversification, supramolecular chemistry, photochemical synthesis); the page reports no reaction counts or accuracy metrics, only that the AI made the same or similar decisions as a human researcher.
evidence.unknown: The page reports no quantitative accuracy metrics, only two robots were used, and the system lacks a 'Eureka' moment.
evidence.ai_role: A heuristic decision-maker processes analytical data and autonomously decides whether a reaction proceeds to the next step.

title: FlyWire: the complete map of neurons in the Drosophila brain
summary: Connectome of the adult Drosophila brain: nearly 140,000 neurons, over 15 million synaptic connections, and over 8,000 cell types. The page says deep neural networks segmented images and extracted neurons, but automated segmentation had millions of errors and required about 33 years of human correction across over 50 labs and citizen scientists.
ai_technology: Deep neural networks for segmentation
organization: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology; Princeton, and FlyWire

evidence.tested: The connectome was checked against an earlier partial map, and connectomes were found to be highly consistent between animals.
evidence.unknown: About 0.5% of neurons have developmental wiring defects, connection signs were predicted rather than measured, and the dataset was not built for a specific medical application.
evidence.ai_role: Deep neural networks segmented electron microscopy images and extracted neurons; the first automated pass had millions of errors and was corrected by humans.

title: TxGNN: repurposing existing drugs for rare diseases
summary: The model covers about 8,000 drugs across 17,080 diseases and is nearly 50% better than competitors at identifying candidates and 35% more accurate on contraindications. It was tested on 1.2 million medical records and on three rare diseases excluded from training. Computational predictions only, with no laboratory or clinical confirmation.
ai_technology: TxGNN (graph neural network)
organization: Harvard Medical School

evidence.tested: The model was checked against about 8,000 drugs and 17,080 diseases, validated on 1.2 million medical records, and asked to find drugs for three rare diseases excluded from training; it was compared with leading drug-repurposing models.
evidence.unknown: Identified therapies would require further evaluation for dosing and delivery, and there is no laboratory or clinical confirmation.
evidence.ai_role: Proposed existing drugs for thousands of diseases, predicted contraindications and side effects, and gave a rationale for each prediction.

title: Nazca: AI helps discover 303 new figurative geoglyphs
summary: An IBM model flagged 1,309 candidates; about a quarter were ground-checked over roughly six months, finding 303 new figurative geoglyphs among 430 already known and increasing the discovery rate 16-fold. Another 968 candidates remain to be checked; the study had been accepted by PNAS at the time of the announcement.
ai_technology: Neural network for aerial images
organization: Yamagata University; and IBM Research

evidence.tested: Field teams ground-checked about a quarter of the 1,309 AI-flagged candidates on foot over roughly six months, finding 303 new figurative geoglyphs.
evidence.unknown: 968 candidates remain unsurveyed, training data was limited, and the study was accepted but not yet published in PNAS at the time of the announcement.
evidence.ai_role: An IBM model that works with few training samples analyzed aerial geospatial imagery to flag likely geoglyph areas.

title: Solvent mixtures for flow batteries found through an AI–experiment cycle
summary: PNNL and Argonne identified solvent mixtures that dissolve three times more than a compound proposed for flow batteries, exploring less than 10% of about 2,000 combinations. The model receives experimental data and guides subsequent experiments; the result concerns solubility, without demonstrating performance of a complete battery.
ai_technology: Machine learning in a loop with high-throughput experiments
organization: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory; and Argonne National Laboratory

evidence.tested: Active learning guided solubility measurements of 2,1,3-benzothiadiazole in binary solvents: 218 measurements from 2,101 candidates found 18 mixtures above 6.20 M; best 6.50 M. On a 98-solvent set, Bayesian optimization needed 17 ± 11 trials versus about 50 ± 27 random.
evidence.unknown: Tested one solute, binary solvents only; solubility is not the only property and viscosity, conductivity and stability were not optimized. Model accuracy on 40 test solvents was R2 = 0.63. Real battery performance not reported.
evidence.ai_role: A Gaussian process model with an expected-improvement rule chose which solvents to measure; a robotic platform prepared samples and NMR measured solubility; humans selected features and candidate lists.

title: AlphaProteo: AI-designed protein binders
summary: A system for designing high-affinity protein binders, tested against seven targets, achieved 88% laboratory success on BHRF1 and bindings 3 to 300 times stronger than the best existing methods. It produced no valid binders for TNFα; strong binding is only a first step.
ai_technology: AlphaProteo
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Binders were designed against seven target proteins and tested in the lab, with 3 to 300 times stronger binding and higher experimental success rates than the best existing methods.
evidence.unknown: Per-target success rates are not given on the abstract page and no limitations are listed.
evidence.ai_role: A family of machine learning models for protein design that generates the binders.

title: CHIEF: detecting cancer and predicting survival from slides
summary: Trained on 15 million patches and 60,000 slides and tested on more than 19,400 slides from 32 datasets and 24 hospitals: it detects cancer with about 94% accuracy across 15 datasets, predicts mutations in 54 genes with over 70% accuracy, and improves survival prediction by 8% across 17 institutions. Retrospective validation; not trained on rare diseases or premalignant tissue.
ai_technology: CHIEF (pathology foundation model)
organization: Harvard Medical School

evidence.tested: Retrospective validation on more than 19,400 slides from 32 datasets at 24 hospitals; cancer detection was about 94% accurate across datasets.
evidence.unknown: Validation beyond these datasets is still needed, rare and non-cancerous conditions and pre-malignant tissue were not tested, and gene prediction accuracy varies by gene and cancer type.
evidence.ai_role: Read digital tumor slides to detect cancer, predict gene mutations and survival, and generate heat maps of tissue features for pathologists.

title: A speech neuroprosthesis reaches 97.5% accuracy after calibration
summary: A man with ALS used a brain-computer interface with machine learning to turn attempted speech into text and synthetic voice. After further training, the system maintained 97.5% accuracy; the study reports more than 248 hours of spontaneous conversation over 32 weeks. Result from one participant with an invasive implant; still experimental.
ai_technology: Neural speech decoding with machine learning
organization: UC Davis Health; and BrainGate

evidence.tested: One participant with ALS in the BrainGate2 trial completed 84 sessions over 32 weeks with over 248 hours of self-paced use; word accuracy was measured per session, with 97.5% maintained after continued data collection.
evidence.unknown: The page does not state the study's limitations, and the result comes from one participant with an invasive implant.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning decoded neural activity into phonemes and then words in real time, with continuous updates, and software generated the voice.

title: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2: silver-medal level at the Math Olympiad
summary: The two systems solved 4 of 6 problems at IMO 2024, scoring 28 of 42 points, one point below the gold threshold. Problems were manually translated into formal language, and some required up to three days of computation instead of the official 4.5 hours.
ai_technology: AlphaProof (Lean) and AlphaGeometry 2
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: The systems solved official IMO 2024 problems, graded under IMO rules by Prof. Timothy Gowers and Dr Joseph Myers, reaching 28 of 42 points; problems were manually translated into formal language first.
evidence.unknown: Two combinatorics problems remained unsolved, translation was manual, and some solutions took up to three days.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaProof solved three problems with formal proofs, and AlphaGeometry 2 proved the geometry problem within 19 seconds of formalization.

source_review.scope: Original institutional announcement checked for the specific results, AI contribution and limitations cited in the antibiotic dossier or mathematical follow-up pilot. Full-paper reanalysis, external replication and an exhaustive follow-up search were not performed.

relationships.reason: AlphaGeometry 2 is explicitly described as an improved AlphaGeometry version; this link concerns the geometry component, not attribution of all four IMO solutions.

follow_up.note: The updated original announcement dates publication of the AlphaProof methodology in Nature to 12 November 2025. This journal transition is not an independent replication and does not apply to every component of the combined system.

follow_up_review.scope: Bounded check of the original announcements cited by the events recorded here, including explicit links to later program work. This is not an exhaustive literature search or ongoing monitoring commitment.

title: NeuralGCM: a hybrid physics-and-learning model for weather and climate
summary: At 1.4° resolution, the model outperformed ECMWF-ENS in 95% of cases for forecasts from 2 to 15 days; at 2.8°, its mean 1980–2020 temperature error was 0.25 °C versus 0.75 °C for atmosphere-only models. It is more than 3,500 times faster than X-SHiELD on a TPU. It models only the atmosphere and is not yet a complete climate model.
ai_technology: NeuralGCM (differentiable dynamical core and neural networks)
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: Evaluated with the WeatherBench 2 benchmark against ECMWF-ENS (better in 95% of 2-15 day cases at 1.4 degrees) and against AMIP climate baselines for 1980-2020 temperature (0.25 vs 0.75 degrees C error).
evidence.unknown: The model covers only the atmosphere and is not yet a complete climate model; oceans and the carbon cycle are future goals.
evidence.ai_role: A neural network learns small-scale physics such as cloud formation, replacing hand-built parameterizations, coupled to a physics-based fluid dynamics solver.

title: ESM3 and esmGFP: a fluorescent protein designed by a language model
summary: ESM3 designed esmGFP, a fluorescent protein of 229 amino acids with 96 mutations relative to the closest known protein (about 58% similarity). In a second round of 96 designs, some proteins glowed as brightly as natural GFPs. The comparison with ‘more than 500 million years of evolution’ is an analogy-based estimate.
ai_technology: ESM3
organization: EvolutionaryScale

evidence.tested: In two rounds of 96 designs, lab measurements of fluorescence found some proteins as bright as natural GFPs; esmGFP differs by 96 mutations and is about 58% similar to the closest natural protein.
evidence.unknown: The page lists no formal limitations; the designed B8 was about 50 times dimmer and slower to mature than natural GFPs.
evidence.ai_role: ESM3 generated new GFP candidates prompted with structural residues from natural GFP.

title: African elephants address one another with calls resembling names
summary: About 470 calls from 101 callers to 117 recipients in Kenya: a model trained only on acoustic structure identifies the intended recipient, and playback experiments show elephants respond more to calls addressed to them. The model confirms a previously suspected pattern; more data are needed to isolate the ‘names’.
ai_technology: Acoustic classification model
organization: Colorado State University; Save the Elephants and ElephantVoices

evidence.tested: About 470 calls from 101 callers to 117 receivers were analyzed, and playback experiments showed elephants respond more to calls addressed to them.
evidence.unknown: More data are needed to isolate the names, it is unknown whether elephants name other things, and naming was not universal.
evidence.ai_role: A model trained only on acoustic structure identified the intended recipient of each call, supporting the name-like finding.

title: AMPSphere: antimicrobial peptides from the global microbiome
summary: Machine learning identified 863,498 candidate sequences in microbial genomes and metagenomes. Of 100 synthesized peptides, 63 inhibited at least one of the eleven strains tested; some showed activity in animal models. The catalog contains candidates, not hundreds of thousands of clinically validated antibiotics.
ai_technology: Machine learning for antimicrobial peptides
organization: University of Pennsylvania; and collaborators

evidence.tested: 100 predicted peptides were synthesized and tested in vitro and in vivo against drug-resistant pathogens and human gut commensals; 63 inhibited pathogens.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no limitations and does not name the strains or animal models used.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning predicted antimicrobial peptides across 63,410 metagenomes and 87,920 genomes, producing a catalog of 863,498 non-redundant candidates.

title: Aurora: a foundation model for the atmosphere
summary: A 1.3-billion-parameter model for high-resolution weather and air-pollution forecasting: it matches or exceeds CAMS on 74% of targets and matches or beats GraphCast on 94%. The roughly 5,000-fold speedup over the IFS system is an estimate; GraphCast remains slightly better up to five days.
ai_technology: Aurora (foundation model)
organization: Microsoft Research

evidence.tested: Forecasts were compared with CAMS for air pollution (Jun-Nov 2022, matched or beat 74% of targets) and with GraphCast (matched or beat 94% of targets) over 2022 evaluation periods.
evidence.unknown: GraphCast was slightly better on specific humidity up to five days, and the page has no dedicated limitations section.
evidence.ai_role: A 1.3-billion-parameter foundation model, pretrained on over a million hours of simulations, forecasts weather and air pollution at 0.1 degrees.

title: AlphaFold 3: structure and interactions of life’s molecules
summary: It predicts joint structures of proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules and ions. DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs report at least 50% greater accuracy than existing methods for protein interactions with other molecules. Free for non-commercial research through the AlphaFold Server.
ai_technology: AlphaFold 3
organization: Google DeepMind; and Isomorphic Labs

evidence.tested: Higher accuracy than docking tools for protein–ligand interactions, than nucleic-acid-specific predictors for protein–nucleic acid interactions, and than AlphaFold-Multimer v2.3 for antibody–antigen prediction.
evidence.unknown: Accuracy on new experimental targets beyond the benchmarks is not described in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: A diffusion-based architecture predicting joint structures of proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, ions and modified residues.

title: ChemCrow: a language-model agent with chemistry tools
summary: An agent with 18 tools and GPT-4 planned and carried out the synthesis of DEET and three thiourea organocatalysts on a cloud platform, and guided discovery of a chromophore absorbing at 336 nm against a 369 nm target; evaluated on 14 cases by four expert chemists. Hallucinations, limited tasks and dual-use risks; 12 of 18 tools were released.
ai_technology: ChemCrow (GPT-4 with tools)
organization: ChemCrow group (Nature Machine Intelligence)

evidence.tested: Expert and LLM judgments were used to evaluate the agent, which planned and executed syntheses of an insect repellent and three organocatalysts and guided discovery of a chromophore.
evidence.unknown: The abstract says LLMs struggle with chemistry and lack external knowledge, and GPT-4 as evaluator could not distinguish clearly wrong completions from ChemCrow's performance.
evidence.ai_role: An LLM agent with 18 expert-designed chemistry tools planned and executed syntheses and guided molecular discovery; the page does not name the underlying model.

title: Sperm whales: a possible ‘phonetic alphabet’ in their calls
summary: Analysis of nearly 9,000 codas from the eastern Caribbean clan, collected over more than ten years, proposes a combinatorial structure involving rhythm, tempo, rubato and ornamentation. Published in Nature Communications; communicative function remains unknown, data cover one clan, and the page does not specify machine-learning methods.
ai_technology: Machine-learning analysis of whale calls
organization: Project CETI; and MIT CSAIL

evidence.tested: Nearly 9,000 codas from the eastern Caribbean clan, collected over more than ten years, were analyzed for context-sensitive features (rubato, ornamentation) and categorical rhythm and tempo.
evidence.unknown: The communicative function of many codas is unknown, whether the features encode intent needs future field research, and the duality-of-patterning link is only a possibility.
evidence.ai_role: Not reported; the page does not specify what machine learning did in the analysis.

title: Closed-loop, distributed discovery of organic laser emitters
summary: In a two-month campaign, more than 1,000 candidates were synthesized and tested at six laboratories across five sites on three continents, identifying at least 21 high-performance candidates as gain materials from a space of more than 150,000 experiments. These are gain candidates, not confirmed lasers; the page gives no laser metrics; source is a consortium press release.
ai_technology: Closed-loop optimization with autonomous laboratories
organization: Acceleration Consortium (University of Toronto)

evidence.tested: Over 1,000 candidates were synthesized and tested in a two-month distributed campaign across six teams in five labs on three continents, identifying at least 21 high-performance gain candidates.
evidence.unknown: The commercialization speed goal was not met, the candidates are gain materials rather than confirmed lasers, and the page gives no laser metrics.
evidence.ai_role: A closed-loop AI reviewed data, selected molecules to synthesize and test, and predicted the next best experiment; a cloud platform coordinated the labs.

title: Protein-surface-designed molecules activate PPARs
summary: A generative model designed molecules from the three-dimensional surfaces of PPAR proteins: synthesized in the laboratory, they increased activity and were tested by Roche. They demonstrate the method and are not intended for commercial development; the tests do not establish safety or efficacy in humans.
ai_technology: Protein-surface-guided generative AI
organization: ETH Zurich; and Roche

evidence.tested: ETH chemists synthesized the AI-designed molecules in the lab, and Roche ran a variety of tests showing they are stable and non-toxic.
evidence.unknown: The article does not state limitations, the molecules were not developed toward market, and the tests do not establish safety or efficacy in humans.
evidence.ai_role: A generative model designed molecules from scratch matched to a protein's three-dimensional surface, without human intervention.

title: OpenCRISPR-1: a genome editor designed by language models
summary: Profluent built an atlas of 5.1 million CRISPR-Cas proteins and generated a Cas9-like editor with 403 mutations relative to SpCas9. Of 48 generated sequences, the best (OpenCRISPR-1) achieved 55.7% on-target editing versus 48.3% for SpCas9, and 0.32% off-target editing versus 6.1%. Human cells in the laboratory only; company data; the page does not indicate peer review.
ai_technology: Protein language models
organization: Profluent

evidence.tested: Of 48 selected generated sequences, the best (OpenCRISPR-1) was tested in human cells: 55.7% on-target editing vs 48.3% for SpCas9, and 0.32% off-target vs 6.1%.
evidence.unknown: The company article has no explicit limitations section and does not state whether a preprint or peer review exists.
evidence.ai_role: A language model pretrained on protein data and steered to CRISPR families using a 5.1-million-protein atlas generated Cas9-like nucleases and compatible sgRNAs.

title: Antibodies designed from scratch with RFdiffusion
summary: Baker’s group showed RFdiffusion can be adapted to generate antibodies: in laboratory tests, designs bound influenza virus and other targets as intended. Proof-of-concept study, first circulated as a preprint in March 2024; experts quoted by Nature call it promising but an early step; no affinity values reported.
ai_technology: RFdiffusion
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: Laboratory tests confirmed that the designed antibodies bind influenza virus and other targets as intended; no affinity values are reported.
evidence.unknown: The work is described as a proof-of-concept study, and no specific limitations are listed.
evidence.ai_role: RFdiffusion was tuned to generate antibodies from scratch.

title: AI identifies semapimod against dormant bacteria
summary: A machine-learning system selected semapimod, a known anti-inflammatory drug, for activity against dormant Gram-negative bacteria. MIT reports laboratory activity against E. coli and A. baumannii and an effect that sensitizes these bacteria to other antibiotics; the result is preclinical and does not demonstrate efficacy in patients.
ai_technology: Machine learning for compound screening
organization: MIT

evidence.tested: Lab-only time-lapse microscopy of E. coli treated with semapimod showed activity against stationary-phase E. coli and A. baumannii and sensitization to other antibiotics.
evidence.unknown: The article states no limitations, no animal or patient testing is mentioned, and no drug combinations are named.
evidence.ai_role: AI-based high-throughput screening of known drug compounds identified semapimod for antibiotic activity.

title: SEEDS: weather ensembles generated with a diffusion model
summary: The model produces 256 members at 2° resolution every three minutes on a TPU and matches or exceeds the operational GEFS ensemble (31 members) on rank histograms, RMSE and CRPS. For the Lisbon heatwave (July 2022), with 16,384 members, none of GEFS’s 31 members was as warm as observed. One extreme case; depends on physics-based forecasts as seeds; published in Science Advances.
ai_technology: SEEDS (diffusion model)
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: The ensemble was compared with the operational GEFS (31 members) using rank histograms, RMSE and CRPS, and with a 16,384-member ensemble for the Lisbon heatwave of July 2022.
evidence.unknown: The heatwave comparisons are single examples, the model depends on physics-based seed forecasts, and the page has no explicit limitations section.
evidence.ai_role: A denoising diffusion model generates large weather-forecast ensembles from one or two operational forecasts.

title: SyntheMol: generated antibiotic candidates against Acinetobacter baumannii
summary: The generative model proposed about 25,000 candidates in under nine hours from more than 130,000 synthesis building blocks; of 58 synthesized, six killed a drug-resistant A. baumannii strain and two were not toxic in mice. Mechanism unknown, efficacy in infected animals untested, and four of the six compounds were not water-soluble.
ai_technology: SyntheMol (generative model)
organization: Stanford Medicine; and McMaster University

evidence.tested: Of 58 synthesized candidates, six killed a drug-resistant A. baumannii strain in the lab, and two of those were not toxic in mice.
evidence.unknown: Four of the six compounds were not water-soluble so were not tested in mice, efficacy in infected animals is untested, and the mechanism is unknown.
evidence.ai_role: A generative model proposed about 25,000 candidate antibiotics and synthesis recipes in under nine hours from over 130,000 building blocks.

source_review.scope: Original institutional announcement checked for the specific results, AI contribution and limitations cited in the antibiotic dossier or mathematical follow-up pilot. Full-paper reanalysis, external replication and an exhaustive follow-up search were not performed.

title: Reliable flood forecasts even where gauges are missing
summary: A model trained on 5,680 gauges improved average global forecast reliability from zero to five days: forecasts at days 4–5 were similar to or better than day-zero forecasts from GloFAS v4. Flood Hub covers more than 80 countries. F1 comparison across 2,092 basins for two-year return-period events; flash and urban floods remain to be covered.
ai_technology: Hydrological forecasting model
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: F1 scores were compared with GloFAS v4 for 2-year return-period events across 2,092 watersheds (2014-2023); reliability at 4-5 day lead times was similar to or better than GloFAS at day zero.
evidence.unknown: Coverage must expand to more locations, flash and urban floods are not yet covered, and the gain is average-level rather than uniform.
evidence.ai_role: Two sequential LSTMs with a mixture density output produce probabilistic streamflow forecasts, trained on 5,680 gauges.

title: Preventing tearing-mode instabilities in a tokamak with AI
summary: A model trained only on past experimental data predicts instabilities up to 300 ms ahead, and an AI controller adjusted plasma shape and beam power to avoid them in a real DIII-D experiment. The authors call it a proof of concept on one machine and one type of instability; paper published in Nature on February 21, 2024.
ai_technology: Prediction and reinforcement-learning control
organization: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory; and Princeton University

evidence.tested: The reinforcement-learning controller was tested in experiments on the DIII-D tokamak, where it kept the tearing likelihood below a threshold, including under unfavorable conditions.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not state the prediction horizon and lists no other limitations; tearing instability is hard to forecast.
evidence.ai_role: A deep reinforcement learning controller, trained in a multimodal dynamic model of tearing instability, adjusted plasma operation to keep it stable.

title: Vesuvius Challenge: the first Herculaneum scroll can be read
summary: The $700,000 prize went to a submission with 11 additional columns and more than 2,000 characters (about 5% of the first scroll), using models to detect ink and automated segmentation. Papyrologists evaluated 15 anonymized columns and recovered more text from the winning submission. Segmentation remains largely manual and costly.
ai_technology: Ink detection with vision models and automated segmentation
organization: Vesuvius Challenge

evidence.tested: Papyrologists independently evaluated 15 anonymized columns, and the winning submission yielded the most text for every reviewer, meeting the stated criteria.
evidence.unknown: The comprehensive study is not yet published, only rough draft transcriptions exist, segmentation is largely manual, and about 5% of the first scroll has been read.
evidence.ai_role: Models detected ink in CT scans (a TimeSformer-based model was strongest), and an automated tool produced the segmentation of the papyrus surfaces.

title: AlphaGeometry: Olympiad geometry without human demonstrations
summary: A language model proposing constructions and a symbolic engine deriving proofs solved 25 of 30 problems in the IMO-AG-30 benchmark (the previous method solved 10; the average gold medalist score was 25.9), trained on 100 million synthetic examples. It covers geometry only and a 30-problem benchmark.
ai_technology: AlphaGeometry (language model and symbolic engine)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: On the IMO-AG-30 benchmark of 30 Olympiad geometry problems, the system solved 25 versus 10 for the previous method, with each solution checked by computer.
evidence.unknown: It covers geometry only, roughly a third of Olympiad problems, and approaches but does not match gold-medalist performance.
evidence.ai_role: A language model proposes auxiliary constructions and a symbolic engine derives proofs, looping until a proof is found.

source_review.scope: Original institutional announcement checked for the specific results, AI contribution and limitations cited in the antibiotic dossier or mathematical follow-up pilot. Full-paper reanalysis, external replication and an exhaustive follow-up search were not performed.

follow_up.note: DeepMind describes AlphaGeometry 2 as an improved version used for the IMO 2024 geometry problem. The combined result also used AlphaProof; it does not belong to AlphaGeometry alone.

follow_up_review.scope: Bounded check of the original announcements cited by the events recorded here, including explicit links to later program work. This is not an exhaustive literature search or ongoing monitoring commitment.

title: From 32 million candidates to a new battery electrolyte
summary: With the PNNL laboratory, Microsoft screened 32.6 million materials using AI models and high-performance computing, narrowing them to 500,000, then 800, 150, and finally an electrolyte replacing some lithium with sodium (about 70% less lithium). PNNL synthesized it and built a working solid-state battery. Validation and optimization are ongoing; the post is by a Microsoft executive.
ai_technology: Azure Quantum Elements (AI and DFT simulations)
organization: Microsoft Azure Quantum; and PNNL

evidence.tested: The top candidates in the Na_xLi_(3-x)YCl6 series were synthesized and experimentally characterized for structure and conductivity; the abstract does not mention battery cell testing.
evidence.unknown: The approximately half-million materials are predictions of potential stability, other candidates are still under investigation, and no explicit limitations are listed.
evidence.ai_role: AI and physics-based models on cloud HPC screened over 32 million candidates and identified 18 promising electrolyte candidates.

title: Satellite map of industrial activity at sea
summary: A model applied to about 2 million GB of Sentinel-1 radar imagery (2017–2021) maps vessels and infrastructure: about 75% of industrial fishing vessels are not publicly tracked, over 25% of shipping and energy activity is missing from AIS data, wind turbines more than doubled, and global fishing fell 12% during COVID. Published in Nature; ‘fishing’ classification is inferred; source is the organization’s own release.
ai_technology: Deep learning on radar imagery
organization: Global Fishing Watch; University of Wisconsin–Madison, Duke, UC Santa Barbara and SkyTruth

evidence.tested: The page describes no ground-truth check, accuracy metric or comparison for the vessel and infrastructure mapping, so the main claim is not evaluated in the source.
evidence.unknown: Not all boats broadcast their position, the 'fishing' classification is inferred, and the page gives no accuracy figures for that step.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning detected vessels and offshore infrastructure in satellite imagery and inferred which non-broadcasting vessels were likely fishing; the model type is not named.

title: A new class of antibiotic candidates against MRSA
summary: A deep-learning model trained on about 39,000 compounds screened about 12 million commercial compounds; of about 280 purchased and tested, two from the same class reduced MRSA burden tenfold in two mouse models, with very low toxicity to human cells. Results from plates and mice; toxicity was partly predicted computationally.
ai_technology: Deep learning with chemical-structure explainability
organization: MIT

evidence.tested: About 283 compounds were bought and tested empirically; one structural class reduced bacterial burden in mouse skin and systemic thigh infection models, and cytotoxicity to human cells was measured.
evidence.unknown: The page does not list specific study limitations; next steps are chemical property analysis and potential clinical use.
evidence.ai_role: Graph neural network ensembles trained on about 39,000 compounds with measured antibacterial and human-cell toxicity predicted both properties for about 12 million compounds and flagged candidates for purchase and testing.

title: Coscientist: autonomous chemical research with language models
summary: A GPT-4-guided system designs, plans and runs experiments using web search, documentation, code and laboratory automation, performing six tasks including optimization of palladium cross-coupling reactions. The abstract does not make clear which tasks used real hardware; only the abstract was reviewed.
ai_technology: Coscientist (GPT-4)
organization: Carnegie Mellon University; and Emerald Cloud Lab

evidence.tested: The system was run on six tasks, including a palladium-catalysed cross-coupling reaction optimization that the abstract reports as successful.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not state which tasks used physical hardware and which used simulation, and states no limitations.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4 planned and executed experiments by using web search, documentation, code execution and experimental automation tools.

title: Designed proteins bind peptides with the highest affinity reported
summary: Using RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN, researchers designed proteins that bind helical peptides such as glucagon, neuropeptide Y and parathyroid hormone, with what the authors consider the highest reported affinity for a computer-generated biomolecule. They detect low concentrations of peptides in human serum and withstand heat; a parathyroid-hormone biosensor produced a 21-fold increase in bioluminescence. The press release gives no affinity values.
ai_technology: RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: Designed binders were tested in the lab for peptide detection (mass spectrometry, including low-concentration peptide detection) and a bioluminescence biosensor produced a 21-fold signal increase with parathyroid hormone; the press release gives no affinity values.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not describe how affinity was measured, does not mention serum testing, and states no limitations; the press release states no limitations.
evidence.ai_role: RFdiffusion, extended for flexible targets and partial diffusion, designed binders to helical peptides, de novo or by refining other designs.

title: FunSearch: new mathematical results with a language model
summary: A language model (PaLM 2) paired with an automatic evaluator found the largest cap sets on record in some dimensions, the biggest increase in 20 years, and bin-packing heuristics using fewer bins than established methods. The problem must first be expressed as code with an evaluation procedure.
ai_technology: FunSearch (PaLM 2 and automatic evaluator)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Programs were scored automatically by an evaluator; on the cap set problem they found larger cap sets than the best known, and on online bin packing their heuristics beat established baselines.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not explicitly state limitations; the blog says the method needs an automatic evaluation procedure and that the bin-packing heuristics were tailored to specific data.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained large language model (PaLM 2) generated candidate programs in an evolutionary search guided by an automatic evaluator.

title: MatterGen: stable materials generated from desired properties
summary: A diffusion model generates stable, novel materials directly from desired properties: 2.9 times more stable, novel and unique structures than CDVAE, and over 250 materials with bulk modulus above 400 GPa versus 2 in the reference dataset. Results were checked with DFT calculations; experimental verification remains the ultimate test.
ai_technology: MatterGen (diffusion model)
organization: Microsoft Research

evidence.tested: Generated structures were checked with DFT calculations and compared with CDVAE and screening baselines (2.9 times more stable, novel and unique structures than CDVAE, per the blog); experimental verification is stated as not yet done.
evidence.unknown: Limitations stated: DFT has known limitations and experimental verification remains the ultimate test; the arXiv abstract states no limitations.
evidence.ai_role: A diffusion model generated new crystal structures conditioned on desired properties.

title: GNoME: 2.2 million new predicted crystals
summary: A graph neural network predicted 2.2 million new crystals, including 380,000 of the most stable, raising the number of known stable materials from about 48,000 to 421,000. External laboratories synthesized 736 predicted structures. Stability is calculated and does not guarantee a material can be produced or will be useful.
ai_technology: GNoME (Graph Networks for Materials Exploration)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Predicted stability was checked computationally with DFT, and external laboratories independently synthesized 736 of the predicted structures.
evidence.unknown: The blog states that most of the 380,000 stable predictions had not been made in a lab and that stability is judged by current scientific standards; manufacturing and usefulness remain open.
evidence.ai_role: A graph neural network trained on about 48,000 stable crystals predicted 2.2 million new crystals, including 380,000 stable ones.

title: A-Lab: an autonomous laboratory for synthesizing inorganic materials
summary: In the Nature paper, the autonomous lab made compounds from computed targets over 17 days of continuous operation. The original press release reported 41 of 58 (71%), while the author’s January 19, 2026 correction reports 36 of 57: on review, 36 of 40 claimed successes were confirmed, 4 were inconclusive from diffraction alone, and ‘new’ meant new to the platform, not to science. One compound was removed because it was in the training data.
ai_technology: A-Lab (autonomous lab with language models and active learning)
organization: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; and UC Berkeley

evidence.tested: The autonomous lab attempted 58 target materials in 17 days of continuous operation and produced 41 novel compounds; failed syntheses were analyzed to suggest improvements.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not name the characterization methods and states no limitations beyond the failed-synthesis analysis; the record notes an erratum published in January 2026.
evidence.ai_role: A robotic platform used computation, literature data, machine learning and active learning to plan and interpret solid-state powder syntheses.

title: Chroma: a generative model for protein design
summary: Generate:Biomedicines published the Chroma model in Nature; it designs new proteins with requested biophysical, biological and therapeutic properties.
