evidence.tested: Of 94 predicted gene clusters selected for testing, experiments validated 42 previously unknown systems; analyses of 1,000 prokaryotic genomes also revealed thousands of uncharacterized protein clusters without homology to known systems.
evidence.unknown: The 42 validated systems came from a selected subset of predictions, not all computationally proposed systems; genome-wide counts are predicted protein clusters, not experimentally tested systems. The source reports a 45% validation rate for 94 tested units.
evidence.ai_role: The machine-learning model identified likely defense proteins beyond conventional defense-island co-localization methods, guiding experimental cloning and phage-challenge validation. Validation confirmed 42 new systems among 94 tested candidates.

title: Interpretable multi-omics machine learning reveals unexpected drug mechanisms in Huntington disease models
summary: An interpretable machine-learning model integrated transcriptomic, epigenomic, metabolomic and proteomic data from Huntington-disease cell models to identify previously unknown mechanisms for protective compounds. The analysis predicted autophagy activation for one compound group and mitochondrial-respiration inhibition for another; follow-up imaging, biochemical and energetics assays experimentally confirmed these effects in the cell model.
ai_technology: Interpretable network-optimization model integrating multi-omics over a molecular-interaction network
organization: University of California San Diego; and collaborators

evidence.tested: The analysis predicted autophagy activation for one compound group and mitochondrial-respiration inhibition for another; follow-up imaging, biochemical and energetics assays experimentally confirmed these effects in the cell model.
evidence.unknown: Findings were experimentally established in STHdhQ111 murine striatal cells, with autophagy effects also checked in human SH-SY5Y and HEK293 cell lines. The paper notes that the model prioritizes pathways but does not resolve every causal step or demonstrate therapeutic efficacy in patients.
evidence.ai_role: The model integrated multiple omics and prioritized cellular pathways as candidate mechanisms of action; researchers tested those predictions with cellular imaging, biochemical assays and energetics measurements. It revealed unexpected mechanisms for compounds with unrelated known targets.

title: Progeni predicts candidate melanoma and colorectal-cancer targets validated in cell models
summary: Progeni combines a probabilistic knowledge graph with graph neural networks to rank disease-associated molecular targets. The authors selected six candidates lacking literature support and reported that knockdown of HSP90AB1 and MME reduced proliferation in a murine melanoma line, while knockdown of ADCY5, ADRA2A and EEF2 reduced proliferation in a murine colorectal-cancer line.
ai_technology: Progeni probabilistic knowledge graph and graph neural network
organization: Tsinghua University; Westlake University; Jilin University; Silexon AI Technology

evidence.tested: The authors selected six candidates lacking literature support and reported that knockdown of HSP90AB1 and MME reduced proliferation in a murine melanoma line, while knockdown of ADCY5, ADRA2A and EEF2 reduced proliferation in a murine colorectal-cancer line.
evidence.unknown: The functional validations were in B16F10 and MC38 murine cell lines, not human tumor samples or clinical settings. The paper evaluates a model and validates selected candidates; it does not establish these as clinically effective therapeutic targets.
evidence.ai_role: The graph neural network ranked new target hypotheses from heterogeneous biological networks and literature co-occurrence evidence. Researchers then tested selected predictions by shRNA knockdown in representative murine cancer cell lines.

title: LIGHTHOUSE identifies riboflavin 5′-monophosphate as a PPAT inhibitor
summary: LIGHTHOUSE, a deep-learning model using protein sequence and chemical representations, nominated riboflavin 5′-monophosphate as an inhibitor of PPAT, a target without reported inhibitors in the paper. A biochemical assay measured PPAT inhibition with an IC50 of 7.5 μM, close to the model’s predicted range; the same study also tested predicted antiviral compounds in cell models.
ai_technology: LIGHTHOUSE (ensemble graph-based deep-learning platform)
organization: Kyushu University; and collaborators

evidence.tested: LIGHTHOUSE, a deep-learning model using protein sequence and chemical representations, nominated riboflavin 5′-monophosphate as an inhibitor of PPAT, a target without reported inhibitors in the paper.
evidence.unknown: The result is an in-vitro enzyme assay, not a validated anticancer treatment. The authors note LIGHTHOUSE can produce false positives; COVID-19 results were also cell-based and had no clinical evidence.
evidence.ai_role: The model scored protein–compound relationships without requiring a 3D target structure and prioritized the compound from >333,000 candidates for experimental follow-up. The authors assayed PPAT activity and confirmed inhibition in vitro.

title: deepDTnet repurposes topotecan as an RORγt inhibitor for multiple-sclerosis models
summary: The deep-learning network deepDTnet predicted retinoic-acid-receptor-related orphan receptor gamma-t (RORγt) as a previously unrecognized target of topotecan. Biochemical assays showed direct inhibition (IC50 0.43 μM), and topotecan improved outcomes in a mouse experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis model of multiple sclerosis.
ai_technology: deepDTnet, heterogeneous drug–gene–disease network embedding with deep learning
organization: Cleveland Clinic; Case Western Reserve University, Harvard Medical School and collaborators

evidence.tested: Biochemical assays showed direct inhibition (IC50 0.43 μM), and topotecan improved outcomes in a mouse experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis model of multiple sclerosis.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is preclinical: direct target and mouse-model assays do not establish safety or effectiveness in people with multiple sclerosis. Topotecan is an established anticancer drug, and its new target/indication remains a repurposing hypothesis.
evidence.ai_role: The model integrated 15 types of chemical, genomic, phenotypic and cellular network profiles to rank new drug targets. It nominated RORγt for topotecan, which the team tested using direct binding/transcriptional assays and a mouse EAE disease model.

title: CLEAN experimentally identifies SAM hydrolase activity in previously uncharacterized proteins
summary: Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign developed CLEAN, a contrastive-learning enzyme-function predictor, and used it to identify the SAM hydrolase activity of the previously uncharacterized protein TTHA0338. In vitro HPLC–MS and enzyme-kinetic experiments also corrected the annotation of MJ1651 and confirmed the multiple activities of SsFIA.
ai_technology: CLEAN (contrastive learning-based enzyme annotation model)
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Cornell University; Georgia Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: In vitro HPLC–MS and enzyme-kinetic experiments also corrected the annotation of MJ1651 and confirmed the multiple activities of SsFIA.
evidence.unknown: The study validated a small, selected set of proteins, and also showed CLEAN can assign functions to non-enzymes; the demonstrated result is specific to the tested proteins. TTHA0338 is one of multiple results reported by this paper; record describes the previously unknown function rather than treating every model benchmark as a separate discovery.
evidence.ai_role: CLEAN predicted enzyme commission functions from protein sequences; researchers then validated the predicted activity experimentally. It was the model that nominated TTHA0338 as a SAM hydrolase, not an autonomous discovery or validation system.

title: deepAMP designs broad-spectrum antimicrobial peptides active against resistant bacteria
summary: Researchers at Hunan University and collaborators used the peptide language model deepAMP to optimize antimicrobial peptides and experimentally tested 29 candidates. More than 90% inhibited Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria better than the reference peptide penetratin; three candidates showed reduced resistance emergence in serial-passage assays and activity in a mouse Pseudomonas wound-infection model.
ai_technology: deepAMP peptide language model (deepAMP-general, deepAMP-AOM, deepAMP-POM and deepAMP-predict)
organization: Hunan University; Cleveland Clinic; National Cancer Institute; Tel Aviv University

evidence.tested: Researchers at Hunan University and collaborators used the peptide language model deepAMP to optimize antimicrobial peptides and experimentally tested 29 candidates.
evidence.unknown: This is a separate discovery study from the AMPSphere microbiome-mining paper already in the tracker: deepAMP optimizes peptide sequences, whereas AMPSphere mined microbiomes. Testing involved 29 candidates and one female mouse wound model; this is preclinical evidence, not clinical efficacy. The article itself calls for more animal-model validation.
evidence.ai_role: The generative and ranking models optimized candidate peptide sequences for antimicrobial potency and membrane-disrupting activity. Researchers synthesized and tested selected sequences in vitro and in a mouse wound infection experiment.

title: AlphaFold-assisted structural clustering discovers new deaminase functions and compact base-editing enzymes
summary: The team used AlphaFold2 structure predictions to cluster the deaminase family and found that most proteins in a DddA-like clade were not double-stranded DNA deaminases. The work characterized smaller single-strand-specific deaminases, developed a compact cytidine deaminase suitable for packaging a base editor into one AAV, and demonstrated robust editing by a clade member in soybean.
ai_technology: AlphaFold2-assisted structure-based protein-family clustering
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Qi Biodesign; BGI-Qingdao; Aarhus University

evidence.tested: The team used AlphaFold2 structure predictions to cluster the deaminase family and found that most proteins in a DddA-like clade were not double-stranded DNA deaminases.
evidence.unknown: This paper is an AI-assisted protein-discovery and engineering study; experimental base editing demonstrates the utility of selected deaminases, while therapeutic application remains prospective. The study was followed by a 2024 correction/erratum; the record references the original research article, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2023.05.041, not the erratum.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold2 predicted protein structures that enabled structure-similarity clustering of a full deaminase family. The clustering guided discovery of functional diversity and selection of enzymes, which the researchers characterized experimentally and used in cell, animal and plant base-editing tests.

title: CataPro-assisted enzyme mining identifies a high-activity Sphingobium enzyme for vanillin production
summary: CataPro, a deep-learning model using pretrained protein-language representations and molecular fingerprints to predict enzyme kinetics, was combined with sequence and structure-based filtering to screen candidate enzymes for converting 4-vinylguaiacol to vanillin. The team experimentally identified Sphingobium sp. CSO (SsCSO), whose measured activity was 19.53 times that of the initial enzyme CSO2, and then used CataPro-guided engineering to increase SsCSO activity a further 3.34-fold.
ai_technology: CataPro
organization: Shandong University; Shanghai Zelixir Biotech; Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: The team experimentally identified Sphingobium sp.
evidence.unknown: The reported 19.53× and 3.34× figures are relative activities for the tested 4-vinylguaiacol oxidation assay; they do not establish industrial-scale yield or process performance. Model predictions were used alongside conventional sequence/structure methods, not as the sole discovery method.
evidence.ai_role: CataPro predicted kinetic parameters to prioritize candidate carotenoid-cleavage-oxygenase family enzymes and rank variants; researchers combined its predictions with BLAST, structural similarity and laboratory enzyme assays. It materially narrowed the enzyme search and guided mutations, while experiments established measured activity.

title: AI-photoswitchable CRISPRi screening identifies new regulators of TFEB localization during starvation
summary: An image-classification-guided pooled CRISPRi screen mapped factors that affect TFEB movement from nucleus to cytosol during prolonged starvation. The screen identified multiple candidate genes, and follow-up assays independently validated 21 of 64 neural-network-called hits; experiments on CREB5 further linked it to TFEB retention and starvation-associated autophagy/lysosomal protein expression.
ai_technology: AI-photoswitchable screening (AI-PS), using SVM classifiers and a convolutional neural network
organization: Janelia Research Campus, Howard Hughes Medical Institute; National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, NIH

evidence.tested: The screen identified multiple candidate genes, and follow-up assays independently validated 21 of 64 neural-network-called hits; experiments on CREB5 further linked it to TFEB retention and starvation-associated autophagy/lysosomal protein expression.
evidence.unknown: Only 21 of 64 neural-network-called TFEB hits were independently validated in secondary assays (about 32%); candidate effectors should not be treated as all confirmed. Results use cultured U2OS cells and prolonged starvation, and do not establish a physiological role in an organism. CREB5 received targeted follow-up but the overall screen has a modest validation rate.
evidence.ai_role: SVM and CNN models classified single-cell images by subcellular protein localization; the system photoactivated cells with the target phenotype for FACS isolation and gRNA sequencing in pooled CRISPRi screening. AI enabled the genome-scale genotype-to-subcellular-phenotype screen.

title: Machine-learning-guided mining identifies 91 previously unknown PET hydrolases, including acid-active enzymes
summary: Researchers iteratively combined sequence mining, machine-learning activity/property predictors and high-throughput assays to screen natural enzyme homologs. They experimentally identified 91 previously unknown PET hydrolases among the 212 candidates assayed; 35 had activity on crystalline PET at pH 4.5, and four matched or exceeded a benchmark enzyme under that screening condition.
ai_technology: Three-round iterative machine-learning pipeline (including VAE/rank model, supervised activity predictors, ESM embeddings and property predictors)
organization: National Renewable Energy Laboratory; BOTTLE Consortium; Agile BioFoundry; SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory; Harvard Medical School

evidence.tested: Researchers iteratively combined sequence mining, machine-learning activity/property predictors and high-throughput assays to screen natural enzyme homologs.
evidence.unknown: The article defines PET hydrolase by demonstrated PET-depolymerizing activity and notes that activity may be promiscuous relative to the enzyme’s native role. Assays are small-scale and 48 hours; the authors say further enzyme engineering is needed for meaningful bioreactor studies. This is distinct from the catalogued AI-engineered FAST-PETase: it discovers natural homologs and diverse acid/temperature activity profiles rather than optimizing one known PETase scaffold.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning activity, thermal-stability and acid-tolerance predictions prioritized natural homologs across successive mining rounds; new assay results updated later predictors. Researchers expressed/purified over 200 candidates and measured PET hydrolysis to verify activity.

title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies mammalian enzymes catalyzing the second step of carnitine biosynthesis
summary: The OSMES workflow screened AlphaFold-modeled vitamin-B6-dependent enzymes by docking the substrate into active sites and ranking catalytically favorable conformations. It identified human SHMT1/2 as enzymes with hydroxytrimethyllysine-aldolase activity, validated in vitro; mouse Tha1 showed much higher catalytic efficiency, supporting a species difference in the pathway. The authors infer that humans may have lost a dedicated gene, with SHMT activity partly compensating.
ai_technology: OSMES (One Substrate–Many Enzymes Screening), automated structure-based docking/ranking workflow using AlphaFold models
organization: University of Parma; University of Padua; Sapienza University of Rome; CNR Institute of Molecular Biology and Pathology

evidence.tested: It identified human SHMT1/2 as enzymes with hydroxytrimethyllysine-aldolase activity, validated in vitro; mouse Tha1 showed much higher catalytic efficiency, supporting a species difference in the pathway.
evidence.unknown: Enzyme activity was validated in vitro. The claim about loss of a dedicated human gene is an evolutionary inference, not a direct gene-knockout demonstration; the authors note unresolved pathway questions.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked candidate enzymes for a specified metabolic reaction using docked substrate conformations and catalytically favorable active-site geometry; guided biochemical testing that verified SHMT1/2 activity.

title: Machine learning and peptide-array experiments reveal new substrates for protein-modifying enzymes
summary: A hybrid workflow coupled machine-learning models with enzyme-treated peptide arrays to predict previously unexplored protein post-translational-modification sites. Experimental validation confirmed 37–43% of proposed sites across SET8 and SIRT1–7; mass spectrometry confirmed dynamic methylation for several SET8 substrates and deacetylation at 64 unique SIRT2 sites. The work also found altered SET8 substrate networks associated with breast-cancer missense mutations.
ai_technology: Enzyme-specific ML-hybrid substrate prediction models trained from high-throughput peptide-array assays
organization: Carleton University; Ben-Gurion University of the Negev

evidence.tested: Experimental validation confirmed 37–43% of proposed sites across SET8 and SIRT1–7; mass spectrometry confirmed dynamic methylation for several SET8 substrates and deacetylation at 64 unique SIRT2 sites.
evidence.unknown: Reported validation rate is 37–43% of proposed sites, so predictions are not uniformly confirmed. Results concern in-vitro enzyme assays and selected sites; disease relevance of the altered SET8 network is not established as a clinical mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Learned enzyme-specific substrate preferences from experimental array measurements and prioritized novel PTM sites for experimental follow-up; this enabled the reported new SET8/SIRT substrate assignments.

title: Machine learning-guided cell-free engineering creates specialized amide synthetases for pharmaceutical molecules
summary: A cell-free design-build-test-learn platform generated sequence-function data from 1,217 McbA variants across 10,953 reactions. Ridge-regression ML guided enzyme variants that produced nine small-molecule pharmaceuticals with activity 1.6- to 42-fold above the parent; initial substrate-promiscuity assays found McbA could make 11 pharmaceutical compounds plus hybrid molecules. This is experimental enzyme engineering, not evidence of therapeutic efficacy of the products.
ai_technology: Augmented ridge-regression ML models within a cell-free sequence-function mapping and enzyme-engineering workflow
organization: Northwestern University; Stanford University

evidence.tested: A cell-free design-build-test-learn platform generated sequence-function data from 1,217 McbA variants across 10,953 reactions.
evidence.unknown: The platform optimizes in-vitro enzyme production of molecules and does not establish drug efficacy, manufacturing readiness, or broad transferability beyond tested reactions. The nine-product gains are relative to the parent enzyme under the reported assay conditions.
evidence.ai_role: Used measured variant fitness data to predict and select higher-activity McbA variants for distinct amide-forming reactions; selected variants were synthesized and assayed.

title: DeepMet anticipates and helps identify dozens of previously unrecognized mammalian metabolites
summary: DeepMet, an LSTM chemical language model trained on known human metabolites, generated a ranked space of metabolite-like structures and was integrated with mass spectrometry data. Researchers report identifying several dozen previously unrecognized mammalian metabolites across standards, human biofluids, mouse tissues and repository data. Some standard-supported assignments still have isomer ambiguity; the study also found known metabolites missing or misannotated in HMDB.
ai_technology: DeepMet chemical language model (three-layer LSTM over SMILES), integrated with MS/MS-spectrum prediction and meta-learning
organization: Princeton University; University of Alberta; University of British Columbia; University of Toronto; Baylor College of Medicine; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Researchers report identifying several dozen previously unrecognized mammalian metabolites across standards, human biofluids, mouse tissues and repository data.
evidence.unknown: A subset of assigned structures retain regioisomer/stereoisomer ambiguity; human oversight helped prioritize structures for synthesis. The model explores chemical space similar to its training set and may miss divergent biosynthetic chemistry. The paper distinguishes novel metabolites from known compounds missing in HMDB.
evidence.ai_role: Learned metabolite-like chemical structures and prioritized structures likely to exist; combined with accurate mass/MS/MS and reference standards to support identification of previously unrecognized metabolites.

title: Machine-learning-guided screening validates 14 previously unreported drug–GPCR interactions
summary: Chemical Space Neural Networks used network-neighborhood labels to predict drug–target interactions and were evaluated with a yeast biosensor screen of 3,773 compound–GPCR pairs (539 compounds and seven human GPCRs). The authors report 14 experimentally significant interactions with no prior literature/database evidence in the relevant chemical neighborhoods, tentatively linking some to adverse effects. This is an in-vitro receptor-screen discovery, not clinical proof of drug side effects.
ai_technology: Chemical Space Neural Networks (CSNN), neighborhood-to-prediction model using network homophily and graph neural networks with labels as features
organization: Technical University of Denmark; Biomia ApS; Joint BioEnergy Institute; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; University of California, Berkeley

evidence.tested: The authors report 14 experimentally significant interactions with no prior literature/database evidence in the relevant chemical neighborhoods, tentatively linking some to adverse effects.
evidence.unknown: Yeast assay is a heterologous in-vitro system and does not establish physiological effects in humans. The article describes the 14 interactions as potentially linked to adverse effects, not confirmed clinical adverse events. Some assay limitations and false positives are discussed; precision for predicted positives is limited.
evidence.ai_role: Used chemical-neighborhood labels to prioritize/annotate compound–GPCR interactions; model outputs were compared with high-throughput yeast biosensor measurements to identify previously unreported hits.

title: Machine learning prioritizes microbiome metabolites that stimulate interleukin-8 secretion
summary: Researchers trained ML models on public drug-development data to prioritize biological properties of microbiome metabolites, then tested predictions prospectively. In vitro experiments identified previously unreported IL-8 secretion stimulation by spermine and spermidine, metabolites previously regarded as anti-inflammatory. The paper reports average accuracy of 92.86% in prospective experiments, while cautioning that sample sizes were small.
ai_technology: Machine-learning property prediction models implemented in KNIME and trained on public drug-development data
organization: Duke University; Duke Microbiome Center

evidence.tested: Researchers trained ML models on public drug-development data to prioritize biological properties of microbiome metabolites, then tested predictions prospectively. The selected metabolites were tested in new in-house assays; this is direct experimental testing within the discovery study.
evidence.unknown: The unexpected activity is demonstrated in vitro and does not establish in-vivo host effects. The article explicitly cautions that prospective validation sample sizes were small; reported model metrics vary by task.
evidence.ai_role: Predicted and triaged microbiome metabolites for target assays, including IL-8 activation; prospective laboratory assays then established the unexpected cytokine-stimulatory activity of spermine and spermidine.

title: KCML links olfactory-receptor perturbations to multicellular organization and colorectal-cancer signaling
summary: Knowledge- and Context-driven Machine Learning (KCML) analyzed perturbation phenotypes across molecular, cellular and population scales. In colorectal-cancer cells, it associated depletion of olfactory receptors and TGFβ/WNT pathway genes with abnormal multicellular organization. The authors integrated the predictions with patient data and found olfactory-receptor expression correlated with WNT/TGFβ signatures and worse outcomes in higher-grade tumors.
ai_technology: KCML, weakly supervised machine-learning framework using support-vector-machine classifiers trained on gene-ontology annotations and high-throughput perturbation phenotypes
organization: University of Oxford; University of Zurich

evidence.tested: Knowledge- and Context-driven Machine Learning (KCML) analyzed perturbation phenotypes across molecular, cellular and population scales.
evidence.unknown: Patient data validate expression associations and outcome stratification, not a causal olfactory-receptor mechanism in tumors. The authors describe KCML as hypothesis-generating; predictions can be indirect through interacting genes. This is a distinct paper/result from later AI cancer models.
evidence.ai_role: Mapped gene-perturbation morphology to context-specific gene functions and nominated olfactory-receptor links to multicellular organization; patient-expression analyses provided an independent association check.

title: MitoReID identifies epicatechin as a cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor
summary: A deep-learning system called MitoReID classified drug mechanisms from time-resolved mitochondrial morphology and membrane-potential images. Among its natural-compound predictions, it nominated epicatechin as a COX-2 inhibitor; the authors report in-vitro follow-up including COX-2 activity, cellular thermal-shift and surface-plasmon-resonance assays. This is a target-mechanism finding, not evidence of clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: MitoReID, deep-learning re-identification model using an Inflated 3D ResNet backbone on temporal mitochondrial images
organization: Zhejiang University; Zhejiang Lab; Zhejiang Chinese Medical University; Harvard University; Karolinska Institute; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Among its natural-compound predictions, it nominated epicatechin as a COX-2 inhibitor; the authors report in-vitro follow-up including COX-2 activity, cellular thermal-shift and surface-plasmon-resonance assays.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is biochemical/in-vitro and does not establish therapeutic efficacy or safety. MitoReID's six unseen-drug mechanism predictions are a separate task; the epicatechin COX-2 result is the specific new mechanistic finding recorded here. Full publisher page was cookie-blocked, but the primary PubMed record and publisher-indexed article text/extended-data caption were read.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked mechanisms of action for compounds by matching learned time-dependent mitochondrial phenotypes against reference drugs; the model nominated COX-2 inhibition for epicatechin, which was tested in vitro.

title: BEAUT uncovers new gut-microbial bile-acid enzymes and the novel bile acid 3-acetoDCA
summary: The BEAUT workflow combines ESM-2 protein-language-model embeddings with a neural classifier and active-site-pocket-similarity data augmentation to search gut microbial proteins for bile-acid enzymes. The authors predicted over 600,000 candidate enzymes and experimentally tested selected predictions; assays identified new bile-acid activities including MABH and ADS. ADS produces 3-acetoDCA, a previously undescribed bile-acid carbon skeleton, reported in human feces and shown to alter microbial composition and promote Lactobacillus-associated effects in experimental studies.
ai_technology: BEAUT, ESM-2 protein-language-model embeddings plus dense neural-network classifier, augmented using active-site-pocket similarity
organization: Peking University; Peking University Third Hospital; Tsinghua–Peking University Joint Center for Life Sciences; Nanchang University

evidence.tested: The authors predicted over 600,000 candidate enzymes and experimentally tested selected predictions; assays identified new bile-acid activities including MABH and ADS.
evidence.unknown: The 600,000 figure is a prediction set, not experimentally characterized enzymes; authors tested selected subsets. Physiological claims are based on study assays and animal/microbial experiments, not demonstrated human clinical effects. The journal full text was inaccessible in this reader; the Peking University research team's detailed release summarizes its Cell paper, methods and experiments.
evidence.ai_role: Screened microbial protein sequences for likely bile-acid-metabolizing function and prioritized candidate enzymes; experimental characterization of selected AI predictions identified enzyme activities and the ADS/3-acetoDCA pathway.

title: Horizyn-1 experimentally identifies enzymes for orphan and nonnatural reactions
summary: Researchers used the reaction–protein dual-encoder model Horizyn-1 to prioritize enzyme candidates, then experimentally validated activity in orphan-reaction deorphaning, enzyme-promiscuity tests and nonnatural transformations. For an uncharacterized Thermus aquaticus protein, LC–MS confirmed dCMP kinase activity; a selected transaminase produced noncanonical amino acids from lysine-derived donors, with isotope tracing supporting predominant alpha-amine transfer.
ai_technology: Horizyn-1
organization: Dayhoff Labs; and collaborating researchers

evidence.tested: Researchers used the reaction–protein dual-encoder model Horizyn-1 to prioritize enzyme candidates, then experimentally validated activity in orphan-reaction deorphaning, enzyme-promiscuity tests and nonnatural transformations.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is from specific in-vitro assays and tested sequences/reactions; model retrieval performance and the tested enzyme activities do not establish broad generalization. The paper reports that the predicted CMP kinase activity for one protein was not confirmed, while dCMP activity was.
evidence.ai_role: A contrastive model jointly embedded reaction fingerprints and ProtT5 protein-sequence representations, ranked candidate enzyme–reaction pairs, and informed experimental selection. The authors assayed predictions with biochemical assays, LC–MS and isotope tracing; some fine-tuning results are predictive-performance findings rather than biological discoveries.

title: CellPaint-POSH screening links AURKAIP1 knockout with reduced mitochondrial abundance and mTORC1 signaling
summary: Self-supervised CP-DINO analysis of pooled Cell Painting CRISPR profiles nominated AURKAIP1 among genes with mitochondrial and mTORC1-related phenotypes. Follow-up AURKAIP1 knockout in A549 cells reduced the mitochondrial marker TOMM20 and pS6, an mTORC1 activity readout, relative to control. The authors propose that mitochondrial translation/metabolism may influence mTORC1, while the causal pathway remains unresolved.
ai_technology: CellPaint-POSH with CP-DINO-1640 self-supervised embeddings and a vision transformer
organization: Broad Institute; and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Self-supervised CP-DINO analysis of pooled Cell Painting CRISPR profiles nominated AURKAIP1 among genes with mitochondrial and mTORC1-related phenotypes.
evidence.unknown: The result is from an A549 cell-line knockout study and supports an association between AURKAIP1 loss, reduced mitochondrial abundance and reduced pS6; it does not establish the molecular mechanism or direct causal pathway between mitochondrial function and mTORC1. The arrayed follow-up used two technical replicate wells per knockout, was not randomized or blinded, and is not an independent replication. The paper identifies HSD17B10 as a previously reported mTORC1 regulator; this record focuses on AURKAIP1.
evidence.ai_role: CP-DINO self-supervised embeddings and morphological similarity analysis of pooled CRISPR knockout profiles identified AURKAIP1 in a cluster with mitochondrial and pS6 phenotypes, prioritizing it for follow-up. The authors then used arrayed RNP knockout and TOMM20/pS6 staining; those assays showed reduced mitochondrial abundance and pS6 after AURKAIP1 knockout. The model enabled candidate prioritization, while the perturbation and marker measurements supplied the specific experimental evidence.

title: AlphaFold-Multimer-guided experiments corroborate six novel human protein interfaces
summary: Researchers developed a fragmentation strategy for AlphaFold-Multimer and applied it to 62 human protein interactions associated with neurological disorders. Eighteen predicted structures were judged correct or likely correct, and experiments corroborated six previously unreported interfaces: FBXO23–STX1B, STX1B–VAMP2, ESRRG–PSMC5, PEX3–PEX19, PEX3–PEX16 and SNRPB–GIGYF1.
ai_technology: AlphaFold-Multimer with a protein-fragmentation strategy
organization: Institute of Molecular Biology Mainz; Hebrew University of Jerusalem and collaborators

evidence.tested: Eighteen predicted structures were judged correct or likely correct, and experiments corroborated six previously unreported interfaces: FBXO23–STX1B, STX1B–VAMP2, ESRRG–PSMC5, PEX3–PEX19, PEX3–PEX16 and SNRPB–GIGYF1.
evidence.unknown: The article reports 18 correct or likely correct models among 62 interactions and experimental support for six interfaces; these are not a comprehensive interactome map. AlphaFold-Multimer showed limited specificity and was sensitive to input-fragment length, as the source explicitly notes.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold-Multimer predicted domain–motif interface structures; researchers tested predictions and used the model-informed fragmentation strategy to prioritize interaction interfaces. Wet-lab assays corroborated six novel contacts, while the tool had limited specificity and performance declined with longer/full-length input sequences.

title: Machine learning prioritizes compounds active against heterogeneous glioblastoma stem-cell models
summary: Researchers trained cell-survival predictors on image-based screening data from six patient-derived glioblastoma stem-cell lines and screened more than 12,000 compounds. Experimental follow-up identified three compounds with activity across the GBM phenotype; HSP90 inhibitor XL-888 eliminated all six tested lines at nanomolar IC50 values, with analyses consistent with HSP90 inhibition and downstream client-protein disruption.
ai_technology: Machine-learning cell-survival predictors trained on high-throughput phenotypic screening
organization: University of Edinburgh; and Cancer Research UK Scotland Centre

evidence.tested: Experimental follow-up identified three compounds with activity across the GBM phenotype; HSP90 inhibitor XL-888 eliminated all six tested lines at nanomolar IC50 values, with analyses consistent with HSP90 inhibition and downstream client-protein disruption.
evidence.unknown: This is an in-vitro lead-discovery study across six patient-derived cell lines, not clinical efficacy. XL-888 is an existing HSP90 inhibitor and its proposed development as a GBM lead needs medicinal-chemistry optimization, including improved blood–brain-barrier penetration; no patient outcomes are reported.
evidence.ai_role: ML models trained on in-house imaging/compound-response data predicted cell survival and prioritized compounds from a >12,000-compound screen; experimental assays across patient-derived GBM stem-cell models validated three leads and tested mechanisms. Researchers performed the wet-lab work and mechanism analyses.

title: XunZi prioritizes CHK2 as a Parkinson’s disease mechanism and therapeutic target
summary: The XunZi AI-biologist integrated literature reasoning with multimodal molecular data and nominated CHK2 and IRAK4 kinase activation in Parkinson’s disease models. Follow-up experiments found that pharmacological or genetic Chk2 inhibition rescued dopaminergic-neuron loss and motor deficits in PD mouse models, supporting CHK2 as a disease-associated mediator in the tested systems.
ai_technology: XunZi AI biologist
organization: Huazhong University of Science and Technology; and Sichuan University

evidence.tested: Follow-up experiments found that pharmacological or genetic Chk2 inhibition rescued dopaminergic-neuron loss and motor deficits in PD mouse models, supporting CHK2 as a disease-associated mediator in the tested systems.
evidence.unknown: The neuroprotective evidence is from experimental Parkinson’s disease models and mice, not human patients or clinical efficacy. XunZi also nominated IRAK4, but the abstract specifically reports Chk2 inhibition rescue; do not imply equivalent causal validation for every AI-nominated target. The Nature article’s complete indexed text was read; direct open may be blocked by a cookie redirect.
evidence.ai_role: XunZi integrated logical reasoning with multimodal data fusion across biomedical literature and molecular datasets to generate and rank de novo disease-target hypotheses. Researchers then tested the CHK2 hypothesis with cellular and mouse experiments, including pharmacological/genetic inhibition; the AI nominated the target, while experiments established the reported effects.

title: Machine-learning network analysis identifies a conserved cell-mechanics gene module
summary: Researchers combined transcriptomic profiles with single-cell mechanical measurements from mouse and human systems and used machine-learning-based discriminative network analysis to infer a conserved five-gene module associated with cell mechanical properties. In perturbation experiments, changing CAV1 expression by silencing or overexpression altered measured cell stiffness, providing experimental support for a selected marker’s role.
ai_technology: PC-corr machine-learning-based discriminative network analysis
organization: Technische Universität Dresden; Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Researchers combined transcriptomic profiles with single-cell mechanical measurements from mouse and human systems and used machine-learning-based discriminative network analysis to infer a conserved five-gene module associated with cell mechanical properties.
evidence.unknown: Only CAV1 was experimentally tested as a selected target in the reported perturbation experiments; the other genes are candidate regulators. Experiments show changes in measured stiffness in specific cell models, not broad physiological or clinical effects. Paper’s eLife assessment notes further validation, especially of genes with previously unknown roles, would strengthen the network.
evidence.ai_role: PC-corr analyzed transcriptomic data linked to measured mechanical phenotypes to identify a conserved five-gene signature and prioritize candidate regulators; selected genes were computationally assessed across six validation datasets, and CAV1 was experimentally perturbed to test effects on cell mechanics.

title: Machine learning screening reveals ABBV-744 as a modulator of P2Y purinergic receptors
summary: Researchers used consensus machine-learning classifiers trained on known P2Y6 agonists to select compounds for pharmacological testing. The anticancer drug ABBV-744 showed non-surmountable inhibition of UDP-induced P2Y6 receptor activation and enhanced P2Y1 receptor activation in cellular assays, revealing previously unreported purinergic-receptor activity for this molecule.
ai_technology: Consensus of deep learning, AdaBoost, naive Bayes, k-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, random forest, SVM and XGBoost classifiers
organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases; and Collaborations Pharmaceuticals

evidence.tested: Researchers used consensus machine-learning classifiers trained on known P2Y6 agonists to select compounds for pharmacological testing.
evidence.unknown: The paper found no novel P2Y6 agonists, which was the initial aim. ABBV-744 inhibited P2Y6 activation at relatively high micromolar concentration (reported IC50 about 75.7 µM); its precise inhibitory mechanism was not determined and requires further assays. P2Y1 enhancement and weak P2Y14 binding effects are assay-specific observations, not clinical pharmacology or therapeutic benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on curated P2Y6 agonist activity data prioritized molecules from compound libraries for experimental screening. Functional calcium-transient assays in receptor-expressing cells and fluorescent binding assays were used to test predictions; ABBV-744 was the principal confirmed hit with unanticipated activity across P2Y receptor subtypes.

title: Knowledge-graph AI prioritizes TPP1 as a Parkinson’s disease target linked to α-synuclein homeostasis
summary: Standigm ASK’s knowledge-graph model ranked Parkinson’s disease target associations; subgraph enrichment and expression analyses narrowed 2,527 predicted targets to five candidates, including TPP1. In a human cell-based α-synuclein seeding model, TPP1 knockdown increased aggregate accumulation and insoluble α-synuclein, experimentally supporting a TPP1–α-synuclein relationship and a possible protective role.
ai_technology: Standigm ASK knowledge-graph path-based deep-learning model with subgraph-level over-representation re-ranking
organization: Standigm; and Ajou University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: In a human cell-based α-synuclein seeding model, TPP1 knockdown increased aggregate accumulation and insoluble α-synuclein, experimentally supporting a TPP1–α-synuclein relationship and a possible protective role.
evidence.unknown: The functional experiment is a human neuroblastoma cell model exposed to α-synuclein preformed fibrils, not a clinical or in-vivo therapeutic demonstration. Knockdown increasing aggregation supports a protective association; direct enzymatic cleavage of α-synuclein is proposed from structural modeling, not established by the reported work. TPP1 is a candidate therapeutic target, not a validated treatment.
evidence.ai_role: The model integrated heterogeneous biomedical databases, encoded relational paths using a convolutional network and attention aggregation, and produced disease-target scores. Researchers applied enrichment and transcriptomic filters to prioritize TPP1, then validated TPP1’s relationship to α-synuclein aggregation via siRNA knockdown and cellular assays; AlphaFold-Multimer modeling suggested, but did not prove, direct proteolysis.

title: Machine-learning-guided genome mining links an Amycolatopsis BGC to dipyrimicins
summary: A machine-learning model that predicted antibacterial activity from biosynthetic-gene-cluster sequences prioritized Amycolatopsis azurea DSM 43854. Bioactivity-guided fractionation recovered dipyrimicins A and B from this strain, and genome analysis linked them to a previously uncharacterized dip BGC with a 76% predicted antibacterial probability; broth-microdilution assays confirmed activity against several test strains.
ai_technology: Machine-learning predictor of antibacterial activity from biosynthetic gene clusters
organization: Vanderbilt University

evidence.tested: Bioactivity-guided fractionation recovered dipyrimicins A and B from this strain, and genome analysis linked them to a previously uncharacterized dip BGC with a 76% predicted antibacterial probability; broth-microdilution assays confirmed activity against several test strains.
evidence.unknown: Dipyrimicins themselves had been reported previously from a related Amycolatopsis strain; the paper’s new result is their isolation from A. azurea DSM 43854 and first linkage to its BGC, not discovery of the molecules as novel compounds. Reported antibacterial potency was moderate and tested against a few strains (for dipyrimicin A, MICs included 32 µg/mL for B. spizizenii and 64 µg/mL for S. aureus; >128 µg/mL for P. aeruginosa). Proposed functions of some tailoring genes remain speculative.
evidence.ai_role: The model ranked biosynthetic clusters and prioritized A. azurea DSM 43854 for experimental work. Researchers performed bioactivity-guided fractionation, isolated the compounds, linked them to the previously uncharacterized dip BGC, and tested antibacterial activity. The dip BGC was absent from the model’s training set, providing an out-of-training-set test of the prioritization approach.

title: Machine-learning screening finds previously unreported antibacterial compounds active against Burkholderia and ESKAPE pathogens
summary: A directed-message-passing neural network trained on a 29,537-compound Burkholderia cenocepacia screen prioritized compounds from a natural-product library. Laboratory testing found five previously uncharacterized compounds that inhibited B. cenocepacia; 22 of 43 tested prioritized compounds inhibited at least one of five ESKAPE pathogens.
ai_technology: Directed-message-passing neural network (D-MPNN) implemented with Chemprop
organization: University of Manitoba

evidence.tested: Laboratory testing found five previously uncharacterized compounds that inhibited B. cenocepacia; 22 of 43 tested prioritized compounds inhibited at least one of five ESKAPE pathogens.
evidence.unknown: The compounds were active in vitro; no clinical effect, safety or therapeutic readiness is established. Several confirmed compounds were known antimicrobials, while five natural-product hits were described as previously uncharacterized. An inferred RpoB mechanism for STL558147 was suggested by CRISPRi sensitivity rather than directly demonstrated binding.
evidence.ai_role: The D-MPNN ranked FDA-approved and natural-product library molecules for predicted antibacterial activity; researchers tested high-ranked compounds in bacterial growth assays and confirmed activity. It was a screening-prioritization tool, not evidence of clinical efficacy.

title: MetGenX annotates two previously uncharacterized metabolites in mouse liver
summary: MetGenX, a structure-informed neural-network workflow for generating structures from tandem mass spectra, was applied to untargeted mouse-liver metabolomics and reported two previously uncharacterized metabolites, adenosyl-cysteine and adenosine 5′-diphosphate 5′-inosine (Ap2I). The paper reports validation against chemical standards using retention time and MS2 spectral matches.
ai_technology: MetGenX structure-informed encoder-decoder neural network with LightGBM reranking
organization: Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and collaborators

evidence.tested: MetGenX, a structure-informed neural-network workflow for generating structures from tandem mass spectra, was applied to untargeted mouse-liver metabolomics and reported two previously uncharacterized metabolites, adenosyl-cysteine and adenosine 5′-diphosphate 5′-inosine (Ap2I).
evidence.unknown: The original Nature full-text route was inaccessible in this session; the primary-source PubMed article page provides the paper abstract and figure captions describing standard-based retention-time/MS2 matches for the two structures. The finding is metabolite annotation in mouse tissue, not evidence of human biological function. Independent replication was not checked.
evidence.ai_role: The model generated and reranked candidate molecular structures from MS2 spectra; researchers applied a multi-step workflow to mouse-liver samples and compared the two reported metabolite candidates with standards. AI proposed annotations, while standard-based chromatographic and spectral matching supported the assignments.

title: Machine learning reveals a nitrogen-assimilation strategy in Bacteroides
summary: A microbiome metabolomics study used random-forest models to associate bacterial metabolite profiles with taxonomy and found a previously undescribed nitrogen-assimilation pattern in Bacteroides/Bacteroidetes. Follow-up growth experiments tested 60 Bacteroidetes strains with asparagine or glutamine as the sole nitrogen source and supported the predicted phenotype; the study also reports a distinct reduced-sulfur utilization result in B. thetaiotaomicron.
ai_technology: Random-forest models over metabolomics profiles
organization: Stanford University; and Chan Zuckerberg Biohub collaborators

evidence.tested: Follow-up growth experiments tested 60 Bacteroidetes strains with asparagine or glutamine as the sole nitrogen source and supported the predicted phenotype; the study also reports a distinct reduced-sulfur utilization result in B. thetaiotaomicron.
evidence.unknown: The study's abstract reports machine-learning discovery of a new metabolism and the figure captions document follow-up culture tests; the article's full text is paywalled in this session, so the exact mechanistic pathway is not asserted. Mouse and culture evidence do not establish a human health effect.
evidence.ai_role: The models identified metabolite features that distinguished taxa and highlighted a previously undescribed Bacteroides metabolic phenotype; researchers then tested bacterial growth under defined nitrogen sources. Comparative-genomics pathways remained candidate explanations rather than proven pathways.

title: LAMBDAZERO generates an experimentally active soluble epoxide hydrolase inhibitor scaffold
summary: The LAMBDAZERO generative active-learning workflow searched for synthesizable soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH/EPHX2) inhibitors and produced a quinazoline scaffold absent from the authors' comparison set of known sEH inhibitors. A synthesized analog, UM0152893, inhibited sEH in vitro with sub-micromolar potency.
ai_technology: LAMBDAZERO generative active learning with deep reinforcement learning and docking
organization: Mila – Quebec AI Institute; Université de Montréal; University of Toronto; collaborators

evidence.tested: The LAMBDAZERO generative active-learning workflow searched for synthesizable soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH/EPHX2) inhibitors and produced a quinazoline scaffold absent from the authors' comparison set of known sEH inhibitors.
evidence.unknown: This is a workshop paper/preprint rather than a clinical study. The reported lead is a biochemical inhibitor of purified sEH; no cellular, animal, safety or therapeutic outcome is established. The authors report 24/35 synthesized analogs active in vitro with potency spanning roughly 90 μM to 0.4 μM; one best lead is sub-micromolar.
evidence.ai_role: The generative model searched molecular space using docking, synthesizability and drug-likeness constraints and proposed the scaffold; researchers synthesized analogs and measured enzyme inhibition in biochemical assays.

title: Cross-species machine learning identifies transcription factors that negatively regulate plant nitrogen-use efficiency
summary: Evolutionarily informed XGBoost and GENIE3 analyses of conserved nitrogen-response expression patterns prioritized transcription factors associated with nitrogen-use efficiency in Arabidopsis and maize. Loss-of-function tests found higher NUE in Arabidopsis myb33 and tcp2 mutants under both low- and high-nitrogen conditions, and in six other tested TF mutants specifically under low nitrogen; a maize nfya3 mutant also showed higher nitrogen-use efficiency under sufficient nitrogen in field tests.
ai_technology: Evolutionarily informed XGBoost models and GENIE3 random-forest gene-regulatory-network inference
organization: New York University; Purdue University and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

evidence.tested: Loss-of-function tests found higher NUE in Arabidopsis myb33 and tcp2 mutants under both low- and high-nitrogen conditions, and in six other tested TF mutants specifically under low nitrogen; a maize nfya3 mutant also showed higher nitrogen-use efficiency under sufficient nitrogen in field tests.
evidence.unknown: The machine-learning prediction scores are not themselves causal evidence; this paper adds functional evidence from specific mutants. Some tested maize candidate roles were assessed through Arabidopsis homologs, and the maize NFYA3 phenotype described here was under sufficient-N field conditions, not a general yield benefit across conditions.
evidence.ai_role: The models ranked conserved nitrogen-responsive genes and transcription factors for contribution or network connectivity to NUE; researchers selected the candidates and tested loss-of-function mutants in Arabidopsis and maize, including field-grown maize.

title: Active learning repurposes BMS-262084 as a potent TMPRSS2 inhibitor that blocks coronavirus entry
summary: A molecular-dynamics and active-learning workflow prioritized the existing compound BMS-262084 as a nanomolar inhibitor of human TMPRSS2 (IC50 1.82 nM). Cell assays reported inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 variants and other coronavirus entry into Calu-3 lung cells.
ai_technology: Molecular-dynamics-informed active learning with a target-specific scoring function
organization: Freie Universität Berlin; Microsoft Research AI for Science, NIH NCATS, German Primate Center and collaborators

evidence.tested: Cell assays reported inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 variants and other coronavirus entry into Calu-3 lung cells.
evidence.unknown: BMS-262084 is a known small molecule repurposed here for TMPRSS2; the discovery claim is its target/antiviral activity under tested conditions. Evidence is biochemical and cell-based, not clinical efficacy or safety. Assay concentrations, viral variants and cell systems limit generalization.
evidence.ai_role: The active-learning workflow used receptor ensembles and target-specific features to iteratively prioritize compounds for testing; researchers measured purified-enzyme inhibition and viral-entry effects in cell assays. This is AI-assisted repurposing of an existing compound, not de novo molecule design.

title: Machine-learning selection uncovers plant enzymes for alkaloid pathway branches
summary: Support-vector-machine ranking selected poppy homologs whose experimental characterization identified aromatic acetaldehyde synthase activity in PsTyDC6 and phenylpyruvate-decarboxylase activity in PsPDC1. In vitro and engineered E. coli metabolomics detected pathway products including norcoclaurine and reticuline, demonstrating alternative routes from tyrosine into benzylisoquinoline alkaloids.
ai_technology: High-dimensional support vector machine (SVM) enzyme-sequence classifiers
organization: Kobe University; Tokyo Denki University, and collaborators

evidence.tested: Support-vector-machine ranking selected poppy homologs whose experimental characterization identified aromatic acetaldehyde synthase activity in PsTyDC6 and phenylpyruvate-decarboxylase activity in PsPDC1.
evidence.unknown: The study demonstrates enzyme activity and pathway products in vitro and engineered E. coli; it does not establish the exact physiological roles of these enzymes in living poppy plants. The paper describes several enzyme activities as potential and says natural pathway roles need further elucidation.
evidence.ai_role: SVM models ranked more than 100 homologous candidate sequences for specialized aromatic-acetaldehyde-synthase and phenylpyruvate-decarboxylase functions. The team selected high-scoring sequences for in-vitro enzyme assays and metabolomics of reconstructed E. coli pathways.

title: Machine-learning Treg framework identifies SMARCC1 as a previously unrecognized regulator
summary: A framework combining single-cell ATAC-seq, motif analysis, topic modeling, machine learning and genetic variation identified SMARCC1 as a previously unrecognized controller of regulatory T-cell chromatin programs. CRISPR-Cas9 deletion of Smarcc1 in Tregs produced the predicted loss of accessibility in topic-3 regulatory regions, supporting the computationally inferred connection.
ai_technology: Integrated machine-learning framework using topic modeling and high-density genetic variation over single-cell ATAC-seq profiles
organization: Harvard Medical School; and Imagine Institute, University of Paris

evidence.tested: A framework combining single-cell ATAC-seq, motif analysis, topic modeling, machine learning and genetic variation identified SMARCC1 as a previously unrecognized controller of regulatory T-cell chromatin programs.
evidence.unknown: CRISPR validation supported the predicted SMARCC1 effect for topic 3; topic 10 was not represented and the authors note possible redundancy with SMARCC2. The result concerns regulatory chromatin programs in Tregs, not clinical or therapeutic outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: The framework organized co-varying open chromatin regions into Treg regulatory modules, inferred transcription-factor effects on those programs, and nominated SMARCC1 as a regulator of topic-3/10 accessibility. The team tested the prediction by CRISPR-Cas9 editing Tregs and profiling chromatin accessibility.

title: Machine-learning microscopy isolates micronucleated cells and reveals chromosome-abnormality formation
summary: The MAGIC platform used an XGBoost image classifier to identify and photolabel micronucleated cells for single-cell genome sequencing. In near-diploid human cell models, the selected cells exposed new chromosome-abnormality formation patterns, including dicentric-associated breakage-fusion-bridge events; measured baseline abnormalities approximately doubled in TP53-deficient cells, and chromosome losses outnumbered gains.
ai_technology: MAGIC adaptive imaging platform with an XGBoost micronuclei classifier
organization: European Molecular Biology Laboratory; and German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), with collaborators

evidence.tested: In near-diploid human cell models, the selected cells exposed new chromosome-abnormality formation patterns, including dicentric-associated breakage-fusion-bridge events; measured baseline abnormalities approximately doubled in TP53-deficient cells, and chromosome losses outnumbered gains.
evidence.unknown: Findings come from near-diploid non-transformed cell lines and sequencing limited mainly to chromosome abnormalities larger than 200 kb in dividing cells. Micronucleated RPE-1 cells did not show significant CA enrichment, unlike MCF10A; spontaneous cell-line results do not establish cancer outcomes in patients.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning examined live confocal images, identified micronucleated cells and drove targeted photolabelling so selected cells could be sorted for downstream single-cell sequencing. The model enabled targeted sampling; it did not itself infer chromosome-abnormality mechanisms from sequence data.

title: Mechanistic machine learning links PI3K to Src-inhibitor effects in cardiac fibroblasts
summary: LogiMML, trained on high-content images of human cardiac fibroblasts, predicted that Src inhibition suppresses actin–myosin stress fibers through PI3K signaling. Follow-up PI3K inhibition reduced stress-fiber formation and procollagen I production in the fibroblasts, supporting the proposed pathway mechanism.
ai_technology: LogiMML, a logic-based mechanistic network coupled to ridge regression
organization: University of Virginia School of Medicine; and Brigham Young University

evidence.tested: LogiMML, trained on high-content images of human cardiac fibroblasts, predicted that Src inhibition suppresses actin–myosin stress fibers through PI3K signaling.
evidence.unknown: The validation is in vitro in primary human ventricular cardiac fibroblasts; it supports a pathway contribution to measured cell phenotypes, not therapeutic efficacy in an animal model or patients. The model's PI3K effect is described as partial.
evidence.ai_role: LogiMML fitted the relationship between high-content microscopy phenotypes and perturbations to an experimentally informed fibroblast signaling network, then predicted pathway mechanisms for pirfenidone and the Src inhibitor WH-4-023. Researchers tested the PI3K component of the Src-inhibitor prediction with PI3K inhibition in human cardiac fibroblasts.

title: Machine-learned multiscale simulations reveal lipid-dependent RAS organization at membranes
summary: The MuMMI machine-learning multiscale simulation ensemble found that local membrane lipid fingerprints correlate with wild-type KRAS clustering and orientation, with many simulated RAS–RAS interfaces appearing nonspecific. Complementary liposome and diffusion experiments supported lipid-dependent RAS adhesion and dynamics, motivating the authors' conclusion that lipids can mediate RAS multimer organization.
ai_technology: MuMMI (Multiscale Machine-learned Modeling Infrastructure)
organization: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory; Los Alamos National Laboratory, and the NCI RAS Initiative

evidence.tested: Complementary liposome and diffusion experiments supported lipid-dependent RAS adhesion and dynamics, motivating the authors' conclusion that lipids can mediate RAS multimer organization.
evidence.unknown: Most specific orientation and interface conclusions are simulation-derived; experimental comparisons provide validation of selected membrane adhesion/diffusion behaviors, not direct demonstration of these mechanisms in intact cells or cancer outcomes. Authors describe absolute diffusion values as semiquantitative and dependent on methods/force fields.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning selects diverse local membrane patches from a macroscale lipid model to launch and couple atomistic/coarse-grained simulations, producing an ensemble of more than 100,000 simulations. The resulting simulations identified lipid-composition relationships with RAS orientation and multimer organization; selected predictions were compared with surface-plasmon resonance, fluorescence-correlation and other biophysical experiments.

title: BIONIC links the natural product NP329 to yeast cell-wall biogenesis and β-1,6-glucan synthesis
summary: The BIONIC graph-convolutional network integrated yeast interaction datasets and predicted essential-gene chemical sensitivities to the uncharacterized compound NP329. Experimental screens supported four BIONIC-predicted sensitive genes in the cell-wall biogenesis process; follow-up tests showed related steroidal alkaloid jervine reduced β-1,6-glucan and KRE6/SKN1 mutations conferred resistance, supporting a pathway-level connection for this compound family.
ai_technology: BIONIC (Biological Network Integration using Convolutions), a graph-convolutional deep-learning network-integration method
organization: University of Toronto; RIKEN Center for Sustainable Resource Science, and collaborators

evidence.tested: Experimental screens supported four BIONIC-predicted sensitive genes in the cell-wall biogenesis process; follow-up tests showed related steroidal alkaloid jervine reduced β-1,6-glucan and KRE6/SKN1 mutations conferred resistance, supporting a pathway-level connection for this compound family.
evidence.unknown: BIONIC predicted chemical–genetic sensitivity, not direct molecular binding. NP329 is pseudojervine; jervine is a related compound tested in follow-up. The authors report jervine reduced β-1,6-glucan and KRE6/SKN1 mutations conferred resistance, implicating but not biochemically proving target engagement. Yeast-specific findings.
evidence.ai_role: BIONIC combined yeast protein-interaction, coexpression and genetic-interaction network features to predict essential-gene chemical sensitivities. For NP329 it predicted four of six experimentally sensitive essential genes in the glycosylation/cell-wall biogenesis process, helping identify this cellular process for follow-up. The later jervine experiments are supportive chemical-family follow-up, not direct proof that BIONIC predicted the jervine interaction.

title: A recurrent neural network uncovers a non-canonical human GRHL1 DNA-binding site
summary: A convolutional recurrent neural network found 46 GRHL1 ChIP-seq sites missed by a conventional position-weight matrix, including sequences lacking the previously considered obligatory CNNG motif. Isothermal titration calorimetry confirmed GRHL1 binding to a selected non-canonical sequence lacking that core motif; nucleotide mutagenesis experiments also showed that model scores tracked measured affinity across tested variants.
ai_technology: Convolutional recurrent neural network trained on GRHL1 HT-SELEX binding data
organization: Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine; Hannover Medical School; Institute of Bioorganic Chemistry, Polish Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: Isothermal titration calorimetry confirmed GRHL1 binding to a selected non-canonical sequence lacking that core motif; nucleotide mutagenesis experiments also showed that model scores tracked measured affinity across tested variants.
evidence.unknown: Only one of the 46 predicted non-canonical sites was directly validated by ITC in this study; 46 is a model-nominated set, not 46 experimentally confirmed bindings. Biochemical affinity was tested with the isolated GRHL1 DNA-binding domain and synthetic DNA, not in vivo transcriptional effects for the novel site.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN/RNN learned GRHL1 sequence-binding patterns from HT-SELEX and scored human-cell ChIP-seq peaks. It identified 46 sites not detected by FIMO/PWM; one selected high-scoring non-canonical site was experimentally confirmed by ITC, and predicted variant affinity changes were compared with ITC results.

title: A protein-language-model workflow discovers high-activity kynureninase enzymes for tumor models
summary: A workflow combining homology search, protein-language-model embeddings and regression prioritized kynureninases by predicted catalytic activity. Researchers experimentally tested four top-ranked candidates; the most active had nearly twice the turnover number of the prior best, and enzyme treatment was associated with a 3.4-fold reduction in tumor weight in a mouse comparison.
ai_technology: Protein language model embeddings coupled with regression in the SeekRank enzyme-prioritization workflow
organization: Seoul National University; and Galux Inc.

evidence.tested: Researchers experimentally tested four top-ranked candidates; the most active had nearly twice the turnover number of the prior best, and enzyme treatment was associated with a 3.4-fold reduction in tumor weight in a mouse comparison.
evidence.unknown: The evidence is a published paper abstract; it describes an enzyme/treatment experiment in a mouse tumor model, not clinical efficacy. The reported tumor-weight reduction is model-specific; no claim of human therapeutic benefit is made.
evidence.ai_role: The model represented homologous kynureninase sequences with protein-language-model embeddings and regressed kinetic activity to rank enzyme candidates. Four high-ranked candidates were tested in vitro and in vivo; the abstract reports one with nearly two-fold improved turnover number and reduced tumor weight in a mouse model.

title: Machine learning uncovers four new extracellular contractile injection-system toxins
summary: An XGBoost classifier trained on genomic and biochemical features prioritized eCIS-associated toxins from bacterial and archaeal genomes. Four candidates, EAT14–17, were experimentally shown to be toxic in bacterial and/or yeast cells; EAT14 also inhibited Rac1/Cdc42-mediated mitogenic signaling in human cells.
ai_technology: XGBoost classifier for extracellular contractile injection-system-associated toxins (EATs)
organization: Hebrew University of Jerusalem; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; collaborators

evidence.tested: Four candidates, EAT14–17, were experimentally shown to be toxic in bacterial and/or yeast cells; EAT14 also inhibited Rac1/Cdc42-mediated mitogenic signaling in human cells.
evidence.unknown: Four of eight selected candidates were toxic under the tested heterologous-expression assays; the authors report an empirical positive predictive value of 50% for this sample and discuss possible host/compartment mismatch. Toxin delivery by native eCIS and physiological target organisms remain incompletely established. EAT14’s signaling effect was shown in human cells, not as a therapeutic effect.
evidence.ai_role: The classifier used genomic and protein biochemical features to score candidate EAT genes across eCIS-positive microbial genomes. The model narrowed candidates for functional tests; heterologous expression assays validated four previously uncharacterized toxins, with follow-up active-site mutations and a human-cell signaling assay.

title: Deep-learning-assisted DIP-MS identifies POLR2E as a constitutive prefoldin-like-complex subunit
summary: DIP-MS combines deep-learning-based signal processing with native-gel fractionation and mass spectrometry to resolve complex isoforms. In human prefoldin-like-complex experiments, repeated coelution and affinity-purification data supported POLR2E as a constitutive PFDL component, updating the view that it was merely an associated protein.
ai_technology: Deep Interactome Profiling by Mass Spectrometry (DIP-MS), including deep-learning-based signal processing
organization: Institute of Molecular Systems Biology; ETH Zurich and collaborators

evidence.tested: In human prefoldin-like-complex experiments, repeated coelution and affinity-purification data supported POLR2E as a constitutive PFDL component, updating the view that it was merely an associated protein.
evidence.unknown: The paper proposes POLR2E as a constitutive PFDL subunit based on coelution and affinity-purification in the tested human-cell system; it does not establish that every cellular PFDL complex contains POLR2E or fully characterize its functional contribution. DIP-MS also recapitulated known ASDURF association, which is not counted here as novel because ASDURF’s PAQosome/PFDL role had been reported earlier.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning signal processing helped resolve coexisting protein-complex isoforms from AP-MS/native PAGE/DIA-MS data. DIP-MS on UXT and PFDN2 baits repeatedly detected PFDL coelution with POLR2E; affinity purification of four tagged PFDL-like subunits also recovered POLR2E, supporting the proposed constitutive association.

title: Machine-learning screening yields novel potent acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitors
summary: NCATS researchers trained machine-learning QSAR models and applied them to a roughly 360,000-compound library. Experimental colorimetric and orthogonal fluorescence assays confirmed new AChE/BChE inhibitors; the study reports 22 AChE and 67 BChE inhibitors with IC50 below 5 μM, including novel structural series, with some submicromolar compounds.
ai_technology: Ensemble comparison of machine-learning QSAR classifiers (including XGBoost, random forest, SVM, neural network and naïve Bayes)
organization: National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, National Institutes of Health

evidence.tested: Experimental colorimetric and orthogonal fluorescence assays confirmed new AChE/BChE inhibitors; the study reports 22 AChE and 67 BChE inhibitors with IC50 below 5 μM, including novel structural series, with some submicromolar compounds.
evidence.unknown: These are biochemical inhibitor assays and early medicinal-chemistry leads; they do not establish brain exposure, in-vivo efficacy, safety or clinical benefit. Several known compounds were newly identified as inhibitors, so the count of all assay hits should not be described as entirely novel molecules.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on quantitative high-throughput screening data prioritized compounds in a ~360,000-compound collection for AChE/BChE inhibition and selectivity assays. Researchers tested 2,762 high-scoring compounds in colorimetric assays and used an orthogonal fluorescence assay to confirm predicted inhibitors; subsequent structure–activity analysis identified novel scaffolds.

title: EnzySFC discovers nitrile-hydratase activity in nitrilases and evolves amide-selective variants
summary: The AI-assisted EnzySFC workflow experimentally validated 10 previously uncharacterized nitrilases selected from 1,113 candidates. A wild-type Phototrophicales nitrilase showed exclusive nitrile hydratase activity; a separate Actinomycetia nitrilase was AI-evolved, with four tested top variants reaching 100% amide yield and complete substrate conversion.
ai_technology: EnzySFC AI-assisted enzyme discovery and functional-evolution platform
organization: China State Institute of Pharmaceutical Industry, Research Center for Systems Biosynthesis

evidence.tested: The AI-assisted EnzySFC workflow experimentally validated 10 previously uncharacterized nitrilases selected from 1,113 candidates.
evidence.unknown: The reported outcomes are enzyme and substrate assays; the abstract does not establish industrial scale performance or application in a living system. The 10 discovery candidates and 16 mutants were experimental follow-ups to model prioritization, not comprehensive validation of all 1,113 sequences.
evidence.ai_role: EnzySFC combined de novo enzyme discovery and multiobjective activity/specificity optimization to rank candidate nitrilases and propose evolved mutants. The study experimentally tested ten discovery candidates and sixteen mutants from one evolution prediction cycle; the named activity switch and product-selective variants were measured in assays.

title: Machine-learning metabolomics identifies widespread promiscuous activities in Escherichia coli enzymes
summary: In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested. Follow-up reconstruction assigned 22 reaction stoichiometries to 11 enzymes, with four reactions experimentally validated; examples include expanded nucleotide-substrate use by DeoA, cofactor and sugar promiscuity in NanK, and FMN dephosphorylation by CobC. Follow-up assays also found that pyrimidine-specific ribonucleoside hydrolase RihB acted on thymidine, guanosine and deoxyuridine, further extending its measured substrate range.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier applied to enzyme metabolomics ion-trace data
organization: ETH Zurich; Weizmann Institute of Science; University Children’s Hospital Zurich and University of Zurich

evidence.tested: In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested.
evidence.unknown: The classifier operated at a 33% false-discovery rate; the 135 ion traces were putatively annotated, and only four of 22 reconstructed reaction stoichiometries were experimentally validated. Therefore the full 11% result is a set of candidate activities, not 11% independently confirmed enzyme functions. The RihB activities were prompted by a low-confidence potassium-thymidine-adduct trace and then tested directly with purified enzyme; they should be distinguished from the classifier’s higher-confidence hit set.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, with a reported false-discovery rate of 33%, detected unexpected changes in metabolite ion traces in the enzyme assays and helped nominate candidate promiscuous activities. The researchers then reconstructed candidate reaction stoichiometries and experimentally validated four reactions.

title: Generative deep learning discovers the RIPK1 inhibitor RI-962 with an unreported scaffold
summary: A target-conditioned generative deep-learning model based on a distribution-learning conditional recurrent neural network generated a tailored compound library that was screened for RIPK1 inhibition. The study reports RI-962 as a potent inhibitor with a previously unreported scaffold, validated in vitro for protection from necroptosis and in vivo in two inflammatory models.
ai_technology: Generative deep-learning distribution-learning conditional recurrent neural network (GDL cRNN)
organization: State Key Laboratory of Biotherapy and Cancer Center, West China Hospital, Sichuan University; West China School of Pharmacy, Sichuan University

evidence.tested: The study reports RI-962 as a potent inhibitor with a previously unreported scaffold, validated in vitro for protection from necroptosis and in vivo in two inflammatory models.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is preclinical: cellular necroptosis assays and two inflammatory mouse models do not establish human efficacy or safety. The paper identifies one leading molecule from a generated library; it does not validate generative-model performance across targets generally.
evidence.ai_role: The GDL cRNN generated a target-tailored virtual compound library; virtual screening and subsequent chemical synthesis and bioactivity assays selected RI-962. This provides direct experimental testing of a model-generated molecule rather than a prediction-only hit.

title: Machine-learning-guided screening identifies Bcl-2-family inhibitors IS20 and IS21
summary: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening followed by surface-plasmon-resonance and biological assays identified IS20 and IS21 as compounds binding anti-apoptotic Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Mcl-1 proteins. Both affected cancer-cell viability and induced apoptosis/autophagic flux in tested cell models; IS21 also reduced tumor growth in leukemia and melanoma mouse models.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening (model family not named in PubMed abstract)
organization: IRCCS Regina Elena National Cancer Institute; Sapienza University of Rome; Italian National Research Council and collaborators

evidence.tested: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening followed by surface-plasmon-resonance and biological assays identified IS20 and IS21 as compounds binding anti-apoptotic Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Mcl-1 proteins.
evidence.unknown: The article calls the compounds potential/new leads; findings are biochemical, cell-based and mouse-model preclinical evidence. It does not establish clinical effectiveness. The PubMed abstract does not specify the machine-learning algorithm, so no specific model architecture is attributed here.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening prioritized putative Bcl-2-family inhibitor compounds; the candidate hits were then evaluated by surface plasmon resonance and in vitro cell assays, and IS21 was evaluated in mouse tumor models.
