The identity links gap, contact-force and overlap scaling relations and had previously been known numerically but not analytically. The authors report that Claude Opus 4.7 derived the core proof idea with minimal supervision, with Sonnet 4.6 helping refine it; the authors found and corrected errors in an early draft, then verified and edited the final proof.
ai_technology: Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7 and Claude Sonnet 4.6
organization: Sapienza University of Rome; CNR-Nanotec Rome; INFN Sezione di Roma 1; Beihang University

evidence.tested: Giorgio Parisi and Francesco Zamponi provide an analytic proof that the critical exponents a and b in the full replica-symmetry-breaking scaling solution for infinite-dimensional dense hard spheres obey a+b=1.
evidence.unknown: The theorem is scoped to the fullRSB scaling equations for the infinite-dimensional dense hard-sphere jamming solution; it is not a general proof about every finite-dimensional jamming system. The result is peer-reviewed and published, but proof validation and correction are attributed to the human authors.
evidence.ai_role: After numerical investigation, Opus generated the analytic proof strategy and proof draft for the previously unproven scaling identity; Sonnet refined minor steps. The authors report 40 prompts, corrected early inconsistencies and verified/edited the published proof.

title: AI-assisted transfer-matrix analysis yields an exact solution for the 1D frustrated q-state Potts model
summary: The study exactly solves the one-dimensional J₁–J₂ q-state Potts model for arbitrary q by reducing its q²×q² transfer matrix to a 2×2 maximally symmetric subspace and mapping it to an effective q-state Potts model in a field. OpenAI’s o3-mini-high reasoning model helped derive the q=3 case; the author then generalized the result to arbitrary q and checked the formulas numerically. The solution nontrivially extends an older mapping known for q=2/Ising and yields q-dependent phase and residual-entropy behavior.
ai_technology: OpenAI o3-mini-high reasoning model
organization: Brookhaven National Laboratory

evidence.tested: The study exactly solves the one-dimensional J₁–J₂ q-state Potts model for arbitrary q by reducing its q²×q² transfer matrix to a 2×2 maximally symmetric subspace and mapping it to an effective q-state Potts model in a field.
evidence.unknown: The AI contribution was to the q=3 transfer-matrix solution; the general-q theorem and full paper are the human author’s derivation, so this is an AI-assisted paper-level theoretical discovery, not an autonomous AI solution for arbitrary q. The exact result concerns the one-dimensional model and does not itself demonstrate a material realization.
evidence.ai_role: Proposed a transfer-matrix construction that enabled an exact solution of the q=3 frustrated Potts model; the author used that result as a starting point to generalize the exact mapping to arbitrary q, prove the subspace correspondence and numerically check the resulting formulas.

title: Gemini derives an exact analytic solution for the cosmic-string gravitational-radiation power integral
summary: A Gemini Deep Think system, guided by tree search and numerical feedback, derived closed-form spectral coefficients for the integral determining gravitational radiation power from cosmic-string loops, resolving the paper’s stated open calculation. The authors compare the expressions against direct numerical integration over ranges of loop harmonic and geometry parameters, finding close agreement. This is a theoretical/computational result, not a new astronomical detection.
ai_technology: Google Gemini Deep Think integrated with tree search, executable Python evaluation and high-precision numerical feedback
organization: Affiliations are not recorded as an organization claim because the consulted arXiv page did not expose them in the checked abstract.

evidence.tested: A Gemini Deep Think system, guided by tree search and numerical feedback, derived closed-form spectral coefficients for the integral determining gravitational radiation power from cosmic-string loops, resolving the paper’s stated open calculation.
evidence.unknown: The source is an unrefereed arXiv preprint. The paper provides derivations and numerical cross-checks, not proof-assistant verification or independent replication. The first recurrence attempt contained an error that the later Gemini-assisted review corrected. The claim is limited to the stated integral for the cosmic-string radiation model and its exact analytic evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: Gemini generated and refined analytical approaches inside a tree-search workflow whose Python harness compared candidate expressions with high-precision numerical integration. A later human-initiated session with a more advanced Gemini model identified a recurrence error and telescoped the series into a finite analytic expression; this was a human–AI handoff, not a fully autonomous end-to-end result.

title: Machine learning identifies disordered twist-angle sequences with strongly reduced thermal conductivity in multilayer graphene
summary: Bayesian optimization and a CNN, coupled to non-equilibrium molecular dynamics, selected two-angle disordered twisted multilayer graphene structures with substantially lower simulated cross-plane thermal conductivity than aligned and periodic stacks. The optimized 14-layer sequence reached 0.095 W m−1 K−1 versus 0.512 W m−1 K−1 in aligned graphene in the reported model; phonon participation ratios and dynamical structure factors support strong partial phonon localization.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization (COMBO) and convolutional neural network coupled to molecular-dynamics simulations
organization: Sun Yat-sen University

evidence.tested: Bayesian optimization and a CNN, coupled to non-equilibrium molecular dynamics, selected two-angle disordered twisted multilayer graphene structures with substantially lower simulated cross-plane thermal conductivity than aligned and periodic stacks.
evidence.unknown: This is a computational prediction supported by molecular-dynamics calculations, not a measured thermal-conductivity result from fabricated multilayer samples. The paper reports 80% reduction relative to aligned graphene for an optimized sequence and interprets phonon participation/structure-factor analyses as evidence of partial localization.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian optimization selected low-conductivity twist sequences; the CNN screened the larger configuration space and proposed low-conductivity structures for subsequent molecular-dynamics evaluation.

title: Machine-learning analysis attributes the apparent pre-Norcia earthquake b-value rise to changing activity across two fault structures
summary: For the 2016–2017 central Italy sequence, a combination of machine-learning techniques resolved two seismicity volumes with distinct fault orientations and Gutenberg–Richter b-values. Each structure retained its own b-value through the sequence; the apparent rise before the Mw 6.5 Norcia earthquake emerged when both were combined as their relative activity changed, showing that spatial heterogeneity can create an apparent temporal b-value signal.
ai_technology: Combination of machine-learning techniques for seismicity structure and b-value analysis (paper abstract does not name a single model)
organization: University of Naples Federico II; Scuola Superiore Meridionale

evidence.tested: For the 2016–2017 central Italy sequence, a combination of machine-learning techniques resolved two seismicity volumes with distinct fault orientations and Gutenberg–Richter b-values.
evidence.unknown: The analysis is retrospective and specific to the 2016/2017 central Italy sequence; the authors state that b-value changes may reflect spatial redistribution as well as other processes and do not claim a usable prospective earthquake precursor.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning analysis separated seismicity into fault-associated volumes and enabled comparison of their distinct b-values over time, supporting the reported explanation of the aggregate temporal change.

title: Machine-learning phase picks constrain the 2025 Drake Passage earthquake depth and activated fault geometry
summary: For the Mw 7.4 Drake Passage earthquake of 2 May 2025, a trained classifier identified depth-sensitive pP–sP seismic phases used to refine focal depths under sparse station coverage. The authors infer a mainshock depth of about 25 km, consistent with the small tsunami, and report aftershocks on west-dipping faults southeast of the epicenter near the Shackleton Fracture Zone; the paper integrates this with seismic-reflection and previously collected imaging data.
ai_technology: Trained machine-learning classifier for depth-sensitive seismic phase identification
organization: Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale (OGS); CNR-ISMAR; University of Urbino; CONICET–University of Buenos Aires

evidence.tested: For the Mw 7.4 Drake Passage earthquake of 2 May 2025, a trained classifier identified depth-sensitive pP–sP seismic phases used to refine focal depths under sparse station coverage.
evidence.unknown: The result is a retrospective analysis of one earthquake sequence. The depth is inferred from phase picks and is consistent with tsunami observations; tectonic interpretation also relies on aftershock mechanisms and independent seismic imaging. The machine-learning component contributes phase identification rather than discovering the earthquake itself.
evidence.ai_role: Identified pP–sP phases in regional records; these phases were incorporated into event relocation and focal-depth determination, helping constrain the mainshock depth where station coverage is limited.

title: OptPDE identifies new candidate integrable PDE families with nontrivial conserved quantities
summary: Automatic differentiation optimized partial-differential-equation coefficients to increase the number of conserved quantities. The published study reports four PDE families with at least one nontrivial conserved quantity and analytically studies one new candidate, u_t = u_x^3; the work establishes candidate systems and conserved quantities, not that every generated family is fully integrable.
ai_technology: OptPDE coefficient optimization with the CQFinder conserved-quantity search
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Automatic differentiation optimized partial-differential-equation coefficients to increase the number of conserved quantities.
evidence.unknown: The peer-reviewed source reports four PDE families with at least one nontrivial conserved quantity and analytically examines one new candidate, u_t = u_x^3. The authors explicitly state that maximizing conserved quantities does not guarantee integrability; the result is a concrete candidate system and its studied properties, not proof that every output family is integrable.
evidence.ai_role: The authors explicitly describe OptPDE as a machine-learning approach. CQFinder computes the conserved-quantity objective from a symbolic PDE basis; OptPDE uses a sigmoid-smoothed objective and backpropagation to optimize 34 trainable PDE coefficients. They ran 5,000 random initializations and used dimensionality reduction to group the outputs into four families. This is a learned, trainable symbolic search, not simply use of an automatic-differentiation library.

title: Machine learning identifies sediment-derived granites in the Hadean zircon record, supporting early subduction
summary: A machine-learning classifier trained on trace-element fingerprints identified detrital zircon signatures from sediment-derived S-type granites as old as 4.24 billion years in the Jack Hills record. Across global detrital zircon data, the authors report long-term cyclic changes in S-type granite proportions and infer that exposed, weathered continental crust and subduction operated by about 4.2 Ga. The result bears on early Earth geodynamics, not a direct fossil or biological discovery.
ai_technology: Trace-element Support Vector Machine (TSVM) classifier
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Macau University of Science and Technology; University of California, Davis; Queen’s University

evidence.tested: A machine-learning classifier trained on trace-element fingerprints identified detrital zircon signatures from sediment-derived S-type granites as old as 4.24 billion years in the Jack Hills record.
evidence.unknown: The early-subduction interpretation is inferred from zircon trace elements and remains one interpretation of sparse Hadean geological evidence. The article reports that only the combination of early subaerial weathering and subduction explains the prevalence of the inferred S-type granites; it does not directly observe tectonics at 4.2 Ga.
evidence.ai_role: Classified zircon as S-type or non-S-type from multielement geochemical fingerprints, allowing the authors to identify the oldest sediment-derived granite signal and quantify its temporal distribution across detrital-zircon records.

title: Interpretable machine learning finds a perpendicular-spin signature consistent with a spinon Fermi surface
summary: A correlator convolutional neural network trained on projective snapshots from numerical simulations of the Kitaev–Heisenberg model identified a characteristic correlation pattern in the intermediate gapless phase when analyzing spin snapshots perpendicular to the applied field. The authors interpret the learned pattern as Friedel oscillations of gapless spinons forming a Fermi surface, supporting earlier theoretical proposals for this phase and suggesting measurable correlations for future experiments.
ai_technology: Quantum-classical QuCl approach using a correlator convolutional neural network and regularization-path analysis
organization: Cornell University; The Ohio State University; Google Research; Harvard University; Ewha Womans University

evidence.tested: A correlator convolutional neural network trained on projective snapshots from numerical simulations of the Kitaev–Heisenberg model identified a characteristic correlation pattern in the intermediate gapless phase when analyzing spin snapshots perpendicular to the applied field.
evidence.unknown: This is a numerical/theoretical result based on DMRG wavefunctions and simulated snapshots, not an experimental observation of a quantum spin liquid. The authors interpret the learned motif as evidence consistent with a spinon Fermi surface and offer it as a prediction to guide experiments; they do not claim it is already experimentally confirmed.
evidence.ai_role: Analyzed simulated projective-measurement snapshots and surfaced the phase signature: spin correlations in the direction perpendicular to the magnetic field, interpreted as the spatial pattern of Friedel oscillations associated with gapless spinons.

title: High-resolution machine-learning catalog outlines a potential unmapped fault in the Weiyuan shale-gas region
summary: A machine-learning event detector combined with waveform cross-correlation produced a high-resolution catalog for injection-induced seismicity in the Weiyuan area, identifying one-third more earthquakes than the routine catalog and improving magnitude completeness. Spatial migration patterns show a pore-pressure diffusion front; a cluster outlines a potential unmapped fault that may have hosted the region’s largest recorded event, the September 2019 Mw 5.2 earthquake.
ai_technology: Machine-learning earthquake detector combined with waveform cross-correlation (the abstract does not name a particular detector architecture)
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Sichuan Earthquake Agency

evidence.tested: A machine-learning event detector combined with waveform cross-correlation produced a high-resolution catalog for injection-induced seismicity in the Weiyuan area, identifying one-third more earthquakes than the routine catalog and improving magnitude completeness.
evidence.unknown: The authors describe the fault as potential and state that it may have led to the September 2019 Mw 5.2 event; this is an interpretation, not a directly imaged fault or established causal proof. Results are from one field area and are limited by the station coverage.
evidence.ai_role: Detected additional earthquakes that enabled higher-resolution relocation and spatiotemporal mapping; authors use the denser catalog to infer a migrating pore-pressure front and identify a cluster outlining a potential fault trace.

title: EQTransformer-based catalog reveals a 50-km-deep outer-rise fault at the Southern Mariana trench
summary: Applying EQTransformer phase detection to near-field ocean-bottom seismometer recordings collected near the Challenger Deep yielded more than 1,975 earthquakes. Relocation and waveform-similarity clustering outlined a southern Mariana outer-rise fault extending approximately 20–50 km below the seafloor (about 50 km maximum depth), inferred to be a reactivated normal fault; the depth suggests more incoming-plate water input than prior estimates.
ai_technology: EQTransformer machine-learning seismic phase detector
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Chinese Academy of Sciences; Qingdao National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology; Southern University of Science and Technology; Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution

evidence.tested: Applying EQTransformer phase detection to near-field ocean-bottom seismometer recordings collected near the Challenger Deep yielded more than 1,975 earthquakes.
evidence.unknown: The fault depth, fault type and hydration implications are inferred from a localized seismic cluster, waveform similarity, and regional tomography; focal mechanisms could not be robustly resolved, and the authors state that limited station coverage does not establish whether such deep faults are widespread.
evidence.ai_role: Detected and picked P- and S-wave phases in near-field ocean-bottom seismometer data, producing a denser earthquake catalog. Researchers manually reviewed selected phases, relocated the events and used waveform-similarity clustering to delineate the fault.

title: Deep learning identifies 216 previously unrecognized Green Pea galaxies in DESI Legacy Survey imaging
summary: A MobileMamba-ECA image classifier searched DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys data and surfaced 775 Green Pea galaxy candidates. Cross-matching with DESI DR1 spectroscopy established 216 as previously unreported Green Pea galaxies: although spectra existed, the standard DESI pipeline had classified them only as generic galaxies. The study’s remaining 511 photometric-only objects are follow-up candidates and are not included in the confirmed count.
ai_technology: MobileMamba-ECA deep-learning classifier (Mamba state-space backbone with efficient channel attention)
organization: Shandong University; National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: A MobileMamba-ECA image classifier searched DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys data and surfaced 775 Green Pea galaxy candidates.
evidence.unknown: The 216 newly identified galaxies have archival spectra and were classified with emission-line and BPT diagnostics; they were not all newly observed. The 511 sources without archival spectral coverage remain candidates and are excluded from this finding. The result is a newly recognized population/sample, not a claim that the galaxies themselves formed recently.
evidence.ai_role: Classified multiband DESI Legacy Survey images to prioritize compact Green Pea galaxy sources from an 843,592-object parent sample; this enabled spectral cross-identification and recognition of 216 previously unreported examples.

title: CNN-guided spectroscopy confirms 28 new extremely metal-poor galaxies
summary: A three-stage convolutional-neural-network pipeline screened more than 7.7 million SDSS DR17 imaging sources lacking SDSS spectra, then selected targets for observation. Follow-up spectra of 45 candidates confirmed all as metal-poor galaxies, including 28 newly discovered extremely metal-poor systems; 18 have weak or undetected [N II] lines and oxygen-abundance upper limits.
ai_technology: Three-stage CNN characterization pipeline (metal-poor galaxy classifier, XMP classifier, and N2-index predictor)
organization: University of California, Davis; Durham University; Isaac Newton Group of Telescopes; Southern Astrophysical Research Telescope

evidence.tested: A three-stage convolutional-neural-network pipeline screened more than 7.7 million SDSS DR17 imaging sources lacking SDSS spectra, then selected targets for observation.
evidence.unknown: The 28 new XMP classifications derive from follow-up of 45 targeted candidates, not the full 7.7-million-source imaging search. For 18 galaxies with weak or absent [N II], oxygen abundance is reported as a 2-sigma upper limit; the paper also reports four possible low-metallicity AGN candidates, which are not counted as confirmed here.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN pipeline ranked imaging-only sources using predicted spectral line ratios to nominate telescope targets; subsequent INT and SOAR spectroscopy established their metallicity classifications and confirmed 28 as new XMP galaxies.

title: MSFA-Net and Balmer-line fitting identify 3,583 new blue horizontal-branch stars
summary: A two-stage deep-learning pipeline searched LAMOST DR12 spectra and retained 27,853 BHB candidate spectra. After removal of previously known objects, stringent Balmer-line-profile fitting, and deduplication, the authors report 3,583 unique newly identified blue horizontal-branch stars. Gaia photometry provides an additional consistency check.
ai_technology: MSFA-Net, a multi-scale and frequency-attention deep neural network, followed by a binary refinement classifier
organization: National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: A two-stage deep-learning pipeline searched LAMOST DR12 spectra and retained 27,853 BHB candidate spectra.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint. The paper says high-confidence objects were identified by Balmer-line profile fitting and Gaia color-magnitude consistency, while acknowledging that a fraction could still be contaminants; some atmospheric-parameter outliers are attributed to inference systematics. Counts are unique objects after deduplication, not 3,923 spectra.
evidence.ai_role: MSFA-Net searched the LAMOST DR12 hot-star spectral domain, used staged classification to reduce the spectra to candidate sets, and aided construction of the new sample; Balmer-line profile criteria and duplicate removal yielded the reported 3,583 unique objects. A separate SLAM model estimated atmospheric parameters rather than serving as the confirmation step.

title: WDNet-guided DESI follow-up confirms 75 new white dwarfs and 7 cataclysmic variables
summary: WDNet detected candidates in DESI Legacy Surveys DR9 images. The researchers cross-matched 18,242 photometric candidates with DESI DR1 spectra, obtaining 719 candidate spectra; manual visual inspection of those spectra identified 75 new white dwarfs and 7 new cataclysmic variables. These spectroscopic classifications, not the much larger image-candidate list, are the reported verified sample.
ai_technology: WDNet, a deep-learning object-detection network based on YOLOv8 with multi-scale feature fusion
organization: Shandong University; National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Yunding Technology

evidence.tested: WDNet detected candidates in DESI Legacy Surveys DR9 images.
evidence.unknown: The authors confirmed 75 new WDs and 7 new CVs among the 719 candidates with DESI spectra, and explicitly note substantial contamination among remaining candidates and selection effects in the spectroscopic subsample. No atmosphere-model fitting was done for all identifications; the authors recommend further high-S/N spectroscopic modeling. The article's abstract/results/conclusion give inconsistent counts for the full detected/candidate catalog (18,242, 61,624, and 63,214 are all reported in different sections); this entry relies only on the consistent 719 spectral matches and 75+7 inspected confirmations. The full photometric catalog is not counted as confirmed discoveries.
evidence.ai_role: WDNet detected and localized white-dwarf candidates in DESI Legacy Surveys photometric images, thereby prioritizing objects for DESI spectral cross-match and manual spectral inspection. Human inspection of DESI spectra supplied the classification confirmation; the neural network did not itself confirm the new stellar classes.

title: Deep-learning-enhanced Sparta earthquake catalog resolves a shallow multifault rupture
summary: For the 2020 Mw 5.1 Sparta, North Carolina sequence, an EQTransformer-based catalog combined with matched-filter detections and differential-time relocations contains 1,761 high-precision events, about 5.8 times the original NEIC count. The denser locations resolve several shallow clusters and support the authors’ interpretation that the mainshock nucleated near the intersection of a blind strike-slip fault and a reverse fault associated with the surface rupture; moment-tensor inversion places its centroid at about 1.3 km depth.
ai_technology: Earthquake Transformer (EQTransformer) deep-learning phase/event detector, followed by matched-filter detection and differential-time relocation
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology; University of Science and Technology of China; North Carolina State University; Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: For the 2020 Mw 5.1 Sparta, North Carolina sequence, an EQTransformer-based catalog combined with matched-filter detections and differential-time relocations contains 1,761 high-precision events, about 5.8 times the original NEIC count.
evidence.unknown: This is a retrospective study of one 2020 earthquake sequence, using a local temporary-network deployment. The authors describe the inferred fault intersection/flower-structure interpretation as possible; the fit for the smallest cluster is poor and its geometry uncertain. The result is not a forecast or general fault model. The AI contribution was event detection within a hybrid workflow, not independent geological validation.
evidence.ai_role: EQTransformer detections expanded the template catalog, which seeded matched-filter detection; the resulting event set was relocated to improve temporal and spatial resolution used to infer the sequence’s shallow fault geometry. The fault interpretation is author analysis from the denser catalog plus waveform and moment-tensor methods, not a model-generated classification alone.

title: Crystal-graph learning and DFT identify 19,512 additional thermodynamically stable materials
summary: The authors trained crystal-graph attention networks on an expanded, composition- and symmetry-balanced dataset and used them to search 2,500 binary and ternary structure prototypes covering about one billion inorganic compounds. Density-functional-theory validation identified 19,512 additional compounds on the calculated thermodynamic convex hull and about 150,000 more within 50 meV/atom of it; the paper also analyzed predicted superconducting and superhard materials and compounds with large gap deformation potentials.
ai_technology: Crystal-graph attention neural networks trained on expanded density-functional-theory materials data
organization: Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg; University of Coimbra; Friedrich Schiller University Jena

evidence.tested: The authors trained crystal-graph attention networks on an expanded, composition- and symmetry-balanced dataset and used them to search 2,500 binary and ternary structure prototypes covering about one billion inorganic compounds.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint and the reported stable compounds are computationally predicted, with DFT convex-hull validation; the study does not report their experimental synthesis. Stability depends on the calculated structures and thermodynamic reference data. The additional ~150,000 compounds are near-hull candidates, not counted as thermodynamically stable discoveries in the title or summary.
evidence.ai_role: The graph networks accelerated screening of roughly one billion prototype-generated candidates, after which density-functional-theory calculations validated stability for identified candidates; machine learning plus ab initio calculations also ranked materials for selected functional properties.

title: Unsupervised clustering links deep-earthquake scaling to hydration differences among northwest Pacific slabs
summary: K-means clustering of Japan Meteorological Agency deep-earthquake catalogs separated the northwest Pacific slab segments; Gutenberg–Richter analysis found a magnitude 3.7–3.8 kink in Honshu and Izu seismicity, with b values falling from about 1.4–1.7 to 0.6–0.7. The authors infer that small-event excess and an approximately kilometre-scale metastable-olivine-wedge rim may reflect deep hydration and enhanced transformational faulting.
ai_technology: Unsupervised machine-learning clustering (K-means, checked against spectral clustering and Gaussian mixture models)
organization: Michigan State University; Freie Universität Berlin; Université d’Orléans–CNRS; University of California, Los Angeles; Yale University

evidence.tested: K-means clustering of Japan Meteorological Agency deep-earthquake catalogs separated the northwest Pacific slab segments; Gutenberg–Richter analysis found a magnitude 3.7–3.8 kink in Honshu and Izu seismicity, with b values falling from about 1.4–1.7 to 0.6–0.7.
evidence.unknown: The observed b-value kink is a statistical result. Hydrous defects and an approximately 1 km unstable wedge rim are the authors’ geodynamic interpretation, not direct water-content measurements; the authors discuss magnitude-detection and model assumptions.
evidence.ai_role: Clustered deep-earthquake distributions into four slab segments, enabling region-specific b-value analyses that exposed the Honshu/Izu magnitude kink and its proposed relation to slab hydration.

title: Machine-learning denoising exposes strong size scaling in deep-earthquake rupture parameters
summary: A multitask neural denoiser recovered teleseismic P-wave pulses from deep Mw 5.0+ earthquakes that had previously been too noisy for source analysis. The study found moment–duration scaling M₀ ∼ τ⁴, stress-drop scaling Δσ ∼ M₀⁰·²¹ and radiated-energy scaling Eᵣ ∼ M₀¹·²⁴; deep events had a median radiation efficiency near 5%, weak directivity and few subevents. After accounting for rigidity, no systematic depth trend in duration, stress drop or radiated energy remained across 100–700 km.
ai_technology: DenoTe, a transfer-learned multitask convolutional encoder–decoder neural network
organization: University of Washington, Department of Earth and Space Sciences

evidence.tested: A multitask neural denoiser recovered teleseismic P-wave pulses from deep Mw 5.0+ earthquakes that had previously been too noisy for source analysis.
evidence.unknown: The study is a source-parameter reanalysis enabled by neural denoising, not prospective earthquake prediction. It reports scaling relations and interpretations from the available global event sample; stress and energy estimates remain subject to waveform, path-correction and source-model uncertainties.
evidence.ai_role: Separated low-SNR teleseismic P-wave signals from overlapping noise, enabling source-parameter estimation from 920 deep-earthquake records, including moderate events ordinarily omitted from these analyses.

title: Machine-learning classification shows rigidity-corrected moment release is similar across earthquake depths
summary: Random-forest classification of source-time-function characteristics for 3,675 global Mw > 5.5 earthquakes showed that depth-dependent rigidity explains much of the differences in rupture duration, length and stress drop between shallow, intermediate and deep earthquakes. Once medium rigidity is corrected, the analyzed events exhibit similar moment-release processes, supporting a constant-strain-drop interpretation across depths and host-rock types.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning classification and feature-importance analysis
organization: University of Science and Technology of China; Mengcheng National Geophysical Observatory

evidence.tested: Random-forest classification of source-time-function characteristics for 3,675 global Mw > 5.5 earthquakes showed that depth-dependent rigidity explains much of the differences in rupture duration, length and stress drop between shallow, intermediate and deep earthquakes.
evidence.unknown: This is a global observational analysis of 3,675 moderate-to-large earthquakes. Its constant-strain-drop conclusion is a supported scaling interpretation, not proof that every earthquake rupture mechanism is identical; depth class and source-time-function estimates have sampling limitations.
evidence.ai_role: Compared source-time-function features across depth classes and identified surrounding-medium rigidity as the principal explanatory feature, enabling the rigidity-corrected cross-depth comparison.

title: CNN-augmented focal mechanisms reveal stress-linked faulting changes around major southern California earthquakes
summary: CNN phase and first-motion pickers supplied additional waveform polarities and arrivals for a 297,478-event southern California focal-mechanism catalog, about 40% larger than the prior catalog. The authors used the expanded catalog to observe systematic post-mainshock faulting-style changes spatially correlated with estimated static stress perturbations from the 2010 El Mayor–Cucapah and 2019 Ridgecrest earthquakes, including changes more than 100 km from the epicentres.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural networks for seismic phase arrival and first-motion polarity picking
organization: University of Southern California; California Institute of Technology; University of Southern California Southern California Earthquake Center

evidence.tested: CNN phase and first-motion pickers supplied additional waveform polarities and arrivals for a 297,478-event southern California focal-mechanism catalog, about 40% larger than the prior catalog.
evidence.unknown: Catalog quality varies with location and station coverage; the authors report uncertainty in some solutions and frame stress processes as associations/inferences. The catalog provides improved observations, not a claim of earthquake predictability.
evidence.ai_role: Extracted additional phase arrivals and P-wave first-motion polarities from noisy seismograms; combined with existing observations in HASH focal-mechanism solutions to increase catalog coverage and resolution for small earthquakes.

title: Random-forest selection and spectroscopy identify 20 new high-redshift quasars
summary: A supervised random-forest search of Pan-STARRS1 and WISE photometry identified follow-up targets in the difficult redshift range around z≈5.5, where quasars resemble red and brown dwarfs. Spectroscopic observations of 37 candidates confirmed 20 previously unknown high-redshift quasars (18 at z=4.6–5.5 and two around z≈5.7), including a source outside common color-cut selections.
ai_technology: Supervised random-forest classification and regression applied to Pan-STARRS1 and WISE data
organization: Max Planck Institute for Astronomy; Steward Observatory, University of Arizona; Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics; European Southern Observatory; other international observatories

evidence.tested: A supervised random-forest search of Pan-STARRS1 and WISE photometry identified follow-up targets in the difficult redshift range around z≈5.5, where quasars resemble red and brown dwarfs.
evidence.unknown: Only the 20 spectroscopically observed confirmations are counted. The much larger candidate catalog and predicted unobserved quasars are not treated as discoveries; the source reports a survey-restriction-dependent completeness and efficiency.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked high-redshift quasar candidates from multiband survey photometry; the resulting sample guided telescope follow-up, and spectroscopy established the 20 reported new quasars.

title: CNN tracking reveals irradiation-driven nanovoid size fluctuations and shrinkage in copper
summary: A convolutional neural network combined with greedy matching to detect, track and measure pre-existing nanovoids in in-situ TEM videos of irradiated copper. The analysis revealed non-monotonic, random-walk-like size fluctuations and shrinkage during irradiation; phase-field simulations were used to investigate the mechanism. Follow-up manual measurements and additional experiments confirmed the size-fluctuation observation.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network for void detection, with greedy matching for tracking and migration analysis
organization: Purdue University; University of Hong Kong; Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen

evidence.tested: A convolutional neural network combined with greedy matching to detect, track and measure pre-existing nanovoids in in-situ TEM videos of irradiated copper.
evidence.unknown: The source reports the finding for pre-existing nanovoids in irradiated copper and uses phase-field simulations to explain it. The observed fluctuation was additionally checked by manual measurements and experiments, but generalization to other materials or irradiation regimes is not established by this study.
evidence.ai_role: Automated defect recognition and tracking across high-volume in-situ microscopy video, making it possible to measure nanovoid evolution at scale; phase-field simulations then analyzed the observed dynamics.

title: Physics-guided machine learning links Southern Ocean regime shifts to a northward-shifting Antarctic Circumpolar Current
summary: Applying THOR to one eddy-permitting CM4 climate simulation, researchers detected a projected dynamical-regime shift where the Antarctic Circumpolar Current crosses the Pacific–Antarctic Ridge under the SSP5-8.5 scenario. Neural-network explanations and transport analysis attributed the modeled change to stronger wind stress shifting the current northward into less topographically constrained waters, where the flow intensifies. This is a model-based scenario result, not an observed future change.
ai_technology: THOR (Tracking global Heating with Ocean Regimes), using NEMI clustering, an ensemble of 50 multilayer perceptrons, SHAP and layer-wise relevance propagation
organization: University of California, Davis; NOAA Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory; European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts; Institut Pierre-Simon Laplace

evidence.tested: Applying THOR to one eddy-permitting CM4 climate simulation, researchers detected a projected dynamical-regime shift where the Antarctic Circumpolar Current crosses the Pacific–Antarctic Ridge under the SSP5-8.5 scenario.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint and computational climate-model analysis using CM4/MOM6, one model and the SSP5-8.5 scenario. The paper reports neural-network validation accuracy around 65–70%; it describes the model output and projected shift, not an observed real-world regime transition.
evidence.ai_role: The clustering and neural-network ensemble identified and tracked local ocean dynamical regimes across model scenarios; SHAP and layer-wise relevance propagation highlighted wind-stress curl and bathymetry for follow-up physical analysis.

title: Machine learning identifies a projected shift from DIC- to alkalinity-dominated ocean CO₂-flux variability
summary: Kernel ridge regression reconstructed present and future air–sea CO₂-flux variability in five Earth-system models. The analysis found dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) and alkalinity to be the main drivers, while DIC’s relative importance generally declines in warming scenarios—especially in the equatorial Pacific, Southern Ocean and North Atlantic—as anthropogenic carbon uptake flattens vertical DIC gradients. This result is conditional on the models and scenarios analyzed.
ai_technology: Kernel ridge regression and machine-learning clustering/classification
organization: NORCE Norwegian Research Centre; Bjerknes Centre for Climate Research

evidence.tested: Kernel ridge regression reconstructed present and future air–sea CO₂-flux variability in five Earth-system models.
evidence.unknown: This is an analysis of outputs from five Earth-system models and four historical/future scenarios, not a measurement of future ocean conditions. The interpretation that anthropogenic-carbon-driven gradient flattening contributes to reduced DIC importance is the authors’ proposed mechanism; relative predictor importance does not alone establish causal attribution.
evidence.ai_role: Kernel ridge regression reconstructed CO₂-flux variability from Earth-system-model variables; machine-learning analysis compared predictor importance among spatial clusters and climate scenarios to identify the changing roles of DIC and alkalinity.

title: Machine-learning classification dates a tectonic transition and probable slab detachment in central Tibet
summary: A random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element data distinguished destructive from constructive plate-boundary signatures, with the paper reporting greater than 98% accuracy on its labeled evaluation set. Applied to basalts from Tibet’s Bangong–Nujiang suture zone, it found mixed signatures before about 108–107 Ma and only destructive-boundary signatures afterward; the authors interpret the transition as likely oceanic-slab detachment, consistent with other geological evidence.
ai_technology: Random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element concentrations
organization: China Geological Survey; Chengdu University of Technology; University of Canterbury; China University of Mining and Technology; Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory; Hunan University of Science and Technology; Nanjing University; China University of Geosciences (Beijing); Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: A random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element data distinguished destructive from constructive plate-boundary signatures, with the paper reporting greater than 98% accuracy on its labeled evaluation set.
evidence.unknown: The specific age and slab-detachment interpretation are geological inferences from classified basalt geochemistry, not direct observation of a detached slab. The authors describe the detachment explanation as likely and note consistency with existing evidence; model accuracy is not independent confirmation of the tectonic interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: The classifier learned trace-element signatures associated with destructive and constructive plate boundaries and applied them to Tibetan suture-zone basalts, revealing a time-ordered change in inferred tectonic setting that supported the authors’ slab-detachment interpretation.

title: Machine-learning analysis identifies kinematic evidence for a protoplanet in the HD 142666 disk
summary: A machine-learning model identified a strong, localized non-Keplerian gas-motion feature in the protoplanetary disk around HD 142666. Hydrodynamic simulations of a system containing a 5-Jupiter-mass planet at 75 au reproduced the observed kinematic structure; the authors conclude that HD 142666 hosts an embedded planet by current field criteria. The planet is inferred from disk kinematics rather than directly imaged.
ai_technology: EfficientNetV2 and RegNet image classifiers (six channel-count variants), trained on synthetic planet/no-planet disk observations
organization: University of Oxford (J. P. Terry’s repository-listed affiliation); University of Georgia (resource support acknowledged in the paper)

evidence.tested: A machine-learning model identified a strong, localized non-Keplerian gas-motion feature in the protoplanetary disk around HD 142666.
evidence.unknown: The paper’s planet conclusion is an inference from gas kinematics supported by simulations, not a direct image or independent dynamical mass measurement. The models were classifiers, not trained to localize planets, and the 5-Jupiter-mass, 75-au configuration is a simulation that reproduces the observed feature, not a separately measured planet parameter.
evidence.ai_role: The classifiers applied to ALMA data assigned high planet-presence scores and their activation maps highlighted the previously unreported non-Keplerian velocity kink; the authors then used standard hydrodynamic simulations to test whether an embedded planet reproduced that feature.

title: AI-assisted proof establishes a dimension-independent KLS isoperimetric bound
summary: Zhao Song and Xinzhi Zhang prove a universal, dimension-independent bound for the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits constant of isotropic log-concave probability measures, resolving the KLS conjecture. Their proof repeatedly refines bounds on polynomial variance and curvature; the authors report that AI tools helped explore more than 100 approaches, obtain the earlier log-star bound, and develop and verify the final proof. Independent researchers also posted proofs, and the paper’s streamlined proof is being formalized in Lean. The 1 October preprint gave a slowly dimension-dependent bound; the 4 October version established the dimension-independent theorem described here.
ai_technology: GPT-6 Astra; GPT-5.6 Sol; Claude Fable 5; Fable (as named in the paper’s AI disclosure)
organization: Microsoft Research; independent research collaboration

evidence.tested: Zhao Song and Xinzhi Zhang prove a universal, dimension-independent bound for the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits constant of isotropic log-concave probability measures, resolving the KLS conjecture.
evidence.unknown: The proof is a recent arXiv preprint, not yet journal peer-reviewed in the source reviewed. Independent proofs were posted, and the Microsoft Research author account reports later Lean formalization of a streamlined proof; the paper version and posted revisions should be checked as the work develops. This entry counts the theorem result once, not the intermediate log-star bound separately.
evidence.ai_role: The authors state that they explored candidate approaches collaboratively with AI tools; the tools helped obtain the earlier log-star bound and develop detailed proof steps, while the researchers selected the direction and completed the repeated refinement argument. The authors state they checked the proofs with AI tools and take responsibility for correctness.

title: AI-discovered proof resolves the Komlós vector-balancing conjecture
summary: The paper proves that for every finite family of Euclidean-norm-at-most-one vectors, signs can be chosen so the signed sum has infinity norm below 3√(2π), independent of vector count and dimension. It derives a corresponding square-root-in-sets bound for Beck–Fiala discrepancy. The authors explicitly credit the Odin Automatic AI Research Agent with discovering the proof; a separate elementary proof was posted independently. The algorithmic construction of such signings is a separate follow-up result and is not claimed here.
ai_technology: Odin Automatic AI Research Agent
organization: Duke University; University of California, Irvine; independent research collaboration

evidence.tested: The paper proves that for every finite family of Euclidean-norm-at-most-one vectors, signs can be chosen so the signed sum has infinity norm below 3√(2π), independent of vector count and dimension.
evidence.unknown: The result is reported in an arXiv preprint, not a peer-reviewed journal source in this review. A separate elementary proof of the conjecture appeared later, providing an independent proof route; the paper’s AI attribution is author-reported. The result establishes existence, not a polynomial-time signing algorithm.
evidence.ai_role: The authors credit Odin with discovering the proof of their vector-balancing theorem; Duke’s official account says the system discovered the proof and human authors scrutinized and organized the argument into the paper.

title: AI-discovered construction improves the lower bound for the complex Grothendieck constant
summary: The authors prove the classical complex Grothendieck constant exceeds 1.35584631827168, closing more than one quarter of the gap between Davie’s lower bound and Haagerup’s upper bound reported in the paper. The numerical search used Hermite projections and a radial weight; interval arithmetic on exact rational inputs rigorously verifies the stated bound. The authors credit the Odin Automatic AI Research Agent with discovering both the lower bound and its proof.
ai_technology: Odin Automatic AI Research Agent
organization: Independent research collaboration

evidence.tested: The authors prove the classical complex Grothendieck constant exceeds 1.35584631827168, closing more than one quarter of the gap between Davie’s lower bound and Haagerup’s upper bound reported in the paper.
evidence.unknown: The source is an arXiv preprint. Its stated lower bound is computer-assisted and the proof includes interval arithmetic with exact inputs; the paper does not determine the exact complex Grothendieck constant. The authors’ AI attribution is not independent evidence about the system’s internal process.
evidence.ai_role: The authors explicitly state that Odin discovered the improved lower bound and its proof; the preprint describes numerical optimization that found a candidate, followed by exact rational inputs and interval-arithmetic verification by the authors’ supplied code.

title: Machine learning predicts timing and fault-state evolution in meter-scale laboratory earthquakes
summary: A Random Forest using a network representation of acoustic-emission event catalogs predicted the timing of meter-scale laboratory mainshocks from tens of seconds to milliseconds ahead (test-set log R²=0.84). Feature analysis found systematic changes in event intervals and seismic moments as failure approached; comparison with dynamic simulations led the authors to infer that acoustic emissions indirectly encode stress evolution on creeping fault patches. This is a laboratory-scale result, not a validated method for forecasting natural earthquakes.
ai_technology: Random Forest machine-learning model; deep-learning comparison model
organization: Kyoto University; Disaster Prevention Research Institute, Kyoto University

evidence.tested: A Random Forest using a network representation of acoustic-emission event catalogs predicted the timing of meter-scale laboratory mainshocks from tens of seconds to milliseconds ahead (test-set log R²=0.84).
evidence.unknown: This is one meter-scale rock-friction experiment (experiment LB12-011) and a corresponding numerical model; forecast skill varies with foreshock density and cannot be generalized to natural earthquakes. The article was corrected on 2026-02-02 to replace an uncorrected proof PDF; the correction says it did not describe a scientific-result change.
evidence.ai_role: The Random Forest model made the time-to-failure predictions from the event catalog; the authors analyzed predictive features and compared the results to dynamic simulations to infer that catalog signals encode evolving fault state. The machine-learning analysis is the core result, not merely automated event detection.

title: AI-assisted seismic catalog links the 2018 Baige landslide-dammed lakes to increased local earthquakes
summary: An earthquake catalog built with the PhaseNet machine-learning phase detector and cross-correlation/template matching revealed a statistically significant (over 99%) increase in small earthquakes as the second Baige landslide-dammed lake approached peak water level; rates returned toward background after breach. Coulomb-stress modeling found about 90% of the earthquakes in regions of positive modeled stress change, supporting likely triggering through direct water loading and pore-pressure diffusion. The paper presents this as evidence that earthquake–surface-hazard triggering can be bidirectional.
ai_technology: PhaseNet machine-learning phase detector, combined with PyOcto association and cross-correlation/template-matching methods
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; WSL Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research; Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Sichuan Earthquake Administration; Géoazur

evidence.tested: An earthquake catalog built with the PhaseNet machine-learning phase detector and cross-correlation/template matching revealed a statistically significant (over 99%) increase in small earthquakes as the second Baige landslide-dammed lake approached peak water level; rates returned toward background after breach.
evidence.unknown: This is a case study of one pair of 2018 landslide-dammed lakes and nearby faults. Event-location uncertainties are several kilometers; fault geometry and fluid-diffusion parameters require assumptions. The authors conclude the lakes likely triggered the sequence, rather than directly observing causality, and the global implication is modeled potential.
evidence.ai_role: PhaseNet detected P- and S-wave arrivals in continuous seismic records; these detections supported a new 2014–2023 earthquake catalog used to identify and statistically test the local seismicity increase. Coulomb-stress modeling then assessed a possible physical mechanism.

title: Machine learning detects volcanic fingerprints and suggests a northern extratropical signal for the unidentified 1809 eruption
summary: A convolutional neural network trained on idealized Earth-system-model simulations classified eruption occurrence and broad latitude band from global surface-temperature anomalies in the first post-eruption summer. Applied to reanalysis and observational climate records, the method identified major historic events and assigned a northern-extratropical footprint to the unidentified 1809 eruption. The same analysis found that some smaller events leave weaker, less distinguishable temperature signals.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network with explainable-AI relevance mapping
organization: German Climate Computing Center (DKRZ); Max Planck Institute for Meteorology; Center for Climate Physics, Institute for Basic Science; Pusan National University

evidence.tested: A convolutional neural network trained on idealized Earth-system-model simulations classified eruption occurrence and broad latitude band from global surface-temperature anomalies in the first post-eruption summer.
evidence.unknown: The model is trained on idealized simulations with only three broad eruption latitude classes and four sulfur-injection strengths. The 1809 geographic inference is an AI classification of a climate fingerprint, not direct observation of the eruption source; predictions show sensitivity to normalization and differing observational datasets. It should be interpreted as a clue, not a definitive eruption-location determination.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN classified volcanic presence/location using post-eruption temperature patterns; explainability analysis localized climate regions driving those classifications and helped infer the 1809 event’s northern-extratropical footprint from observational/reanalysis data.

title: Self-supervised learning identifies two previously unreported seismic sequences during the Mayotte submarine eruption
summary: A SimSiam self-supervised representation model with t-SNE and DBSCAN clustering explored two months of continuous seismological records from near the Fani Maoré submarine volcano. Researchers identified two previously undocumented multi-day sequences in October–November 2019, each beginning with increased volcano-tectonic events and followed by tremor-like, hydroacoustic or mixed signals. The paper describes the sequences as potentially associated with ongoing eruptive activity.
ai_technology: SimSiam self-supervised learning with t-SNE dimensionality reduction and DBSCAN clustering
organization: University of Strasbourg; Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris; NORSAR; University of Haute-Alsace; IFREMER

evidence.tested: A SimSiam self-supervised representation model with t-SNE and DBSCAN clustering explored two months of continuous seismological records from near the Fani Maoré submarine volcano.
evidence.unknown: The event data are from two months in 2019 and a nearby ocean-bottom seismometer; the study does not establish exact event locations or independently prove that each sequence was eruptive. Authors state that instrumental noise cannot be ruled out for some high-energy signals, and describe the volcanic association as potential. It is a peer-reviewed 2025 issue paper published online 2024-10-10.
evidence.ai_role: The self-supervised model constructed signal representations from full continuous seismograms; clustering surfaced two coherent, previously undocumented temporal event sequences that the researchers then interpreted using expert signal review. This avoids treating the result as a detector-only tool release.

title: GPU phase folding and deep learning identify five statistically validated ultra-short-period sub-Earth planets in Kepler data
summary: A GPU-based transit search paired with a convolutional neural network identified five sub-Earth-size ultra-short-period transit signals in Kepler light curves: Kepler-158d, Kepler-963c, Kepler-879c, Kepler-1489c, and KOI-4978.02. The authors applied transit vetting, false-alarm tests, and statistical false-positive probabilities below 1% to each, and statistically validated the five signals as planets. The validation is photometric/statistical rather than independent radial-velocity or spectroscopic confirmation; KOI-4978.02 remains designated as a KOI object in the source.
ai_technology: GPFC algorithm: GPU phase folding with convolutional neural network transit scoring
organization: Shanghai Astronomical Observatory; Stanford University; Princeton University; University of Geneva

evidence.tested: A GPU-based transit search paired with a convolutional neural network identified five sub-Earth-size ultra-short-period transit signals in Kepler light curves: Kepler-158d, Kepler-963c, Kepler-879c, Kepler-1489c, and KOI-4978.02.
evidence.unknown: The paper calls the five objects statistically validated, not all independently confirmed by spectroscopy or radial velocities. Validation relies on Kepler photometry, transit vetting, estimated false-positive probabilities and false-alarm tests. KOI-4978.02 retains its KOI designation. One paper-level result; individual planets are not split into separate entries.
evidence.ai_role: GPU phase folding searched Kepler light curves and a CNN scored/identified transit-like signals; follow-up statistical and transit-shape tests vetted the model-discovered signals. Authors report FPP below 1% for all five.

title: Generative machine learning guides experimental synthesis of LiZn₂Pt and NiPt₂Ga Heusler phases
summary: Researchers combined a generative probabilistic crystal-graph model (PGCGM) with an ALIGNN stability predictor to propose and screen ternary structures, then used the model outputs to guide synthesis. They experimentally synthesized phase-pure LiZn₂Pt and NiPt₂Ga; the measured NiPt₂Ga adopts a tetragonal Heusler structure rather than the model’s cubic proposal, with DFT comparisons supporting its lower energy. They also synthesized LiZn₂Pd as a human-selected follow-up that was not among PGCGM’s candidate outputs. This is one paper-level AI-enabled synthesis workflow and three related compounds, not three separate records.
ai_technology: PGCGM generative Wasserstein GAN for ternary crystal structures; ALIGNN graph neural network for decomposition-enthalpy stability screening
organization: Johns Hopkins University; Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory; Gdansk University of Technology

evidence.tested: Researchers combined a generative probabilistic crystal-graph model (PGCGM) with an ALIGNN stability predictor to propose and screen ternary structures, then used the model outputs to guide synthesis.
evidence.unknown: The reported synthesis outcome is experimentally characterized in the paper, but the AI was a candidate-generation and stability-screening aid rather than an autonomous discoverer: expert chemistry selected candidates and performed synthesis. LiZn₂Pt’s composition and Fm3̄m structure were already represented in Materials Project/OQMD training data, so its novelty is experimental realization rather than structure invention. The NiPt₂Ga experimental structure is tetragonal P4/mmm, differing from the cubic PGCGM proposal; the paper gives a DFT energy comparison. No superconductivity was observed, and magnetic ordering temperature for NiPt₂Ga was unresolved.
evidence.ai_role: PGCGM generated candidate crystal structures and ALIGNN screened their predicted stability. Researchers used these model outputs to down-select and choose Heusler-family candidates for synthesis. The authors note that expert judgment remained necessary and that LiZn₂Pt’s composition/structure appeared in the model training databases; NiPt₂Ga’s experimentally realized tetragonal structure was not the exact cubic structure proposed by PGCGM.

title: AI- and DFT-guided synthesis identifies a previously unreported calcium-ruthenate phase
summary: An autonomous materials-discovery workflow used AI-feedback density-functional-theory simulations to select six previously well-explored ternary oxide systems for synthesis. In the Ca–Ru–O campaign, experiments yielded two previously unreported phases; room-temperature diffraction and follow-up characterization most clearly support an isolated low-temperature calcium-rich phase, approximately Ca1+xRuO3+y, distinct from conventional CaRuO3. The authors state the realized phases were not the specific crystal structures predicted by the simulation.
ai_technology: CAMD (computer-aided materials discovery), an AI-feedback density-functional-theory phase-search workflow
organization: Toyota Research Institute; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; University of California, Berkeley; North Carolina State University; Lucideon

evidence.tested: An autonomous materials-discovery workflow used AI-feedback density-functional-theory simulations to select six previously well-explored ternary oxide systems for synthesis.
evidence.unknown: One low-temperature phase was isolated and extensively characterized; the second high-temperature phase remained multiphase/metastable and structurally unresolved, so this record rests on the better-supported low-temperature result. Exact composition and location of excess Ca remain under investigation. AI/DFT guided chemical-system selection but did not correctly predict the realized phase structure; authors report only one successful system among six and do not claim AI accelerated the overall process.
evidence.ai_role: CAMD mapped candidate phases across chemical systems and informed expert down-selection. Human researchers designed and ran synthesis and characterization. The successful calcium-ruthenate phases emerged experimentally in the AI-prioritized system but did not match the exact predicted crystal structures; authors describe one success among six systems and stress current AI-guided synthesis limitations.

title: XLuminA computationally discovers a super-resolution microscopy blueprint combining two optical principles
summary: The XLuminA differentiable optical-design system rediscovered established STED beam shaping and optical-vortex approaches, then identified a previously unreported experimental blueprint combining principles from both to produce sub-diffraction imaging in the study’s computational model. This is a specific theoretical/optical-design result, not a report of an independently built and experimentally validated microscope implementing the new blueprint.
ai_technology: XLuminA auto-differentiating optical experiment-design framework; transformer-based code-generation model used in the discovery workflow
organization: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light; Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg

evidence.tested: The XLuminA differentiable optical-design system rediscovered established STED beam shaping and optical-vortex approaches, then identified a previously unreported experimental blueprint combining principles from both to produce sub-diffraction imaging in the study’s computational model.
evidence.unknown: The novel design is established through computational optical modeling and simulation; the paper does not report physical construction or experimental validation of this specific blueprint. The three rediscovered designs are prior work and are not counted as new. Interpret as a computationally proposed optical design, not a demonstrated imaging instrument or biological discovery.
evidence.ai_role: AI-guided computational search generated and evaluated candidate optical experimental designs; numerical simulations identified a previously unreported combination of optical principles with predicted sub-diffraction capability. Researchers analyzed and interpreted the design.

title: Autonomous BTSbot-nearby follow-up captures an infant supernova’s flash spectrum and constrains progenitor mass loss
summary: The BTSbot-nearby system used the BTSbot machine-learning classifier to identify SN 2024jlf in ZTF data and autonomously trigger a spectroscopic follow-up request, enabling spectroscopy about 0.7 days after first light. The early spectra showed short-lived Hα, He II and C IV flash-ionization features; comparison with two radiative-hydrodynamics model grids constrained the red-supergiant progenitor’s enhanced pre-explosion mass-loss rate to roughly 10⁻⁴–10⁻³ solar masses per year.
ai_technology: BTSbot machine-learning transient classifier integrated with the BTSbot-nearby autonomous follow-up program
organization: Northwestern University; California Institute of Technology; Stockholm University; Liverpool John Moores University; NSF-Simons AI Institute for the Sky; Zwicky Transient Facility collaboration

evidence.tested: The BTSbot-nearby system used the BTSbot machine-learning classifier to identify SN 2024jlf in ZTF data and autonomously trigger a spectroscopic follow-up request, enabling spectroscopy about 0.7 days after first light.
evidence.unknown: The AI contribution is event identification and automated prioritization, not inference of the stellar mass-loss physics. The rate is model-dependent and derived from two radiative-hydrodynamics code grids under adopted wind assumptions. The paper reports an individual nearby Type IIP event; this is not a population-level claim. The transient was originally reported to the Transient Name Server by a human observer, while the BTSbot-nearby program supplied rapid automated follow-up.
evidence.ai_role: BTSbot identified the transient in ZTF alert data; host-distance and youth filters in BTSbot-nearby automatically triggered target-of-opportunity spectroscopy. This shortened latency to approximately seven minutes from alert-filter pass to first spectrum (spectroscopy was obtained about 0.7 days after first light), enabling observation of ephemeral flash features. Human and instrument teams obtained/interpreted observations; radiation-hydrodynamics models supported the mass-loss inference.

title: Physics-informed retrieval-augmented language model guides synthesis of five previously unreported inorganic crystals
summary: Researchers built PIRAG-LM, which combines a structured knowledge base of experimental synthesis routes, physics-based chemical/structural/thermodynamic similarity retrieval, and LLM route reasoning. In prospective tests, it guided synthesis of five compounds previously unreported in experimental literature: BaMo0.3In0.7O2.95, BaNb0.4In0.6O2.9, Hg[B(CN)4]2, CoCo(CN)6 and SrNb2Fe2(PO4)6. Powder X-ray diffraction patterns were consistent with target phases. This is one paper-level synthesis-planning result, not five separate entries.
ai_technology: PIRAG-LM, physics-informed retrieval-augmented language model, with DeepSeek-V4 used in the structured synthesis-knowledge-base extraction workflow
organization: Soochow University; Zhengzhou University; Fudan University; Hefei National Laboratory

evidence.tested: Researchers built PIRAG-LM, which combines a structured knowledge base of experimental synthesis routes, physics-based chemical/structural/thermodynamic similarity retrieval, and LLM route reasoning.
evidence.unknown: This is a source-checked preprint (not treated as peer-reviewed here). The reported new-compound claims refer to absence from experimental literature and prospective synthesis; PXRD matches support target phase formation, but the paper does not establish broad application performance or independent replication. Experts selected materials and adjusted operational conditions; the system did not autonomously run experiments. Five compounds remain bundled as one paper-level finding.
evidence.ai_role: PIRAG-LM retrieved synthesis precedents by chemical, structural and thermodynamic similarity and proposed synthesis methods, precursors and processing conditions. Experts evaluated routes and refined practical parameters; researchers synthesized and characterized the five target phases. The final route class, precursor logic and main processing sequence generally followed model recommendations.

title: LLM-guided iterative optimization yields a previously unreported Rb3BiI6 perovskite-inspired thin film
summary: A closed-loop materials workflow combined an LLM that distilled synthesis knowledge from papers, high-throughput hyperspectral imaging, and multi-objective Bayesian optimization with experimental feedback. In a demonstration, the team synthesized previously unreported Rb3BiI6 thin films and validated optimized films with optical bandgap analysis and X-ray diffraction. LLM-assisted initialization produced more Pareto-optimal samples and higher hypervolume than matched Latin-hypercube initialization in the reported paired campaign.
ai_technology: LLM-assisted synthesis-knowledge extraction and initialization with multi-objective Bayesian optimization and high-throughput hyperspectral imaging
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Toyota Research Institute; University of Tokyo

evidence.tested: A closed-loop materials workflow combined an LLM that distilled synthesis knowledge from papers, high-throughput hyperspectral imaging, and multi-objective Bayesian optimization with experimental feedback.
evidence.unknown: This is a preprint. The specific Rb3BiI6 result is reported as a previously unreported compound experimentally synthesized as thin films and checked by XRD and optical bandgap analysis; the study does not establish independent replication, long-term stability or device performance. Do not treat the accompanying optimization benchmark as an independent discovery.
evidence.ai_role: The LLM distilled literature synthesis expertise and initialized candidate experimental choices; Bayesian optimization iteratively selected subsequent conditions based on measured hyperspectral outcomes. Human operators synthesized thin films and performed optical/XRD validation.

title: AI-guided proof search solves five open problems in Banach space theory
summary: A research project used ChatGPT 5.5 Pro and Codex agents to develop proof ideas and proofs for five Banach-space problems. The resulting paper gives affirmative solutions to questions on toroidal Elton–Odell separation, non-Calkin unital Banach algebras, strict cosingularity and adjoints, weakly compact basis factorization, and primariness of Lp(L1). The authors report that models generated the core mathematics; human mathematicians checked and refined the proofs. The results are presented in an unrefereed preprint, and the authors take responsibility for correctness.
ai_technology: ChatGPT 5.5 Pro and Codex agents using an automated open-problem search pipeline
organization: Lancaster University; University of Bern

evidence.tested: A research project used ChatGPT 5.5 Pro and Codex agents to develop proof ideas and proofs for five Banach-space problems.
evidence.unknown: Unrefereed arXiv preprint. Authors state that humans verified and refined the proofs and are responsible for correctness; the proofs are not formally machine-checked. The five problems were selected by mathematicians, while a separate pipeline component automatically found other candidate problems. The five results remain bundled as one paper-level report.
evidence.ai_role: In the pipeline component, agents searched arXiv literature for open problems and attempted solutions. For the five selected Banach-space problems, the authors say model attempts generated the proof ideas and essentially complete arguments before human verification, editing and integration; models were not limited to exposition.

title: Deep-learning seismic catalog reveals a potentially reactivated blind fault in Taiwan’s 2025 Dapu earthquake sequence
summary: A RED-PAN deep-learning phase picker enabled a catalog of 6,805 relocated events for the 11-day sequence following the M6.4 Dapu earthquake. Analysis of those events, focal mechanisms and velocity structure identified an east-dipping plane at about 5–10 km and a west-dipping plane at about 10–15 km; the authors infer the mainshock involved a previously unrecognized blind west-dipping fault and interactions with the known Muchiliao–Liuchia system. This is a localized structural interpretation, and the authors describe some fault associations as potential.
ai_technology: RED-PAN deep-learning seismic phase picker
organization: Academia Sinica; National Central University; National Taiwan University; Central Weather Administration of Taiwan

evidence.tested: A RED-PAN deep-learning phase picker enabled a catalog of 6,805 relocated events for the 11-day sequence following the M6.4 Dapu earthquake.
evidence.unknown: Peer-reviewed open-access short report. The principal west-dipping plane is interpreted as a potentially reactivated, previously unmapped blind fault; the paper calls some extended activity potential and recommends further monitoring. It is one earthquake sequence and the AI created the event catalog rather than independently deriving the tectonic model. A companion WTMA paper (DOI 10.1007/s44195-025-00095-9) analyzes the same Dapu sequence and similar two-plane geometry; it is a related, partly overlapping report and is not counted separately.
evidence.ai_role: RED-PAN detected P- and S-wave arrivals from continuous seismic recordings and supported event association and catalog construction; this catalog provided the relocated aftershock distribution used with focal mechanisms and velocity profiles to infer fault geometry. The fault interpretation itself involved human analysis, not an autonomous AI conclusion.

title: Euclid and machine-learning selection identify 31 spectroscopically confirmed quasars at redshift 6.6–7.8
summary: Using Euclid Wide Survey photometry over about 3,000 square degrees, the team applied several photometric selection methods, including XGBoost classifiers and probabilistic modeling, then obtained telescope spectra for candidates. Spectroscopy confirmed 31 new quasars at redshifts 6.6–7.8; 12 are at z≥7, and the paper reports EUCL J172902.75+641018.1 at z≈7.77 as the highest-redshift quasar known at publication. The sample extends quasar studies to fainter luminosities at z>7.
ai_technology: XGBoost machine-learning classifiers and Extreme-Deconvolution high-redshift quasar selection, alongside probabilistic spectral-energy-distribution methods
organization: Euclid Consortium; Leiden University; University of Michigan; University of Arizona; Max Planck Institute for Astronomy; University of California, Santa Barbara; international telescope partners

evidence.tested: Using Euclid Wide Survey photometry over about 3,000 square degrees, the team applied several photometric selection methods, including XGBoost classifiers and probabilistic modeling, then obtained telescope spectra for candidates.
evidence.unknown: Peer-reviewed Euclid Consortium study. Candidate ranking was AI-assisted, but human review and spectroscopic follow-up were essential to confirmation. The redshift record is the authors’ claim at the article’s publication date, not a claim about the present-day record. This is one paper-level sample of 31 confirmed quasars; candidate lists and the 31 individual objects are not separate entries.
evidence.ai_role: Multiple photometric selection methods ranked high-redshift quasar candidates from Euclid colors; XGBoost estimated quasar probabilities and redshifts. Humans visually removed artifacts and prioritized follow-up, and Keck, Magellan and LBT spectra established the 31 quasar identifications.

title: EarthLink identifies an eight-month predictor set for Atlantic Niño hindcasts
summary: On an open-ended climate-analysis task, the EarthLink agent autonomously selected two Atlantic-internal predictors for the summer ATL3 index at an eight-month lead: the SON-to-November tendency of the equatorial east–west sea-level-pressure gradient and November western-equatorial-Atlantic sea level as a thermocline-tilt proxy. Rolling-origin hindcasts for 1995–2023 achieved a temporal correlation of about 0.46, above persistence (~0.13) and ENSO-only baselines. The paper proposes a Kelvin-wave/Bjerknes-feedback explanation for the association.
ai_technology: EarthLink multi-agent AI research system based on foundation language models and climate data/tools
organization: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory; Fudan University; Institute of Atmospheric Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology; Ocean University of China; Columbia University

evidence.tested: On an open-ended climate-analysis task, the EarthLink agent autonomously selected two Atlantic-internal predictors for the summer ATL3 index at an eight-month lead: the SON-to-November tendency of the equatorial east–west sea-level-pressure gradient and November western-equatorial-Atlantic sea level as a thermocline-tilt proxy.
evidence.unknown: This is an unrefereed arXiv preprint and a retrospective rolling-origin hindcast from one observational/reanalysis data setup. The physical pathway is an AI-generated, testable hypothesis that the authors explicitly say requires further validation; the source does not establish a causal mechanism or demonstrated prospective operational forecast. Skill is ~0.46 and falls short of the authors’ 0.5 target.
evidence.ai_role: Given an open-ended Atlantic Niño precursor problem, EarthLink autonomously planned analyses, generated code, tested predictors using regression models, reviewed literature and synthesized a physical mechanism. The paper states the proposed AI-generated hypothesis needs further validation.

title: Unsupervised seismicity categories distinguish documented preparatory phases before three large earthquakes
summary: A K-means framework grouped earthquake families by catalog-derived spatial, temporal, magnitude and seismo-mechanical features. Retrospective analyses found highly localized families with higher interaction and strain release before the 2023 Kahramanmaraş, 2009 L’Aquila and 2014 Iquique earthquakes; similar critical categories were absent before the 2016 Amatrice and 2024 Noto events, where no catalog-visible preparatory phase was detected. The work describes a conditional diagnostic, not a general earthquake prediction system.
