summary: Machine-learning screening and expert down-selection identified Ba–Sr cerate oxide compositions for synthesis. The researchers used an automated rapid-sintering and dielectric-characterization platform and reported X-ray diffraction evidence of single-phase solid-solution specimens with refined orthorhombic Pnma structures. The finding is an experimental validation of selected ML-predicted compositions and a process-structure result; it does not establish device performance or broad predictive success.
ai_technology: Gradient-boosting perovskite classifier; VAE and composition-embedding screening
organization: Queen Mary University of London; QinetiQ

evidence.tested: Machine-learning screening and expert down-selection identified Ba–Sr cerate oxide compositions for synthesis.
evidence.unknown: The paper experimentally reports selected ML-predicted Ba–Sr cerate compositions as single-phase by XRD and refines their structures, while additional tested compositions showed multiple phases; ML prediction alone did not guarantee synthesis. The text is inconsistent about the Sr fraction for one reported specimen (abstract/table/figure versus one results sentence), so this entry avoids assigning that composition. The paper validates selected members of a prior predicted set rather than claiming a universal synthesis predictor. Dielectric analysis is reported, but no application/device performance is established.
evidence.ai_role: A gradient-boosting classifier trained on experimental perovskite/non-perovskite structures screened roughly 0.6 million possible compositions, assigning high perovskite likelihood to a candidate set. Variational-autoencoder and element-composition embeddings, plus human literature and synthesis-feasibility review, down-selected compositions that were then synthesized and characterized.

title: Data-science-guided experiments discover a Co–Ta–Sn rutile alloy oxide with tunable transparency and acid-stable electrocatalysis
summary: A high-throughput optical screen and data-science models identified a Co–Ta–Sn composition region whose optical trends indicated phase behavior beyond simple mixtures. Follow-up X-ray diffraction verified a rutile substitutional-alloy oxide, (Sn,Co,Ta)O₂. Composition tuning produced optical transparency and oxygen-evolution electrocatalytic activity with stability in strong-acid electrolyte, as reported by the authors.
ai_technology: Physics-aware data-science phase-diagram and emergent-property models
organization: Google Research; California Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: A high-throughput optical screen and data-science models identified a Co–Ta–Sn composition region whose optical trends indicated phase behavior beyond simple mixtures.
evidence.unknown: The phase inference initially came from optical data and the authors discuss potential false positives from extrinsic film morphology; the selected Co–Ta–Sn rutile phase was followed up and verified by XRD. The optical screen identifies promising regions, not all possible phases, and may miss phases without emergent optical signatures. Reported oxygen-evolution performance and acid stability are laboratory electrocatalysis results; no commercial device or scale-up is established.
evidence.ai_role: Models analyzed high-throughput optical absorption measurements across 376,752 compositions in 108 three-cation oxide systems. They inferred candidate phase diagrams and flagged optical trends inconsistent with lower-order phase mixtures, guiding the Co–Ta–Sn follow-up composition and XRD experiments that verified a rutile alloy phase; this screening also guided catalytic characterization.

title: Machine-learning-guided synthesis realizes four single-phase refractory carbide compositions
summary: A random-forest model ranked new chromium-containing multicomponent carbide compositions by predicted entropy-forming ability. After density-functional calculations and experimental synthesis, X-ray diffraction identified four previously unreported single-phase rock-salt compositions: CrMoNbVWC₅, CrMoNbTaWC₅, CrMoTaVWC₅, and CrMoTiVWC₅. The first three were high-EFA selections; CrMoTiVWC₅ was a medium-EFA composition and required extended annealing to reach chemical homogeneity.
ai_technology: Random-forest models using chemical attributes, with and without CALPHAD thermodynamic features
organization: University of California San Diego; Duke University

evidence.tested: A random-forest model ranked new chromium-containing multicomponent carbide compositions by predicted entropy-forming ability.
evidence.unknown: Only seven of the 70 model-screened candidates were selected for DFT and synthesis, and several tested compositions formed multiple phases. Single-phase identification used XRD and was supported by microstructure, elemental mapping and EBSD; the medium-EFA CrMoTiVWC₅ sample required extended annealing. The paper establishes synthesis and phase formation, not measured application performance or engineering readiness.
evidence.ai_role: The random-forest models learned entropy-forming ability from 56 previously reported carbide compositions and rapidly screened 70 new chromium-containing candidates. Model rankings guided selection of seven compositions for DFT calculations and synthesis; experimental phase outcomes agreed with predicted rankings, including four single-phase materials.

title: Generative machine learning identifies and validates new dual- and tri-phase eutectic compositionally complex alloys
summary: A conditional variational autoencoder generated candidate alloy compositions and an artificial neural network ranked eutectic-forming likelihood. The team experimentally validated previously unreported eutectic compositionally complex alloys across quaternary to senary systems. Reported examples include Al₁₆Cr₁₈Fe₂₄Ni₄₂ with a dual-phase FCC/BCC eutectic lamellar structure and Al₁₁.₃Nb₁₃.₇Co₃₆.₆Cr₈.₂Fe₇.₉Ni₂₂.₃ with a tri-phase FCC/BCC/Laves eutectic structure, supported by XRD, SEM and DSC.
ai_technology: Conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and artificial neural network (ANN)
organization: City University of Hong Kong; Shenzhen University

evidence.tested: A conditional variational autoencoder generated candidate alloy compositions and an artificial neural network ranked eutectic-forming likelihood.
evidence.unknown: The authors report five newly identified ECCA compositions across the studied systems; this is one paper-level result, not five records. The entry names two representative experimentally examined compositions. Validation is limited to the reported arc-melted samples and XRD/SEM/DSC characterization; no long-term mechanical performance or application testing is established. The training data were sparse and imbalanced, and dataset filtering was part of the framework.
evidence.ai_role: A CVAE generated candidate compositions conditioned on eutectic/non-eutectic microstructure labels; an ANN trained on composition and thermodynamics-derived descriptors estimated eutectic-forming likelihood and selected generated candidates for experimental validation. Dataset preprocessing with PCA and K-means addressed class imbalance. The ML pipeline directly proposed the compositions whose eutectic structures were examined experimentally.

title: X-ray machine-learning analysis reveals opposing Cd/Re displacements and Re 5d involvement in Cd₂Re₂O₇ structural order
summary: Unsupervised X-ray diffraction temperature clustering (X-TEC) analyzed high-volume temperature-dependent diffraction data from Cd₂Re₂O₇. The extracted selection rules indicate that Cd and Re displacements are approximately equal in amplitude and opposite in phase, revealing a previously unrecognized involvement of Re 5d electrons in the structural order. The analysis also resolves X-ray diffraction evidence for fluctuations associated with the structural transitions. This is a data-driven interpretation of measured diffraction, not a new direct imaging of atom trajectories.
ai_technology: X-ray diffraction temperature clustering (X-TEC), an interpretable unsupervised machine-learning method using Gaussian-mixture clustering and reciprocal-space label smoothing
organization: Cornell University; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Tennessee, Knoxville; University of Maryland; National Institute of Standards and Technology

evidence.tested: Unsupervised X-ray diffraction temperature clustering (X-TEC) analyzed high-volume temperature-dependent diffraction data from Cd₂Re₂O₇.
evidence.unknown: The displacement relation and Re 5d involvement are physical interpretations inferred from XRD selection rules and X-TEC clustering, not direct atom-by-atom imaging. The work reports XRD evidence for a structural Goldstone mode; it does not claim that all Goldstone-mode physics in Cd₂Re₂O₇ was previously unknown. The findings concern the analyzed crystal and temperature-dependent synchrotron diffraction data.
evidence.ai_role: X-TEC clustered temperature trajectories of diffraction intensities across a high-volume reciprocal-space dataset to identify structural order parameters and weaker diffuse-scattering fluctuations. Its data-driven selection rules exposed the reciprocal-space pattern from which researchers inferred approximately equal, out-of-phase Cd and Re displacements and the Re 5d contribution; the manual crystallographic analysis would have required selecting only a small number of peaks.

title: AI-classified XPCS links local relaxation episodes with bulk stress changes in a colloidal glass
summary: In rheo-XPCS measurements of a sheared silica-nanoparticle glass, an unsupervised convolutional autoencoder and K-means clustering grouped two-time correlation patterns by relative relaxation rate. Changes in the frequencies of slow-dynamics classes tracked non-monotonic shear-stress relaxation, while some later local slow-dynamics episodes appeared without a corresponding change in the bulk stress signal. This is a measured microscopic-to-macroscopic relationship in the study’s model colloidal system.
ai_technology: AI-NERD: convolutional autoencoder for XPCS correlation images with K-means clustering in the learned latent space
organization: Argonne National Laboratory; University of Chicago; University of Illinois Chicago

evidence.tested: In rheo-XPCS measurements of a sheared silica-nanoparticle glass, an unsupervised convolutional autoencoder and K-means clustering grouped two-time correlation patterns by relative relaxation rate.
evidence.unknown: The findings come from rheo-XPCS of a model concentrated silica-nanoparticle suspension under the reported shear/relaxation protocol. Cluster labels encode relative relaxation rates and latent-space distances are not quantitative physical measures. The authors describe the stress/dynamics relationship qualitatively and say further work is needed to extract quantitative physical information. A publisher correction dated 2024-09-09 corrected corresponding-author information; it did not report a change to the results.
evidence.ai_role: The unsupervised neural autoencoder compressed experimental two-time X-ray photon correlation functions into a latent representation, then K-means grouped frames by dynamical similarity. Class-transition frequencies over experimental time let researchers compare local relaxation patterns with simultaneous rheometer stress measurements, revealing where local slow dynamics coincided with stress minima and where they did not.

title: Deep learning detects an emerging anthropogenic warming fingerprint in daily precipitation
summary: A convolutional neural network trained on 80 CESM2 large-ensemble members detected an emerging climate-change signal in observed daily precipitation fields. Across four satellite, merged-observation and reanalysis products, the model’s annual estimated global-mean temperature exceeded the historical internal-variability range from the mid-2010s onward. The signal was driven mainly by precipitation variability on timescales shorter than 10 days, with hotspots including the tropical eastern Pacific and mid-latitude storm tracks; rain-gauge checks over the eastern United States were consistent with the increase in high-frequency variability.
ai_technology: Deep detection (DD) convolutional neural network
organization: Chonnam National University; Pohang University of Science and Technology; University of Washington; University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa; Institute for Basic Science; Pusan National University

evidence.tested: A convolutional neural network trained on 80 CESM2 large-ensemble members detected an emerging climate-change signal in observed daily precipitation fields.
evidence.unknown: This is an observational detection and attribution result using a CNN trained on climate-model simulations; it is not a direct causal experiment or a forecast of individual storms. The long-term mean precipitation change remained indistinguishable from natural variability in the analysis. Precipitation products disagree in some estimates, especially where direct ocean measurements are sparse, and the reported hotspots depend on the selected datasets and attribution methods. The paper reports an emerging signal beginning in the mid-2010s, not a uniform increase in all regions or at every timescale.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN was trained on paired daily precipitation anomaly maps and annual global-mean surface-air-temperature values from 80 CESM2 Large Ensemble members. Applied to observed precipitation products, it learned spatial and temporal patterns that predicted the warming metric and exposed an emergent signal that conventional linear detection did not resolve. Explainability analyses (occlusion sensitivity, with SHAP and integrated-gradients checks) localized the strongest contributions to high-frequency precipitation variability.

title: Autonomous microscopy discovers an edge plasmon in layered MnPS₃
summary: Deep-kernel-learning-guided STEM-EELS measurements identified a low-energy edge-localized plasmon response in the layered antiferromagnet MnPS₃, distinct from the higher-energy bulk plasmon response. The system used local structure to predict spectra and uncertainty, then autonomously selected where to measure based on a physics-defined objective. After 10–25 spectra, about 1% of the image-space points, it localized the edge mode to the flake boundary.
ai_technology: Deep kernel learning (feed-forward neural-network feature embedding with a Gaussian-process kernel and physics-based acquisition/scalarizer)
organization: Oak Ridge National Laboratory; University of Tennessee, Knoxville

evidence.tested: Deep-kernel-learning-guided STEM-EELS measurements identified a low-energy edge-localized plasmon response in the layered antiferromagnet MnPS₃, distinct from the higher-energy bulk plasmon response.
evidence.unknown: The paper demonstrates the mode in the reported exfoliated MnPS₃ flake and STEM-EELS setup. The physical search objective was supplied by researchers (a spectral feature below the bulk-plasmon peak), so the AI did not independently formulate the scientific question. The authors report that the edge response varied with local boundary shape and present this as a proof-of-concept discovery workflow, not a complete theory of MnPS₃ plasmon behavior.
evidence.ai_role: The model learned a structure-to-electron-energy-loss-spectrum relationship from sequential measurements and used its predicted response and uncertainty to choose subsequent STEM probe locations. A user-specified spectral scalarizer prioritized a low-energy feature relative to the bulk plasmon; the closed-loop instrument then discovered and mapped an edge-localized response without pretraining on MnPS₃ sample data.

title: Machine-learning-assisted neutron scattering shows hydrostatic pressure tunes interactions in spin ice
summary: Machine-learning-assisted analysis of diffuse neutron scattering from Dy₂Ti₂O₇ at ambient pressure and about 1.3 GPa extracted pressure-dependent Hamiltonian parameters and found that hydrostatic pressure modifies further-neighbor magnetic interactions and the material’s nanoscale magnetic-glass ordering. The analysis supports using pressure to tune the spin-ice glass state. A transition at substantially higher pressure is a model-based prediction, not an observed transition in this experiment.
ai_technology: Nonlinear autoencoder, radial-basis generative surrogate and hierarchical clustering for neutron-scattering analysis
organization: Oak Ridge National Laboratory; Argonne National Laboratory; Instituto de Física de Líquidos y Sistemas Biológicos, UNLP-CONICET

evidence.tested: Machine-learning-assisted analysis of diffuse neutron scattering from Dy₂Ti₂O₇ at ambient pressure and about 1.3 GPa extracted pressure-dependent Hamiltonian parameters and found that hydrostatic pressure modifies further-neighbor magnetic interactions and the material’s nanoscale magnetic-glass ordering.
evidence.unknown: The reported pressure comparison is between ambient pressure and an estimated hydrostatic pressure of about 1.3 GPa, using separate measurement setups. The change in magnetic couplings and glass morphology is inferred by fitting a spin model to scattering with ML-assisted analysis, not measured as a direct microscopic coupling. The authors predict that substantially higher pressure may induce a phase transition; no such transition was observed here. Some analysis and experimental steering remained manual.
evidence.ai_role: The nonlinear autoencoder compressed measured and simulated diffuse neutron-scattering volumes; a trained generative surrogate enabled fast forward prediction of scattering from spin-Hamiltonian parameters, while clustering and inverse mapping constrained parameters against the experiment. Those ML components made it practical to analyze pressure-dependent measurements and infer the change in further-neighbor couplings during the neutron experiment workflow.

title: Random-forest alert screening leads to spectroscopic confirmation of four changing-look AGNs
summary: A hierarchical random-forest classifier in the ALeRCE broker applied to Zwicky Transient Facility alert-stream light curves helped select candidate changing-look active galactic nuclei from objects previously classified as type 2. New spectra confirmed significant changes in broad Balmer emission in four of six observed candidates, establishing new type 2-to-type 1 transitions. The other two observed objects had only tentative evidence and are not counted as confirmed transitions.
ai_technology: ALeRCE light-curve classifier (hierarchical imbalanced random forest)
organization: Universidad de Valparaíso; Universidad de Chile; European Southern Observatory; Millennium Institute of Astrophysics; California Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: A hierarchical random-forest classifier in the ALeRCE broker applied to Zwicky Transient Facility alert-stream light curves helped select candidate changing-look active galactic nuclei from objects previously classified as type 2.
evidence.unknown: Only six of the 30 visually retained candidates received new spectra in this paper, selected partly for observability; four showed clear >3σ broad-line changes and two were tentative. Thus the reported ≥66% success rate is a small, selected follow-up sample, not an unbiased prevalence estimate. The authors note possible 30–50% misclassification in the parent type-2 sample and that the ZTF alert threshold makes the method incomplete.
evidence.ai_role: The ALeRCE random-forest classifier used variability features from ZTF light curves and ZTF/AllWISE photometric colors to classify alert sources as AGN-like. Its classifications were cross-matched against a pre-existing spectroscopic type-2 AGN sample to produce candidates with current type-1-like variability; this AI-assisted shortlist enabled follow-up spectroscopy that confirmed the transitions.

title: Bayesian search and synthesis reveal a high-anisotropy [Fe/Co/Fe/Ni]₁₃ multilayer
summary: A first-principles and Bayesian-optimization workflow selected [Fe/Co/Fe/Ni]₁₃ for experimental fabrication from four-element, four-layer-period magnetic multilayer candidates. The researchers grew the repeated monoatomic-layer structure and measured it with X-ray diffraction and SQUID magnetometry. They report a magnetic anisotropy constant of 374 kJ m⁻³ and saturation magnetization of 1313 emu cm⁻³, and identify the material as a new ferromagnetic multilayer with reported magnetocrystalline anisotropy exceeding L1₀ FeNi and FeCo benchmarks.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization with expected-improvement acquisition and a Matérn 5/2 kernel, coupled to first-principles magnetic-anisotropy calculations
organization: Tokyo University of Science; National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS)

evidence.tested: A first-principles and Bayesian-optimization workflow selected [Fe/Co/Fe/Ni]₁₃ for experimental fabrication from four-element, four-layer-period magnetic multilayer candidates.
evidence.unknown: This is a proof-of-concept search over a restricted four-element, four-layer-period design space; the best candidate required 52 monoatomic layers in its repeated stack. The sample’s measured spontaneous easy axis remained in-plane and its shape-corrected effective anisotropy was negative, even though the authors report a large intrinsic magnetocrystalline-anisotropy value. Their proposed local perpendicular domains were a hypothesis requiring microscopy follow-up. The study does not establish a practical permanent magnet or device.
evidence.ai_role: The model sequentially used first-principles magnetocrystalline-anisotropy calculations to rank discrete layer sequences and search for high-anisotropy multilayers. The top three candidates were fabricated and characterized; the resulting [Fe/Co/Fe/Ni]₁₃ experimental sample gave the paper’s highest measured anisotropy and saturation magnetization among the three. This ML-guided candidate selection and iterative calculation materially directed the new synthesis.

title: Autonomous ML search and experiments find Fe–Co–Ir/Pt alloys above the Slater–Pauling magnetization limit
summary: A game-tree search using Gaussian-process predictions and first-principles calculations proposed dilute Ir and Pt additions as a counterintuitive way to raise Fe–Co magnetization. Combinatorial sputtering and magnetic measurements experimentally found Fe–Co–Ir and Fe–Co–Pt compositions with magnetization exceeding the conventional Fe₃Co₁ Slater–Pauling limit; the highest-moment points reported in the ternary maps were near Fe₈₁Co₁₅Ir₄ and Fe₈₅Co₁₁Pt₄. The study’s calculations attribute the effect to Ir/Pt-induced increases in local Fe and Co moments.
ai_technology: Autonomous materials search using a Gaussian-process regression model with game-tree search and an upper-confidence-bound acquisition rule, coupled to KKR-CPA first-principles calculations
organization: NEC Corporation; National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST); Tohoku University; University of Tokyo; Japan Atomic Energy Agency

evidence.tested: A game-tree search using Gaussian-process predictions and first-principles calculations proposed dilute Ir and Pt additions as a counterintuitive way to raise Fe–Co magnetization.
evidence.unknown: The highest-moment composition suggested by the autonomous search (Fe₈₂Co₁₃Ir₄Pt₁) was not itself the maximum in the measured ternary composition spreads; the Fe–Co–Ir and Fe–Co–Pt maps identified different peak compositions. The finding is based on sputtered, annealed thin-film composition spreads and room-temperature MOKE/SQUID measurements, not bulk ingots or device testing. The eight-element search space was narrowed by preliminary calculations. KKR-CPA results assume ideal disordered bulk states at 0 K, unlike the film measurements.
evidence.ai_role: The autonomous system iteratively selected compositions in an eight-component disordered-alloy search using ab-initio magnetic-moment estimates and a game-tree Gaussian-process model balancing exploration and exploitation. After about 43 days it proposed Fe₈₂Co₁₃Ir₄Pt₁; that hypothesis directed combinatorial synthesis and testing of Fe–Co–Ir and Fe–Co–Pt spreads. The follow-up measurements found compositions surpassing the prior Fe₃Co₁ benchmark and motivated theoretical analysis of impurity-enhanced Fe/Co local moments.

title: Real-time discovery and characterization of AT2020xnd, an AT2018cow-like fast transient
summary: ZTF observations identified AT2020xnd (ZTF20acigmel) at redshift 0.243 as the first unambiguous AT2018cow analogue found and confirmed in real time. Follow-up showed a rapid optical rise, persistently hot blue emission, luminous radio, millimetre and X-ray output, no classical radioactive-supernova peak, and a dwarf-galaxy host. The authors argue that these properties support a distinct fast-blue-optical-transient phenomenon, while its progenitor and central engine remain uncertain.
ai_technology: Zwicky Transient Facility real-time alert stream with a deep-learning real-bogus classifier and a custom contextual transient filter
organization: Zwicky Transient Facility collaboration; California Institute of Technology; Liverpool John Moores University; University of California, Berkeley; collaborating observatories

evidence.tested: ZTF observations identified AT2020xnd (ZTF20acigmel) at redshift 0.243 as the first unambiguous AT2018cow analogue found and confirmed in real time.
evidence.unknown: This is one transient and a small class comparison, not a general population measurement. The AI contribution was alert filtering, not autonomous physical interpretation or confirmation; telescope follow-up was essential. The suggested distinct phenomenon is supported by shared observed properties, while the progenitor/engine interpretation remains unresolved and model-dependent.
evidence.ai_role: The paper’s custom search filter required the ZTF alert’s deep-learning real-bogus score to exceed 0.65, along with repeated detections, a high Galactic latitude and no coincident stellar counterpart. This AI-based alert filtering contributed to selecting AT2020xnd in real time; rapid multiband photometry and spectroscopic and multiwavelength human follow-up established its astrophysical nature and unusual properties.

title: Machine-learning-guided experiments identify a high-power-factor PbSe:SnSb thermoelectric family
summary: A closed-loop error-correction learning workflow guided synthesis of PbSe alloyed with SnSb and documented a previously unexplored low-temperature thermoelectric family. At 300 K, the best tested composition, 2 wt% SnSb-doped PbSe, had a measured power factor above 850 µW mK⁻² and more than twice that of PbSe. Density-functional calculations attribute the modeled transport improvement to Sn/Sb interactions that reduce hole effective mass.
ai_technology: Closed-loop error-correction learning with a neural-network update to a prior materials-property model; composition representations compared included Magpie, Roost and CrabNet
organization: University of Toronto; King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)

evidence.tested: A closed-loop error-correction learning workflow guided synthesis of PbSe alloyed with SnSb and documented a previously unexplored low-temperature thermoelectric family.
evidence.unknown: The result is specific to the tested powder-processing, composition and measurement protocol, including synthesis below 300 °C; it is not evidence of device-level or commercial performance. The reported mechanism for the increased power factor is supported by DFT calculations, not a direct measurement of carrier effective mass. The paper compares the 2 wt% composition with PbSe and reports more than 2× power factor at room temperature.
evidence.ai_role: A model trained on published experimental thermoelectric data ranked candidate compositions, and a dense neural-network error-correction model incorporated local experimental comparisons to adapt predictions to the authors’ synthesis and measurement conditions. Iterative model-guided experiments selected the PbSe:SnSb family and 2 wt% SnSb-doped PbSe for characterization. AI supplied composition down-selection and adaptive experiment guidance; the authors synthesized and measured the samples.

title: Machine-learning-guided Fe₂P-type alloys reach cryogenic magnetocaloric temperatures without rare earths
summary: An artificial neural network trained on reported experimental compositions guided optimization of Fe₂P-type Mn–Fe–P–Si alloys for sub-77 K magnetocaloric use. Experiments measured a 97 K transition for Mn₁.₇₀Fe₀.₃₀P₀.₆₃Si₀.₃₇ at 1 T; replacing a small fraction of Fe with Co lowered the transition to 73 K. The Co-containing composition showed a 7.5 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ magnetic entropy change and a 1.4 K reversible adiabatic temperature change under a 0–5 T field.
ai_technology: Artificial neural network trained on a curated, literature-mined dataset of experimental Fe₂P-type magnetocaloric compounds
organization: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS); South China Normal University

evidence.tested: An artificial neural network trained on reported experimental compositions guided optimization of Fe₂P-type Mn–Fe–P–Si alloys for sub-77 K magnetocaloric use.
evidence.unknown: The reported compositions are rare-earth-free but still contain transition metals and phosphorus/silicon; results characterize laboratory alloys and do not establish a working hydrogen-liquefaction refrigerator. The 73 K transition requires Co substitution and is reported with a modest reduction in magnetization. The 1.4 K reversible adiabatic change is measured over 0–5 T; stated performance and operating window should not be generalized beyond the investigated alloys.
evidence.ai_role: The team mined published experimental composition/property results to train an artificial neural network for composition optimization toward lower transition temperatures. Predictions guided selection of Mn₁.₇₀Fe₀.₃₀P₀.₆₃Si₀.₃₇, then a minor Co-for-Fe substitution was tested experimentally to reduce its transition temperature below 77 K. AI guided composition selection; the reported magnetic and caloric properties came from measurements on synthesized samples.

title: Explainable neural-network analysis isolates aerosol-sensitive regional climate signals in CESM1
summary: Using explainable AI on single-forcing CESM1 large ensembles, the study identified the North Atlantic, Southern Ocean and Southeast Asia as key regional temperature patterns for dating the climate simulations, particularly before the early 21st century. When applied to reanalysis observations, the neural network trained on an ensemble with industrial aerosols fixed at 1920 levels predicted the actual year more closely than networks trained on the all-forcing or greenhouse-gas-fixed ensembles. The authors interpret this as evidence that simulated regional temperature signals are sensitive to aerosol forcing.
ai_technology: Artificial neural network trained on CESM1 single-forcing and all-forcing large ensembles, interpreted using layer-wise relevance propagation and an uncertainty mask
organization: Colorado State University; National Center for Atmospheric Research; collaborators

evidence.tested: Using explainable AI on single-forcing CESM1 large ensembles, the study identified the North Atlantic, Southern Ocean and Southeast Asia as key regional temperature patterns for dating the climate simulations, particularly before the early 21st century.
evidence.unknown: This is a model-based attribution analysis from one climate model (CESM1) and historical/RCP8.5 simulations, with reanalysis used for evaluation; it is not a direct experiment or causal attribution of every observed regional trend. The relevance maps identify patterns useful to the trained network and do not by themselves prove a physical mechanism. The authors discuss other forcings, feedbacks and internal variability, and the net influence of aerosols remains uncertain.
evidence.ai_role: The ANN learned to predict year from global near-surface-temperature maps in simulations with different combinations of greenhouse-gas and industrial-aerosol forcing. Layer-wise relevance propagation identified regional patterns driving those predictions, and the trained networks were then tested on 20th Century Reanalysis observations. This analysis exposed the model’s aerosol-sensitive regional signal and the higher year-prediction correlation of the network trained with aerosols held at 1920 levels.

title: AI-derived symbolic formula improves dark-matter halo overdensity estimates in a cosmological simulation
summary: A graph neural network trained on a detailed N-body cosmological dark-matter simulation was distilled by symbolic regression into an analytic estimator for a halo’s overdensity from its mass and the masses, positions and velocities of nearby halos. On the analyzed simulation snapshot, the new expression reduced mean absolute error to 0.0882, compared with 0.121 for the authors’ existing hand-designed estimator. The formula’s mass-weighted neighborhood term decreases with separation and includes dependence on the central halo’s mass.
ai_technology: Sparse-representation Graph Neural Network followed by Eureqa genetic-programming symbolic regression
organization: Princeton University; DeepMind; New York University; Flatiron Institute; Carnegie Mellon University

evidence.tested: A graph neural network trained on a detailed N-body cosmological dark-matter simulation was distilled by symbolic regression into an analytic estimator for a halo’s overdensity from its mass and the masses, positions and velocities of nearby halos.
evidence.unknown: The formula was derived and evaluated on a single final-time-step dataset from an N-body simulation (215,854 halos), not validated against observations or independent cosmological simulations. The authors note that some terms’ physical interpretation was unclear and reserved detailed interpretation for future astrophysics work. It is a new useful estimator for the studied simulated halo population, not a confirmed universal law of dark-matter structure.
evidence.ai_role: The team trained a graph neural network to predict dark-matter halo overdensity using a cosmological N-body simulation. L1 regularization encouraged a compact learned message representation; Eureqa symbolic regression then fitted explicit equations to the learned graph-network components and replaced them with a closed-form model. This process yielded a previously unreported analytic halo-environment estimator and enabled comparison against the existing hand-designed formula.

title: Active-learning experiments reveal distinct on-field and off-field polarization-switching behavior in ferroelectrics
summary: An active-learning workflow paired with automated piezoresponse-force microscopy discovered relationships between local ferroelectric domain structure and polarization-switching hysteresis. The experimentally selected sampling paths and points differed substantially between on-field and off-field hysteresis loops, indicating that the two measurement modes are dominated by different mechanisms. This is a bounded result from the reported ferroelectric sample and spectroscopy workflow, not a universal mechanism established for all ferroelectrics.
ai_technology: Machine-learning active-learning framework for automated piezoresponse force microscopy and spectroscopy
organization: Oak Ridge National Laboratory; Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago; Nagoya Institute of Technology and collaborators

evidence.tested: An active-learning workflow paired with automated piezoresponse-force microscopy discovered relationships between local ferroelectric domain structure and polarization-switching hysteresis.
evidence.unknown: The authors report experimental correlation and different on-field/off-field discovery paths, interpreting this as evidence that the measurement modes are dominated by different mechanisms. The study does not establish a universal causal account across materials; it reports a specific automated PFM/spectroscopy investigation.
evidence.ai_role: The model learned correlations between high-dimensional local domain structure and hysteresis-loop switching characteristics, and used loop descriptors and uncertainty to guide the automated microscopy and spectroscopy measurements. Human physics insight was encoded in the acquisition function.

title: Machine learning and ab initio screening predict 60 stable two-dimensional ferroelectric bimetal phosphates
summary: A data-driven machine-learning search combined with high-throughput ab initio calculations screened 2,964 two-dimensional bimetal phosphates and identified 60 computationally stable structures with out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization: 16 predicted ferroelectric metals and 44 predicted ferroelectric semiconductors, including seven predicted multiferroics. The calculations analyze how bimetal displacement can support polarization alongside metallicity. These are theoretical candidates and proposed physical explanations, not experimentally synthesized or measured phases.
ai_technology: Data-driven machine-learning screening with orbital-based descriptors, combined with high-throughput ab initio calculations
organization: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; and collaborators

evidence.tested: A data-driven machine-learning search combined with high-throughput ab initio calculations screened 2,964 two-dimensional bimetal phosphates and identified 60 computationally stable structures with out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization: 16 predicted ferroelectric metals and 44 predicted ferroelectric semiconductors, including seven predicted multiferroics.
evidence.unknown: The 60 phases and their stability and ferroelectric properties are computational predictions from high-throughput ab initio calculations. The paper does not report experimental synthesis or measurement of these predicted structures; practical stability and device behavior remain unverified.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning with newly developed electronic-orbital descriptors enabled systematic screening of 2,964 candidate 2D bimetal phosphates; first-principles calculations evaluated stability, polarization, and electronic structure for the reported candidate family.

title: Deep learning extends the mapped extent of a North Anatolian Fault slow-slip event
summary: A deep convolutional autoencoder trained on synthetic deformation and atmospheric-noise time series recovered millimeter-scale ground motion from real InSAR without being given the fault location. Applied to COSMO-SkyMed observations of the 2013 North Anatolian Fault slow-slip event, it detected about 2 mm of slip beyond the previously identified segment and revised the estimated along-strike event length from about 10 km to 15–20 km. The same paper used the approach to resolve transient millimeter-scale subsidence at California’s Coso geothermal field. This is one paper-level finding enabled by the model’s extraction of deformation signals from noisy satellite data.
ai_technology: Deep convolutional autoencoder trained on synthetic InSAR time series
organization: Los Alamos National Laboratory; École Normale Supérieure; University of California, Santa Cruz and collaborators

evidence.tested: A deep convolutional autoencoder trained on synthetic deformation and atmospheric-noise time series recovered millimeter-scale ground motion from real InSAR without being given the fault location.
evidence.unknown: The newly resolved extension is a reanalysis of an existing 2013 InSAR event, not a newly occurring earthquake. The paper’s reported extension is model-derived; the original expert analysis had detected the larger slow-slip segment, while the autoencoder identifies an additional lower-amplitude portion. The model assumes atmospheric noise characteristics represented by its synthetic training data and omits some noise sources, including ionospheric perturbations. Coso results are a separate application within the same paper and are not counted separately.
evidence.ai_role: The deep autoencoder separated persistent ground deformation patterns from atmospheric noise in real InSAR data without prior fault-location information, resolving the additional 2 mm slow-slip segment; the model was trained on synthetic data and was not fine-tuned on the real case.

title: Machine-learning selection and Gaia astrometry confirm a 62-Jupiter-mass brown dwarf orbiting G 15-6
summary: A machine-learning search of Gaia DR3 two-body astrometric orbits flagged G 15-6 as a likely low-mass companion system. Combining Gaia’s astrometric orbit with archival radial-velocity measurements resolved the inclination ambiguity and yielded a companion mass of 62.43 (+6.16/−5.44) Jupiter masses, firmly in the brown-dwarf range. The authors identify it as the first independently validated brown-dwarf companion selected by their ML method. The radial-velocity data predate the study; the new result is the Gaia orbit and AI-guided identification that resolve the companion mass, not a newly observed companion in 2025.
ai_technology: Semi-supervised anomaly detection, extreme gradient boosting, and random-forest classifiers applied to Gaia DR3 astrometric-orbit solutions
organization: European Space Agency (ESA), European Space Astronomy Centre

evidence.tested: A machine-learning search of Gaia DR3 two-body astrometric orbits flagged G 15-6 as a likely low-mass companion system.
evidence.unknown: The source study is an ML-assisted target-identification and Gaia-orbit analysis, not a 2025 direct detection. Archival radial-velocity observations already established binary motion but did not constrain the inclination enough to prove a substellar mass; Gaia astrometry supplies that missing orbital constraint. The wider candidate list includes false-positive Gaia solutions and unresolved stellar/substellar cases, which are not counted as confirmed companions here.
evidence.ai_role: The machine-learning pipeline ranked Gaia DR3 two-body systems for likely low-mass companions and selected G 15-6 as a brown-dwarf candidate. The Gaia astrometric orbit, combined with the independent archival radial-velocity orbit, resolved the inclination and established the companion’s mass; the models used only the Gaia orbital solutions for their candidate selection.

title: Machine learning identifies seismic tremor precursors to Whakaari eruptions
summary: A structured machine-learning analysis of nine years of Whakaari seismic records identified four-hour energy bursts that occurred hours to days before most of the five major eruptive episodes studied. The authors interpret the pattern as possible charging of the vent hydrothermal system by hot magmatic fluids. In cross-validation, the prototype alert model gave advance warning for four of five unseen eruption instances, including at least four hours before the 2019 eruption.
ai_technology: Structured machine-learning pipeline using engineered seismic time-series features, a random forest, and an alert decision model
organization: University of Auckland; University of Otago

evidence.tested: A structured machine-learning analysis of nine years of Whakaari seismic records identified four-hour energy bursts that occurred hours to days before most of the five major eruptive episodes studied.
evidence.unknown: This is a study of five major eruptive episodes at one volcano. The 4/5 warning result is cross-validation on this historical record, not independent operational validation; the model was described as a prototype. The ensemble alert score is not a calibrated eruption probability, and alert thresholds trade missed events against false alarms. The proposed hydrothermal charging mechanism is an interpretation of the seismic pattern.
evidence.ai_role: The machine-learning pipeline analyzed continuous seismic tremor data, selected precursor patterns, and modeled short-term eruption alerts. Its feature analysis identified the four-hour energy-burst pattern; the proposed hydrothermal charging mechanism is the authors’ geophysical interpretation, not a direct measurement of subsurface fluid movement.

title: Unsupervised seismic clustering reveals distinct drainage signals at Gornergletscher
summary: An unsupervised analysis of five weeks of seismic records from Gornergletscher, Switzerland, separated cryoseismic signals into clusters associated with the 2007 Gornersee lake flood and with afternoon/evening meltwater flow. One high-energy, broadband noise cluster began about two days before the reported onset of subglacial flooding; the authors suggest it captures the earlier initiation of englacial and subglacial drainage and improves the flood chronology.
ai_technology: SpecUFEx unsupervised feature extraction: non-negative matrix factorization, hidden Markov modeling, principal component analysis, and k-means clustering
organization: Columbia University; ETH Zurich; Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research (WSL)

evidence.tested: An unsupervised analysis of five weeks of seismic records from Gornergletscher, Switzerland, separated cryoseismic signals into clusters associated with the 2007 Gornersee lake flood and with afternoon/evening meltwater flow.
evidence.unknown: The analysis covers five weeks at one glacier using the 2007 flood record. The inferred drainage start precedes lake-level evidence by about two days, but the source cannot definitively exclude ice-bed slip, till deformation, or small fractures as explanations for some spectral features. The study interprets cluster timing and spectra as hydrologic signals; it does not directly image subglacial drainage pathways.
evidence.ai_role: The unsupervised learning pipeline reduced seismic spectrograms to fingerprints and grouped similar continuous-noise and icequake signals without labels. Comparing the learned clusters with lake level, GPS, temperature, and event timing exposed distinct clusters associated with lake-flood drainage and daily meltwater flow, which supported the revised drainage chronology.

title: Machine learning isolates aerosol-driven cloud-cover increase after the Holuhraun eruption
summary: Using MODIS satellite observations and a random-forest counterfactual trained on meteorology and non-eruption years, researchers estimated cloud responses to the 2014 Holuhraun volcanic aerosol plume. They found cloud fraction increased by about 10% across the studied region; this change contributed more to the estimated aerosol cooling than the smaller radiative effect from brighter clouds with smaller droplets. The study supplies an observational constraint on aerosol–cloud climate forcing.
ai_technology: Random-forest ML-MODIS surrogate trained on meteorological reanalysis and MODIS satellite data from 2001–2020, excluding the 2014 eruption year
organization: University of Exeter; ETH Zurich; UK Met Office; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; University of Cambridge; University of Leeds

evidence.tested: Using MODIS satellite observations and a random-forest counterfactual trained on meteorology and non-eruption years, researchers estimated cloud responses to the 2014 Holuhraun volcanic aerosol plume.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns one volcanic natural experiment, Holuhraun in 2014, and satellite observations of a North Atlantic/Northern European region. The cloud response is estimated by comparing observations with an ML counterfactual and is not a randomized intervention; it depends on model and MODIS retrieval assumptions. The paper reports about a 10% cloud-cover increase and attributes the leading radiative contribution to cloud fraction, while the droplet-size effect is also present and the liquid-water-path contribution is weak.
evidence.ai_role: The random forest estimated the cloud properties expected under observed meteorological conditions without volcanic aerosol, creating a counterfactual baseline. Comparing these predictions with 2014 MODIS observations let the authors isolate cloud changes associated with the Holuhraun aerosol perturbation from meteorological co-variability and estimate the relative radiative contributions of cloud-fraction, liquid-water-path, and droplet-size changes.

title: Machine learning reveals tropical aerosol-driven cloud expansion despite stronger rainfall
summary: Using satellite observations of four Kīlauea volcanic outgassing episodes in 2008 and 2018, an ML counterfactual analysis found that volcanic aerosols increased cloud cover and reflected sunlight over tropical marine shallow-convective clouds, even as rainfall strengthened. Cloud-cover adjustment contributed about 65% of aerosol–cloud cooling under mixed meteorological conditions and 84–87% in humid conditions; under humid, stable conditions, a 30% increase in droplet number could correspond to up to a 50% relative increase in cloud cover. The result identifies a tropical regime in which aerosol cloud expansion is strong and its response varies with humidity and stability.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning surrogates of MODIS cloud properties, radiative fluxes, and precipitation, trained on 20 years of satellite observations and meteorology while excluding volcanic years 2008 and 2018
organization: University of Exeter; Met Office; ETH Zurich; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; University of Cambridge; University of Leeds; University of Reading

evidence.tested: Using satellite observations of four Kīlauea volcanic outgassing episodes in 2008 and 2018, an ML counterfactual analysis found that volcanic aerosols increased cloud cover and reflected sunlight over tropical marine shallow-convective clouds, even as rainfall strengthened.
evidence.unknown: This is an observational ML-counterfactual analysis of four Kīlauea plume months over tropical marine shallow-convective clouds, not a controlled aerosol intervention or a direct test of deliberate cloud seeding. The source reports strong cloud-cover responses and radiative estimates, especially under humid/stable conditions, but results depend on satellite retrievals and the learned unperturbed baseline. The authors’ proposed mechanism for increased cloud cover alongside stronger rainfall is explicitly a hypothesis requiring further testing; do not treat the marine-cloud-brightening scenario as experimentally demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: The random-forest surrogates estimated unperturbed cloud properties and radiative fluxes for given meteorological conditions. Comparing those counterfactuals with observations in four volcanic plume episodes isolated aerosol-associated signals from meteorological co-variability and enabled estimates of cloud-cover, rainfall, and radiative-forcing responses across distinct tropical meteorological regimes.

title: AI reconstruction extends the 1911 French heatwave signal into September
summary: A partial-convolution U-Net trained on CMIP6 climate simulations and transferred to European station-based extreme indices reconstructed the poorly observed 1911 heatwave. The model estimates that in parts of southern France, more than 40% of September days exceeded the 90th percentile of maximum temperature, extending the heatwave signal into fall. The reconstructed pattern is similar to 20th Century Reanalysis Version 3 and aligns spatially with higher French mortality in 1911; the HadEX3 gridded record does not show the same pronounced heat.
ai_technology: Climate Reconstruction AI (CRAI), a U-Net with partial convolutions trained on CMIP6 historical simulations and transferred to the HadEX-CAM European extreme-index dataset
organization: German Climate Computing Center (DKRZ); Met Office; University of New South Wales; Freie Universität Berlin

evidence.tested: A partial-convolution U-Net trained on CMIP6 climate simulations and transferred to European station-based extreme indices reconstructed the poorly observed 1911 heatwave.
evidence.unknown: The September 1911 values are AI reconstructions rather than newly recovered thermometer readings; the paper states the source observations are sparse or missing. CRAI is trained on CMIP6 simulations and applied to European station-based extreme-index fields, so model-prior dependence remains. The article reports a similar spatial pattern in 20CRv3 and correlation with 1911 mortality, but these support the reconstructed pattern rather than directly validate each missing grid cell. The reported >40% refers to predicted percentage of days above the local 90th percentile for maximum temperature.
evidence.ai_role: The deep-learning reconstruction inferred missing monthly temperature-extreme indices from spatial context and learned climate-model patterns. This enabled a detailed estimate for the poorly observed September 1911 period; the model output exposes hot extremes in southern France that are not clearly represented in the standard HadEX3 map and supports comparison with independent 20th Century Reanalysis and historical mortality patterns.

title: ML-guided PtFeCu nanocatalyst shows enhanced oxygen-reduction activity and durability
summary: A first-principles database and neural-network-potential search explored 396,862 Pt–Fe–Cu nanoparticle configurations and mapped candidate compositions. The team synthesized PtFeCu variants and measured oxygen-reduction reaction (ORR) performance. A tested PtFeCu formulation showed about 3.1-fold higher specific activity (776 μA cm⁻² Pt) and 3.2-fold higher mass activity (0.67 A mg⁻¹ Pt) than Pt/C at 0.9 V; the authors attribute activity and improved durability to Cu-dependent surface-strain modulation and reduced Fe segregation, supported by calculations and experimental tests.
ai_technology: DFT-integrated neural-network potentials and machine-learning configuration search
organization: Yonsei University; Korea Institute of Energy Research; Hyundai Motor Company

evidence.tested: A first-principles database and neural-network-potential search explored 396,862 Pt–Fe–Cu nanoparticle configurations and mapped candidate compositions.
evidence.unknown: The result is a PtFeCu catalyst-composition/configuration finding, not a claim that the ternary system itself was previously unknown. The paper labels the high-/low-Cu variants inconsistently between its abstract/results and conclusion, so the quoted activity values are not tied here to a disputed variant name. Activity was measured in O2-saturated 0.1 M HClO4 using a rotating-disk setup; durability used a 30,000-cycle accelerated stress test, not a full fuel-cell operating lifetime. The reported 2 g batch capacity is a synthesis-scale result, not commercial manufacturing validation.
evidence.ai_role: The authors built neural-network potentials from first-principles data, screened 396,862 PtFeCu nanoparticle configurations, and used the predicted ternary configuration/composition map to guide experimental synthesis and selection of catalyst variants. The model-supported search was used to identify composition-dependent ORR activity and stability relationships; measurements and physical interpretation were performed by the research team.

title: Robot-guided optimization identifies six non-aqueous electrolytes with improved fast-charge performance
summary: A closed-loop platform paired Clio, an automated electrolyte-formulation and conductivity-testing robot, with Dragonfly Bayesian optimization. In 42 experiments over two workdays, it selected six non-aqueous electrolyte formulations from a LiPF₆ and EC/EMC/DMC design space. The team tested these formulations in 220 mAh graphite‖NMC pouch cells; all showed improved fast-charging capability relative to a baseline electrolyte selected in advance from the same design space. The search reached its reported target about six times faster than random search using the same automated setup.
ai_technology: Dragonfly Bayesian optimization coupled to the Clio robotic electrolyte experimentation platform
organization: Carnegie Mellon University

evidence.tested: A closed-loop platform paired Clio, an automated electrolyte-formulation and conductivity-testing robot, with Dragonfly Bayesian optimization.
evidence.unknown: This is a search within a defined design space of LiPF₆ in EC/EMC/DMC solvents, not a claim that the constituent chemicals or all six electrolyte recipes were wholly unprecedented. The optimization target was bulk ionic conductivity, with fast-charge cell performance as a subsequent validation. Pouch-cell tests used nominal 220 mAh graphite‖LiNi0.5Mn0.3Co0.2O2 cells and a baseline chosen from the same design space; results do not establish commercial-scale manufacturing or long-term fleet performance. The paper compares optimization time with random search in the same automated experiment.
evidence.ai_role: Dragonfly selected electrolyte formulations for experiments and used measurement feedback from Clio to adapt subsequent selections. The closed-loop system optimized measured ionic conductivity over a non-aqueous single-salt/ternary-solvent search space; selected formulations were then assembled and evaluated by the researchers in pouch cells.

title: Active-learning search experimentally realizes a high-zT Cu₁₋ₓAgₓGaTe₂ thermoelectric
summary: Compressed-sensing symbolic regression and active learning screened the Cu₁₋ₓAgₓGaTe₂ thermoelectric series and guided synthesis of selected compositions. The published study reports a p-type Cu₀.₄₅Ag₀.₅₅GaTe₂ sample with a measured thermoelectric figure of merit zT of about 1.90 at 770 K, using measured heat capacity in the analysis. This is one paper-level materials result from a targeted search, not a claim that every composition in the series is new.
ai_technology: SISSO compressed-sensing symbolic regression within an active-learning workflow
organization: University of Science and Technology of China; Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: Compressed-sensing symbolic regression and active learning screened the Cu₁₋ₓAgₓGaTe₂ thermoelectric series and guided synthesis of selected compositions.
evidence.unknown: The zT value is the final peer-reviewed paper’s reported result using measured heat capacity; an earlier preprint version of the same study reported a different higher estimate (about 2.8 at 827 K), so that preprint value is not substituted here or counted as a separate finding. The reported result is a laboratory thermoelectric sample at elevated temperature, not a device or commercial-performance demonstration. Active learning searched a defined composition series and does not establish that every searched composition was novel.
evidence.ai_role: The authors used SISSO to derive interpretable descriptors from their experimental thermoelectric dataset, then used active learning to rank prospective compositions for synthesis and measurement. The model guided candidate selection; the researchers synthesized and characterized the samples and measured the properties.

title: Adaptive learning finds higher-activity Fe–N–C oxygen-reduction catalysts
summary: An adaptive-learning design-of-experiments loop guided robotic high-throughput synthesis of Fe–N–C oxygen-reduction electrocatalysts across a six-dimensional process/composition space. Starting from 36 characterized samples, the team synthesized 14 additional catalyst formulations from a nominal search space of roughly 10 billion combinations. Four outperformed the best sample in the initial dataset; the best showed about 33% higher ORR activity, reported as 16.3 mA mg⁻¹ at 0.8 V in rotating-disk measurements.
ai_technology: Adaptive learning framework with machine-learning surrogates, statistical inference, uncertainty quantification, and global optimization, paired with robotic high-throughput synthesis
organization: Los Alamos National Laboratory; Argonne National Laboratory

evidence.tested: An adaptive-learning design-of-experiments loop guided robotic high-throughput synthesis of Fe–N–C oxygen-reduction electrocatalysts across a six-dimensional process/composition space.
evidence.unknown: The finding concerns optimized Fe–N–C catalyst formulations and synthesis conditions within the study’s defined six-dimensional search; it is not discovery of a new catalyst family or proof that all approximately 10 billion combinations were tested. The 33% improvement is relative to the best sample in the initial 36-sample dataset. Activity was measured using rotating-ring disk electrode testing, not a fuel-cell device or long-duration operating demonstration. The study reports 14 new synthesized catalysts and four that beat the initial samples; these are one paper-level result, not separate entries.
evidence.ai_role: The model-based design-of-experiments tool used current measurements and uncertainty to select subsequent synthesis conditions in a six-dimensional search space. It guided the selection of 14 samples for synthesis and measurement, producing four catalysts that exceeded the initial best. Robotic high-throughput synthesis and RRDE testing generated the experimental feedback; researchers interpreted the results.

title: Machine-learning unmixing links acid rain and subsurface flowpaths to watershed CO₂ drawdown
summary: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was applied to stream-chemistry time series from three watersheds to infer solute endmembers and their changing contributions without predefining endmember chemistry. Combined with geological interpretation and independent geochemical evidence, the model separated shallow acid-rain-affected flow from deeper pyrite-weathering contributions. The analysis found that acid rain can reduce a watershed’s long-timescale CO₂-sequestration capacity and that omitting sulfide oxidation/acid-rain reactions overestimates weathering-driven CO₂ drawdown.
ai_technology: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) machine-learning blind-source-separation model applied to stream chemistry
organization: Pennsylvania State University; Syracuse University

evidence.tested: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was applied to stream-chemistry time series from three watersheds to infer solute endmembers and their changing contributions without predefining endmember chemistry.
evidence.unknown: This is an inference from historical stream chemistry and watershed-specific geology, not a direct measurement of global CO₂ sequestration or a causal intervention. The NMF endmembers were interpreted as subsurface flowpaths using geological knowledge and supporting geochemical evidence; the inferred acid-rain sulfate export at Shale Hills includes a 19–31-year lag estimate. The result applies to three studied watersheds and the weathering timescales considered. Endmember counts and interpretations depend on the model setup and watershed reaction-front assumptions.
evidence.ai_role: The NMF model simultaneously inferred endmember chemical signatures and per-sample mixing proportions from solute ratios without preset endmember compositions. Researchers interpreted those patterns using watershed geology, sulfur isotopes, weathering profiles and calcite saturation, then estimated mineral-weathering rates and CO₂ sequestration. The ML decomposition enabled source separation where conventional endmember assumptions were uncertain; it did not directly measure a global carbon flux.

title: CNN-assisted search confirms quadruply lensed quasar PS J2107−1611
summary: A convolutional neural network trained on simulated lens images screened 27,760 preselected quasar candidates with multiple nearby Pan-STARRS detections. Researchers visually inspected the top 2,000 scores and selected follow-up targets; spectroscopy and multi-survey imaging established PS J2107−1611 as a quadruply imaged quasar at redshift 2.673, with a 4.3-arcsecond image separation and a lensed host-galaxy arc. Its fold-image optical fluxes are roughly 15 times fainter than a smooth lens-mass model predicts, while radio flux ratios are consistent with that model. The date is the original preprint posting; the journal version appeared in November 2023.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network trained on simulated quadruply lensed quasars, applied to Pan-STARRS gri image cutouts
organization: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne; University of Liège; European Southern Observatory; Universidad Andrés Bello

evidence.tested: A convolutional neural network trained on simulated lens images screened 27,760 preselected quasar candidates with multiple nearby Pan-STARRS detections.
evidence.unknown: This is a single confirmed system from a prefiltered candidate set; the authors visually reviewed high-scoring candidates and performed follow-up. Spectroscopy confirms the source is a quasar at z=2.673, while the four-image lens interpretation is supported by high-resolution imaging, lens modeling, a host-galaxy arc, and wavelength-dependent flux ratios. The ∼15-fold optical fold-pair anomaly is relative to the smooth macromodel; the cause is not resolved in this letter. Detailed JWST/VLT/EVN follow-up was left for future work.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN ranked image cutouts of 27,760 quasar catalog entries that already had multiple nearby Pan-STARRS detections. The team visually examined the top 2,000, selected 131 promising systems, and followed targets with imaging/spectroscopy; the model therefore enabled prioritization but did not itself confirm lensing. Human follow-up established the quasar redshift and lens configuration.

title: Symbolic regression derives aircraft aerodynamic scaling across sharp-cone and blunt-body geometries
summary: A Chain of Symbolic Regression (CoSR) analysis of hypersonic simulation data derived an interpretable non-power-product scaling relation for axial-force coefficient across sharp-cone and blunt-body configurations. It combines angle of attack, Mach number and Reynolds number through a dominant term and a viscous correction; the relation has a shared functional form but geometry-specific fitted constants. The authors interpret the constants as reflecting differences in shock/base drag, friction drag and pressure drag. This is a new model-derived scaling result from simulations, not a wind-tunnel or flight measurement.
ai_technology: Chain of Symbolic Regression (CoSR), a progressive symbolic-regression framework for dimensionless physical relations
organization: Northwestern Polytechnical University; International Joint Institute of Intelligent Fluid Mechanics; National Key Laboratory of Aircraft Configuration Design

evidence.tested: A Chain of Symbolic Regression (CoSR) analysis of hypersonic simulation data derived an interpretable non-power-product scaling relation for axial-force coefficient across sharp-cone and blunt-body configurations.
evidence.unknown: The aerodynamic relation was inferred from hypersonic simulation data for two configurations (sharp cone and blunt body), not independently measured flight or wind-tunnel data. It is a parameterized model over the analyzed configuration/data range; external validation and broader geometry coverage are not established in the source. The simpler dominant component is linked to known hypersonic invariance, while the learned viscous correction and geometry-specific scaling provide the paper’s new modeled relationship. Do not treat the authors’ drag-component interpretations as direct measurements.
evidence.ai_role: CoSR progressively searched for interpretable dimensionless groups and combined their relationships instead of fitting one end-to-end expression. Applied to hypersonic simulation data, it identified a dominant angle-of-attack/Mach term and a Reynolds-number-dependent viscous correction, then fitted geometry-specific constants for two body shapes. Earlier canonical-law and fluid examples in the same paper are framework validations and are not counted separately here.

title: Unsupervised learning guides high-zT ScNiSb-based half-Heusler thermoelectrics
summary: Iterative unsupervised clustering of half-Heusler compounds, using known thermoelectric materials as labeled reference points, guided selection of ScNiSb-based compositions for experimental testing. The team measured peak zT ≈0.5 at 925 K for p-type Sc₀.₇Y₀.₃NiSb₀.₉₇Sn₀.₀₃ and ≈0.3 at 778 K for n-type Sc₀.₆₅Y₀.₃Ti₀.₀₅NiSb. The paper reports these as compositionally optimized thermoelectric properties, not a new crystal structure or a device-level demonstration.
ai_technology: Iterative unsupervised clustering using prototype-based, density-based and hierarchical machine-learning algorithms
organization: Harbin Institute of Technology; Xi’an Jiaotong University; Inner Mongolia University of Technology

evidence.tested: Iterative unsupervised clustering of half-Heusler compounds, using known thermoelectric materials as labeled reference points, guided selection of ScNiSb-based compositions for experimental testing.
evidence.unknown: The measured materials are doped/alloyed variants of the known ScNiSb half-Heusler parent; the article does not claim discovery of a new crystal structure. Reported zT values are laboratory measurements at elevated temperatures, not performance from a fabricated waste-heat device or a commercial deployment. The two compositions are part of one paper-level screening and experimental result; do not split them into separate records.
evidence.ai_role: The authors applied unsupervised clustering to Materials Project descriptors for 456 half-Heusler compounds, iteratively using clusters containing 20 known thermoelectric materials as reference groups to shortlist candidates. The resulting ScNiSb-based choices guided synthesis and transport-property measurements; the model supported candidate selection, while the researchers performed synthesis, characterization and interpretation.

title: Active learning discovers three high-entropy thermoelectrics with zT above 2
summary: A Gaussian-process model and Bayesian active-learning loop used an average thermoelectric quality factor as a physics-informed descriptor to search a nine-element chalcogenide composition space of 16,206 candidates. Across six iterations, the team synthesized and measured 80 samples; three high-entropy chalcogenides reached peak zT values of about 2.1 at 573 K, 2.3 at 473 K and 2.1 at 723 K. Atomic-scale analysis of one composition also found Cu-rich interstitial clusters and local lattice strain, proposed to contribute to low lattice thermal conductivity.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process regression with Bayesian active learning and a physics-informed average thermoelectric quality-factor descriptor
organization: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology; Seoul National University; Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science; Hanbat National University; Korea University

evidence.tested: A Gaussian-process model and Bayesian active-learning loop used an average thermoelectric quality factor as a physics-informed descriptor to search a nine-element chalcogenide composition space of 16,206 candidates.
evidence.unknown: The zT values are experimental material-property measurements, not efficiencies demonstrated in a fabricated commercial thermoelectric device. The model used the average quality factor as a surrogate descriptor and trained on only 80 samples from the large composition space; it did not experimentally test all 16,206 candidates. Proposed high-entropy segmented-element efficiencies assume idealized interfaces. The Cu interstitial-cluster mechanism is supported by microscopy/spectroscopy for the characterized sample but is the authors’ interpretation of why performance improves.
evidence.ai_role: The model used uncertainty-aware exploration and exploitation to select the next formulations for synthesis from a 16,206-composition design space. Experimental feedback from 80 samples across six active-learning iterations updated the Gaussian-process surrogate; model-guided selection yielded three compositions with measured zT above 2. The authors then characterized the materials and interpreted atomic arrangements and transport properties.

title: Noise-aware active learning selects a high-latent-heat Ti–Ni–Hf shape-memory alloy
summary: A noise-aware Kriging model with active-learning acquisition selected candidate compositions from a million-composition NiTi-based alloy design space. After four experiments, researchers reported Ti₀.₂₆₆Ni₀.₄₈₄Hf₀.₂₅ with a measured latent heat of −36.08 J g⁻¹, 9.2% greater in magnitude than the best value in the initial training data (−33.04 J g⁻¹). The alloy also had an austenite-finish temperature of 481.71 °C and relatively small transformation hysteresis, making it a candidate for high-temperature thermal energy storage.
ai_technology: Noise-aware Kriging surrogate model with an active-learning acquisition strategy incorporating experimental-data noise
organization: Shanghai University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Xi’an Jiaotong University

evidence.tested: A noise-aware Kriging model with active-learning acquisition selected candidate compositions from a million-composition NiTi-based alloy design space.
evidence.unknown: The reported latent heat retains the source’s negative sign; the 9.2% improvement is a comparison of absolute magnitudes against the initial dataset’s best value. This is one material result from an active-learning search, not exhaustive exploration of the million-composition space. The reported temperature/hysteresis properties are laboratory characterizations; the paper does not demonstrate a deployed thermal-storage module or independent reproduction.
evidence.ai_role: The model estimated the measurement-noise level from noisy experimental data, incorporated that level into Kriging predictions, and used a noise-augmented acquisition strategy to choose the next NiTi-based compositions. Four experiments in the closed loop identified Ti0.266Ni0.484Hf0.25 as a promising high-latent-heat alloy; researchers synthesized and measured the material properties.

title: Machine learning derives new idealized ocean-eddy momentum and heat-flux closures
summary: Relevance-vector-machine sparse regression applied to high-resolution idealized ocean simulations produced compact momentum and temperature-flux closures for coarse grids. In the authors’ simulated setup, the inferred momentum terms include energy transfers absent from then-current closures; the parameterizations improved selected statistics when implemented in an idealized 30-km ocean model. This is a model-derived closure result, not an observation of a previously unknown ocean process.
ai_technology: Relevance vector machine (RVM) sparse Bayesian regression; physically constrained convolutional neural network used as a comparison
organization: University of Oxford; University of California, San Diego

evidence.tested: Relevance-vector-machine sparse regression applied to high-resolution idealized ocean simulations produced compact momentum and temperature-flux closures for coarse grids.
evidence.unknown: Derived from idealized, eddy-resolving double-gyre simulations and tested in an idealized coarse-resolution shallow-water model, not validated against observational ocean data or a global coupled climate model. The inferred tensor structure relates to earlier Reynolds-stress and deformation-based theories; the paper’s stated novelty is the additional data-derived terms/energy pathways and resulting parameterizations, not discovery of a new observed ocean phenomenon.
evidence.ai_role: RVM selected compact closed-form terms from candidate functions of simulated velocity, vorticity and deformation fields to infer subgrid momentum and temperature forcing. The authors report the expressions captured energy pathways omitted from existing parameterizations. A physically constrained CNN was also trained and evaluated, but the interpretable closure result comes from the RVM.

title: THESEUS derives resource-efficient designs for high-dimensional photonic GHZ and heralded Bell states
summary: The interpretable THESEUS design algorithm produced a three-dimensional six-photon GHZ-state blueprint that suppresses unwanted state terms toward arbitrarily high fidelity, with lower count rates, and a heralded three-dimensional Bell-state blueprint using destructive interference to cancel vacuum contributions. The same graph-based reasoning generalized the constructions to larger photon numbers or dimensions.
ai_technology: THESEUS
organization: University of Toronto; Vector Institute; Griffith University; Freie Universität Berlin

evidence.tested: The interpretable THESEUS design algorithm produced a three-dimensional six-photon GHZ-state blueprint that suppresses unwanted state terms toward arbitrarily high fidelity, with lower count rates, and a heralded three-dimensional Bell-state blueprint using destructive interference to cancel vacuum contributions.
evidence.unknown: These are theoretically calculated experiment blueprints, not experimentally demonstrated states in this paper. For the six-photon GHZ design, unwanted amplitudes can be reduced arbitrarily by adjusting graph weights, at the cost of lower count rates; feasibility is argued for contemporary photonics. The heralded Bell design’s estimated count rate and fidelity are modeled, not measured.
evidence.ai_role: The authors’ AI-enabled automated design algorithm used an interpretable weighted, colored-graph representation of photonic experiments, gradient-based optimization, and topology reduction to search open experiment-design problems and expose generalizable physical concepts. The authors identify the work as explainable AI; the contribution is the algorithmically found design/concept, not merely faster benchmarking.

title: Satellite-image clustering guides discovery of four late Miocene fossil sites in Mozambique’s Urema Rift
summary: Unsupervised k-means clustering of seven Landsat 8 spectral bands highlighted a small set of priority areas for paleontological field survey in Gorongosa National Park. The 2018 campaign documented four new late Miocene fossil localities; three lay within the model’s target cluster and the fourth was less than 90 m away in the same gully system. Together, the sites expose the first reported estuarine coastal-forest fossil setting in the East African Rift System, filling a regional paleoenvironmental gap.
ai_technology: Unsupervised k-means clustering of Landsat 8 imagery
organization: University of Oxford; University of Coimbra; University of North Carolina at Greensboro; University of Algarve; Gorongosa National Park

evidence.tested: Unsupervised k-means clustering of seven Landsat 8 spectral bands highlighted a small set of priority areas for paleontological field survey in Gorongosa National Park.
evidence.unknown: This was a pilot study in a 36 km² area and the model had notable false positives: reported precision was 55.56%, despite 84.6% overall accuracy. Three of four new localities overlapped the selected cluster; the fourth was less than 90 m away and was found by surveying the same gully system, so model localization for that site is indirect. The findings are four new fossil localities, not four new hominin taxa; the reported estuarine coastal-forest interpretation is a paleoenvironmental inference.
evidence.ai_role: The authors clustered seven spectral bands without pre-labeled land-cover classes, compared clusters with known fossil localities, and selected the cluster containing most known sites as a predictive target for field prospecting. This decision-support workflow directed the 2018 field survey that documented the new localities; a random forest was separately used to estimate spectral-band importance.
