title: Active learning guides experimental design of lead-free solder alloys
summary: Uncertainty-aware Gaussian-process models and multi-objective Bayesian acquisition guided seven design–experiment iterations. The study reports two selected alloys, Si-4 and Se-5, tested for tensile strength and fracture elongation. Reported averages follow the authors’ stated one-sigma selection of repeated tensile tests. Performance was mixed: the tested samples had poorer wettability and solder-joint shear strength than the commercial comparator. This is one laboratory alloy-design campaign, not evidence of industrial deployment or across-the-board superiority.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process models; multi-objective Bayesian active learning
organization: Shanghai University; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

source_review.scope: Primary npj Computational Materials indexed full text, publication history, experimental characterization and author affiliations.

evidence.tested: Seven design–experiment iterations included tensile testing of selected Si-4 and Se-5 alloys and evaluation of additional solder properties against a commercial comparator.
evidence.unknown: Averages follow a stated one-sigma selection of repeated tensile tests; wettability and joint shear strength were worse than the comparator. No industrial deployment or independent replication was established.
evidence.ai_role: Gaussian-process models represented experimental uncertainty and Bayesian multi-objective acquisition selected compositions for successive synthesis and testing rounds.

title: Machine learning identifies a low-tin lead-free relaxor composition window
summary: A multimodal literature-mining workflow and a physics-guided deep ensemble screened more than 150 million hypothetical compositions. The study reports that the x=0.01 and x=0.02 members of (Sr0.48Na0.26Bi0.26)(Ti1−xSnx)O3 met the authors’ predefined dielectric-stability targets while retaining room-temperature permittivity above 3300. The parent composition family and Sn substitution were already known; the result is a constrained low-Sn composition window, not a new parent chemistry. The reported upper-temperature stability criteria do not establish device certification or deployment.
ai_technology: Multimodal literature mining; deep neural-network ensemble
organization: Seoul National University; Korea University; Yeungnam University

source_review.scope: Primary PubMed record, article abstract, first-online date and affiliations.

evidence.tested: The authors report experimental validation of the x=0.01 and 0.02 Sn compositions against predefined dielectric-stability targets and room-temperature permittivity above 3300.
evidence.unknown: The parent family and substitution were known; the stated criteria do not establish full device certification or deployment. Direct publisher page was inaccessible, so evidence is limited to PubMed metadata and abstract in this check.
evidence.ai_role: Multimodal literature mining curated prior measurements and a deep neural-network ensemble screened candidate dielectric compositions and guided refinement.

title: Multi-omics models guide experimental validation of flowering-time genes
summary: Researchers trained models on genomic, transcriptomic and methylomic data for Arabidopsis traits and used feature interpretation to select flowering-time gene candidates. The preprint reports nine experimentally validated genes inferred to contribute to flowering time, tested using mutant phenotypes. Random-forest and ridge-regression models were used, so do not assign every gene to the random forest alone. Count one study, not nine discoveries. This draft follows the primary 2023 preprint version; the journal paper appeared in 2024.
ai_technology: Random-forest models; ridge regression; multi-omics integration
organization: DOE Great Lakes Bioenergy Research Center, Michigan State University; Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 full text, posted-date line, abstract, methods and author affiliations.

evidence.tested: The preprint reports experimental validation of nine flowering-time gene candidates using single- and/or double-mutant phenotypes.
evidence.unknown: Individual candidate-selection routes are not all attributed to one model; the result is from a preprint version and does not establish independent replication.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest and ridge-regression models used multi-omics data to predict plant traits and identify features associated with flowering-time predictions.

title: Deep learning helps experimentally map a ribozyme neutral network
summary: After earlier experimental evolutionary rounds, the authors trained a deep classifier to guide the final in-silico generation and experimentally tested candidates. They measured all 2^16 intermediates between two active RNA ligase ribozymes separated by 16 mutations and report an extensive network of neutral paths. The result applies to this ribozyme and assay, not all RNA evolution. The paper also notes possible model overfitting and the restricted classifier’s accuracy.
ai_technology: Deep-learning classifier; evolutionary algorithm
organization: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology Graduate University

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications indexed full text, abstract, main text, publication metadata and author affiliation.

evidence.tested: The study reports experimental activity measurements for all 2^16 connecting sequence variants and a screen of more than 120,000 ribozyme sequences.
evidence.unknown: The neutral network is bounded to one RNA ligase ribozyme and assay; generality across other landscapes is not established, and the paper notes potential classifier overfitting.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning classifier trained on prior experimental generations guided in-silico selection, mutation and recombination in the final generation.

title: Machine learning guides fatty acyl-ACP reductase engineering
summary: A machine-learning-guided iterative design–test–learn workflow engineered fatty acyl-ACP reductase variants for microbial fatty alcohol production. Across ten rounds, the study reports over twice the production of the starting natural sequences under tested conditions; the top sequence also had enhanced catalytic rate on palmitoyl-ACP. These are laboratory results, not industrial-scale production. The journal article date is used here; the earlier preprint’s exact posting and result-version differences were not checked.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided protein engineering; Gaussian-process optimization
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications indexed full text, abstract, article date, author affiliations; preprint chronology not fully checked.

evidence.tested: The paper reports ten design–test–learn rounds, in-vivo microbial fatty-alcohol production and catalytic-rate characterization on palmitoyl-ACP.
evidence.unknown: Results are under the study’s microbial test conditions and do not establish industrial production; exact preprint-version results remain unchecked.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models iteratively selected reductase sequences for experimental testing and subsequent model updates.

title: Machine learning guides engineering of fluorescent calcium indicators
summary: An ensemble of three regression models trained on experimentally derived GCaMP mutation libraries screened 1,423 uncharacterized variants. The study reports eGCaMP and eGCaMP+ with faster kinetics and larger fluorescence responses than previously published fast variants, and eGCaMP2+ with greater dynamic range than the tested sixth-, seventh- and eighth-generation indicators. The preprint reports cell and neuron assays. These are laboratory sensor results, not human or clinical validation. This is one study; the journal article is a later version.
ai_technology: Ensemble of three regression models
organization: University of Washington

source_review.scope: Primary Research Square v1 full text, posted-date header, abstract/results, author affiliations and version-of-record note.

evidence.tested: The study reports experimental evaluation in vitro, HEK293 cells and primary neurons for selected GCaMP variants.
evidence.unknown: Results are laboratory sensor assays, not evidence of human or clinical use; the record uses the 2023 preprint version while the journal paper appeared in 2024.
evidence.ai_role: An ensemble of three regression models predicted mutation effects and screened 1,423 GCaMP variants for experimental follow-up.

title: Knowledge-graph-guided discovery of antibiotic-resistance associations
summary: KIDS combined an expert-curated knowledge graph with learned link-prediction models to rank gene–antibiotic resistance hypotheses for experiments. The authors report 93 validated associations involving 83 E. coli genes and 15 antibiotics, including six genes they describe as previously unknown resistance genes; five tested Salmonella homologs also showed resistance. These are laboratory gene–drug associations, not clinical validation. The article’s second-round percentage conflicts with its counts (29/90 is 32.2%, although the text states 28.8%). Count one study.
ai_technology: Knowledge graph with PRA, multilayer perceptron, AdaBoost-stacked model, TransE and TransD
organization: University of California, Davis

source_review.scope: Primary Nature indexed full text, article dates, affiliations, methods/results, contributions and stated counting discrepancy.

evidence.tested: The authors report wet-lab validation of 93 gene–antibiotic associations, including five tested Salmonella homologs.
evidence.unknown: Reported percentages are internally inconsistent for 29 of 90 second-round tests; these assays do not establish clinical relevance or treatment outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: KIDS ranked gene–antibiotic links from an expert-curated graph with learned link-prediction models, directing experiments to candidate resistance associations.

title: Deep learning detects slow slip events in Cascadia GNSS data
summary: A detector combining convolutional and attention-based neural networks, trained on synthetic geodetic time series, was applied to raw GNSS data in Cascadia from 2007 to 2022. The authors report 78 detections, including 35 of 40 events in the 2007–2017 comparison catalog and 43 additional events. Detection patterns align with tremor activity, but the paper says independent acquisition-data validation is needed, and shorter/low-confidence events remain uncertain. This method is specific to this station network and does not predict earthquakes.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network and Transformer attention model
organization: ISTerre, Université Grenoble Alpes; Université Savoie Mont Blanc; CNRS; IRD; Université Gustave Eiffel; GIPSA-lab, Université Grenoble Alpes; Grenoble INP; Institut Universitaire de France

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full text, abstract, methods/results, affiliations and publication history.

evidence.tested: Applied detector outputs were compared with a prior event catalog and tremor activity in real Cascadia GNSS data.
evidence.unknown: Some additional/short detections remain uncertain; article states validation with an independent acquisition dataset is needed. This is not earthquake prediction.
evidence.ai_role: A CNN plus Transformer trained on synthetic GNSS series classified slow-slip windows in raw multistation GNSS data and produced event detections.

title: Deep clustering surfaces tremor-like episodes before the 2023 Türkiye earthquake
summary: An autoencoder and deep embedded clustering surfaced low-frequency tremor-like episodes in seismic records preceding the 2023 Türkiye earthquake. The authors then used source-location and particle-motion analyses to suggest an association with nearby cement-quarry activity. They explicitly state that evidence is insufficient to establish that industrial activity caused or influenced the earthquake; the paper is a retrospective signal interpretation, not an earthquake forecast or causal finding.
ai_technology: Autoencoder and deep embedded clustering
organization: Helmholtz Centre Potsdam, GFZ German Research Centre for Geosciences; Stanford University

source_review.scope: Primary PubMed metadata/abstract plus full primary article PDF from institutional repository; methods, conclusion and affiliations.

evidence.tested: The study applies clustering to seismic records and follows with source-location and particle-motion analyses.
evidence.unknown: The authors state they cannot establish a causal relation between quarry activity and the earthquake; this is retrospective and not a forecast.
evidence.ai_role: Deep embedded clustering of autoencoder representations identified low-frequency tremor-like episodes for subsequent geophysical source analysis.

title: AI-generated cell-penetrating peptide selected with molecular-dynamics simulations
summary: An RNN generated peptide sequences and molecular-dynamics-based scoring prioritized Pep-MD for synthesis. In cell assays, the authors report less toxicity than TAT and stronger cell permeability under the tested conditions. The paper proposes a membrane-entry mechanism based partly on simulated structures; these cell results do not establish therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: Recurrent neural network sequence generator with molecular-dynamics-based selection score
organization: Tokyo Institute of Technology; RIKEN; The University of Tokyo; National Institute for Materials Science

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full PDF, methods/results, publication information and author affiliations.

evidence.tested: The selected synthesized peptide was tested in cell-viability, confocal-imaging and FACS permeability assays against TAT.
evidence.unknown: Cell-based assays and a single comparator; no clinical or therapeutic efficacy evidence; mechanistic interpretation partly depends on modeled structures.
evidence.ai_role: An RNN generated candidate peptides; a simulation-derived score prioritized one sequence for synthesis and experimental cell testing.

title: Machine learning helps recover dimension from quantum periods for a class of Fano varieties
summary: A feed-forward neural network classified the dimension of Fano varieties from quantum-period coefficients with 98% accuracy on the authors’ dataset. The authors report that machine learning helped formulate rigorous asymptotic results, which prove dimension recovery for specified low-Picard-rank toric Fano classes. The broader conjecture that the quantum period uniquely determines every Fano variety remains open; the empirical classification accuracy is not itself a proof. The journal article appeared 2023-09-08, before the same work’s 2023-09-11 arXiv posting.
ai_technology: Feed-forward neural network
organization: Imperial College London; University of Nottingham

source_review.scope: Primary author-hosted full manuscript plus primary publisher article metadata; checked authors, method, theorem scope and chronology.

evidence.tested: The article combines a dataset classification result with rigorous asymptotic proofs for specified classes.
evidence.unknown: 98% is empirical accuracy on the paper’s dataset; the broad uniqueness conjecture remains open. Journal publication preceded arXiv submission.
evidence.ai_role: A neural network analyzed quantum-period coefficients and helped identify dimension-related patterns used to formulate asymptotic results, which the authors prove for restricted classes.

title: Machine learning assists a proved dimension bound for affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties
summary: The authors used computational data and machine-learning pattern exploration to study affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties. They report rediscovering the previously known virtual-dimension formula, then using the exploration to formulate and prove a new lower bound on actual dimension. The mathematical theorem, not model accuracy or rediscovery of the known formula, is the specific result. The 2024 journal article and 2023 arXiv v1 are versions of one study.
ai_technology: Linear models, support-vector machines and neural networks
organization: Beijing International Center for Mathematical Research, Peking University; Center for Machine Learning Research, Peking University; University of Hong Kong

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 full text and primary journal indexed full text, including methods, theorem, affiliations and version dates.

evidence.tested: The paper reports mathematical proof of a lower bound prompted by machine-learning exploration.
evidence.unknown: The virtual-dimension formula was previously known and is not the new theorem; the work is not a formal automated proof.
evidence.ai_role: Models explored generated mathematical data and highlighted patterns that led mathematicians to formulate and prove a new lower bound.

title: Machine-learning analysis motivates proved criteria for Galois groups
summary: Interpretable decision trees applied to Dedekind-zeta coefficients helped the authors identify patterns in Galois extensions of degrees 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10. They formulated and proved mathematical criteria, including a nonic result: for the stated class, a₁₀₀₀(K) ≤ 4.5 implies the extension is cyclic. This theorem is a specific result; dataset classification accuracy is not a universal guarantee, and the paper reports a counterexample to an apparently perfect classifier branch. The arXiv v1 of 2025-08-08 and the 2026 journal version are one study.
ai_technology: Interpretable decision trees and logistic regression
organization: Department of Mathematics, University of Connecticut; Korea Institute for Advanced Study; Department of Mathematics, University of California, Berkeley

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 and publisher full text, including result, proof scope, dates and affiliations.

evidence.tested: The authors report conventional proofs of criteria motivated by model interpretation.
evidence.unknown: The criteria apply to stated classes; model accuracy is data-dependent and a branch with apparent perfect performance has a stated out-of-sample counterexample.
evidence.ai_role: Decision-tree patterns in number-field coefficients motivated mathematical criteria that the authors then proved using conventional reasoning.

title: Machine learning guides discovery of hard Fe–Nb–B metallic-glass films
summary: Random-forest models for glass formation and hardness helped select Fe–Nb–B composition regions for sputtered-film experiments. The study reports a maximum measured hardness of 29 GPa for Fe₃Nb₂₅B₇₂ and an H/E ratio of 0.09 for Fe₂₀Nb₁₂B₆₈. H/E is used as an estimate of wear resistance, not a direct wear test. Samples were 500–800 nm films with substrate-effect corrections; bulk properties and industrial production were not demonstrated. This extends earlier machine-learning/high-throughput work on metallic glasses and is one study.
ai_technology: Random-forest models for glass formation and hardness
organization: Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource, SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory; Colorado School of Mines; National Renewable Energy Laboratory; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Maryland

source_review.scope: Primary full article PDF, title/DOI/date, affiliations, methods, composition/result and measurement limitations.

evidence.tested: Nanoindentation and synchrotron characterization were used to test sputtered films and measure hardness and structure.
evidence.unknown: Thin-film results; H/E is an estimated wear-resistance metric, not direct wear testing or evidence of bulk/industrial performance.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest predictions helped select Fe–Nb–B composition regions for high-throughput sputtered-film synthesis and measurement.

title: Active deep learning identifies emission-line object candidates in LAMOST spectra
summary: An active-learning workflow with a 12-layer convolutional network analyzed about 4.1 million LAMOST DR2 spectra and used human labeling of uncertain cases. After visual inspection and rejection of 58 poor spectra, the paper reports 4,321 spectra from about 3,788 objects, including 1,013 spectra of 948 objects not matched to SIMBAD or the specified Hou et al. 2016 catalog. Visual inspection supported emission signatures, but catalog non-match does not prove universal prior absence and proposed subtypes remain hypotheses. Count the catalog study once.
ai_technology: 12-layer one-dimensional convolutional neural network with uncertainty-sampling active learning
organization: Astronomical Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences; Faculty of Information Technology, Czech Technical University in Prague

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv metadata/abstract and journal full indexed results, publication dates, affiliations, and stated catalog limits.

evidence.tested: The paper reports human-oracle labeling and visual inspection of candidates, confirming emission signatures in retained spectra.
evidence.unknown: “New” means not matched to the named SIMBAD/Hou catalogs at the study date; proposed object classes require further classification.
evidence.ai_role: An active-learning CNN prioritized emission-line spectra in a large archive and asked human annotators to label uncertain examples.

title: Hybrid machine learning guides experimental discovery of multicomponent metallic glasses
summary: Hybrid classification and regression models with physically motivated descriptors, trained on about 5,000 metallic-glass compositions, guided exploration of multicomponent alloy compositions. Researchers synthesized 23 selected compositions: 12 predicted glass-formers produced glass in bulk, ribbon or both, while 11 predicted negative comparisons did not form glass under the tested preparation conditions. Six of the positive designs formed bulk glass; six formed glassy ribbons only. These selected experiments are not an unbiased estimate of global predictive accuracy. Some authors disclosed inventorship on a filed patent related to the new bulk compositions; composition-level prior art and independent replication remain open.
ai_technology: Hybrid classification/regression models including adaptive boosting, SVM, KNN and rational-quadratic Gaussian-process regression
organization: City University of Hong Kong

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full indexed article and institutional full-text copy, methods, results, date, affiliation and patent disclosure.

evidence.tested: The study reports synthesis and diffraction/thermal characterization of selected predicted positive and negative compositions.
evidence.unknown: Selected validation set, not unbiased global accuracy; patent inventorship disclosed and composition-level novelty/replication remain open.
evidence.ai_role: Hybrid models trained on prior metallic-glass data prioritized compositions for synthesis and measurement.

title: Machine learning selects Eu²⁺-activated green and blue-green phosphors
summary: A bagged gradient-boosted regression model trained on 129 Eu²⁺-activated phosphors predicted emission wavelengths and helped select 20 host candidates for synthesis. The authors report three Eu²⁺-activated phosphors with green or blue-green emissions: Li₂Ca₄Si₄O₁₃:Eu²⁺, Na₂Ca₂Si₂O₇:Eu²⁺, and SrLaGaO₄:Eu²⁺. The host compounds were known; novelty concerns their activator-specific luminescence. Some powders contained impurities, and selected-particle diffraction/spectroscopy characterization does not establish phase-pure bulk yields or device suitability. This is one campaign.
ai_technology: Bagged gradient-boosted regression trees
organization: Research and Services Division of Materials Data and Integrated System, National Institute for Materials Science; Osaka Metropolitan University; Research Center for Functional Materials, National Institute for Materials Science

source_review.scope: Primary full article/PDF, date, affiliations, methods/results, candidate measurements and stated limitations.

evidence.tested: Twenty candidates were synthesized and characterized; three showed designed green or blue-green Eu²⁺ emission.
evidence.unknown: Some samples contain impurity phases; selected-particle evidence and host-specific results do not establish phase-pure bulk/device performance or complete prior-art priority.
evidence.ai_role: A model trained on known phosphors ranked host candidates by predicted emission wavelength for experimental synthesis and characterization.

title: Machine learning guides Fe–Mn–Ni catalysts for NOx reduction
summary: An artificial neural network trained on literature data and a genetic algorithm helped identify Fe–Mn–Ni catalyst compositions for ammonia selective catalytic reduction. Researchers synthesized and tested model-guided candidates and report good NOx conversion for Fe₀.₃₁₉Mn₀.₂₀₆Ni₀.₄₇₅ over the tested temperature range. The work combines model selection, human screening and controlled experiments; the ratio is not a complete oxide formula and does not demonstrate industrial exhaust performance. The article text differs on whether the workflow involved two or four iterations, so this summary avoids an iteration count.
ai_technology: Artificial neural network and genetic algorithm
organization: State Environmental Protection Key Laboratory of Integrated Surface Water-Groundwater Pollution Control, Southern University of Science and Technology

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text, PubMed metadata/affiliation and publisher date chronology.

evidence.tested: The paper reports synthesis and catalytic conversion testing of selected Fe–Mn–Ni formulations.
evidence.unknown: Article reports inconsistent iteration counts; test range and lab results do not establish durability or practical flue-gas performance.
evidence.ai_role: An ANN and genetic search ranked candidate Fe–Mn–Ni compositions; experimental results were used in the iterative optimization workflow.

title: Machine-learning-guided evolution identifies higher-activity sortase A variants
summary: Two machine-learning-guided directed-evolution series for sortase A were run with and without the known high-activity 5M variant in the initial training set. The authors report new variants with higher activity than 5M in a GFP/YFP cross-linking assay. This is not a 2.2–2.5-fold improvement over wild type; the known 5M comparator is already engineered. Feature selection used ability to find 5M and may bias exploration. The related GB1 analysis uses an existing dataset, not a second laboratory discovery. Sequence-level comparison with later sortase work remains open.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process Bayesian selection model
organization: Tohoku University

source_review.scope: Primary ACS indexed full article and Tohoku research announcement; methods/results and journal timing.

evidence.tested: Constructed variants were assayed for SrtA-catalyzed GFP/YFP cross-linking; resulting variants exceeded the 5M comparator.
evidence.unknown: The assay is specific; 5M is an already high-activity engineered comparator; feature selection may bias to 5M; independent sequence-level overlap/replication open.
evidence.ai_role: A Gaussian-process ML model ranked variants from initial and second-round data to design subsequent SrtA mutant libraries.

title: Machine learning guides direct synthesis of higher-silica faujasite
summary: Machine-learning models learned relationships between crystallization composition/conditions and zeolite characteristics from prior synthesis records, guiding human selection of conditions for faujasite synthesis. The team reports directly synthesized, unseeded, organic-structure-directing-agent-free FAU with Si/Al 3.5, compared with the prior reported maximum 2.8. Following ion exchange, laboratory tests report improved propane cracking and dehydrogenation rates per proton site relative to the lower-silica comparator. The FAU framework was already known; this result concerns composition and route, not a new framework or industrial performance.
ai_technology: Geometric harmonics, neural networks and Gaussian-process regression
organization: University of Minnesota; Dalian University of Technology; Johns Hopkins University; Argonne National Laboratory; California Institute of Technology; Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

source_review.scope: Primary Caltech institutional record and deposited published article/supplement; date, affiliations, methods and abstract/results.

evidence.tested: Researchers synthesized and characterized FAU and tested acid catalysts in propane cracking/dehydrogenation under laboratory conditions.
evidence.unknown: Known framework; activity comparison is assay-specific and does not establish industrial gains.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on prior synthesis records identified composition/condition settings that guided direct high-silica FAU synthesis.

title: Machine learning guides refinement of DNA aptamers binding NGAL
summary: Neural models trained on particle-display affinity-screening data guided sequence mutation and candidate nomination, followed by synthesis and experimental affinity testing. The authors report a 23-nucleotide truncation of candidate G13 with measured dissociation constant 1.5 nM, compared with about 8 nM for the full-length parent under their assay. This is a binding result, not demonstrated diagnostic or therapeutic efficacy. The screening set is not 187,499 independently validated agents; sequence-level prior art remains open.
ai_technology: Neural-network models trained on particle-display affinity data
organization: Google Research; Aptitude Medical Systems

source_review.scope: Primary publisher indexed full text, article dates, methods/results, affiliations and disclosed limitations.

evidence.tested: The study reports particle-display screening and measured NGAL binding, including full Kd for truncated and parent G13.
evidence.unknown: Binding assay only; no diagnostic/therapeutic outcome; one holdout set used for tuning and sequence novelty requires further review.
evidence.ai_role: Trained neural models extrapolated from experimentally measured sequences to nominate and iteratively refine higher-affinity DNA aptamers and truncations.

title: Machine learning guides a near-infrared Mo/Sb halide phosphor
summary: A regression model trained on experimental and theoretical data guided Mo/Sb/Br co-doping for a lead-free near-infrared phosphor. The authors report synthesizing Cs₂Zr(Cl₀.₄₆Br₀.₅₄)₆:12%Mo⁴⁺/3.6%Sb³⁺, with emission near 920 nm, internal quantum efficiency of 92.4%, and external quantum efficiency of 65.9% under the reported conditions. Its measured intensity was about 20% higher than the authors’ orthogonal-design comparator. A separate diffusion model was used for image reconstruction demonstrations; this does not establish clinical diagnostic performance. Earlier composition-level prior art and independent replication remain open.
ai_technology: Transformer-based regression model
organization: Guangxi University; South China University of Technology

source_review.scope: Primary indexed publisher article and NLM publication metadata; abstract/results, model roles, online date and measured outcomes.

evidence.tested: Authors report synthesis and optical characterization of the predicted composition, LED device testing, and separate imaging demonstration.
evidence.unknown: Study-specific efficiency/intensity results; earlier independent reports and composition-level priority remain unverified; imaging is not clinical diagnostic validation.
evidence.ai_role: A model trained on experimental/theoretical data predicted co-dopant concentrations for researchers to synthesize and test; a separate diffusion model reconstructed imaging outputs.

title: Machine learning helps select nickel(I)–phenyl complexes that insert CO₂ at room temperature
summary: The researchers calculated descriptors for 132 bidentate phosphine ligands, used k-means clustering to identify 21 candidate ligands, then applied DFT barrier calculations and human selection before synthesis. They isolated and characterized Ni(I)–phenyl complexes, including an X-ray-confirmed i-Pr-Xantphos complex. The i-Pr-Xantphos and dtbpf complexes underwent CO₂ insertion at room temperature in the reported experiments; nickel carboxylation was also tested. The study does not establish CO₂ insertion or Ni(I) chemistry generally as new; its result concerns bounded ligand selection/speciation.
ai_technology: Unsupervised k-means clustering of DFT-derived ligand descriptors
organization: Institute of Organic Chemistry, RWTH Aachen University; University of Jyväskylä

source_review.scope: Primary JACS full text, abstract, methods/results, chronology and affiliations.

evidence.tested: Synthesis, X-ray characterization, CO₂ insertion assays and catalytic carboxylation tests reported for selected Ni complexes.
evidence.unknown: Only representative ligands from predicted groups were experimentally evaluated; prior Ni(I)-CO₂ chemistry exists; results do not imply commercial carbon capture.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised clustering of computed descriptors identified a set of ligands to evaluate; DFT and researcher selection further narrowed candidates before synthesis and testing.

title: Machine learning guides yeast alcohol dehydrogenase specificity for trans-2-nonenal
summary: Researchers measured a training library of yeast alcohol dehydrogenase I variants, used support-vector activity regression/classification and a thermostability model to rank combinations, then tested 22 prioritized variants. Four showed higher specific activity toward trans-2-nonenal than wild type; LWFMY also showed improved thermostability under the study’s tests. The result is laboratory enzyme engineering, not an industrial process or validated product. The primary journal version was published 2026-11-01; a search result for an earlier-hosted copy had ambiguous date/provenance, so this entry does not claim it was the first public version.
ai_technology: Support-vector regression/classification models and docking-informed mutation selection
organization: RIKEN Center for Sustainable Resource Science; Graduate School of Science, Technology, and Innovation, Kobe University

source_review.scope: Primary Springer full article and PubMed metadata; methods, dates, affiliations and outcomes.

evidence.tested: The top 22 ranked variants were experimentally evaluated; four outperformed wild type on trans-2-nonenal, with one also improved in thermal stability.
evidence.unknown: Small selected validation set; specific activity differs from catalytic efficiency across substrate concentrations; ambiguous earlier-hosted copy means first-public date is not asserted.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on measured variant data ranked combinations in unexplored sequence space for experimental testing.

title: Gaussian-process-assisted engineering of a ketoreductase for an ipatasertib precursor
summary: A six-round engineering campaign combined mutational scans, structure-guided libraries and Gaussian-process models. The model-aided library yielded M3, reported with 22-fold higher apparent activity than wild type in the UV assay. Three subsequent conventional mutagenesis rounds produced M6, a 10-substitution descendant with 64-fold higher apparent kcat, but also about 12-fold higher apparent KM; do not attribute M6 as a direct model output or treat kcat as production yield. The authors report a 100 g/L laboratory process test with ≥98% conversion and 99.7% diastereomeric excess after 30 hours. These are process-relevant laboratory results, not a commercial production run or drug efficacy.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process regression
organization: Institute of Chemistry and Biotechnology, Zurich University of Applied Sciences; F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd.

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full article, methods/results, publication history, affiliations and chronology of model and conventional rounds.

evidence.tested: M3 and later M6 were tested for activity; article reports preparative reactions at 100 g/L substrate and conversion/stereoselectivity under specified laboratory conditions.
evidence.unknown: M6 follows conventional site-mutagenesis rounds after the AI-informed step; apparent kcat differs from process yield and KM changed; no commercial production/clinical efficacy claim.
evidence.ai_role: Gaussian-process predictions informed smaller follow-up variant libraries within a broader workflow that also used mutational scanning, rational design and conventional evolution.

title: ML-guided synthesis conditions produce EMT zeolite
summary: Researchers trained models on 174 prior synthesis attempts and selected six EMT synthesis conditions for testing. Five yielded EMT by X-ray diffraction; two used starting-mixture Si/Al ratios outside the training range. EMT is an established framework, and the small, researcher-selected study does not establish a general success rate or independent replication.
ai_technology: XGBoost classifier, PCA and pretrained foundation models
organization: University of Houston

evidence.tested: As described in the primary source
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and global priority not established by this review.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost classifier, PCA and pretrained foundation models

source_review.scope: Primary publisher/preprint material inspected for identity, AI role and bounded result.

title: Bayesian optimization identifies active non-noble oxygen-evolution oxides
summary: Multiobjective Bayesian optimization guided robotic synthesis and electrochemical testing in a researcher-defined Co–Mn–Sb–Sn–Ti oxide space. The study identifies Mn-rich candidates and reports improved activity after Ti incorporation into MnOx following short accelerated-stress testing. Its 17-fold acceleration compares measurement time with a hypothetical exhaustive triplicated grid; it does not establish commercial electrolyzer lifetime or universal superiority.
ai_technology: Multiobjective Bayesian optimization with multitask Gaussian-process surrogate
organization: Forschungszentrum Jülich; Friedrich-Alexander University Erlangen-Nürnberg; Helmholtz Institute Erlangen-Nürnberg for Renewable Energy

evidence.tested: As described in the primary source
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and global priority not established by this review.
evidence.ai_role: Multiobjective Bayesian optimization with multitask Gaussian-process surrogate

source_review.scope: Primary publisher/preprint material inspected for identity, AI role and bounded result.

title: ML prioritization identifies two antimicrobial peptide candidates
summary: CalcAMP ranked 16,384 14-residue sequences in a researcher-defined LL-37-derived design space bounded by patent WO2015088344. Researchers selected GDST-038 and GDST-045 for laboratory tests; the paper reports activity against tested bacteria and elimination of detectable adherent S. aureus in a 3D human epidermal infection model at concentrations of at least 15 µM. Retro-inverso variants were prepared and tested after selection. These results do not establish human safety or clinical efficacy, and exact sequence-level patent priority remains open.
ai_technology: CalcAMP machine-learning activity ranking
organization: Amsterdam University Medical Centre; Leiden University; Leiden University Medical Center

source_review.scope: Primary MDPI full article, abstract/results and author-affiliation block reviewed.

evidence.tested: The primary article reports in-vitro antimicrobial testing, biofilm assays and a 3D human epidermal infection model for selected parent/retro-inverso peptides.
evidence.unknown: These are in-vitro and tissue-model findings, not clinical efficacy or human safety. Sequence-level patent scope and independent replication are not established.
evidence.ai_role: CalcAMP ranked peptide sequences by predicted antimicrobial activity; researchers selected and experimentally tested two lead sequences and retro-inverso variants.

title: Diffusion-guided peptide design yields antimicrobial candidate Arcinin
summary: ARCADIAMP combines iterative discrete diffusion generation, ESM2-based activity classifiers and sequence novelty filtering. Eight of ten experimentally screened candidates met the paper’s MIC threshold; Arcinin showed activity against tested pathogens and reduced bacterial burden in a mouse wound infection model. These are selected preclinical findings, not evidence of human safety or treatment efficacy; formal resistance-evolution testing remains future work.
ai_technology: Iterative discrete diffusion model with ESM2 classifiers and novelty filter
organization: University of California, Davis

evidence.tested: As described in the primary source
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and global priority not established by this review.
evidence.ai_role: Iterative discrete diffusion model with ESM2 classifiers and novelty filter

source_review.scope: Primary publisher/preprint material inspected for identity, AI role and bounded result.

title: Deep-learning feature-guided design yields antimicrobial peptides D1 and D2
summary: DLFea4AMPGen uses deep-learning activity models and SHAP feature attribution to define peptide fragments used in a candidate sequence space. Sixteen selected peptides were synthesized; the primary article reports 12 with at least two tested activities and identifies D1 and D2 as active against drug-resistant bacterial isolates. D1 also reduced bacterial load in a reported mouse infection experiment. This is preclinical evidence, not human treatment or safety; the study does not establish that every generated sequence or all three activity classes were validated.
ai_technology: Deep-learning activity prediction and SHAP-guided feature-fragment generation
organization: Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences; Inner Mongolia University; Academy of Military Medical Sciences; Western Medical Branch of PLA General Hospital

evidence.tested: The primary source reports the described assays.

evidence.unknown: Performance is limited to the reported cell chemistry, 1 M LiFSA configuration and cycling protocol; it does not establish full-cell energy density, lifetime in commercial formats or manufacturing readiness.
evidence.ai_role: A sequential active-learning framework selected each batch of candidate solvents using Bayesian experimental design and Bayesian model averaging, then incorporated measured electrochemical outcomes to update its next selections.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications full text as indexed; primary PMC text with methods/results/contributions; institutional full-paper manuscript mirror.

title: PhotoCat guides experimental discovery of photocatalytic reactions
summary: The PhotoCat Transformer was pretrained on general reaction data and fine-tuned on the authors’ photocatalysis database to predict products and reaction conditions. In the 2023 ChemRxiv version, the authors report using it to guide experimental validation of previously unreported photocatalytic reactions. The later 2026 journal version describes four novel validated reactions, whereas the preprint reports five; this entry makes no exact-count claim and treats the journal article as a revised version of the same study.
ai_technology: Transformer-based deep-learning reaction predictor pretrained on USPTO and fine-tuned on PhotoCatDB, with reaction-condition inputs
organization: Zhejiang University of Technology

evidence.tested: The PhotoCat Transformer was pretrained on general reaction data and fine-tuned on a photocatalysis database to predict products and conditions. The 2023 ChemRxiv version reports wet-lab validation of five predicted reactions; the 2026 journal abstract reports four novel validated reactions.
evidence.unknown: The preprint and journal version differ in their reported count of validated novel reactions. This record states the shared model-guided experimental discovery claim and makes no exact-count claim.
evidence.ai_role: A Transformer reaction predictor was pretrained on USPTO and fine-tuned on PhotoCatDB to rank photocatalytic reaction outcomes and conditions, guiding experimental validation.

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv v2 full-text PDF and version-history metadata; primary PMC full-text journal version and publication metadata. The preprint and journal versions report different counts (five versus four); the summary preserves this discrepancy.

title: Machine learning screening identifies an efficient molecular photocatalytic CO2-reduction system
summary: A machine-learning-accelerated descriptor workflow screened 3,444 molecular photosensitizer–catalyst systems, including 180,000 conformations, and selected six candidates for experimental validation. The primary article reports that the optimal tested system reached a turnover number of 4,390 and uses time-resolved spectroscopy and first-principles calculations to examine dipole coupling. The reported outcome is bounded to the tested system and the study’s screening scope.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening using descriptors for photosensitization, electron transfer, and catalysis
organization: University of Science and Technology of China

evidence.tested: The article reports experimental validation of the machine-learning-screened molecular photocatalytic systems; its optimal system achieved a turnover number of 4,390. The study screened 3,444 systems and selected six promising candidates.
evidence.unknown: The summary does not identify a catalyst or photosensitizer structure because the accessible primary indexed passage did not unambiguously tie a named complex to the reported maximum. Performance is specific to the reported experimental conditions; deployment and independent replication are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning accelerates high-throughput screening with descriptors spanning photosensitization, electron transfer and catalysis, reducing the 3,444-system search to six candidates selected for experimental validation.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Catalysis indexed article text, abstract, extended-data descriptions, metadata and affiliation block; institutional research announcement checked as corroboration.

title: Machine learning-guided synthesis of two-dimensional AgBi iodide perovskites
summary: The authors combined an 80-amine high-throughput synthesis dataset, chemistry-informed molecular descriptors, subgroup discovery and a support-vector classifier to rank organic spacers for 2D AgBi iodide perovskites. Of 13 model-selected candidates taken forward, eight were successfully synthesized and characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and powder X-ray diffraction. The study reports a 61.5% success rate in this selected validation set; it does not establish universal synthesis performance across other perovskite families.
ai_technology: Subgroup discovery and support-vector classification using physicochemical and molecular-topology descriptors
organization: Southeast University

evidence.tested: The primary article reports successful synthesis of 8 of 13 machine-learning-selected 2D AgBi iodide perovskites (61.5%), with crystal structures determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and bulk-phase purity confirmed by PXRD.
evidence.unknown: The validation concerns a selected set under common laboratory synthesis conditions and one AgBi iodide family; generalization to other material families is not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Subgroup discovery identifies an applicable data region and a support-vector classifier estimates synthesis feasibility from molecular descriptors; the model ranks candidate organic spacers for experimental synthesis.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications publisher PDF indexed full text including Results, Methods, author contributions and article metadata; Southeast University institutional announcement checked for corroboration.

title: Deep learning identifies antimicrobial peptides hidden in prion-related proteins
summary: APEX 1.1 screened 19.3 million peptide fragments from 2,897 prion-related proteins and identified 1,179 candidate antimicrobial peptides, termed prionins. Among 75 synthesized candidates, 59 inhibited at least one tested bacterial strain; two selected peptides reduced Acinetobacter baumannii burden in a mouse skin-abscess model. The study shows that prion-related sequences can yield experimentally active antimicrobial fragments, but does not show that these peptides are naturally released or function as host-defense agents in their source organisms.
ai_technology: APEX 1.1 deep-learning antimicrobial-peptide prediction and prioritization
organization: University of Pennsylvania

evidence.tested: Of 75 synthesized APEX-selected prionins, 59 inhibited at least one bacterial strain in vitro; two selected peptides reduced A. baumannii burden in a mouse skin-abscess model.
evidence.unknown: No evidence shows these fragments are naturally released from their source proteins or physiologically function as host-defense peptides in native organisms. Mouse results do not establish human efficacy or safety.
evidence.ai_role: APEX 1.1 scored peptide fragments for predicted antimicrobial activity and prioritized candidates from a search across prion-related proteins for synthesis and experimental screening.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Microbiology full text as indexed, including methods, results, author contributions and affiliations.

title: Machine learning screening identifies GW3965 activity against invasive group A Streptococcus
summary: A neural network trained on measured growth responses from 2,560 compounds screened 6,111 FDA-evaluated compounds for activity against multidrug-resistant emm92 group A Streptococcus. Of nine selected compounds tested, GW3965 reduced bacterial survival by 99% at an MIC of 6.25 μM. The authors also report improved wound closure in an infected human skin-equivalent model and reduced lesion area and bacterial burden in mice. This is preclinical evidence and does not establish efficacy or safety in people. The peer-reviewed journal article followed on 2026-05-30 and reports the same core GW3965 result.
ai_technology: Deep neural network trained on compound SMILES and measured bacterial growth responses; model screened an FDA-evaluated compound library
organization: West Virginia University

evidence.tested: The model was trained on 2,560 compounds and screened 6,111. Nine selected compounds were validated; GW3965 had MIC 6.25 μM and reduced viable emm92 iGAS by 99%. In a human skin-equivalent model infected tissues treated with GW3965 showed wound closure; in a mouse SSTI model 30 mg/kg reduced lesion size and day-6 wound bacterial burden by about 2 logs on average.
evidence.unknown: Results come from in-vitro assays and animal/tissue models; the preprint reports no synergy with ampicillin. Human clinical efficacy, dosing, safety and mechanism against GAS remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: A neural network learned structure–growth-inhibition patterns from measured compound screening data, prioritized GW3965 for follow-up, and the selected candidate was experimentally tested in bacterial, human skin-equivalent, and mouse infection models.

source_review.scope: Primary Research Square v1 full-text PDF, including posted date, affiliations, Methods and experimental outcomes; primary Nature publisher indexed article text and journal-version abstract/results.

title: AI-assisted analysis reveals retrospective seismicity before the Dingri earthquake
summary: A PhaseNet-assisted workflow combined phase detection, polarisation analysis and template matching on records from one permanent station to reconstruct seismicity in the two years before the 2025 Mw 7.1 Dingri earthquake. The authors report increased event rate and clustering beginning about 45 days before the mainshock. This retrospective pattern is interpreted as compatible with late-stage nucleation; the study does not establish a prospective earthquake forecast.
ai_technology: PhaseNet deep neural-network seismic phase picker combined with polarisation analysis and template matching
organization: Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale (OGS)

evidence.tested: PhaseNet-assisted phase detection, polarisation analysis and template matching reconstructed 289 template events and 1,138 augmented events at one station before the 2025 Dingri earthquake. The authors report increased event rate and clustering beginning about 45 days before the mainshock.
evidence.unknown: This is a retrospective analysis from one station. The authors describe a pattern compatible with late-stage nucleation; it does not establish a prospective forecast or earthquake prediction.
evidence.ai_role: PhaseNet, a deep neural-network phase picker, supported detection and event-catalogue construction; the resulting catalogue enabled retrospective identification of the pre-mainshock activity increase.

source_review.scope: Primary Scientific Reports indexed article, including abstract, Methods, Results, article dates and author-affiliation block.

title: Machine-learning seismic catalogue reveals a long-period swarm before Sierra Negra eruption onset
summary: A machine-learning phase-picking and template-matching workflow expanded the catalogue for the 2018 Sierra Negra eruption onset, identifying a northwestern-caldera swarm of long-period microearthquakes missing from earlier manually picked records. The authors report the swarm began about two hours after a Mw 5.4 intra-caldera earthquake and preceded edifice failure and magma intrusion. The proposed fluid-triggering sequence is an interpretation of retrospective seismic and geodetic observations, not a prospective eruption forecast.
ai_technology: Volpick EQTransformer-based seismic phase picker combined with template matching and geodetic analysis
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

evidence.tested: An EQTransformer-based phase picker and template matching expanded the seismic catalogue for the 2018 Sierra Negra eruption onset. The authors report 1,224 volcano-tectonic and 711 long-period events and identify a long-period swarm missing from the earlier manually picked catalogue, beginning about two hours after the Mw 5.4 earthquake.
evidence.unknown: The proposed fluid-triggering sequence is an interpretation of retrospective seismic and geodetic observations; this study does not establish prospective eruption prediction.
evidence.ai_role: The learned EQTransformer-based phase picker supported a denser event catalogue; combined with template matching, this exposed a previously unreported long-period swarm in the archived seismic record.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications indexed article text and PDF-indexed article content, including abstract, Results, Methods, metadata and author-affiliation section.

title: Experimental feedback guides ESM-2 to brighter CreiLOV variants
summary: Reinforcement Learning from eXperimental Feedback (RLXF) used a learned fluorescence reward model to align ESM-2 with measured CreiLOV sequence-function data. In the peer-reviewed study, the authors expressed 60 generated variants in E. coli and measured cellular fluorescence; six of ten aligned ESM-2 five-mutant designs exceeded CreiLOV fluorescence, and three aligned designs exceeded CreiLOV-T7S. The first bioRxiv version (posted 2025-05-08) already described experimentally enhanced fluorescence from RLXF-aligned designs; detailed measurements here are from the 2026 journal version. The earlier ICLR workshop comparison was computational and did not report new wet-lab fluorescence assays.
ai_technology: 650-million-parameter ESM-2 protein language model aligned by reinforcement learning from experimental feedback using a learned sequence-fluorescence reward model
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison

evidence.tested: The journal article reports 60 CreiLOV designs expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3) and measured for total cellular fluorescence. Six of ten aligned ESM-2 five-mutant designs exceeded CreiLOV fluorescence, and three aligned designs exceeded the prior CreiLOV-T7S control; the brightest reported design was 1.2-fold above T7S.
evidence.unknown: The measurements use total cellular fluorescence and are specific to tested designs/conditions; broader cellular contexts, protein function beyond fluorescence, and independent reproduction are not established. The qualitative enhanced-fluorescence result is present in the 2025 preprint abstract; detailed design-set metrics are verified from the later journal version.
evidence.ai_role: A learned sequence-fluorescence reward model trained on measured CreiLOV variant data guides supervised fine-tuning and PPO alignment of ESM-2. The aligned model generates the candidate sequences that were expressed and assayed.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 abstract, posting-date and affiliation metadata; primary GEM@ICLR workshop paper full text for methods and experimental outcomes; primary Nature Communications indexed text for later journal-version comparison.

title: A biophysics-informed protein language model designs functional GFP variants
summary: Mutational Effect Transfer Learning (METL) combines transformer pretraining on simulated protein biophysics with fine-tuning on experimental sequence–function data. Using only 64 experimental GFP examples, the authors designed 20 previously untested variants and measured their fluorescence; 16 showed measurable fluorescence, although none was brighter than wild-type GFP. The result demonstrates functional design under a small-data setup, not improved brightness over wild type. The result was present in the bioRxiv version posted 2024-03-17; the GEM@ICLR 2024 workshop paper provides the detailed 20-variant assay report, and the later journal version is the same study.
ai_technology: Mutational Effect Transfer Learning (METL), a transformer protein language model pretrained on simulated biophysical features and fine-tuned on experimental data
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison

evidence.tested: Twenty METL-designed GFP variants were synthesized and experimentally measured; 16 showed measurable fluorescence, but none exceeded wild-type brightness.
evidence.unknown: The panel contains 20 designed variants in a specific GFP task; the result does not show improvement over wild-type brightness or establish general performance across protein families.
evidence.ai_role: METL-Local was pretrained on simulated GFP sequence/biophysical data, fine-tuned using 64 experimental examples, and used with sequence optimization to select variants for wet-lab testing.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 indexed abstract, posting date and affiliation metadata; primary GEM@ICLR workshop paper full text with methods and experimental outcomes.

title: Machine learning guides engineering of an alkaloid-biosynthesis enzyme
summary: Researchers developed MutComputeX, a structure-based residual neural network for assessing amino-acid substitutions in protein–ligand environments, and used it with a 4′-O-methylnorbelladine biosensor to engineer the plant methyltransferase Nb4OMT in Escherichia coli. The paper reports engineered variants with 60% higher product titer, twofold higher catalytic activity, threefold lower off-product regioisomer formation and 5 °C higher thermostability; ligand-aware predictions helped identify the beneficial A53M substitution. These enzyme and product results do not demonstrate complete microbial production of galantamine.
ai_technology: MutComputeX structure-based residual neural network for protein–ligand mutation design
organization: University of Texas at Austin

evidence.tested: MutComputeX-guided, manually curated Nb4OMT variants were assayed using a 4NB biosensor and biochemical methods. The article reports 60% higher product titer, twofold higher catalytic activity, threefold lower off-product formation and 5 °C higher thermostability for engineered variants.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns a pathway enzyme and branchpoint intermediate in the reported microbial/biochemical systems; full pathway production of galantamine and industrial manufacturing were not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: MutComputeX predicted sequence substitutions in a modeled protein–ligand microenvironment and guided selection of Nb4OMT variants for biosensor screening and enzyme assays; ligand-aware predictions supported A53M.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications full text as indexed, including methods/results, author contributions and affiliation block.

title: Similarity-informed machine learning guides experimental high-entropy alloy catalyst discovery
summary: A graph neural network augmented with quantum-inspired adsorption-site similarity reduced the DFT training data needed for a given prediction accuracy from 1,600 to 800 calculations. The model identified a five-metal Fe–Co–Ni–Ir–Ru high-entropy alloy candidate for oxygen reduction; the author group reports experimental validation and performance above a Pt/C comparison. The publisher abstract gives a predicted overpotential of 0.24 V, which is not presented here as the measured value. This is a laboratory catalyst result, not a fuel-cell deployment claim.
ai_technology: Similarity-augmented graph neural network for adsorption-site and alloy-composition screening
organization: Computational Laboratory for Energy and Nanoscience

source_review.scope: Primary ScienceDirect indexed abstract and metadata; primary author-group publication page. Direct publisher full-text open was blocked, so no full Methods or complete article affiliation review is claimed.

evidence.tested: The author group reports experimental validation identifying a five-metal high-entropy alloy oxygen-reduction catalyst that outperformed its Pt/C comparison. The publisher describes experimental study of four additional HEAs; the 0.24 V overpotential is a model prediction, not stated here as an experimental measurement.
evidence.unknown: The publisher full Methods and supplementary results were not reviewed in this pass. The abstract-level material does not provide the measured ORR performance values, test uncertainty, durability, or full experimental protocol. No independent replication or fuel-cell device performance is established.
evidence.ai_role: The graph neural network incorporated quantum-inspired similarity between adsorption sites, reducing the required DFT training-set size from 1,600 to 800 while maintaining prediction accuracy. Its predictions nominated HEA compositions for experimental synthesis and ORR evaluation.

title: HydrAMP-guided design of short tryptophan-rich antimicrobial peptides
summary: HydrAMP generated analogues from a short Arg/Trp prototype, with AMPlify scoring and empirical filters used to select candidates. The authors synthesized three peptides and measured antimicrobial activity across bacterial strains; AMP3 showed the broadest activity among those tested, including MIC50 values of 15 μM against E. coli and 125 μM against P. aeruginosa. This is a small, model-assisted peptide panel built on a known sequence motif, not evidence of therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: HydrAMP deep-learning peptide sequence generator and AMPlify deep-learning antimicrobial-activity scorer
organization: University of Napoli Federico II

evidence.tested: Three peptides were synthesized and tested in vitro. The lead AMP3 had reported MIC50 values of 15 μM against E. coli and 125 μM against P. aeruginosa, with broader spectrum than AMP1/AMP2 in the tested panel.
evidence.unknown: The design starts from a known short Arg/Trp peptide motif and tests a very small selected set; clinical efficacy, safety, and broad-spectrum performance beyond the strains tested are unknown. The accessible source comparison establishes it is not the Pexiganan/Temporin-A wet-lab result reported in the earlier HydrAMP paper, but does not assert exhaustive sequence-prior-art completeness.
evidence.ai_role: HydrAMP generated candidate analogues from the AMP1 prototype; the AMPlify learned model scored antimicrobial propensity, followed by empirical candidate filtering and wet-lab testing.

source_review.scope: Primary Wiley publisher full-text indexed article including sequences, Methods, MIC results and publication date; PubMed metadata/abstract/affiliation; separate primary Nature Communications article reviewed to compare the prior HydrAMP wet-lab prototypes and results.

title: Uni-Mol screening guides experimental validation of β-sheet tetrapeptide assemblies
summary: A fine-tuned Uni-Mol model used simulation-derived data to screen 160,000 tetrapeptides. Researchers experimentally tested 26 selected tetrapeptide candidates: 15 formed β-sheet assemblies, including seven hydrogelators, as assessed with structural and assembly assays. The study reports experimental validation across 46 candidates overall; the 15/26 result is specific to the screened tetrapeptide set. This is a materials-science preprint, not evidence of medical function or clinical use. A related 2023 study explored tetrapeptide hydrogelation; this record makes no claim that every sequence is unprecedented and is limited to the present paper’s β-sheet structural validation.
ai_technology: Fine-tuned Uni-Mol machine-learning model for Amyloid-Like Tendency prediction, guided by hybrid-resolution molecular-dynamics simulations
organization: Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School

source_review.scope: ChemRxiv v1 page, full manuscript and Supplementary Information; official bioRxiv API metadata/abstract for cited 2025 computational preprint; primary 2023 hydrogel paper and linked supplementary-data index. Full-text source limits and the bounded result are stated.

evidence.tested: In the Uni-Mol-screened tetrapeptide set, 26 candidates were experimentally characterized; 15 formed β-sheet assemblies and seven were reported as hydrogelators. The authors also report validation of 46 candidates across the study overall.
evidence.unknown: The 46-candidate set combines tripeptide and tetrapeptide validations; the 15/26 result is specific to the tetrapeptides. The work is a preprint and establishes laboratory assembly outcomes only, not biomedical function, clinical utility, or independent replication. No claim is made that every sequence is unprecedented.
evidence.ai_role: Uni-Mol was fine-tuned on simulation-derived data and used to screen 160,000 tetrapeptides for Amyloid-Like Tendency; predictions guided candidate selection for further simulation and experimental structural characterization.

title: Iterative Gaussian process screening discovers selective aurein-derived antifungal peptides
summary: An uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression workflow iteratively selected 23 synthetic α/β-peptide analogues for synthesis and measurements of fungal inhibition and human-red-blood-cell hemolysis. One lead, peptide 6-4, was a measured variant of an existing aurein-derived template and achieved a selectivity index of 57.1 (60.9 using the study’s finer MIC interval) versus 1.2 for aurein 1.2. Its high selectivity was driven by low hemolysis; the result is a specific peptide-design and assay contribution, not a new peptide scaffold or evidence of therapeutic efficacy. The ChemRxiv v1 result was posted on 2024-10-04; the peer-reviewed journal article followed in 2025.
ai_technology: Iterative uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression using molecular descriptors and measured antifungal/hemolysis labels
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison

evidence.tested: Across six iterative rounds, uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression selected 23 peptide variants for synthesis and antifungal/hemolysis assays. Lead 6-4 had a selectivity index of 57.1 (60.9 using the study’s finer MIC interval), versus 1.2 for aurein 1.2; the authors attribute the selectivity to reduced hemolysis.
evidence.unknown: Peptide 6-4 modifies a known aurein-derived template. The result is a measured sequence and assay outcome, not evidence of a new scaffold or therapeutic efficacy. The version-specific first public result is the 2024 ChemRxiv preprint; the journal article followed in 2025.
evidence.ai_role: An uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression model selected peptide variants for synthesis and assays, and measured outcomes were fed back into subsequent selection rounds.

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv version-history record and v2 manuscript; primary RSC indexed full article PDF, including sequence tables, Results, Methods and publication metadata; PubMed primary abstract/affiliation metadata.

title: Family-specific machine learning prioritizes enzyme variants for prospective testing
summary: Researchers screened 1,513 natural SGNH-hydrolase homologues and trained task-specific sequence CNNs on the resulting activity, thermostability, and substrate-preference data. The models helped select candidates for a prospective 230-sequence assay panel, where CNN-selected candidates were enriched for target traits relative to generalist pretrained and physics-based baselines; the panel also included other selection strategies and random controls. Assays used clarified E. coli lysates and measured relative maximum velocity, integrating expression and catalysis. The first result-bearing version was posted to bioRxiv on 2026-06-03; a Research Square version followed on 2026-06-05.
ai_technology: Task-specific convolutional neural networks trained on amino-acid sequences; CNN-based HEV and UCB selection strategies
organization: CSIRO Environment

evidence.tested: A prospective panel of 230 previously untested sequences was assayed; CNN selection strategies were enriched for the predicted target traits compared with generalist pretrained and physics-based approaches. The panel pooled sequences selected by multiple strategies and included random controls.
evidence.unknown: Clarified lysate MaxV integrates enzyme expression and catalytic activity and is not a purified-enzyme turnover measurement. The result is scoped to this enzyme family and the reported assay setup; prospective panel composition was mixed across selection strategies.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised family-specific CNNs trained on sequence and assay data ranked untested homologues for activity, thermostability, and substrate preference, and guided candidate selection for prospective experimental testing.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 full text as indexed, including title, posting date, affiliations, methods, prospective assay results and limitations; primary Research Square v1 identity/date record.

title: Machine-learning screening guides ionic-liquid polymer electrolytes for lithium-metal batteries
summary: A machine-learning and quantum-chemistry workflow screened ionic liquids for conductivity and electrochemical-window properties, then guided selection for rigid-rod polyelectrolyte membranes. The 2022 preprint reports ~50 μm membranes and lithium-cell testing, including symmetric-cell cycling up to 800 hours at room temperature and reversible operation at 6 mA cm−2 at 80°C. Its preprint abstract reports 146 mAh g−1 at 5C/80°C; the later 2023 journal abstract lists 3C, so those version-specific figures are not conflated.
ai_technology: Graph-convolutional neural network and ensemble SVM/random-forest/XGBoost screening with Psi4 quantum-chemistry descriptors
organization: Fudan University

evidence.tested: The 2022 preprint reports a machine-learning/quantum-chemistry workflow that screened 2,356 ion pairs and recommended 40 for testing in rigid-rod polyelectrolyte membranes. It reports symmetric-cell cycling up to 800 hours at room temperature and reversible operation at 6 mA cm−2 at 80°C; its abstract reports 146 mAh g−1 at 5C/80°C.
evidence.unknown: The 2023 journal abstract reports the same study but gives 146 mAh g−1 at 3C rather than 5C. The record keeps the version-specific preprint metric separate and does not transfer it to the journal version. A publisher correction changes plot labels, not the core study claim.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models and quantum-chemistry calculations screened ionic-liquid properties and guided selection for experimental polymer-electrolyte membranes and cell testing.

source_review.scope: Primary Research Square v1 full-text PDF, including version date, affiliations, Methods and Results; primary Nature Communications journal article indexed text and metadata; primary publisher correction notice.

title: Machine-learning screening identifies bacterial-selective membrane-active compounds
summary: The June 2026 bioRxiv version describes an initial machine-learning-guided screen of ZINC20 compounds balancing predicted antibacterial activity, mammalian-cell toxicity, and mechanism-of-action novelty. Among 61 purchased candidates, six showed partial growth inhibition; 49 were non-toxic to HepG2 cells at 50 μM. Flow cytometry indicated membrane disruption for four of the six initial active hits and membrane depolarization for two. A September version reports additional screening and revised models; its expanded results are not attributed to the June version here. The study does not report a novel protein target or clinical antibiotic.
ai_technology: Graph-convolutional neural networks for antibacterial activity/toxicity with XGBoost mechanism-of-action classification and novelty filtering
organization: Princeton University

evidence.tested: The June 2026 v1 reports that 61 purchased candidates were tested, six showed partial growth inhibition, and 49/61 were non-toxic to HepG2 cells at 50 μM. Flow cytometry indicated membrane integrity disruption for four initial active hits and membrane depolarization for two.
evidence.unknown: The initial work does not report a novel protein target and is limited to the stated bacterial assays and HepG2 toxicity concentration. The September version adds expanded screening and revised analyses; those later results are not attributed to the June v1.
evidence.ai_role: Learned activity and toxicity models, together with a mechanism-novelty classifier, prioritized compounds for purchase and experimental testing.

source_review.scope: Primary PMC-indexed full text for the June bioRxiv v1, primary PubMed preprint abstract/metadata, and primary PMC/PubMed metadata for the later September version to distinguish version-specific results.

title: Machine-learning screening identifies two drug-repurposing candidates against tuberculosis
summary: A virtual-screening workflow combined XGBoost and graph-neural-network models to screen 11,576 DrugBank compounds. Researchers selected 15 candidates for evaluation; four met the study’s activity cutoff against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv. Aldoxorubicin and quarfloxin were further tested against multidrug-resistant isolates, intracellular bacteria and recombinant DNA gyrase. These are laboratory repurposing results, not evidence of patient benefit or clinical safety. A same-team patent-family publication predates the journal article; this record makes no priority claim over patent disclosures. Concentration values are omitted because of inconsistent units in the rendered tables.
ai_technology: Ensemble virtual screening with XGBoost and graph neural networks
organization: Institute for Artificial Intelligence & Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University

evidence.tested: The article reports follow-up testing of 15 selected compounds, four meeting the authors’ activity cutoff against H37Rv, and additional assays of aldoxorubicin and quarfloxin against multidrug-resistant isolates and recombinant DNA gyrase.
evidence.unknown: All reported results are in vitro. The study does not establish patient efficacy, clinical safety or the compounds’ cellular mechanism. Precise concentration values are omitted because table units are inconsistent; an earlier patent-family publication is noted without a priority claim.
evidence.ai_role: Multiple learned models, including XGBoost and graph neural networks, predicted antitubercular activity in a DrugBank screen and contributed to selection of candidates for experimental evaluation.

source_review.scope: Primary Oxford Academic full indexed article, including abstract, Methods, results, article history and author affiliations; patent-family chronology checked from the patent family page. A-version patent text was not reviewed.

title: AI-assisted virtual screening identifies a dual-stage antimalarial candidate
summary: An AI-assisted virtual-screening cascade using shape-based and machine-learning models prioritized potential Plasmodium kinase inhibitors. Eight virtual hits were experimentally evaluated; LabMol-167 inhibited P. berghei ookinete conversion and P. falciparum blood-stage parasites at nanomolar concentrations and showed low cytotoxicity in mammalian cells. A possible additional PK5 target was proposed from computational target fishing and docking, not demonstrated experimentally. This is a preclinical hit result and does not establish therapeutic efficacy. The article appeared online on 2021-03-16.
ai_technology: AI-assisted virtual screening combining shape-based and machine-learning models
organization: Federal University of Goiás

evidence.tested: Eight virtual hits were evaluated; LabMol-167 showed nanomolar activity in P. berghei ookinete conversion and P. falciparum blood-stage assays, with low mammalian-cell cytotoxicity.
evidence.unknown: The PK5 dual-target mechanism is proposed from computational target fishing and docking; in-vivo efficacy and clinical benefit are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Shape-based and machine-learning virtual screening prioritized candidates for experimental evaluation; the abstract explicitly links the integrated AI-assisted screen to this candidate-identification workflow.

source_review.scope: Primary PubMed abstract, publication metadata, and author-affiliation block; claim limited to the findings explicitly stated in the abstract.

title: Physics-informed machine learning guides experimental Curie-temperature validation in Ce–Zr–Fe alloys
summary: A machine-learning model trained on measured Curie temperatures selected two compositions in the (Zr1−xCex)Fe2 system, (Zr0.16Ce0.84)Fe2 and (Zr0.94Ce0.06)Fe2, for experimental validation. The study also reports a relationship between electronic states near the Fermi level and Curie temperature, including a breakdown of de Gennes scaling below a rare-earth-content threshold. This is a materials discovery study, not evidence of a finished permanent magnet or deployed technology.
ai_technology: Physics-informed machine-learning model trained on experimentally measured Curie temperatures
organization: Ames National Laboratory, U.S. Department of Energy; Iowa State University

evidence.tested: The authors selected (Zr0.16Ce0.84)Fe2 and (Zr0.94Ce0.06)Fe2 for experimental Curie-temperature validation of the model-guided predictions.
evidence.unknown: The exact Curie-temperature measurements and uncertainty are not included here. This study does not establish a finished permanent magnet, device-level performance, or zero-carbon deployment.
evidence.ai_role: A learned model trained on experimentally measured Curie temperatures was used to predict multicomponent magnetic-material properties and select the two Ce–Zr–Fe compositions for experimental validation. The paper also reports that the model captured electronic-structure trends associated with Curie temperature.
