title: Random-forest target selection supported nine millisecond pulsar discoveries
summary: A random-forest classifier ranked unidentified Fermi-LAT sources, from which the team selected 79 targets for MeerKAT UHF observations. This entry covers only the nine MSP discoveries. Six slower pulsars were also reported, but five were found in a wider incoherent beam and are not included in the AI-linked result. The authors note earlier optical redback-candidate identification for PSR J1910−5320 and single-pulse reports in the J0657−4657 beam; no claim is made that these were the first observations at all wavelengths.

organization: The University of Manchester; National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 full text for model-based target selection, coherent-beam results, affiliations and prior-source caveats; primary OUP indexed journal record and author-deposited peer-reviewed version for publication date and claim confirmation.

evidence.tested: The survey observed 79 random-forest-selected Fermi-LAT sources and reports nine new MSPs, all detected in coherent tied-array beams; seven were confirmed as Fermi-LAT counterparts through gamma-ray pulsations.

The paper also reports six slow pulsars, but five were detected in the wider incoherent beam and are not included in this AI-linked claim. The authors note an earlier optical redback-candidate identification for J1910−5320 and single-pulse reports from the J0657−4657 beam; the entry does not claim priority across wavelengths or treat those reports as prior radio-pulsar discoveries.
evidence.ai_role: A random-forest model ranked unassociated Fermi-LAT sources for target selection; radio searches of 79 selected targets yielded the nine coherent-beam MSP discoveries.

title: PICS-assisted survey reported seven new Small Magellanic Cloud pulsars

The paper does not identify each pulsar’s PICS score, so this is an AI-assisted survey-level result rather than a claim that the model independently discovered all seven sources. The paper also reports pulsar–nebula associations; the later timing paper follows this cohort and is not counted again.

organization: The University of Manchester; Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy; South African Radio Astronomy Observatory; INAF-Osservatorio Astronomico di Cagliari; University of Cape Town; Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics; Leibniz University Hannover; Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics; Western Sydney University

title: PICS-assisted survey reported seven new Large Magellanic Cloud pulsars
summary: A MeerKAT survey of its first four Large Magellanic Cloud pointings reported seven new radio pulsars. The search pipeline applied the Pulsar Image-based Classification System (PICS), a deep-neural image classifier, to folded candidates and retained candidates above a PICS score threshold before human visual classification. The AI narrowed the candidate set; volunteers performed the final candidate classification and follow-up observations supplied additional checks. Six pulsars were detected again in follow-up; the incoherent-beam pulsar was not. A later paper reports 12 discoveries from additional pointings and timing follow-up of some Paper I pulsars, which are not additional discoveries in this entry.
ai_technology: Pulsar Image-based Classification System (PICS), a deep-neural image classifier for folded candidate plots
organization: University of Cape Town

evidence.ai_role: PICS applied a pulsar-like score to folded candidate plots and filtered the survey candidate set before human visual classification; the paper does not attribute final discovery confirmation to the model alone.

title: Machine-learning variable selection supports 90-day heart-failure risk prediction
summary: In 3,189 patients hospitalized for heart failure, machine-learning variable selection supported a logistic model for 90-day acute-heart-failure readmission or death. LASSO selection and logistic regression yielded a reported AUC of 0.760, compared with 0.744 for logistic regression alone. This single-centre retrospective analysis used internal cross-validation; external performance and benefits from model-guided care were not tested.

title: Random forest evaluates two-year risks in a Japanese atrial-fibrillation registry
summary: Random forest models evaluated two-year thromboembolism, major bleeding and mortality risks in 7,406 patients from the J-RHYTHM atrial-fibrillation registry. Thromboembolism discrimination exceeded logistic regression (C-statistic 0.66 versus 0.59), while mortality discrimination was comparable. This retrospective model evaluation used internal cross-validation; participants were Japanese, most received warfarin, and no direct oral anticoagulants were used. Clinical benefits from using the predictions were not tested.

title: AI-QCT plaque measurements associate with cardiovascular events in CONSERVE
summary: A post hoc analysis applied Cleerly AI-QCT to coronary CT images from 747 participants in the selective-referral arm of CONSERVE. Quantified plaque burden was associated with one-year major cardiovascular events; event rates increased across plaque-volume categories. Estimated reductions in invasive angiography and costs were hypothetical decision-model outputs, not observed effects of randomized AI-guided care. Stenosis-based event discrimination was similar to clinical readers, and no blinded quantitative angiography comparison was available.

title: AutoParis-X quantifies longitudinal urine-cytology signals of bladder-cancer recurrence
summary: AutoParis-X extracted cell and cluster features from 1,259 urine specimens from 135 bladder-cancer patients to explore longitudinal recurrence markers. This exploratory retrospective study accounted for delayed entry but lacked external validation; treatment recording, sporadic follow-up and competing mortality limited inference. Clinical decision benefits remain untested.

title: TGFBIp expression adds prognostic information in an ovarian-cancer ML study
summary: In a retrospective tissue-microarray cohort of 155 epithelial ovarian-cancer patients, support vector machine and random forest models combined clinicopathological features with tumor and stromal TGFBIp expression. Adding both expression compartments improved held-out vital-status discrimination by a reported AUC difference of 0.038 (95% CI 0.002–0.092). Validation was internal, follow-up duration varied, and binary endpoints did not model event timing or censoring. Recurrence specificity and calibration were limited, and clinical utility remains unproven.

title: MRI radiomics supports individualized Duchenne disease-trajectory reconstruction
summary: XGBoost combined baseline MRI radiomics and clinical features to estimate muscle fat-fraction trajectory parameters in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The final dataset included 98 unique participants, with 68 soleus and 64 vastus-lateralis analyses; held-out reconstructed trajectories had reported mean absolute errors of 0.04 and 0.06. Targets came from a previously fitted nonlinear mixed-effects model, rather than directly observed trajectory parameters. The retrospective analysis identified candidate progression subgroups but did not establish treatment response, prospective prediction or external generalizability.

title: Label-free mitochondrial imaging distinguishes perturbed retinal-cell states
summary: AutoMitoNetwork combined learned image segmentation and support vector classification to analyze label-free mitochondrial images from a human retinal-cell line. Across 62 control, 65 respiration-inhibited and 62 glycolysis-inhibited cells, the study measured treatment-associated network changes and distinguished subtler perturbed states using combined image features. title: Elastic-net analysis links positive self-processing with reward motivation in depression
summary: Elastic-net models compared cognitive and physiological predictors of self-reported reward responsivity and approach motivation in 202 young adults spanning depression severity. Positive self-referential processing was the most robust, modest predictor; held-out variance explained ranged from 5.0–12.2% for approach motivation and 9.7–28.0% for reward responsivity. Nested cross-validation and a repeat assessment supported prediction within this restricted sample. These observational associations do not establish causal direction or an effective intervention.

title: External frozen-image study evaluates AI colorectal-polyp characterization
summary: An external study tested a ResNet152-based colorectal-polyp characterization system on 115 images from 66 patients, using histology as the reference. For diminutive polyps, reported negative predictive values were 80% with white light and 90.9% with image enhancement, with wide confidence intervals; surveillance-interval agreement exceeded 90%. title: Wearable-data models evaluate near-term binge-eating risk
summary: In a four-week observational study of 30 adults with recurrent binge eating, random-forest models used smartwatch physiology or self-reported affect to evaluate episode risk. The first three weeks trained models and the final week tested them within the same participants. Sensor-only AUROC was 0.78, with sensitivity 0.92 but specificity 0.35; macro-averaged accuracy did not significantly exceed self-report. No model met both prespecified sensitivity and specificity thresholds, and benefits from adaptive intervention remain untested.

title: Deep-learning chest-radiograph pressure estimates associate with heart-failure prognosis
summary: A post hoc analysis of 534 acute-heart-failure admissions applied a previously developed VGG16-based model to estimate pulmonary arterial wedge pressure from chest radiographs. Higher discharge estimates and smaller decreases during hospitalization were associated with death or heart-failure readmission after adjustment; 223 patients reached the composite endpoint. This single-centre observational analysis does not establish a causal treatment target or improved care. Imaging-view differences and exclusion of in-hospital deaths limit interpretation.

title: Random-forest screening identifies a breast-cancer growth-suppressing role for PCAT19
summary: A random-forest survival model helped prioritize lncRNAs from 1054 breast-cancer expression profiles; overlap with differential expression and a separate expression database nominated PCAT19. Knocking down PCAT19 increased proliferation in two breast-cancer cell lines, while overexpression reduced xenograft growth in mice. The work supports a preclinical growth-suppressing role, not a validated treatment. Predicted regulatory networks remain hypotheses, and inconsistent clinical-prognosis wording is not used to establish patient benefit.

title: Speech language features predict six-year Alzheimer dementia progression in a small cohort
summary: In 166 Framingham Heart Study participants with mild cognitive impairment, pretrained language embeddings of recorded cognitive-test transcripts supported retrospective prediction of progression to Alzheimer dementia within six years. Nested, participant-grouped cross-validation gave the text-only model an AUC of 0.778 and accuracy of 78.2%. The predominantly White, older cohort and lack of prospective external validation limit generalization; this is not a demonstrated screening or treatment benefit.

title: MRI edema grades improve retrospective neural-network prognosis for Guillain–Barré syndrome
summary: A two-institution retrospective study used a shallow neural network to estimate residual symptoms six months after discharge in 354 Guillain–Barré syndrome patients. The model includes a muscle-strength score measured at discharge, so it is not an admission-only forecast. External testing used 118 patients from a second institution; treatment benefit and prospective deployment were not tested.

summary: Spatially aware neural fitting of diffusion MRI was evaluated in 20 previously studied glioma patients with WHO grade references. summary: A random forest evaluated acute coronary syndrome in 2,400 emergency chest-pain patients using demographics, medical history and neighborhood measures. title: Random forests identify surface geometry relationships associated with reduced bacterial attachment
summary: A screen of 2176 polymer surface patterns supplied measurements for random-forest models linking geometry to bacterial attachment. Held-out topographies supported predictive associations between attachment and surface coverage, feature size and spacing; the models outperformed a simpler roughness descriptor. title: Multitask neural screening identifies compounds active against Leishmania infantum in vitro
summary: Multitask neural classification and regression screened approximately 1.3 million purchasable compounds for Leishmania infantum activity. After physicochemical and human structural filtering, 20 selected compounds were tested; nine inhibited promastigotes in vitro. Three had more favorable source-reported selectivity, with LC-15 showing an IC50 of 1.05 µM and selectivity index 30.9. LC-15 was already disclosed in a 2023 antitrypanosomal study; this entry represents the Leishmania result, not a new chemical entity. Intracellular parasite activity, animal efficacy and a proposed proteasome mechanism were not established.

LC-15 is the same chemical entity disclosed in the 2023 antitrypanosomal study, whose supplement also reports the same MRC-5 cytotoxicity value; independently new cytotoxicity evidence is not inferred. Its proteasome mechanism remains a hypothesis, and the observed hit rate is not a controlled comparison with conventional screening.
evidence.ai_role: Multitask DNN classifiers and regressors transferred information across three Leishmania species to prioritize untested molecules; physicochemical filters, similarity analysis and human inspection then selected 20 for experiments.

Earlier metadata lookup had retrieved a different paper and is not used as evidence. Compared the original 2023 and 2024 author supplements by exact LC-15 chemical name, structure, supplier identifier and NMR evidence; the represented novelty is the Leishmania assay, not chemical-entity novelty.

summary: A two-level nearest-neighbor classifier used dynamic resting-state MRI features to distinguish bipolar-depression patients with a recent suicide-attempt history. title: Automated fat measurements associate with prostate therapy survival
summary: Deep-learning body segmentation measured fat compartments on routine PET/CT in 86 men receiving PSMA radioligand therapy. A higher intramuscular-fat proportion was associated with shorter overall survival, with volumetric measurements adding information beyond a single lumbar slice in the same cohort. This retrospective association does not establish a causal effect of fat, independent prediction or improved treatment selection.
ai_technology: Body and Organ Analysis; deep-learning CT segmentation
organization: University Hospital Münster; University of Münster; West German Cancer Centre

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Clinical overall-survival associations of automated three-dimensional and single-slice fat measurements, with multivariable analysis in 86 treated patients.
evidence.unknown: Independent validation and clinical decision benefit remain unestablished; selection, limited sample size and model fitting/evaluation in the same cohort can produce optimistic estimates.
evidence.ai_role: The pretrained BOA segmentation framework delineates body compartments to derive volumetric fat fractions for clinical survival-association analysis.

title: AI imaging measures change during cardiac amyloidosis treatment
summary: Automated cardiac segmentation quantified serial SPECT/CT scans in 45 patients receiving transthyretin amyloidosis therapies. Several tracer-uptake markers decreased after treatment, and selected changes were associated with functional measures. These exploratory observational results do not prove treatment causality or removal of amyloid deposits; affected-volume measures did not significantly decline.
ai_technology: TotalSegmentator; foundational deep-learning CT segmentation
organization: Medical University of Vienna; University Hospital Essen

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Serial baseline/follow-up clinical imaging, automated cardiac-region quantification and exploratory associations with functional measurements.
evidence.unknown: Controlled treatment effects, cross-scanner generalizability and clinical decision benefit remain unestablished; the paper has inconsistent aggregate marker counts and small treatment subgroups.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained anatomical segmentation network maps cardiac structures to SPECT, enabling standardized regional tracer measurements over time.

title: Learned immune phenotypes associate with lung cancer survival
summary: Unsupervised clustering identified two lung-adenocarcinoma immune-expression patterns, and a random forest assigned tumors in additional cohorts. The more immune-infiltrated pattern was associated with better overall survival, including in external gene-expression datasets. This observational classification does not establish treatment response or a causal protective effect of immune infiltration; immunotherapy outcomes were not available for validation.
ai_technology: Consensus unsupervised clustering; random forest
organization: Fudan University; Zhongshan Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Expression-derived phenotypes in 514 TCGA tumors, with classifier assignment and survival comparisons in 1,063 GEO tumors and a 34-patient institutional cohort.
evidence.unknown: Prospective treatment-response utility and causal biology remain unestablished; immune-cell abundance is inferred from bulk expression and aggregate patient totals differ between the abstract and full text.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised clustering learns infiltration patterns and a random forest transfers those patterns to additional cohorts for clinical survival-association analysis.

title: Neural heart measurements reveal a chest-pain risk association
summary: Two U-Net models measured heart volume in CT scans from 3,798 PROMISE participants. Smaller body-size-indexed volume was associated with subsequent major adverse events, particularly in patients with non-obstructive coronary disease. This retrospective secondary analysis is hypothesis-generating; it does not establish a causal mechanism, a normal-volume threshold or improved clinical decisions.
ai_technology: Cascaded U-Net convolutional neural networks
organization: Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School; Duke University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Automated CT measurements linked to independently adjudicated events over median 26-month follow-up in a randomized-trial cohort.
evidence.unknown: Independent prognostic validation and clinical utility remain unestablished; patients with known coronary disease or heart failure were excluded and subgroup event counts were limited.
evidence.ai_role: Two pretrained U-Nets localize and segment the heart, enabling standardized volumetric measurements for clinical event-association analysis.

title: CT learning detects gastric cancer downstaging after chemotherapy
summary: Linear support-vector models analyzed baseline and restaging CT in a retrospective 292-patient gastric-cancer study. Models were evaluated in two separate testing cohorts against downstaging defined by baseline clinical and postoperative pathological stages; restaging AUCs were 0.922 and 0.850. The study did not demonstrate improved surgical decisions, and selected images, small same-centre tests and inconsistent abstract cohort labels limit interpretation.
ai_technology: Linear support-vector classifier; radiomic feature selection
organization: Nanjing University; Jinling Hospital; Deepwise

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Model development with nested cross-validation, followed by two held-out same-centre clinical testing cohorts and a postoperative pathology-based stage reference.
evidence.unknown: Prospective decision benefit and multicentre generalization remain unestablished; clinical baseline staging can be inaccurate, and low-quality images were excluded.
evidence.ai_role: Linear support-vector classifiers learn relationships between selected CT texture features and recorded post-chemotherapy downstaging.

title: Learned MRI markers associate with subtle cognitive decline
summary: Previously trained support-vector and relevance-vector models generated Alzheimer-like atrophy and brain-age scores in 80 cognitively intact older adults followed for 4.5 years. Scores were associated with decline in specific visuospatial or executive tests, rather than global cognition. No participant developed mild cognitive impairment; the small selected cohort does not establish dementia prediction or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Support-vector machine; relevance-vector regression; AD-RAI; BrainAGE
organization: University of Geneva; Geneva University Hospitals; Technical University of Munich; Jena University Hospital; University of Freiburg

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Independent pretrained MRI scores related to longitudinal neuropsychological changes, with observational regression comparisons in 80 participants.
evidence.unknown: Dementia conversion, independent prognostic replication and clinical utility remain unestablished; multiple domain tests and the healthy, educated cohort limit interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on separate MRI cohorts quantify Alzheimer-like atrophy and age-related structural patterns, enabling associations with subsequently recorded domain-specific cognitive change.

title: Learned CT perfusion patterns correlate with pulmonary hypertension
summary: A Bayesian Gaussian-mixture model separated lung attenuation patterns after neural segmentation in CT scans from 52 patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. A larger normal-attenuation fraction was associated with lower pulmonary vascular resistance and other measured severity indicators. These single-centre correlations do not establish causality, prognosis or replacement of catheter measurements.
ai_technology: Variational Bayesian Gaussian-mixture model; TotalSegmentator
organization: Charles University; Motol University Hospital; Brno University of Technology

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Automated CT measures compared with invasive hemodynamics, clinical biomarkers and radiologist annotations, with multiple-comparison correction.
evidence.unknown: External clinical utility and outcome prediction remain unestablished; a fixed three-component assumption and scanner/artifact effects can alter inferred tissue classes.
evidence.ai_role: A learned mixture model fits patient-specific attenuation distributions while a pretrained neural network delineates lungs and veins for spatial quantification.

title: Ultrasound neural maps identify pathology-defined prostate cancer tissue
summary: A three-dimensional CNN and multilayer perceptron combined quantitative ultrasound features to map clinically significant prostate cancer. Development involved 250 patients, followed by 77 later-enrolled patients; reported voxel-level AUC was 0.884 in that later group. Pathology registration and a surgical-enriched cohort limit interpretation. This does not establish patient-level diagnostic accuracy, biopsy benefit or equivalence to MRI-guided care.
ai_technology: Three-dimensional convolutional neural network; multilayer perceptron
organization: Eindhoven University of Technology; Amsterdam UMC; Leiden University Medical Center; Angiogenesis Analytics

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Patient-partitioned development and temporally separate same-centre testing, using reconstructed prostatectomy pathology or negative MRI/biopsy references.
evidence.unknown: Lesion/patient-level clinical performance and treatment benefit remain unestablished; entire-dataset feature standardization and registration uncertainty limit a strictly untouched-test interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Three CNN feature branches learn ultrasound patterns and an MLP combines them into voxel-level cancer probability maps.

title: Chest radiograph learning estimates invasively measured filling pressure
summary: A VGG16-based regression network estimated pulmonary artery wedge pressure from chest radiographs in 936 cardiovascular patients. In 188 held-out patients, estimates correlated moderately with catheter measurements (r = 0.62), with wide agreement limits around plus or minus 11 mmHg and underestimation at high pressures. This clinical measurement study does not establish catheter replacement, prognosis or improved care.
ai_technology: VGG16-based regression convolutional neural network
organization: Nihon University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Separate 188-patient internal test against right-heart catheter pressure, after model tuning within the 748-patient development set.
evidence.unknown: External clinical utility remains unestablished; radiographs and catheter measurements were not simultaneous, high pressures were underestimated and several lung/device conditions were excluded.
evidence.ai_role: A transfer-learned convolutional network regresses radiograph features onto measured pulmonary artery wedge pressure.

title: Neural pathology quantification links enlarged brain spaces to vascular amyloid
summary: Convolutional models quantified vascular amyloid and related pathology in donated brain tissue. In 19 cerebral-amyloid-angiopathy cases, enlarged perivascular spaces were associated with amyloid burden in overlying vessels after accounting for other pathology. Paired MRI and histology supported anatomical interpretation. Cross-sectional autopsy findings do not establish impaired clearance as the cause or the sequence of changes.
ai_technology: Aiforia convolutional neural networks; three-dimensional U-Net; SmartInterpol
organization: Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School; University College London; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Leiden University Medical Center

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Cross-sectional autopsy tissue quantification, regional MRI/histology comparisons and mixed-effects association analysis in 19 amyloid-angiopathy cases.
evidence.unknown: Causal direction, clearance dynamics and population generalizability remain unestablished; the selected donation cohort was small and automated in-vivo MRI segmentation was not reliable.
evidence.ai_role: Validated CNNs quantify vascular amyloid/fibrin pathology, while learned high-resolution MRI segmentation supports regional anatomical analysis.

title: Learning classifies severe paraspinal muscle fatty infiltration
summary: XGBoost classified severe multifidus fatty infiltration in a retrospective 316-patient lumbar-surgery cohort, using MRI-defined infiltration as the reference. Internal validation reported AUC 0.87, with age, sex and facet degeneration prominent among model features. Pre-split imputation and feature ranking can inflate performance; these cross-sectional associations do not show causes, future deterioration or improved surgical outcomes.
ai_technology: XGBoost; random-forest feature ranking and imputation
organization: Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Hospital for Special Surgery; University Hospital Ulm

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Recorded preoperative characteristics compared with MRI-defined severe muscle fatty infiltration using a 70:30 internal patient split.
evidence.unknown: Independent clinical utility and causal direction remain unestablished; preprocessing/feature ranking before partitioning and the surgical-only population constrain interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Gradient-boosted trees learn clinical/imaging associations with severe fatty infiltration, allowing classification and exploratory feature ranking.

title: EQTransformer expands the earthquake catalog for the 2000 Tottori sequence
summary: An attention-based neural detector and phase picker reanalyzed five weeks of seismic recordings from the 2000 western Tottori earthquake sequence. Using 18 stations, the study detected and located 21,092 events, compared with 8521 in an earlier manually picked catalog using 57 stations. The inferred catalog included smaller events and sparse seismicity beneath the eastern flank of Mount Daisen. These are retrospective source-reported detections and locations, not individually independently confirmed new earthquakes or a forecasting result.
ai_technology: EQTransformer; hierarchical attention; convolutional and recurrent neural networks
organization: Stanford University; Georgia Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: A model trained without Japanese waveform data was applied to 18 Japanese stations. Phase association and relocation yielded 21,092 events. Approximately 42,000 common phase picks were compared with human picks; about 15%of associated events were not retained in the final catalog.
evidence.unknown: Newly inferred events were not each independently confirmed. Simple phase association and station coverage limit catalog completeness and error assessment; no earthquake forecast or new physical mechanism is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: A multitask attentive neural network detected earthquake waveforms and picked P/S arrivals; conventional association and relocation then converted those learned measurements into the regional event catalog.

source_review.scope: Primary full model Methods and regional application Results; exact current PubMed DOI/title and publisher date/status. The qualifying result is the Tottori field catalog, beyond generic detector benchmarking.

title: Random-forest screening helps identify kinase inhibitors with activity against two malaria targets
summary: A random-forest classifier combined with molecular docking helped select five known kinase inhibitors for experimental evaluation. Afatinib and pexidartinib inhibited both synthetic hemozoin formation and the malaria parasite protein kinase G in vitro; their kinase IC 50 values were about 2.6 micromolar, and hemozoin-formation inhibition required much higher concentrations. The strongest compounds in the overall study came from a separate selection route based on chemical-space mapping and docking. These results identify laboratory starting points, not an effective malaria treatment.
ai_technology: Random-forest classifier
organization: Stellenbosch University; University of Cape Town; GenAIRx

evidence.tested: Five purchased compounds belonged to the random-forest-plus-docking selection route, including one shared with the other route. Afatinib and pexidartinib each had protein-kinase-G IC 50 values around 2.6 micromolar and synthetic-hemozoin-formation IC 50 values of 230 and 140 micromolar, respectively.
evidence.unknown: These are in vitro enzyme and crystallization assays, not clinical efficacy or safety. The most promising overall compounds were selected without the random forest. The small test set does not establish one selection route as superior. PMC and Crossref record online publication on 15 February 2026 and an earlier issue date of 12 February; this entry uses the online date.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest trained on 379 literature compounds and 1190 molecular fingerprint features predicted protein-kinase-G activity. Its probability threshold, applicability-domain filter and docking scores selected five purchased compounds; PCA enrichment and docking formed a separate route.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text Methods, compound-level selection table and assays, exact article-front DOI/title/PMCID, deposited date metadata and current PubMed publication-status metadata.

title: Explainable regression guides laboratory tests of malaria candidates
summary: Piecewise-regression models learned activity relationships from 386 Open Source Malaria compounds and prioritized fragments for a commercial-library search. Researchers tested 22 selected compounds and followed three in concentration-response and human-cell cytotoxicity assays. A02 and A10 showed qualitatively consistent parasite-growth inhibition across the initial screen and follow-up curves. The third candidate, A22, has an unresolved screen-versus-curve discrepancy. These are modest-potency laboratory starting points, without established treatment efficacy or secure strongest-hit and selectivity claims.
ai_technology: modSAR supervised piecewise linear regression; SHAP
organization: King's College London; London School of Economics and Political Science; London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine; University College London

evidence.tested: Twenty-two model-prioritized commercial compounds underwent direct parasite-growth screening. A02 and A10 showed consistent qualitative inhibition across screen and follow-up; the paper additionally reports A22 concentration-response and human-cell cytotoxicity measurements, with its conflicting screen result retained.
evidence.unknown: Clinical efficacy, mechanism and independent replication are unestablished. A 22 shows only 18.6% mean inhibition at 10 micromolar in the initial screen despite a later reported IC 50 of 8.29 micromolar; the discrepancy is unresolved, so exact potency and selectivity are not represented as secure estimates.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted model learns fingerprint breakpoints and region-specific activity coefficients, prioritizing fragments and predicting activity to narrow 934 commercial compounds to 97, then 22 after additional chemical filters.

source_review.scope: Primary author-institution-deposited published version read through indexed PDF text for Methods, fragment-to-test selection, experimental results and front metadata; matched third-party journal-PDF figure inspected separately, with access distinction and numerical inconsistency retained. Current PubMed notice metadata checked.

title: Multitask neural screening identifies four experimentally active antitrypanosomal hits
summary: Multitask neural activity models guided identification of four experimentally active compounds. This record represents the antitrypanosomal assay result, not four unprecedented chemical entities. LC-15 also appears in a later Leishmania study, which is a separate measured result.
ai_technology: Multitask feedforward and message-passing neural networks
organization: Federal University of Goiás; University of Brasília

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports four experimental hits. Official supplementary computational tables compare multitask classification/regression with single-task baselines.
evidence.unknown: Main article Methods were inaccessible; operational assays were not reviewed. No mechanism, animal or clinical efficacy, absolute chemical novelty, or independent replication is claimed. Publisher online September 13 differs from the August issue date in indexing metadata.
evidence.ai_role: Multitask neural models learn compound activity across related tasks and prioritize experimental candidates.

source_review.scope: Primary abstract/front, fresh bibliographic status metadata and official supplementary computational tables. Previously reviewed exact LC-15 identity comparison reused without reopening structures or procedures.

title: Neural-network screening guides a tested soft-magnetic iron alloy
summary: An artificial neural network fitted literature magnetic-property measurements and guided selection of Fe83B9P3C4Nb1 for synthesis. The annealed ribbon showed saturation magnetic flux density of 1.71 tesla and coercivity of 0.5 amperes per metre. These are laboratory measurements of one selected composition, without established broad predictive accuracy or device benefit.
ai_technology: Artificial neural network regression
organization: Guilin University of Electronic Technology

evidence.tested: One model-selected alloy was synthesized, structurally characterized and magnetically measured in as-spun and annealed states.
evidence.unknown: The March 2022 preprint already reports this composition and experimental verification; quoted measurements come from the later journal version. Predicted coercivity differed substantially.
evidence.ai_role: An ANN learned composition-property relationships; predicted magnetic-property filters narrowed a combinatorial composition search before experimental selection.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary journal Methods/results and exact SSRN posted-date/abstract evidence; current publisher and Crossref metadata checked.

title: Active learning guides a tested ternary hydrogen-evolution catalyst
summary: Gaussian-process active learning guided nanoparticle experiments using metal-precursor ratios. A Pt0.65Ru0.30Ni0.05 precursor mixture yielded a catalyst requiring 54.2 millivolts overpotential at 20 milliamperes per square centimetre, versus 68.2 for similarly prepared platinum. The final particles differed from the precursor composition. This laboratory result does not establish commercial electrolyzer performance.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process regression; active learning
organization: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology; Seoul National University; Harvard University; Kookmin University

evidence.tested: Iteratively selected catalysts underwent synthesis, microscopy, elemental characterization and acidic-electrolyte hydrogen-evolution measurements against same-method comparators.
evidence.unknown: The precursor ratio is not the measured particle stoichiometry. Independent replication, commercial durability and broad model generalization remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: A Gaussian process maps eight-component precursor fractions to overpotential; uncertainty and predicted performance guide experiments whose measurements update the model.

source_review.scope: Author-deposited primary full Methods/results through indexed PDF, exact front identity, publisher online date and current PubMed notice metadata.

title: Generative models estimate higher-order plant co-occurrence patterns
summary: A generative model fitted to 5153 observed plant patches in four Spanish dryland communities estimated that conditioning on additional species often weakens positive lower-order co-occurrence associations, with species-specific exceptions. The conditional frequencies were estimated from model-generated patches, not 300000 field observations. This is a descriptive relationship in a learned distribution; it does not establish causal ecological interactions or actual succession.
ai_technology: Generative adversarial networks fitted to species-presence distributions
organization: University of Valencia; Spanish National Research Council; University of Sussex

evidence.tested: GAN models learned joint species-presence distributions from 5153 recorded vegetation patches. Generated composition abundance and soil-affinity patterns were compared with the observed data; higher-order conditional association estimates were derived from generated configurations.
evidence.unknown: The specific third- and fourth-order conditional frequencies were not independently checked in held-out field data. Generated patches and repeated model initializations are not independent field replication. Co-occurrence does not prove competition, facilitation or other mechanisms. VAE-generated succession, pioneer rankings and restoration benefits are outside this record; reconstruction accuracy is not ecological forecast accuracy.
evidence.ai_role: GANs learn the high-dimensional joint distribution of plant presence and supply conditional co-occurrence estimates that describe how associations change when additional species are present.

source_review.scope: Full primary author-deposited published PDF front, input/model Methods, conditional-association Results and Discussion, plus independent Sol ecological-scope review and fresh primary publication metadata.

title: Learned anomaly search identifies three previously unlisted gravitational-lens candidates
summary: A learned image-representation and human-feedback anomaly search prioritized unusual sources in nearly four million galaxy images. The study identified three gravitational-lens candidates absent from the catalogs it cross-matched, alongside five previously listed lens systems. These are image-based candidates rather than newly confirmed lenses; spectroscopy and more reliable redshift information are needed to establish their physical nature.
ai_technology: EfficientNetB0 image representations; isolation forest; active learning with human feedback
organization: University of the Western Cape; South African Radio Astronomy Observatory; University of Manchester; University of Toronto; National Centre for Nuclear Research

evidence.tested: Visual inspection of learned-ranked DECaLS sources yielded three previously unlisted candidates, source labelsL6–L8. The source distinguishes one known confirmed lens and four known lens candidates from these three newly proposed objects.
evidence.unknown: The three objects are suspected lenses based on image morphology, not spectroscopically confirmed systems. Source photometric redshifts are unreliable for lens interpretation, and chance alignments remain possible. The broader 1635 anomaly count includes known objects and merger candidates and is not a count of newly established physical discoveries. This record dates the fully read March 29,2024 arXiv version; an earlier September 15,2023 version exists, with no absolute earliest-priority claim.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained EfficientNetB0 network supplies learned image representations. Isolation forest and active learning incorporating human interest scores prioritize objects for visual examination, leading to the specific three new lens-candidate proposals.

source_review.scope: Full relevant primary arXiv v2 image/model Methods, candidate-specific Table3 and lens interpretation limitations; exact version history and current journal publication-status metadata.

title: Machine learning identifies a synthesis-time relationship in oxygen-reduction catalysts
summary: Learned models ranked factors in 225 literature-derived catalyst records and highlighted pyrolysis duration alongside temperature. Researchers then varied these conditions in iron-nitrogen-carbon catalysts and measured a volcano-like relationship between duration and oxygen-reduction half-wave potential, alongside changes in nitrogen species. This is a laboratory synthesis-performance relationship, not proof that model importance alone establishes an atomic mechanism or that the result generalizes to other catalyst families.
ai_technology: Supervised tree ensembles; artificial neural networks; SHAP feature interpretation
organization: Nanjing University

evidence.tested: Model-guided control experiments varied pyrolysis duration and temperature in ZIF-derived Fe-N-C catalysts, with electrochemical measurements and nitrogen-species characterization.
evidence.unknown: Feature importance is associative; the represented relationship does not establish every proposed atomic mechanism. Independent replication, other catalyst families and practical fuel-cell benefits remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Nine learned model families, including tree ensembles and neural networks, related catalyst properties and synthesis parameters to activity and pyridinic-nitrogen content; model interpretation prioritized duration for controlled experiments.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher front metadata and abstract; complete official supplementary modeling, synthesis and characterization sections, including model-importance tables and control-series captions. Main article body was paywalled and not read. Current Crossref update relationships checked.

title: Learned photocatalyst recommendations identify a productive ruthenium alternative for an ATRA reaction
summary: A reaction-language model trained on literature examples recommended photocatalysts for a previously reported atom-transfer radical addition reaction. A ruthenium catalyst omitted from the original catalyst screen gave the highest yield among the catalysts tested in the new study, with productive results also observed for two related substrates. This is a specific measured catalyst–reaction result within known chemistry, rather than discovery of a new transformation or proof that model confidence predicts yield.
ai_technology: BERT-based reaction-language model for photocatalyst recommendation
organization: University of St Andrews; Allchemy; Institute of Organic Chemistry, Polish Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: Top-five model recommendations were tested in the published ATRA system, with quantitative NMR yields from two independent experiment repeats. Source-labelled Ru1 was absent from the original screen and gave the highest measured yield among the newly compared catalysts; two related substrates also gave productive outcomes.
evidence.unknown: The journal also evaluates other known reactions, but the represented finding is this specific catalyst alternative. Yield depends on photoreactor/light setup; the authors observe a discrepancy with an earlier eosin-Y result and explicitly state model confidence does not track yield. Co-catalysts, additives and reaction conditions are not model inputs. An earlier July 2025 preprint differs in the number of evaluated reactions; this record uses the fully read December 2025 journal version without claiming earliest public disclosure.
evidence.ai_role: The learned language model maps substrate and reaction-core representations to rankings over 31 photocatalysts, selecting a previously unscreened catalyst alternative for subsequent laboratory comparison.

source_review.scope: Full primary journal/PMC data curation, BERT-model Methods, ATRA experiments/Fig3–4 captions and discussion; exact front identity/date and fresh primary notice metadata. Earlier preprint-version result equivalence not asserted.

title: Active learning guides copper-alloy catalysts with improved acetate selectivity
summary: An active-learning workflow combined learned adsorption-energy prediction with first-principles calculations to nominate copper–silver and copper–palladium catalyst compositions. Both synthesized candidates showed higher acetate selectivity than the pure-copper comparator in laboratory carbon-monoxide electrolysis. The result concerns these measured catalysts and conditions; mechanistic interpretation additionally depends on computational modelling, and commercial performance is not established.
ai_technology: Random-forest and XGBoost adsorption-energy prediction; active learning with first-principles calculations
organization: Worcester Polytechnic Institute

evidence.tested: Learned-model-nominated Cu/Ag(3:1) and Cu/Pd(2:1) candidates were synthesized, characterized and evaluated against pure Cu in a zero-gap CO electrolyzer. Both improved measured acetate selectivity.
evidence.unknown: The abstract and Results reverse the 47%/50% Faradaic-efficiency assignment between the two alloys; this record therefore does not assign those exact values or rank the alloys. It represents the final 2025 CO-electroreduction study, not an earlier differently titled CO2 preprint. Absolute first-public priority and full preprint-version equivalence are unestablished. Mechanistic predictions, global optimality, industrial lifetime and deployment are outside the represented finding.
evidence.ai_role: Starting from 55 simulated alloy systems and 76 descriptors, iterative learned adsorption-energy prediction and new DFT calculations refine candidate selection. Random forest is the initial model and XGBoost the final comparison winner; the workflow selects the two compositions subsequently tested.

source_review.scope: Full primary journal/PMC text: exact identity, active-learning Methods, alloy selection, synthesis characterization, experimental Results/Fig8 caption and numerical-conflict caveat. Fresh primary bibliographic/status metadata.

title: Iterative learning guides discovery of a cobalt-doped nitride battery catalyst
summary: Iteratively updated regression models screened transition-metal compositions and guided synthesis of three candidate battery catalysts. Cobalt-doped molybdenum nitride, Co 0.1 Mo 0.9 N, showed the best reported performance of these candidates in laboratory lithium-carbon-dioxide and lithium-air cells. Reported low overpotentials were measured at 50 milliamperes per gram; they do not establish commercial cell performance or broad model accuracy.
ai_technology: Iterative supervised regression; random forest; Gaussian-process regression; XGBoost; nearest-neighbor regression
organization: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China; Zhejiang University

evidence.tested: Three selected catalyst compositions were synthesized and characterized; Co 0.1 Mo 0.9 N was evaluated against MoN and carbon-nanotube cathode comparators in laboratory battery tests.
evidence.unknown: Generalization is not established by the reported 0.106-volt mean absolute error on only three selected candidates. Practical battery durability, manufacturing and device-level benefit are unestablished; reported overpotential depends on current density and cell conditions.
evidence.ai_role: Regression models learned catalyst-descriptor/overpotential relationships, with measurements added across five iterations before screening 15012 compositions and selecting three for synthesis.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher article-front metadata and abstract, complete official author supporting information Methods/model tables/experimental characterizations and result captions, and current PubMed notice metadata. Paywalled main article body was not read; no independent replication performed.

title: Learned screening identifies early antiviral candidates with enzyme and cell-entry assay activity
summary: A two-stage learned screen combined SchNet molecular representations with XGBoost to prioritize compounds for laboratory evaluation. Follow-up assays identified early candidates with protease-inhibition and cell-entry activity, with additional cell and human-airway tissue-model tests. These are moderate-potency laboratory hits; direct target binding, clinical benefit and reduced resistance were not established.
ai_technology: SchNet molecular graph classification; XGBoost candidate prioritization
organization: National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, National Institutes of Health; Texas Biomedical Research Institute; National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

evidence.tested: The learned screen prioritized roughly 500 compounds from about 170000 library entries. The source reports 27 initial follow-up hits and examines a smaller representative subset using enzyme, cell-entry, cell-based and 3D airway-tissue assays. Four of eight detailed representatives showed moderate protease inhibition; others primarily showed entry-assay activity.
evidence.unknown: This is not evidence that every hit has a confirmed dual mechanism. Direct specific target binding remains unconfirmed; aggregation or protein-destabilization artifacts were not excluded. Some tissue-model effects coincide with cytotoxicity, and incomplete inhibition complicates potency estimates. Reduced resistance, patient efficacy and a clinical therapeutic window were not tested. The current readable journal version is represented; the publisher version-history endpoint was rate-limited, so exact timing of any later text updates is unresolved.
evidence.ai_role: SchNet learns molecular representations from prior screening measurements and filters library compounds; a second learned XGBoost layer incorporates descriptors to prioritize candidates before new laboratory measurements.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front DOI/title/date and fresh primary notice metadata; computational model/data Methods and high-level assay results/limitations read. No operational pathogen procedures represented or archived in the case evidence.

title: Learned reaction models guide improved yields for three ester hydrogenations
summary: Learned models of ruthenium-catalysed ester hydrogenation guided laboratory condition choices for four previously studied substrates. Three experiments gave higher alcohol yields than the corresponding literature conditions; a fourth failed despite a high predicted yield. The represented result is a bounded improvement of known reactions, rather than a new catalyst, transformation or universally accurate yield predictor.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process regression and comparative learned reaction models
organization: University of Cambridge; Université Paris Cité; University of St Andrews

evidence.tested: The journal paper reports measured alcohol yields of 96%,63% and 99% compared with corresponding literature values of 3%,0% and 32%. The fourth experiment yielded below 1% despite an 84% model prediction.
evidence.unknown: An earlier matching preprint,10.26434/chemrxiv-2022-t1zsn, is dated January 10,2022; its full original body was not authenticated, so this record uses the documented May 1,2023 journal version and does not claim first public priority. The substrates and catalysts were known; improvements concern these conditions, not new chemical entities or general catalyst superiority. Prediction errors and high-yield-biased data limit generalization.
evidence.ai_role: Learned regressors map substrate/catalyst descriptors and reaction conditions to measured yield and guide new condition choices subsequently tested in the laboratory.

source_review.scope: Full primary author-deposited journal PDF front, learned-model Methods, experimental validation and Table2; exact matching preprint relationship and current Crossref status. Journal-version result represented; original preprint result content not asserted.

title: Learned screening helps identify pralatrexate antiviral activity in cell assays
summary: A hybrid screen combined learned drug–protein binding predictions with molecular simulations to select four existing drugs for laboratory evaluation. The study found antiviral activity for pralatrexate in cell assays. This is an in-vitro drug-repurposing result, with no established effectiveness or safety as a COVID-19 treatment; the computational target hypothesis does not by itself establish the cellular mechanism.
ai_technology: DFCNN dense neural network; DeepBindBC learned binding classification; molecular simulation
organization: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Shenzhen Third People’s Hospital; Institute of Microbiology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: Four drugs selected after a hybrid learned-model and simulation screen underwent laboratory evaluation, including direct cell-assay evidence for pralatrexate activity. This is not clinical efficacy.
evidence.unknown: Primary preprint v1 metadata dates June 23,2020 and its deposited abstract already reports this drug/result; v2 followed August 24 and journal December 31,2020. Detailed selection was read in primary v2, not full v1. Pralatrexate was already approved for an unrelated cancer indication. Patient efficacy, therapeutic window for this infection and definitive cellular target mechanism remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: DFCNN and DeepBindBC learn protein–drug binding patterns and jointly filter candidates before molecular simulations select the laboratory follow-ups; attribution is to the hybrid workflow.

source_review.scope: Original preprint metadata/deposited abstract; relevant primary v2 learned-screening Methods/high-level result; current journal front/status. No operational pathogen protocol represented.

title: Learned catalyst search guides oxygen-evolution catalysts made from meteorites
summary: A robotic chemistry system combined a neural-network performance model with theoretical calculations and experimental calibration to select a catalyst formulation from five Martian meteorite feedstocks. Laboratory testing of the selected formulation measured an oxygen-evolution overpotential of 445.1 mV at 10 mA per square centimetre, lower than the compared theory-only and experiment-only search formulations. The work demonstrates a terrestrial laboratory catalyst result; oxygen production on Mars and a globally optimal composition were not independently established.
ai_technology: Neural-network oxygen-evolution performance prediction; model-guided composition search
organization: University of Science and Technology of China

evidence.tested: The primary journal supplement compares measured overpotentials of 445.1 mV for the combined model-guided formulation, 467.4 mV for experiment-guided optimization and 542.7 mV for theory-guided selection. The original preprint abstract already reports the 445.1 mV result and more than 550000 seconds of operation.
evidence.unknown: The first located preprint was posted March 23, 2023; the journal version appeared November 13, 2023, with a March 2024 issue date. The preprint body was inaccessible; version-specific result presence is established from its primary deposited abstract, while detailed comparator measurements come from the journal supplement. Search-space coverage does not prove global optimality. Mars deployment, resource extraction at scale and integrated life-support performance remain untested.
evidence.ai_role: A learned neural-network model combines first-principles and robot-generated experimental information to predict oxygen-evolution performance and guide which mixed-meteorite catalyst formulation to synthesize and test.

source_review.scope: Primary preprint metadata and deposited abstract; journal front/abstract/code-availability and full author supplement, including model-guided experimental comparison. Main journal body and preprint body were not read.

title: Deep-learning image search helps identify three Nasca geoglyphs verified in field surveys
summary: A learned object detector trained on pictorial elements from 21 known geoglyphs guided human inspection of aerial-image candidates and subsequent on-site surveys. The 2023 primary report documents verified legs, fish and bird figures. These objects were already among the geoglyphs identified by 2022; this record dates the detailed 2023 report and does not claim they were first discovered that year. A fourth humanoid figure announced in 2019 is excluded from this record.
ai_technology: Deep-learning object detection on multiscale aerial imagery
organization: Yamagata University; IBM Japan

evidence.tested: Primary university Methods/results describe 307 element/multiscale training images from 21 known figures, human review of model detections and on-site verification of the legs, fish and bird geoglyphs.
evidence.unknown: The documented June 1,2023 report first publishes these three figures’ photographs and illustrations, but says they were already included among 358 geoglyphs identified by 2022. No absolute first-public-discovery priority is claimed. The source-reported 21-fold candidate-search speed comparison is not an independently replicated overall archaeological productivity gain. The earlier 2019 humanoid and separate 2024 catalog result of 303 geoglyphs are not counted here.
evidence.ai_role: A trained deep-learning detector learns pictorial components at multiple image scales and proposes aerial-image candidates for human review and field investigation, directly linking learned image search to the three recorded archaeological finds.

source_review.scope: Exact publisher title/DOI/abstract and full primary university two-page research Methods/results release. Original publisher full paper inaccessible; a third-party journal reproduction was only corroborative and is not treated as authenticated primary Methods.

title: Decision-tree predictions guide synthesis of a cadmium-copper-antimony Laves phase
summary: A decision-tree classifier trained on known intermetallic structures guided experiments on cadmium-copper-antimony compositions. The researchers synthesized a limited antimony-substitution range adopting the cubic MgCu 2-type Laves structure, supported by diffraction and elemental measurements. This is a measured structural finding; predictions for more than 400000 other candidates are not experimental discoveries, and the classifier also produced false positives.
ai_technology: Decision-tree classifier
organization: University of Alberta; Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur

evidence.tested: Primary supporting tables compare model predictions with experimental phase outcomes, including CdCu 1.8 Sb 0.2; diffraction patterns and elemental analysis support the synthesized limited solid-solution range.
evidence.unknown: Functional material performance and broad predicted-candidate validity are unestablished. Nominal and measured compositions differ slightly; the optimized model predicts some compositions that did not form the target phase.
evidence.ai_role: A decision tree learned structure classes from about 3700 known AB 2 phases using elemental descriptors, predicted candidate compositions and guided experimental targeting of the cadmium-copper-antimony system.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher article-front metadata and abstract, complete official author supporting information Methods/model tables/experimental characterizations and result captions, and current PubMed notice metadata. Paywalled main article body was not read; no independent replication performed.

title: Generative design leads to a synthesized magnesium-based thermoelectric composition
summary: A generative model combining a variational autoencoder, residual layers and discriminators proposed thermoelectric compositions from literature-derived data. Researchers synthesized the selected Mg 3.1 Sb 0.5 Bi 1.497 Te 0.003 composition and reported a thermoelectric figure of merit of 0.75 at 300 kelvin. This laboratory measurement is separate from the larger catalogue of predicted high-performance materials; it does not establish that all predictions were synthesized or that this room-temperature sample exceeded a figure of merit of 1.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder; residual neural network; learned discriminators
organization: Harbin Institute of Technology; Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: The official supporting TableS 7 explicitly marks Mg 3.1 Bi 1.497 Sb 0.5 Te 0.003 as synthesized in this study and reports its transport properties and thermoelectric figure of merit of 0.75 at 300 kelvin.
evidence.unknown: Broad experimental success across the predicted catalogue, independent replication and practical device benefit remain unestablished. The reported 100 materials above a predicted figure of merit of 1 are computational candidates, not 100 newly tested materials.
evidence.ai_role: A conditional generative architecture learns composition/property relationships using a variational encoder-decoder with residual layers, discriminators and a diversity-related loss, generating candidate compositions for experimental selection.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher front metadata and abstract, complete official supporting information model architecture and measured-versus-predicted tables, plus current PubMed notice metadata. Paywalled main article body was not read; no independent replication performed.

title: Learned synthetic CT enables physically tested lung-radiotherapy dose planning
summary: A UNet++ model converted cone-beam scans into synthetic CT images for lung-cancer radiotherapy planning. Plans based on 17 patients’ images were compared with planning-CT references and checked through actual phantom irradiation. Measured dose deviations were 2–7%, comparable to the reference-plan deviations in that experiment. This supports a bounded medical-physics feasibility result, not formal dosimetric equivalence, improved patient outcomes or demonstrated adaptive treatment delivery.
ai_technology: UNet++ with ResNet50 backbone for synthetic CT generation
organization: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; MedMind Technology; Tsinghua University

evidence.tested: Model development used 70 patients and image evaluation 15;17 additional patients supplied paired cone-beam/planning CT scans for offline planning comparisons. Generated-image plans underwent physical ArcCHECK and thermoluminescent-dose measurements on phantoms, with 2–7% dose deviations reported.
evidence.unknown: The clinical images and plan comparison were retrospective; phantom irradiation does not establish actual adaptive patient-treatment benefit. Nonsignificant dose differences do not prove equivalence. The tumor-volume gradient index differed, and some tumor-dose metrics had weaker agreement. The source’s percentage image-MAE improvement is inconsistent with its displayed means and is not reproduced here. Validation is limited to the studied scanner/workflow and geometry.
evidence.ai_role: UNet++ learns the image-to-image conversion needed to reduce cone-beam CT intensity errors before conventional dose calculation. The generated-image plans, rather than only image-quality scores, are tested against physical dose measurements.

source_review.scope: Exact primary XML front DOI/title/date; full patient/model Methods, generated-plan comparison and actual phantom/TLD measurement Results. Fresh Crossref publication-status metadata; PubMed/EPMC status access was limited.

title: External ALS trial data show limited added prediction accuracy from learned progression models
summary: Random-forest and ensemble models trained on 3160 ALS trial participants were evaluated in a separate 509-patient trial dataset. They predicted later functional scores with performance similar to a linear mixed-effects model, with only marginal improvements in error and explained variation. Missing-data handling improved generalization. The result is retrospective clinical prediction validation; suggested clinical-trial power gains came from simulations, not an actual improved treatment trial.
ai_technology: Random forest; super learner ensemble; random-forest missing-data imputation
organization: University of Michigan; Genentech

evidence.tested: Final models trained on 3160 PRO-ACT patients were compared against observed ALSFRS-R trajectories in 509 patients from a separate completed olesoxime trial. The learned models marginally outperformed a conventional mixed-effects comparator, with roughly 1percentage-point additional explained variation.
evidence.unknown: Both datasets were existing clinical-trial records. Prediction became poorer farther from baseline, and results do not establish treatment-effect estimation or patient benefit. A simulated16% effective-sample-size gain under a hypothetical treatment effect is not an observed clinical-trial gain. Random-forest and ensemble models do not explicitly account for within-person longitudinal correlation; missing-at-random assumptions may fail outside these data.
evidence.ai_role: Random forests and an ensemble learn relationships between baseline clinical covariates, time from baseline and later functional scores. Predicted trajectories are evaluated against an independent historical trial and used separately in trial-power simulations.

source_review.scope: Exact primary XML article-front identity/date, clinical cohorts, covariates, model/imputation and validation Methods, observed prediction Results and simulation/longitudinal limitations; fresh primary notice metadata.

title: Learned video measurements associate surgical instrument use with operative experience
summary: DeepLab-based recognition measured instrument appearance in 55 recorded robotic gastric-cancer operations. The study found shorter relative stapler and large-clip appearance times in the later-experience group than in the earlier cases. These are retrospective associations in four surgeons’ procedures, not a validated general skill score or evidence that AI improved surgery or patient outcomes.
ai_technology: DeepLab v3+ learned surgical-instrument image segmentation
organization: Keio University; Harvard University

evidence.tested: An instrument-recognition model trained on 1234 annotated video images and assessed on 149 additional images was applied to 55 recorded operations. Comparing 22 earlier-experience cases with 33 later cases yielded associations between relative instrument-appearance time and experience.
evidence.unknown: Frames were randomly selected from the 55 videos; separation by operation or surgeon in image testing is not established. Instrument appearance is an estimated proxy for use, not independently validated surgical skill. Case mix and operation duration differed, surgeon-level clustering is not established, and outcome differences do not demonstrate an AI intervention effect. The model sometimes confused partly visible instruments.
evidence.ai_role: DeepLab v3+ learns instrument segmentation from annotated frames, then supplies per-instrument appearance-duration measurements for the retrospective experience-group comparison.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front identity/date, clinical cohort, instrument-model/statistical Methods, image evaluation and experience-group instrument-duration Results/Table3. Surgical procedure instructions are outside the represented evidence; fresh primary notice metadata checked.

title: Survival forests associate clinical and treatment-plan features with glioma survival
summary: A retrospective 95-patient high-grade glioma study used random survival forests to relate clinical characteristics and radiotherapy dose-volume features to observed survival. Age, tumor volume, grade, performance status, IDH status and a dose-coverage feature were selected by the learned model. This is an exploratory cohort association; the study does not establish that changing radiation dose improves survival or that its prediction performance generalizes to new hospitals.
ai_technology: Random survival forest; support-vector-machine comparison
organization: Zhejiang University

evidence.tested: The source analyzes 95 historical patients, randomly dividing 57 for model development and 38 for testing. The survival forest selects clinical factors and a treatment-plan dose-coverage feature associated with recorded outcomes.
evidence.unknown: Continuous variables were converted using outcome-optimized cut points before the described split; preprocessing isolation is not established, so reported test accuracy may be optimistic. Feature selection and small-cohort risk thresholds need validation. Treatment choices, tumor size and case mix can confound dose–survival relationships. Decision-curve analysis is model-based, not demonstrated clinical utility, and no causal dose-prescription guidance follows.
evidence.ai_role: The survival forest learns nonlinear relationships between clinical/dose-volume features and survival, selecting a multifeature risk representation for retrospective outcome analysis.

source_review.scope: Exact primary BioC document ID and article-front DOI/title/PMID; clinical/statistical model Methods and survival Results/limitations. Current primary notice metadata checked; treatment instructions are not represented.

title: Generative lattice design produces experimentally tested energy-absorbing structures
summary: A 3D convolutional predictor and conditional generative adversarial network guided lattice geometries for high energy absorption. Selected stainless-steel structures were 3D printed and compression tested, with favorable energy-absorption behavior relative to the compared conventional designs. An additional analytical-equation and genetic-algorithm step tuned acoustic cavities, producing measured broadband sound absorption. The learned model enables geometry generation for the mechanical objective; the separate acoustic optimization is not attributed to neural learning.
ai_technology: 3D convolutional energy-absorption prediction; conditional3D DCGAN geometry generation
organization: Chinese University of Hong Kong; National University of Singapore; Newcastle University

evidence.tested: Learned-generated 316L stainless-steel lattice samples were manufactured and evaluated under compression. The acoustically tuned structure was tested in an impedance tube, with an average reported absorption coefficient of 0.69 across the examined band.
evidence.unknown: The predictor learns primarily from 1000 finite-element design/performance pairs; the 20,000design generative set is not 20,000 measured specimens. Comparisons to other lattice families combine source-defined densities, designs and literature context and do not establish universal superiority. Acoustic geometry was optimized with governing equations and a genetic algorithm, rather than a learned acoustic surrogate. Protective equipment, aerospace and infrastructure uses are proposed, not deployed outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: The 3D CNN learns geometry-to-energy-absorption mappings and labels structures for conditional DCGAN training. The generative network then proposes geometries targeted to high absorption, which are fabricated and tested; neural learning is not credited with the separate analytical acoustic search.

source_review.scope: Exact primary article-front DOI/title/PMCID/date; full geometry-generation, CNN/DCGAN training, analytical acoustic-search Methods and experimental compression/acoustic Results, with fresh primary notice metadata.

title: A learned MRI model localizes known dysplasia lesions in FLAIR-negative images
summary: A convolutional model trained on lesion-image patterns was evaluated on 18 FLAIR-negative images from 12 patients with histologically confirmed focal cortical dysplasia. The source reports localization in 15 of the 18 images. This is a small retrospective lesion-localization result, not validated population screening or proof of improved surgical outcomes.
ai_technology: Net-Pos convolutional network; activation-maximization pattern localization
organization: Beijing Institute of Technology; Sixth Medical Center of PLA General Hospital

evidence.tested: The overall source dataset has 34 FLAIR images from 19 patients; the FLAIR-negative evaluation contains 18 images from 12 patients. CNN training/test image-block sets are described as coming from unique patients. Localization is compared with lesion regions marked using operative locations.
evidence.unknown: The abstract calls 15/18recall subject-wise, but its denominator is18 images from 12 patients; it is not presented here as 15 patients detected. Surgical/pathology-selected cases and marked lesion references do not establish accuracy in unselected MRI-negative epilepsy patients. The small dataset, image-block construction and modest segmentation overlap limit generalization; no independent clinical deployment is shown.
evidence.ai_role: A six-layer CNN learns lesion-associated image-block features; activation maximization derives representative patterns used to localize suspected lesions in FLAIR-negative images.

source_review.scope: Exact primary publisher title/DOI/date; relevant indexed primary cohort, learned-model and reference-validation Methods/Results and limitations. Fresh Crossref publication-status metadata, no linked update; direct full-page access limited.

title: Synthetic CT supports retrospective upper-abdominal radiotherapy dose validation
summary: A CycleGAN trained on scans from 11 patients generated synthetic CT images for six other liver-cancer patients. Dose calculations on those images were compared with deformably registered planning-CT references and generally agreed more closely than calculations using raw cone-beam CT. This is a small retrospective medical-physics validation, with remaining air–tissue interface errors, not demonstrated improved treatment delivery.
ai_technology: Cycle-consistent generative adversarial network for synthetic CT
organization: Columbia University Irving Medical Center

evidence.tested: Seventeen historical hepatocellular-carcinoma cases supplied 11-patient training and six-patient testing groups. Synthetic-image dose-volume and profile calculations were compared with deformed-planning-CT and raw cone-beam calculations in the six test cases.
evidence.unknown: The reference is a deformably registered planning image, not an independently measured true delivered patient dose. Model calibration is specific to the studied imaging-system pair; single-slice processing and limited field of view constrain use. Air–tissue interface errors remain. Gamma passing rates alone could miss evident dose underestimation. The study does not establish superior patient outcomes or formal clinical equivalence.
evidence.ai_role: CycleGAN learns cone-beam/CT image-domain mappings that preserve anatomy while correcting intensity values needed for conventional dose calculations; the resulting generated-image dose estimates answer a defined upper-abdominal planning question.

source_review.scope: Exact primary publisher title/DOI/date; relevant indexed primary cohort, learned-model and reference-validation Methods/Results and limitations. Fresh Crossref publication-status metadata, no linked update; direct full-page access limited.

title: Radiomic models distinguish pathology-defined pancreatic cyst risk in surgical cohorts
summary: Learned CT-radiomic scores combined with a conventional imaging feature distinguished source-defined benign and malignant pancreatic cyst groups in surgical cohorts. Models developed using 262 patients were evaluated in two 50-patient test sets and a separately recruited 34-patient cohort. The result is retrospective pathology-reference diagnostic evaluation, not evidence that the models improve screening or decisions about surgery.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection; multiple learned radiomic classifiers; clinical-radiomic regression
