organization: Peking Union Medical College Hospital; Guangzhou Medical University; Chengdu First People’s Hospital

evidence.tested: Eleven radiomic classifiers were trained in 262 patients, assessed in 50 temporal internal and 50 external cases, and combined with solid-component information. A34-patient prospectively recruited cohort was subsequently analyzed with those models.
evidence.unknown: All included patients underwent surgery, restricting the disease spectrum and reference availability. Prospective recruitment does not establish that a frozen model was evaluated before outcomes; validation is classified as retrospective. Full preprocessing/feature-selection nesting is not completely specified. The source-defined grouping combines different lesion types/grades and is not a universal management threshold. Separate fluid-omics mechanism claims are outside this record.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers map selected CT image features to pathology-defined cyst labels; resulting radiomic scores add information to a clinical imaging-feature model evaluated in separate patient datasets.

source_review.scope: Exact primary XML front DOI/title/PMCID/date; clinical cohorts, pathology-label definitions, radiomic/statistical model and validation Methods/Results. Raw biological assay protocols and mechanistic omics sections not processed. Same-day primary bibliographic/notice snapshot reused.

title: A neural model classifies neuroblastoma risk groups in small plasma-sample cohorts
summary: A neural classifier combined exosomal enzyme measurements with clinical indicators to distinguish recorded neuroblastoma risk groups. The source used 30 pretreatment plasma specimens for development and 14 later diagnostic samples for evaluation. This is a small retrospective risk-label classification study, not a validated forecast of future outcomes or evidence that the biosensor or AI improves treatment.
ai_technology: Neural-network clinical/biomarker classification compared with ten other learned classifiers
organization: Henan Children’s Hospital; Zhengzhou Children’s Hospital

evidence.tested: A classifier combining exosomal uracil-DNA glycosylase and four clinical indicators was evaluated against recorded low/intermediate versus high-risk labels, including a later 14-sample cohort.
evidence.unknown: The initial 50 specimens include repeated samples, so they are not 50 independent patients. Model selection among 11 classifiers and small evaluation groups can inflate apparent accuracy. Some clinical inputs are themselves related to standard risk-group definitions; independent additional prognostic information and future-event prediction are not established. The separate biosensor design, biological imaging and drug-resistance experiments are outside AI attribution in this record.
evidence.ai_role: The learned neural classifier combines a measured plasma biomarker with clinical variables to estimate existing risk-group labels; AI is not credited with engineering the biosensor or the separate experimental mechanisms.

source_review.scope: Exact primary DOI/title/PMID/date; safe clinical cohort, classifier/statistical description and high-level risk-classification Results. Biosensor construction, cell/animal procedures and sequences were not used. Same-day primary status metadata reused.

title: Random forests identify joint rheological relationships associated with hydrogel printability
summary: A study of 180 hydrogel formulations combined measured rheology and printing scores with random forests, Boruta selection and SHAP interpretation. It identified 13 informative rheological measures whose combined behavior distinguished printable formulations within the study. The finding is a learned physical structure–performance relationship, not a universal printability rule or a prospective demonstration of an AI-designed new formulation.
ai_technology: Random forest; Boruta feature selection; SHAP interpretation
organization: University of Würzburg

evidence.tested: Measured rheological and printing data for 180 formulations supplied 65 initial features. Repeated random-forest/Boruta selection identified 13 measures; repeated cross-validation and SHAP analysis described their joint associations with printability.
evidence.unknown: Feature screening and interpretation use the same formulation library; independent composition-family validation is not established. Class resampling changes printable/nonprintable proportions and apparent metrics should not be transferred to real-world prevalence. The model shows conditional associations rather than causal rheological laws. No newly fabricated model-nominated formulation or clinical application is represented. A publisher note corrects a funding number only.
evidence.ai_role: Random forests learn a nonlinear mapping from rheological measures to printability; Boruta and SHAP identify combinations and conditional contributions that support the specific material-property relationship.

source_review.scope: Exact primary publisher front identity/date; full relevant indexed primary computational selection/interpretation Methods and physical printability Results. Funding-only correction recognized; no biological procedures represented.

title: Learned serum-marker combinations improve internal melanoma progression classification
summary: In 323 early-stage melanoma patients, classifiers combined serum IL-4, GM-CSF and dermcidin with tumor thickness to distinguish subsequent metastatic progression. Nested internal validation supported added discrimination beyond thickness alone; this does not establish clinical benefit or external validity.
ai_technology: Regularized logistic regression; support vector machine; decision tree; naive Bayes; nearest neighbors
organization: University of the Basque Country; Biocruces Bizkaia Health Research Institute

evidence.tested: Classifiers were assessed with nested cross-validation in a clinical cohort with 74 metastatic outcomes. Scaling, oversampling, feature selection and tuning were assigned to the inner loop.
evidence.unknown: Internal validation only; unequal follow-up and incomplete sentinel-node information limit interpretation. This is postoperative risk classification, not diagnosis-time screening or an intervention benefit. Publisher first-online June 2 differs from the June 24 date in primary indexing metadata; the publisher date represents this journal version.
evidence.ai_role: Learned multivariable classifiers link measured circulating markers and tumor thickness to subsequent clinical outcomes.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher front date and safe clinical/statistical Methods and Results. Operational assay sections are outside the represented evidence.

title: Neural-network interpretation identifies a metabolic panel associated with Moyamoya disease
summary: A neural network learned serum patterns distinguishing Moyamoya disease from healthy controls. Model interpretation helped select six metabolic signals; their later three-center evaluation reported AUC 0.867, rather than the higher full-fingerprint result.
ai_technology: Neural network; integrated gradients
organization: Fudan University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University

evidence.tested: Discovery data comprised 144 patients and 144 controls; repeated spectra were averaged per sample. The six-signal panel was evaluated in 86 later samples, including 49 cases.
evidence.unknown: Selected case-control evaluation; preprocessing and feature-selection nesting are incompletely established. Metabolite assignments are tentative. No population screening, stroke prevention or mechanistic claim.
evidence.ai_role: The network learns diagnostic patterns; integrated gradients guides signal selection alongside statistical comparisons.

source_review.scope: Primary front identity/date and relevant clinical/model Methods and classification Results; operational sample procedures excluded.

title: A learned stemness index guides a signature associated with breast-cancer outcomes
summary: Researchers used a pre-existing one-class logistic-regression stemness index to derive a breast-cancer expression signature. Higher positive-signature expression was associated with shorter relapse-free survival and with recorded five-year metastasis in a separate cohort. These are observational associations, not proof of a causal stem-cell mechanism.
ai_technology: One-class logistic regression-derived stemness index
organization: Shandong University

evidence.tested: Expression from 1,247 TCGA records was correlated with the learned index to define positive and negative signatures. Outcome analyses used 2,032 relapse-free-survival records and 1,979 METABRIC records.
evidence.unknown: Existing learned index reused; signatures and cohorts may overlap, and no new independent risk-model accuracy or causal effect is claimed. Experimental mechanisms and compound results elsewhere in the paper are outside this record.
evidence.ai_role: A previously trained one-class logistic-regression index supplies the stemness representation used to select the outcome-associated signature.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front metadata and computational signature, bioinformatics and nonactionable clinical-association Results; operational experimental sections excluded.

title: Learned network models nominate two cancer-drug combinations for laboratory follow-up
summary: A transfer-learning framework combining learned drug and disease representations with biological-network propagation nominated two drug combinations. The paper reports laboratory growth-inhibition synergy for the selected cancer-cell models. This is a preclinical candidate result, not demonstrated treatment efficacy in patients.
ai_technology: Graph isomorphism network embeddings; fully connected neural networks; transfer learning
organization: Tianjin Medical University; Tsinghua University

evidence.tested: The case study links learned drug-disease scores and a refined combination model to selection of two combinations for laboratory assessment.
evidence.unknown: No clinical efficacy, safety, independently replicated mechanism or broad generalization is established. Many additional network/pathway predictions are computational only and are outside the represented result. The model description contains inconsistent optimizer-setting statements. Operational experimental procedures were not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Learned molecular embeddings and neural interaction models contribute to combination nomination; deterministic network propagation is only one component of the hybrid workflow.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front tuple, computational embedding/model/selection Methods and nonactionable case-study result. Operational assays excluded.

title: Multimodal neural fusion distinguishes tissue states in a small preclinical imaging cohort
summary: A two-branch neural network combined Raman spectra and optical-coherence images to distinguish dysplasia/cancer from control tissue. Animal-separated evaluation in a small longitudinal cohort reported 92.3% pooled accuracy. This is preclinical feasibility, not clinical diagnostic accuracy.
ai_technology: Multimodal convolutional neural network; ResNet-18; Grad-CAM
organization: King's College London

evidence.tested: Fivefold animal-independent evaluation used 196 paired observations from 11 mice. Every contributing animal was withheld once.
evidence.unknown: Small exploratory cohort; early-stopping validation partition is incompletely specified. Measurements used externally positioned tissue rather than deployed endoscopy. Pooled and fold-average metrics differ. No human screening, earlier diagnosis or treatment benefit is demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Learned spectral and image representations are fused for the specific pathology-reference classification.

source_review.scope: Primary front tuple and safe computational fusion/evaluation Methods and nonactionable classification Results; animal procedures excluded.

title: Multimodal learning separates functional motor disorders from controls
summary: A random forest combined gait, postural, neurophysiological and MRI measures in 75 people with clinically diagnosed functional motor disorders and 75 healthy controls. Repeated internal cross-validation reported AUC 0.921. MRI regions were initially derived from group differences, which may inflate performance. This does not establish differentiation from organic movement disorders, causal mechanisms or routine diagnostic utility.
ai_technology: Random forest
organization: University of Verona; University of Salerno; University of Naples Federico II; IRCCS San Raffaele Scientific Institute

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Clinically defined cases versus healthy controls in a multicentre cross-sectional study with repeated five-fold internal validation.
evidence.unknown: Independent patient-versus-patient diagnostic validation and clinical utility remain unestablished; whole-sample imaging-region screening may introduce optimism despite later within-fold selection.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest combines behavioral, electrophysiological and imaging features to distinguish clinically established case/control labels.

title: XGBoost identifies pathological microvascular invasion risk in liver cancer
summary: An XGBoost model combined tumor diameter and three preoperative blood measures in 1,106 liver-cancer patients from two hospitals. Against postoperative pathology, AUC was 0.845 in 130 internal test patients and 0.793 in 451 patients from the second hospital. This retrospective classification does not establish improved surgical choices, survival benefit or a causal role of inflammation.
ai_technology: XGBoost; recursive feature elimination
organization: Yangzhou University; Northern Jiangsu People’s Hospital; Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital; Nanjing Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Training-cohort feature selection with internal and separate-hospital validation against pathological microvascular invasion.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical utility and treatment benefit remain unestablished; model selection compares multiple algorithms across validation cohorts and applicability beyond resected HCC is uncertain.
evidence.ai_role: Boosted decision trees learn preoperative clinical associations with pathology-confirmed microvascular invasion.

title: Learned cell-death signature associates with lung cancer survival
summary: LASSO and random-forest screening identified a five-gene programmed-cell-death index in 500 lung-adenocarcinoma cases. Higher scores were associated with poorer overall survival, with similar associations in three public external cohorts. Separate tissue staining examined selected model genes. Drug sensitivity and immunotherapy response were computational estimates, rather than demonstrated treatment effects or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: LASSO; random forest; consensus clustering
organization: Shandong University; Shandong First Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective survival associations of a learned five-gene signature in TCGA and three additional GEO cohorts; selected protein-expression checks in tissue.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical utility, treatment-response prediction and causal roles of the signature remain unestablished; cohort-specific thresholds and retrospective selection limit interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Penalized regression and random-forest selection prioritize genes for an outcome-linked expression signature, enabling survival-association analyses.

title: Learning nominates a cathepsin role in lung cancer cells
summary: CoxBoost and elastic-net selection included CTSH in a seven-gene lung-cancer signature. Subsequent experiments in HCC827 cells found that reducing CTSH increased migration and invasion and reduced apoptosis. This supports a model-specific functional role after learned candidate selection; it does not establish a protective effect in patients, a treatment or an in-vivo mechanism.
ai_technology: CoxBoost; elastic-net survival regression
organization: Fujian Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Learned candidate selection followed by CTSH perturbation and measured cell migration, invasion and apoptosis in one lung-cancer cell line.
evidence.unknown: In-vivo confirmation, broader cell-model generalization and therapeutic benefit remain unestablished; survival models were selected using validation-cohort performance.
evidence.ai_role: CoxBoost and elastic net nominate a seven-gene signature containing CTSH, which the authors select for subsequent functional cell experiments.

title: Learned mitochondrial expression patterns associate with kidney cancer survival
summary: Consensus clustering and Boruta selection separated mitochondrial-expression patterns in TCGA clear-cell renal cancer data, with different recorded overall survival. Iterative LASSO and survival forests also produced exploratory prognostic models fitted to these data. This is a retrospective association; optimized survival cutoffs and model selection make performance optimistic, and predicted drug sensitivity does not establish treatment response or a therapeutic mechanism.
ai_technology: Consensus clustering; Boruta; iterative LASSO; random survival forest
organization: Dalian Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Outcome associations of unsupervised expression groups and exploratory supervised prognostic fitting using recorded TCGA survival data.
evidence.unknown: Independent prognostic validation, causal mitochondrial mechanisms and clinical treatment utility remain unestablished; no held-out cohort is described for the reported model performance.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised clustering and forest-based feature selection learn mitochondrial-expression patterns that can be compared with recorded survival.

title: Learning classifies concurrent cardiac injury markers in cancer and COVID-19
summary: A random forest combined eight laboratory and chest-imaging measures in 201 cancer patients with COVID-19. Internal evaluation distinguished patients with troponin-defined cardiac injury, with reported AUC 0.94. Predictor timing relative to injury was not established, and outcome-informed screening preceded validation. This supports an exploratory concurrent classification result, not prediction before injury or improved patient outcomes.
ai_technology: Random forest; LASSO feature screening
organization: Jilin Cancer Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective comparison with troponin-defined injury status in 67 cases and 134 non-cases, with reported ten-fold internal validation.
evidence.unknown: Pre-injury forecasting, independent diagnostic validation and clinical benefit remain unestablished; imputation and outcome-informed feature ranking may introduce optimism.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest learns relationships between selected laboratory/imaging measurements and recorded biochemical cardiac-injury status.

title: Independent live colonoscopy check records histology-confirmed lesions
summary: Clinicians used the pretrained GI Genius detector during 298 colonoscopies in Singapore. Removed polyps included histology-confirmed adenomatous lesions and 14 sessile serrated adenomas. This independent prospective deployment supports real-time clinical feasibility. Its historical comparison used baseline polypectomy rates rather than baseline adenoma detection, so it does not securely establish the claimed detection-rate improvement or reduced cancer incidence.
ai_technology: GI Genius convolutional neural-network computer-aided detection
organization: Sengkang General Hospital; SingHealth

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Independent clinical team used a pretrained commercial detector prospectively during live procedures, with subsequent histology and independent video review.
evidence.unknown: A randomized same-endpoint improvement estimate, cancer prevention and broader clinical generalization remain unestablished; clinician selection and a short uncontrolled pilot limit interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: The pretrained CNN flags potential lesions in live endoscopy images for clinician assessment and removal, with histology determining lesion type.

title: Simplified medical reports improve comprehension in a randomized reader study
summary: A Mainz study randomly assigned 576 adult participants to an original or GPT-4-simplified version of one of five German medical documents. Among 439 completed comprehension questionnaires, simplified texts generally produced more correct answers, with the pathology comparison not statistically significant. This measures immediate understanding of selected, researcher-checked texts, not improved treatment adherence or health outcomes. Single-site recruitment, incomplete questionnaires and only one text pair per document type limit generalization.
ai_technology: GPT-4 text simplification
organization: University Medical Center Mainz

source_review.scope: Primary model operation, randomized reader-study Methods, results and limitations; exact front-matter identity/date and current PubMed/PMC correction/retraction metadata. Supplementary questionnaire and independent semantic validation were not inspected.

evidence.tested: Randomized assignment to original or pre-generated simplified German medical reports, followed by immediate multiple-choice comprehension questions; 576 participants, with 439 completed comprehension questionnaires.
evidence.unknown: Generalization beyond five selected text pairs and a single German clinical department, long-term retention, adherence and clinical outcomes remain unestablished. Education/health-literacy measures were not collected; results include incomplete questionnaires. Output generation settings are described inconsistently as configured parameters and default web sessions; the represented result concerns the actual selected texts.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4 rewrites physician-authored medical reports into lay language; those generated texts form the experimental intervention used to test readers’ immediate comprehension.

title: Learning distinguishes meditation styles in experienced monks’ brain connectivity
summary: A linear support-vector machine distinguished focused-attention from open-monitoring fMRI connectivity patterns in twelve experienced monks, with reported internal accuracy of 65.6%; classification was not significant in ten novice meditators. Model inspection implicated salience and default-mode connections. This small observational comparison does not establish that meditation training caused the differences. Caption and Methods differ on whether validation splits separated participants or repeated samples, so unseen-person generalization is not established.
ai_technology: Linear support-vector machine; training-fold ANOVA feature selection
organization: University of Chieti-Pescara; Sapienza University of Rome

source_review.scope: Primary relevant participant/task, connectivity and SVM Methods, validation/results and discussion; exact article-meta DOI/title/PMCID/date and current PubMed notice relationships. Supplementary ROI table not inspected.

evidence.tested: Internal fMRI-connectivity classification of two meditation styles in twelve experienced and ten novice male meditators, with training-fold feature selection and label permutations. Reported style accuracy was 65.6% in experts and 54.4% in novices, the latter not significant.
evidence.unknown: Independent subject-level validation and causal training effects remain unestablished. Fig.1 describes participant-level splitting while the Methods describe sample-level splitting; repeated blocks and model-weight interpretations limit generalization. The small groups differ in experience, age and recruitment.
evidence.ai_role: The linear SVM learns combinations of between-region functional connectivity that distinguish the two recorded meditation conditions; feature-selection frequency and learned weights identify connections contributing to that discrimination.

title: Forest models link land-use patterns to recorded envenomation incidence
summary: Random forests analyzed monthly reported scorpion, snake and spider envenomation across 645 São Paulo municipalities from 2010 to 2024. Urban land proportion had the highest permutation importance for observed incidence in all three models, ahead of weather variables. This is an ecological predictive association, not evidence that urbanization causes individual incidents. Random train/test splitting ignored spatial and temporal dependence, reporting may be incomplete, and hypothetical warming outputs are unmeasured sensitivity scenarios.
ai_technology: Random forest; permutation feature importance
organization: Federal University of Rio Grande; Federal University of Alagoas

source_review.scope: Primary indexed PMC full text: data/model Methods, measured-incidence feature-importance results and limitations, exact canonical citation identity/date, current primary PubMed notice relationships. Warming scenarios reviewed as predictions; supplementary municipality rankings not inspected.

evidence.tested: Random-forest models of existing municipal notification records, with 80:20 random train/test splitting and out-of-bag permutation importance. The represented result concerns predictor importance for observed 2010–2024 incidence.
evidence.unknown: Causal individual risk, generalization under spatially or temporally separated validation and actual effects of future warming remain unestablished. Socioeconomic and surveillance differences were omitted; underreporting can affect recorded incidence.
evidence.ai_role: Forest ensembles learn nonlinear relationships between municipal land-use/weather measurements and reported incidence; permutation increases in out-of-bag error identify the predictors most informative within each fitted model.

title: Boosted trees characterize distressing hot flashes after breast cancer treatment
summary: LightGBM analysis of cross-sectional surveys from 360 early-breast-cancer patients associated reported hot-flash frequency and age with symptom-related distress. Nested internal validation gave AUC 0.731, and partial-dependence analysis suggested greater distress around seventeen or more hot flashes per week. This characterizes concurrent symptoms, not future toxicity or treatment efficacy. Recall bias, inconsistent survey-scale origins and predictors reflecting responses to existing symptoms limit interpretation.
ai_technology: LightGBM gradient-boosted decision trees; conditional partial dependence
organization: University of Ottawa; Ottawa Hospital Research Institute; Western University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant outcome definition, predictor construction, LightGBM and nested-validation Methods, results and limitations. Supplementary Appendix C was not inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Survey-derived classification of current high versus low Hot Flush Night Sweats problem scores, with nested ten-fold outer/five-fold inner validation, Bayesian tuning and permutation-and-retraining importance.
evidence.unknown: Prospective symptom forecasts, independent validation and benefits of symptom screening or medication remain unestablished. Drug use and cancer-treatment changes may follow rather than precede severe symptoms; the symptom threshold is exploratory.
evidence.ai_role: Boosted trees learn nonlinear relationships among survey measurements and current reported symptom burden, with conditional partial dependence characterizing frequency/age associations.

title: CT model distinguishes recorded psychiatric diagnosis groups
summary: A DenseNet-based multiple-instance model classified CT scans from patients with bipolar disorder or schizophrenia and healthy controls. Development used 685 people, with another 105 from two additional centers for testing; the paper reports 72.4% external accuracy. Cases and healthy controls came from different hospitals, so acquisition or site differences may contribute to classification. The retrospective result does not establish a diagnostic brain mechanism, screening benefit or performance beyond these selected groups.
ai_technology: DenseMD three-dimensional DenseNet multiple-instance learning
organization: Shandong University; Shandong First Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant recruitment/reference, patient partition, DenseMD model Methods, Table1–3 and primary Fig2, Results and limitations; supplementary scanner table not inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective three-group classification against DSM-V-based clinical diagnoses and healthy-control assessments. Training/validation used 506 psychiatric patients and 179 controls; external testing used 65 patients and 40 controls, with Table2 accuracy .724. Primary Fig2 explicitly shows Normal, Bipolar and Schizo outputs, resolving an inconsistent binary-task phrase in the Results.
evidence.unknown: Performance independent of hospital/scanner confounding, medication effects and selection bias remains unestablished. Patients and controls were sourced from different centers in both development and testing. No screening effectiveness or patient benefit was tested.
evidence.ai_role: A shared three-dimensional DenseNet encoder learns representations from eight brain-CT patches per person, fuses them and classifies recorded clinical groups through multiple-instance learning.

title: Decision trees compare caregiver ratings with clinical ADHD diagnoses
summary: In 326 Italian children and adolescents referred for suspected ADHD, a decision tree using caregiver questionnaires agreed with clinician diagnoses in 74% of leave-one-out evaluations. Analysis of fitted-model errors linked autism-related symptom ratings to classification patterns. This is a retrospective comparison with clinical assessments, not an independently validated remote diagnostic service. Shared questionnaire information, a selected mostly male sample and exploratory error analysis limit interpretation.
ai_technology: Decision tree; random forest and support-vector-machine comparisons
organization: IRCCS Eugenio Medea

source_review.scope: Primary relevant participant/reference, questionnaire, tree/LOO Methods, Results and limitations. Supplementary data-cleaning appendix not inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Among 342 referred children, sixteen with extensive missing data were excluded, leaving 326. A decision tree was evaluated against DSM-5-based clinician assessments using leave-one-out validation; accuracy was 74%, sensitivity 92% and specificity 50%. Separate error-pattern analyses used fitted full-sample predictions.
evidence.unknown: Generalization to other referral populations, independent diagnostic reference assessment and prospective telehealth effectiveness remain unestablished. The clinicians’ diagnostic process incorporated caregiver information also available to the algorithm; exploratory autism/error associations do not establish causal confounding or independently validated subgroup performance. Supplementary data-cleaning details were not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: The tree learns questionnaire-score splits that classify clinician-assessed ADHD status; learned classifications and their errors support analysis of which reported symptom patterns depart from the full in-person evaluation.

title: Recurrent networks classify cancer-bearing mouse ovary images
summary: A convolutional LSTM classified optical-coherence tomography of excised ovaries from sixteen mice, half from an ovarian-cancer model and half wild-type controls. Tissue pathology supported the disease labels. Across repeated leave-one-animal-out evaluations, mean AUC was 0.81; the best run reached 0.98. This is a small retrospective preclinical imaging validation, not human ovarian-cancer screening or evidence of earlier detection or improved treatment outcomes.
ai_technology: Convolutional long short-term memory; VGG and three-dimensional CNN comparisons
organization: University of Arizona

source_review.scope: Primary relevant animal-cohort/reference, preprocessing, learned architecture, animal-wise validation Methods, Results/Table2 and limitations; cited earlier experimental protocols not independently re-reviewed. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Existing ex-vivo ovarian OCT recordings from eight cancer-model and eight wild-type mice, with pathological verification and leave-one-animal-out testing repeated ten times. Mean convolutional-LSTM AUC .81 is distinguished from the selected peak .98.
evidence.unknown: Human diagnostic transfer, clinical screening, early-stage detection and benefit remain unestablished. Only sixteen animals and one held-out animal per fold limit uncertainty estimates; peak-run performance is not representative average performance.
evidence.ai_role: The convolutional LSTM learns sequential relationships between depth-resolved OCT slices and classifies tissue from cancer-model versus wild-type animals, using pathology-supported labels.

title: Pathology networks identify gastric-cancer lymph-node metastases
summary: A cascade of Faster R-CNN/DeepLab and fused Xception/DenseNet models analyzed lymph-node slides from 222 gastric-cancer patients. In the reported 327-slide test cohort from 94 patients, metastasis classification had positive and negative predictive values of 93.53% and 97.99%. This is a single-center archival clinical validation; the paper’s “prospective” terminology does not establish a new frozen-model clinical trial. Poorly differentiated and scattered tumor cells were more often missed, and no improved patient outcome was demonstrated.
ai_technology: Faster R-CNN; DeepLab; fused Xception and DenseNet-121
organization: Peking University Cancer Hospital; Tsinghua University

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full relevant cohort/reference, model and validation Methods, Results and discussion; supplementary materials not inspected. Publisher canonical front DOI/title and online date verified. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Pathology-reference classification of lymph-node metastases in archival 2009–2019 gastric-cancer slides. The source describes 594 training slides and 327 test slides, with reported test-cohort PPV 93.53% and NPV 97.99%; these are not patient-level screening-benefit estimates.
evidence.unknown: External-center generalization, prospective frozen-model performance and patient benefit remain unestablished. The Methods alternate image-random-split and patient-cohort descriptions, leaving the exact grouping of repeated slides incompletely documented. Hard-to-distinguish histological subtypes had more false negatives.
evidence.ai_role: Faster R-CNN/DeepLab locate and segment lymph nodes; fused Xception/DenseNet learned features classify metastatic tissue against expert pathology labels.

title: Surgeons’ risk judgments diverge from forest-model estimates
summary: Thirty-nine spine surgeons estimated complication and reoperation risks for nine adult-spinal-deformity case vignettes. Their judgments varied widely and had low agreement with estimates from an existing random-survival-forest calculator. This measured disagreement does not show that the calculator was more accurate for these cases: actual patient outcomes were not the comparator. A 39% response rate, selected vignettes and inconsistent directional wording in the paper limit interpretation.
ai_technology: Random survival forest surgical-risk calculator
organization: Vall d’Hebron University Hospital; European Spine Study Group; International Spine Study Group

source_review.scope: Primary Duke author-deposited journal PDF front matter, relevant calculator/survey Methods, Results/Tables1–3 and discussion/limitations. Publisher canonical identity and journal online date corroborated. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Comparison of 39 surgeons’ elicited risk estimates for nine fixed case vignettes against an existing random-survival-forest calculator. Mean indices of agreement with the model ranged .122–.416 across complication/reintervention endpoints and follow-up horizons.
evidence.unknown: Accuracy versus actual outcomes, improved counseling and patient benefit were not established by this comparison. Group-average differences were not statistically significant; low individual agreement should not be recast as proven machine superiority. One Results sentence reverses the temporal direction shown in tables and discussion, so directional over/underestimation claims are omitted.
evidence.ai_role: A previously trained random survival forest generates case-specific risk estimates that provide the learned comparator for measuring agreement with human judgments.

title: Abdominal-X-ray network classifies recorded colorectal-cancer status
summary: A DenseNet-121 analyzed abdominal X-rays against recorded colorectal-cancer labels in Taiwanese hospital data. It achieved AUC 0.738 in 16,875 internal-validation patients and 0.656 in 15,876 patients from a community hospital; external sensitivity was 47.7% at the selected cutoff. Cancer was uncommon, registry records could miss diagnoses elsewhere, and the one-year follow-up/label timing limits claims about detection at the image date. This retrospective study does not establish effective screening or earlier diagnosis.
ai_technology: DenseNet-121 convolutional neural network
organization: Tri-Service General Hospital; National Defense Medical Center

source_review.scope: Primary relevant cohort/label, DenseNet operation and threshold Methods, validation Results and limitations; supplementary architecture/training appendix not independently read. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Patient-separated development, tuning and validation cohorts, one randomly selected KUB radiograph per person, and registry/EMR colorectal-cancer labels. The threshold chosen in the tuning set was reused in both validation cohorts; external AUC .656 and sensitivity 47.7% were lower than internal results.
evidence.unknown: Prospective screening performance, time gained before diagnosis and clinical benefit remain unestablished. Prior cancer was excluded and one-year follow-up used, but the precise diagnosis-to-image timing is not fully specified. Low case prevalence, distal-tumor imbalance and incomplete capture of outside-hospital diagnoses limit interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: A 121-layer DenseNet learns radiographic patterns associated with recorded colorectal-cancer labels and returns a case probability for a single abdominal radiograph.

title: Nursing-record features improve estimation of home-care use
summary: Random-forest analysis of 4,323 Dutch home-care clients found that recorded nursing diagnoses and symptoms added information beyond existing case-mix groups. Reported internal cross-validated R-squared for weekly care hours increased from 22.4% to 32.1% when nursing-record features were added. The result concerns observed service use at one provider, not objectively necessary care or improved payment policy. Documentation differences and underprediction of high-use clients limit generalization.
ai_technology: Random forest; recursive feature elimination
organization: Dutch Healthcare Authority; Tilburg University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant client selection, outcome and forest/validation Methods, Results and limitations; supplementary parameter-tuning and feature-elimination details not independently reviewed. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: One randomly selected assessment per client was retained to prevent repeated-client leakage. Forest models were compared using ten-fold validation against average weekly care hours in the 28 days after assessment, with demographic/case-mix and nursing-record feature sets.
evidence.unknown: Performance at other providers, clinically appropriate care need and reimbursement-policy effects remain unestablished. The primary body describes feature elimination but its exact nesting/tuning details are in an unreviewed supplement. Care hours combine nursing and personal care, and documentation practices can vary.
evidence.ai_role: Forest ensembles learn interactions among demographic, case-mix and nursing-assessment variables to estimate recorded care-hour use; comparing feature sets measures the information added by nursing records.

title: Learning models show no clear gain in hemorrhage outcome prediction
summary: In 388 patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, tree boosting, neural networks and other models did not clearly outperform traditional models using admission clinical and imaging information. The best reported AUC was 0.78 for combined features, versus 0.76 using Glasgow Coma Scale information alone. This is a retrospective clinical comparison, not proof of equivalence or evidence that learning cannot help other cohorts or inputs. Single-institution sampling and incomplete outcome records limit generalization.
ai_technology: CatBoost tree boosting; multilayer perceptron; support-vector machine; generalized linear models
organization: Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin

source_review.scope: Primary relevant patient/reference, predictor, preprocessing and model-validation Methods, Results and limitations; supplementary detailed metric tables not independently reviewed. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective admission-feature prediction against later favorable/unfavorable modified Rankin outcomes. Patient-level 80:20 splits repeated fifty times, with ten-fold tuning and training-set imputation/scaling; 388 analyzed after twenty patients lacking outcomes were excluded.
evidence.unknown: Generalization to other centers, incremental value of different inputs and clinical decision benefit remain unestablished. Absence of a clear performance advantage in this cohort is not formal statistical equivalence, and no intervention allocation was tested.
evidence.ai_role: Boosted trees, a multilayer perceptron and other fitted classifiers learn admission-feature/outcome relationships; their held-out clinical performance is compared with regression and models using established severity scores.

title: Boosted models classify INR-defined coagulopathy after brain injury
summary: A glmBoost/gradient-boosting model classified INR-defined coagulopathy in older adults with traumatic brain injury, using 484 MIMIC-IV and 788 eICU records. The primary figure reports AUC 0.901 in derivation data and 0.701 in eICU. Both cohorts influenced model selection, so the latter is not an independent validation estimate. Timing, imputation and inconsistent narrative reporting limit interpretation; the study does not establish early warning or benefit from treatment changes.
ai_technology: glmBoost feature selection; gradient boosting machine
organization: Huizhou Municipal Central Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary relevant cohort/reference, imputation/model-selection Methods, Results, actual Figure3 and limitations. Supplementary-file endpoint timed out; no supplementary table review claimed. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective classification against INR greater than 1.2 using clinical/laboratory features. Figure 3 identifies 13 selected variables and reported AUC .901/.701 in the two datasets; the model was chosen using average performance across both cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Independent validation, prediction before coagulopathy and clinical benefit remain unestablished. Data extraction/imputation includes incompletely specified hospitalization timing. Text gives inconsistent average AUC/variable counts; the quoted cohort AUCs are explicitly those in the primary figure and corresponding Discussion.
evidence.ai_role: glmBoost selects clinical/laboratory features, then a gradient boosting machine learns their relationship with the recorded INR-based coagulation label.

title: Echo networks detect vegetations in selected endocarditis images
summary: YOLOv12 and RT-DETR models were evaluated on transesophageal echocardiography from 329 patients with confirmed left-sided endocarditis and visible vegetations, plus 70 controls without suspected endocarditis. Patient-separated internal testing reported diagnostic AUC 0.91 for YOLOv12. This selected case-control result does not establish screening performance or improved prognosis; other intracardiac structures can mimic vegetations, and right-sided disease was excluded.
ai_technology: YOLOv12; RT-DETR object detection
organization: Hospital Clínico Universitario de Valladolid

source_review.scope: Primary relevant clinical selection/reference, annotation/model and patient-split Methods, Results and limitations; supplementary per-split metric tables not independently reviewed. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Expert-labeled cine-loop frames, with all images from each patient kept in one subset. Ten random train/optimization/test splits were averaged; each diagnostic comparison used sixty held-out positive cases and the same seventy controls. A frame-detection ratio was used for diagnostic scoring.
evidence.unknown: Performance in a consecutive suspected-endocarditis population, other intracardiac masses, right-sided disease and clinical benefit remain unestablished. Positive cases were selected for visible vegetations, controls came from one center, and multiple-loop aggregation into a patient score is incompletely specified.
evidence.ai_role: The networks learn image patterns to locate vegetation bounding boxes in echo frames; the proportion of detected frames supplies a diagnostic score compared with expert clinical-image labels.

title: Claims-based models estimate later inflammatory-bowel-disease care events
summary: Random forests and LASSO models used one year of insurance claims to estimate subsequent-year hospitalizations and surgery in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. In a temporally shifted cohort of 69,165 patients, reported AUCs were 0.73 for hospitalization and 0.71 for surgery. The training cohort contained 72,178 patients. This retrospective utilization prediction does not establish prevention benefit; possible patient overlap between annual cohorts, claims-based outcomes and validation-set threshold selection limit interpretation.
ai_technology: Random forest; LASSO logistic regression
organization: University of California, Los Angeles; Leiden University Medical Center; Cedars-Sinai Medical Center

source_review.scope: Primary relevant cohort/timing, outcome definitions, model/threshold Methods, Results and limitations. Current linked Editorial/Comment metadata and publisher/author-repository access checked; editorial body and supplementary feature tables not read. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: 2015 baseline claims/2016 events supplied training data, while 2016 baseline/2017 events supplied temporal evaluation. Outcomes were claims-defined IBD hospitalization and surgery; the model compared fitted predictions with later recorded events.
evidence.unknown: Independent-patient generalization, biological disease mechanisms and improved treatment decisions remain unestablished. The source does not explicitly establish nonoverlapping patients across annual cohorts. Thresholds were selected on validation predictions; calibration was imperfect. A linked editorial was authenticated as an Editorial/Comment from primary metadata, but its subscription-only body was not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Forests and penalized logistic models learn associations between prior-year utilization features and next-year claims-defined care events, enabling measured retrospective outcome-prediction comparisons.

title: Early cardiac MRI images identify pleural effusions in retrospective testing
summary: An adapted HRNet segmented early anatomical cardiac MRI images and quantified pleural fluid. In a 200-scan test set containing 42 report-positive effusions, fluid quantification distinguished report-positive scans with an AUC of 0.906. Adaptive scanning and patient benefits were proposed rather than tested.
ai_technology: HRNet convolutional neural network
organization: Imperial College London; Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust

source_review.scope: Read primary full-text cohort, HRNet training, reconstruction/calibration and statistical Methods, pleural-effusion Results and limitations. Author cardiac-MRI page checked; it provides a high-level description, not additional calibration documentation. Supplementary ROC figure not independently inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective 575-scan study across two hospitals and two scanner manufacturers: 375 scans for training/validation and 200 for testing. Clinicians labelled 1,500 development slices. HRNet segmentation and 3D fluid quantification yielded pleural-effusion AUC 0.906 against final clinical reports; 42 of 200 test scans had reported effusions.
evidence.unknown: Report-based reference rather than an independently adjudicated effusion standard; no prospective workflow or patient-benefit test. Generalization beyond these centers remains uncertain. Separate chamber-size claims require manufacturer-specific regression calibration whose fitting partition is unclear, and are not represented here. Threshold-specific accuracy is omitted because optimal cut-offs were evaluated in the study dataset.
evidence.ai_role: An adapted HRNet learned pixel labels from clinician annotations; segmented slices were reconstructed into a 3D fluid volume used to distinguish report-positive pleural effusions.

title: Gradient-boosted trees distinguish historical autism diagnostic categories
summary: Gradient-boosted trees classified historical DSM-IV autism categories using assessment scores, demographics and comorbidities. In a person-separated SPARK test set, the multiclass model correctly classified 80.5% of individuals; 12.6% were assigned a different autism-spectrum category. This retrospective result does not establish screening performance under current DSM-5 criteria.
ai_technology: Gradient-boosted decision trees
organization: Montera, Inc. (Forta)

source_review.scope: Read actual primary dataset/reference definition, person-separated partition, gradient-boosted model/tuning Methods, input table, classification Results and limitations. Supplementary ABIDE tables were not independently inspected; their outcomes are not represented as external validation. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: SPARK supplied 36,965 individuals, split 80:20 without person overlap; fivefold training-only grid search optimized gradient-boosted trees. The multiclass model correctly classified 5,951 of 7,393 test individuals (80.5%), with 933 assigned a different autism-spectrum category. Separate one-versus-reference models yielded AUROCs 0.863–0.980. ABIDE supported a separately developed model, not external testing of the SPARK model.
evidence.unknown: Historical professional DSM-IV diagnoses were the reference; absence of diagnostic codes defined non-spectrum controls. Assessment inputs overlap with information used in diagnostic evaluation, limiting independent screening interpretation. SPARK and ABIDE models used different inputs and were fitted separately. No prospective workflow, patient benefit or current DSM-5 diagnostic validation was established; PDD-NOS positive predictive value was low.
evidence.ai_role: Gradient-boosted trees learned associations between clinical/assessment features and recorded diagnostic categories, then classified unseen individuals from the same retrospective dataset.

title: AI angiography detects more reference coronary lesions than visual estimation
summary: An ensemble-based angiography system detected 1,705 of 1,828 manually defined coronary lesions in 420 patients, compared with 69% detection by visual estimation. Models trained on separate 2016 data were tested retrospectively on selected 2022 images from three hospitals. The result establishes reference-based lesion detection, not improved treatment outcomes.
ai_technology: MPXA-2000; DeepLabV3+, U-Net++ and U²-Net segmentation ensemble
organization: Asan Medical Center; University of Ulsan College of Medicine; Ulsan University Hospital; Keimyung University Dongsan Medical Center

source_review.scope: Read actual primary cohort, separate model-training data, named segmentation ensemble, blinded manual/AI/visual-reference Methods, detection definition, statistical Methods, Results and limitations. Supplementary training tables were not independently inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective three-center evaluation of 1,076 selected angiography images from 420 patients. Nine view-specific segmentation models combined DeepLabV3+/EfficientNet-B4, U-Net++/EfficientNet-B4 and U²-Net; training images from 2016 were separate from 2022 evaluation data. Against blinded manual QCA, the system detected 1,705/1,828 lesions (93%) versus 69% for visual estimation; on multiple-lesion images it identified all reference lesions in 86% versus 33%.
evidence.unknown: Manual QCA is the anatomical reference, not physiological significance or clinical outcomes. Selected frames excluded occlusions and poor-quality images; only reference lesions meeting size/stenosis criteria were counted. Lesion observations repeat within patients, and reported significance does not establish cluster-adjusted uncertainty. No prospective procedural or patient benefit was tested; training details in the supplementary material were not independently inspected.
evidence.ai_role: Learned vessel segmenters generated lumen boundaries; an ensemble and downstream lesion analysis located and quantified lesions for comparison with manual QCA and cardiologist visual estimates.

title: Language models flag spiritual pain in palliative nursing notes with many false positives
summary: Gemini 2.5 Flash and Microsoft Copilot detected all 56 expert-labeled spiritual-pain notes in a selected 500-note palliative-care sample. Positive predictive values were only 34% and 25%, respectively. The retrospective study identifies substantial over-detection rather than validating an autonomous diagnostic or clinical screening workflow.
ai_technology: Gemini 2.5 Flash; Microsoft Copilot language-model service
organization: Tohoku University; Tohoku University Hospital

source_review.scope: Read actual primary record sampling/filtering, consensus annotation, named language models and prompting Methods, result/error tables and limitations. Supplementary prompt appendices were not independently inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: From 6,858 nursing records in the last three weeks of life of 109 patients, keyword filtering retained 1,808 records and 500 were sampled. Two researchers annotated spiritual pain with consensus resolution. Japanese few-shot prompts supplied definitions/examples to Gemini 2.5 Flash and Copilot. Both detected all 56 reference-positive notes; specificity was 0.75/0.61 and positive predictive value 0.34/0.25. Gemini false positives frequently confused declining physical function and delirium with spiritual pain.
evidence.unknown: Selected single-hospital Japanese records, multiple notes per patient and keyword enrichment limit generalization and apparent sensitivity. Reference is retrospective note interpretation, not direct patient assessment. Copilot underlying model version was not specified. No unfiltered-record screening, prospective clinical utility, improved care or autonomous diagnosis was established; human verification remains necessary.
evidence.ai_role: Pretrained language models applied prompted spiritual-pain definitions to free-text nursing notes, producing classifications compared with independent expert annotations; error analysis characterized their misinterpretations.

title: Clinical-record models show modest discrimination of cardiac events after checkpoint therapy
summary: Elastic-net regression, gradient-boosted trees and random forests showed similar exploratory discrimination of coded cardiac events after immune checkpoint therapy, with test AUCs around 0.72. Positive predictive values remained below 5%. The selected retrospective cohort and outcome-informed preprocessing limit interpretation as a ready-to-use baseline risk tool.
ai_technology: Elastic-net logistic regression; gradient-boosted trees; random forest
organization: University of California, Irvine; Okayama University

source_review.scope: Read actual primary outcome/exposure definitions, selection window, feature construction, cohort-wide initial screening, patient partition, named model/tuning Methods, performance Results and limitations. Supplementary modeling tables were not independently inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: TriNetX retrospective cohort of 61,117 patients receiving checkpoint therapy in 2010–2023, including 1,172 coded cardiac inflammatory events within 90 days. A stratified 70:30 patient split yielded 18,335 test patients. Models used baseline demographic, diagnosis and medication features with resampling and cross-validated tuning. Test AUCs were 0.718, 0.718 and 0.719; all models had positive predictive values below 5%.
evidence.unknown: Diagnostic codes plus hospitalization, not adjudicated drug causation, defined events. Event-free patients needed at least 60 days on therapy, conditioning eligibility on post-baseline exposure. Initial feature prevalence screening used event cases from the entire cohort before splitting, so evaluation is not completely isolated from feature selection. Missing diagnoses/exposures were treated as absent; calibration and rare-event precision were limited. No independent prospective validation, prevention benefit or causal risk factors were established.
evidence.ai_role: Learned regression/tree models mapped recorded baseline characteristics to coded 90-day events; comparisons measured their modest retrospective prognostic discrimination and false-positive limitations.

title: Random forests link CT features to catheter-measured endpoints in CTEPH
summary: Random forests combined CT measurements and qualitative findings to classify catheter-measured hemodynamic endpoints in patients with operable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. Retrospective internal testing reported AUC 0.82 for a pulmonary-pressure category and 0.74 for a pulmonary-artery oxygen-saturation category. Replacement of invasive testing or improved management was not demonstrated.
ai_technology: Random forest
organization: Technical University of Munich; Saarland University Medical Center; University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein; Robert Bosch Hospital

source_review.scope: Read primary cohort/reference, CT-feature assessment, normalization/random-forest evaluation Methods, endpoint Results and limitations. Actual source describes threefold random sampling; a more detailed nested validation design is not inferred. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Single-center retrospective cohort of 127 operable CTEPH patients from 2015–2020 with CT and preoperative right-heart catheterization. Pulmonary pressure was available in 127 patients and pulmonary-artery oxygen saturation in 55. Random forests used normalized quantitative and qualitative CT features, evaluated through a source-described threefold random-sampling procedure. Reported endpoint-classification AUCs were 0.82 and 0.74.
evidence.unknown: Small selected surgical cohort, including only 55 patients for the oxygen endpoint; no external model validation. Exact normalization/filtering nesting and hyperparameter selection were incompletely specified. CT-feature associations are observational, and feature importance is not causation. Benefits for patient management and replacement of catheterization remain untested.
evidence.ai_role: Random forests learned combinations of CT-derived measurements and qualitative imaging findings to classify catheter-referenced hemodynamic categories; feature filtering characterized the model-relevant signals.

title: Forest-based gene selection links PGAP1 and TMBIM1 expression to systemic sclerosis
summary: Boruta and random forests prioritized PGAP1 and TMBIM1 from systemic-sclerosis expression data. The selected genes showed opposite expression changes in two small human skin datasets, with corresponding expression changes reported in mouse fibrotic tissues. The result is an association and expression validation, not a demonstrated disease mechanism or treatment.
ai_technology: Boruta random-forest feature selection; random forest
organization: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi’an Jiaotong University

source_review.scope: Read primary data/cohort, Boruta/random-forest feature selection and validation-set filtering Methods, human expression Results, high-level mouse expression Results and mechanistic limitations. Operational experimental procedures and supplementary replicate details are outside the represented evidence scope. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Single-cell data from 12 systemic-sclerosis and 3 control skin samples informed candidate genes. Boruta-confirmed genes were intersected with top random-forest importance ranks. Human bulk datasets comprised 18 cases/15 controls and 10 cases/5 controls; the second dataset also participated in final gene filtering. PGAP1 was lower and TMBIM1 higher in affected human skin, with corresponding transcript/protein expression findings in source-reported mouse fibrotic tissues.
evidence.unknown: Small reused human datasets; the nominal validation dataset helped select genes, so it is not an untouched external diagnostic test. Mouse expression association does not establish causal antagonism, Th17 specificity, human diagnostic utility or therapeutic efficacy. PGAP1 lung expression changed with time. Detailed experimental replicate counts and supplementary datasets were not independently inspected; drug/docking predictions are not represented as treatments.
evidence.ai_role: Boruta and random-forest ranking reduced disease-associated candidates to genes taken forward for cross-dataset expression comparisons and targeted tissue-expression checks.

title: Deployed delirium model retains discrimination at a second hospital
summary: A frozen random-forest system combining clinical data and an NLP risk score was evaluated during deployment at a second Mount Sinai hospital. Retrospective workflow analysis reported AUC 0.91 and positive predictive value 25.9%; targeted assessments had a higher delirium yield than a historical period. Selective verification and changing workflows prevent a causal patient-benefit interpretation.
ai_technology: Random forest with structured clinical features and an NLP-derived risk score
organization: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; Mount Sinai Morningside Hospital; The Mount Sinai Hospital; NYC Health + Hospitals

source_review.scope: Read actual primary model operation, frozen deployment, cohort/reference and workflow Methods, performance and yield Results, limitations, plus publisher-linked invited-commentary context. Publication date follows original publisher and PMC Article Information November 4; indexed November 2 is retained separately without a first-ever-version claim. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Frozen model deployed without local retraining at Mount Sinai Morningside in November 2024. Retrospective analysis compared 9,020 admissions there with 21,186 contemporaneous development-hospital admissions and 2,889 historical predeployment admissions. At the second hospital, reported AUC was 0.91 and positive predictive value 25.9%. Only 2,649 of 9,020 admissions received CAM assessments; the rest relied on diagnosis codes. Mean monthly yield among CAM assessments rose from 9.23% to 19.59%.
evidence.unknown: Same-health-system transportability, not independent-health-system validation. Model-guided CAM assessment creates incomplete verification and incorporation biases; remaining reference labels use diagnosis codes. Site thresholds differ, calibration was not the primary endpoint and false positives were frequent. Historical2018–2019 versus2024–2025 comparisons are confounded and measure yield per assessment, not incidence or improved outcomes. Linked invited commentary emphasizes these interpretation limits.
evidence.ai_role: A trained random forest fused structured/semistructured clinical information with an NLP-derived note score to prioritize live clinical delirium assessments; the study measured its within-system transportability and operational assessment yield.

title: Leukocyte RNA retention modestly changes platelet-based cancer classification
summary: Ten learned classifiers tested whether leukocyte-associated RNA retention affects platelet RNA cancer detection. In a matched 754-sample analysis, training on high-retention samples modestly improved some classifiers; most differences were not significant. Adding the retention score to a full-cohort classifier changed AUC only from 0.9247 to 0.9249, challenging a blanket assumption that this signal should always be removed.
ai_technology: SVM; LightGBM; XGBoost; random forest and other learned classifiers
organization: University of Gdansk; Medical University of Gdansk; Gdansk University of Technology; Polish Academy of Sciences; University of Utah; Amsterdam UMC

source_review.scope: Read actual primary marker/data and matched-cohort definitions, ten named classifiers, splitting/tuning Methods, actual performance tables 1–2, Results and interpretive limitations. Operational sample-processing procedures and supplements are outside the represented evidence scope. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Analysis combined 2,351 public platelet RNA samples with a marker panel derived from single-cell data from 29 donors. Matching yielded 377 high-retention and 377 low-retention samples, with cancer type balanced but residual collection-center imbalance. Ten classifiers used separate training/validation/test sets across repeated splits and validation-only hyperparameter optimization. SVM mean test AUC was 0.76 when trained on low-retention versus 0.84 on high-retention samples; corresponding LightGBM values were 0.74/0.79 and XGBoost 0.71/0.74. Most other training-retention comparisons were not significant.
evidence.unknown: RNA retention score is a compositional proxy, not physical purity or a causal manipulation. Residual collection-center confounding remains; repeated overlapping splits do not provide 30 independent biological replications. Model-specific modest effects do not establish universally beneficial retention, a correction standard or clinical benefit. The full-cohort added-score comparison was nearly null, and generalization to separately collected clinical cohorts is untested.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers provided the cancer-detection experiments needed to quantify how differing RNA-retention strata change diagnostic performance; the finding concerns assay signal composition rather than a new general classifier architecture.

title: Low-field shoulder MRI with learned reconstruction agrees with surgical findings
summary: A paired prospective study evaluated 0.55 T shoulder MRI reconstructed with Deep Resolve Boost against conventional 1.5 T imaging. Among 25 patients with suspected rotator-cuff injury, 16 underwent arthroscopy; MRI findings showed good to perfect agreement with surgery. Different coils, hardware and reconstruction prevent attributing the system comparison solely to AI.
ai_technology: Deep Resolve Boost convolutional neural-network MRI reconstruction
organization: Peking University First Hospital; Siemens Healthineers

source_review.scope: Read primary named CNN reconstruction operation, paired prospective cohorts, blinded reading/reference Methods, lesion Results and limitations. Original PMC article publication date October20 is distinguished from November issue date. Supplementary acquisition tables and vendor training datasets were not independently inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Prospectively enrolled 25 volunteers and 25 patients, each examined with both MRI systems. The 0.55 T system used a vendor-trained CNN reconstruction combining noise maps and raw sensor data; the 1.5 T comparator did not use DL. Blinded randomized readings compared image quality and lesion assessment. Sixteen patients received arthroscopy; source-reported lesion agreement was perfect for the senior reader and good to perfect for the junior reader. Both systems had closely agreeing lesion assessments.
evidence.unknown: Small single-center selected rotator-cuff cohort and partial surgical verification; not an unbiased sensitivity/specificity screening study. Field strength, coils, hardware and reconstruction differ simultaneously, with no same-scanner DL ablation or 1.5 T DL comparator. The study validates the combined configuration, not an isolated causal AI benefit or improved patient outcome. Vendor training data and supplementary acquisition details were not independently inspected.
evidence.ai_role: Deep Resolve Boost CNNs reconstructed the low-field images from raw measurements and noise maps, producing the images used for blinded clinical lesion evaluation and surgical-reference comparison.

title: LightGBM estimates treatment-machine leaf errors in separate patient plans
summary: A LightGBM model predicted logged multi-leaf collimator position errors in radiotherapy plans from previously unseen patients. Six held-out plans had mean absolute error 0.054 mm; nine additional patient plans supported dose-recalculation agreement. These are machine-log and calculated-dose validation results, with no measured patient benefit or independent physical dose validation.
ai_technology: LightGBM gradient-boosted decision trees
organization: Shahid Beheshti University; Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences; Tehran University of Medical Sciences; Amirkabir University of Technology

source_review.scope: Read actual primary patient/plan partition, signed-error/log reference, LightGBM tuning/feature selection, separate nine-patient dosimetric Methods, Results and limitations. Original article-meta online October27 is distinguished from November collection date. Supplementary raw logs were not independently inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Twenty-nine patient plans were split by patient/plan into 23 development and six held-out test plans. GroupKFold tuning and development-only feature selection preceded final fitting. Against delivered-position machine logs, test MAE was 0.054 mm and RMSE 0.144 mm. Nine further patients supplied independent plans over six fractions; predicted and logged leaf positions were separately inserted into plans for dose recalculation on patient CTs. Agreement concerns reconstructed dose distributions, not in-vivo measured dose.
evidence.unknown: Single treatment center and accelerator; many leaf/control-point observations derive from few patients. Machine logs are the position reference and both dose distributions use the same dose-calculation system, so no independent physical dosimetry or outcome benefit is established. Dosimetric deviations were small and gamma agreement already high for delivered plans; the study does not establish detection of clinically dangerous failures or safer treatment.
evidence.ai_role: LightGBM learned plan/mechanical/initialization features to estimate delivered leaf-position errors; predicted positions enabled patient-plan dose recalculations compared with log-derived delivery estimates.

title: Learned blood-omics factors track Rett syndrome status and severity in a small cohort
summary: Unsupervised integration of four blood-omics measurements identified a disease-associated molecular factor and a second factor correlated with clinical severity in nine people with Rett syndrome and eight controls. The learned factors connect measurements across molecular layers, but remain exploratory within-cohort associations. They are not validated diagnostic tests, causal disease mechanisms or demonstrated treatment-response markers.
ai_technology: MOFA2 unsupervised multi-omics latent-factor learning
organization: University of Sydney; Children’s Hospital at Westmead; Macquarie University; Translational Genomics Research Institute; Baylor College of Medicine; Emory University

evidence.tested: Four matched molecular-data layers from nine Rett syndrome participants and eight controls were integrated using MOFA2 latent-factor learning. The main computational Methods specify normalized inputs, participant-identifier joins and associations between factor scores and clinical severity. Factor 1 separated the sampled clinical groups; Factor 2 correlated with severity among the nine affected participants, with reported Spearman rho 0.77 and nominal p 0.016.
evidence.unknown: Seventeen people and nine severity observations are too few to establish generalizable biomarker performance. Factor selection and severity association used the same cohort, without held-out diagnostic evaluation or demonstrated multiplicity-adjusted confirmation of the severity result. Age, cell composition, medication, diet and systemic physiology may influence molecular profiles; peripheral blood does not directly establish brain mechanisms. Orthogonal measurement of an individual metabolite does not independently validate the learned latent factors. No longitudinal response-to-treatment or causal effect was tested.
evidence.ai_role: MOFA2 learned shared variation across transcript, protein, phosphorylation and metabolite measurements, enabling the represented cross-layer disease and severity-associated factor analysis beyond separate differential-expression tests.

source_review.scope: Read primary cohort/reference metadata, computational normalization/integration/MOFA2 factor and severity-association Methods, corresponding factor Results and clinical/confounding limitations. No laboratory procedures were independently adjudicated. Individual metabolite confirmation is not counted as independent latent-model validation. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned simulator analysis resolves interaction-dependent effects in a perovskite solar-cell model
summary: A LightGBM surrogate of a specified perovskite solar-cell simulator identified absorber-thickness and acceptor-doping effects that largely cancel when averaged across the sampled parameter space but reverse direction under different defect-density or band-alignment conditions. Original simulator data supported those conditional patterns. The finding concerns a computational response surface; no fabricated device or experimentally realized efficiency improvement was demonstrated.
ai_technology: LightGBM surrogate regression; Sobol global sensitivity analysis
organization: Netaji Subhas University of Technology

source_review.scope: Read indexed original publisher Methods2, global-sensitivity Results3.4, original-simulator stratification and doping branches3.5, verification sweeps3.6, optimization failures3.7 and computational-only Conclusion. Exact publisher DOI/title/date matched current canonical Crossref metadata; current relation/update fields and publisher notice context checked. Supplement not read.

evidence.tested: A seven-parameter SCAPS-1D dataset retained 4,396 runs, with 3,525 training and 871 separately sampled test points. The selected LightGBM model was refitted on all retained runs for 262,144-evaluation sensitivity analysis. The source attributed 17.8% of modeled efficiency variance to interactions. Thickness and acceptor doping had near-zero first-order sensitivity but nonzero total effects; stratified original simulator data showed sign reversals. Separate simulator verification exposed wrong donor-density trends and overoptimistic ranking of the surrogate-selected optimum.
evidence.unknown: Results depend on the chosen simulator, layer stack, sampled ranges and numerical assumptions. Known defect-density effects were recovered rather than established as new physics. Surrogate sensitivity shares are not measured device variance, and original simulator checks are not external experimental replication. Several trends and selected-optimum ranking disagreed with direct simulation; no global physical optimum or fabricated high-efficiency device is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: The learned surrogate made a high-dimensional global sensitivity decomposition tractable and localized conditional parameter effects that pooled or single-parameter summaries concealed. Those interpretations were compared with original simulator data and explicit verification runs.

title: Automated spinal-lesion measurements retain an association with neurological recovery
