ai_technology: Adversarial cycle-consistent SPECT-to-PET image translation with a U-Net generator
organization: Kyushu University; Tokyo Women’s Medical University

evidence.tested: Seventy-one patients had matched SPECT/PET examinations. Thirty-one supplied image-level training/validation data; forty different patients supplied the clinical test set. Two radiologists and one cardiologist performed blinded, randomized-order consensus scoring against PET. Regional inferior-wall overscoring was reduced in the translated images, while the source documented an example of a real perfusion defect disappearing after correction.
evidence.unknown: Internal training/validation images were randomly split within thirty-one patients, rather than a demonstrated patient-separated validation split. Training SPECT/PET scans could be separated by up to three years; test scans were separated by roughly forty-six days on average. Single-center selection, small and biased clinical subgroups, consensus readers and reference-scan temporal differences limit generalization. Some image-error metrics worsened and reduced significance against PET is not proof of equivalence. True-defect erasure prevents any claim of uniformly safe correction. No clinical outcome, radiation-dose benefit or replacement utility was established.
evidence.ai_role: The learned adversarial translation transformed non-attenuation-corrected SPECT images into PET-like representations, enabling the represented patient-level comparison of regional attenuation artifacts and correction failures against an imaging reference.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary cohort/reference timing, adversarial translation/training and held-patient test Methods, blinded regional scoring/statistics, clinical image Results and documented overcorrection/limitations. No claim that nonsignificant differences prove equivalence or that corrected images safely replace the reference. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Neural ECG classifier reduces inconclusive readings across four devices
summary: A prospective diagnostic study compared a residual neural classifier with four device algorithms against physician-interpreted ECGs. Among 824 recordings from 206 patients, inconclusive results fell from 16% to 1.2%. This selected hospital study does not establish population-screening or workload benefit.
ai_technology: PulseAI residual convolutional neural network
organization: University Hospital Basel; PulseAI

evidence.tested: Near-contemporaneous physician-interpreted 12-lead references; blinded adjudication. Training contained no smart-device recordings.
evidence.unknown: 52 of 258 recruited patients lacked complete recordings. Selected electrophysiology patients, vectorized exports and unrepeated inconclusive recordings limit generalization. Four recordings per participant are correlated. Vendor-affiliated authors participated; no clinical-outcome benefit tested.
evidence.ai_role: A trained residual CNN classifies rhythm from raw single-lead signals.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary clinical/model Methods, Results and limitations; exact front/date/current PubMed notices.

title: Learned transcriptomic selection identifies a pediatric-sepsis blood-marker pattern
summary: Three learned feature-selection approaches converged on CYSTM1, MMP8 and CD177 in public pediatric blood-expression data. The source reports higher expression and case-control discrimination in a further dataset. This is a retrospective molecular association, including a less-studied CYSTM1 candidate, without established diagnostic specificity, clinical utility or causal treatment relevance.
ai_technology: Random forest, SVM recursive feature elimination and LASSO logistic feature selection
organization: Zhejiang University; Shaoxing People’s Hospital; Columbia University

evidence.tested: The analysis combined GSE26378 and GSE26440, with primary series metadata listing 180 septic-shock and 53 normal-control blood-expression profiles in total. Differential/module filtering preceded RF, SVM-RFE and tenfold-tuned LASSO selection. Their intersection identified CYSTM1, MMP8 and CD177. The paper reports increased expression and discrimination in GSE13904, a separately indexed pediatric inflammatory-spectrum dataset.
evidence.unknown: Distinct series/sample identifiers do not prove independent people. GSE13904 includes inflammatory-response, sepsis and septic-shock samples; the exact analytic subset and repeated-person separation were not independently reconstructed. Feature filtering used clinical labels before selection, and healthy-control contrasts do not establish real-world diagnostic specificity. Source prose twice refers to rheumatoid arthritis despite the sepsis analysis; no RA result is adopted. MMP8/CD177 links to sepsis were already known, and CYSTM1 remains a candidate association without functional or therapeutic validation. Reported ROC/decision curves do not demonstrate clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: The three learned selectors prioritized a shared measured-expression marker set after broad filtering, enabling the represented candidate-pattern and subsequent source-described case-control comparison. Immune deconvolution or network diagrams alone are not the admission basis.

source_review.scope: Read original computational cohort/filtering/RF/SVM-RFE/LASSO and ROC Methods, candidate/validation-expression Results and stated limits; separately read primary GEO series-level cohort metadata and exact GSM intersections. Patient-level independence and full validation subset were not reconstructed. No operational biological procedures or causal treatment claim. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned satellite mapping characterizes mixed floating-debris accumulation along the Tisza
summary: A support-vector classifier applied to 61 Sentinel-2 images mapped mixed natural and human-made floating-debris patches along 175 kilometers of the Middle Tisza River. The estimates identified a large persistent accumulation upstream of Kisköre Dam and changes across years and river stages. Moderate test performance, coarse pixels and biased visibility of large patches limit these estimates; they are not a plastic-mass inventory or proof that the dam caused the pattern.
ai_technology: RBF support-vector classification of multispectral satellite pixels
organization: University of Szeged; Tanta University

evidence.tested: Training/validation used 1,974 labeled satellite pixels with an 80:20 random split; three separate litter-patch regions were used for size/generalization testing against higher-resolution imagery. The selected SVC had F1 approximately 0.62 on that broader test, below its random-pixel validation result. The model was then applied to 61 images from 2015–2021 across a 175-kilometer reach to estimate patch distributions and temporal changes.
evidence.unknown: Mixed debris includes substantial natural vegetation and wood; artificial litter cannot be separately quantified. Labels emphasized large persistent accumulations, and reference imagery differed in acquisition time. Spatially correlated pixels, tuning on limited data, false positives from vegetation/shadows/structures and missed sub-pixel patches constrain estimates. Three patch regions do not establish broad independent geographic validation. Temporal map patterns are model-derived observations, without independent field verification of every mapped patch or causal attribution to dam operation.
evidence.ai_role: The learned SVC separated debris-like from non-debris pixel signatures across repeated satellite observations, enabling the represented regional spatial and temporal accumulation analysis beyond the detector leaderboard.

source_review.scope: Read original labeling/scene acquisition, model/tuning and split Methods, three-patch test performance, SVC application to 61 mapping scenes and regional spatio-temporal Results/limitations. Represented finding is the bounded regional debris map analysis, not a benchmark-only detector claim. Original online April 28 distinguished from May issue. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Clinical coronary CT comparison finds medium-strength learned reconstruction gives the clearest plaque images
summary: In 51 patients, a paired comparison of fourteen reconstructions per coronary CT scan found that medium-strength deep learning reconstruction received the highest plaque-image quality ratings. High-strength reconstruction reduced noise most, but readers noted blurring of small plaque contours. The study tested image quality, without invasive angiography as a diagnostic reference or demonstrated clinical outcome benefit.
ai_technology: TrueFidelity deep neural network reconstruction trained on high-quality filtered-back-projection images
organization: Sapienza University of Rome; Sant’Andrea University Hospital

evidence.tested: Prospective single-center enrollment yielded 51 patients and 714 reconstructed datasets. Each acquisition was reconstructed using filtered back-projection, ten ASiR-V strengths and three learned reconstruction strengths. Two experienced radiologists, blinded to reconstruction protocol, assessed four selected reconstructions in consensus, with randomized reading order and separated sessions. Medium-strength DLIR had the highest subjective plaque-image quality; high-strength DLIR had lower noise but did not significantly outperform maximum-strength ASiR-V on the reported objective noise, SNR and CNR comparisons.
evidence.unknown: One vendor and center, selected subjective comparison datasets, consensus readers without separate-reader reproducibility, and exclusion of severe motion or high heart rates limit generalization. No invasive coronary reference was routinely available, so agreement between image reconstructions does not establish diagnostic accuracy. No radiation-dose reduction, patient outcome benefit or dedicated stent subgroup result was tested.
evidence.ai_role: The pretrained neural reconstruction selectively suppressed image noise in actual patient acquisitions, enabling the paired clinical test of image-quality and plaque-contour tradeoffs across reconstruction strengths.

source_review.scope: Read actual original cohort, neural reconstruction, paired objective/subjective evaluation and statistical Methods, corresponding Results and source limitations. Direct test refers to controlled paired clinical image-quality measurement, not prospective diagnostic outcome validation. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned Holter analysis agrees with physician AF-burden estimates
summary: A trained ECG-analysis system estimated atrial-fibrillation burden in seven-day recordings. In 47 recordings with intermediate burden, correlation with physician review was 0.998 and agreement bias was −0.006. This validates measurement agreement in a selected cohort, not treatment or outcome benefit.
ai_technology: Cardiomatics trained ECG rhythm-classification system
organization: University Hospital Basel; University of Basel

evidence.tested: 100 recordings from82 patients;53 zero/full-burden recordings were separated from the47 intermediate-burden comparisons. Repeated recordings were assessed with a patient-random-intercept sensitivity analysis.
evidence.unknown: Small sample and few women limit transfer. Paced rhythms were excluded. Training architecture and training/test overlap were not fully documented in the study; no efficiency or clinical-outcome benefit measured.
evidence.ai_role: Previously trained algorithms classify ECG rhythm and aggregate detected AF duration into burden.

source_review.scope: Primary indexed clinical/reference/software/statistical Methods, results and study limitations; exact fresh PubMed date/status.

title: Retrospective screening study measures the sensitivity–specificity trade-off of learned hypertension detection
summary: A random-forest model evaluated on a held-out subset of an Italian blood-pressure screening campaign identified previously unrecognized high blood pressure with a different sensitivity–specificity trade-off from a simple risk-factor protocol. The endpoint was same-visit elevated blood pressure, not future hypertension. Results were modest and did not establish cost savings, better patient outcomes or universal superiority over clinical screening.
ai_technology: Random forest classification with training-set undersampling
organization: University of Urbino Carlo Bo; Istituto Auxologico Italiano; University of Milano-Bicocca; University of Bologna; University of L’Aquila; University of Brescia

evidence.tested: From 37,110 campaign participants in 2015–2019, the analysis retained 20,206 adults without known or treated hypertension, including 4,192 newly detected cases defined by measured blood pressure. Data were randomly split into 14,144 training and 6,062 validation records; hyperparameter search used training cross-validation and resampling was applied to training data. The selected undersampled random forest reported sensitivity 0.818, specificity 0.629 and AUC 0.816.
evidence.unknown: Volunteer participation, complete-case exclusions, self-reported predictors and same-visit blood-pressure labeling limit interpretation. The clinical risk-factor comparator was applied to the original dataset, while model performance used the validation subset; this is not a paired matched-set intervention comparison. Models/configurations were compared on one internal validation cohort, without independent geographic/temporal replication. Single-visit elevated pressure does not establish future onset or longitudinal clinical diagnosis.
evidence.ai_role: The learned RF combined questionnaire and demographic predictors to classify measured previously unrecognized elevated blood pressure, enabling a specific retrospective clinical-screening validation and its observed sensitivity–specificity trade-off.

source_review.scope: Read actual participant/reference definition, exclusions, features, 70:30 split, training-only resampling/tuning, held-out clinical Results and comparator scope. Original article-meta December29 publication date read. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Echo videos estimate CT-referenced coronary-calcium categories
summary: A video neural network estimated coronary-calcium categories from echocardiograms. In 92 patients from a separate hospital, AUC was 0.75 for zero calcium and 0.85 for high calcium. This retrospective clinical validation does not establish screening benefit or replacement of CT.
ai_technology: R2+1D convolutional neural network; EchoNet-Dynamic transfer learning
organization: University of California, San Francisco; Cedars-Sinai Medical Center; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Development used 2,881 echocardiograms from 1,635 patients, paired with CT calcium scores; the reported external set contained 92 patients.
evidence.unknown: Selected patients had both tests within one year. Internal splitting is described by echocardiograms rather than clearly separated patients; external results are represented separately. Preventive-treatment benefit and population-screening performance were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained spatiotemporal CNN learns echo-video features associated with CT-derived calcium labels.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front DOI/title/PMCID/date, indexed primary clinical/model Methods and Results, fresh primary publication-status metadata. Author PDF returned HTTP202 and was not read.

title: AI-assisted CT risk score retains mortality discrimination in a later COVID-19 cohort
summary: A five-variable model combining demographic data, oxygen saturation and automatically extracted CT measurements distinguished recorded mortality in a later COVID-19 cohort. Developed from 1,125 first-wave patients, AI-SCoRE achieved a reported AUC of 0.808 in 213 second-wave patients. This supports a bounded clinical prognostic validation, without demonstrated treatment benefit or proof that the predictor was locked before validation outcomes accrued.
ai_technology: Pretrained U-Net lung segmentation with quantitative CT feature extraction, logistic risk modeling and CART risk binning
organization: Vita-Salute San Raffaele University; IRCCS San Raffaele Scientific Institute

evidence.tested: A multicenter first-wave dataset was reduced from 1,575 enrolled patients to 1,125 complete records, including 292 deaths. Repeated train/test splits and repeated cross-validation compared candidate models and selected a five-variable logistic model. Pretrained learned segmentation enabled automated lung measurements. A later, prospectively collected single-center cohort of 213 patients, including 31 deaths, yielded AUC 0.808 with reported 95% confidence interval 0.740–0.877.
evidence.unknown: Prospective cohort collection does not establish that the model and thresholds were fixed before its outcomes were known. Complete-case selection, different pandemic waves, one-center later validation and historical treatment conditions limit transportability. The paper inconsistently describes 213 versus 214 validation patients and presents four low-risk deaths as 1.8% without a clearly appropriate low-risk denominator; those percentages and post-hoc exclusions are not adopted here. Supplemental acquisition/endpoint details were not independently read. No causal CT mechanism, intervention benefit or current clinical utility is established.
evidence.ai_role: Pretrained neural segmentation converted patient CT scans into quantitative lung features used with clinical variables in the represented mortality score; learned risk modeling and binning enabled the patient-outcome discrimination analysis.

source_review.scope: Read primary front identity/date, clinical study design, modeling and segmentation Methods, cohort/model/later-wave mortality Results and limitations. Supplemental Methods were not independently read. Later cohort collection was prospective; temporal predictor locking was not established. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned MRI analysis distinguishes postanoxic coma from healthy controls in a small cohort
summary: A three-dimensional convolutional network distinguished 29 postanoxic-coma patients from 34 healthy volunteers using structural and functional MRI measurements. Posterior-cingulate functional connectivity provided the strongest reported internal discrimination, outperforming the tested structural inputs. The result is a small clinical imaging feasibility study, without independently validated prediction of recovery or demonstrated bedside benefit.
ai_technology: Custom three-dimensional convolutional neural network for multimodal brain MRI classification
organization: Toulouse III Paul Sabatier University; Inserm; CNRS; Toulouse University Hospital

evidence.tested: A prospectively collected single-center cohort included 29 postanoxic-coma patients and 34 healthy volunteers. Separate structural and functional MRI inputs were evaluated with a custom 3D CNN using ten-times repeated tenfold cross-validation. Input intensity normalization used training-set values. Posterior-cingulate functional-connectivity inputs achieved reported mean accuracy 0.96, versus 0.82 for T1 structural input.
evidence.unknown: Small groups, a healthy-control contrast, one scanner/center and repeated internal cross-validation limit clinical specificity and generalization. Prospective collection is not an external locked-model evaluation. Convolutional activation maps were derived from correctly classified training samples and do not establish causal consciousness mechanisms. Post-hoc favorable outcomes among a few misclassified patients are not independent recovery prediction. No clinical deployment, prognosis-guided intervention or outcome benefit was demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: The trained 3D CNN learned spatial features from patient and control MRI volumes, enabling the represented clinical-status discrimination and comparison of the informative content of different MRI inputs.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary patient/control and clinical reference selection, imaging input, 3D CNN architecture/training/normalization/cross-validation Methods, modality-comparison Results and interpretive limitations. Post-hoc recovery hints and training activation maps are not admitted as validated prognosis or causal mechanisms. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Neural phase-label flickering tracks atypical courses in a small surgical-video study
summary: Researchers found that unstable phase labels from a pretrained surgical-video network coincided with complicated or atypical courses in fifteen recorded operations. The observed pattern supplied an exploratory alert signal beyond ordinary phase-recognition accuracy. Flicker measures and thresholds were developed on the same videos, so the result does not establish an independently validated complication detector or better clinical documentation.
ai_technology: TeCNO convolutional temporal surgical-phase recognition with post-hoc flicker analysis
organization: Technical University of Munich; Klinikum rechts der Isar

evidence.tested: TeCNO was trained on 52 surgical videos and applied to fifteen further cholecystectomy videos, independently phase-annotated by a highly experienced surgeon. Investigators then reviewed unstable label clusters and derived flicker thresholds on those same fifteen cases. The source reports that threshold rules identified five of six apparently divergent courses; one gallbladder perforation produced no substantial flicker increase.
evidence.unknown: Post-hoc pattern recognition, same-cohort cutoff derivation and a very small event count create substantial optimism and selection risk. Independent blinded complication adjudication and external alert validation were not established. Phase-annotation agreement, report generation and exploratory event association do not demonstrate complete or safer operative documentation, real-time deployment, improved outcomes or reliable detection of specific complication types.
evidence.ai_role: The neural network generated time-ordered surgical-phase predictions; instability in those learned predictions exposed the represented association with atypical observed operative courses. The reporting interface itself is not treated as a scientific discovery.

source_review.scope: Read original training/inference video separation, expert annotation, learned phase and post-hoc flicker analysis Methods, observed atypical-case Results and discussion limitations. Represented result is the exploratory video-event association; generated reporting software is not an admission basis. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned tracking and agent models examine rapid mouse route choice
summary: Neural tracking supported evidence that mice favor shorter routes and smaller shelter angles before escape experience. Model-based learning agents reproduced rapid route choice from recorded exploration, whereas the tested model-free agent failed under that limited experience.
ai_technology: DeepLabCut neural pose estimation; model-based reinforcement learning
organization: University College London

evidence.tested: Custom-trained pose estimation measured trajectories. Q-learning, DYNA-Q and Influence Zones agents were compared using42 retained exploration sessions.
evidence.unknown: Agent agreement does not identify the biological learning algorithm. Recorded sessions and repeated trials are not independent neural-mechanism tests; alternative prior-knowledge explanations remain. No causal brain mechanism is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: A learned pose network extracts movement; reinforcement-learning agents test algorithmic explanations of recorded behavior.

source_review.scope: Safe tracking/RL computational Methods and high-level Results/Discussion; primary date/status. No operational animal procedure needed for represented scope.

title: Serial CT and clinical features support learned early classification of malignant stroke edema
summary: An LSTM combining serial clinical assessments and automated CT measurements identified malignant edema cases in an internal analysis of 598 stroke patients. Twenty patients required decompressive surgery or died with substantial midline shift. The source reports stronger internal precision than regression and a fully connected network, but rare events, imaging-based selection and absent external validation limit clinical interpretation.
ai_technology: Long short-term memory recurrent neural network combining serial clinical and CT-derived measurements
organization: Washington University in St. Louis; Jagiellonian University; Helsinki University Hospital

evidence.tested: A retrospective imaging substudy of a prospectively enrolled three-center stroke cohort retained 598 patients with baseline and follow-up CT, including twenty malignant-edema endpoints: twelve decompressive hemicraniectomies and eight deaths with midline shift of at least five millimeters. The main Methods describe nested stratified tenfold cross-validation with patients held out from training/tuning. The source reports LSTM recall 100%, precision 87% and AUPRC 0.97, compared with regression precision 32% and AUPRC 0.74 using the automated feature set.
evidence.unknown: Only twenty positive events and selection for available repeat imaging leave substantial uncertainty about transportability and overfitting. External cohorts, prospective locked-model evaluation and clinical decision benefit were not tested. The outcome combines a clinical intervention decision with edema-related death; CT and clinical assessment timing varied. Supplemental implementation/imputation details were not independently read, so fold-specific preprocessing isolation is not authenticated here. Model feature attribution is predictive association, not causal edema biology.
evidence.ai_role: The LSTM learned nonlinear dependencies across baseline and follow-up clinical/imaging measurements, enabling the represented patient-endpoint discrimination beyond the separately assessed regression and feed-forward models.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary clinical eligibility/outcome/timing, automated feature and LSTM/nested patient-cross-validation Methods, endpoint/model Results and limitations. Supplemental implementation/imputation Methods were not independently read; no claim that every preprocessing operation was fold-isolated. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned OCT texture analysis distinguishes sampled brain-metastasis tissue from healthy tissue
summary: A support-vector classifier separated OCT images of sampled brain metastases and healthy brain tissue using histology-derived labels. The analysis retained fourteen tissue samples from a twenty-patient collection. Reported image-level accuracy is exploratory: cross-validation split B-scans, without demonstrated separation of tissue samples or patients, and does not establish surgical diagnostic performance.
ai_technology: Support-vector machines on OCT texture features with PCA dimensionality reduction
organization: Ruhr University Bochum; Technische Hochschule Georg Agricola

evidence.tested: Twenty patients contributed twenty-two tissue samples; histologic purity criteria retained ten tumor and four healthy samples. An experienced neuropathologist assigned tissue-composition reference labels. Texture features from 14,336 OCT B-scans were reduced with PCA and classified using grid-tuned SVMs with tenfold cross-validation. The source reports up to 96.83% image-level discrimination of pooled vital/necrotic tumor versus healthy tissue.
evidence.unknown: B-scans from the same tissue specimen are correlated, and the described allocation does not establish specimen-level or patient-level separation between folds. Normalization/PCA isolation and nested tuning are not established. Purity-selected specimens and small sample counts constrain interpretation; thousands of images do not substitute for independent patients. No intraoperative clinical deployment, margin-level ground truth, recurrence reduction or survival benefit was demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: The SVM combined learned boundaries over multifeature OCT texture measurements to discriminate histology-labeled sampled tissue categories, supplying a specific ex-vivo diagnostic feasibility result. PCA alone is not treated as the enabling AI contribution.

source_review.scope: Read original patient/specimen selection and histology reference, image/texture/PCA/SVM and cross-validation Methods, classification Results and clinical translation limitations. Other laboratory processing details were not independently adjudicated. Source image-level results are explicitly distinguished from unestablished patient-held-out diagnostic accuracy. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Multimodal learned features classify prostate lymph-node involvement
summary: A stacked model combined pretrained MRI image features, radiomics and clinical information to classify pathology-referenced pelvic lymph-node involvement. Its AUC was 0.92 in 71 internal test patients and0.76 in 50 second-center patients. This retrospective validation does not establish avoided surgery or routine clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Pretrained image-network embeddings; random-forest signatures; AutoGluon stacked ensemble
organization: Nanjing Medical University; Soochow University

evidence.tested: 401 selected surgical patients:280 development,71 internal test and50 second-center test. Only six second-center patients had positive nodes; sensitivity there was50% at the development-selected threshold.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective surgical selection, small external positive count and site-specific readers limit transfer. Tumor segmentation used radiological-pathological correlation; preprocessing and feature-selection isolation are not completely specified. Source feature-importance description contains unrelated linker terminology. Surgery avoidance and decision-curve benefits are hypothetical.
evidence.ai_role: ImageNet-pretrained networks embed tumor/peritumoral MRI regions; forests select/learn imaging signatures and an ensemble integrates them with clinical and reader variables.

source_review.scope: Actual primary clinical/model Methods2.1–2.8, diagnostic Results3.2 and limitations; fresh exact PubMed date/notice metadata. No independent implementation or supplementary detail reproduction.

title: AI-assisted cardiac measurements show an in-hospital mortality association
summary: In the retrospective international WASE-COVID cohort, left-ventricular longitudinal strain was associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment. Left-ventricular measurements combined machine-learned software output with two blinded human reads. This is a selected-cohort association, not an AI-only mortality predictor or demonstrated clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Ultromics machine-learned left-ventricular measurement algorithms
organization: University of Chicago; MedStar Health Research Institute; Ultromics

evidence.tested: 870 hospitalized patients at13 centers;722 had usable left-ventricular analysis. Final measurements averaged one automated and two blinded human reads. Adjusted strain association OR1.179,95%CI1.045–1.358.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective first-wave population selected for clinically indicated echocardiograms; variable missing views and same-cohort stepwise adjustment. 89 missing two-chamber measurements imputed. No locked external mortality evaluation; individual strain discrimination limited. Right-ventricular measures used a separate semiautomated package. Software architecture/training supplement uninspected.
evidence.ai_role: Previously learned commercial algorithms generated ventricular volumes, ejection fraction and strain used with human reads in the association analysis. Conventional regression estimated the association.

source_review.scope: Actual primary Methods/Results/limitations and both linked letters read in supported Chrome. Letters debate interpretation and utility; response clarifies odds ratios and all-cause in-hospital death, not PPV or COVID-specific death.

title: Learned artifact localization supports a bounded radiotherapy-dose comparison
summary: An Inception-V3 classifier localized dental artifacts in CT images. In fifteen separate head-and-neck treatment plans, its outputs guided comparisons of artifact-management choices; calculated target-coverage differences stayed below 0.25 percentage points. This is a retrospective planning result, not measured delivered-dose equivalence or evidence of safer treatment.
ai_technology: Inception-V3 convolutional neural network
organization: University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

evidence.tested: Classifier development used 549 patients with patient-separated partitions. Fifteen other plans supplied comparisons of calculated dose after model-guided artifact localization.
evidence.unknown: One institution and planning system; no independent physical dosimetry, clinical outcomes or general treatment recommendation. Dose calculations are comparisons between modeled management scenarios.
evidence.ai_role: The learned slice classifier identifies locations used to define the compared artifact-management regions.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary full clinical/model Methods and dosimetric Results/discussion; exact front identity/date and current primary notice metadata.

title: Forests identify built-environment associations in recorded drug-crime patterns
summary: Random forests analyzed 52,567 reported drug-related incidents in Chicago during 2016–2019. Vacant lots and buildings ranked highly in models distinguishing recorded heroin and synthetic-drug clusters. These are neighborhood-level associations in police records, not causal effects or measures of individuals’ behavior.
ai_technology: Space-time random forest; guided regularized random forest; partial dependence
organization: University of Maryland; Oak Ridge National Laboratory

evidence.tested: Forest feature selection and importance analysis compared recorded cluster patterns with built-environment, demographic and lagged variables.
evidence.unknown: Policing practices were unavailable and may influence recorded patterns; ecological associations do not identify individual risk or prove neighborhood causes. Temporal-window selection used the studied series. No treatment-service or policing benefit was tested.
evidence.ai_role: Forest ensembles learn nonlinear feature combinations; corrected importance and partial dependence characterize the source-specific observed spatial associations.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary data/model/feature-selection Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary front date/affiliations and fresh primary notice metadata.

title: Learned CT block scores track reported opacity burden in a small COVID-19 cohort
summary: In 30 COVID-19 patients from an Italian CT cohort, a learned block-analysis score correlated with source-reported ground-glass-opacity values. The paper describes generating each patient’s score using a model trained without that patient. This is a small retrospective imaging association, not evidence that the score predicts clinical deterioration or measures physiological disease severity.
ai_technology: Random forest and related learned CT block classifiers
organization: Bennett University; University of Eastern Piedmont; AtheroPoint; University of Cagliari

evidence.tested: The source cohort contained 30 COVID-19 patients and 30 controls, contributing 705 and 990 CT slices respectively. Segmented lungs were divided into twelve spatial blocks and learned classifiers contributed to block-level scoring. For the specific patient-level association, Methods/Results state that all slices of each patient were scored by a system trained on all other patients. Appendix Table 12 lists 30 COVID-19 patients with the derived score and GGO values; the source reports correlation approximately 0.9145.
evidence.unknown: The score and GGO comparator describe the same images, rather than independent clinical outcomes or a causal mechanism. Small single-center retrospective data, sex imbalance and incomplete score-reference documentation limit interpretation. Image-level classification leaderboard metrics are omitted because their cross-validation description does not establish patient-disjoint partitions. The severity label used by the authors is not treated as a validated measure of prognosis, physiology or treatment need.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers distinguish CT-block feature distributions and contribute to a patient-level block score, enabling the represented comparison with reported CT-opacity values.

source_review.scope: Read actual cohort/reference and preprocessing Methods, learned classification/block-score workflow, explicit leave-patient-out score evaluation paragraph68 and full original Appendix Table12. Kept this patient-level opacity association separate from image-fold classification benchmarks. Original publisher January26 date read. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned ultrasound features classify breast sentinel-node involvement
summary: Image-pretrained convolutional models were fine-tuned on breast ultrasound images and combined with axillary ultrasound findings. In a retrospective second-hospital test of 395 women, the combined model classified pathology-referenced sentinel-node involvement with an AUC of 0.848. Avoided surgery was hypothetical, not an observed clinical benefit.
ai_technology: ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural networks with ultrasound fine-tuning
organization: Harbin Medical University

evidence.tested: 937 patients from two hospitals: 542 for development and 395 for testing; 3,049 images. The reference was surgical lymph-node assessment. Radial and anti-radial image-model probabilities were fused.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective exclusions and ultrasound-visible lesion selection limit transfer. Images were processed individually without explicitly modeling their correlation. The separate sequential non-sentinel-node analysis has conditional denominators and is not represented by the quoted AUC. Supplementary architecture and threshold-selection details were not independently inspected; no reduced surgery or outcome benefit was measured.
evidence.ai_role: Convolutional networks pre-trained on 1.28 million ImageNet images learned ultrasound features through fine-tuning; their predicted probabilities enabled the node-involvement evaluation.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary clinical design, convolutional-model operation, reference evaluation and limitations; exact primary DOI/title/PMCID and fresh PubMed electronic date/notice metadata.

title: Learned network features relate to simulated protein-network mechanics
summary: Gradient-boosted surrogates linked imaged network geometry to simulated mechanical responses. Density features dominated stress/strain estimates; segment inhomogeneity was most important for simulated buckling. These are conditional computational relationships, not measured in-vivo mechanics.
ai_technology: Gradient-boosted regression trees
organization: University of Stuttgart; University of Freiburg

evidence.tested: Thirty-seven imaged networks supported finite-element simulations; surrogate training/test contained33/4 networks with fivefold training cross-validation.
evidence.unknown: Linear elasticity, generic loading and failure criteria borrowed from another filament system limit interpretation. Imaging resolution and the four-network test restrict confidence. No causal architecture or experimentally measured mechanical function is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: Learned surrogates map26 structural descriptors to simulated responses and rank feature contributions.

source_review.scope: Computational Methods2.5–2.7, Results3.4 and limitations4.4; primary front/date/status. Experimental preparation sections were not used.

title: Learned reconstruction reduces perfusion-measurement bias in shortened cardiac SPECT data
summary: A residual network reconstructed full-acquisition-like cardiac SPECT from reduced-count or reduced-projection data derived from 363 patient scans. Internal comparisons found closer perfusion-deficit measurements to the full acquisitions than the uncorrected shortened data. These are image-based clinical measurement results, without independently acquired short-scan validation, established diagnostic accuracy or demonstrated radiation-dose benefit.
ai_technology: Twenty-layer dilated residual convolutional neural networks for projection-domain SPECT reconstruction
organization: Geneva University Hospitals; University of Geneva; Sharif University of Technology; Iran University of Medical Sciences; Tehran University of Medical Sciences; University of Groningen; University of Southern Denmark

evidence.tested: A prospectively collected 363-person clinical cohort supplied full-acquisition list-mode data. Shorter-time data used the first half of acquisition events, while fewer-projection data omitted alternate views. Residual networks learned projection restoration; the source describes tenfold cross-validation on the cohort. Reconstructed clinical perfusion measures, including total perfusion deficit, were compared with full acquisitions using commercial quantitative software and agreement analyses. Learned reconstructions reduced measured bias relative to uncorrected reduced data.
evidence.unknown: Reduced acquisitions were derived from the same full scans, rather than separate real-world short scans. Full-acquisition reconstruction is a measurement reference, not independent disease truth. Detailed fold-specific preprocessing/tuning isolation is not established. Gated functional performance, diagnostic decisions, patient outcomes and actual lower-dose acquisition were not tested. Some headline image-metric labels and dispersion values are inconsistent, so they are not adopted as precise comparative claims.
evidence.ai_role: The learned residual networks restored projection information before reconstruction, enabling the represented within-cohort test of clinical perfusion-measurement agreement under reduced data.

source_review.scope: Read authenticated primary institution-deposited PDF front DOI/title, original clinical acquisition and reduced-data derivation, ResNet/training/cross-validation and quantitative clinical evaluation Methods, perfusion Results and limits. Exact publisher online April 28, 2020 distinguished from December 2021 issue. Supplements were not read. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Histology and clinical features classify recorded HER2-positive recurrence in a separate cohort
summary: A ResNet50-based model combined histology features with clinical data to classify recorded recurrence or metastasis in HER2-positive breast cancer. Developed in 127 patients, it achieved a reported AUC of 0.72 in 123 TCGA patients. The result is retrospective clinical validation, without a time-calibrated recurrence forecast or demonstrated treatment benefit.
ai_technology: ResNet50; multimodal compact bilinear fusion
organization: Chifeng Municipal Hospital; Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences; Genies (Beijing) Co., Ltd.

evidence.tested: ResNet50 patch features were fused with clinical variables; patch scores were averaged per slide. Separate TCGA data supplied the represented AUC.
evidence.unknown: Internal two-fold splitting is described in terms of patches/samples without established patient separation. Follow-up horizons and censoring are not adequately specified for a time-calibrated prognosis. Histology heterogeneity and different cohort characteristics limit reproducibility. No prospective validation, avoided treatment or improved clinical outcomes were measured.
evidence.ai_role: Learned image features and multimodal fusion enable the source-specific classification of recorded recurrence outcomes.

source_review.scope: Primary front, clinical labels/cohort, computational imaging/fusion/classification Methods, recurrence Results and limitations

title: Learned breast-cancer feature selection nominates survival-associated transcripts
summary: Random-forest recursive feature elimination and XGBoost analysis of breast-cancer expression data nominated genes subsequently associated with distant-metastasis-free survival in a basal breast-cancer subgroup. Higher POU2AF1 and S100B expression was associated with longer survival in the reported analysis. These are exploratory expression–outcome associations, not causal mechanisms or a clinically validated prognostic test.
ai_technology: Random-forest recursive feature elimination; XGBoost
organization: International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology; Regional Centre for Biotechnology

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and scoped computational/clinical model Methods and corresponding Results; no operational laboratory protocols evaluated

evidence.tested: The source pooled 1,150 expression samples, including 623 triple-negative cases, to learn subtype-discriminating gene sets. Genes passing further differential-expression filtering were examined with KM Plotter and Cox analysis for distant-metastasis-free survival.
evidence.unknown: External subtype classification helped choose the final gene sets and is not an untouched evaluation of survival prognosis. Survival analysis used a St Gallen basal-subtype definition; exact survival sample counts, cutoff selection, overlap with discovery samples and multiplicity control are not fully resolved in the inspected main text. Whole-data batch adjustment and unclear feature-selection nesting can inflate classification performance, so those metrics are not the represented finding. CT83 p=.052 is not treated as significant. No perturbation or clinical-treatment effect is established.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted random-forest feature elimination and boosted-tree classification narrow the candidate transcript sets before the scoped posthoc clinical-outcome association analysis.

title: Learned stromal expression score associates with colon-cancer outcomes
summary: A 31-gene score selected using elastic-net and penalized survival learning was associated with worse relapse-free and overall survival in retrospective colon-cancer data. A higher score also showed adverse-outcome associations in a separate TCGA cohort. The result is a clinical expression–outcome association, not proof of chemotherapy resistance or a treatment-selection benefit.
ai_technology: Elastic-net learning; LASSO-Cox feature selection
organization: Southern Medical University; Sun Yat-sen University

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and selected computational/clinical Methods and corresponding high-level Results; operational laboratory protocols excluded from review

evidence.tested: The score was developed using five GEO datasets totalling 990 cases and examined in 382 TCGA-COAD cases. Outcome-informed resampling and expression cutoffs selected genes; the final score subtracts the mean expression of negatively signed selected genes from the positive group. The source reports adjusted survival associations.
evidence.unknown: Prognostic outcomes inform development, selection and cutoffs; derivation-cohort associations are not independent validation. Treatment comparisons are observational and do not identify causal benefit or intrinsic resistance. Computational drug-response and pathway predictions are not measured clinical response. Supplemental implementation and treatment-confounding details were not inspected; separate experimental mechanisms are not represented.
evidence.ai_role: Elastic-net models learn stromal-group discriminators, and repeated penalized Cox fits select the expression features that constitute the measured-outcome-associated score.

title: Consensus-learned lung-cancer groups associate with survival
summary: An ensemble of seven multi-omics clustering methods identified three lung-adenocarcinoma groups. The LIMOC2 group had shorter observed overall survival, with a similar ordering reported after template-based assignment in two additional archived cohorts. This is an exploratory model-defined clinical association, not proof of a biological taxonomy or vaccine/drug response.
ai_technology: LIMOC; consensus multi-omics clustering including CIMLR and MoCluster
organization: Fujian University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

source_review.scope: Exact primary identity and scoped safe computational/clinical Methods and high-level Results; evidence access distinguished in case ledger; no operational laboratory procedures evaluated

evidence.tested: Primary indexed Methods 2.2 describe seven fitted clustering algorithms, a co-assignment consensus matrix and hierarchical consensus grouping. The top subtype-associated expression features supplied nearest-template assignments in a meta-cohort and GSE72094. Results3.1 report the survival ordering.
evidence.unknown: The subtype labels and selected features depend on preprocessing, immune-feature selection and consensus choices. Exact cohort-level numerical effect sizes and supplemental overlap checks were not inspected, so no independent causal or forecasting claim is made. Antigen immunogenicity, vaccine suitability and predicted compound response are not measured treatment effects and are outside the represented result. Primary PubMed records April24; the migrated SPJ publisher page says April30. The earlier documented article date is used with this conflict retained, not as an absolute-priority claim.
evidence.ai_role: Data-fitted multi-omics partitions generate the patient groups whose clinical survival distributions are compared; dimensionality-reduction graphics alone are not the enabling evidence.

title: Regularized glioma expression score associates with survival across archived cohorts
summary: A stepwise-Cox plus ridge model constructed from a supplied glioma expression signature was associated with survival across nine archived cohorts. The final model was selected using average validation-cohort performance, so those cohorts do not provide an untouched external test. The narrow result is a retrospective score–outcome association, not a verified treatment target or clinical-benefit claim.
ai_technology: Mime; stepwise Cox selection; ridge-regularized survival learning
organization: Central South University

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and selected computational/clinical Methods and corresponding high-level Results; operational laboratory protocols excluded from review

evidence.tested: Mime compared 117 combinations across one development and eight additional glioma cohorts. The selected STRICOM score separated survival outcomes using cohort median scores, and adjusted analyses considered established clinical/molecular covariates.
evidence.unknown: All additional cohorts informed final model selection and model-ranking comparisons; performance can be optimistic. Risk cutoffs are cohort-specific. Input signatures and clinical cohorts are reused, not new randomized or prospective evidence. The SDC1 example includes previously reported biology and is not represented as a newly discovered causal mechanism. Operational perturbation procedures and supplementary experimental details were not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A fitted ridge survival model following feature selection supplies the patient score whose observed survival association is assessed; software availability and visualization alone are not the represented result.

title: Learned clinical and genetic features classify radiation pneumonitis in a small cohort
summary: Learned feature selection and classifiers evaluated radiation-pneumonitis outcomes in 59 lung-cancer patients. A four-variable set combining clinical, treatment-volume and genetic information yielded a reported XGBoost AUC of 0.815 in repeated internal evaluation. This is exploratory cohort validation, without an independently tested pretreatment risk tool or demonstrated treatment benefit.
ai_technology: LASSO; recursive feature elimination; XGBoost; random forest; support-vector machine
organization: Yonsei University; Hanyang University

evidence.tested: Prospectively collected 2017-2019 cohort data were analyzed using internal nested cross-validation and training-fold oversampling. The endpoint was grade2-or-higher radiation pneumonitis, occurring in about20% of59 patients.
evidence.unknown: Prospective collection does not establish a locked prospective predictor. Final features were aggregated across folds before another evaluation, so full selection-pipeline isolation is not established. Model/feature-set choice reused the same small cohort; no external or cross-ethnicity validation, causal genetic mechanism or clinical benefit was demonstrated. Supplementary details and operational laboratory procedures were not independently reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Learned regularized feature selection and classifiers link measured clinical/genetic inputs to recorded pneumonitis outcomes, supporting the bounded retrospective evaluation.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front, clinical cohort/endpoint, computational feature-selection/classifier Methods, Results and limitations; operational genotyping procedures not inspected

title: Penalized learning identifies a cardiomyopathy-associated cytokine pattern
summary: A LASSO-selected four-cytokine combination distinguished chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy from rheumatic heart disease in a small cross-sectional clinical study. The represented finding is a cohort-specific multivariable immune-profile association, not a verified causal inflammatory pathway or a deployable diagnostic test.
ai_technology: LASSO-regularized logistic learning
organization: Federal University of Minas Gerais; Federal University of Paraná

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and selected computational/clinical Methods and corresponding high-level Results; operational laboratory protocols excluded from review

evidence.tested: The study included 38 chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy cases, 17 rheumatic heart disease cases and 12 healthy controls. An 80:20 random split was described for LASSO logistic classification; the selected panel comprised IL-12p70, IL-7, IL-1Ra and IL-4.
evidence.unknown: A claimed 100% separation comes from a very small selected sample; the main result does not establish precision, external generalization or a robust future-patient operating threshold. Disease groups have different sex distributions, and controls were much younger. Parameter-selection nesting and test counts are incompletely specified. Conventional pairwise cytokine differences, generic networks and t-SNE visualization are separate from the enabling penalized model. No pathogen experimentation or therapeutic intervention is represented.
evidence.ai_role: Regularized fitted classification selects a joint cytokine pattern from measured clinical variables; the scoped finding concerns its observed disease-group association.

title: Consensus learning nominates a pulmonary-hypertension miRNA pattern
summary: Four fitted feature-selection approaches consistently selected miR-636 and miR-187-5p in a pulmonary arterial hypertension study. The clinical miRNA models showed moderate discrimination in a small held-out subset. These are exploratory diagnostic-reference and feature-association findings, not established clinical utility or causal pulmonary mechanisms.
ai_technology: Boruta random forest; LASSO; regression partition trees; XGBoost
organization: University of Sheffield; Imperial College London

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and selected computational/clinical Methods and corresponding high-level Results; operational laboratory protocols excluded from review

evidence.tested: The miRNA cohort comprised 64 PAH cases and 43 combined healthy/systemic-sclerosis-without-PH controls. Models were developed using 72 people and assessed on 35; repeated cross-validation supported feature selection and tuning. Both nominated miRNAs recurred across the four approaches and alternative selection analyses.
evidence.unknown: Model and feature comparisons used the same small validation sample. The Results claim 30/35 correct for Boruta, while the table reports a different classification rate; no single accuracy is promoted here. Whole-data filtering and multiple selection analyses require caution. Whole-blood gene-target classification involved refitting on different features and is not external validation of the original miRNA classifier. A five-year follow-up does not make the already-collected diagnostic evaluation prospective. No pathway causality or laboratory mechanism is adopted.
evidence.ai_role: Learned forests, boosted trees and regularized/partition models select diagnostic features and produce patient-level predictions; agreement of selected features and held-out reference discrimination supply the scoped finding.

title: Multi-omics learning distinguishes endocrine hypertension subtypes retrospectively
summary: A random-forest model using 57 selected multi-omics features distinguished four hypertension subtypes in an internal held-out test, with approximately 92% balanced accuracy and AUC .95. The best single-omics comparator had approximately 81% balanced accuracy. The study supports a sample-specific diagnostic-reference validation, without establishing prospective screening benefit or biological mechanisms.
ai_technology: Random forest; Boruta feature selection; multi-omics classification
organization: University of Dundee; University of Glasgow; Technische Universität Dresden

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and scoped computational/clinical model Methods and corresponding Results; no operational laboratory protocols evaluated

evidence.tested: The main-table complete-data cohort comprises 307 hypertensive participants (100 primary aldosteronism, 69 pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma, 30 Cushing syndrome and 108 primary hypertension); 101 normotensive volunteers were excluded from model fitting/testing. Data were initially split 80:20, with 100 repeated development splits and a final test set.
evidence.unknown: The abstract disease counts differ from the post-quality-control table; the represented cohort uses the latter rather than mixing denominators. Feature frequency cutoffs and outlier/class-balancing choices were developed empirically; their complete nesting requires supplemental detail not inspected here. This is an internal random holdout from expert referral centres, with small minority classes and no untouched external or prospective clinical evaluation. Comparing the best selected mono-omics and multi-omics models is study-specific, not a general guarantee of diagnostic improvement.
evidence.ai_role: Learned forests combine selected measurements to classify established clinical subtypes; the scoped result is the observed held-out diagnostic-reference performance rather than PCA visualization or conventional correlations.

title: Learned macrophage expression signature associates with transplant outcomes
summary: A data-derived Boolean expression signature was associated with kidney-graft loss in two archived recipient cohorts totalling 517 people. The signature summarizes a model-defined reactive–tolerant axis. This retrospective association does not establish a causal macrophage mechanism, a universal cell-state taxonomy or a clinical treatment benefit.
ai_technology: SMaRT; Boolean Network Explorer; adaptive threshold fitting and unsupervised implication-rule discovery
organization: University of California San Diego

source_review.scope: Exact primary front, safe computational threshold/rule-learning Methods and high-level clinical outcome Results; no operational biological interventions evaluated

evidence.tested: The model was built from 197 archived macrophage-expression samples. StepMiner fitted data thresholds, BooleanNet inferred implication relationships, and BoNE formed equivalence groups and selected paths; known activation labels oriented the axis. The source reports a reactive signature associated with graft loss across two kidney-transplant cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Cluster/path selection and activation labels shape the signature; it is not a universally established biological state definition. The kidney-graft association is consistent with earlier inflammatory-macrophage findings, so novelty is limited to this derived signature/application. Primary Figure4 describes testing the StepMiner threshold and threshold plus or minus its noise margin, introducing adaptive cutoff selection and multiplicity concerns. Cohort overlap and adjusted effect sizes were not independently resolved from supplemental data. No reported genetic/pharmacological intervention, causal reprogramming or prospective clinical utility is adopted.
evidence.ai_role: Data-fitted thresholds and unsupervised symbolic implication/cluster discovery derive the expression signature subsequently compared with observed clinical outcomes; the graph drawing itself is not the enabling operation.

title: Learned birth-expression signature associates with later neonatal sepsis
summary: Retrospective LASSO analysis of blood collected while newborns appeared healthy identified a four-gene signature associated with early-onset sepsis during the following week. A small external diagnostic check gave AUC .72, but those external samples were collected after illness onset. This does not independently validate pre-symptom screening or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: LASSO; sparse partial least-squares discriminant analysis
organization: Simon Fraser University; University of British Columbia; London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine

source_review.scope: Exact primary identity and scoped safe computational/clinical Methods and high-level Results; evidence access distinguished in case ledger; no operational laboratory procedures evaluated

evidence.tested: The prospective source cohort enrolled 720 newborns; day-of-birth expression comparisons included 14 later early-onset cases, six late-onset cases, 12 localized-infection cases and 32 healthy controls. Repeated development splits selected features; the final four-gene model used all available birth samples. The separate GSE26440 check comprised six early-onset cases and six controls.
evidence.unknown: Prospective sample collection does not establish that the fitted model was frozen before outcomes. The headline development AUC .94 is not a held-out future-patient estimate; Monte Carlo testing and final whole-cohort fitting are distinct analyses. External post-onset samples do not test prediction before clinical symptoms. Tiny case counts, clinical sepsis definitions and selected controls limit generalization. No prevention or causal immune-development mechanism is represented.
evidence.ai_role: Penalized model fitting selects and combines expression features linked to subsequent clinical status; the learned signature, not conventional differential expression alone, supplies the scoped finding.

title: Learned brain-imaging measurements agree with expert references across separate cohorts
summary: A CNN and YOLO-based pipeline automated region selection for a brain diffusion-imaging index. In a separate 1000-person UK Biobank test, agreement with the average of two neurologists’ measurements gave an intraclass correlation of 0.90; smaller OASIS3 and EPAD tests gave 0.80 and 0.78. These validate measurement agreement, not direct brain waste clearance or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: VGG-style convolutional network; YOLOv5s; dALPS
organization: Sun Yat-sen University

evidence.tested: Development used 1000 subjects from four other cohorts, with subject-level training/validation splits. The finalized pipeline was tested against averaged expert measurements in 1000 UKB subjects and 200 each from OASIS3 and EPAD.
evidence.unknown: Manual measurements are an imperfect expert reference, not a physiological gold standard. Cohort/scanner distributions differed. Abstract and discussion quote ICC 0.95, while specific independent-test Results give0.90/0.80/0.78; this entry follows those explicit test results. No causal genetic, medication or disease mechanism, treatment guidance or outcome benefit is represented. Supplementary methods were not independently inspected. The linked corrigendum adds OASIS acknowledgments without a stated scientific result change. External archived cohorts do not establish prospective new-data testing or separate-team replication.
evidence.ai_role: CNN slice selection and learned object detection automate the original index region placement; the index formula itself is preserved. Their outputs enable the cross-cohort reference-agreement evaluation.

source_review.scope: Primary institution-deposited article front, computational imaging development, independent expert-reference testing Methods/Results and measurement caveats; primary linked correction body

title: Learned RNA outlier analysis supports rare-disease diagnosis
summary: Denoising-autoencoder outlier analysis supported transcriptomic interpretation in 22 of 102 previously genetically undiagnosed patients, including 12 source-reported diagnoses. The remaining interpretations included support for known findings and proposed mechanisms. This is a clinical diagnostic-workflow yield, not 22 independently validated new diseases or a prospective comparison with standard care.
ai_technology: DROP; OUTRIDER; FRASER2.0; denoising autoencoders
organization: The University of Hong Kong; Hong Kong Children’s Hospital

source_review.scope: Exact primary identity and scoped safe computational/clinical Methods and high-level Results; evidence access distinguished in case ledger; no operational laboratory procedures evaluated

evidence.tested: The 2021–2024 clinical cohort came from two Hong Kong hospitals after routine genetic testing. Primary indexed computational Methods specify DROP1.3.3, expression/splicing outlier modules with autoencoder confounder modeling, multiple-testing correction and manual clinical review. Ten interpretations were hypothesis-driven and twelve hypothesis-free.
evidence.unknown: The authors combine model-derived outlier evidence with prior variants, phenotype and manual review; the whole diagnostic yield is not attributable to an autonomous model. This selected unsolved cohort has no randomized comparator or independent population sensitivity estimate. The six proposed mechanisms are not treated as established clinical diagnoses. Laboratory and variant-specific procedural material was not reviewed, and no operational genetic instructions are represented.
evidence.ai_role: Autoencoders learn expected expression/splicing structure and flag patient deviations, supplying otherwise unavailable functional evidence for the scoped clinical interpretation process.

title: Agent-designed detector uses fewer measured baseband cycles at unresolved error-rate difference
summary: A Claude coding agent designed a platform-specific signal detector and tested its implementation on commercial baseband silicon. It used34010 cycles per frame versus39520 for the ported reference, a13.9% reduction. The error-rate evaluation could not resolve a difference between them; this is a bounded hardware-specific algorithm result, not an over-the-air network benefit.
ai_technology: Claude Fable5; agent-assisted algorithm design
organization: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence; NXP Semiconductors; RPTU University Kaiserslautern-Landau

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, actual structural/model Methods, specific result evaluation and source caveats

evidence.tested: The new ec_frozen detector reuses a frozen inverse as a preconditioner, with measured platform profiles guiding agent structural choices. Cycle counts were reproduced exactly on silicon.
evidence.unknown: One campaign and reduced workload dimensions limit transfer to the original large detector. Error intervals overlap and stored outcomes do not permit a fully paired comparison. No real radio-channel, power or network-level improvement was measured. Human constraints and frozen evaluators shaped the design; generic porting/coding speedups are not the represented discovery.
evidence.ai_role: The agent selected the new detector structure from measured hardware costs, rather than only implementing a fully specified human algorithm.

title: Data-guided equation search finds a flexible empirical car-following model
summary: Agent-guided and evolutionary symbolic search identified AERM, an empirical equation combining relative-speed response with spacing-dependent restoration. On three driving datasets, its equation fitted complete trajectories more closely than seven classical models when each trajectory was independently calibrated. The result concerns fitted reconstruction, not forecasting unseen drivers or a universal behavioral law.
ai_technology: Agent-guided symbolic regression; evolutionary equation learning
organization: Tongji University

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, actual structural/model Methods, specific result evaluation and source caveats

evidence.tested: Equation structure was selected using US-101, highD and exiD; Shanghai, I-80 and Waymo supplied additional reconstruction comparisons with recalibrated coefficients.
evidence.unknown: Per-trajectory calibration fits the same complete trajectory subsequently reconstructed. Common-parameter results were mixed and Gipps was better on Waymo. The selected0.1-second delay is not established human reaction time; analytical stability assumes zero delay. The reasoning agent base model is not identified in the inspected primary Methods. No predictive transfer, traffic intervention or causal driver mechanism was established.
evidence.ai_role: Data-fitted evolutionary symbolic search and evidence-guided structural proposals generated the equation form; this is not merely parameter fitting of a pre-specified classical model.

title: Physics-guided learning reaches a measured radio-link threshold with fewer samples
summary: A shallow physics-guided network fitted a radio-link model from received-signal-strength measurements for a fixed reconfigurable surface. In the tested setup it reached53dB with400 measurements, versus1600 for the compared CSM method. This is a setup-specific recorded-measurement validation, not a general mobile-network or energy-efficiency benefit.
ai_technology: Parametric physics-guided neural blind beamforming; P-PGNBB
organization: University of Warwick

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, actual learned model Methods, clinical/physical-reference evaluation and limitations

evidence.tested: A14-parameter model learned from measured surface configurations and signal strengths. A256-element surface and fixed transmitter/receiver geometry supplied the field dataset.
evidence.unknown: The comparison concerns one fixed setup and subsets of a recorded acquisition. Test prediction error was about4.38dB; noise, model mismatch and temporal variation were not separately isolated. More flexible PGNN had lower prediction error at larger budgets. Classical phase-coherence observations and perfect-CSI simulation bounds are separate from the learned result.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted physics-guided network estimates a configuration-to-signal mapping used to select surface settings, enabling the measured sample-budget comparison.

title: Manifold learning tests electrolyte categories against paired clinical measurements
summary: A neural ECG model classified potassium, calcium and magnesium categories using paired laboratory measurements in MIMIC-IV. In the study cohort of8599 patients, potassium macro-F1 was0.61, calcium0.50 and magnesium0.40. This is retrospective clinical-reference evaluation, not a validated replacement for laboratory testing.
