organization: Harvard University; Duke Kunshan University; Duke University

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, actual learned model Methods, clinical/physical-reference evaluation and limitations

evidence.tested: The study paired18037 ECG recordings with nearby serum measurements and used patient-level time-based partitions. A learned source network and ECG encoder were jointly fitted with a graph residual objective.
evidence.unknown: One-center archived data, imbalanced categories and up-to-one-hour pairing differences limit transportability. Medication/demographic metadata contribute to prediction, especially for calcium/magnesium; the result is not ECG-only inference. Preprocessing can truncate late waveform content. No prospective independent clinical validation, diagnostic deployment or patient benefit was established.
evidence.ai_role: Learned waveform features, task-aware graph-source inference and metadata fusion enable the source-specific laboratory-referenced category classification.

title: Learned quantum-battery controls link high stored energy with suppressed participation
summary: Soft actor-critic learning selected time-dependent couplings in a simulated anisotropic Dicke quantum battery with Kerr nonlinearity and photon loss. Compared with fixed couplings, the learned controls sustained higher stored energy alongside a persistently lower participation ratio. This is a conditional computed dynamical relationship, not a measured battery or proof of a general charging advantage.
ai_technology: Soft actor-critic reinforcement learning
organization: Northwest Normal University

source_review.scope: Primary v1 front, physical model, RL ResultsIII.3, conclusions and computational convergence context

evidence.tested: The learned policy changes rotating and counter-rotating couplings in the specified dissipative model. Participation-ratio trajectories were compared with a fixed-coupling reference across three Kerr strengths.
evidence.unknown: The result depends on the Hamiltonian, initial state, dissipative model and numerical truncation. Optimized variable controls have a broader control space than the fixed-coupling baseline. The participation ratio is a dynamical diagnostic, not an independently established universal mechanism. Separate analytically computed phase-transition results are not credited to AI; no physical device or energy-efficiency benefit was measured.
evidence.ai_role: A learned policy generates the time-dependent controls whose simulated energy and participation-ratio trajectories support the scoped dynamical finding.

title: Learned process groups expose different time profiles in traffic-fine records
summary: NMF-based process grouping in150370 traffic-fine records produced groups concentrated in different periods despite calendar dates being excluded from their encodings. Three groups had88-94% of traces ending in2000-2004, while two others had86-97% ending in2009-2013. These exploratory temporal associations do not identify the causes of process change.
ai_technology: TracePrism; non-negative matrix factorization; k-means
organization: Fraunhofer IAIS; City St George’s, University of London; University of Seville; Eindhoven University of Technology; University of St. Gallen

source_review.scope: Primary v1 front and safe computational/model Methods, specific application Results and statistical limitations

evidence.tested: An analyst iteratively fitted NMF topics and formed process groups, with k-means used on topic weights in a later round. Posthoc end-date distributions compared accepted group memberships.
evidence.unknown: Group thresholds, encoding choices and commit order were analyst-selected on the same log. No reseed stability study or dedicated drift analysis separated behavior from calendar policy changes; late open cases can reflect right-censoring. The result is a data-specific association, not evidence of an administrative cause or improved process performance.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted topic representations and learned partitions supply behavior-based groups whose subsequently examined date distributions reveal the temporal contrast. UMAP is a visual aid rather than the enabling operation.

title: Learned forecasts distinguish directional search and COVID-data relationships
summary: Matched LightGBM forecasts of eight Google-search and COVID-related series found that opposite directions could differ in both prediction error and error-distribution behavior. For US loss-of-smell searches and reported cases, adding search history gave a 9.9% equivalent mean RMSE reduction, while the reverse direction changed error-distribution descriptors without improving mean accuracy. These are model-dependent observational patterns, not causal effects or a validated real-time warning system.
ai_technology: LightGBM gradient-boosted regression trees
organization: Petrozavodsk State University; University of Manouba

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, computational Methods, application Results and limitations; no independent reproduction

evidence.tested: Each 400-day window used 14-day histories, one- to fourteen-day horizons and chronological 223-origin training/150-origin evaluation. Target-only and source-augmented branches shared settings. Results Tables 6 and 9 separate mean log-RMSE and forecast-error distribution entropy (FEDE).
evidence.unknown: Adjacent windows share 399 days and are not independent replications. Window/history settings were chosen sequentially for distributional stability. Relative Google Trends sampling, query wording, common media/seasonal/reporting effects and the fixed model class limit interpretation. No temporally constrained surrogate-source null test was included. Similar broad lead-lag findings were known; the represented refinement is the matched metric-dependent directional contrast, not the discovery that searches can precede cases.
evidence.ai_role: Learned tree ensembles generate matched conditional forecasts whose held-out errors reveal the source- and direction-specific contrast; FEDE itself is a statistical descriptor, not a separate learned model.

title: Learned tutoring policies show different classroom learning and override patterns
summary: In a probability-tutor classroom study, an apprenticeship-learned policy overrode student choices less often than a conservative-Q-learning policy (28.2% versus 66.7% of recorded decisions). Among non-ceiling students, the apprenticeship group had a higher mean standard posttest score (.908 versus .842), with a marginal planned one-sided pretest-adjusted contrast. Small samples, repeated decisions and an augmented historical control limit broader superiority claims.
ai_technology: StuEDM; energy-based distribution matching; conservative Q-learning
organization: North Carolina State University

source_review.scope: Original v1 dissertation front, authorship/version distinctions and Chapter 7 learned-policy Methods, classroom design, Results and limitations

evidence.tested: StuEDM was trained on 244 earlier student trajectories; StuCQL used 2,716. The Spring 2026 live study had 104 completers. Removing perfect-pretest students left 26 StuEDM and 27 StuCQL students; the random-mode Expert comparator was augmented with 11 prior-semester students. Table 7.1 reports a planned one-sided adjusted contrast p=.048 for StuEDM versus StuCQL; the three-group omnibus test was not significant.
evidence.unknown: The Expert arm is partly historical, and non-significant baseline tests do not prove population equivalence. Other direct learning comparisons against StuCQL were not significant. Multiple directional outcomes, ceiling exclusions, a single course and small samples limit inference. Override counts include repeated decisions within students; decision-level significance is not independent-person replication. Longer tutor time is measured engagement, not proof of benefit. Earlier dissertation chapters reproduce published methods, which are not represented as new here; October 20 is the located arXiv version date, not a claim of absolute first circulation.
evidence.ai_role: An energy-based neural policy learned from student demonstration occupancy selects presentation modes and overrides conflicting choices during new classroom use; measured learning and choice patterns are the represented field result. Formatting assistance by a separate language model is unrelated to this contribution.

title: Learned spatial expression mode associates with treatment response in a small cohort
summary: An unsupervised spatial-learning model fitted 20 expression modes in pretreatment samples from 21 cutaneous squamous-cell-cancer patients. A subsequently selected mode showed greater neighboring-cell contrast in responders than non-responders. This is an exploratory same-cohort spatial association, not an independently validated treatment-response predictor.
ai_technology: SAIL; unsupervised sparse spatial projection learning
organization: University of Warwick

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, computational objectiveIII-C, clinical applicationV-D and statistical limitations; no operational laboratory protocols

evidence.tested: Spatial modes were fitted without response labels from 28 pretreatment biopsies in 21 patients. Response comparisons subsequently selected the most discriminative of 20 modes.
evidence.unknown: Post-training mode selection uses the same 21 response labels. Nominal comparisons across 20 modes do not establish multiplicity-adjusted confirmation or held-out predictive accuracy. Prior work already linked spatial organization to response; this refinement does not establish a causal immune mechanism or treatment benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Learned sparse projections optimize spatial coherence rather than simply plotting coordinates. The resulting mode supplies the patient-level contrast examined against recorded response.

title: Learned bubble reconstruction shows focus-dependent distribution agreement
summary: A convolutional multitask model trained on simulated optical images was applied without experimental fine-tuning to bubble shadowgraphs at four radial planes. Reconstructed size distributions overlapped in-focus experimental references by approximately 68–92%, with poorer agreement farther from the focal reference. This is a configuration-specific population measurement validation; experimental three-dimensional coordinates were not independently known for each bubble.
ai_technology: Focus-conditioned convolutional multitask neural network
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, computational Methods, application Results and limitations; no independent reproduction

evidence.tested: The model jointly predicts depth relative to the known focal plane and physical-equivalent diameter. Experimental populations contained 142, 971, 859 and 204 reconstructed bubbles; distributions were compared with plane-specific in-focus references. A separate 11,679-bubble center-plane reference comparison is reported.
evidence.unknown: The 97.6% normalized depth accuracy belongs to synthetic data, not experimental depth truth. Model training describes a randomized crop development split alongside a timestamp-separated test; these partitions should not be conflated. Experimental references are distribution-level and share the imaging facility. Center-reference comparisons use differing summaries (approximately 92% versus 86% overlap); no single pooled value is inferred. Optical configuration, segmentation, overlap and defocus limit transfer; no general three-dimensional accuracy or improved flow process was established.
evidence.ai_role: A learned convolutional appearance representation, conditioned on focal-plane position, jointly infers size and depth from optical signatures and enables the scoped distribution-level reference comparison.

title: Simulation-trained network locates a physical magnetic resonator
summary: A convolutional-transformer regressor trained on simulated signals with measured noise located a physical magneto-mechanical resonator on a robot-positioned grid. Across repeated static recordings, median position error was 7.26 millimeters and the 95th percentile was 23.7 millimeters. This validates a specific laboratory readout under fixed-orientation conditions, without demonstrating clinical tracking.
ai_technology: Convolutional-transformer regressor
organization: Hamburg University of Technology; University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf; Fraunhofer IMTE

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, signal/data/model Methods, robot-reference experiment, evaluation Results and limitations

evidence.tested: A model trained on 100000 simulated signals was tested on physical recordings at75 grid positions,25 frames each, against robot positions.
evidence.unknown: One resonator and fixed orientation, repeated static frames and one coil system limit generalization. Frame-level bootstrap uncertainty is not independent hardware replication. Errors were greater near the coil surface; normalized inputs can lose information there. No moving-device clinical test, outcome benefit or general parameter-estimation claim was established.
evidence.ai_role: The learned inverse mapping estimates three-dimensional position directly from measured multichannel time signals, enabling the reported robot-reference localization evaluation.

title: Learned decoding validates a photonic receiver on a recorded transition trace
summary: Six learned decoders were fine-tuned on 1,502 recorded transitions from a phase-aware photonic receiver. Their voting ensemble classified 98.31% of 1,363 transitions in the immediately subsequent held-out trace. This is a specific retrospective physical-readout validation under the tested drift conditions, without a matched superiority comparison against the separate analytical decoder.
ai_technology: XGBoost; LightGBM; CatBoost; random forest; Extra-Trees; neural network
organization: Technical University of Munich

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, physical readout context, learned decoding Section6 and Tables1–2, conclusion; later-version context separately checked

evidence.tested: Physics-based synthetic pretraining followed by recorded-trace fine-tuning and an immediately subsequent experimental test trace. Learned features comprise normalized output-power differences and the preceding decoded state.
evidence.unknown: Back-to-back traces may share drift and hardware conditions. Sequential inference requires a previous-state reference and limited drift. No independently acquired locked-model deployment, energy, latency, network benefit or unrestricted phase-noise robustness was established. The receiver design and separate 96.19% analytical result are not credited to AI.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers map measured receiver power changes plus the preceding state to the next codeword, enabling the reported held-out physical readout evaluation.

title: Learned postoperative records distinguish readmission in a colorectal-surgery cohort
summary: A bidirectional LSTM classifier was evaluated for readmission using records from 4,336 colorectal-surgery patients. The source reports internal discrimination with an 80:20 training/test split, using perioperative and postoperative information. The result is a retrospective clinical model evaluation, without established preoperative prediction, external validation or demonstrated benefit from changing surgical care.
ai_technology: Bidirectional LSTM classifier applied to reshaped clinical patient records
organization: University of Portsmouth; Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust

evidence.tested: A prospectively maintained surgical database covered 4,336 operations during 2003–2019, including 321 readmissions. The paper compared multiple classifiers and describes an 80:20 split for readmission analysis. Its three-hidden-layer bidirectional LSTM reportedly achieved sensitivity 84.1% and specificity 90.9%. Predictor candidates included clinical, operative and postoperative variables; a reduced set retained length of stay and operative details.
evidence.unknown: Prospective database maintenance does not make model evaluation prospective. Feature selection and preprocessing isolation from testing are incompletely specified, and no external or temporal test was reported. Inclusion of postoperative variables prevents a preoperative risk claim; the permissible prediction time and all-variable leakage risks are not fully established. The reported 87.5% accuracy equals the mean of reported sensitivity and specificity, so it is not adopted as an authenticated population-weighted accuracy. Reshaping records for LSTM does not establish genuine longitudinal sequence learning. No causal effect of surgical approach or improvement in care was tested.
evidence.ai_role: The learned classifier combined clinical-record features to discriminate observed readmission labels, supplying the represented retrospective outcome-evaluation result. Conventional descriptive associations with surgical approaches are not attributed to AI discovery.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary clinical data provenance, preprocessing, feature selection, BI-LSTM architecture and split Methods, readmission Results and prediction-time limits. Source model code was not executed. Other length-of-stay/mortality models are not separately admitted or treated as causal clinical findings. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned mutation score associates with survival in checkpoint-treated gastroesophageal cancer
summary: An XGBoost mutation score separated observed survival groups in public cohorts of checkpoint-treated gastroesophageal cancer. The source used 123 patients for initial fitting and two additional cohort groups of 42 and 66 for model comparison. Because those comparison cohorts helped select the final model, the result is an exploratory prognostic association rather than untouched external validation or evidence of treatment benefit.
ai_technology: XGBoost mutation-feature selection and boosted survival-risk modeling
organization: Soochow University; Xuzhou Medical University; Nantong University; Nanjing Medical University

evidence.tested: The paper defined overall survival in checkpoint-treated gastroesophageal cancer as the endpoint. A 123-person MSK cohort supplied initial prognostic-gene filtering. It compared 297 algorithm combinations using cohort groups of 42 and 66 and selected the highest mean test-cohort concordance. The selected XGBoost procedure retained twelve mutation features, with a training-derived median score threshold separating survival groups across the represented cohorts.
evidence.unknown: The purported validation cohorts were used for final model selection and therefore do not establish an untouched external test. Participant overlap between public source cohorts was not independently reconstructed. Small cohort groups, extensive model searching and differing sequencing panels increase optimism and transportability concerns. Survival among treated patients does not identify benefit relative to no treatment or distinguish predictive treatment-response effects from general prognosis. Drug-sensitivity predictions and cell-line experiments are outside this admitted case, and no therapeutic efficacy is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: The learned feature-selection and boosted model combined tumor mutation profiles into the represented survival-associated score; immune enrichment analyses alone are not the admission basis.

source_review.scope: Read original clinical cohort/overall-survival and computational model-selection Methods, XGBoost signature and survival Results. Experimental drug work is not an admission basis or independently adjudicated. Validation-cohort model selection and treatment-benefit distinction explicitly retained. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned eleven-gene melanoma score associates with survival in public expression cohorts
summary: A penalized survival-model pipeline produced an eleven-gene melanoma score associated with observed survival in public expression cohorts. Model selection used both internal testing and an additional cohort, so the latter is not an untouched external test. The represented result is a retrospective prognostic association, without establishing novel cell types, causal tumor biology or improved treatment decisions.
ai_technology: Scissor phenotype-linked feature selection followed by LASSO Cox and ridge survival modeling
organization: Zhejiang University; Harbin Genars Technology; GenVista Technology

evidence.tested: The source linked single-cell data to bulk survival data using Scissor, derived prognosis-related gene sets and compared seventy-two model combinations. It selected a LASSO Cox/ridge eleven-gene score using average performance across testing datasets. The paper reports a survival-group association in GSE65904, described as 215 samples, with modest time-dependent discrimination.
evidence.unknown: Outcome-informed upstream filtering and use of testing cohorts to choose the final model compromise independent validation. The paper reports 469 available TCGA records but a different final subgroup count in discussion, without a reconstructed participant flow here. Reported survival-time labels differ between text and figure captions, so exact time-specific AUCs are not adopted. Single-cell cluster labels, including the claimed MITF-positive T-cell population, were not independently authenticated as new biological cell types. Many individual genes already have melanoma associations. No causal mechanism, treatment benefit or clinical decision utility was demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Phenotype-linked selection and penalized learned survival modeling combined expression measurements into the represented score, enabling observed survival stratification beyond generic clustering or pathway enrichment.

source_review.scope: Read actual clinical dataset, Scissor/feature/clustering and penalized model-selection Methods, final eleven-gene score and survival Results. Novel cell-type identity and causal biology are not adjudicated or admitted. Cohort-accounting and time-label inconsistencies are retained explicitly; no untouched external test claimed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Boosted survival models evaluated in women after bladder-cancer surgery
summary: A gradient-boosting model was evaluated for postoperative survival in women after radical cystectomy, using 4,536 registry records and 67 patients from another hospital. The separate hospital cohort showed moderate discrimination with wide uncertainty. This is retrospective prognostic validation of established factors, without evidence that using the score improves treatment or that chemotherapy effects are causal.

organization: Pingxiang Second People’s Hospital; Nanchang University; Anxi County Hospital

evidence.tested: The primary Methods retained 4,536 eligible SEER records and split them 3,175:1,361 for training/internal testing. Overall survival was defined from surgery to all-cause death, with alive patients censored at last follow-up. External GBDT AUCs were reported as 0.839, 0.801 and 0.747 for one-, three- and five-year survival; external differences versus most alternative models were not statistically significant.
evidence.unknown: The external cohort is small, retrospective and selected for complete clinical data. Registry treatment timing, exact binary-model handling of censoring and supplementary implementation detail were not independently reconstructed. Model-comparison optimism and transportability remain concerns. Established clinical/pathological predictors are not new biological discoveries. SHAP attribution and observational chemotherapy associations do not establish causal treatment effects; calibration/decision curves are not evidence of actual clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: The trained boosting model combined clinical and pathological features into the represented postoperative survival estimates and their cross-cohort prognostic evaluation.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary patient selection, endpoint/censoring, training feature/model and evaluation Methods, internal/external Results and model-comparison limits. Supplemental implementation was not independently read. Original online December 27, 2025 distinguished from publisher issue metadata December 2026. title: Learned gene selection highlights IGSF9 in early-stage lung-tumor tissue comparisons
summary: Random-forest and LASSO selection prioritized expression markers from 45 paired early-stage lung adenocarcinoma and adjacent-tissue samples. These are retrospective molecular associations, without demonstrated early screening utility or proof that IGSF9 drives malignant transformation.

organization: China Three Gorges University; Yichang Central People’s Hospital

evidence.tested: The source used 45 paired early-stage tumor/adjacent specimens in GSE32863 for differential filtering and RF/LASSO selection, yielding nine candidate markers. Expression comparisons used further public series. In GSE63459, comprising 33 tumors and 32 adjacent controls, IGSF9 expression showed reported AUC 0.903 with 95% confidence interval 0.816–0.960. Survival associations were assessed separately in GSE31210 and TCGA expression cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Candidate prioritization incorporated the additional cohort results, so the final singled-out marker is not an untouched independently selected test. Surgical tissue contrasts do not establish noninvasive screening, diagnostic specificity against other lung diseases or clinical benefit. Paired tissues, platform differences and cohort composition may confound expression signals. Prior lung-cancer work already implicated IGSF9; no first causal-role claim is made. Pseudotime, inferred cell communication and copy-number patterns do not prove that IGSF9 causes malignant differentiation, immune escape or invasion; the source explicitly lacked functional validation.
evidence.ai_role: The learned RF/LASSO intersection reduced measured expression candidates for subsequent tissue-reference and outcome comparisons, enabling the represented marker prioritization. Generic pathway analysis or pseudotime alone is not treated as an enabling causal finding.

source_review.scope: Read actual public clinical cohort/normalization, RF/LASSO selection, additional-cohort ROC and survival Methods/Results and source limitations. Functional/mechanistic claims from computational trajectories are not admitted. Original online March 29, 2026 distinguished from December issue metadata. title: Learned five-gene score associates with survival in triple-negative breast-cancer cohorts
summary: A CoxBoost/elastic-net score built from five expression markers was associated with survival in public triple-negative breast-cancer cohorts of 121 and 107 patients. Model choice and risk thresholds used both cohorts, so the comparison does not establish an untouched external predictor. The result is a retrospective prognostic association, without validated treatment selection or proof that a cell-line finding validates the clinical model.

organization: Harbin Medical University Cancer Hospital

Small samples and outcome-informed filtering increase optimism. Modest GSE58812 concordance is not robust clinical utility, and inferred drug sensitivity is not patient treatment response. Source cell-line SEPT3 experiments were not independently adjudicated or counted as validation of the survival model. No causal pyrimidine-metabolism mechanism or improved patient outcome is established.

title: Learned tissue-feature panel distinguishes early-onset colorectal cancer in a small cohort
summary: Random-forest selection identified a ten-feature metabolic pattern separating early-onset colorectal tumors from later-onset tumors and adjacent tissue in a 45-specimen study. Repeated internal cross-validation suggested discrimination, but whole-cohort feature filtering, small groups and putative metabolite identities limit the result. organization: Zhejiang Cancer Hospital; Hangzhou Institute of Medicine; Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: The source measured fifteen early-onset tumors, fifteen later-onset tumors and fifteen adjacent-normal tissue specimens. A separate public transcriptomic dataset was used only for pathway-level comparison, not validation of the metabolic classifier.

Specimen-level versus patient-level separation of adjacent tissues was not reconstructed, and age, stage or other cohort differences may explain some signals. Metabolite annotations were mainly database matches without universal authentic-standard confirmation. No independent classifier validation or clinical screening utility was demonstrated. title: External dementia-risk evaluation shows cohort matching changes apparent performance
summary: A revised gradient-boosted dementia-risk model trained on ADNI was evaluated in 244 AddNeuroMed participants, including thirty later dementia diagnoses. Performance differed when evaluation was restricted to demographically matched participants, demonstrating how cohort selection changes apparent validation results. This is retrospective clinical model validation, without proven preventive benefit or prospective clinical deployment.

organization: Fraunhofer Institute for Algorithms and Scientific Computing; University of Bonn; Erasmus MC; University of Oxford; UCB Biosciences

evidence.tested: A feature-restricted GBM was retrained on ADNI to match available AddNeuroMed measurements, retaining thirty-two clinical, imaging and genetic features. It was then evaluated in 244 initially normal or mildly impaired AddNeuroMed participants, thirty of whom later received a dementia diagnosis. The reported external concordance index was approximately 0.81. Across one hundred propensity-score matchings, the average matched set contained 164 participants and twenty conversions, with concordance approximately 0.88.
evidence.unknown: External evaluation was retrospective; prospective cohort follow-up does not establish predictor locking before clinical outcomes were known. Only thirty external events and fewer at long horizons limit precision. Matching changes the selected population and can improve apparent performance without improving the model or eliminating all bias. The revised model differs from the earlier full-feature model. No clinical prevention, treatment selection, economic benefit or general-population diagnostic utility was demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: The trained GBM combined multimodal baseline features into time-dependent risk estimates; its concrete external clinical evaluation exposed the effect of cohort composition on reported performance. Propensity-score matching alone is not treated as the enabling AI contribution.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary cohort comparison/matching, revised GBM feature/training and external evaluation Methods, unmatched/matched dementia Results and limitations. Supplement implementation was not independently read. Specific clinical external evaluation is distinguished from the earlier model publication and generic six-year-prediction headlines. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Machine learning links a three-gene lung-cancer score to retrospective survival differences
summary: LASSO and random-forest selection identified a three-gene lung-adenocarcinoma score associated with observed survival in public cohorts. Comparison cohorts showed limited and inconsistent discrimination: TCGA five-year AUC was approximately 0.50, while another cohort reached approximately 0.68. This supports a bounded retrospective association, without established clinical utility or causal gene effects.
ai_technology: LASSO and random forests for prognostic gene selection; consensus clustering for RAS expression subtypes
organization: The Third People’s Hospital of Chengdu

evidence.tested: The source reports 624 GEO lung-adenocarcinoma profiles used for derivation. LASSO with ten-fold cross-validation and random-forest feature selection intersected at MAPK10, PLA2G12B and SHC3. The resulting score was compared with observed survival in TCGA and GSE13213. Reported one-, three- and five-year AUCs were 0.608, 0.535 and 0.496 in TCGA, and 0.620, 0.654 and 0.682 in GSE13213.
evidence.unknown: Outcome-optimized risk cutoffs limit interpretation of group survival differences as locked external prediction. Exact cohort eligibility accounting and supplementary implementation were not reconstructed. Weak TCGA discrimination limits clinical claims; decision-curve calculations do not demonstrate actual patient benefit. Transcriptomic associations and drug predictions do not establish causal mechanisms or treatment efficacy. Original online date is May 28, 2026; the assigned December issue is later.
evidence.ai_role: Learned LASSO and random-forest feature selection produced the three-gene signature whose relationship with measured patient survival was evaluated across cohorts. General clustering benchmarks and untested drug predictions are not the admitted finding.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary cohort acquisition, consensus clustering, gene selection, LASSO/random-forest and risk-score evaluation Methods, cohort survival/AUC Results and limitations. Supplementary code and individual-patient eligibility were not independently reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned three-gene score shows retrospective survival association in hepatitis-associated liver cancer
summary: CoxBoost combined with elastic-net regression formed a three-gene survival score for hepatitis-B-associated hepatocellular carcinoma. The paper reports survival separation in sixty TCGA and fifty-seven comparison-cohort samples. Both cohorts informed algorithm selection, limiting independent validation. The finding is a retrospective clinical association, without demonstrated treatment benefit or causal immune regulation.
ai_technology: CoxBoost and elastic-net regression for a three-gene survival-risk score
organization: Zhejiang Chinese Medical University

evidence.tested: The source selected sixty TCGA and fifty-seven HCCDB18 samples with clinical information. It compared 101 combinations of ten algorithms, using C-indices in both cohorts to choose CoxBoost plus elastic net with alpha 0.4. The learned score combined PARP1, KPNB1 and FARP2. Kaplan–Meier and time-dependent ROC analyses reported associations with observed overall survival in both cohorts.
evidence.unknown: The comparison cohort influenced model selection and is not an untouched external test. Small selected cohorts, incompletely reconstructed eligibility and outcome-informed comparisons limit generalization. Exact figure-level performance values were not independently transcribed. This record does not adopt predicted drug synergy, therapeutic reversal, causal immune effects or experimental biological claims.
evidence.ai_role: Boosted Cox learning and elastic-net fitting combined the three expression features into a risk score linked to measured patient survival. Univariate gene screening, generic enrichment and AI-agent drug suggestions alone are not the admitted result.

source_review.scope: Read primary clinical cohort acquisition, ten-algorithm/101-combination selection, CoxBoost/elastic-net evaluation Methods and survival-model Results. Operational biological procedures and drug claims were not processed or adjudicated. Figure-level numerical performance and supplements were not independently reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Unsupervised expression subtypes differ in measured lung function in pulmonary fibrosis
summary: Consensus clustering of oxidative-stress-related expression profiles identified pulmonary-fibrosis subgroups with different measured respiratory function and symptom scores. Primary Figure1 shows subtypeB with better FVC, DLCO and respiratory quality-of-life scores, despite its higher computed oxidative-stress score. This direction conflicts with the abstract narrative, so the result is retained only as a retrospective subtype association, without causal or treatment claims.
ai_technology: Unsupervised consensus clustering of gene-expression profiles; LASSO, random forests and SVM-RFE for ancillary marker selection
organization: Beijing University of Chinese Medicine

evidence.tested: The primary Methods used GSE32537 as the training dataset and ConsensusClusterPlus to learn two subgroups from154 oxidative-stress-related genes. Figure1H–J and main Results associate subtypeB with lower StGeorge respiratory-questionnaire scores and higher percent-predicted FVC and DLCO than subtypeA. These are measured patient characteristics rather than clustering-separation benchmarks.
evidence.unknown: The abstract implies better respiratory status at lower oxidative-stress scores, whereas Figure1F/H–J and main Results show better function in the subgroup with higher computed scores. The biological direction is unresolved and is not adopted. The clustering relationship is retrospective; reproducible clinical subtype assignment, causal mechanisms, antioxidant treatment benefit and prospective utility are unestablished. Ancillary animal and drug claims are not independently adjudicated.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised consensus learning defined expression-based patient subgroups whose association with measured respiratory function constitutes the represented clinical finding. PCA separation alone and biomarker classification benchmarks are not treated as discoveries.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary PMC cohort/consensus-clustering and marker-selection Methods, respiratory-function and clinical subgroup Results; directly viewed primary Figure1 to verify direction. Publisher canonical front metadata and fresh PubMed relationships checked. Operational animal/cell procedures, drug effects and supplementary implementation not adjudicated. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: LASSO expression score distinguishes delayed kidney-graft function in retrospective cohorts
summary: A three-gene LASSO score was evaluated against observed delayed graft function after kidney transplantation. The study reports AUC 0.730 in an internal test split and 0.773 in a small separate biopsy cohort. This is retrospective clinical discrimination, without demonstrated prevention, treatment benefit or prospective deployment.
ai_technology: Ten-fold cross-validated LASSO for a three-gene delayed-graft-function score
organization: Capital Medical University; Beijing Chao-Yang Hospital

evidence.tested: From 202 post-reperfusion samples with graft-function information, the source made a 70:30 training/internal-test split. Training-set LASSO selected ANXA1, HSP90AA1 and NFKBIA. Reported AUC was 0.730 internally and 0.773 in GSE90861, a separate cohort of 23 paired-biopsy recipients, twelve with delayed and eleven with immediate graft function.
evidence.unknown: Small retrospective datasets and donor-type differences limit generalization. The separate cohort also informed earlier expression confirmation of candidate genes, so it is not a wholly untouched evaluation of the entire discovery workflow. Individual-patient split independence and supplementary implementation were not reconstructed. No causal necroptosis mechanism, reduced rejection, therapeutic benefit or locked prospective prediction was established by the represented model evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO learned nonzero expression features and coefficients for a combined score evaluated against measured clinical graft-function outcomes. Generic pathway enrichment and recovery of known inflammatory biology are not the represented finding.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary PMC cohort acquisition, gene-screening, LASSO training/internal split and external-evaluation Methods plus DGF Results through the web primary-text route. Publisher canonical front and fresh PubMed notice metadata checked. Graft-survival supplementary model and individual-patient reconstruction were not independently adjudicated. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Neural text analysis maps changing COVID-19 discussion and sentiment in Australian tweets
summary: Neural topic and sentiment models analyzed a corpus of 2.9 million Australian-sphere COVID-19 tweets. The study identified evolving discussion themes and a predominantly mixed positive/negative conversation, with geographic differences in model-assigned sentiment. These are observations about a selected English-language Twitter corpus, without validated population mental-health estimates, causal lockdown effects or prospective outbreak prediction.
ai_technology: LSTM informed neural network with VADER-derived prior features; variational-autoencoder topic model with Sentence-BERT embeddings
organization: Queensland University of Technology

evidence.tested: The source collected 2.9 million keyword-selected tweets dated November 27, 2019 to April 7, 2020 and removed non-English posts. An LSTM sentiment model combined learned text representations with lexicon-based prior features. Neural topic modeling identified themes including spread control, isolation/work from home, reported cases and racism. Corpus analyses reported positive-labelled tweet fractions around one-half during much of the observed period and location-dependent variation.
evidence.unknown: Tweet selection, inferred locations and user composition limit representativeness. Model-assigned sentiment is not a clinical measure of distress, and the main corpus was not independently labelled throughout. Temporal alignment with reported cases does not establish causal policy effects or validated early-warning performance. Detailed train/test implementation and corpus-level annotation were not independently reconstructed; no first-outbreak chronology claim is adopted.
evidence.ai_role: Learned neural classifiers and topic representations converted large-scale text into sentiment/topic measurements underlying the specific observational social-discussion findings. Architecture benchmarks alone and raw tweet-volume correlations are not the admitted result.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary corpus acquisition/preprocessing, LSTM/VADER informed-network and VAE/Sentence-BERT topic-model Methods, sentiment/topic corpus Results and source comparison descriptions. Corpus annotation and detailed train/test implementation were not reconstructed; no clinical mental-health or causal-policy claim adopted. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned image segmentation reveals size-dependent pancreatic-organoid treatment responses
summary: A trained StarDist image model enabled longitudinal measurement of pancreatic-cancer organoids. The study reports size-dependent gemcitabine responses, with larger organoids more affected, while highlighting limits of intensity-based health labels and endpoint viability assays. These are in-vitro model observations, without demonstrated patient treatment benefit or a validated clinical therapy-selection test.
ai_technology: OrganoIDNet custom-trained StarDist segmentation of bright-field organoid images
organization: Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences; University Medical Center Göttingen

evidence.tested: StarDist was trained on manually annotated human and mouse pancreatic-cancer-organoid images. Learned segmentation enabled image-derived counts, area and size-group trajectories during experimental treatment. The source reports greater gemcitabine-associated effects in larger organoids and comparison with an endpoint viability assay. The represented finding is a measured size-response pattern in experimental models, rather than segmentation accuracy alone.
evidence.unknown: Small model panels and image-derived measurements limit generalization. Healthy/unhealthy labels were assigned by a fixed intensity threshold after segmentation, not learned biological-state classification; debris and merging affect counts. Endpoint viability and imaging disagreed in immune-cell co-cultures, so no secure immune-mediated killing or immunotherapy-potency claim is adopted. Operational culture/treatment procedures and independent assay replication were not adjudicated.
evidence.ai_role: Learned StarDist segmentation extracted individual-organoid size and area from longitudinal images, enabling the reported size-dependent response observation. Fixed intensity thresholds and generic platform feasibility alone are not the admitted finding.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary section2.9 image-analysis Methods, trained StarDist operation and postprocessing; high-level size/response Results, health-label/debris limitation and imaging-versus-endpoint-assay disagreement. Complete abstract and original front metadata checked. Operational biological culture/treatment procedures and supplements were not adjudicated. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Random forests capture cancer-specific variation in measured immune-cell response assays
summary: Random-forest models combined receptor–ligand expression measurements to estimate experimentally observed natural-killer-cell responses to tumor samples. Cancer-specific models generalized better within their studied cancer types than a pan-cancer model, whose separate-test AUC fell to 0.638. This is assay-level biological model validation, without established clinical treatment-selection benefit.
ai_technology: Random forests combining receptor–ligand expression features for assay-response classification
organization: University of Science and Technology of China

evidence.tested: The source analyzed 76 distinct NK-cell samples against fourteen ovarian-cancer cell lines, then extended modeling across cancers. Random forests used 70:30 training/test partitions, ten-fold grid-search tuning and twenty random repetitions. A separate pan-cancer test set produced AUC 0.638 and accuracy 63.52%; source-reported breast- and gastric-cancer models reached separate-test AUCs 0.831 and 0.865. The result concerns measured assay response and its cancer-dependent generalization.
evidence.unknown: Random tumor–immune-cell pair partitions do not establish complete donor/cell-line independence; shared entities could affect apparent generalization. Upstream feature screening isolation and supplementary pair-level reconstruction were not verified. Five patient-derived AML samples and one treated patient do not establish prospective clinical efficacy or broad therapy-selection utility. Operational cell preparation, experimental manipulation and treatment protocols were not adjudicated.
evidence.ai_role: Random forests learned nonlinear combinations of expression features linked to measured assay outcomes, enabling the observed distinction between cancer-specific and pan-cancer response prediction. Generic classifier benchmarks alone and untested clinical benefit are not the admitted claim.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary computational model construction/tuning Methods and ovarian/pan-cancer/cancer-specific assay-prediction Results, plus high-level AML validation limitations. Operational biological preparation/manipulation protocols and supplements were not processed or adjudicated. Existing-data assay evaluation is classified retrospectively. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Post hoc neural gait analysis detects a tandem-walk metric difference in an ataxia trial
summary: A deep pose-estimation pipeline extracted gait measurements from a small convenience subset of a randomized ataxia trial. Post hoc analysis found a tandem-walk metric difference between troriluzole and placebo, while the natural-walk comparison was nonsignificant and treatment did not reduce falls. The result supports a bounded retrospective measurement finding, without confirmatory evidence of clinical benefit.
ai_technology: MPII-trained multi-stage deep neural network for human pose estimation; derived Pose Dispersion Index
organization: Yale School of Medicine; Biohaven Pharmaceuticals; Massachusetts General Hospital; UCLA School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Among 218 randomized participants, interpretable paired videos were available for 67 tandem-walk and 56 natural-walk participants. The pretrained deep network tracked body keypoints used to calculate pose dispersion. An adjusted treatment-by-visit mixed model reported a week 48 tandem-walk coefficient 0.584, 95% CI 0.137–1.031, p=0.010. The natural-walk difference was nonsignificant, and the source explicitly reports no treatment effect on falls.
evidence.unknown: The video endpoint was post hoc and was not the original recording purpose. Convenience and quality selection retained only 30.7% and 25.7% of participants, respectively, introducing selection and measurement limitations. Only baseline/final recordings were analyzed, supplementary metric implementation was not independently reconstructed, and the finding does not establish prespecified efficacy, reduced falls or clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: The learned pose model extracted body coordinates from trial videos, enabling a source-specific gait metric and treatment-group comparison that standard clinician ratings did not directly provide. Trial randomization does not make this later AI-derived endpoint a locked prospective evaluation.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary trial/video eligibility, pretrained pose-model and derived-index Methods, post hoc mixed/Poisson evaluation, tandem/natural-walk Results, no-falls-benefit statement and convenience-video limitations. Supplementary metric implementation not independently reconstructed. No prospective locking or clinical-benefit claim adopted. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned sepsis groups show different observed hospital mortality in an ICU cohort
summary: K-means clustering of eleven routine first-day measurements grouped 8,817 sepsis records into two clinical patterns. Observed hospital mortality differed between groups and remained associated after statistical adjustment. This is a retrospective cohort relationship, without established biological subtypes, causal treatment effects or validated bedside deployment.
ai_technology: Unsupervised K-means clustering of routine ICU clinical measurements
organization: Wuhan University; Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University

evidence.tested: The source selected 8,817 MIMIC-IV sepsis patients and used eleven expert-selected variables measured during the first ICU day. It compared two-to-eight clusters and selected two using clustering criteria. Hospital mortality was 29.4% in the smaller group versus 8.5% in the larger group; adjusted odds ratio was 2.214, 95% CI 1.780–2.754. Outcome differences are actual cohort observations beyond cluster-separation scores.
evidence.unknown: The groups were derived and compared in the same retrospective single-center database, without external transportability testing. They may reflect severity and clinical heterogeneity rather than distinct biological entities. Missing lactate and oxygenation values required imputation; absent baseline SOFA and unmeasured infection characteristics may bias case definition and associations. No causal therapy-response difference, prospective prediction or operational benefit was shown.
evidence.ai_role: K-means learned multivariable patient groups without using mortality as its clustering target; subsequent outcome analysis linked those learned groups to observed hospital mortality. PCA visualization alone and recovery of known individual severity markers are not the represented result.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary sepsis eligibility, variable selection/imputation, K-means cluster-number selection and adjusted-outcome Methods, group mortality Results and limitations. Supplementary implementation and individual records not independently reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned correction improves retrospective infliximab concentration estimates in young patients
summary: XGBoost corrected errors from a population-pharmacokinetic Bayesian model using measured infliximab concentrations in young patients with Crohn’s disease. Internal cross-validation reduced concentration prediction error, but some cases worsened and no external or prospective treatment-benefit evaluation was shown. The result concerns measured drug concentrations, without established improvements in dosing safety or disease outcomes.
ai_technology: XGBoost error correction integrated with population-pharmacokinetic Bayesian estimation
organization: Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center; University of Cincinnati; Connecticut Children’s Medical Center; Nationwide Children’s Hospital; Children’s Hospital of Wisconsin

evidence.tested: The source analyzed 292 successive-concentration pairs from 93 patients aged 2–22 years. XGBoost learned prediction errors using clinical features and prior drug measurements. Five-fold evaluation reported RMSE 3.78 ± 0.85 micrograms/mL versus 4.8 for Bayesian estimation alone. Absolute error improved modestly on average; the source also reports worsened predictions in a subset.
evidence.unknown: Multiple observations per patient were present, but explicit patient-grouped folds were not established in the reviewed Methods. Correlation-based feature selection and algorithm comparisons may affect internal performance; independent final evaluation was absent. Low concentrations below quantification were excluded. This is retrospective evaluation, without demonstrated clinical remission, safety improvement or validated continuous-learning deployment.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost learned residual prediction patterns and adjusted the prior pharmacokinetic estimates; comparison with measured subsequent concentrations supplies the specific clinical validation result. The pre-existing Bayesian model/dashboard alone is not treated as a new discovery.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary clinical cohort/consecutive-concentration design, Bayesian and XGBoost residual-learning/tuning/evaluation Methods, measured-concentration error Results and limitations. Patient-grouped fold independence and supplementary implementation were not established; dosing procedures or clinical recommendations not represented. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: AI-measured retinal vessel features show modest associations with later colorectal cancer
summary: Deep-learning retinal vessel measurements were associated with later colorectal-cancer diagnoses in 55,798 UK Biobank participants. Four vascular features retained associations after clinical adjustment, with modest effect sizes. This retrospective analysis of longitudinal records does not establish causal cancer mechanisms, validated screening accuracy or benefit from changing cancer-surveillance decisions.
ai_technology: RMHAS deep-learning retinal vascular segmentation and automated feature measurement
organization: Southern Medical University; Guangdong Provincial People’s Hospital; Hong Kong Polytechnic University; Shantou University; Chinese University of Hong Kong

evidence.tested: The source analyzed 55,798 initially colorectal-cancer-free participants with usable fundus images, documenting 652 incident cancers over median 11.32-year follow-up. RMHAS segmented arteries, veins and optic disc before quantifying vascular geometry. After adjustment, four features remained associated with incidence; greater arterial-tortuosity variability had a per-standard-deviation hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 1.01–1.06. Sensitivity analyses were reported, including exclusion of early diagnoses.
evidence.unknown: Observational associations have modest effect sizes and may reflect shared risk factors, reverse causation or residual confounding. Multiple-feature screening and selective imaging eligibility limit interpretation; 93% of participants were White. This was retrospective analysis despite prospective original cohort collection. No independent screening model, incremental clinical utility, causal angiogenesis or reduced cancer mortality was established by the represented finding. Supplementary results were not independently reconstructed.
evidence.ai_role: The pretrained RMHAS deep-learning pipeline segmented retinal structures at cohort scale, enabling quantitative vascular features linked to subsequent recorded cancer diagnoses. Cox regression alone and generic vessel-segmentation benchmarks are not treated as the enabling AI result.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary UK Biobank eligibility, RMHAS segmentation/feature-extraction, clinical outcome linkage, covariate/FDR/sensitivity-analysis Methods and incidence Results/limitations. Original RMHAS development paper and supplements not independently read. Specific measured cohort association, not screening deployment or causal mechanism, represented. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Urine-output neural model shows retrospective discrimination of severe kidney-injury events
summary: A convolutional neural network analyzed urine-output trends in 35,573 ICU patients to estimate later severe kidney-injury events under a restrictive urine-plus-creatinine definition. Patient-separated retrospective testing reported AUC 0.89, above logistic regression. Clinical prevention, calibrated alarm yield and prospective bedside benefit were not established.
ai_technology: Stacked and parallel convolutional neural networks with highway connections for urine-output time series
organization: Politecnico di Torino; National Research Council of Italy; Perugia Hospital; Terni Hospital

evidence.tested: The source pooled eICU and MIMIC-III records and separated patients across training, validation, calibration and test sets. The CNN used twelve-hour urine-output windows, with case series truncated six hours before the defined event. In the 7,080-patient test cohort, reported AUC was 0.89 versus 0.85 for logistic regression. The target required both creatinine increase and urine-output reduction; dialysis patients were excluded.
evidence.unknown: This was retrospective pooled-database evaluation, not a locked prospective clinical test. Urine output contributes to both model input and event definition; imputation and restrictive exclusions limit generalization to broader AKI. Reported likelihood ratios must not be read as positive predictive value or five true cases per six alarms. Individual-record timing, exact alarm yield and calibrated probabilities were not independently reconstructed. No reduced kidney injury, mortality or treatment benefit was demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN learned temporal urine-output features linked to later recorded severe-AKI labels and was compared with a logistic baseline. The admitted result is specific retrospective clinical discrimination, not recovery of a single urine-output cutoff or a validated intervention.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary AKI target/eligibility, urine imputation and time truncation, patient-separated training/validation/calibration/test, CNN architecture and evaluation Methods plus clinical discrimination Results. Alarm likelihood-ratio interpretation checked and excluded from represented yield claims; individual-record timing and supplement not reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Learned preoperative record features improve retrospective orthopedic VTE classification
summary: Genetic-algorithm feature selection and a deep neural classifier distinguished recorded postoperative venous-thromboembolism events in a large orthopedic-procedure dataset. The final table reports better discrimination than using established risk factors alone. Patient overlap, procedure coding and model-selection uncertainty limit this retrospective result; no causal medication risk or improved prophylaxis outcome was demonstrated.
ai_technology: Genetic-algorithm feature selection with gradient boosting; fully connected deep neural network classification
organization: University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee; Oklahoma State University; Istinye University; University of Wisconsin-Whitewater

evidence.tested: The source derived 541,354 procedure records from 392,661 patients, using prior diagnosis/medication windows and coded VTE within thirty days. A 70:30 random procedure split evaluated a six-hidden-layer DNN. Final Table 6 reports AUC 0.901 after genetic feature selection versus 0.780 using established risk factors. The abstract instead cites 0.873, which main text assigns to a preliminary feature-selection stage.
evidence.unknown: Patients could contribute multiple procedures, and patient-level partition isolation was not established. Broad procedure-code ranges may include operations beyond hip/knee replacement. Genetic selection/tuning isolation from final evaluation remains unclear; excluding postoperative prophylaxis also limits preoperative applicability. The Table6/abstract difference is not silently resolved. Drug-feature importance is associational and does not establish medication harms or benefit from changing treatment.
evidence.ai_role: Learned feature selection and nonlinear classification linked preoperative record patterns to measured/coded postoperative outcomes, providing a specific retrospective clinical evaluation beyond a generic architecture benchmark. No discovered causal risk factor or clinical intervention effect is adopted.

source_review.scope: Read actual full primary PMC clinical cohort/procedure construction, endpoint/windows, holdout, genetic/GBT feature-selection and DNN Methods; directly read primary Tables4/6 and model Results. Abstract-versus-main AUC association and procedure/patient separation caveats checked. Individual records and detailed patient-level test isolation not reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Cascaded prostate-MRI model shows limited lesion detection and classification in clinical testing
summary: A cascaded 3D U-Net and residual-network system was evaluated on held-out clinical prostate MRI scans, with partial targeted-biopsy comparison. It detected 56.1% of expert-marked lesions and achieved 30.8% overall PI-RADS classification accuracy. The result documents limitations of retrospective clinical performance, without established cancer-screening benefit or evidence that the system can replace biopsy.
ai_technology: Cascaded 3D U-Net lesion segmentation and 3D residual networks for BPH filtering and PI-RADS classification
organization: National Cancer Institute; National Institutes of Health; NVIDIA

evidence.tested: The source reports 150 held-out scans with 198 expert-marked lesions. After benign-hyperplasia filtering, the algorithm detected 111 of 198 lesions, with PPV 62.7% and overall PI-RADS accuracy 30.8%. Among 136 lesions with targeted biopsy, 82.3% of detected reference lesions were tumor-positive, while 50.9% of missed reference lesions were benign. This is a specific clinical evaluation with partial pathology follow-up, beyond a public image benchmark alone.
evidence.unknown: Detection/reference categories were defined by one expert radiologist rather than complete histopathology. False-positive regions lacked targeted-biopsy validation, preventing full cancer detection-rate assessment. Cohort totals are supported by Figure 1, but abstract/Methods split counts conflict; pathology-grade subtotals also do not fully reconcile. Prostate-X includes repeated scans, and individual-patient separation across all partitions was not reconstructed. No reader-assistance benefit, prospective workflow evaluation or clinical efficacy was demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Learned networks detected and classified suspicious regions from patient MRI; comparison with expert labels and available biopsy outcomes produced the represented diagnostic-validation result. Low performance is retained rather than treated as evidence of clinical utility.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary clinical cohort, expert reference, cascaded 3D U-Net/residual architecture and hold-out evaluation Methods; test detection/classification, partial biopsy Results and limitations. Directly viewed Figure1; split-count and pathology-grade discrepancies preserved. Supplements and individual scans not independently reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Automated prostate-extension grading shows a sensitivity–specificity tradeoff against pathology
summary: A cascaded segmentation and random-forest pipeline was evaluated against surgical pathology in a retrospective prostate-cancer cohort. In 127 held-out patients, one threshold produced lower sensitivity but higher specificity than the radiologist comparison. This is a bounded clinical-validation finding, without established superiority, improved surgical decisions or independent replication of the reused segmentation model.
ai_technology: Reused 3D U-Net/residual segmentation pipeline with random-forest extraprostatic-extension grading
organization: National Cancer Institute; National Institutes of Health

evidence.tested: The source split 634 prostatectomy patients into 507 development and 127 test patients. Fixed segmentation models produced prostate/lesion masks; geometric features trained random forests with repeated cross-validation. At EPE≥1, test sensitivity/specificity were 0.67/0.73 versus 0.81/0.62 for the radiologist, using pathology as reference. Four-grade balanced accuracy was limited, and individual grade AUCs ranged 0.55–0.70.
evidence.unknown: This retrospective analysis used prospectively recorded radiologist assessments, without prospective AI-model locking. Development grades partly incorporated pathology, while comparison grades came from the radiologist. Reused segmentation models and overlapping institutional recruitment periods mean the full pipeline is not established as wholly unfamiliar with test patients. No paired clinical reader-assistance or treatment-benefit trial was performed, and no general superiority is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: Learned segmentation extracted lesion/capsule features and a trained random forest mapped them to extension grades; comparison with actual surgical pathology supplies the distinct clinical-validation result. This extends a previously developed segmentation workflow rather than constituting independent replication of it.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary clinical selection/patient split, radiologist/pathology label construction, fixed segmentation-feature and random-forest training/evaluation Methods, pathology-reference test Results and comparison limits. Source reference27 checked against previously read segmentation paper. Individual overlap across reused model training and this cohort not reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.

title: Weights linked to AI sycophancy also support factual correction
summary: Researchers pruned 1,000 weights selected for their role in agreeing with incorrect user claims in Llama 3.1 and Qwen2.5. The intervention reduced this kind of agreement, but it also weakened the models’ tendency to correct their own wrong answers after seeing accurate claims. The result suggests the two behaviors partly share mechanisms in the models and tasks studied.
ai_technology: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
organization: Harvard University; Stanford University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §4 pruning and controls, Figures 3/D2, and Appendices D.1–D.3

evidence.tested: Pruning was compared with unpruned models and magnitude-matched random pruning. Tests distinguished accurate and inaccurate claims, source cues, independent factual recall, and weight-set overlap.
evidence.unknown: The experiment establishes a contribution of the selected weights on two checkpoints and controlled tasks. It does not establish a single mechanism for all forms of sycophancy.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers used gradient responses of two pretrained language models to select weights associated with agreeing with incorrect user claims, then intervened on those weights.

title: An unstated country representation guides Qwen’s capital answers
summary: In a controlled two-step geography task, researchers changed a representation of a country that was never named in the prompt. At the city token, the intervention redirected Qwen2.5-7B to the paired country’s capital in 79% of 1,038 pairs. The country was also readable later in the prompt, where the intervention had no effect at the tested layers. This experiment is reported in the November 11 preprint version.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-7B, cross-fitted country subspaces
organization: Independent research

source_review.scope: arXiv metadata and v3 §5 and Appendix E, with v1/v2 text checked for the country-to-capital experiment

evidence.tested: The preregistered intervention compared held-out matched city pairs against random and copied-embedding subspaces, whole-state replacement, and same-country pairs.
evidence.unknown: The test concerns one model and a constrained task on cities the model already answered correctly. Other tasks and weak latent signals remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Country subspaces were estimated on one half of the pretrained Qwen2.5-7B city examples, then used in a controlled intervention on matched held-out city examples.

title: Human factual judgments improved after a matched AI debate
summary: Among 92 people who reconsidered the same factual item after reading both sides of a Claude Opus 4.5 debate, accuracy rose from 41.3% to 57.6%. The result concerns non-experts in one online study and a protocol that held the question’s subtopic fixed.
ai_technology: Claude Opus 4.5
organization: University of Genoa

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 authors and affiliations, human protocols and model setup, and Table 5

evidence.tested: Table 5 reports paired pre/post accuracy for the same-subtopic protocol, with a 16.31 percentage-point change and a Holm-adjusted McNemar p-value of 0.028.
evidence.unknown: The paired change does not establish how the protocol compares with alternatives, which differed in what participants saw or judged. The study did not measure long-term retention or behavior.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Opus 4.5 generated the opposing sides of a same-subtopic debate before people re-answered the same factual item.

title: A learned simulator identified training orders that delayed detectable reward failures
summary: In controlled experiments with language models trained to write code, researchers used a fitted simulator to select four orderings of training examples. In subsequent runs, the selected orderings reached the threshold for detectable reward failures an average of 96.6% later than four baseline orderings.
ai_technology: SimHack, Qwen3
organization: Google Research; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §2 onset endpoint, §3 learned simulator, and §5.1/Figure 6 measured intervention

evidence.tested: Actual model training runs compared the time to a fixed detectable-failure threshold for four simulator-selected and four baseline orderings.
evidence.unknown: The result depends on the studied coding tasks, failure detector and threshold. Delaying the detector’s threshold does not establish prevention or generalize to deployment behavior.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted SimHack behavior model predicted the onset under candidate training-example orderings and selected four for actual model runs.

title: Deep GraphCast features align with where cyclones are headed
summary: An analysis of 205 tropical cyclones found that deeper GraphCast layers carried features that aligned better with cyclone position and pressure structure six hours ahead than at the input time. Researchers identified those features using fitted sparse autoencoders and compared them with historical cyclone tracks and pressure fields.
ai_technology: GraphCast, sparse autoencoders
organization: Tsinghua University; University College London

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §2 data and feature fitting, §3.2/3.3 and Figure 4

evidence.tested: The retrospective analysis compared feature alignment at the input time and six hours ahead over 2,115 time steps, across 16 processing layers and five separate sparse decompositions of layer 8.
evidence.unknown: Feature alignment does not demonstrate that GraphCast uses a particular feature causally or that the feature improves operational forecasts.
evidence.ai_role: Sparse autoencoders learned features from GraphCast activations, allowing the researchers to compare feature patterns with distinct cyclone attributes at matching and later times.

title: Penalizing length changed an AI model’s grammatical choices
summary: Researchers trained Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct to turn structured events into English sentences. Penalizing longer answers increased its preference for shorter grammatical variants, including unfamiliar constructions with an optional “that.” Transfer to more distant constructions was limited.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, spaCy en_core_web_trf
organization: New York University; The University of Texas at Austin

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §§3–4, Figure 7, and Appendices B–C

evidence.tested: Post-training varied the length penalty and KL regularization across three seeds, then tested unseen examples of trained and untrained grammatical alternatives.
evidence.unknown: This controlled experiment used one small language model. It did not measure human comprehension or show that an analogous penalty caused the language patterns observed in frontier models.
evidence.ai_role: A trained dependency parser and learned classifiers quantify linguistic features, and length-penalty post-training of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct tests grammatical transfer.

title: A hidden-state shift can cause a language model to repeat one token
summary: Researchers isolated a shift shared across responses during language-model preference training. Inserting the learned shift into an untreated model reproduced a failure in which one token dominated generation. The failure appeared in 14 of 17 tested model lineages under the study’s per-token ranking objective.
ai_technology: Preference-optimized language models, including Llama-2 and Llama-3.1
organization: The University of Tokyo; TIER IV; Huawei

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §§4–5 and 7, Appendix B.17, and primary intervention controls

evidence.tested: The authors isolated the shared offset, compared transplantation with magnitude-matched random directions, and tested masking of the component in the training loss.
evidence.unknown: The failure depends on model and objective. Related hidden shifts were also observed without generation collapse in tested standard preference-training runs.
evidence.ai_role: The researchers isolated a common direction learned during preference training and tested its contribution by transplanting it into an untreated language model.

title: Video diffusion models were sensitive at similar denoising steps across prompts
summary: Researchers reduced attention in one denoising window at a time. Within each of four pretrained video models, the windows that most changed the final video were similar across eight prompts. Median rank correlations against the other prompts ranged from 0.95 to 1.00.
ai_technology: Wan2.1, Wan2.2, HunyuanVideo
organization: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences; KlingAI Research; Peking University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §3 attention sensitivity, Figure 2, Appendix D.1 leave-one-out tests

evidence.tested: The experiment compared final-video error with dense attention and ranked ten windows separately for each prompt, holding each prompt out from the comparison rank.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns within-model rankings for a small set of prompts and the tested attention perturbation. It does not establish that the same window order applies to other models or sampling settings.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers selectively altered attention in trained video diffusion models and measured how the resulting videos departed from the dense model output.

title: Carbides became rounder and occupied more of a tempered steel
summary: Researchers used a trained image classifier to separate carbide particles from the surrounding high-speed steel in electron micrographs. After isothermal holding, the measured carbide volume fraction was 9.9%, up from 8.3% in directly quenched reference samples, and mean particle circularity rose from 0.881 to 0.914.
ai_technology: Trainable Weka Segmentation
organization: Ruhr University Bochum; RWTH Aachen University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 PDF front matter, image segmentation methods, Figures 3–4, Tables 1–2, discussion and conclusions

evidence.tested: Microscopy with learned segmentation measured about 1,600 carbides per condition. The stereological measurement error reported for each volume fraction was ±0.4 percentage points.
evidence.unknown: The population-level differences apply to the tested alloy and thermal conditions. They do not distinguish growth of existing particles from nucleation of new ones or prove an epitaxial growth mechanism. Carbide rounding during holding had been reported in earlier high-speed-steel research; the represented contribution is quantitative measurement in this alloy.
evidence.ai_role: Trainable Weka Segmentation fit a classifier from manually labeled microscopy regions and separated carbide from matrix, enabling particle-area and shape measurements.

title: Fewer biased answers after model compression often coincided with more abstention
summary: On the BBQ question-answering benchmark, 20 of 26 quantization configurations with fewer biased answers also abstained more often on questions they could answer. The comparison covered models from the Qwen3, Gemma 3 and SmolLM2 families.
ai_technology: Qwen3, Gemma 3, SmolLM2
organization: University of Hull

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §§3–5, exact quantization comparison, prompt variation and forced-choice appendix

evidence.tested: The authors compared multiple quantization configurations and reported correct, biased, and abstaining answers separately. They also changed prompt wording and removed the abstention option in a separate comparison.
