evidence.unknown: The 20-of-26 result is conditional on configurations with lower observed bias in this benchmark. It does not measure fairness in real use or establish that all compression increases abstention.
evidence.ai_role: The researchers compared outputs from Qwen3, Gemma 3 and SmolLM2 across model sizes and quantization settings, separating abstention from biased or non-biased answers.

title: CLIP linked different car classes through shared backgrounds or objects
summary: On UrbanCars, 94.8% of highly similar image pairs from different vehicle classes shared a background or a co-occurring object, compared with 18.1% of random cross-class pairs. Researchers selected the similar pairs using pretrained CLIP features before consulting the dataset’s attribute labels.
ai_technology: CLIP
organization: Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §4 similarity audit, Table 3 and Figure 2

evidence.tested: The audit compared randomly chosen cross-class training pairs with pairs selected using high cosine similarity in the frozen feature space.
evidence.unknown: The reported proportions concern a dataset constructed with two labeled shortcut attributes and the study’s similarity selection. They do not measure real-world shortcut prevalence.
evidence.ai_role: A frozen pretrained vision encoder determined which cross-class examples were closest without using known shortcut labels; audit labels were applied afterward.

title: Retrieval improvements shrank when combined in a RAG pipeline
summary: Five changes to a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline each improved document ranking when tested alone. Adding their individual gains gave an expected score of 0.667, but the combined system scored 0.483 against a baseline of 0.412. The result concerns the tested retrieval components and queries.
ai_technology: HyDE query augmentation, cross-encoder reranking
organization: IBM

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §§4–5, Table 6, §D.14/Figure 9 and limitations on faithfulness additivity

evidence.tested: A matched component-composition experiment compared individual changes and the combined pipeline using NDCG@10, with a paired bootstrap over 93 queries.
evidence.unknown: The result does not establish that every retrieval pipeline shows the same interaction. The paper’s answer-faithfulness comparison used different component configurations and did not directly establish additivity.
evidence.ai_role: Learned query augmentation and cross-encoder reranking change query–document rankings; matched component perturbations test whether those changes add together.

title: Training AI models on one value shifted their responses on another
summary: Researchers fine-tuned four language models using examples framed around restraint. On held-out scenarios, all four shifted toward responses labeled collectivist, although individualism was not the training target. The finding describes changes in model responses under a synthetic evaluation.
ai_technology: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B, Gemma-3-12B-Instruct, Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512
organization: University of Copenhagen; University of Cambridge

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §§3–4, Appendix C.3/C.4 and Tables 7–11

evidence.tested: Adapters and their original models scored the same held-out scenarios, with 1,500 examples per value pole. The shift in relative likelihood was significant in each of the four models under the reported multiple-comparison correction. For restraint-trained adapters, the signed table entries correspond to decreases in the raw high-individualism likelihood margin.
evidence.unknown: The categories and response examples are synthetic operationalizations. The result does not establish model beliefs, human preferences or behavior in deployment.
evidence.ai_role: The study separately fine-tuned four pretrained language models on synthetic examples of individual cultural-value dimensions and then tested labeled response preferences in unrelated dimensions.

title: A coding agent made a verified Lean lookup 5.46 times as fast
summary: Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol rewrote the sheet lookup in a Lean port of the Cheat command-line tool. The rewrite searched directly instead of building an intermediate list, and ran 5.46 times as fast as the original Lean function on withheld timing inputs. Lean checked that the two functions return the same result.
ai_technology: Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol, Lean 4
organization: University of California, Berkeley; Amazon Web Services

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §5.2 and Appendix D.3, named findConsolidated rewrite and proof scope

evidence.tested: The study reports repeated paired performance trials and an equality theorem checked by the Lean kernel for the specific rewrite.
evidence.unknown: The speedup concerns the named function on the study’s workloads. The equality theorem covers the migrated Lean reference, while agreement with the original Go program was assessed by differential testing.
evidence.ai_role: Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol generated a direct reverse-search implementation and a Lean equality proof.

title: Matching final answers masked different forgetting patterns during fine-tuning
summary: Researchers recovered 100% final performance on an old generation task across several replay budgets for a Qwen model. The same training runs nevertheless followed different trajectories in the probability assigned to correct old answers. The finding came from evaluating checkpoints throughout training as well as the final model.
ai_technology: Qwen and Mistral language-model fine-tuning
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 controlled replay budgets and objective allocation, Table 7 and endpoint analysis

evidence.tested: The study varied old-task replay budgets at matched training settings and separately measured old-task generation at the endpoint and negative log-likelihood across training checkpoints.
evidence.unknown: The result is specific to these models, old-task response tests and replay schedules. Checkpoint behavior cannot establish whether knowledge was removed or merely harder to elicit. The qualified original Qwen retained-response bank contained only 17 examples; its 100% endpoint is not broad preservation of old-task knowledge.
evidence.ai_role: Fine-tuned Qwen and Mistral models enabled direct measurement of task outputs and loss at multiple checkpoints under matched training protocols.

title: Medical model training changed privacy risk more than who ranked highest
summary: Across six clinical datasets, privacy-risk rankings were broadly similar under many changes to model training. In one chest X-ray cohort, stronger regularization reduced the share of patients above the study’s risk threshold from 88% to 30%. The rankings were compared across training changes using an audit of 7,789 medical-model instances.
ai_technology: ResNet, EfficientNet, vision transformers, ECGFounder, MRI-CORE
organization: University of Crete; Foundation for Research and Technology–Hellas; University of Maryland

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 PDF affiliation, aggregate Figures 2 and 4, cohort and risk-stability comparison

evidence.tested: A defensive study compared aggregate risk distributions and ordinal stability under seed, architecture, regularization and fine-tuning changes, including comparisons with trained seed replicates.
evidence.unknown: The outcomes measure estimated likelihood of training-set membership disclosure under the study’s audit. They do not represent observed patient disclosures or complete invariance across all settings.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers trained several thousand medical-model instances, including ECGFounder and MRI-CORE adaptations, and compared aggregate distributions of measured privacy risk across training regimes.

title: Routine questions led AI agents to disclose sensitive inferences in simulation
summary: A simulated GPT-5.6 Sol agent revealed restricted conclusions in 85 of 1,200 benign queries designed to be answerable from one document. The study tested synthetic documents and confidentiality controls, showing that an ordinary question can cause an agent to combine information into a restricted inference.
ai_technology: GPT-5.6 Sol and studied agent harnesses
organization: University of Southern California

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 aggregate defensive experimental design, §5.2–§5.3, Figure 1 and Table 16

evidence.tested: Researchers measured aggregate disclosures across controlled synthetic queries, reporting a 7.08% rate with a 95% interval of 3.75–10.67% for GPT-5.6 Sol across the tested safeguard and document conditions.
evidence.unknown: These are controlled outcomes on synthetic material and specified access settings. The rate does not estimate real-world disclosure frequency.
evidence.ai_role: Language-model agents including GPT-5.6 Sol process synthetic documents; researchers compare aggregate disclosure frequencies under confidentiality controls.

title: Dominant sparse-autoencoder features were often harder to explain
summary: In 65.2% of the sparse autoencoders tested, explanations of the highest-contribution quarter of features ranked activation examples less accurately than explanations for the remaining features. The pattern varied by autoencoder architecture.
ai_technology: Sparse autoencoders over pretrained language-model activations
organization: Purdue University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §3 dominance and explanation tests, §4 Table 2 and Figure 3; same aggregate result in v2

evidence.tested: The study tested a dominance-aware explanation-ranking measure across seven autoencoder architectures and checked robustness to firing-frequency matching and different explanation and judging models.
evidence.unknown: This is an explanation-ranking proxy, not a complete account of each feature’s meaning or its causal role in downstream decisions.
evidence.ai_role: Trained sparse autoencoders represent language-model activations, and model-generated feature explanations are checked using ranked activation evidence.

title: An agent trace detector misread repeated calculator calls as verification
summary: A human audit of calculator-assisted AI traces found that repeated calculator calls could be mislabeled as verification of earlier outputs. The October 21 preprint already reported this failure pattern and 14 disagreements. Its November 18 revision additionally reported fair agreement across 81 trace labels (κ = 0.29).
ai_technology: Tool-using language models
organization: University of Illinois Chicago; Argonne National Laboratory

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 original human audit and failure pattern, checked against v2 §§2–5, Tables 4 and 8 and updated agreement statistic

evidence.tested: The study introduced controlled calculator errors, measured agent behavior, and compared automated labels with human reading of the trace.
evidence.unknown: A visible tool call cannot reveal every internal check. The annotated sample and controlled arithmetic setting do not establish reliability on other tools or tasks. One author audited a selected, flag-guided sample with automated labels visible; this was not a blind independent annotation. The agreement statistic was reported in v2, after the underlying audit appeared in v1.
evidence.ai_role: Multiple learned agents produce calculator-assisted reasoning traces on controlled arithmetic tasks. Human auditors compare these traces with automatically generated labels.

title: AI decoders missed 168 verifiable messages in a controlled audit
summary: In an audit of 7,200 language-model outputs, researchers found 168 verifiable hidden messages that the original model decoders failed to recover. The result shows that decoder failure alone can miss successful encoding in this controlled test.
ai_technology: Gemini, Claude, GPT language-model encoders and decoders
organization: University of Maryland, College Park

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 aggregate encoding/decoding contingency results and validity distinctions

evidence.tested: The researchers compared original model-decoder results with an independent deterministic verification of the output.
evidence.unknown: The result applies to the tested synthetic messages and verification criteria. It does not estimate prevalence in real communications. Of the 168 cases, 58 were recovered with exploratory procedures added after inspecting the corpus. Verification also allowed normalized letter-sequence matches, rather than requiring byte-exact messages, and does not establish intentional encoding.
evidence.ai_role: Learned language models produced and attempted to recover messages. An independent deterministic audit checked recoverability to evaluate what the model decoders missed.

title: Unacknowledged suggestions influenced AI reasoning through question and filler tokens
summary: Researchers found that activation changes at questions and filler tokens carried part of an unacknowledged suggestion’s influence in two language models. Swapping those native activations partially shifted the models’ next-token predictions toward the predictions made without the suggestion.
ai_technology: Gemma-4-E4B-it, DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison; University of Oxford

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 causal analysis §§4.1–4.2, Figures 5–7 and matched token controls

evidence.tested: The two-target patch recovered 16.2% of the counterfactual distribution shift in Gemma and 19.3% in the DeepSeek model, measured by the study’s KL-divergence recovery metric. Equal-size random token controls recovered less.
evidence.unknown: The experiment concerns held-fixed responses under the tested suggestions. It establishes partial mediation at the selected locations, with effects that differ by model.
evidence.ai_role: A fitted residual stream editor identified candidate locations where hidden representations preserve a suggestion’s influence, which researchers tested with independent native activation patching.

title: Safety probe errors followed predictable scaling across three model families
summary: Researchers fit scaling laws to safety probes trained on smaller language models. The fits predicted the error of the next larger model to within 0.02 in 52 of 72 comparisons at the largest label budget. They tested these held-out predictions in the Qwen2.5, Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 families.
ai_technology: Learned activation probes on Qwen2.5, Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4
organization: University of Washington; Anthropic

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§3–5.1, Figure 10 and E.6 held-out model-size comparisons, confirmed core claim in v2

evidence.tested: The study trained two probe architectures across twenty models and compared held-out next-size forecasts with measured performance. Probe error was one minus AUROC.
evidence.unknown: The held-out extrapolation covers three model families and the study’s six safety tasks. The fitted constants and accuracy may differ with other data or probe designs.
evidence.ai_role: Learned activation probes trained on up to a million labels per setting generate measurement curves; power-law fits on smaller models predict performance on a held-out larger model.

title: Antihypertensive use was linked to slightly longer time without recorded cognitive impairment
summary: In a retrospective All of Us analysis targeting a high-risk population with model-derived weights, baseline antihypertensive use was associated with slightly longer time without a first recorded mild cognitive impairment diagnosis. The ratio of geometric mean time capped at 48 months was 1.012 overall and 1.026 in a subgroup with cardiometabolic and depressive multimorbidity.
ai_technology: Regularized logistic regression, cross-fitted XGBoost
organization: Columbia University; University of Michigan

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §4 propensity/outcome models, logistic risk weights, sample construction, Table 3 and Figure 3

evidence.tested: The study trained its risk model in a non-overlapping internal reference set of 83,745 participants and estimated associations in a 37,577-participant analysis set with 500 first recorded MCI diagnoses within 48 months. Model-derived weights target a high-risk population without restricting the cohort to a directly observed high-risk stratum.
evidence.unknown: The estimates are associations involving baseline medication use and the first recorded diagnosis. Treatment initiation, adherence, causal benefit and external validation were outside the study.
evidence.ai_role: A regularized logistic model fitted to the non-overlapping reference sample estimates target high-risk membership; cross-fitted XGBoost models estimate treatment propensity and outcomes.

title: More specific wording narrowed semantic representations in four language models
summary: Researchers compared sentences that made a meaning more specific with sentences that merely added detail. Across four language models, the more specific versions formed tighter neighborhoods in model activation space. The pattern persisted after removing five dominant directions of variation.
ai_technology: Gemma 4, Llama 3.2, Qwen2.5, Pythia
organization: Imperial College London

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 abstract and affiliation, refinement design, Figure 5, permutation tests and quality-controlled rerun

evidence.tested: Controlled refinement and elaboration chains were checked using blind human judgments. Across the four models, the contraction contrast persisted in 86–100% of layers after the five dominant directions were removed.
evidence.unknown: The result depends on the constructed text contrasts and representation measures. It does not demonstrate causal use of the contraction in other language tasks.
evidence.ai_role: Pretrained activation geometry is measured as controlled texts move from broader meanings to more specific descriptions, with blind human checks on the contrasts.

title: A latent safety monitor flagged fewer harmful prompts than model refusals
summary: Across 15 language models and a held-out set of reworded prompts, one activation-based monitor flagged about 23% of harmful prompts at the same false-alarm rate as a string-matched refusal reference, which flagged about 32%. A later activation readout caught more, but analyses linked much of that gain to the model’s own refusal decision.
ai_technology: Latent Guard, linear and multilayer activation probes
organization: University of Massachusetts Amherst

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, aggregate §6 out-of-distribution reader comparison and matched false-alarm analysis

evidence.tested: The authors compared trained readers and string-matched model refusal at matched false alarm rates and tested how their scores tracked the models’ planned replies.
evidence.unknown: The comparison covers particular rewordings and learned monitors. It does not establish the limits of every activation-based safety monitor. Refusal wording can be missed by the reference detector; a sampled audit found only 13 of 135 replies labeled answered actually provided harmful assistance. Later-readout gains therefore do not all represent detection of genuine unsafe compliance.
evidence.ai_role: Learned latent readers classify prompts from instruction-tuned model activations and are checked against observed refusals and embedding models.

title: Early recommendations shaped what AI groups chose later
summary: In a controlled music recommendation study, 13 language-model populations evaluated the same 48 unfamiliar song lyrics. When popularity strongly influenced what agents saw, the first 30 agents’ choices predicted later popularity better than recommendations made without popularity information for all 13 populations.
ai_technology: Thirteen language-model populations; Suno v4.5 stimuli
organization: Cornell University; Stanford University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§2–3, Figure 1 design, Figure 5 temporal comparison, appendix robustness and Table S2

evidence.tested: Each model had an independent baseline and eight simulated populations per influence condition. The study compared early choices and independent rankings as predictors of later recommendations.
evidence.unknown: The experiment used synthetic lyrics and a controlled interface, so the magnitude of herding may differ in other recommendation settings.
evidence.ai_role: Thirteen learned language-model populations select and recommend previously unseen Suno-generated lyrics under random exposure to popularity ordering and counts or independent evaluation.

title: Speech model representations tracked estimated quality less well under severe distortion
summary: Four pretrained speech encoders tracked estimated quality better for mildly distorted recordings than for severely distorted ones. Researchers compared clean and degraded versions of 100 English utterances across four levels of simulated distortion.
ai_technology: WavLM, HuBERT, SPEAR, Wav2Vec 2.0
organization: KAIST

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §2 severity and representation analysis and Figure 2

evidence.tested: The study compared rank correlations between encoder distances and several quality estimators, including a conventional spectral-distance check, with bootstrapped uncertainty.
evidence.unknown: The degradations were simulated and the outcomes were based on quality proxies. The study did not measure how listeners rated or understood the recorded speech.
evidence.ai_role: WavLM, HuBERT, SPEAR and Wav2Vec 2.0 encode clean and artificially degraded speech, enabling direct comparisons of preserved acoustic information across severities.

title: Reasoning models usually inherited the revision marker “wait” before reinforcement learning
summary: In 17 of 18 tested reinforcement-learning runs starting from models that rarely wrote “wait,” the word stayed rare even as math accuracy improved. In the traced OLMo-3 lineage, the word appeared during mid-training before reinforcement learning and became more frequent afterward.
ai_technology: OLMo-3, Qwen2.5, Qwen3, Mistral
organization: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab; Peking University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 affiliations, main provenance contrasts, released-checkpoint lineage and robustness appendix

evidence.tested: The analysis compared published checkpoint histories and controlled training runs, using fewer than 0.05 occurrences per thousand generated tokens as its absence criterion.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns a visible marker on the sampled tasks. It does not show whether a model reconsidered an answer without writing “wait.”
evidence.ai_role: Researchers sampled language-model outputs across recorded training stages and externally released and newly trained reinforcement-learning checkpoints.

title: AI captions added unsupported detail in the middle and more reference-unmatched content near the end
summary: In long captions for 198 images, six AI models produced more reference-unsupported specifics in the middle. The mean share assigned to a residual reference-unmatched category rose from 10.3% in the first quarter to 28.1% in the last. This category need not mean that a sentence is objectively vague.
ai_technology: Qwen3-based claim extraction and verification; Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5 and LLaVA captioners
organization: Beihang University; Kuaishou Technology; Fudan University; Zhejiang University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §3, Figure 1/Table 1, appendix comparison to 347 human rubric judgments and sampled visual recheck

evidence.tested: Researchers divided captions into quarters, assessed claims against human-derived image rubrics, and checked a sample of verifier judgments with human reviewers.
evidence.unknown: A caption can include a true detail omitted from its reference. The reported pattern concerns this sample and reference-based labeling, with only sampled image-level checks.
evidence.ai_role: Qwen models extract and verify ordered atomic claims from human references and generated captions; human annotators validate a sample of judgments.

title: Coding agents broke verified site behavior after completing requested changes
summary: In 107 of 586 benchmark runs that completed the requested website change and had comparable baseline checks, the coding agent broke an already verified browser state. In 78 of those 586 runs, a continuity check still failed at the end.
ai_technology: Coding agents evaluated with ProductWebBench
organization: Beihang University; IQuest Research; Huawei Technologies

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 controlled task construction, §§4–5, Table 4 and Appendix C provenance comparison

evidence.tested: The study replayed checks against untouched repositories and states that each run had previously passed. The 586-run subset had evidence from both comparisons.
evidence.unknown: The rates are specific to the completing runs with both baselines available, and do not estimate production software regression rates.
evidence.ai_role: Thirteen language-model systems implement requested code changes; browser checks on baseline and altered repositories expose regressions.

title: Country names and query language shifted AI answers in different ways
summary: In tests with three language models, naming a country in the user’s message moved open-ended responses 30–44% closer to the same model’s answers when assigned that country as a persona. Changing the query language instead shifted multiple-choice responses away from the associated persona in all three models.
ai_technology: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512, Gemma-3-27B-IT
organization: University of Copenhagen; Aalborg University Copenhagen; Bocconi University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§3–5.2, Figure 2, annotation and translation sensitivity appendices

evidence.tested: The controlled study compared named-country and language cues across survey-derived choices and about 1.6 million open-ended responses.
evidence.unknown: The reference was each model’s own persona-conditioned responses rather than people’s values. Country and language stand in for only a small part of cultural identity, and the measured shifts depended on prompt design.
evidence.ai_role: Llama, Ministral and Gemma generate answers under matched national persona, named-country and language cues; learned annotation and translation models support value comparisons.

title: People adopted false facts from confident AI tutors
summary: In a study with 32 volunteers, participants selected an assistant’s planted false answer for about 60% of quiz items assigned false information, compared with 11% of items assigned correct information. Mean scores fell from 7.4 to 2.9 out of 10 between fully accurate and fully falsified GPT-5-mini briefings.
ai_technology: GPT-5-mini
organization: Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham; Indian Institute of Science

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 trial design §§3.1–3.7, Table 3, §4.2 and ethics statement

evidence.tested: The counterbalanced study used five briefing reliability levels and 104 completed quizzes, with independently randomized topic order and corrective debriefing.
evidence.unknown: This was a small study with one underlying model, deliberately confident responses, and immediate quizzes. Retention over longer periods and responses to other assistants were not assessed. Participants could continue consulting the same assistant during each quiz. The measured choices do not establish unaided memory retention or durable internalized beliefs.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5-mini chat assistants explained science topics from briefings containing controlled levels of plausible false claims.

title: A judge flagged more concerning answers early in OLMo reinforcement learning than at the end
summary: In tests of OLMo-3-7B-Think, GPT-4o flagged 25.0% of outputs after supervised fine-tuning, 46.1% early in reinforcement learning, and 11.8% at the final checkpoint. The labels cover text that the judge classified as power-seeking or related behavior. The two judges agreed least near the apparent peak.
ai_technology: OLMo-3-7B-Think, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash
organization: Barış Alparslan, Sandy Tanwisuth and Caleb Petterson (affiliations not stated in the reviewed preprint)

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 checkpoint methods §§2–4, §4.1 trajectory, inter-judge comparisons and Appendices A.2/A.4

evidence.tested: The authors repeated the same 76 benchmark questions across 16 released post-training checkpoints and compared binary labels from two judging models.
evidence.unknown: The rates describe one primary judge’s classification of written answers. They do not demonstrate the model’s internal goals or behavior in deployment.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4o rates outputs across the same 76 items in 16 OLMo-3 checkpoints; Gemini 2.0 Flash provides a secondary comparison.

title: Saved shared notes were associated with better puzzle-solving workflows
summary: An audit of 28,568 language-model workflows found that those using a persistent shared document tended to solve more puzzles correctly. Across ten testable puzzles in held-out searches, the median accuracy difference was 13.5 percentage points.
ai_technology: GPT-5.4 family workflow agents; LightGBM
organization: Dartmouth College; Allen Institute for AI

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 workflow search corpus, LightGBM validation design, §V and fixed held-out association Table VI

evidence.tested: The authors mined features of executable workflow variants and evaluated the shared-memory association in held-out search runs. Six of ten comparable test puzzles had intervals strictly above zero.
evidence.unknown: The comparison is observational across searched workflows on selected puzzles. Other choices can correlate with shared memory, and the analysis does not establish a causal advantage on other tasks.
evidence.ai_role: Language models contribute executable workflow variants and mine feature hypotheses; a fitted LightGBM regressor checks predictive features before held-out searches are opened.

title: The lightest and heaviest jiu-jitsu classes showed distinct match progression
summary: A fitted model of 78 men’s no-gi Brazilian jiu-jitsu matches found that the 66 kg and over-99 kg groups differed from the middle weight classes in how recorded match states led to eventual outcomes. The matches came from one 2019 championship.
ai_technology: Hierarchical absorbing Markov model with Bayesian random-partition clustering
organization: Texas A&M University; Brigham Young University; University of Brasília

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 data scope, hierarchical random-partition fit, and aggregate posterior comparisons for sports weight categories

evidence.tested: The model pooled recorded transitions across classes and compared posterior probabilities of eventual match outcomes separately by weight class. The analysis used 244 sequences after excluding the absolute division from the original 93-match dataset.
evidence.unknown: The findings concern this tournament and the model’s grouping and state definitions. They do not establish a causal effect of body weight or generalize to other competitions.
evidence.ai_role: A fitted hierarchical absorbing Markov model and an Ewens–Pitman attraction random-partition model infer transition patterns by weight class from recorded matches.

title: A learned feature increased sawtooth-lead use in generated music
summary: Researchers used a sparse autoencoder to find a feature associated with a sawtooth synthesizer lead in the text2midi model. Increasing the feature produced that instrument on 14 of 20 prompts, compared with 1 of 20 using a random direction. A second set of ten prompts showed a similar effect.
ai_technology: text2midi, sparse autoencoders
organization: Warsaw University of Technology

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§4–5, prespecified confirmation and Table 5, held-out matched random direction, dictionary recurrence and limitations

evidence.tested: The prespecified confirmation compared the feature edit with a matched random edit and unmodified generation. The second test used disjoint prompts and a different seed.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns one feature in one selected model and an instrument represented explicitly in its MIDI vocabulary. It does not establish control of arbitrary musical attributes.
evidence.ai_role: A fitted sparse autoencoder discovers a feature in text2midi, whose decoded direction is directly varied on paired prompts to test instrument control.

title: Coarser AI robot planning helped only when feedback was less frequent
summary: In four controlled tasks on a physical Franka robot, using fewer steps to sample actions from a learned policy lowered success under frequent replanning but improved success when the robot executed a longer action sequence before checking again. A moving-target task still needed frequent feedback.
ai_technology: Flow-matching vision-language-action policies including π₀ and π₀.₅
organization: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 matched solver-by-horizon interventions, trajectory assessment and physical Franka experiments, Figure 5

evidence.tested: The study crossed two sampling depths and two execution horizons and ran 40 matched rollouts per setting for its physical evaluation.
evidence.unknown: The interaction was observed in the tested policies and tasks. It does not support coarse sampling as a general strategy for contact-rich or highly dynamic settings.
evidence.ai_role: Flow-matching control policies produce action trajectories with varied solver depths and replanning periods under matched evaluations.

title: An expanded document audit found training matches for 35.2% of test pages
summary: An expanded audit of the RVL-CDIP benchmark found training-set matches for 14,076 test pages, or 35.20%, and 14,151 validation pages, or 35.38%. The search used learned image matching and counted near-duplicates that shared a document template as well as copies. A smaller 2023 analysis had already identified substantial duplication.
ai_technology: CLIP, SuperPoint, LightGlue
organization: Vanderbilt University

source_review.scope: June arXiv v1 front matter, §§4.1–4.2 learned matching and Table 3; October v1 extension introduction and stated matching result; EACL 2023 §5 sampled overlap estimate.

evidence.tested: Learned CLIP embeddings proposed likely cross-split matches before SuperPoint and LightGlue visual matching and a text-similarity check. The calibration set contained 403 matched pairs among 1,600 candidate pairs, with 82.9% recall at the chosen threshold.
evidence.unknown: The audit includes same-template pages and may miss matches. The earlier 2023 sample-based estimate of about 32% uses a different method and is not a baseline for measuring a change in duplication.
evidence.ai_role: Learned CLIP embeddings screen scanned documents for likely matching pairs, and SuperPoint and LightGlue match their visual structure before final duplicate classification.

title: Robot model activations signaled failures before recovery became unlikely in simulation
summary: Researchers found that OpenVLA activation features could distinguish eventual failures from successful rollouts before recovery became unlikely in a simulated robot benchmark. The predictor reached an AUROC of 0.71 before the study’s estimated point of no return.
ai_technology: OpenVLA-7B, sparse autoencoders
organization: University of Utah

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §2 OpenVLA rollouts, §2.2/Table 1 and Appendix E recoverability estimates

evidence.tested: The study used 500 rollouts over ten simulated manipulation tasks, held out 95 trajectories, and estimated recoverability with alternative branched rollouts.
evidence.unknown: Recovery was defined using the study’s simulated branching protocol. The result does not establish reliable physical-robot intervention or superiority over raw activation predictors. Recoverability used only four alternative continuations per probe and depended on the tested policy and remaining time budget. Across reported alarm thresholds, false alarms ranged from 64% to 14% while actionable detections fell from 88% to 33%.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted sparse autoencoders decompose OpenVLA activation patterns and fitted outcome predictors compute early warnings on held-out robot-policy traces.

title: AI-assisted forensics found 30 additional bridge links in documented Ethereum cases
summary: Researchers reexamined 20 documented Ethereum money-laundering cases and identified 30 links between individual cases and cross-chain bridge protocols that were absent from the public reports they collected. A trained classifier flagged likely uses, which the researchers checked manually.
ai_technology: XGBoost
organization: Taiyuan University of Technology

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 aggregate evaluation setup, trained classifier comparison and §IV-D/Table V manual case-level confirmation

evidence.tested: The forensic study recovered all 11 case–bridge pairs already documented in the collected reports and manually verified 30 additional pairs. A protocol used several times in a single case counted once.
evidence.unknown: The selected cases are not representative of all Ethereum activity. The result does not establish legal responsibility or how common such links are outside the cases reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: An XGBoost classifier identifies likely cross-chain use, enabling reviewers to manually confirm connections between known cases and protocols on the public ledger.

title: DINOv2 patch features are more ambiguous near object-part boundaries
summary: In an analysis of 26,459 foreground patches from PartImageNet, frozen DINOv2 features became less distinguishable near labeled object-part boundaries. Boundary distance correlated negatively with feature entropy (−0.38) and positively with the margin between the two closest part prototypes (+0.36). The study measured these relationships for one encoder and one labeled dataset.
ai_technology: DINOv2 ViT-B/14; learned visual embeddings
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, experimental setup, Section 5 and Appendix B

evidence.tested: Part prototypes were anchored to high-purity labeled training patches. Distances from foreground patches to the nearest labeled boundary were compared with entropy and the top-two margin in the learned feature space.
evidence.unknown: The analysis uses one patch grid and one labeled dataset. It does not isolate grid size experimentally or measure the effect in other encoders.
evidence.ai_role: Frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 embeddings were compared with part prototypes formed from high-purity training patches.

title: Learned image groups reveal a low-sensitivity slice in cardiomegaly detection
summary: A fitted subgroup model assigned chest X-rays in a 22,281-image CheXpert-Plus test set to image groups. Across discovered groups, cardiomegaly sensitivity ranged from 0.10 to 0.98. One group associated with higher BMI and male sex had sensitivity of 0.10 and specificity of 0.95. The group was defined by learned image features and classifier scores, and its demographic profile was assessed afterward.
ai_technology: DOMINO Gaussian mixture; CLIP; BiomedCLIP; ResNet-50
organization: University of Bern; Bern University Hospital; Diabetes Center Berne; Technical University of Denmark; University of Tübingen; University of Lucerne

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, Results, Discussion example SG A0 and Methods including dataset, cluster fitting and classifier

evidence.tested: The authors fitted subgroup memberships on 22,263 validation images and then assigned an existing separate test partition. Real-world subgroup analyses were distinct from synthetic-artifact checks.
evidence.unknown: The subgroup is defined by the fitted model, with demographic enrichment assessed afterward. The low sensitivity is imprecise (0.103 ± 0.097, reported 95% Wilson uncertainty). Methods describes an image split and does not establish patient-disjointness. The study does not establish causal effects of BMI or sex or externally reproduced clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: A modified DOMINO Gaussian mixture learned image subgroups using pretrained CLIP or BiomedCLIP features and the predictions of a trained ResNet-50 cardiomegaly classifier. The mixture was fitted on the validation set and assigned memberships in the test set.

title: A paired venture screening study recorded lower analyst time for AI-assisted reports
summary: In a paired study of 20 applications at one investment firm, mean analyst time was 44.7 minutes for manual screening and 18.9 minutes for screening with GPT-6 Luna-assisted reports. Assisted time included verifying sources and making corrections. Seventy percent of reports needed at least one correction.
ai_technology: GPT-6 Luna; document interpretation and evidence-assisted scoring
organization: Queen’s University Belfast; Sapphire Capital Partners

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 timing and factual-support protocol and results, Appendix A model configuration, funding and ethics notes

evidence.tested: Each application was independently processed by both workflows, with a different analyst in each and roles counterbalanced. The analysts also adjudicated the factual support of 240 cited claims.
evidence.unknown: Two analysts affiliated with the participating fund completed the unblinded comparison. Each application was assessed by a different analyst in each workflow, so counterbalancing leaves analyst-by-workflow effects unresolved. The assisted time excludes unattended machine time. Decision quality and returns were outside this comparison.
evidence.ai_role: DealsFlow used GPT-6 Luna to extract and score supporting information from application documents and retrieved sources. Analysts then verified and corrected the resulting reports.

title: Simulations estimate how solvents affect excited biphenyl’s relaxation
summary: Using learned MACE potentials, simulations estimated excited-state torsional relaxation in unsubstituted biphenyl across nine solvents. Mean times to complete about 63% of the relaxation broadly increased with viscosity in six aprotic solvents, from 0.254 to 3.519 picoseconds. Three protic solvents fell below that trend. Earlier experiments reported a qualitatively similar pattern for a substituted molecule.
ai_technology: MACE interatomic potential; PULSES multi-agent workflow
organization: Emory University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 primary PDF Section 2.5, Figure 4 and supported solvent comparison

evidence.tested: The analysis used 48 trajectories per solvent. Held-out reference geometries gave force-prediction R² of 0.9721 on the excited-state surface. The solvent trend was evaluated from simulated threshold-crossing times.
evidence.unknown: The relationship rests on a single-surface simulation and a classical solvent representation. Relaxation times for this specific molecule were not independently measured in the study.
evidence.ai_role: Agent-trained MACE interatomic potentials supplied the excited-state solute forces for trajectory ensembles of unsubstituted biphenyl.

title: A stenosis detector was tested on an external coronary angiography cohort
summary: A learned detector using coronary-vessel features achieved AP@50 of 0.434 on 48 angiography images from 27 Oxford Acute Myocardial Infarction study patients. Test-time augmentation raised it to 0.480. Standard YOLOv11-L scored 0.339 without augmentation. These are lesion-localization scores from a small retrospective cohort.
ai_technology: Fusion-YOLOv11-L; UNet++; learned vessel segmentation and lesion detection
organization: University of Oxford; Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 date, Methods §2.1–2.4 and external test results, especially Table 5

evidence.tested: The study trained and tuned the model on ARCADE-derived data and assessed localization of 85 stenoses on separately sourced OxAMI frames.
evidence.unknown: The result covers selected end-diastolic frames and a small external sample. Patient-level diagnostic performance and clinical outcomes were outside this evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: Fusion-YOLOv11-L combined learned coronary-vessel segmentation features and lesion detection features to localize stenoses in angiography frames.

title: Language models trusted incorrect reassurances more than incorrect warnings in a defensive audit
summary: In tests of a prerecorded defensive audit dataset, incorrect reassurances moved language-model verdicts toward agreement more than incorrect warnings did. A prespecified check on seven additional model configurations found a mean asymmetry of 0.16, with a 95% interval of 0.10–0.24. This measures verdict behavior under controlled evaluation conditions.
ai_technology: DeepSeek; Qwen; GLM; Kimi audit models
organization: Seoul School of Integrated Sciences and Technologies; Liaoning Mechanical & Electrical College of Technology

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 Methods, experimental setup and §6.4 aggregate defensive behavior

evidence.tested: The study analyzed 16,572 evaluations on 916 matched pairs across eleven configurations. The seven-configuration confirmation used prerecorded samples and paired comparisons against valid evidence.
evidence.unknown: The confirmation was conducted by the same team. The data and decision conditions are controlled and do not measure real-world incidence.
evidence.ai_role: Eleven language model configurations independently evaluated prerecorded audit examples and supplied verdicts that were compared under paired evidence conditions.

title: Shared cell ancestry inflates apparent skill in a cell-response model
summary: In a retrospective audit of STATE, mean correlation on expected-null cases in one donor fell from 0.260 with reference cells sharing ancestry to 0.005 with independently sampled references, against 0.081 for a context-mean baseline. The model also fell below baseline with independent references in three additional donors. The finding concerns apparent predictive skill under the tested evaluation design.
ai_technology: STATE cell-response transfer model
organization: National University of Singapore

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, section 2.7, Figure 7, relative baseline comparison and non-operational evaluation of reported model outcomes

evidence.tested: The audit compared reference overlap conditions, with equal reference sample sizes and the same learned predictions. The primary quantitative comparison uses one donor, with follow-up STATE comparisons across four available donors.
evidence.unknown: This retrospective audit characterizes the tested data and model, with expected-null cases defined operationally. It does not measure biological benefit or imply all transfer estimates are inflated.
evidence.ai_role: The trained STATE transfer model generated cell-response estimates whose accuracy could be compared against overlapping and independent reference samples.

title: Chemistry helps flag stability disagreements in GNoME materials
summary: Within a selected subset of GNoME materials, a fitted ranking using composition and hull distance found 45.8% of the cases where two density functional workflows disagreed, compared with 40.4% for hull distance alone. Both figures use a 20% screening budget across held-out prototype-cluster splits. Either workflow’s verdict can differ from experimental stability.
ai_technology: GNoME; fitted logistic regression
organization: Accretion Labs

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, data provenance, Sections 3 and 4.12 and limitations

evidence.tested: The ranking comparison used 117,018 records initially labeled stable with 7,822 structural-prototype proxy clusters, repeated over 20 cluster splits. The target was a precomputed change in stability verdict.
evidence.unknown: The sample was selected for available recomputations. Relative ranking varied with chemistry and reference construction. Actual thermodynamic stability and out-of-catalog performance were untested.
evidence.ai_role: The audited population comes from GNoME candidate discovery. Fitted logistic regression used chemistry-cell disagreement rates and distance to the reference hull to rank candidates for review.

title: Learned light-curve templates date the observed phase of supernova Ares
summary: Gaussian-process light-curve templates estimated that the JWST spectrum of the lensed Type IIb supernova Ares was taken about 34 rest-frame days after peak brightness, with a reported 25–44 day interval. Fits to three nearby analogues gave similar estimates. The source’s classification and predicted future images came from separate spectroscopic and lens-model analyses.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process regression; learned light-curve templates
organization: Space Telescope Science Institute; Johns Hopkins University; University of Texas at Austin; Chiba University; University of Toronto; Princeton University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, Section V.2 Gaussian-process template learning and phase fit, spectroscopic cross-check

evidence.tested: The study fit photometry to three nearby Type IIb supernova templates and a population template. Its phase estimates were consistent with spectral comparisons within uncertainty.
evidence.unknown: The analysis covers one event. Population and individual templates share source observations, and spectroscopic estimates informed phase priors.
evidence.ai_role: Gaussian-process regression inferred continuous light-curve templates from observed local Type IIb supernovae. The astronomy team fitted SN Ares photometry to these learned templates.

title: Better classifier discrimination did not improve a defensive gateway’s recall
summary: In a replay of 25,000 labeled prompts, repairing a learned classifier increased its stand-alone AUC from 0.392 to 0.855, while recall for the complete defensive gateway fell from 80.67% to 80.34%. The repair and substitution experiments measured divergence between component and system performance.
ai_technology: DeBERTa-v3-small; BARBICAN defensive classification
organization: Iskenderun Technical University

source_review.scope: v1 defensive comparison with classifier and system outcomes

evidence.tested: The same benchmark corpus was evaluated under original and repaired conditions, with substitutions for additional comparisons.
evidence.unknown: The labels and operating conditions are benchmark specific and do not estimate field incidents. The recall drop occurred entirely in the synthetic subset, with no recall change across the four public corpora. A stronger substituted classifier elsewhere in the paper slightly improved recall, so this repair result does not establish a general inverse relationship between component quality and system performance.
evidence.ai_role: A quantized DeBERTa-v3-small classifier supplied learned verdicts in a layered defensive gateway.

title: Image scorers relied less on generated descriptions after reward training
summary: Replacing an image’s generated reasoning with a description of another image reduced the rank correlation with human ratings by 0.548 for base 7B Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct and by 0.084 after score-reward training on KADID-10k. The tested 32B model retained greater sensitivity to the swap. The experiment measures dependence on the generated words for these image-scoring tasks.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct; reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards
organization: University of Bristol; Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics; China University of Mining and Technology; City University of Hong Kong

source_review.scope: v1 model setup and §5 intervention table

evidence.tested: The paper compares base and score- or rank-reward models on standard image-quality datasets, using donor-chain substitution and other interventions.
evidence.unknown: The experiment tests observable descriptions and task performance. It does not establish reasoning mechanisms for other tasks or model families.
evidence.ai_role: Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct image scorers were trained with verifiable rewards and evaluated with reasoning descriptions swapped across images.

title: Masked patch training changes visual correspondence differently at different model sizes
summary: Under matched ImageNet-1K training, adding iBOT with its associated masking weakened patch correspondence in small and base Vision Transformers. Final-block patch matching improved by roughly 3.3 and 4.0 percentage points in the large and huge variants, while some local appearance details became harder to recover from deep features. These effects were measured with one training recipe.
ai_technology: DINO-style ViT-S/B/L/H; iBOT; fitted linear appearance probes
organization: National University of Singapore; Nanyang Technological University

source_review.scope: v1 training §3, patch and appearance diagnostics §4, Limitations

evidence.tested: Within each scale, the comparison toggled the iBOT branch and student masking. The position diagnostic used paired local and global crops. Separate linear probes assessed appearance.
evidence.unknown: Data volume, loss weight, training duration and specific diagnostics limit transfer to full-scale commercial checkpoints.
evidence.ai_role: Vision Transformers trained with and without iBOT supplied patch embeddings for crop matching and linear appearance decoding.

title: Controlled stimuli reveal motion information in video Transformer features
summary: Under controlled motion stimuli, a statistical test flagged 28.7% to 92.1% of final-layer coordinate axes across the tested video Transformers, with zero flags in the frame-by-frame DINOv2 control. The study measured co-variation with specified motion profiles. Activation interventions gave mixed evidence that the flagged features drove model decisions.
ai_technology: VideoMAE; V-JEPA2; TimeSformer; DINOv2; sparse autoencoders
organization: University of Chicago; Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago

source_review.scope: v1 Methods §3–4, Table 1 and Appendix F

evidence.tested: The authors evaluated final-layer coordinates and learned sparse features on designed visual stimuli, with multiple-comparison thresholds and an image-encoder comparison.
evidence.unknown: Positive tests indicate some temporal dependence under these stimuli and definitions. Rates do not measure pure temporal-feature prevalence or identify a mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Pretrained video Transformers provided learned features whose activation covariances were tested under controlled motion stimuli.

title: Actor–critic training showed a local reversal in model-size scaling
summary: In Craftax, a larger actor–critic model outperformed a smaller one at 10¹⁴ training FLOPs, fell behind at 3×10¹⁴ FLOPs, and regained its lead by 10¹⁵ FLOPs. The result shows a local departure from monotonic scaling for the tested policy models. The authors proposed a learning-dynamics explanation based on in-game achievements.
ai_technology: Actor–critic reinforcement learning; empirical compute scaling
organization: Google DeepMind

source_review.scope: v1 actor–critic setup, §4.4 and Figure 5

evidence.tested: The experiment trained model sizes across compute levels and examined the crossover alongside achievement frequencies.
evidence.unknown: The crossover concerns the evaluated sizes, training setup and game environment. The proposed explanation is observational.
evidence.ai_role: Trained actor–critic policies at different sizes and budgets generated behavior traces used to test local compute scaling.

title: World models understated changes in robot policy success across simulated scenes
summary: Seven learned world models understated the reference change in policy success in 400 of 420 comparisons across 60 paired RoboTwin settings. The authors re-estimated success at the paired endpoints with separate reference runs. Comparisons shared settings and some endpoints. The finding concerns the simulated scene pairs.
ai_technology: World models including Ctrl-World and Cosmos-Predict-2.5
organization: WorldFailBench research team

source_review.scope: v1 §3 benchmark construction, §4 setup and simulation-boundary comparisons, Figure 11

evidence.tested: Matching compared policy rollouts under selected paired scene variations with re-estimated reference simulator rates.
evidence.unknown: The pairs were selected to characterize transition boundaries. They are not a representative sample of robotics settings or a physical validation of those transitions. The paper does not specify author affiliations.
evidence.ai_role: World models including Ctrl-World and Cosmos-Predict-2.5 generated rollouts for policies evaluated on matched simulated setups.

title: GPT-4o’s gender associations for inattentive ADHD changed with cue wording
summary: In a controlled association task, female-associated responses for inattentive ADHD prompts fell from 80.4% with explicit gender categories to 38.5% with implicitly gendered names. The study measures GPT-4o’s choices under these prompt conditions. It did not test patient diagnosis or estimate ADHD prevalence.
ai_technology: GPT-4o; Context Association Test
organization: Aarhus University

source_review.scope: v1 cue-list methods, reference sample notes and Study 1 results

evidence.tested: The study compared explicit and name-based cue lists on researcher-written contexts, including a control category and an auxiliary clinical-sample proxy.
evidence.unknown: Effects may depend on the model, names and prompts. The clinical sample is selective and cannot establish true population prevalence.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4o assigned gendered associations to research prompts using differently expressed cues under a Context Association Test.

title: Matching global force left local interface laws unresolved in a learned model
summary: In a simulated three-fiber composite, matching the global force–displacement curve did not reliably recover the local interface laws, even when the reference and inverse fits used the same fixed learned constitutive prior. Adding local strain observations improved recovery of the known simulated reference. The study tests a conditional computational inference limit, without validation on physical specimens.
ai_technology: Physics-constrained neural constitutive model; fitted latent coordinates
organization: Northwestern University

source_review.scope: v1 Section 3 three-fiber simulation and Figures 24–29

evidence.tested: The authors held the learned constitutive network fixed and compared force-only, strain-only and combined inverse fits across 144 interface latent variables.
evidence.unknown: General force-based nonidentifiability and the value of local strain observations were known; novelty is limited to this prior-restricted conditional example. Synthetic reference data were generated within the same learned family, so robustness to an incorrect prior, physical specimens or untested geometries is not established. Numerical failure of a fit is not a formal impossibility proof.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained physics-constrained constitutive network represented local adhesion laws. Fitted latent variables enabled comparing different observation regimes under a consistent learned family.

title: Familiar physics persisted in video-model answers after simulated rules changed
summary: On matched questions about altered simulated dynamics, Qwen3.8-27B chose the incorrect Earth-normal answer on 94.76% of text-only trials and 63.69% when given ordered frames. Other model configurations showed different shifts.
ai_technology: Qwen3.8-27B; video-language models
organization: Fudan University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

source_review.scope: v1 model input conditions, reference definitions and Appendix H Table 8

evidence.tested: The authors varied visual evidence for the same questions. Nonanswers remained in the denominator and answer positions varied.
evidence.unknown: The results come from generated scenes and a prompted answer format.
evidence.ai_role: Video-language models infer altered physical rules from matched text and simulator frames.

title: A low-rank probe recovered motion-state information from frozen 3D features
summary: A fitted rank-eight probe on frozen π³X features reached 91.67% balanced accuracy when classifying whether token pairs shared a motion state. Shuffling training labels reduced balanced accuracy to 50.34%. The result is specific to this probe and these recordings.
ai_technology: π³X; fitted low-rank motion probe
organization: Technical University of Munich; Munich Center for Machine Learning; Obsphera

source_review.scope: v1 rank-restricted probing, Table 5 and Appendix D.3

evidence.tested: The test compared probes with matched or within-frame shuffled targets on YouTube-VOS validation pairs.
evidence.unknown: Semantic content and object identity can contribute to the signal. The test does not establish an intrinsic motion basis.
evidence.ai_role: Matched and shuffled motion labels trained low-rank quadratic probes on frozen π³X visual tokens.

title: A clinical de-identification model lost accuracy on intensive-care notes
summary: EdgeDeID, trained on synthetic notes, scored 0.478 F1 on 2,434 MIMIC intensive-care nursing notes, compared with 0.994 on 100 synthetic notes. A separately trained clinical text model scored 0.675 on the intensive-care set. The test corpora differ in writing style and annotation conventions.
ai_technology: EdgeDeID; Qwen3-0.6B; clinical entity recognition
organization: Sharif University of Technology; Mayo Clinic; Yale University

source_review.scope: v1 §4.1 and Table 4 external clinical-text evaluation

evidence.tested: External notes use replaced identifiers and human labels. The paper also reports an analysis limited to the 823 Safe Harbor spans.
evidence.unknown: The evaluation does not establish safe redaction or portability. Style and label differences both affect the synthetic-to-clinical comparison.
evidence.ai_role: Fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B detects surrogate identifiers in clinical notes.

title: Tasks solvable separately became harder in a shared recurrent model
summary: Across 100 artificial cognitive tasks, individually trained linear recurrent models solved 52 tasks, while a single flat linear recurrent model solved 14. Introducing task-specific features recovered individually solvable linear cases. The comparisons characterize the tested training setup.
ai_technology: Almost-linear RNNs; fitted hierarchical task features
organization: Ernst Strüngmann Institute; Goethe University Frankfurt

source_review.scope: v1 architecture, Figure 2 and §4.2

evidence.tested: The authors varied nonlinear capacity and separation of task parameters across a synthetic task battery and jointly trained subsets.
evidence.unknown: Training failure does not prove mathematical impossibility or establish human or animal learning effects.
evidence.ai_role: Almost-linear recurrent nets learned individual or jointly shared task dynamics under varied nonlinear capacity.

title: A trained optical processor reproduced functions with more harmonics than its input encoding
summary: A visible-light processor refined through reinforcement learning approximated a nine-harmonic function using an input encoding with four harmonics. The measured output reproduced regions of rapid oscillation as the scalar input changed. The result concerns the bandwidth of the processor’s input–output function.
ai_technology: Proximal policy optimization; learned diffractive optical decoder
organization: University of California, Los Angeles; California NanoSystems Institute

source_review.scope: v1 visible-light experiment, in situ PPO and Figure 7

evidence.tested: The authors initialized the physical decoder from optical simulation, refined it from measured responses and compared its output with the target function.
evidence.unknown: The physical test covers designed target functions on a finite input range. Deviations remain near sharp peaks and low signal amplitudes.
evidence.ai_role: A trainable diffractive decoder initialized by optical simulation was refined in hardware with PPO using measured responses.

title: Sales agents applied policies more reliably in static probes than interactive tasks
summary: In controlled sales scenarios based on the same policies as static questions, eight language-model backbones showed 89.9–99.1% compliance on the static probes and 3.0–17.3% on interactive tasks. Scoring the actions also required a verified safe ending, so the gap reflects several differences between conditions.
ai_technology: Qwen3-8B and other language-agent backbones; paired static and interactive evaluation
organization: Tsinghua University; Futura Lab, Futura.AI

source_review.scope: v1 Methods, confirmatory benchmark experiment and stated measurement limitations

evidence.tested: The confirmatory study included 21,888 runs over 19 semantic cores and 12 configurations. The comparison of ranges covers the eight backbone configurations.
evidence.unknown: The scripted Chinese-language setting and stricter action criteria limit interpretation. The gap does not estimate an effect of sales pressure or real deployment failure rates. The semantic violation scorer had no released human-calibration accuracy estimate, and shared provider-family judging was not ruled out; its hard-violation flags materially influence action scores.
evidence.ai_role: Eight language-model backbones reason about sales policies and choose actions in matched scripted interactions.

title: Interface-name checks rejected some AI-written code that passed behavioral tests
summary: In a post hoc analysis of AI-written code, 19 of 36 artifacts rejected solely for dropping leading underscores from parameter names passed the original hidden behavioral checks after only that name-comparison rule was bypassed. The original study kept those artifacts recorded as contract failures. The selection covers one specific failure reason in the study’s coding tasks.
ai_technology: Claude Opus 5.5; Qwen3-Coder; Nemotron Cascade 2
organization: Independent researcher

source_review.scope: v1 §§9.3–9.4 coding delegation and post hoc hidden-test diagnostic

evidence.tested: A secondary offline diagnostic applied selected generated artifacts unchanged to fresh task copies, bypassing only strict parameter-name comparison, then ran the original sealed behavioral checks. No parent review or end-to-end acceptance was replayed.
evidence.unknown: This selected subset cannot estimate overall pass rates or establish that contract requirements were unnecessary in deployment. Original saved records were private and not independently auditable; passing these author-supplied checks does not prove general software correctness.
evidence.ai_role: Existing language models acting as coding workers generated artifacts assessed under an interface contract and hidden behavioral tests.

title: Simulated robots sometimes completed tasks while violating safety requirements
summary: In controlled simulations across six manipulation tasks, 82 valid executions completed their tasks while violating at least one separately checked safety rule. The tests evaluated learned ACT and RDT control policies under deliberately introduced faults. Counts refer to simulated executions in a focused test campaign.
ai_technology: ACT; RDT robotic manipulation policies; EAST digital-twin testing
organization: Macau University of Science and Technology; Beihang University; University of Nottingham Ningbo China; Swinburne University of Technology

source_review.scope: v1 design, independent runtime outcome checks, equal-budget campaigns and unsafe-success results

evidence.tested: Five campaigns used the simulator to verify that test conditions occurred and evaluated task completion separately from predefined safety requirements.
evidence.unknown: The cases may share tasks and scenarios. This fault-focused simulation does not estimate physical incident rates. Earlier safety benchmarks already reported successful-but-unsafe robot trajectories; this result is a further specific policy/task validation, not discovery of that general gap.
evidence.ai_role: Two learned manipulation policy families, ACT and RDT, produced execution traces in which task completion and predefined safety rules were evaluated separately.

title: Language models flagged missing evidence less often when an unsupported premise was usable
summary: In paired arithmetic tasks, making an unsupported premise usable reduced missing-evidence flags by 8–30 percentage points across four tested language models. The source support was unchanged. Some answers may reflect conditional reasoning because the instructions did not require rejection of premises supplied in the question.
ai_technology: Gemma and Qwen language models
organization: Google

source_review.scope: v1 Methods, paired premise design, §4 and Limitations

evidence.tested: The controlled factorial design varied actionability and the mention of relevant entities on GSM8K. All 16 primary paired contrasts survived Holm adjustment.
evidence.unknown: The selected tasks and instructions limit how broadly the result applies. It does not show that all answers accept unsupported statements as facts. Pattern-based scoring was revised after a 40-response audit; residual condition-dependent scoring error was not bounded by that small check.
evidence.ai_role: Four pretrained Gemma and Qwen language models answered mathematically matched prompts with equally unsupported premises that varied in usability.

title: A learned prover exposed ambiguous translations of unique-answer math problems
summary: A learned prover found two distinct Lean-accepted answers for 5.4% of the tested formal statements pooled across three autoformalizers. The original problems had unique answers, so these examples expose a mismatch between the formal statements and their intended problems.
ai_technology: Gobble-Prover 1.7B and 4B; Lean 4
organization: University of California, Riverside

source_review.scope: v1 Methods, unique-answer argument, Appendix D Table 5

evidence.tested: The audit combined evidence from two learned provers across three autoformalizers and five contest problem datasets. Lean checked acceptance of distinct answers.
evidence.unknown: The detected rate is a lower bound for these tested versions. A translation can be wrong in ways this multiple-answer test does not flag.
evidence.ai_role: Gobble-Prover models generated verifiable proof terms for numerical candidates under independently autoformalized competition problems.

title: Successful human puzzle players voiced qualitative explanations more often than language agents
summary: In an ARC-AGI-3 trajectory study, qualitative descriptions appeared in 72 of 144 successful human runs and 17 of 119 successful runs from three agent systems. The human data came from think-aloud recordings and the model data from agent traces. The comparison measures recorded descriptions in successfully completed games.
ai_technology: GPT-5.6 Sol assisted analysis; ARC-AGI-3 agent traces
organization: Nanyang Technological University; Technical University of Darmstadt; Basis Research Institute; Harvard University; Cornell University

source_review.scope: v1 annotation workflow, participant selection, Section 4 trajectory results

evidence.tested: The authors collected 144 human trajectories across 64 participants and 25 games, collected 250 publicly released model trajectories, and analyzed successful subsets. They spot-checked parts of the model-assisted annotation.
evidence.unknown: Differences in what humans say aloud and what agents write or log limit claims about underlying cognitive representations.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5.6 Sol implemented trigger detectors and annotated cognition from aligned transcripts and game traces. Learned agent trajectories supplied matched-task comparison material.

title: An intrinsically trained fly model matched an observed future-turn signal
summary: Among 20 intrinsic learning objectives, DIAYN produced virtual fly policies that most closely matched the relationship between neural and behavioral prediction of future turns in prior fruit-fly recordings. The comparison evaluated signals 15 to 8 seconds before a turn. It supports a computational model of the observed behavior.
ai_technology: DIAYN; NeuroMechFly; elastic-net logistic decoding
organization: University of Maryland, College Park; Carnegie Mellon University

source_review.scope: v1 policy comparison, prospective decoding Figure 3 and Results

evidence.tested: The researchers held the digital embodiment and comparison assay consistent while varying intrinsic learning objectives and comparing frozen policies with prior aggregate observations.
evidence.unknown: The behavior and neural comparisons test a simulated model. They do not establish that live flies optimize the same objective. The comparison selected among 20 objectives and seven candidate internal representations; decoder hyperparameters were tuned on the biological data. Agreement is not an untouched validation of a uniquely identified biological objective.
evidence.ai_role: DIAYN and other learned intrinsic-motivation algorithms train hierarchical policies. Fitted elastic-net decoders compare future-turn information in the models and prior fly recordings.

title: Later attention queries rescued selected early-loop retrieval errors
summary: Moving same-item later-loop attention queries into the first loop corrected 89.8% and 96.9% of selected synthetic two-hop errors in two Ouro models. Queries shuffled between items corrected 23.7% and 20.6%, respectively. The result applies to questions answered incorrectly in the first loop and correctly later.
ai_technology: Ouro-1.4B; Ouro-2.6B; activation transplantation
organization: University of British Columbia

source_review.scope: v1 query swap Methods, Table 2 and natural-question caveats

evidence.tested: The primary synthetic test included 600 scenes per model, with 245 and 223 qualifying early-loop errors, respectively. Same-item and shuffled queries were compared at aligned positions.
evidence.unknown: Natural-question rescue was smaller and did not establish bridge redirection. A positional contribution remains possible. In Ouro-1.4B the rescue changes four-candidate ranking, not greedy generated answers. The intervention supplies a separate query at every layer/head, not one vector; the two model sizes share developmental history.
evidence.ai_role: The authors intervened on pretrained Ouro attention query activations and compared matched late-loop and shuffled donors.

title: An audit found errors in screened AI-extracted electro-optic values
summary: A curated-reference audit found that 30 of 112 electro-optic records extracted with GPT-4o and accepted by automated checks were defective. Errors included incorrect tensor components, units and measurement conditions. The audit covered three selected legacy papers and does not estimate error rates for the full database.
ai_technology: GPT-4o; materials literature extraction
organization: New Jersey Institute of Technology; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

source_review.scope: primary v1-only PDF §§3 and 5.2, production audit and source comparison

evidence.tested: The audit reviewed records already accepted by the extraction pipeline against curated source information and physical consistency checks.
evidence.unknown: These papers were selected as a stress test. Different formats and data complexity could yield different error rates.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4o extracted reported electro-optic property values and contexts from primary documents for database construction.

title: Inferring driver intent increased aligned steering assistance in a simulator study
summary: In an urban driving simulator, 8 of 11 participants with paired observations received more steering assistance aligned with their intent under the intent-conditioned policy. Collisions occurred in 4 of 147 intent-conditioned trials, 10 of 130 trials with assistance lacking intent inference, and 2 of 121 unassisted trials.
ai_technology: Dream2Assist; recurrent state-space world model; reinforcement learning
organization: Toyota Research Institute

source_review.scope: v1 urban simulator human study, §6.4 objective results and preliminary on-vehicle scope

evidence.tested: Participants experienced within-subject simulator trials under intent-conditioned, non-intent, and unassisted conditions in randomized order. Physical driving was only a preliminary deployment.
evidence.unknown: Trial counts are repeated within people and collisions were concentrated among a few participants. The measurements do not establish an on-road safety benefit.
evidence.ai_role: A trained recurrent world model infers driver intent and conditions the assistance policy. The same architectural comparator omits the intent predictor.

title: Agents reversed fewer correct judgments when they recorded evidence before feedback
summary: Across 75 passing draft evaluations, five Gemini models reversed a correct decision in 41 standard trials and 34 trials when the models wrote a claim checklist after feedback. The full pre-feedback checklist condition recorded 9 reversals. The test used a fixed set of deliberately mistaken critiques.
ai_technology: Gemini language models; controlled claim and feedback ordering
organization: Google

source_review.scope: v1 controlled Turn-2 report review, §4.3 Table 3 and evaluation limits

evidence.tested: A controlled report-review study compared the order of evidential self-assessment and feedback, with 20 scenarios per model and separate cases containing valid correction.
evidence.unknown: Scenario and model dependence matter: the same scenarios were reused and the benchmark uses selected passing or flawed drafts.
evidence.ai_role: Five Gemini models reevaluated their reports, with the timing of recording earlier claims varied around identical mistaken criticism.

title: Layers important to LoRA adaptation varied across tasks
summary: In an intervention study on fine-tuned Qwen2.5-0.5B, the seven layers most important to adaptation had a mean pairwise overlap of 39.5% by the Jaccard measure across four tasks. Only the first three layers appeared in every top-seven list.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-0.5B; low-rank adaptation; activation path patching
organization: East China Normal University; Brunel University of London

source_review.scope: Qwen2.5-0.5B four-dataset path-patching Methods and Figure 3

evidence.tested: The intervention compares layer-level learned contributions, then ranks the layers separately for the four task datasets.
evidence.unknown: The overlap depends on selected datasets, model, rankings and layer cutoff. It does not establish identical sparsity across architectures.
evidence.ai_role: Path patching intervened on learned LoRA activations to measure each layer’s contribution on four datasets.

title: Judge-labeled invalid coding traces were longer in two related models
summary: Code-generation reasoning traces labeled invalid by a model-judge ensemble averaged 17,163 tokens for DeepSeek-R1-0528, compared with 7,102 for valid-labeled traces. Its distilled 8B variant showed the same direction. These labels concern reasoning coherence and are explicitly distinct from whether the final code passes functional tests.
