ai_technology: DeepSeek-R1-0528; DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University

source_review.scope: v1 task/model setup, trace taxonomy and §§4.1–4.2 differences by outcome

evidence.tested: Researchers collected traces under matched prompting and decoding. Three model judges each rated trace validity three times; confidence-weighted votes labeled high-confidence cases and two human annotators adjudicated the remainder. The reported length contrast groups these trace-validity labels, not final code correctness.
evidence.unknown: Validity judgments include coherence and unnecessary detours, which may themselves relate to trace length; the contrast does not establish a causal effect of long reasoning or a functional-code failure rate. The models share a lineage, selected complete traces exclude incomplete or unparsable responses, and verbal traces need not faithfully reflect internal reasoning.
evidence.ai_role: DeepSeek R1 models generated traces; DeepSeek-V3.2, Gemini-3-Flash and GLM-5.1 judged their validity, while learned semantic annotators classified reasoning actions.

title: Calibrated spin models better matched a measured diamond ensemble spectrum
summary: For a measured zero-field nitrogen-vacancy ensemble spectrum, calibrating effective spin-model terms reduced held-frequency error from 0.008835 to 0.003872 across four folds. The source models were learned from single-center spectra, and both comparisons fitted the same linewidth and optical-readout terms.
ai_technology: Symbolic regression; learned effective spin Hamiltonians
organization: University of New South Wales; Cryo-X Tech; Xidian University

source_review.scope: primary v1-only PDF learned source models and Section IV experimental ensemble fits

evidence.tested: The authors used a matched comparison across held frequencies in a 38-point experimental scan and froze each learned source expression before fitting the target ensemble.
evidence.unknown: Other effective compositions can produce comparable spectra, so this does not uniquely determine microscopic parameters. The independent field-condition test reported elsewhere in the paper uses simulation.
evidence.ai_role: Constrained symbolic regression selected and fitted spin Hamiltonian models from measured single-center spectra. The models formed the starting point for ensemble calibration.

title: Language models missed more requirements with little wording in common with the final request
summary: Across 405 CL-bench Life tasks, direct answers from four language models passed 67.4% of rubric criteria with low wording overlap with the final request, compared with 81.1% of higher-overlap criteria. The analysis uses word overlap as a proxy and does not establish that wording alone caused the difference.
ai_technology: GPT-6 Luna; Kimi K3; Grok 4.7; GLM-5
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Macao Polytechnic University; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University

source_review.scope: v1 CL-bench Life task corpus description, lexical rubric groups and direct-answer results

evidence.tested: The study grouped 5,333 classifiable rubric criteria by overlap with the final request. The evaluators assessed individual outputs under the benchmark rubric.
evidence.unknown: Groups can differ in underlying difficulty and scoring criteria. Rubrics are nested within tasks, and the result does not establish effects in live workflows.
evidence.ai_role: Four frozen language models generated corpus-task answers. A rubric judge scored outputs from the same benchmark before testing the proposed harness.

title: Parkinson’s connectivity retrieval found similarly mixed neighbors for cases and controls
summary: Among 40 participants in the TaoWu cohort, the ten closest matches in a learned connectivity representation were 79.5% Parkinson’s cases for diagnosed participants and 81.0% for controls, on average. The source pool included 139 people with Parkinson’s among 169 participants. Retrieval did not consistently improve classification beyond pretraining alone.
ai_technology: Graph convolutional autoencoder; functional-connectivity retrieval
organization: Carl von Ossietzky University of Oldenburg

source_review.scope: v1 cohort Methods, Table 1 and Figure 2 controls; PDF author affiliation

evidence.tested: A frozen encoder was trained on external cohorts. The researchers summarized matched neighbor labels and compared prediction variants using repeated cross-validation in the separate TaoWu cohort.
evidence.unknown: The study is small and the source lookup is label-imbalanced. Same-fold checkpoint selection and cohort differences limit interpretation of classification metrics.
evidence.ai_role: A graph convolutional autoencoder learned functional-connectivity embeddings from 169 external individuals. Neighbor identities and a downstream classifier evaluated a separate 40-person sample.

title: Rank compression followed delayed generalization in tested Transformers
summary: In 29 one-layer Transformer runs that developed delayed generalization on modular arithmetic, the steepest effective-rank drop followed the rise in test accuracy by about 900 training steps. In a separate intervention, restricting embedding rank prevented delayed generalization in 15 of 20 runs.
ai_technology: One-layer Transformers; rank-constrained training
organization: Lossfunk

source_review.scope: v1 one-layer Transformer results, rank intervention and Appendix E

evidence.tested: The paper used a predefined test-accuracy threshold and compared rank restrictions with factorized full-rank models across seeds.
evidence.unknown: Results concern small arithmetic models. Timing and intervention findings do not exclude other roles for representation compression in other training regimes.
evidence.ai_role: Trained modular-arithmetic Transformers and matched factorized controls serve as instruments for evaluating weight rank and generalization timing.

title: An AI-assisted audit found eight maintainer-confirmed software regressions
summary: An audit of 1,459 merged pull requests in four Python projects used language models to generate behavior checks. The study found nine reproducible regression candidates, of which eight were confirmed by maintainers. The result concerns a targeted software audit.
ai_technology: ORION; learned test generation and behavioral oracles
organization: Beihang University; National University of Singapore

source_review.scope: v1 ORION design and §V-E real-world regression evaluation

evidence.tested: ORION flagged 28 requests. The authors retained and manually reviewed currently reproducible warnings before submitting nine candidates for maintainer confirmation.
evidence.unknown: The reviewers did not comprehensively assess unflagged changes, so recall and general defect rates are unknown. This is not a count of security vulnerabilities.
evidence.ai_role: ORION uses a learned model to infer intended software behavior and generate checks for regression candidates in existing projects.

title: AI reviewers favored confident wording in matched research papers
summary: In a 504-paper experiment, all six model reviewers more often gave higher scores to rewrites with confident wording. Claude Sonnet 4.6 favored the confident version in 40% of pairs and the less confident version in 6%, with 54% tied. Researchers checked text similarity and wording shifts before comparing evaluations.
ai_technology: Claude Sonnet 4.6; GPT-5.5; Gemini; Gemma; Qwen; GLM
organization: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security; German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence; University of Technology Nuremberg; Inria

source_review.scope: v1 paired rewrite checks and 504-paper comparative review experiment, Table 4

evidence.tested: Each model independently evaluated one rewrite at a time for each pair under standardized review instructions. The study checked style manipulation and content similarity on the rewritten manuscripts.
evidence.unknown: Rewriting can introduce small uncontrolled meaning changes. The experiment concerns model scores and does not measure actual conference decisions.
evidence.ai_role: Language models generated matched high- and low-confidence prose variants and six model reviewers independently scored the rewritten versions.

title: Symbolic regression fitted a finite-Reynolds-number correction for turbulent velocity profiles
summary: A data-fitted expression adjusted the outer wake contribution in zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers as Reynolds number varied. The mean-velocity relation was compared with 35 simulation and experiment profiles across friction Reynolds numbers from 252 to 72,526. Its high-Reynolds-number limit was imposed during modeling.
ai_technology: PySR; physics-constrained symbolic regression
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Northwestern Polytechnical University

source_review.scope: v1 reference datasets, symbolic-regression implementation and Sections 4.1–4.2

evidence.tested: The authors identified the fitted correction from specified direct- and large-eddy-simulation profiles and compared the relation with other profiles including experimental datasets.
evidence.unknown: Out-of-fit profiles were not an independent statistical validation set. The limiting value is a design constraint, and reported data sources differ in the outer layer.
evidence.ai_role: PySR fit near-wall and finite-Reynolds-number corrections under prescribed physical asymptotes.

title: A vision-assisted drone tracked moving pipes in a physical test
summary: In a physical moving-pipe test, a small drone using learned visual label detection and a model-predictive controller recorded 6.73% average tracking error, compared with 15.13% under a standard PID controller. The study compared control methods in a bounded experimental rig.
ai_technology: YOLOv5; learned visual label detection; model predictive control
organization: Northwestern Polytechnical University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University

source_review.scope: v1 learned perception Methods and matched Tello experiments, Table III

evidence.tested: The study used a Tello drone to compare controller behavior in three lab scenarios, with camera-based detection feeding position estimates.
evidence.unknown: This tests the integrated labeled setup under controlled conditions and does not establish field inspection reliability or collision reduction.
evidence.ai_role: YOLOv5 detects visual pipe labels so that both feedback designs can estimate relative position.

title: Both driving models detected the other vehicle before most simulated collisions
summary: On the NeuroNCAP simulator, object tracking met the study’s detection criterion before 95.9% of DiffusionDrive’s collisions and 95.8% of SparseDrive’s collisions. The audit distinguished missed actors from collision episodes in which the learned detection system had tracked the actor.
ai_technology: DiffusionDrive and SparseDrive, learned vehicle detection and planning
organization: University of Stuttgart; Mercedes-Benz

source_review.scope: §IV.A–B, Table I and front matter

evidence.tested: The authors separated stock-model simulation episodes by collision outcome and by whether vehicle tracking met a prespecified analysis criterion.
evidence.unknown: The result depends on the simulator, models and tracking definition. The presence of a detection does not identify the cause of an individual crash or establish road performance.
evidence.ai_role: The learned perception systems provided the actor tracks compared with closed-loop simulation outcomes.

title: Eight learned streamflow models underestimated peak days in a basin audit
summary: A 162-basin evaluation found median peak-day biases of 27% to 44% below observed flow across eight learned models, versus 13% below for the National Water Model. The learned models also underestimated peak days in a broader analysis of 1,139 basins.
ai_technology: LSTM, GRU, EA-LSTM and five other learned streamflow models
organization: Rutgers University; Apple; University of Alabama; University of Maryland

source_review.scope: §§3–4.2, Tables 1–2 and front matter

evidence.tested: Models trained through water year 2010 were scored against recorded streamflow over 2011–2022. Bias was summarized over basins.
evidence.unknown: Model tuning and inputs were constrained. The external National Water Model used its developers’ calibration, which may overlap the test period. Flow estimates at extremes carry observational uncertainty.
evidence.ai_role: Eight models learned mappings from weather history and basin attributes to daily streamflow; their held-out errors revealed the common peak-day deficit.

title: Tactile guidance improved immediate racket-skill ratings in a randomized study
summary: After ten minutes of practice, 12 learners given contact and motion guidance improved by 0.72 levels on a four-level expert rating scale. Twelve learners who received only proficiency-level feedback gained 0.05 levels. The difference was 0.67 levels (95% confidence interval 0.39 to 0.98).
ai_technology: GNN–LSTM pose estimator; graph-informed drive–grip encoder and decoder
organization: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

source_review.scope: Front matter; hand–racket reconstruction, control organization, mechanism-guided learning, and Supplementary Notes 14–16

evidence.tested: A separate cohort of 24 was randomly assigned to equal-duration practice. Three experts rated shuffled before-and-after clips without labels identifying the group or assessment time.
evidence.unknown: This small study evaluated immediate changes on five racket skills. Durability and transfer to match play were unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: A learned pose estimator reconstructed contact geometry from tactile input. Learned control representations and regional analysis informed feedback on how each learner’s contact and timing differed from an expert reference.

title: A certified input extends a lower bound for qubit-channel capacity
summary: An AI-assisted search found a 45-qubit input with positive coherent information at per-Pauli error probability 0.064966. The author used the prior certifier unchanged, extending the earlier certified point of 0.064956. This gives a lower bound for where the depolarizing channel can transmit quantum information.
ai_technology: Claude Sonnet 5.5; Infinity Machine research agent
organization: Harish Santhanalakshmi Ganesan, independent researcher

source_review.scope: Zenodo v1 exact-certificate deposit and metadata; Infinity Machine §3.2 and Appendix A.1; prior certified bound

evidence.tested: Exact arithmetic enclosed coherent information between 2.31 and 2.78 × 10⁻⁸ bits. The total Pauli error probability is three times the per-Pauli probability.
evidence.unknown: The bound applies to the supplied input. The optimal threshold is unknown, and the cited author check does not establish independent confirmation.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Sonnet 5.5 wrote and ran an optimizer starting with an earlier witness. The human operator supplied the task, seed and verification tools.

title: Language-model safety probes transferred despite shifts in learned directions
summary: Across four language-model families, the directions fitted to separate benign and harmful requests shifted by about 17° to 35° after distillation or instruction tuning. Applying the base probes unchanged shifted AUC by −0.011 to +0.027 on XSTest and −0.015 to +0.053 on an independent prompt set.
ai_technology: Fitted linear activation probes; Qwen2.5, Llama 3.1 and distilled DeepSeek-R1 variants
organization: Independent researcher Marios Tsatsos

source_review.scope: §§3–6, Appendix B and front matter

evidence.tested: Linear classifiers trained on the four base models were evaluated unchanged on two matched successors per family. Transfer was compared with the same probe’s performance on the base model.
evidence.unknown: Similar observed accuracy does not establish equivalence, and XSTest fold intervals are too narrow. On OR-Bench the probes flagged 29% to 42% of benign prompts that sounded harmful.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted activation classifiers estimated directions and classification performance on base and successor models. Their transfer separated change in direction from change in discrimination.

title: Claude Fable produced a quadratic-query algorithm for a hidden cycle problem
summary: Claude Fable 5.1 designed a solver for CycleUncover, a black-box problem that hides an even cycle in a bitstring fitness function. The solver reconstructs a two-coloring from fitness queries. Lean checked the expected O(n²) query bound, while the paper proves an exponential bound for the classical (1+1) evolutionary algorithm on this problem.
ai_technology: Claude Fable 5.1; staged algorithm design and Lean proof generation
organization: University of Birmingham

source_review.scope: §5.2/Theorem 5.1, Table 2, Appendices E and F.7 and front matter

evidence.tested: The authors defined the hidden-cycle oracle and supplied a staged formal framework. Their report gives a Lean-checked bound for the generated algorithm and a separate lower-bound argument for the comparator.
evidence.unknown: This result concerns one constructed oracle family. It neither establishes that the bound is optimal nor demonstrates empirical speed or general maximum independent-set efficiency.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Fable proposed the oracle-query solver and produced the formal expected-query proof under the supplied framework.

title: Distilled equations predicted instability in simulated multi-planet systems
summary: Researchers distilled a neural network trained on three-planet simulations into compact equations for orbital instability time. Tested on previously simulated five-planet systems, the equations captured changes of orders of magnitude near strong orbital resonances. A systematic error remained for closely spaced planets.
ai_technology: Sparse neural feature learning; PySR symbolic regression
organization: Cornell University; MIT; Harvey Mudd College; University of Cambridge

source_review.scope: Model equations, Results, Figures 2–4, Appendices A–C and physical interpretation

evidence.tested: The equation used sparse statistics from short numerical integrations. It was tested on held-out three-planet simulations and on an existing five-planet grid under a neighboring-trio approximation.
evidence.unknown: The five-planet grid used equal masses and circular coplanar orbits. Results are approximate predictions of simulated dynamics, with compressed prediction ranges and no observational validation.
evidence.ai_role: The network learned sparse combinations of orbital elements. PySR converted its predicted instability times into closed-form expressions over those learned variables.

title: Newly appearing links concentrated around hubs in three news narratives
summary: In language-model maps of coverage of three news events, 44% to 51% of next-day emerging links touched an entity in the top tenth by network degree. A ranking based on endpoint degree beat a historical-link baseline on these emerging links, and the margin shrank when high-degree entities were removed.
ai_technology: Claude Haiku, GPT-4.1 and Gemini semantic edge extraction
organization: Arizona State University

source_review.scope: §§3–5, Figures 8–9 and front matter

evidence.tested: The retrospective comparison covered the Canadian Freedom Convoy, Hurricane Melissa and the 2025–26 Iranian protests. It used rolling windows and three separate language-model extractors.
evidence.unknown: The graphs use model-extracted relations without human gold labels. Candidate negatives were sampled randomly, favoring degree-based rankings. The result describes links represented in coverage of three events.
evidence.ai_role: Language models resolved references and extracted semantic relations from each article, which supplied the networks used to quantify where next-day links appeared.

title: A confidence probe rose on repeated wrong answers in Qwen2.5
summary: A probe trained to read answer correctness from first-turn activations gave higher scores when Qwen2.5-7B repeated an incorrect answer. On questions held out from probe training, scores rose by about 0.32 after either a re-ask or agreement. Other confidence measures disagreed, and the pattern did not reproduce consistently across tested models.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-7B and other language models; fitted linear activation probe
organization: Hanoi University of Science and Technology

source_review.scope: §§3 and 5–8, held-out grouped analysis, and front matter

evidence.tested: A frozen first-turn probe was compared against three other confidence measures. The post hoc check refitted the probe in five folds grouped by question and compared it with probes fit to shuffled labels.
evidence.unknown: The strongest result concerns short-answer tasks in Qwen2.5-7B. A cleaned Llama-3 analysis provided support; four other models failed to reproduce the pattern consistently. Probe scores do not directly measure belief.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted linear readout made it possible to compare answer-related signals from learned model activations with confidence estimates from the same dialogue.

title: Pose errors became easier to read after two vision models fused their views
summary: On 903 valid difficult image pairs, linear probes distinguished VGGT pose errors with an AUC of 0.935 from its late features and about 0.65 from its per-image encoder. A second reconstruction model showed a similar layer pattern. The signal emerged after the networks began combining information across views.
ai_technology: VGGT; π³; fitted linear activation probes
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison; Chalmers University of Technology

source_review.scope: §§3–5, Figure 3 and Tables 3–4

evidence.tested: The probes used frozen activation features and category-held-out evaluation, with shuffled-label and image-size controls. The authors also compared predictions with confidence outputs and tested transfer to other datasets.
evidence.unknown: The pairs were deliberately hard and the failure signal varied with dataset and rotation versus translation errors. Layer profiles show decodable information; they do not establish the causal computation or improvements in multi-view reconstruction.
evidence.ai_role: Linear predictors fitted to features at successive layers measured where information about pose failure became available.

title: Vision models often encoded the same concept change differently across contexts
summary: Across 46 vision encoders, the direction for a change such as dry to wet was detectable within individual visual contexts much more often than across them: 97.8% versus 18.3% of the compared cases in that example. The contrast varied substantially by concept.
ai_technology: Pretrained vision encoders including ViT; learned embedding representations and fitted probes
organization: University of Tübingen; KAIST

source_review.scope: §§3–5, Table 1 and probe-transfer analysis

evidence.tested: The authors matched image embeddings for ten concept families, then compared within-context and cross-context direction consistency against random baselines. They also tested linear probe transfer across contexts.
evidence.unknown: Matching approximates changes in one concept using images that may differ in other ways. Detection rates depend on the chosen concepts, contexts, models, direction metric and statistical controls.
evidence.ai_role: Learned vision embeddings supplied concept-transition vectors for within- and cross-context tests, and fitted probes tested whether aligned directions predicted transfer.

title: Two model-screened magnesium alloy routes passed tensile tests
summary: A model-screened magnesium alloy containing gadolinium and yttrium reached 296 MPa yield strength and 398 MPa tensile strength in lab tests. A separate route using recycled feedstock produced AZ31 with similar mechanical properties to its primary-feedstock comparison. The study estimated 40.4% lower operating costs and 88.9% lower emissions for that route.
ai_technology: Physics-informed ensemble of random forests and XGBoost
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials

source_review.scope: Primary v1 PDF front matter, ensemble training, Methods, and experimental validation in Figures 3–4

evidence.tested: The study screened composition and microstructure candidates, selected two routes and tested prepared materials with tensile measurements and microstructural characterization.
evidence.unknown: The cost and emissions figures are modeled for the study’s feedstock and process assumptions. The two lab-scale cases do not establish production-scale performance or savings.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted ensemble predicted strength and linked candidate microstructures to processing routes, supporting selection of the two experimentally tested alloys.

title: A Golay logical-zero circuit uses 44 two-qubit gates in six layers
summary: An AI-assisted search found a circuit that prepares the logical-zero state of the 23-qubit Golay code with 44 two-qubit gates and two-qubit depth six. The author checked it by stabilizer algebra and full-state simulation. A previously posted 44-gate circuit used seven two-qubit layers under its stated labeling convention.
ai_technology: Claude Sonnet 5.5; Infinity Machine research agent
organization: Harish Santhanalakshmi Ganesan, independent researcher

source_review.scope: Zenodo v1 author's circuit record; Infinity Machine §3.2 and Appendix A.4; earlier QuSynth table and September circuit

evidence.tested: The checks compare the output state with the target up to wire relabeling. The controlled-Z gates are equivalent to CNOTs up to free one-qubit Clifford gates in this comparison.
evidence.unknown: The result assumes unrestricted connectivity and no extra qubits. It does not establish a depth or gate-count optimum, fault-tolerant preparation, or hardware performance.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Sonnet 5.5 wrote a search program and found the circuit starting from a published depth-eight seed supplied by the operator.

title: A two-dimensional qutrit input extends positive coherent information
summary: A numerical search found an input for the qutrit depolarizing channel that the author reduced to a uniformly mixed state on two of its three levels. An interval calculation placed the zero of its coherent information near 0.2910672 in the channel’s mixing parameter. The full three-level mixed input’s hashing point is about 0.287087.
ai_technology: Claude Sonnet 5.5; Infinity Machine research agent
organization: Harish Santhanalakshmi Ganesan, independent researcher

source_review.scope: Zenodo v1 interval-certificate note metadata; Infinity Machine §3.2 and Appendix A.2; earlier qudit capacity study

evidence.tested: The author derived a single-use formula for the rank-two input and numerically certified the zero. Positive coherent information gives an achievable lower bound on capacity.
evidence.unknown: The reported point is a lower bound rather than an optimal capacity threshold. The author notes that the observation may be previously known and makes no priority claim.
evidence.ai_role: A Claude Sonnet 5.5 proposer ran a numerical search that found a two-qutrit state. The human operator identified its factorization into two rank-two single-use inputs and supplied the closed-form analysis.

title: An AI-guided TESS search flagged a planet candidate around G 249-11
summary: An agent-guided search of archived TESS observations found repeating dips around the nearby red dwarf G 249-11 at a period of about 5.31 days. An ephemeris fitted to two sectors predicted dips in two held-out sectors. If the signal comes from a planet, its fitted radius is about 1.6 times Earth’s.
ai_technology: Claude Sonnet 5.5; Infinity Machine research agent
organization: Harish Santhanalakshmi Ganesan, independent researcher

source_review.scope: Zenodo v1 author research note record; Infinity Machine §3.6 and Appendix A.10 source and held-out test

evidence.tested: The author used two sectors for initial fitting and two other existing sectors for a timing check. A combined false-alarm probability of about 0.002 was estimated from 400 end-to-end null realizations.
evidence.unknown: A bound eclipsing companion and a nearby faint source remain plausible alternatives. The candidate is unconfirmed; the held-out data came from existing observations.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Sonnet 5.5 proposed and executed a box-least-squares search of TESS light curves. The author applied photometric, catalogue and held-out timing checks.

title: A laboratory-data model classifies retrospective COVID-19 severity labels
summary: Tuned logistic regression in 8,844 repeated blood tests from 2,935 unvaccinated patients estimated retrospective COVID-19 severity labels, reporting an AUC of 0.8512. Tuning raised sensitivity from 36.59% to 78.05% while lowering specificity from 96.38% to 77.00%. This internal test-level evaluation does not establish early prognosis for new patients.
ai_technology: Logistic regression
organization: University of Alicante; University and Polytechnic La Fe Hospital of Valencia

source_review.scope: Primary article full-text bibliographic metadata and relevant computational evaluation Methods/Results: se0030, se0080, se0120, se0150, se0160. Primary-source caveat and denominator review; candidate-panel identity corrected where relevant.

evidence.ai_role: Logistic regression fitted the represented classification or candidate-selection model; preprocessing and expert reference labels are distinguished from the learned contribution.
evidence.tested: Five-fold stratified evaluation split blood tests, approximately 7,075 for training and 1,769 for testing per fold; model and scaler combinations were compared and logistic regression was tuned.
evidence.unknown: Patient grouping across folds is not established. Availability-based feature selection and model tuning are not shown to be nested within independent patient-level validation; multiple tests per patient can inflate apparent generalization. Samples after ICU admission were excluded; no prospective benefit or new biomarker mechanism is established. Model/scaler selection used evaluation folds. A figure caption and cohort breakdown describe the nonsevere group differently; no conclusion about hospitalization status is drawn. The operating-point tradeoff is distinct from the small AUC change from 0.8418 to 0.8512.

title: A small temporal cohort checks machine-learning estimates of dental pain
summary: A random-forest model estimated severe pain after third-molar extraction. Its AUC fell from 0.879 in internal evaluation to 0.724 in 38 later procedures, illustrating the limits of the initial result. The study does not establish improved pain management or independent-site validation.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection and random forest
organization: Sun Yat-sen University

source_review.scope: Primary article full-text bibliographic metadata and relevant computational evaluation Methods/Results: sec2.7, sec2.8, sec3.3.

evidence.ai_role: LASSO feature selection and random forest fitted the represented classification or candidate-selection model; preprocessing and expert reference labels are distinguished from the learned contribution.
evidence.tested: The study included 185 patients and 202 procedures. Models were developed using 164 procedures from 2022 and evaluated on 38 procedures from 2023; five features were selected by LASSO.
evidence.unknown: Seventeen patients contributed another contralateral procedure; patient overlap across development and temporal sets is not established. Feature selection isolation and model locking before later outcomes accrued are not demonstrated, so this is a retrospective/temporal check. A November 2024 erratum corrects author order, not the represented measurements.

title: A video study measures missed landmarks and conditional clinician acceptance
summary: A YOLOv7 study of 40 laparoscopic videos found test recall of 77.3% for one anatomical landmark and 88.0–91.7% for the other landmark subtypes. Both required landmarks were detected in 342 of 360 eligible test images. Three surgeons accepted an average of 95.71% of overlays only in that successfully detected subset; no surgical outcome improvement was established.
ai_technology: YOLOv7
organization: Prince of Songkla University

source_review.scope: Primary article full-text bibliographic metadata and relevant computational evaluation Methods/Results: sec2.2, sec2.7, sec3.1, sec3.2. Primary-source caveat and denominator review; candidate-panel identity corrected where relevant.

evidence.ai_role: YOLOv7 fitted the represented classification or candidate-selection model; preprocessing and expert reference labels are distinguished from the learned contribution.
evidence.tested: The 3,200 annotated images were split into 2,240 training, 320 validation and 640 test images. Both landmarks were present in 360 test images; the model detected both in 342, which were rated by three surgeons.
evidence.unknown: Video/patient separation between image splits is not established. Overlay acceptance excludes 18 images with missed joint detections and is an average of surgeon judgments, not a patient outcome. The live demonstration does not establish prospective comparative benefit.

title: Learned screening links separate heart-disease expression candidates
summary: Separate learned feature screening of acute-infarction and ischemic-heart-failure datasets nominated candidates that were linked through a protein-interaction database. A four-gene score was constructed and evaluated in 27 archived ventricular samples, with a reported AUC of 0.907. The panel was not a shared predictor set across both diseases and does not establish disease progression or a diagnostic test.
ai_technology: LASSO, random forest and support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination
organization: Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

source_review.scope: Primary article full-text bibliographic metadata and relevant computational evaluation Methods/Results: sec2.1, sec2.4, sec2.6, sec3.5. Primary-source caveat and denominator review; candidate-panel identity corrected where relevant.

evidence.ai_role: LASSO, random forest and SVM-RFE separately screened the disease datasets; a subsequent database interaction analysis, rather than shared selection, connected the four represented candidates.
evidence.tested: Three selectors yielded six infarction and twelve heart-failure nominees separately. STRING interactions linked IL1B from the former with TIMP2, IFIT3 and P2RY2 from the latter. The four-gene ROC model was developed/evaluated within 13 heart-failure and 14 control ventricular samples from GSE116250.
evidence.unknown: Disease stages and tissues differ across discovery datasets, and there is no longitudinal post-infarction cohort. The validation data were used to construct/evaluate ROC models; a locked external predictive score is not established. Individual TIMP2 AUC 0.989 and combined AUC 0.907 are reported on this same small dataset; these do not establish causal mechanisms.

title: A small clinical dataset tests machine-learning infection classification
summary: In 25 emergency patients selected for suspected severe limb infection and ultrasound-detected fascial fluid, a six-feature random forest reported apparent sensitivity of 90.4% and specificity of 92.2% for necrotizing infection versus cellulitis. These small-cohort estimates do not establish performance for general soft-tissue infections.
ai_technology: Random forest
organization: Chang Gung Memorial Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary article full-text bibliographic metadata and relevant computational evaluation Methods/Results: sec2.3, sec3.4. Primary-source caveat and denominator review; candidate-panel identity corrected where relevant.

evidence.ai_role: Random forest fitted the represented classification or candidate-selection model; preprocessing and expert reference labels are distinguished from the learned contribution.
evidence.tested: Thirteen infection cases and twelve cellulitis controls contributed the dataset. Four algorithms were evaluated over ten random 80/20 splits; six features were selected using random-forest Gini importance.
evidence.unknown: Initial significance screening and later feature selection are not shown to be nested inside held-out evaluation. Each nominal test split contains about five patients; repeated splits are not independent cohorts. No prospective utility, separate-team replication or causal mechanism is established. This was a selected fluid-positive cohort with different diagnostic ascertainment for infection cases and cellulitis controls, including pathology for the former. The six-feature table does not independently establish a new held-out evaluation after feature selection.

title: A small CT study evaluates learned pneumothorax classification
summary: A convolutional model classified selected, preprocessed coronal CT slices from 26 surgical patients with primary spontaneous pneumothorax and 26 surgical controls. EfficientNetB3 classified 43 of 46 unaugmented test images correctly. The image-level result does not establish screening performance or show that AI discovered the anatomical feature described by surgeons.
ai_technology: EfficientNetB3 transfer learning
organization: National Tsing Hua University; Tungs' Taichung MetroHarbor Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary article full-text bibliographic metadata and relevant computational evaluation Methods/Results: sec2.1, sec2.2, sec2.3, sec2.6, sec3, tbl2. Primary-source caveat and denominator review; candidate-panel identity corrected where relevant.

evidence.ai_role: EfficientNetB3 transfer learning fitted the represented classification or candidate-selection model; preprocessing and expert reference labels are distinguished from the learned contribution.
evidence.tested: Twenty-six cases and twenty-six surgical controls supplied multiple CT images. Authors report assigning patients separately to training, validation and testing; the unaugmented test table contains 21 true positives, 22 true negatives, two false positives and one false negative.
evidence.unknown: Only a small number of patients supplied test images; the exact patient denominator of the 46-image test is not explicit. Cases and controls differ in age, sex and body habitus. The 903 augmented test images are transformations, not independent patients. Two surgeons defined/reviewed the anatomical feature; the learned contribution is the classifier, not initial anatomical discovery.

title: A small study checks AI-selected coronary disease expression markers
summary: Learned feature selection in 198 archived blood-expression samples nominated five coronary disease candidates. In a separate laboratory check of 10 cases and 10 controls, higher NEFL and lower FAM166B and POLDIP3 expression matched the initial directions. PRSS37 showed no significant difference, while ZNF594 changed in the opposite direction. These preliminary associations do not establish a diagnostic test or a causal disease mechanism.
ai_technology: LASSO and support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination
organization: Shaanxi Provincial People's Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary article XML bibliographic dates, computational feature-selection Methods, expression Results and limitations; primary GEO study identity.

evidence.ai_role: LASSO and SVM-RFE selected five overlapping expression candidates from the discovery dataset, determining the markers examined in the subsequent blood-sample check.
evidence.tested: Discovery used 198 whole-blood microarray samples: 99 angiographic coronary disease cases and 99 controls with less than 50% stenosis. The within-study expression check used 10 coronary disease cases and 10 healthy volunteers; three candidate directions agreed, one comparison was nonsignificant and one direction reversed.
evidence.unknown: The small laboratory comparison was not a separate-team replication or a prospective clinical test. Nominal expression significance does not establish adjusted biomarker performance, disease mechanism or clinical benefit. The reported diagnostic AUC of 0.75 was evaluated in the discovery dataset and is not the represented validation result.

title: An image model labels hybrid nerve-tumor slides in a small held-out set
summary: A retrospective study of 115 nerve-sheath tumors compared image classifiers for hybrid neurofibroma/schwannoma and related diagnoses. In 17 held-out hybrid-only slides from another center/scanner, the best reported model reached mean accuracy 0.96. This selected positive-class test does not establish specificity against other tumors or clinical utility.
ai_technology: ResNet50 features and clustering-constrained attention multiple instance learning
organization: University of Augsburg; University Hospital Hamburg-Eppendorf

source_review.scope: Primary full-text bibliographic dates, computational classification Methods, held-out Results and explicit cohort/reference limitations.

evidence.tested: The 115 tumors supplied 375 histological sections across three German centers. Authors report patient-separated cross-validation; a 17-slide hybrid-only holdout assessed scanner/center transfer. The reported best mCLAM/ResNet50 configuration with stain normalization achieved accuracy 0.96 ± 0.05 and F1 0.98 ± 0.03.
evidence.unknown: The holdout contains only hybrid-tumor slides, so it does not measure external three-class specificity. Its distinct patient count is not clear from the main text. Different configurations were compared on the test set, and best test performance is not a locked-model estimate. Expert-curated referral cases, artifacts and center/scanner confounding limit generalization; prospective clinical outcomes were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Learned image features and multiple-instance classifiers predicted diagnostic slide labels; expert histology supplied reference diagnoses.

title: A small imaging study reproduces one surgeon’s recorded flap decisions
summary: An ensemble nearest-neighbor classifier trained on seven surgical fluorescence videos reproduced one expert’s recorded tissue-label decisions in three held-out patient videos. It classified 148 of 149 sampled image grids consistently with the reference. This retrospective agreement test does not establish optimal tissue removal, viability prediction or better patient outcomes.
ai_technology: Ensemble subspace k-nearest-neighbor classification of fluorescence-curve features
organization: University College Dublin; Mater Misericordiae University Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary full-text bibliographic dates, computational classification Methods, held-out Results and explicit cohort/reference limitations.

evidence.tested: Seven training videos supplied 28 sampled lines and 1,413 image grids; three test videos supplied three lines and 149 grids. Testing agreed on 138 of 138 reference retain labels and 10 of 11 reference excise labels, giving 99.3% overall grid accuracy.
evidence.unknown: All ten patients were selected for absence of later partial or total flap necrosis. The reference was one experienced surgeon’s original decisions, not an independent tissue-viability endpoint. Many adjacent grids came from only three held-out patients; internal ten-fold grid validation is not independent-patient validation. Prospective recording of videos does not establish prospective deployment or clinical benefit of the learned model.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted ensemble classified spatial fluorescence-feature samples using the surgeon’s labels, enabling an explicit held-video reference-agreement test.

title: A coronary CT model retains diagnostic discrimination in sex subgroups
summary: A post-hoc analysis tested an existing coronary CT ischemia model against invasive pressure measurements in two cohorts. Vessel-level AUCs in women and men were 0.85 and 0.87 in CREDENCE and 0.81 and 0.86 in PACIFIC-1. These subgroup results do not establish equivalent performance, prospective clinical benefit or a newly developed model.
ai_technology: Convolutional coronary CT analysis and random-forest ischemia classifier
organization: Leiden University Medical Center; Amsterdam UMC

source_review.scope: Original full-text bibliographic date, relevant computational/statistical Methods and Results, bounded cohort and selection caveats; no operational clinical instructions.

evidence.tested: The previously developed classifier used quantitative plaque and stenosis features from neural image analysis; its random forest was trained in a separate 307-patient CREDENCE derivation cohort. This post-hoc study evaluated the 305-patient/868-vessel CREDENCE validation cohort and 208-patient/612-vessel PACIFIC-1 cohort. Sex-specific AUCs exceeded SPECT/MPI comparators; differences from PET in PACIFIC-1 were not significant.
evidence.unknown: Vessels are clustered within patients; subgroup tests were post hoc and do not establish equivalence or subgroup fairness. These are reused observational trial cohorts, not four independent samples or a new prospective deployment. Nonsignificant PET differences do not prove equivalence. Clinical outcomes and cost-effectiveness were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Existing neural segmentation/plaque quantification supplied features to a separately trained random forest for vessel-level ischemia prediction.

title: Automated CT muscle measurements reveal exploratory shoulder-motion associations
summary: In 13 patients contributing 14 shoulders, automated preoperative CT muscle measurements were associated with motion after reverse shoulder replacement. Larger deltoid volume correlated with anterior elevation (rho 0.640), while several other muscle measures showed exploratory associations. The small unadjusted study does not establish a clinical prediction rule or causal effects.
ai_technology: TotalSegmentator deep-learning anatomical segmentation
organization: Kyoto University; Kobe City Medical Center General Hospital

source_review.scope: Original full-text bibliographic date, relevant computational/statistical Methods and Results, bounded cohort and selection caveats; no operational clinical instructions.

evidence.tested: A retrospective single-center cohort had at least one year of follow-up. TotalSegmentator segmented six muscles; conventional CT attenuation thresholds quantified composition. Scapular-volume-normalized deltoid volume correlated with anterior elevation at rho 0.640 (reported P=.014). No significant external-rotation associations were established.
evidence.unknown: One patient contributed both shoulders, with within-person dependence not explicitly handled. Many exploratory correlations were tested without a stated multiplicity adjustment; no adjustment for age, sex, indication or baseline motion was performed. Some reported bootstrap confidence intervals cross zero despite nominal P<.05. Methods describe cuff-tear arthropathy, but Results also include osteonecrosis and rheumatoid arthritis. Repeating the same automated pipeline is not independent segmentation validation.
evidence.ai_role: Learned anatomical segmentation supplied muscle regions; fixed attenuation thresholds and ordinary Spearman statistics then quantified composition and associations.

title: A seven-feature model estimates complications after congenital heart reoperation
summary: Researchers trained a retrospective seven-feature risk model in 1,011 adults undergoing repeat congenital heart surgery. The selected gradient-boosted model reported test AUC 0.763 and validation AUC 0.782 for a composite of death and major complications. External validation and evidence of clinical benefit remain absent.
ai_technology: XGBoost gradient boosting and SHAP feature analysis
organization: Mayo Clinic

source_review.scope: Original full-text bibliographic date, relevant computational/statistical Methods and Results, bounded cohort and selection caveats; no operational clinical instructions.

evidence.tested: The 2010–2022 single-center cohort was randomly split 70%/20%/10% for training/testing/validation. Eighteen preselected clinical variables were reduced to seven using SHAP contribution. Systemic ventricular ejection fraction was most influential in the fitted models. Reduced-model test/validation AUCs were .763/.782, with reported validation CI .568–.804 and five-fold range .631–.764.
evidence.unknown: Authors selected a model at the 90th percentile AUC from bootstrapped model distributions; this is not an unbiased locked-model estimate. Rare composite events, single-center surgical selection and feature/model selection constrain generalization. Logistic-regression AUC .727 had overlapping confidence intervals, so superiority is not established. Conventional survival analysis of heart failure is separate from the machine-learning result, and SHAP influence is not causation.
evidence.ai_role: Gradient boosting fitted clinical variables to a composite postoperative outcome; SHAP ranked model contributions and supported a reduced seven-variable model.

title: Voice classifiers distinguish COVID groups in a small held-out sample
summary: A study trained voice classifiers in 210 participants and tested their combined predictions in 30 additional participants. The system classified 24 of 30 correctly, including all 10 positive cases. The selected symptomatic, Italian-speaking sample does not establish asymptomatic screening performance or population-level accuracy.
ai_technology: Radial-basis support vector machines on acoustic features
organization: University of Pavia; University of Rome Tor Vergata

source_review.scope: Primary full-text bibliographic dates, computational classification Methods, held-out Results and explicit cohort/reference limitations.

evidence.tested: Three cohorts of 70 participants supplied voice recordings for feature selection and binary SVM training. Separately recruited test participants comprised 10 positive,10 recovered and 10 healthy individuals. Table 5 reports 24/30 correct,10/10 positive,8/10 healthy and 6/10 recovered. Majority voting combined three tasks and three binary comparisons.
evidence.unknown: Training feature selection/ranking precedes the described ten-fold evaluation, so internal cross-validation is not clearly nested; repeated recordings also need participant-level separation. The 30-person test is a small balanced within-study sample, not independent replication. Table 5 includes one uncertain recovered participant, despite an abstract statement that all errors were classified positive. Most positive/recovered patients were symptomatic, and language/ethnicity restrictions constrain generalization. Long-term vocal effects and surveillance benefit were not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: SVMs learned acoustic distinctions between clinically defined groups from extracted voice features; voting combined task-specific predictions.

title: A small vascular pilot compares simulated endoleak risk with observed outcomes
summary: A single-center pilot assessed a learned endoleak risk index in 10 historical and 10 planned vascular-repair cases. In the historical group, four of six high-risk cases developed the target endoleak, while four low-risk cases did not. The small mixed study does not establish that model-guided planning reduces complications.
ai_technology: Finite-element digital twins and machine-learned Endoleak Risk Index
organization: Justus Liebig University Giessen; Saint-Joseph Hospital Marseille

source_review.scope: Primary full-text bibliographic dates, computational classification Methods, held-out Results and explicit cohort/reference limitations.

evidence.tested: The commercial model combines about 50 engineered simulation indicators using machine learning. In 10 retrospective cases with at least 3 years of follow-up,6 had elevated risk and 4 developed type 1a endoleak;2 elevated-risk cases remained event-free. The additional 10 planned cases assessed clinician decisions; not all underwent the originally planned intervention, and follow-up was short.
evidence.unknown: Only 10 historical cases support the represented outcome comparison, with no controlled assessment of planning benefit. The learned algorithm architecture and training overlap are not detailed here. Prospective decisions changed treatment or prevented the planned intervention in some cases, so absence of an event cannot validate an untreated counterfactual. The planned cohort had only median 3 months follow-up and no target events.
evidence.ai_role: Learned aggregation of geometric/biomechanical simulation indicators produced a patient-specific risk category; clinicians retained decision responsibility.

title: Digital kidney-biopsy damage features are associated with later graft loss
summary: Deep-learning image analysis quantified tissue damage in 789 kidney-transplant biopsy slides from two cohorts. A damage score from 12-month biopsies was associated with subsequent graft loss in both cohorts. Baseline-score survival association was not confirmed in the smaller Australian cohort, and clinical utility remains untested.
ai_technology: Mask R-CNN and U-Net histopathology analysis
organization: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; University of Sydney

source_review.scope: Primary full-text bibliographic dates, computational classification Methods, held-out Results and explicit cohort/reference limitations.

evidence.tested: Networks were developed on 60 selected biopsy slides and tested on 33 others. The pipeline then analyzed 478 baseline and 311 twelve-month slides from 404 GoCAR and 212 AUSCAD participants. In 200 GoCAR and 111 AUSCAD twelve-month biopsies, composite tissue/inflammation scores were associated with later death-censored graft loss; thresholds were derived in GoCAR.
evidence.unknown: This is retrospective image/outcome analysis of previously collected cohorts, not prospective evaluation of a frozen clinical tool. GoCAR supplies both selected model-development slides and outcome analyses, with exact patient overlap not separated here. Baseline ITAS survival association was not confirmed in AUSCAD. Observational associations, selected thresholds, limited graft-loss events and cohort differences prevent causal, treatment-benefit or universal surrogate-endpoint claims.
evidence.ai_role: Neural tissue/immune-cell segmentation supplied quantitative damage features, which ordinary survival analysis related to subsequent graft outcomes.

title: Retinal-image models detect diabetic kidney disease across multiple cohorts
summary: A retinal-image model trained for diabetic kidney disease achieved AUCs of 0.791–0.826 across ten external datasets totaling 65,406 participants. A separate task distinguished isolated diabetic nephropathy from other kidney disease in small biopsy-referenced cohorts. These results support diagnostic investigation without establishing improved patient outcomes or replacement of confirmatory tests.
ai_technology: ResNet-50 with momentum-contrastive pretraining
organization: Shanghai Sixth People’s Hospital; Shanghai Jiao Tong University

source_review.scope: Version-specific original computational/statistical Methods and Results plus primary bibliographic dates. Clinical benefit, causal effects and independent replication are not inferred.

evidence.tested: DeepDKD used 734,084 pretraining images and 486,312 development/internal-validation images from 121,578 participants. The image-only classifier averaged scores across each participant’s available images. Internal DKD AUC was .842; ten external cohorts had AUC .791–.826. The biopsy-related task used 267 development participants and 244 external participants, with external AUC .733–.844. A 325-person prospective primary-care proof-of-concept reported sensitivity 89.8% and specificity 47.6% against subsequent confirmatory findings.
evidence.unknown: The represented principal result is retrospective multicohort diagnostic validation. External datasets and a prospectively collected cohort do not establish improved clinical outcomes. Camera/domain differences and population selection constrain transfer. The small prospective study selected a previously defined high-sensitivity operating point; specificity was low, and the apparent specificity improvement versus metadata was not significant (P=.072). Model-development split details and diagnostic-reference definitions are in an appendix not independently read here. The retinal model is an ancillary screen, not a non-invasive tissue biopsy or proven substitute for laboratory/biopsy confirmation.
evidence.ai_role: Contrastively pretrained image features were supervised for kidney-disease categories; a frozen image encoder and linear classifier supported the separate nephropathy task.

title: A Danish study estimates small average net-benefit gains from a complex warning model
summary: An October 2025 preprint compared early-warning models in 2.16 million hospital encounters. Although its gradient-boosted model discriminated 24-hour mortality better than NEWS, the maximum average decision-curve net-benefit difference was 1.8 per 10,000 across tested thresholds. These are retrospective weighted estimates, not measured lives saved or proven clinical efficiency gains.
ai_technology: XGBoost and distilled multilingual sentence embeddings
organization: University of Copenhagen; Imperial College London

source_review.scope: Primary full-text bibliographic dates, computational classification Methods, held-out Results and explicit cohort/reference limitations.

evidence.tested: The original preprint analyzed 2,161,689 encounters from 829,610 individuals after excluding encounters with major subsequent interventions, then reweighted the remaining sample. Hospital-grouped ten-fold evaluation reported XGB-EWS AUC .932 versus NEWS .902. Decision-curve analysis reported maximum overall net-benefit differences of 1.8 per 10,000 for XGB-EWS versus NEWS and 1.7 for NEWS versus NEWS-Light.
evidence.unknown: The represented claim uses the October 14, 2025 preprint; the November 2026 journal abstract changes the cohort and numerical results, which are not assigned to the earlier date. Encounters from one person can recur and were treated as independent; hospital grouping does not establish patient separation across hospitals. Weighting depends on exchangeability and measured treatment predictors; unmeasured clinical factors can bias the hypothetical no-intervention estimate. Net benefit is a threshold-dependent weighted statistic, not a count of lives saved. Simulated staff-time savings and real-world implementation effects were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Learned clinical-history embeddings and gradient boosting combined prior records, vital signs and laboratory values to estimate mortality risk; ordinary decision-curve analysis compared model outputs.

title: A liver-ultrasound classifier is evaluated in a South Indian community sample
summary: A study evaluated a neural ultrasound classifier using expert-agreed fatty-liver grades in a rural South Indian cohort. On a 66-person internal holdout, AUC was 0.90 for moderate-to-severe steatosis. Performance declined on an external dataset with a different reference and target; the result does not establish clinical outcomes or universal transfer.
ai_technology: ImageNet-pretrained InceptionResNetV2 convolutional neural network
organization: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine; ICMR National Institute of Nutrition

source_review.scope: Original community-analysis computational Methods, Table4 and primary article dates; systematic-review pooled findings kept separate.

evidence.tested: Of 261 expert-review candidates, 219 had usable scans and agreement by two blinded radiologists. Training, validation and test splits were at participant level, and image probabilities were averaged within each participant at test. The 66-person internal holdout contained 15 moderate-to-severe cases and yielded AUC .90 (CI .77–1.00). Without additional fine-tuning, an external 55-person biopsy-referenced dataset yielded AUC .76 (CI .64–.89) for any steatosis, a different target.
evidence.unknown: This record represents the original clinical analysis, not pooled performance of the accompanying systematic review. Selecting only radiologist-agreed cases removes difficult disagreements; initial inter-reader kappa was .44. Reference grades are visual ultrasound judgments, not biopsy confirmation for the community holdout. Different reported thresholds are optimized by Youden index, with independent threshold locking not established. External testing changes both outcome definition and reference, and subsequent fine-tuning uses that external population. No patient benefit, independent replication or broad population calibration is demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained neural image model was fine-tuned on liver-ultrasound labels and generated participant-level probabilities from video-frame predictions.

title: A brain-connectivity model maps task-defined functional regions in tumor patients
summary: A graph neural model used resting-state brain scans to estimate language and motor regions in 62 brain-tumor patients. Repeated cross-validation against task-fMRI-derived labels reported language-region AUC 0.76. The reference was task-fMRI, and the study did not establish agreement with invasive mapping or improved surgical outcomes.
ai_technology: Multi-task graph neural network for resting-state fMRI connectivity
organization: Johns Hopkins University

source_review.scope: Primary clinical-cohort, computational model/split Methods and clinical Results; synthetic healthy-brain experiments kept distinct.

evidence.tested: The retrospective 62-patient tumor cohort supplied expert-confirmed task-fMRI pseudo-reference labels. Resting-state connectivity and manually identified tumor regions were used at inference. Repeated ten-fold evaluation reported parcel-level language AUC .76, finger .83, foot .78 and tongue .80, with different task denominators. Hyperparameters were selected using a separate healthy HCP dataset. An exploratory holdout trained on 57 unilateral-language patients and tested five bilateral cases.
evidence.unknown: Task-fMRI labels and atlas parcels are indirect references rather than invasive stimulation mapping. The bilateral holdout is only five patients. Task participation, expert thresholding and tumor segmentations constrain applicability to patients unable to perform tasks, and a single-center retrospective cohort does not establish clinical benefit. Simulated tumors in healthy HCP subjects are a separate synthetic experiment, not additional tumor patients or independent clinical confirmation.
evidence.ai_role: The learned graph model combined resting-state connectivity with tumor-region information to estimate multiple functional-network labels simultaneously.

title: Admission images and records classify COVID outcomes across six Italian hospitals
summary: A December 2020 preprint studied admission chest X-rays and records from 820 hospitalized patients. A combined image-feature and clinical classifier reported mean accuracy 0.743 in leave-one-center-out evaluation for a composite severe outcome. This retrospective first-wave study does not establish prospective benefit or superiority over clinical records alone.
ai_technology: Convolutional image features with classical supervised classifiers
organization: University Campus Bio-Medico of Rome; Fondazione Bruno Kessler

source_review.scope: Original v1 archive metadata and PDF clinical-data/model-validation Methods and Tables4/5; exact results compared with later journal full text. Version-header and submission dates remain distinguished.

evidence.tested: The six-hospital cohort had 820 admission examinations, with outcomes classified as mild versus non-invasive ventilation, intensive care or death. Training-fold normalization, feature selection and parameter fitting were described. In original v1 Table 5, GoogleNet image features plus clinical data and logistic regression achieved mean accuracy .743±.061, sensitivity .769±.189 and specificity .685±.155 across held-out centers; clinical-data SVM accuracy was .734±.044. The later August 2021 journal tables retain these values.
evidence.unknown: Many configurations were compared, and displayed best performances do not constitute an untouched locked-model evaluation. Center-held-out evaluation reuses one first-wave study rather than independent replication. Severe outcome combines several care decisions and mortality; the results do not establish time-to-event prognosis, treatment effect, capacity improvement or clinically significant added value over records alone. The v1 archive says submitted December 11, 2020, while its PDF carries a December 14 version header; this entry uses the dated PDF version and does not assert a first-public-day priority. Journal publication was August 28, 2021.
evidence.ai_role: Neural features extracted from admission radiographs were combined with clinical variables by supervised classifiers to estimate the recorded composite outcome.

title: Learned tract maps link postoperative network changes with language changes
summary: In a small retrospective subgroup of 21 children undergoing epilepsy surgery, changes in model-defined white-matter networks were associated with changes in language scores. Combined language-network efficiency changes correlated with core language-score changes at R=.674. Both pre- and postoperative scans were used; this was not a preoperative prediction of future outcomes.
ai_technology: ESM-AnatTractNet modified 1D ResNet tract classifier
organization: Wayne State University

source_review.scope: Original full-text clinical cohort and nonprocedural computational/statistical Methods and Results; model output distinguished from association and treatment effects.

evidence.tested: An 85-child preoperative tractography cohort supplied 47 training, 20 test and 18 later temporal-validation cases. Separate clinical analyses included 45 children with paired scans and 21 with paired scans/language assessments. In the 21-child language analysis, learned tract maps defined connectivity networks, and ordinary Pearson analysis related efficiency changes to core language-score changes (R=.674, P<.001). CCA additionally fitted multivariate associations on these data.
evidence.unknown: The 21-child association is an exploratory within-study analysis, with multiple network/language comparisons and no stated independent CCA holdout. It uses postoperative imaging and cannot predict an unknown postoperative result from preoperative data alone. Clinical management was blinded to the analysis and was not altered. Cohort/scanner specificity, varying follow-up and incomplete outcome data limit generalization; surgical benefit, optimal margins and causal language effects were not established.
evidence.ai_role: A learned tract classifier identified language-pathway groups; conventional network measures and correlation analysis then related imaging changes to measured language changes.

title: Automated heart-shape measurements are associated with later cardiomyopathy
summary: The March 2023 journal analysis of 38,897 UK Biobank participants with normal conventional heart measurements linked greater left-ventricular roundness with later cardiomyopathy. The fully adjusted hazard ratio was 1.47 per standard-deviation increase in sphericity. This is an observational association, not proof that a rounder heart causes disease; an earlier 2022 preprint reported related findings.
ai_technology: Fully convolutional neural-network cardiac segmentation
organization: Cedars-Sinai Medical Center; Stanford University

source_review.scope: Original full-text clinical cohort and nonprocedural computational/statistical Methods and Results; model output distinguished from association and treatment effects.

evidence.tested: A pretrained cardiac-segmentation network enabled automated short-axis/long-axis shape measurement in 38,897 selected participants. Blinded comparison with two cardiologists used 100 random images. Cox analysis of later diagnosis codes adjusted for demographics, clinical factors, ejection fraction and ventricular volume; the journal fully adjusted cardiomyopathy HR was 1.47 (CI 1.10–1.98), and atrial-fibrillation HR 1.20 (CI 1.11–1.28).
evidence.unknown: This entry represents the fully adjusted journal analysis, not a first-disclosure claim. The July 21, 2022 original preprint already described related cohort associations, with different reported adjustment/estimates; its direct full-text/PDF routes were blocked and only indexed primary segments were available. UK Biobank/MRI healthy-selection bias, diagnosis-code misclassification and single-cohort analysis constrain risk use. Genetic analysis found no evidence that sphericity causes cardiomyopathy or AF; reverse-causality evidence for cardiomyopathy influencing shape was sensitivity-method-dependent. Clinical prediction utility and independent replication were not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained neural segmenter measured ventricular shape at cohort scale; ordinary survival/genetic analyses related the derived shape phenotype to outcomes.

title: Learned cell maps reveal opposing spatial-density associations with breast-cancer survival
summary: An analysis of breast-cancer tissue images linked two tumor–lymphocyte spatial-density features with survival in opposite directions. Neural nucleus classification enabled the measurements in 822 selected TCGA cases. The retrospective associations and within-dataset prognosis evaluation do not establish immune mechanisms, treatment response or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: HD-Yolo nucleus detection, classification and segmentation
organization: UT Southwestern Medical Center; Northwestern University

source_review.scope: Original clinical-cohort, neural-pipeline, survival-selection Methods and spatial-feature Results; model interpretation kept separate from immune causation.

evidence.tested: The study used 653 infiltrating-ductal and 169 infiltrating-lobular female breast-cancer cases with stage information. Patients were split into 658 training and 164 testing cases. Neural cell labels supported tumor, stromal and lymphocyte density maps; ElasticNet-regularized Cox models combined image and clinical features. Lymphocyte-to-tumor spatial projection had a negative model coefficient, while tumor-to-lymphocyte projection had a positive coefficient; training selection and test survival ranking were described.
evidence.unknown: Feature/model selection and association estimates are exploratory within one public cohort. No lobular-only test analysis was possible because that subgroup had no deaths in the test set. Opposing spatial coefficients are model associations and do not prove lymphocyte suppression or tumor inhibition. Statements that the features were more prognostically significant than receptor status are not independent evidence of clinical superiority. No external survival replication, therapy-effect study or clinical decision benefit was established.
evidence.ai_role: A learned nucleus detector/segmenter classified cell types, enabling spatial-density measurements subsequently analyzed using ordinary survival models.

title: Ascites-image models stratify recorded platinum resistance in ovarian cancer
summary: OVCAP analyzed pretreatment ascites cytology from 438 women with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer. Internal and two additional-site validation cohorts yielded resistance-classification AUCs of 0.894, 0.863 and 0.828. This retrospective treatment-response study does not establish that model-guided treatment improves outcomes.
ai_technology: Prov-GigaPath features, TransMIL and multi-scale late fusion
organization: Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center; Northern Jiangsu People’s Hospital

source_review.scope: Original model/clinical cohort, outcome definition, patient-level training selection and held-out Results; exploratory biological interpretation and clinical benefit kept bounded.

evidence.tested: The 2019–2023 cohort comprised 367 Xuhui-campus cases split into 254 training and 113 internal-validation patients, plus 51 Pudong-campus and 20 Northern-Jiangsu validation patients. Patient-level three-fold training cross-validation selected among 15 encoders and hyperparameters. The retained multi-scale predictor was applied unchanged to the held-out cohorts. Resistance meant progression during therapy or recurrence/progression within six months after completing platinum treatment; the reported internal/external AUCs were .894/.863/.828.
evidence.unknown: The three sites represent two institutions; one additional-site cohort shares the same cancer center as development. The smallest cohort contains only 20 people. Retrospective selection of patients with evaluable outcomes, histologic concentration in high-grade serous cancer and preparation/scanner differences constrain transfer. AUCs are not treatment-benefit estimates. Attention-selected morphology and integrated single-cell associations are hypothesis-generating, not established mechanisms of resistance. Clinical vignettes and comparison with later-available kinetic biomarkers do not demonstrate prospective clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: Pathology foundation-model embeddings and attention-based multiple-instance learning estimated response risk from image patches; trained multi-scale fusion combined the prediction streams.

title: Graph-selected brain connectivity is associated with ADHD symptom scores
summary: A dynamic graph convolutional network analyzed resting-state scans from 603 ADHD-200 participants. Model-selected connectivity features were associated with symptom severity in a 172-person subgroup. These retrospective, post-selection associations are exploratory and do not establish a causal ADHD mechanism or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Dynamic graph convolutional network (dGCN) and isolation forest
organization: Lehigh University; University of Maryland; University of Pennsylvania; Georgia State University; Georgia Institute of Technology; Emory University

source_review.scope: Original publication metadata, computational Methods2.1/2.2.6, Results3.1/3.3.1–3.3.3 and limitations4.2 actually read; no author code executed.

evidence.tested: The selected four-site sample contained 260 ADHD and 343 control participants after isolation-forest outlier removal. dGCN combined connectivity with seven personal-characteristic variables and reached 72.0% diagnostic accuracy in site-stratified ten-fold cross-validation; leave-site-out accuracy ranged from 67.9% to 74.3%. Across 172 Peking University participants with symptom scales, regression on model-selected regional features yielded cross-validated symptom-score correlations of .33–.36. Selected within-frontal, within-posterior-fossa and subcortical–posterior-fossa connectivity showed symptom correlations of .28–.34, reported with FDR correction.
evidence.unknown: Regional selection used model weights averaged across diagnostic cross-validation. Its independence from the subsequent symptom regression and correlation analyses is not established; FDR correction does not remove selection bias. All symptom analyses used a subset of the same source dataset. Imaging alone did not supply the reported diagnostic predictions: age, sex, handedness and IQ-related inputs were included. Site-held-out classification is not independent replication of the selected biological associations. No causal direction, independent symptom-cohort confirmation or benefit from clinical use is established. The November2021 online version is represented; the issue date is February2022, and the bounded search does not establish earliest public priority.
evidence.ai_role: Learned graph convolutions ranked regional connectivity features used to investigate symptom associations; a separate conventional linear regression quantified symptom-score prediction. The claimed result is the exploratory AI-selected association, not a causal mechanism.

title: Learned brain patterns link pain ratings and cognitive measures
summary: A machine-learning mediation analysis identified brain patterns jointly related to heat intensity and pain ratings, and connectivity patterns related to fluid intelligence and working-memory accuracy. The December 2022 journal analysis used existing fMRI datasets; a related preprint appeared in October 2022. The authors explicitly avoid causal interpretation.
ai_technology: 3D convolutional neural network and ridge-regression connectome predictive modeling
organization: Johns Hopkins University; Dartmouth College

evidence.tested: Pain models used 209 training participants across seven studies and a 75-person eighth-study evaluation, with activation patterns related to heat intensity and pain ratings. The pain-model association was absent for aversive sound trials in that evaluation; leave-study-out mediation was significant for five of eight pain datasets. A separate HCP analysis used 558 training and 240 test participants, identifying connectivity patterns jointly related to fluid intelligence and working-memory accuracy.
evidence.unknown: These are statistical mediation associations, not established neural causal pathways. Training Methods explicitly evaluated iteration-specific mediation on test data and selected the most stable indirect effect; those test results are therefore not a wholly untouched final confirmation. The pain data had previously been analyzed with a different mediation method, and familiar pain regions were recovered alongside exploratory differences. SHAP localization and its arbitrary threshold do not establish independent biological mechanisms. The primary preprint API dates version1 to October 11, 2022, but its full result tables were not read; journal-specific claims are not assigned that earlier date. The HCP split is within one source cohort, not a separate independently collected cohort.
evidence.ai_role: A fitted CNN compressed activation maps into learned mediators optimized through the path model; ridge-regression connectome modeling supplied the second application. Conventional path analysis and bootstrapping tested the resulting associations.

source_review.scope: Original primary computational training, clinical/sample definition, represented Results and bounded Discussion/limitations actually read; earlier primary preprint API metadata/abstract read, not its full tables.

title: Generative embedding distinguishes recorded two-year depression trajectories
summary: In a retrospective reanalysis of 85 NESDA patients, a support-vector classifier using modeled brain connectivity distinguished chronic depression from rapid remission with 79% balanced accuracy in nested cross-validation. The February 2020 journal analysis follows a September 2019 preprint. Small groups, reused data and uncontrolled treatment limit clinical interpretation.
ai_technology: Linear support vector machine with dynamic-causal-model generative embedding
organization: University of Zurich; ETH Zurich; Radboud University; King’s College London; University of Melbourne; Amsterdam UMC; Leiden University; University of Groningen
