evidence.tested: Baseline face-processing fMRI and available two-year follow-up identified 39 rapid-remission, 31 gradual-improvement and 15 chronic-course patients. SVM hyperparameters were optimized using training-only inner five-fold cross-validation inside leave-one-person-out evaluation. Chronic versus rapid-remission classification reached 79% balanced accuracy and ROC AUC .87; gradual versus rapid remission reached 61% but did not survive the stated multiple-comparison correction, and chronic versus gradual improvement was at chance.
evidence.unknown: This is retrospective prognostic modeling in a selected 85-person cohort, not prospective evaluation of a frozen model. The chronic group comprised only 15 patients; age differed and source-reported age adjustment reduced balanced accuracy to 74%. Treatments and intervening life events were not standardized. An earlier Schmaal analysis used the same source cohort and clinical-trajectory grouping, so this reanalysis is not independent confirmation or first discovery of those trajectories. Source footnotes warn that McNemar comparisons between cross-validated classifiers may be optimistic. The original preprint API dates version1 to September 18, 2019; only its metadata/abstract were available in this review, so journal-specific metrics are not backdated. No individualized-treatment benefit or causal neural mechanism is established.
evidence.ai_role: A learned SVM classified later clinical-trajectory labels using posterior connectivity parameters from a conventional generative model; the AI contribution is the discriminative classifier, not an assumption that causal-model terminology proves causation.

source_review.scope: Original primary computational training, clinical/sample definition, represented Results and bounded Discussion/limitations actually read; earlier primary preprint API metadata/abstract read, not its full tables.

title: An EEG model retrospectively estimates outcomes across critical-illness etiologies
summary: A one-dimensional convolutional network analyzed EEGs from 358 adults with acute consciousness impairment. Patient-held-out cross-validation yielded AUCs of .721 for six-month survival and .703 for favorable functional outcome. Higher-confidence subsets had better performance at reduced coverage; this was retrospective modeling, not a randomized test of AI-guided care.
ai_technology: t-VGG GAP one-dimensional convolutional neural network
organization: University of Bern; Lausanne University Hospital; University of Lausanne; University Hospital Basel; Hôpital du Valais

source_review.scope: Original publication/affiliation metadata, computational Methods2.1–2.4, clinical endpoints and Results3.2/Table2/Table3; bounded Discussion limitations actually read.

evidence.tested: This post-hoc analysis reused the four-hospital CERTA EEG trial. A fixed previously published CNN architecture used overlapping epochs, while stratified five-fold splitting kept all epochs from a patient together; patient predictions averaged epoch outputs. Prognosis used survival at six months and the best Cerebral Performance Category measured at four weeks or six months. All 358 patients contributed prognostic evaluation; diagnostic etiology classification used 277 eligible patients and reached 54.5% accuracy.
evidence.unknown: Original trial randomization concerned EEG recording strategy, not this learned model. The best-of-two-timepoints functional endpoint is not a fixed six-month recovery measure. Model-output confidence selected progressively smaller subgroups and does not establish calibrated clinical certainty; higher-confidence performance must not be reported as whole-cohort accuracy. Earlier random-forest work used the same cohort, so this is not an independent replication of its findings. Treatment decisions and withdrawal of life support may affect observed prognosis; authors argue that using the first EEG reduced but did not remove that concern. There was no held-out new hospital, prospective model-guided treatment or demonstrated patient benefit. The represented date is the documented August 2022 online journal version, without an earliest-priority assertion.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN learned EEG features directly to classify clinical outcomes and etiologies; Grad-CAM and visual review explored model behavior without proving a new causal mechanism.

title: Learned diffusion-MRI enhancement changes migraine-group statistical contrasts
summary: Fourteen learned reconstruction methods were evaluated on scans from 50 episodic and 50 chronic migraine patients after training data from healthy controls. Improved recovery of group-difference voxels also introduced differences absent from the fuller-sampling reference. This is a bounded reconstruction audit, not proof that the added voxels are biologically false.
ai_technology: CNNs, U-Nets, denoising autoencoders, SARDI-Net and Swin Transformer reconstruction
organization: Universidad de Valladolid; Cardiff University; University of Rochester

evidence.tested: Training data comprised 60 healthy controls with 61-direction diffusion MRI; 14 participating methods reconstructed maps from 21-direction input for 50 episodic and 50 chronic migraine patients, whose group identities were hidden from participating teams. Identical TBSS analysis compared reconstructed group contrasts with the organizers’ 61-direction silver-standard contrast maps. New recovered reference-positive voxels and reference-negative significant voxels covaried across methods, with reported R-squared values .907 for axial diffusivity and .749 for mean diffusivity.
evidence.unknown: False positive here means significant after reconstruction but absent from the 61-direction statistical reference; this is not an independent biological ground truth or a clinical diagnostic false-positive rate. Differences concern 100 migraine patients under one acquisition setting and training on a different clinical group; the paper explicitly disallows generalization to all imaging tasks. Methods used heterogeneous training/validation arrangements, including synthetic training and model-selection differences. The reference-derived registration and skeleton were shared across comparisons. Image-quality improvement does not establish preservation of inferential conclusions, and the associations across 14 methods do not establish a universal numerical law.
evidence.ai_role: Trained reconstruction networks transformed reduced-direction diffusion data or its derived measures. The qualifying result is the source-specific effect of those learned transformations on measured clinical-group statistical contrasts, not a ranking of generic image-quality metrics.

source_review.scope: Original primary computational Methods, cohort/reference definitions, represented Results and bounded limitations actually read; no code executed or independent reanalysis.

title: A random forest ranks mortality-associated markers in the Italian CORIST cohort
summary: An exploratory random forest analysis of 3,894 hospitalized COVID-19 patients ranked renal function, C-reactive protein and age as influential mortality-classification features. Conventional survival analyses in the same cohort supported associated risks. These retrospective findings are neither causal effects nor an independently validated clinical risk tool.
ai_technology: Random forest, permutation feature importance and k-nearest-neighbor imputation
organization: Mediterranea Cardiocentro; IRCCS Neuromed; CORIST collaboration

evidence.tested: The retrospective 30-center Italian cohort included 3,894 patients admitted from February 19 to May 23, 2020; 712 died and 532 were still hospitalized at the May 29 cutoff. RF development used 2,725 patients and a random 1,169-patient test subset, with training hyperparameter search. Renal function and C-reactive protein ranked above age in the reported feature-importance analysis; conventional Cox models analyzed associations with time to in-hospital death.
evidence.unknown: Imputation and normalization are described before the train/test split, without clear fold-specific fitting. Although Methods discuss test-set importance, the primary figure caption places the permutation-importance analysis in the training sample; this record does not claim independently reproduced feature rankings. The test subset came from the same pooled cohort, not a new hospital or external population. Ongoing hospitalization at cutoff complicates a binary death/no-death target. High reported survival sensitivity coexisted with low specificity; overall accuracy is not validated mortality sensitivity. Missing smoking/obesity data, absent vital signs, treatment differences and residual confounding limit interpretation. Cox hazard ratios are conventional same-cohort associations, not AI-derived causal findings.
evidence.ai_role: The learned forest and permutation analysis provided an exploratory nonlinear feature ranking; conventional survival modeling supplied complementary association estimates. Their agreement is not independent confirmation.

source_review.scope: Original primary computational Methods, cohort/reference definitions, represented Results and bounded limitations actually read; no code executed or independent reanalysis.

title: AI-assisted whole-pancreas MRI measurements correlate with CT attenuation
summary: In 158 paired MRI/CT examinations, whole-pancreas fat fraction and CT attenuation showed a Spearman correlation of −.755. A locally trained U-Net assisted part of the MRI annotation, with manual correction of every assisted segmentation. The retrospective study also found substantial slice-to-slice variability; it did not independently validate automated segmentation or disease prediction.
ai_technology: U-Net pancreas annotation assistance and CNN-based liver segmentation
organization: Mayo Clinic

source_review.scope: Original publication metadata, computational/annotation Methods, Results and bounded prior-work/limitations Discussion passages actually read.

evidence.tested: Of 543 potentially paired examinations, selection/exclusion yielded 158 subjects with MRI and non-contrast CT within six months, plus 59 MRI-only examinations for 217 total MRI measurements. Mean pancreatic MRI fat fraction correlated inversely with CT attenuation (Spearman −.755); slice-to-slice MRI variation increased with mean whole-pancreas fat fraction (Spearman .51). The prior CT-only study is acknowledged separately.
evidence.unknown: All pancreas masks were manually drawn or manually corrected after CNN assistance. The source does not quantify how many final subjects required learned assistance, and this is not a model-accuracy validation. The locally trained MRI U-Net requires independent testing according to the authors. Referral-based inclusion, exclusion of inflammatory/neoplastic disease, image-quality selection, imperfect MRI resolution and up-to-six-month modality separation constrain interpretation. No pancreatic histological ground truth or equivalence of fat measures is established by correlation, and demographics/diabetes associations are observational. The source extends earlier CT-only measurements; it is not a first discovery that fat and CT attenuation are related.
evidence.ai_role: A U-Net trained during the annotation process assisted later MRI masks before manual correction; a separate CNN estimated liver fat. Learned segmentation aided measurement collection, while conventional correlations provided the scientific result.

title: Transformer-classified reviews map regional patterns in EV availability discussions
summary: BERT and XLNet classified topics in an archive of 127,257 U.S. charging-station reviews. Spatial analysis placed relatively frequent availability discussions in smaller communities in parts of the West and Midwest, with different patterns in the South and Northeast. The result concerns review-topic frequency, not independently measured charging shortages.
ai_technology: BERT and XLNet supervised topic classification
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: The 2011–2015 archive covered 12,720 charging locations and 29,532 users. Human-designed topics were learned from expert-annotated reviews; ten cross-validation runs gave overall accuracy 91.6% and F1 .83/.84 for BERT/XLNet. Predicted topic frequencies were mapped using 2013 metropolitan/micropolitan boundaries and standardized separately into regional quantiles. The source describes smaller-community availability discussion patterns in parts of the West/Midwest and more major-metropolitan patterns in the South/Northeast.
evidence.unknown: Availability is a broad discussion topic encompassing whether stations are available; frequent discussion is not a direct estimate of shortage, station failure or unmet demand. Regional quantile normalization prevents treating the map as a common absolute availability scale. Reviews appear only when users post, do not contain charging transactions and cannot establish population-wide access or causal infrastructure effects. The data were reanalyzed from an existing archive, and topics were manually specified rather than discovered unsupervised. Annotator experts were trained students, not industry professionals; the 100-review audited comparison does not establish universal superhuman annotation. Full supplemental training partitions and spatial counts were not reviewed, so geographic unit-count claims are not reproduced. This represents the January 2021 journal version, despite the 2020 DOI token.
evidence.ai_role: Learned language classifiers scaled manual topic labels across the review corpus, enabling the source-specific spatial analysis. Conventional mapping summarized those learned labels; predicted discussion is kept distinct from observed infrastructure conditions.

source_review.scope: Original primary cohort, learned-model evaluation, represented applied Results, reference labels and bounded limitations actually read; supplementary material not fully assessed.

title: A human-in-the-loop classifier reduces non-tumor-cell gallery review
summary: A self-supervised image encoder and clinician-updated SVM were evaluated on additional blood-image data from 10 metastatic breast-cancer patients. Their proposed gallery contained higher fractions of expert-identified circulating tumor cells than CellSearch galleries, while each system found cells the other missed. This does not establish complete sensitivity or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: DINO self-supervised XCiT encoder, SVM and cluster-targeted human-in-the-loop labeling
organization: University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf; Heidelberg University Hospital; German Cancer Research Center

source_review.scope: Original computational encoder/classifier Methods, patient-level partitions, human-labeling experiments and final 10-patient Results/Table2 actually read.

evidence.tested: The 90-patient archive supplied 60 patients for self-supervised training, 20 for downstream development/testing, and 10 additional patients for final comparison. In those 10, candidate-gallery positive predictive values ranged from .479 to .878 for the final HiL pipeline versus .094 to .365 for CellSearch events. Actual CTC counts were similar overall, but CellSearch-only cells averaged 7 per patient and HiL-only cells averaged 6.
evidence.unknown: One expert reviewed both galleries, with blinding not stated; these labels are not an independent molecular ground truth. Selection of the uncertain development cluster used test-set performance before new examples were labeled, so development-test improvement is not untouched confirmation. The separate final 10-person comparison is small and selected; each pipeline missed cells found by the other, and complete CTC sensitivity is unknown. Higher gallery PPV does not establish improved diagnosis, survival or treatment selection. This extends prior learned cell-image representation work, rather than independently discovering a new encoder.
evidence.ai_role: The trained encoder represented cell images and the SVM prioritized candidates after targeted human relabeling; the qualifying result is the additional-patient gallery/reference comparison, not a generic sampling benchmark.

title: Learned muscle segmentation adds constraints to head-and-neck radiotherapy replanning
summary: In a retrospective ten-patient planning study, learned organ segmentations enabled additional masticatory-muscle constraints in an automated optimizer. All replanned cases then satisfied the selected muscle-dose criteria. This was a computational plan comparison using previously developed cases, not evidence of reduced trismus in treated patients.
ai_technology: UnetSA and DeepLabV3+ with ResNet-101 organ segmentation
organization: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center

source_review.scope: Original learned-segmentation Methods2.1, planning/measurement Methods2.2–2.3 and Results3.1 actually read; no clinical patient-outcome claim.

evidence.tested: Each of 10 cases was replanned with the conventional ECHO optimizer under manual masks, learned replacement masks, and learned masks plus additional muscle constraints. The latter configuration met both selected muscle criteria for all cases, correcting one remaining violation in the other configurations. Comparisons used the 20-Gy boost phase, with criteria scaled from the full prescription; these units explain the differing table/abstract dose values.
evidence.unknown: These ten cases had previously been used to develop the planning pipeline and are not a fresh independent validation cohort. The trismus criteria came from an earlier observational risk model; no prospective patient follow-up or reduction in actual trismus was measured. Learned masks and manually defined masks differed geometrically, so nominal plan dose changes are not directly established improvements in delivered anatomy. The additional constraints did not yield statistically significant overall organ-dose differences in the compared scenarios. Existing clinical ECHO use for other cancer sites does not validate this head-and-neck application.
evidence.ai_role: Previously trained segmentation networks supplied organ/muscle masks that reduced the annotation burden for adding structures. ECHO optimization and dose calculation were conventional components, not silently attributed to learned AI.

title: Low-field MRI-derived synthetic CT is tested in liver treatment replanning
summary: In 37 liver cases, U-Net-generated synthetic CT images from low-field MRI were evaluated in retrospective treatment replanning. Both loss-function variants met the reported planning objectives in this source cohort. The study does not establish clinical equivalence, independent deployment safety or patient benefit.
ai_technology: U-Net with MSE and VGG16-based perceptual loss
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison

evidence.tested: The 37 patients supplied 2,561 liver-region image slices. Ten-fold evaluation grouped patients, leaving 3–4 people out per fold. Synthetic images generated for held-out cases were compared with each patient’s original CT in target/organ-at-risk planning. Perceptual and MSE variants had mean absolute image errors of 35.64 and 35.67 HU, and all synthetic-CT plans met the source planning objectives.
evidence.unknown: The same small single-system cohort informed preliminary training choices, so this is not an external independent validation. Missing fine structures such as ribs and registration between separately acquired MRI/CT remain limitations. Reported nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests, and visual image quality is not delivered-dose safety. Manual target contours were transferred from original CT; an entirely CT-free clinical workflow was not tested. No actual treatment-outcome comparison or demonstrated clinical benefit is reported. The August 2021 online version is represented; its issue date is 2022.
evidence.ai_role: Learned MRI-to-CT synthesis supplied images for a defined dosimetric reference comparison; conventional treatment-planning software computed the plans.

source_review.scope: Original computational training/partition Methods, represented applied Results and relevant limitations actually read; no source code executed.

title: Learned sensor labels reveal different hen behavior transitions across housing
summary: A learned inertial-sensor classifier was used to compare behavior in cages and floor pens in five laying hens. Floor pens showed more detected transitions involving several comfort and activity behaviors. The small repeated-measure experiment does not establish a general welfare scale, and housing-specific classifier errors may affect comparisons.
ai_technology: Multilayer perceptron behavior classification from accelerometer and gyroscope features
organization: Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology

evidence.tested: A two-hen labeled training/evaluation step supplied separate housing-specific classifiers. A later recording step used five hens in both housing systems, averaging 4.5 recording days per bird/housing condition. Those later recordings were not reused training data. The source reports more detected transitions involving moving, preening, dust-bathing, litter scratching, resting, tail-wagging and body shaking in floor pens. Visual-scan comparison in a sampled floor-pen video gave correlation .94.
evidence.unknown: There were only five birds in the housing comparison; repeated days/intervals are not independent birds. Basic same-bird classification accuracy differed substantially by housing (77.5% cages, 96.3% floor pens), and overlapping sensor windows may affect internal validation. The source does not establish that differential errors cannot explain part of the transition contrast. Training-bird overlap with the later five-bird population is not excluded, although recording data were separate. Pooling days and thresholding transitions do not establish a population-general causal welfare measure. Spatial location came from a colored marker rather than a learned tracking model.
evidence.ai_role: The trained multilayer classifier converted sensor streams into behavior labels; conventional temporal counting/statistical comparisons then quantified the source-specific housing contrast.

source_review.scope: Original computational training/partition Methods, represented applied Results and relevant limitations actually read; no source code executed.

title: ScreenDx identifies previously underdetected interstitial lung disease in COPDGene scans
summary: A retrospective COPDGene analysis used a learned CT model to detect cases subsequently relabeled as clinically significant interstitial lung disease. The original abstract reports 84.8% sensitivity and 98.0% specificity in a deliberately sampled cohort. This does not establish prospective screening benefit.
ai_technology: ScreenDx deep learning CT classifier
organization: Stanford University; IMVARIA; University of North Carolina; University of Utah; University of Alabama at Birmingham

evidence.tested: The source selected patients subsequently relabeled by COPDGene investigators as ILD-positive and sampled COPD/control negatives to target approximately 1–2% ILD prevalence. At a previously selected threshold, abstract-reported sensitivity was 84.8%(95% CI 68.1–94.9%) and specificity 98.0%(97.3–98.5%).
evidence.unknown: This review had the complete original abstract and primary bibliographic metadata, not full Methods. Exact sample counts, details of clinical adjudication, model-development overlap and threshold-lock timing were not authenticated. Positives had already been relabeled by investigators; these are not newly confirmed diagnoses made in a prospective AI screening program. Deliberate negative sampling limits prevalence-dependent interpretation. No improved patient outcomes or causal clinical benefit is established. The original journal history gives online publication November 26,2025, while PubMed records November 27; the represented date follows the original publisher.
evidence.ai_role: A learned ScreenDx model evaluates CT features compatible with ILD; this is a retrospective test against subsequently assigned clinical reference labels.

source_review.scope: Complete original PubMed/EuropePMC abstract plus indexed original journal abstract and original publisher publication history actually read; full Methods unavailable (journal403).

title: Random forests map South African particulate pollution patterns
summary: A random-forest analysis combined ground stations, satellite data and environmental predictors to estimate daily particulate pollution around Gauteng during 2014–2018. It mapped persistent hotspots and seasonal differences, with lower estimated concentrations in much of the region after 2016. The comparison does not establish a policy effect.
ai_technology: Random forest exposure regression
organization: Emory University; Council for Scientific and Industrial Research; North-West University; University of Pretoria

evidence.tested: The model used 9,853 station-day observations from 20 monitors and 40 predictors. Random ten-fold cross-validation gave R² .80 and RMSE 9.40 µg/m³. Predicted winter concentrations were highest; Johannesburg and surrounding areas showed little clear change between 2014–2015 and 2016–2018 while much of the domain decreased.
evidence.unknown: Station-day random folds do not demonstrate transfer to unseen monitoring sites or future years. The model underestimates very high concentrations; top-quintile CV R² was .69. Satellite missingness and correction introduce additional uncertainty. A before/after-policy indicator is itself a model predictor, and the comparison has no causal control or counterfactual. Maps are modeled estimates, not complete ground measurements. No individual health benefit is measured.
evidence.ai_role: Learned tree ensembles infer particulate concentrations from satellite, meteorological, land-use and socioeconomic inputs; the field result is the resulting bounded regional exposure pattern.

source_review.scope: Original ground measurements, integration, random-forest Methods, policy analysis and represented Results actually read.

title: Plasma spectra show exploratory endocrine-response discrimination
summary: An exploratory ANNE-trial analysis used learned classifiers on plasma spectra from small breast-cancer groups. When classifier family was selected inside validation, AUC was .616 for baseline Ki 67 response and .854 for later PEPI response. These internal estimates do not establish clinical benefit or external generalization.
ai_technology: RBF support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors and nested classifier selection
organization: Barretos Cancer Hospital; Federal University of Uberlandia; Queen’s University

evidence.tested: The original abstract reports 49 patients for Ki 67 classification (41 responders, eight nonresponders) and 36 for PEPI (10 responders, 26 nonresponders). Baseline plasma and plasma after 2–4 treatment weeks addressed different response labels. Joint hyperparameter/SMOTE selection used inner stratified four-fold validation within outer leave-one-out evaluation. Selecting classifier family within the inner loop gave AUC .616 and .854 respectively, below separately selected best-family values .738 and .869.
evidence.unknown: Evidence access is limited to the complete original abstract and metadata, not full Methods or supplements. The parent trial was prospective, single-arm phase II; that label does not make this a prospective frozen-model evaluation. Cohorts are small and imbalanced, repeated spectra handling and detailed endpoint ascertainment remain unauthenticated, and the selected classifier-specific maximum can be optimistic. Spectral molecular assignments are tentative. No treatment selection benefit or external validation is established.
evidence.ai_role: Learned spectral classifiers distinguish clinically defined response labels; the narrow contribution is exploratory response discrimination under explicitly reported internal model selection.

source_review.scope: Complete original EuropePMC/PubMed abstract and primary bibliographic affiliations actually read; original institutional publication listing checked. No full Methods authenticated.

title: Environmental exposures classify recorded diabetes in NHANES
summary: A learned exposure model distinguished recorded diabetes in a random NHANES holdout with AUC .78. The analysis used 8,501 participants from 2005–2016. It establishes a retrospective predictive association, with no proof that the measured chemicals cause diabetes or predict its future onset.
ai_technology: Random-forest feature screening and LASSO regression
organization: Nanjing Medical University; Nanjing University Medical School

evidence.tested: The original abstract reports 5,953 discovery and 2,548 validation participants, training-set ten-fold feature selection using RF and LASSO, and diabetes AUC .80 versus .78. Separate linear-model validation R² values were .40 for insulin, .15 for fasting glucose and .17 for two-hour glucose; these are not additional independent discovery records.
evidence.unknown: This review had the complete original abstract and metadata, not full computational Methods. Exact feature identities, endpoint definition, sampling/measurement subsets, survey weighting, missingness and detailed preprocessing containment were not authenticated. The random validation set comes from the same survey periods; no external cohort or prospective incident-diabetes prediction is established. Chemical levels can reflect correlated exposure or disease-related processes; prediction does not establish causation. A bibliographic trial label does not make this observational analysis a randomized intervention.
evidence.ai_role: Learned feature selection and penalized regression quantify the predictive association between measured environmental exposures and recorded diabetes.

source_review.scope: Complete original primary abstract, dates and institutional affiliations actually read; full-text details were not available in this bounded review.

title: Topic models reveal differing clinical-note trajectories around vasculitis treatment
summary: An unsupervised analysis of 113,048 notes from 660 vasculitis patients found differing documentation trajectories around treatment initiation. Kidney-inflammation mentions peaked near treatment start, whereas other manifestations were more persistent; psychiatric symptoms also appeared before treatment. These are patterns in documentation, not measured disease incidence or causal treatment effects.
ai_technology: Latent Dirichlet allocation with cross-run topic stabilization
organization: Brigham and Women's Hospital; Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School

evidence.tested: Three learned 100-topic models yielded 90 stable topics, which two vasculitis experts independently labeled and reconciled. Notes were aligned from two years before to five years after treatment in three-month windows. Topics for glomerulonephritis peaked near treatment initiation while pulmonary and other symptom mentions persisted. Source-reported correlations with structured-data trends were .80 for treatment and .92 for glomerulonephritis.
evidence.unknown: This is one retrospective healthcare-system cohort of prevalent PR3/MPO-ANCA-positive cases, with no non-vasculitis comparator or independent clinical validation. Before-treatment notes were fewer and involved fewer patients. Topic scores are fractions of assigned words within pooled documentation windows, not patient risks or incidence; copy-and-paste, templates, note density and outside-system care can affect trends. Psychiatric symptoms and diagnostic delays were already known in vasculitis; this analysis does not establish their first discovery. No causal treatment effect or prospective diagnostic performance is shown.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised learned word-topic distributions expose documentation themes and temporal contrasts that would be missed by restricting analysis to structured codes.

source_review.scope: Original cohort definition, note preparation, learned topic generation, statistical trend analysis, full represented Results and Discussion limitations actually read.

title: Learned cervical-cancer recurrence models show modest internal discrimination
summary: In a retrospective four-hospital cervical-cancer analysis, learned models estimated recurrence and survival using recorded clinical and pathological factors. The 1,023-person test set was a random split of the same hospital pool. Site-specific recurrence discrimination was modest, and external clinical benefit was not established.
ai_technology: Support vector machine and tree-based survival/classification models
organization: Fudan University; Shanghai Key Laboratory of Female Reproductive Endocrine-Related Diseases; Shanghai Changjiang Science and Technology Development

evidence.tested: The source analyzed 5,112 surgically treated patients, 268 deaths and 343 recurrences, with an 80:20 stratified split, training-only ADASYN and five-fold grid search. For all 22 variables, test recurrence AUC was .794 for SVM versus .785 for logistic regression; site-specific recurrence AUC was .781 versus .776. SVM local/distant test sensitivities were .472/.424 at the represented operating points.
evidence.unknown: The source calls the test external, but Methods randomly divide patients pooled from the same four hospitals; this is internal evaluation. Some feature subsets are selected from whole-cohort Cox associations, and containment is not established. Inputs include postoperative pathology/adjuvant treatment, so this is not preoperative prediction or a causal treatment-effect model. Recurrence event counts differ 343 versus 344 across source locations. Binary risk endpoints do not supply a frozen future prediction horizon. Source claims of a universally best model are not supported across all displayed table cells; no clinical surveillance benefit is measured.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers and representations evaluate a defined clinical staging or recurrence target; conventional clinicopathologic associations are not separately counted as AI discoveries.

source_review.scope: Original patient cohort, computational Methods and represented Results actually read

title: Combined gastric radiopathomics lacks a significant gain in a small test cohort
summary: A retrospective gastric-cancer analysis combined CT features and learned pathology-slide features to classify stage groups. The combined model reached test AUC .837 in 60 patients, but its test advantage over the component models was not statistically established. Surgical slides limit claims of preoperative use.
ai_technology: ResNet-18 features, LASSO, SVM and multilayer perceptron
organization: Guangxi Medical University; Guangxi University of Chinese Medicine

evidence.tested: Two hundred surgically resected cases were split 140/60 by patient. ResNet-18 learned tumor-region features from pathology patches; selected pathology and CT signatures were combined. Component test AUCs were .797 for CT and .792 for pathology; combined AUC was .837. Original Results explicitly state no significant test superiority over either component despite a training difference.
evidence.unknown: This is one retrospective institution and a small random internal test. Methods do not clearly establish training-only fitting of every normalization, correlation filter and LASSO step. The best model families/signatures were selected after comparisons; untouched external confirmation is absent. Pathological slides came from surgical cases, with no demonstrated preoperative-biopsy deployment. Nonsignificant differences do not establish equivalence, and a nonsignificant goodness-of-fit test does not prove perfect calibration. Decision curves do not measure clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers and representations evaluate a defined clinical staging or recurrence target; conventional clinicopathologic associations are not separately counted as AI discoveries.

source_review.scope: Original patient cohort, computational Methods and represented Results actually read

title: Survival-forest-prioritized EPC1 suppresses measured A549 cell phenotypes
summary: A lung-cancer study selected EPC1 after it ranked highest in a learned survival model. Overexpression experiments in A549 cells then reduced proliferation, migration, invasion and colony formation. The finding is limited to one cell line; neither a clinical therapy nor direct control of autophagy was established.
ai_technology: Random survival forest gene-importance ranking
organization: Handan Central Hospital; Hebei General Hospital; Hebei Medical University

evidence.tested: A random survival forest selected from 117 model combinations ranked EPC1 highest among 69 candidate genes. Original Results explicitly link that ranking to selection for gain-of-function testing. The source reports three independent experimental repeats in A549 cells, reduced proliferation at later measured time points and reduced migration, invasion and colony formation.
evidence.unknown: EPC1 had already appeared in an earlier 2020LUAD prognostic signature; this record does not claim first discovery of EPC1 or its association with lung cancer. The prognostic model was selected by average performance across training and two nominal validation cohorts, so those cohorts do not independently confirm a frozen selected model; no prognostic performance number is promoted here. One cell line and overexpression do not establish physiological dose effects, patient benefit or a general tumor-suppressor role. Phenotypic assays do not demonstrate that EPC1 directly regulates chaperone-mediated autophagy. Search absence does not prove experimental priority.
evidence.ai_role: Learned survival-forest importance guided selection of the experimentally tested gene, following conventional coexpression/differential-expression screening.

source_review.scope: Original computational gene selection, ensemble model selection/importance Results and biological outcome Results actually read; no experimental recipe needed.

title: Three-gene neural model distinguishes tumor from adjacent liver tissue arrays
summary: A learned three-gene model distinguished known HBV-associated liver-tumor tissue from adjacent tissue in public expression datasets. The source reports validation AUC .849 across 140 arrays; the original dataset includes multiple samples from 11 patients. This is tissue classification, with no evidence of early screening or future cancer conversion.
ai_technology: Random forest, SVM-RFE, LASSO and three-gene artificial neural network
organization: Southwest Medical University; Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich; Ohio University; University of South Dakota

evidence.tested: Intersecting RF, SVM-RFE and LASSO selections produced HHIP, CXCL14 and CDHR2. The source used GSE121248 with 70 tumor/37 adjacent arrays for development and GSE55092 with 49 tumor/91 adjacent arrays for reported validation AUC .849(95% CI .773–.916), compared with training AUC .948. Original GEO metadata describes up to 17 whole-liver tissue samples per liver from 11 HCC patients, with selected laser-capture samples also included.
evidence.unknown: Array counts are not independent patient counts. Adjacent tissues come from livers already affected by HCC, not a prospective cohort of people with uncomplicated hepatitis B. Multiple regions and sample modalities can affect discrimination and uncertainty. GeneScore median thresholds were computed on each dataset, so the validation transformation is not a demonstrated frozen deployment rule. No blood test, prospective early detection, future HBV-to-cancer conversion, causal immune mechanism or clinical benefit was validated. The source association/subtype analyses reuse these datasets.
evidence.ai_role: Learned feature-selection algorithms and an ANN discriminate tissue labels; conventional enrichment and inferred immune scores are not separately counted as new experimental biology.

source_review.scope: Original data definition, learned feature screening, ANN Methods and reported validation Results actually read; original GEO indexed study-design metadata independently checked.

title: Neural-model optimization improves tested silver-carp oil extraction
summary: An ANN-guided search selected extraction conditions for silver-carp viscera oil, followed by physical confirmation. The measured yield was 79.44%, compared with 76.68% at a response-surface-selected setting. This is a small process-optimization experiment; separate encapsulation improvements were not shown to be AI-selected.
ai_technology: Multilayer perceptron with genetic-algorithm search over its learned response surface
organization: China Agricultural University; Mississippi State University

evidence.tested: The ANN learned from 17 response-surface-design experiments, with 70/15/15 training/test/validation allocation and a three-input, ten-hidden-node architecture selected through trials. Its learned response served as the genetic-search fitness function. The selected setting predicted 82.45% extraction; follow-up measurements yielded 79.44%, versus 76.68% for the response-surface setting, with source-reported significant difference.
evidence.unknown: Seventeen training-design runs produce very small evaluation subsets, and architecture choice by trial/error limits generalization claims. The physical optimized-setting measurement is distinct from the reported high fit correlation; its 79.44% yield is below the 82.45% prediction. The result concerns one byproduct/process system rather than universal extraction efficiency. Gelatin/coacervation optimization, capsule stability and simulated digestion are separate conventional downstream experiments, so they are not credited as additional AI-guided discoveries.
evidence.ai_role: A learned nonlinear extraction-response model actively supplied the search objective for a newly tested process setting, rather than only fitting previously measured yields.

source_review.scope: Original ANN/search construction,17-experiment comparison/validation Methods and represented extraction Results actually read; later microencapsulation claims not attributed to learned optimization.

title: A learned RNA score associates with survival in archived bladder-cancer data
summary: A ten-RNA LASSO score separated overall-survival groups in archived bladder-cancer data. The internal validation subset reported one-, two- and three-year AUCs of 0.663, 0.624 and 0.630. This is a retrospective association with outcome-informed screening, not a verified immunotherapy-response test.
ai_technology: LASSO
organization: Wenzhou Medical University; Zhejiang University

source_review.scope: Primary computational Methods on score construction and cohort data; Results on TCGA survival; no experimental protocol review

evidence.tested: The TCGA analysis split 406 cases into 204 training and 202 validation records after prognostic screening; cohort-specific median scores defined high and low groups.
evidence.unknown: Outcome screening preceded the split, so the validation subset is not untouched. The separate 65-case local series is stated as collected in 2022–2023 yet reports three-year AUCs in a May 2024 article; that timeline is unresolved and its performance is excluded here. Cohort counts vary between 412 and 406. Treatment-response proxies, drug predictions and proposed molecular mechanisms are not validated clinical outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO fitted the ten-RNA survival signature after univariate outcome screening, enabling the represented score-to-recorded-survival comparison.

title: Learned screening identifies liver-expression differences across archived cohorts
summary: Three feature-selection methods nominated five expression candidates for fatty liver disease. The source reports concordant expression differences in pooled external liver datasets, with individual-marker AUCs of 0.652–0.751. This is a retrospective tissue association, not a diagnostic test or a causal immune mechanism.
ai_technology: LASSO; support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination; random forest
organization: Fudan University

source_review.scope: Primary front;computational Methods2.1,2.5 and Results3.4–3.5;primary deposited metadata status;experimental procedures not reviewed

evidence.ai_role: LASSO,SVM-RFE and random forest fitted disease-label feature selectors; their intersection selected BBOX1,FOSB,NR4A2,RAB26 and SOCS2 for later expression comparisons.
evidence.tested: Training combined50 disease and31 control samples. External pooled datasets contained271 disease and85 control samples; source-reported marker AUCs were0.734,0.751,0.709,0.670 and0.652.
evidence.unknown: Original datasets and batch correction can confound retrospective comparisons; no prospective or separate-team clinical validation is established. BBOX1 was not significantly different in the206-case/10-control dataset alone, despite significance in the pooled set. Source figure captions inconsistently call the five-marker intersection seven markers; RF selection counts also vary. Earlier roles of FOSB and SOCS2 are acknowledged. Protein experiments, mechanistic claims and inferred immune-cell causality are outside this represented result.

title: Answer timings classify insomnia-questionnaire labels in a student cohort
summary: Learned classifiers used the time taken to answer seven questionnaire items to distinguish concurrent insomnia-symptom score labels. Repeated internally balanced evaluations reported an AUROC of 0.824 for raw timings. This is agreement with a self-report scale, not an insomnia diagnosis or a forecast.
ai_technology: Logistic regression; multilayer perceptron
organization: Nanjing Medical University

source_review.scope: Original primary front;Sections2.1–2.7,3.4–3.5 and4;current primary bibliographic status metadata

evidence.ai_role: Logistic regression and a multilayer perceptron learned a mapping from seven response durations to the concurrent ISI score threshold; model interpretation assessed derived timing features.
evidence.tested: A 2,729-student screening cohort supplied questionnaire timings. Ten random balanced samples each contained141 symptom-positive and141 symptom-negative participants, evaluated with10-fold cross-validation. Raw-timing logistic regression and MLP each reported AUROC0.824.
evidence.unknown: Reference labels are ISI scores of at least8, not independent clinical interviews. The same questionnaire supplied timing features and reference scores. Model comparison and first-fold tuning do not establish a fully nested evaluation; preprocessing and feature selection containment are incomplete. The source reports inconsistent final participant denominators, and balanced resampling does not establish population predictive values. The single-university setting and uncontrolled device/environment effects limit generalization; prospective utility is unestablished.

title: Learned screening guides a blood-marker comparison between stroke subtypes
summary: Learned feature screening nominated FCER1G for a subsequent clinical blood-expression check. In the source’s selected samples, the marker differed between 36 cardioembolic and 25 large-artery stroke cases, with an apparent AUC of 0.8444. This preliminary result does not establish an early diagnostic test or a causal immune mechanism.
ai_technology: LASSO; random forest
organization: Nanyang Normal University; Nanyang Central Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary feature-selection Methods and high-level original clinical expression Results; assay protocols excluded

evidence.tested: LASSO and RF intersected with a coexpression screen to select FCER1G. The original clinical assay series contained 98 samples across five groups; the represented contrast is cardioembolic versus large-artery stroke.
evidence.unknown: Discovery combined blood and atrial-tissue datasets with different phenotypes, which limits interpretation of the screening model. The clinical comparison is small, selected and subject to age and cardiovascular comorbidity confounding. The apparent AUC comes from the same assayed cases, not an external diagnostic test. The separate nomogram includes cardiogenic-etiology information and is not represented as an independent prediction result. Laboratory procedures were not independently reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted LASSO and random forest selected the marker for the later expression comparison; network analysis alone is not credited as enabling AI.

title: A learned prostate-expression score associates with recorded progression
summary: A CoxBoost and random-survival-forest score separated progression-free-survival groups across archived prostate-cancer datasets. Reported three-year AUCs ranged from 0.677 to 0.933 in the additional datasets. All those datasets informed final model selection, so they do not provide untouched external validation.
ai_technology: CoxBoost; random survival forest
organization: Xinjiang Medical University

source_review.scope: Original primary computational model-selection and cohort survival Methods/Results only

evidence.tested: The source trained on 494 TCGA records and considered 101 algorithm combinations. Five additional dataset groups, totaling 597 records as reported, were used to choose the best average concordance model. The final signature contained 13 genes.
evidence.unknown: The additional cohorts selected the final model, and group-specific median scores do not validate a fixed threshold. Cross-database patient independence and endpoint harmonization are not fully established. High training performance and retrospective associations do not establish calibrated clinical prediction, mast-cell causality or benefit from immunotherapy. Drug-sensitivity predictions are excluded.
evidence.ai_role: CoxBoost and random survival forests fitted and selected a progression-related expression score; the learned model enables the represented survival association.

title: Recorded symptoms classify persistent smell and taste complaints after COVID-19
summary: In a 413-person retrospective questionnaire dataset, learned models classified reported smell and taste complaints persisting beyond four weeks. The selected 83-record test reported AUCs up to 0.96 for taste and 0.97 for smell. This does not establish an early prospective forecast or improved treatment.
ai_technology: Random forest; XGBoost; LightGBM
organization: Qassim University

source_review.scope: Original primary clinical design, model training, persistence Results and Table8; archived publication metadata

evidence.tested: The study used a random 330-record training/validation set and 83-record test. Persistence predictors included symptom continuation after two weeks and smell/taste loss during infection.
evidence.unknown: The study is described as cross-sectional and does not establish that every predictor was recorded before outcome ascertainment. Whole-data feature ranking and test-informed algorithm selection limit generalization. Confusion-matrix paragraph denominators and percentages conflict with Table8; this record uses only table/ROC AUC ranges, not its accuracy or sensitivity claims. No external clinical validation, calibrated population risk or causal effect is established.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted tree ensembles map questionnaire and symptom features to recorded persistent-complaint labels; the represented result is retrospective clinical-label evaluation.

title: Selected stroke-expression candidates show uneven agreement across datasets
summary: LASSO selected 19 expression candidates in archived stroke samples. Four candidates—SCO2, ARF1, APP and NFE2L2—were reported as elevated in both additional datasets, while the full sets of significant genes differed. This is a retrospective expression association, not validation of a 19-gene diagnostic test or a cell-death mechanism.
ai_technology: LASSO
organization: Guangxi Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary data/LASSO Methods and external expression Results; primary GEO study metadata; no operational laboratory procedures reviewed

evidence.ai_role: A fitted LASSO classifier selected 19 genes from 30 prefiltered candidates, determining the panel examined in the additional datasets.
evidence.tested: The discovery dataset contains 69 stroke specimens sampled at three post-event times plus 23 control specimens. Additional datasets included 39 stroke/24 control records and 10 stroke/5 control specimens; the latter also has repeated time points.
evidence.unknown: Repeated specimens are not independent patients. The discovery AUC of 1 is an apparent fit, not external diagnostic performance; additional analyses compare individual gene expression and ROC curves rather than a frozen combined panel. Screening, time-point and batch effects limit inference. The genes came from a previously defined pathway list, and no new causal role, biological subtype or clinical utility is established.

title: A learned six-gene score associates with archived glioma survival
summary: Random-forest and LASSO selection produced a six-gene score associated with overall survival in archived lower-grade glioma data. The source also reports survival separation in three additional datasets using each cohort’s own median cutoff. This does not establish a fixed clinical threshold, a causal tumor mechanism or benefit from a selected drug.
ai_technology: Random survival forest; LASSO
organization: Xinjiang Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary data/model-construction Methods and survival Results only; no operational laboratory procedures reviewed

evidence.ai_role: Random forest and LASSO selected overlapping genes, followed by multivariable Cox scoring; the learned selection enables the represented expression-to-survival association.
evidence.tested: The source divided 497 TCGA cases into 348 development and 149 internal-validation records. Six genes remained after intersecting selectors and Cox refinement; survival comparisons were repeated in CGGA325, CGGA693 and GSE16011.
evidence.unknown: Prognostic screening before the split and reuse of the full TCGA cohort as Test2 limit independence. The three additional datasets used cohort-specific medians, so fixed-threshold validation is unestablished. Dataset overlap, endpoint harmonization and full preprocessing isolation were not independently reconstructed. Outcome-selected clusters are not newly verified biological subtypes; inferred immune activity and drug sensitivity are outside this result.

title: Three selected expression candidates agree in an osteoarthritis cell comparison
summary: A multi-algorithm expression screen nominated four osteoarthritis candidates. In the source’s subsequent cell comparison, MAP3K8 was higher and AGMAT and PER1 were lower, while XIST showed no significant difference. This limited assay result does not establish diagnostic performance, a causal disease role or treatment benefit.
ai_technology: LASSO; random forest; bagged trees; Bayesian classifier; Boruta; learning vector quantization
organization: Harbin Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary computational selection Methods and high-level measured Results/Figure8; primary GEO metadata; no operational laboratory procedures reviewed

evidence.ai_role: Six fitted feature-selection/classification methods nominated genes selected by at least five approaches, determining the four candidates checked in the later assay.
evidence.tested: The computational screen used GSE12021 and GSE55235. The source’s original assay Results and Figure8 report three concordant candidate-expression directions and one nonsignificant comparison.
evidence.unknown: The original GSE12021 counts are arrays, not unique people: its 20 osteoarthritis arrays represent 10 patients across paired platforms, and 13 control arrays represent nine people. The single-cell series comprises three osteoarthritis donors with relatively intact and damaged tissues, not independent healthy donors. Synovial screening and the later cartilage-cell comparison concern different contexts. Experimental replication details and procedures were not independently inspected; the result is not clinical or separate-team validation.

title: A mortality model is evaluated in five retrospective bypass-surgery cohorts
summary: A three-learner ensemble evaluated recorded mortality after isolated coronary bypass surgery. It reported AUCs of 0.9145 in a 952-person internal test and 0.8585 and 0.8553 in two additional hospital cohorts. These retrospective results do not establish a preoperative warning system or improved care.
ai_technology: XGBoost; CatBoost; LightGBM ensemble
organization: Shandong University; Nanjing Medical University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Tongji University; Ningxia Medical University

source_review.scope: Original clinical eligibility/outcome/model design and external-cohort discrimination Results;current PubMed bibliographic metadata

evidence.ai_role: XGBoost,CatBoost and LightGBM classifiers were trained and combined as the XCL ensemble to estimate recorded postoperative mortality.
evidence.tested: A 4,764-person pool from three hospitals was split into 3,812 development and 952 internal-test records. Additional hospital cohorts contained 1,733 and 415 patients. The outcome was death within 30 days or during postoperative hospitalization.
evidence.unknown: Inputs include perioperative variables, and an exclusively preoperative prediction time is unestablished. Optimal thresholds used Youden indices; model/threshold comparisons do not establish locked prospective performance. Low event counts, retrospective missing-data exclusions and an Asian cohort limit generalization. AUC differences and decision-curve analyses do not demonstrate clinical benefit or causal effects.

title: A learned gastric-expression score associates with recorded survival
summary: An autoencoder-derived expression score was associated with survival in archived gastric-cancer cohorts and a TCGA comparison. The score used learned transcriptomic features followed by survival regression. The result does not establish a new stem-cell identity, treatment response or a clinically deployable risk threshold.
ai_technology: One-class logistic regression; autoencoder neural network
organization: Zhengzhou University

source_review.scope: Original selected computational/data Methods and represented cohort/physical Results; laboratory/sample preparation procedures excluded

evidence.ai_role: One-class logistic regression derives a source-defined stemness index. A trained autoencoder learns nonlinear expression features subsequently selected and combined with Cox survival modeling, enabling the represented score-outcome association.
evidence.tested: Five expression datasets containing 1,051 samples were split 4:1 for model development and internal assessment. The source reports survival separation in both subsets and in TCGA, where each cohort was divided at its own median score.
evidence.unknown: Discovery preprocessing and stemness-feature selection can reuse cohort information; an untouched fixed-threshold test is not established. The text mentions nine selected prognostic features but displays a five-feature formula; full final coefficient selection remains unverified because the primary supplementary workbook was inaccessible. No reconstruction of the trained model was performed. Treatment-response extrapolations, inferred immune states and the cell-population identity claim are excluded.

title: A small smartwatch study shows uneven detection of known heart disease
summary: A trained neural model classified weekly heart-rate patterns in a 12-person test set with known cardiovascular-disease labels. The selected contrastive-loss variant reported mean weekly sensitivity of 67% with a 47-point between-person standard deviation and specificity of 100%. Some affected participants were consistently missed; these results do not establish safe disease exclusion.
ai_technology: Neural curve classifier; weekly logistic aggregation
organization: Delft University of Technology; Haga Teaching Hospital

source_review.scope: Official primary BioC original article sections: Curve classifier/weekly aggregation;ME-TIME cohort;subject-separated tuning;Table3 and clinical limitations; no laboratory-method validation

evidence.ai_role: A trained two-layer neural classifier maps acceleration/deceleration heart-rate curves to disease labels; learned weekly aggregation and contrastive training enable the represented clinical-label test.
evidence.tested: The ME-TIME cohort contained 42 participants. Thirty were used for development and subject-separated tuning; the test comprised six reference participants and six with atrial fibrillation or heart failure. Sensitivity/specificity average per-person weekly scores, not independent weekly patients.
evidence.unknown: Reference and disease groups differ in age, BMI and comorbidity. Twelve test participants and correlated weeks limit precision and generalization. Variant comparisons are exploratory. Several discussion paragraphs conflict with Table3 or misinterpret high specificity as a rule-out guarantee; neither rule-out safety nor prevention benefit is represented. Prospective data collection does not establish a frozen prospective model evaluation.

title: An infant cohort model ranks perinatal features for gastrointestinal outcomes
summary: A random-forest analysis of 6,060 infants ranked birth weight, cord-blood pH and maternal age as important features for recorded first-year gastrointestinal-disorder labels. The result describes model importance in one hospital cohort, not causal risk factors or a validated preventive-care tool.
ai_technology: Random forest
organization: University of Salento; University of Naples Federico II

source_review.scope: Official primary BioC original article sections: Participants/outcome reference;ML/preprocessing/feature selection;random-forest ranking Results and model limitations; no laboratory-method validation

evidence.ai_role: A fitted random forest ranks variables by impurity reduction when classifying clinician-assessed colic, regurgitation and constipation outcomes. The learned ranking, not conventional regression alone, enables the represented feature pattern.
evidence.tested: Outcomes were assessed by a trained pediatrician using RomeIV criteria during first-year follow-up. The source reports a 70:30 split, model comparisons and weighted-average F1 of0.74, without a complete condition-specific independent-validation account.
evidence.unknown: Prospective enrollment is distinct from model locking before new outcomes. Preprocessing/feature-selection containment and class resampling details are incomplete. Impurity importance can favor continuous variables and does not establish effect direction or causation. The source alternates between the random-forest classification model and a logistic-regression web tool; no deployed-tool accuracy, prevention benefit or independent cohort confirmation is represented.

title: A plasma-ratio search identifies exploratory Alzheimer case-label associations
summary: An SVM-guided search selected plasma-protein ratios associated with Alzheimer case labels in 60 stored donor samples. Candidate combinations included KYNU/MSR1, NCAN/PRTG and IL-5Rα/GFRα-1. The groups differed in average age by about 13 years, and the search reused the evaluation data; this is not independent diagnostic validation.
ai_technology: Linear support vector machine; feature-subset search
organization: University of Massachusetts Lowell; Bedford VA Healthcare System

source_review.scope: Official primary BioC original article sections: Clinical donor metadata;preprocessing;SVM and global feature search;ratio Results and age analysis; no laboratory-method validation

evidence.ai_role: Linear SVM classification and exhaustive/forward subset search select protein ratios for separating donor-group labels; the learned selection enables the represented candidate associations.
evidence.tested: The reanalysis used 38 control and22 Alzheimer-labeled samples, with82 protein measurements generating6,642 ordered ratios. Leave-one-out scores informed selection of best subsets; observed selected-ratio differences were then examined in the same samples.
evidence.unknown: Feature search and hyperparameter selection reused the LOOCV results, so headline98–100percent separation is selection-informed and not a new independent test. Mean ages were66.5 versus79.7; adding age as another classifier input does not adjust that confounding. The source also mixes22 and23 disease-sample denominators in some results. This is a reanalysis of previously collected data, without new assays, causal protein interactions or demonstrated clinical utility.

title: Registry models link prescribing patterns to clinic and medication context
summary: In 864,339 registry patients with atrial fibrillation, an enhanced XGBoost model identified documented anticoagulant prescriptions with a test AUROC of0.811. Clinic-location income, clinic size and region contributed permutation importance alongside age and concurrent medications. These are descriptive prescribing-pattern associations, not causal socioeconomic effects.
ai_technology: XGBoost; random forest; penalized logistic regression
organization: Stanford University; American College of Cardiology

source_review.scope: Official primary BioC original article sections: Registry/outcome/feature Methods;patient split/tuning;test permutation-importance Results and limitations; no laboratory-method validation

evidence.ai_role: Fitted classifiers map patient and clinic features to documented prescriptions. Permutation analysis on the test set identifies model-used contextual information beyond a clinical risk-score feature set.
evidence.tested: PINNACLE records from January2017–June2018 were split80:20 by patient; hyperparameters used fivefold training cross-validation. Prescription status and inputs came from the most recent three-month record window.
evidence.unknown: Income is a clinic-ZIP-code mean, not each patient’s household income. Concurrent medications and INR can reflect prescribing or monitoring consequences rather than causes; same-clinic records can occur on both sides of the random split. Missing fields and voluntary outpatient practices limit representativeness. The CHA2DS2-VASc comparator is a clinical stroke-risk score, not a prescription model; no causal disparity, guideline benefit or improved treatment outcome is established.

title: Registry models estimate lead-extraction adverse-event labels
summary: Models trained on European lead-extraction registry data were evaluated against major adverse events in a separate UK series. A support-vector classifier reported an ROC area of0.764 versus0.677 for the EROS score. Test-set feature selection limits this as a fully independent assessment, and neural scores were not calibrated individual probabilities.
ai_technology: Support vector machine; shallow neural network
organization: King's College London; Guy’s and St Thomas’ Hospital

source_review.scope: Actual relevant primary computational/clinical Methods and high-level Results read; no operational biological protocols inspected; original indexed publisher publication history and PubMed date conflict checked.

evidence.ai_role: Fitted classifiers map registry clinical/procedural features to documented major adverse-event labels.
evidence.tested: The analyzed development group contained3122 patients with53 events and the analyzed UK group998 with24 events; nominal recruited cohort sizes were3555 and1171. Registry-overlapping UK patients were removed.
evidence.unknown: Sequential backward feature selection explicitly used the test dataset, so the external series was not untouched. Missing binary records were excluded and other values imputed as normal. The source percent for3122/3555 is inconsistent. Neural softmax scores should not be interpreted as calibrated individual event probabilities; no prospective decision benefit or statistically established superiority is claimed. The original publisher publication history gives online publication on April 27, 2022, while PubMed records April 28; the represented date follows the original publisher.

title: ECG models identify concurrent high-risk imaging features in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
summary: A pretrained variational-autoencoder ECG representation supported classifiers for four imaging findings in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. In233 patients at another centre, ROC areas ranged from0.68 for extensive enhancement to0.91 for apical aneurysm, with only one aneurysm-positive patient. This is retrospective reference-label evaluation, not a demonstration that imaging can safely be omitted.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder; dense neural-network classifiers
organization: Johns Hopkins University; Tufts Medical Center; Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences

source_review.scope: Actual relevant primary computational/clinical Methods and high-level Results read; no operational biological protocols inspected

evidence.ai_role: A VAE pretrained on88105 ECGs provides24 latent features to learned classifiers, alongside age, sex and heart rate, linking electrical patterns to contemporaneous imaging labels.
evidence.tested: Tufts1930 patients were partitioned1544 development and386 holdout, followed by233 Amrita patients. Endpoints were reduced ejection fraction, extreme wall thickness, apical aneurysm and extensive late gadolinium enhancement.
evidence.unknown: Only one external aneurysm-positive case makes that endpoint highly uncertain. CMR labels were available in selected1584/1930 development-site and104/233 external patients. Hypothetical imaging savings combined development and evaluation cases; they are not prospective savings or safety evidence. A linked editorial is authenticated as Comment/Editorial, not a correction; its full body was not reviewed. No clinical-benefit or causal interpretation is established.

title: Learned symptom clusters track heart-failure emergency outcomes
summary: Fitted k-means partitioned nine recorded symptoms in438 emergency patients with prior heart failure into three groups. The indigestion group had adjusted odds ratios of1.8 for both acute heart-failure exacerbation and30-day adverse cardiac events compared with the group lacking indigestion and dyspnea. These are exploratory same-cohort associations, not a validated triage intervention.
ai_technology: K-means clustering
organization: University of Pittsburgh; University of Pittsburgh Medical Center

source_review.scope: Original primary clinical/computational Methods, reference definitions, model evaluation and Results independently read; no operational laboratory sections

evidence.ai_role: Fitted k-means learns symptom-based patient partitions; the resulting assignments enable clinical outcome comparisons. PCA performed poorly and was not the retained partition.
evidence.tested: A secondary analysis of prospectively collected emergency presentations used438 patients and nine binary symptoms. Silhouette analysis selected three clusters of178,100 and160 patients. Two reviewers adjudicated clinical outcomes; regression adjusted for selected baseline variables.
evidence.unknown: The same selected cohort was used to discover and test clusters, with univariate-informed adjustment. Confidence intervals for the reported odds ratios round to1.0; no independent replication or causal interpretation is established. Outcomes include a heterogeneous composite; clustering is not proof of distinct disease mechanisms or improved emergency decisions.

title: Learned marker selection precedes mixed macrophage expression checks
summary: LASSO-based selection and network prioritization nominated five periodontitis-associated candidates. A source-reported macrophage comparison found ATF3 and CXCR4 higher, and TXN, CBX3 and MBP lower, at RNA and protein levels. This record represents those expression observations, without adopting a clinical diagnostic test or a causal disease mechanism.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection
organization: Guangxi Medical University

source_review.scope: Actual relevant primary computational/clinical Methods and high-level Results read; no operational biological protocols inspected

evidence.ai_role: LASSO selects22 expression candidates, followed by protein-network prioritization of five that undergo a new expression check. AI credit is limited to nomination, not downstream causal interpretation.
evidence.tested: Actual computational selection sections and nonactionable expression Results were read. The source reports concordant RNA/protein directions in an inflammatory macrophage comparison.
evidence.unknown: Operational culture/assay protocols and supplementary replicate details were not inspected. Archived discovery and validation arrays contain repeated gingival sites per patient, with healthy sites within periodontitis patients and possible cohort overlap; another series includes peri-implantitis and a further RNA-sequencing series includes gingivitis. Clinical discrimination, independent patient validation, novel macrophage taxonomy and therapeutic/causal claims are outside the represented result. The reported model C-index is not adopted as an AUC.

title: ECG-image model identifies concurrent low ejection fraction in archived records
summary: A DenseNet121 model learned to identify echocardiography-referenced ejection fraction below50% from ECG images. It reported ROC areas of0.92 on an internal ECG test set and0.88 at another healthcare centre. The study tests concurrent diagnostic-label discrimination, without establishing early warning or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: DenseNet121 convolutional neural network
organization: Narayana Health

source_review.scope: Original primary clinical/computational Methods, reference definitions, model evaluation and Results independently read; no operational laboratory sections

evidence.ai_role: A trained convolutional network maps cropped ECG trace images to a concurrent echocardiographic low-ejection-fraction label.
evidence.tested: Development used119,281 same-day ECG/echo pairs from104,697 people. ECGs were randomly split into107,147 training,2,020 validation and10,114 test records. Another centre supplied roughly24,300 pairs; the internal-test Youden threshold0.18 was carried to that cohort.
evidence.unknown: Random ECG-level splitting does not establish separation of repeated patients. The external denominator is24,323 in text versus24,319 in the table. The internal threshold was selected on test outcomes; the external data are archived, not a prospectively frozen workflow. Standardized device images and same-day selected imaging pairs limit generalization; no screening benefit or diagnosis of future dysfunction is established.

title: Patient models distinguish recorded STEMI mortality outcomes
summary: A random-forest model evaluated on an internal holdout from1700 STEMI patients reported ROC areas of0.808 for in-hospital mortality and0.783 for30-day mortality. This source-specific evaluation uses clinical and complication-related inputs; it does not establish a pre-treatment warning tool or improved care.
ai_technology: Random forest; multilayer perceptron; tree ensembles
organization: Govind Ballabh Pant Institute of Post Graduate Medical Education and Research

source_review.scope: Actual relevant primary computational/clinical Methods and high-level Results read; no operational biological protocols inspected

evidence.ai_role: Supervised classifiers learn clinical-feature relationships to observed in-hospital and30-day mortality; SHAP describes model-used features.
evidence.tested: Patients were recruited in2021–2023 and later divided1360/340 for training and internal evaluation, stratified by mortality; resampling was limited to training. The cohort had168 in-hospital and210 thirty-day deaths.
evidence.unknown: Outcome-informed feature screening and data refinement are described before the isolated split, with incomplete nesting detail. Inputs include shock, treatment delay, mechanical complications and echocardiography, so an early pre-treatment prediction time is not established. The paper calls random forest best, but Table3 gives higher30-day ROC areas to other models; no overall-best or significance claim is adopted. Prospective recruitment alone does not establish prospective model validation; no external cohort or treatment benefit was demonstrated.

title: Generative models nominate unconfirmed MDM2-binding candidates
summary: RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and AlphaFold supported two source-labeled candidate designs for the oncology-related MDM2–p53 interaction. Conventional enhanced-sampling simulations favored one candidate over the other and the reference. These are unconfirmed computational candidates, without measured binding affinity or therapeutic evidence.
ai_technology: RFdiffusion; ProteinMPNN; AlphaFold
organization: University of Science and Technology of China; University of Nigeria; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

source_review.scope: Exact original publisher front, primary abstract and nonprocedural Conclusion in author deposit; full operational sequence/design Methods not read or retained

evidence.ai_role: The primary Conclusion attributes backbone generation to RFdiffusion, candidate sequence modeling to ProteinMPNN and structure prediction/refinement to AlphaFold. Learned design is separate from the conventional simulation comparison.
evidence.tested: The source reports two computational candidates and an enhanced-sampling comparison favoring its Pep1 candidate relative to Pep2 and the reference. Validation3 refers only to the reported explicit computational comparison within the discovery study, not experimental binding confirmation.
evidence.unknown: No empirical affinity, target novelty, clinical benefit or independent replication is established. Operational sequences/design recipes and full simulation implementation details were not inspected or retained. Molecular simulations do not establish actual inhibitor activity or therapeutic utility; the represented result remains conditional on the source’s computational models.

title: Smartwatch QT estimates show limited agreement with manual ECG readings
summary: The QT-logs study applied a trained U-Net to smartwatch ECGs and compared QTc estimates with blinded manual12-lead measurements. Among66 day-ten comparisons, mean bias was about−1 millisecond, but agreement limits extended from−46 to45 milliseconds. The selected low-risk cohort contained very few critical QTc prolongations, leaving accuracy for dangerous prolongation uncertain.
ai_technology: U-Net convolutional neural network
organization: Aix-Marseille University; Assistance Publique–Hôpitaux de Marseille; Cardiologs

source_review.scope: Original clinical reference/readout Methods, CNN operation/training description, paired agreement Results/Table2 and limitations; drug efficacy not assessed

evidence.ai_role: A U-Net trained on6315 annotated resting/Holter recordings identifies waveform boundaries; beat-level QTc estimates are aggregated for received smartwatch tracings. No smartwatch ECGs were used in training.
