evidence.tested: Newly transmitted smartwatch ECGs were automatically analyzed in a prospective paired-measurement study. Eighty-five people entered;76 received daily follow-up. Manual12-lead reference comparisons were available for71 baseline,53 day-six and66 day-ten visits, with blinded readers.
evidence.unknown: Recordings were not consistently simultaneous and agreement was only moderate; very few critical prolongations prevented validation of clinically dangerous thresholds. Young selected participants, technical exclusions and incomplete transmissions limit transfer. No drug-safety, arrhythmia-prevention or treatment-effect conclusion is adopted. Validation3 reflects the direct paired measurement check, not independent replication or proven model-guided clinical benefit.

title: Kidney-injury models show changing laboratory contributions before recorded onset
summary: A reweighted XGBoost analysis of hospital records compared feature contributions at24,48 and72 hours before kidney-injury onset. Laboratory measurements accounted for54.5% of the model-score contrast increase from72 to24 hours. This describes learned-model attributions in one hospital, not the causal effect of changing those measurements.
ai_technology: Reweighted XGBoost; SHAP
organization: Jinan University; University of Kansas Medical Center

source_review.scope: Original primary clinical/computational Methods, model evaluation and high-level Results read; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: Modified feature-sampling weights emphasize prespecified modifiable feature views; fitted models and SHAP-derived score contrasts quantify how learned associations differ by retrospective prediction window.
evidence.tested: The24-hour cohort contained144084 encounters; models trained on2010–2016 and tested on2017–2018. Cohort sizes differed for longer windows. Fifty random-seed repetitions informed mean attributions.
evidence.unknown: Feature views were deliberately reweighted, so their importance is conditional on that modeling choice. AKI cases were anchored to first onset, controls to last creatinine measurement; repeated encounters and different window cohorts limit comparisons. Correlations among modifiable factors were not modeled explicitly. The source’s predicted intervention benefits are not measured treatment effects, patient-specific causal risks or prevention evidence. Supplementary algorithm/hyperparameter details were not independently read.

title: External ICU tests expose low positive predictive value for an AF model
summary: A CatBoost model trained on Amsterdam ICU records reached ROC areas of0.77 in MIMIC-IV and0.84 at Ghent when transferred directly. In the respective imbalanced evaluation sets, positive predictive values were0.07 and0.02. Local retraining improved some metrics, but these retrospective tests do not establish a clinically useful alert.
ai_technology: CatBoost gradient boosting
organization: Ghent University; Amsterdam University Medical Centers

source_review.scope: Actual original relevant clinical/computational Methods, reference labels, evaluation Results and limitations read

evidence.ai_role: Learned CatBoost classifiers use12-hour clinical-feature windows ending before recorded AF and are tested for hospital transfer; Powershap selects features.
evidence.tested: Development used18163 admissions, including2000 with nursing-chart AF. Matched AF/no-AF pairs stayed together in an80:20 split, and unmatched controls formed the imbalanced test set. External evaluation covered archived MIMIC-IV and Ghent cohorts; reported direct-transfer precision is specific to those sampled event/control constructions.
evidence.unknown: Nursing-chart timing may lag actual arrhythmia; prior AF history was unavailable, so this is not securely new-onset AF. Admission-level splitting does not establish isolation of repeated people. External feature availability influenced the common feature set. What the source calls recalibration includes local model retraining, not merely a probability adjustment. Calibration/ROC metrics do not prove a calibrated patient-specific AF risk or clinical benefit; event-aligned retrospective windows are not live alarms. Online supplementary procedures were not independently read.

title: Clinical model distinguishes selected rare-infection diagnoses in archived admissions
summary: HistGradientBoosting used early-admission clinical records to distinguish a selected composite of rare infections from urgent-admission controls. The primary holdout table reports an ROC area of 0.937; a separate comparative validation table reports mean sensitivity of 61.9%. This is internal retrospective evaluation, without demonstrated earlier diagnosis or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Histogram gradient boosting; SHAP
organization: Auburn University; Mayo Clinic

source_review.scope: Original primary clinical/computational Methods, model evaluation and high-level Results read; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: A fitted boosted-tree classifier maps early clinical and laboratory features to chart-confirmed diagnostic labels; SHAP describes model-used features.
evidence.tested: The study used1494 cases and10000 sampled controls from2010–2023, with a70:30 patient split. Training-only cross-validation, SMOTE and isotonic recalibration are described. The paper distinguishes a448-case/3001-control test composition.
evidence.unknown: The abstract and cross-validation table report AUC0.947 while the separate holdout/ablation table reports0.937; these are retained as different reported evaluations, not silently equated. Early predictor timing does not prove predictions preceded actual diagnosis. The selected six-disease composite and sampled-control prevalence limit calibration and clinical transfer. Supplementary inclusion details were not read. No pathogen methods, treatment protocol, real-world alert deployment or prospective outcome benefit is represented. The 61.9% sensitivity comes from the comparative validation table, not an authenticated operating point for the separate holdout AUC of 0.937.

title: Small clinical CT-image check reveals COVIDC classification errors
summary: In a radiologist-supervised hospital check using scans excluded from training, COVIDC classified9 of10 supplied COVID-labeled images and8 of10 non-COVID images correctly. A separate20-image severity check classified19 correctly. This small selected image-level reference evaluation does not establish patient-level diagnosis, prognosis or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Pretrained CNN feature extraction; support vector classifier
organization: University of Azad Jammu and Kashmir; Abbas Institute of Medical Sciences

source_review.scope: Original clinical dataset, pretrained feature/classifier Methods, cross-validation and separate AIMS evaluation Results read

evidence.ai_role: ImageNet-pretrained CNN feature maps feed learned support-vector classifiers for supplied COVID/non-COVID and severe/mild image labels.
evidence.tested: After development on public CT images, the source reports20 raw hospital images for COVID classification and another20 for severity, not included in training and evaluated under radiologist supervision. The observed confusion counts are retained rather than the near-perfect development benchmark.
evidence.unknown: The source does not establish unique patient counts, PCR/reference-label ascertainment, blinded case selection or independence between the two small hospital sets. Development cross-validation shuffled images rather than demonstrating patient-grouped folds. Selecting model variants on development comparisons limits generalization; supplied severity labels are not future deterioration outcomes. No quarantine, intensive-care recommendation or patient benefit is adopted.

title: Phone features complement self-reports for questionnaire-defined risk labels
summary: In selected Korean smartphone participants, random-forest models combining passive features with daily self-reports achieved cross-validated ROC areas of0.82 for depression-risk labels and0.86 for anxiety-risk labels. These are weekly questionnaire-defined states, with overlapping symptom-report windows, not clinical diagnoses or future-onset forecasts.
ai_technology: Random forest; gradient boosting; XGBoost
organization: Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute; Korea University; Batoners

source_review.scope: Actual original relevant clinical/computational Methods, reference labels, evaluation Results and limitations read

evidence.ai_role: Fitted tree ensembles combine mobility/activity summaries and brief symptom reports to classify weekly PHQ-9/GAD-7 threshold labels.
evidence.tested: Of455 recruited adults,277 depression and275 anxiety participants met coverage requirements. Repeated observations remained with their participant in fivefold evaluation; fourteen-day observation windows preceded weekly questionnaire dates.
evidence.unknown: Coverage thresholds and window length were selected using the same cross-validation framework, without an established untouched configuration test. Active daily mood/anxiety reports overlap conceptually and temporally with questionnaire references; weekly PHQ-9 repeats a two-week recall window. Many participants were excluded for coverage, and there was no external or temporal validation. Sleep features are phone-motion proxies. Average-precision numbers are not used here without independently resolving positive-class prevalence/encoding details. Prospective collection does not establish a prospectively frozen model or benefit.

title: Trained recurrent model preserves cue geometry across a memory delay
summary: A trained256-unit recurrent model of context-dependent decisions retained cue-specific population geometry across a delay despite changing single-unit activity. Numerical subspace analysis linked low-activity delay states with later context-specific integration. This is a conditional computational interpretation, not a newly observed biological memory mechanism.
ai_technology: Rate-based recurrent neural network
organization: South China University of Technology

source_review.scope: Actual relevant primary computational/clinical Methods, model/result context and limitations read; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: Training the recurrent weights for a delayed contextual task creates the dynamics being analyzed; epoch-specific subspace analysis tests how learned cue representations persist and guide integration.
evidence.tested: Original model/training Methods and cue-delay/manifold Results were read. The model learned color-versus-motion context rules, and numerical trajectories and fixed/slow points were analyzed within its fitted dynamics.
evidence.unknown: Known mixed-selectivity, dynamic-memory and low-activity theories are substantial precedents, limiting novelty. The analysis concerns a trained artificial model, without new neural recordings or independent biological validation. Dale-type excitatory/inhibitory constraints and biological plasticity were not implemented; numerical line-attractor analysis is not a formal proof or a universal account of working memory.

title: Histology transformer distinguishes recorded glioma marker labels
summary: ViT-WSI used whole-slide histology to classify recorded IDH1 status in pooled institutional and TCGA glioma data, reporting a patient-level ROC area of0.960. The labels included clinical immunohistochemistry and sequencing references. This is retrospective label-discrimination evidence, not a new mutation discovery or replacement for molecular testing.
ai_technology: Vision transformer; weakly supervised multiple-instance learning
organization: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology; Harbin Medical University

source_review.scope: Actual relevant primary computational/clinical Methods, model/result context and limitations read; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: Pretrained patch embeddings and a learned attention aggregator produce slide representations, fine-tuned for recorded marker-label classification and aggregated across a patient’s slides.
evidence.tested: The wider institutional dataset had5216 slides from1211 patients, with biomarker-defined subsets pooled with TCGA glioma slides for marker modeling. Methods explicitly keep patients distinct across splits; reported IDH1 AUC is patient-aggregated.
evidence.unknown: TCGA was pooled rather than reserved as a wholly untouched external test. Molecular predictors were initialized from a subtype model, whose overlap with downstream test cases was not independently reconciled. The paper describes both ten random70:30 splits and tenfold evaluation; tuning containment is incomplete. Immunostaining proxies and direct sequencing are heterogeneous references. No causal genotype mechanism, real clinical benefit or independent replication is established.

title: Learned metasurface codes produce measured single and paired beams
summary: A physics-assisted ResNet34 produced coding configurations applied to a programmable metasurface. Measurements of four designs showed fields in prescribed single- and dual-beam directions, with unequal beam strength in one case. This is a limited physical design check, without AI credit for a new electromagnetic law or autonomous tracking deployment.
ai_technology: ResNet34; physics-assisted unsupervised learning
organization: Southeast University

source_review.scope: Original selected computational/clinical or physical Methods, model role, specific Results and limitations read; operational biological sections excluded

evidence.ai_role: The trained inverse network outputs metasurface coding from human-specified beam targets; a conventional electromagnetic forward model supplies the learning loss. Learned coding is separate from the human-designed metasurface and macroscopic physics.
evidence.tested: Four network-generated configurations were measured in an anechoic chamber for forward/slanted single beams and paired beams. Measurements covered only a limited angular region. Additional static target-position examples were shown.
evidence.unknown: The forward model omits mutual coupling; the source reports degraded performance when interactions are included. Continuous network phase outputs approximate a binary physical surface. One dual-beam case showed unequal intensity attributed to specular reflection. Selected tests do not establish arbitrary-beam generalization, independent replication, real closed-loop tracking or a physical mechanism discovered by AI.

title: Learned multi-omics panel is evaluated against pediatric pneumonia severity
summary: A learned eight-feature panel combined five protein and three metabolite measurements to distinguish mild from severe pediatric pneumonia. The source reports an ROC area of 0.82 in a further 50 clinical samples. This is severity-label discrimination, not mortality prediction, a demonstrated early forecast or a treatment effect.
ai_technology: Random-forest feature ranking; logistic regression
organization: Shenzhen University; Shenzhen Nanshan People's Hospital

source_review.scope: Original selected computational/clinical or physical Methods, model role, specific Results and limitations read; operational biological sections excluded

evidence.ai_role: The Results attribute feature ranking to a random-forest model, while the Methods describe the selected five-protein/three-metabolite panel entering a logistic classifier. AI credit is limited to learned panel nomination/evaluation, not pathways or treatment mechanisms.
evidence.tested: Initial recruitment comprised 57 affected children and 10 healthy controls. The source describes a 70:30 development/test split and a separate 50-sample clinical validation for the severity panel, with reported AUC 0.82.
evidence.unknown: Exact model ordering differs between Results and Methods and is not fully reconciled. Matched multi-omics sample counts, repeated-sample independence and additional cohort timing/composition are incompletely specified in reviewed passages. Some redundancy filtering is described before the split. Validation is retrospective and single-centre, not an established independently frozen clinical test. A heading mentions mortality, but modeled labels are mild versus severe disease. Operational laboratory/pathogen procedures were not inspected.

title: Later perioperative records improve persistent kidney-injury classification
summary: An ensemble evaluated on 595 later-year cardiac-surgery patients reported ROC areas increasing from 0.807 with preoperative inputs to 0.878 with information through 48 hours after surgery. The target was postoperative kidney injury failing to recover within three days. This is retrospective temporal evaluation, not proof of live prevention or benefit from changing model-ranked factors.
ai_technology: Random forest; XGBoost; extra-trees soft-voting ensemble
organization: Seoul National University; Yonsei University

source_review.scope: Original selected computational/clinical or physical Methods, model role, specific Results and limitations read; operational biological sections excluded

evidence.ai_role: Three learned tree ensembles combine progressively updated perioperative records; SHAP characterizes predictive contributions rather than causal intervention effects.
evidence.tested: The cohort contained 2285 patients, including 168 persistent-injury cases. Earlier 2018-2022 patients trained/tuned models with patient-separated fourfold evaluation; 2023 patients formed the 595-person temporal test. Imputation was fitted inside development folds.
evidence.unknown: Patients dying within two days or missing key biosignals were excluded, limiting applicability to the full preoperative population. The 48-hour model uses later information closer to the outcome, not real-time streaming. The comparator score targets dialysis-requiring failure rather than the same persistence endpoint, so broad clinical superiority is not claimed. Single-centre Korean data and retrospective development do not establish external transfer, a prospectively frozen workflow or modifiable causal targets.

title: Learned serum profiles separate sampled cardiac and control infants
summary: In a study of 52 infants with single-ventricle heart disease and 48 controls, random-forest analysis distinguished circulating metabolite profiles, reporting a 7.49% error and separate leave-one-out group discrimination. This represents an exploratory multivariate sample pattern, not an established diagnostic test or an AI discovery of the reported metabolic pathways.
ai_technology: Random forest
organization: University of Colorado

source_review.scope: Actual relevant original clinical/computational Methods and Results read;111 original v1 and later journal checked separately; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: A fitted forest learns group-discriminating patterns from relative metabolite abundances and ranks features by permutation importance. Conventional differential/pathway analyses and univariate outcome trends are separate.
evidence.tested: The source describes random-forest group classification, out-of-bag-style error reporting and leave-one-out evaluation on the sampled infant cohorts. The represented case/control comparison uses the existing metabolomic measurements.
evidence.unknown: Cases and controls differ in age and blood-sampling site; medication, support and surgical context can confound profiles. Exact patient-level containment across repeated/multiple-site samples is not fully established in the reviewed model description. Clinical-outcome metabolite associations did not survive multiplicity correction and are not adopted. Relative measurements and one high-altitude centre limit transfer. The linked editorial is authenticated by primary metadata, but its body was not reviewed. No causal pathway, postoperative benefit or independently replicated clinical test is claimed.

title: CT fat-feature model predicts events within a deliberately enriched cohort
summary: DeepFat-assisted segmentation and a 15-feature elastic-net Cox model yielded a test C-index of 0.69 in 80 held-out patients from a 400-person, event-enriched cohort. Test-set risk reclassification was not statistically established. The result was already present in the January 2024 preprint; it is not evidence of general-population risk calibration or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: DeepFat deep-learning segmentation; elastic-net Cox model
organization: Case Western Reserve University

source_review.scope: Actual relevant original clinical/computational Methods and Results read;111 original v1 and later journal checked separately; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: A previously developed learned segmenter provides manually checked epicardial-fat masks; selected handcrafted spatial/intensity features enter a fitted regularized survival model. AI credit concerns measurement and model fitting, not a new fat-inflammation mechanism.
evidence.tested: The original v1 Methods and Results use 400 archived CT records, with 56% event prevalence and a random 320/80 development/test split. Feature selection is described as training-only. The v1 reports the same 0.69 test C-index as the later journal version.
evidence.unknown: The cohort was deliberately enriched by event/calcium-score groups, so natural prevalence, absolute risk and transportability are not established. DeepFat masks were manually corrected. The test reclassification statistic had a confidence interval crossing zero and p=0.463 despite a favorable narrative; no significant incremental reclassification claim is adopted. The composite includes revascularization and all-cause death. Later journal Methods/Results were separately read; they are not treated as a new discovery or silently backdated to v1.

title: Video model reproduces pressure estimates but remains limited against catheter measurements
summary: A SlowFast video classifier achieved weighted AUROC 0.854 against cardiologist right-atrial-pressure estimates in 2,618 external ultrasound studies. Against catheter measurements in 319 paired studies, categorical accuracy was 49.5%, compared with 48.9% for cardiologists. This retrospective agreement study does not establish equivalence, clinical benefit or reliable invasive-pressure replacement.
ai_technology: SlowFast R50 convolutional video classifier; learned ultrasound-view classifiers
organization: University of California, San Francisco; California Institute of Technology; Montreal Heart Institute

source_review.scope: Actual primary clinical data selection, patient split, SlowFast model Methods, Tables 1-4 and limitations read; current primary PubMed date and notice metadata checked.

evidence.ai_role: Learned view classifiers select inferior-vena-cava inspiration videos; a trained SlowFast R50 model assigns three pressure categories from their static and temporal features.
evidence.tested: 15,828 archived studies from 11,869 patients were divided by patient into 12,664 training, 1,582 validation and 1,582 test studies. The full test AUROC was 0.823; the abstract's 0.844 refers to a quality-filtered 554-study subset. External evaluation retained 2,618 Montreal studies and yielded weighted AUROC 0.854 against cardiologist categories. All 319 catheter-paired studies were kept in testing; model accuracy against binned catheter values was 49.5%, versus 48.9% for cardiologist estimates.
evidence.unknown: Catheter and ultrasound measurements could be up to 30 days apart. A nonsignificant difference is not an equivalence test. External reference labels were cardiologist estimates rather than catheter measurements, and external image-quality filtering excludes many original studies. Weighted metrics use UCSF class frequencies. Automated scan selection can pick a different video from the one used clinically. No prospective workflow benefit, prevention effect or safe replacement of invasive measurement is established.

title: A Lean proof constructs a maximally entangled state for nine ten-level parties
summary: A formal proof generated with GPT-5.6 Sol constructs a pure state for nine ten-level quantum systems whose reduction to any four is maximally mixed. The exact result concerns existence of an AME(9,10) state.
ai_technology: GPT-5.6 Sol; h1 Lean proof-search harness
organization: Meta FAIR

source_review.scope: Pinned Atlas Lean theorem and August 28 merge; September Formal Conjectures proof acceptance; h1 Table 1 and Appendix D; follow-up Appendix B.1

evidence.tested: The encoded construction supplies a normalized state and verifies its reductions. The Formal Conjectures maintainer linked the original work, and a later independent paper analyzes the construction.
evidence.unknown: The early maintainer replay exceeded its time limit for this proof. Source review did not include replay. The mathematical construction does not demonstrate hardware preparation.
evidence.ai_role: The h1 harness used GPT-5.6 Sol to generate a proof script with feedback from the Lean 4 checker.

title: A Lean proof establishes the word count behind OEIS A108081
summary: GPT-5.6 Sol produced a formal proof counting words generated by a reverse-and-shift concatenation rule. For length n, the count is A108081 at index n−1, a known Fibonacci transform whose connection to the word rule is the result proved.
ai_technology: GPT-5.6 Sol; h1 Lean proof-search harness
organization: Meta FAIR

source_review.scope: Pinned Atlas Lean theorem and August 28 merge; September Formal Conjectures PR and its independent axiom check; h1 Table 1 and Appendix D

evidence.tested: The proof relates the words of each positive length to the sequence using the matching coordinate enumeration. A maintainer reviewer independently replayed the linked version and reported only standard Lean axioms.
evidence.unknown: This is a theorem about the specified combinatorial word-generation rule. The existing integer sequence predates the proof.
evidence.ai_role: The h1 harness used GPT-5.6 Sol to generate a proof script with feedback from the Lean 4 checker.

title: A Lean proof establishes the two-sum Ruzsa–Turjányi limit
summary: GPT-5.6 Sol proved that for a zero-density asymptotic additive basis, the ratio of the number of two-term sums up to 2N to the number of basis elements up to N tends to infinity. The statement is the two-sum variant of the older Ruzsa–Turjányi result for three-term sums.
ai_technology: GPT-5.6 Sol; h1 Lean proof-search harness
organization: Meta FAIR

source_review.scope: Pinned Atlas Lean theorem and August 28 merge; h1 Table 1 and Appendix D; September separate formal proof and Formal Conjectures statement

evidence.tested: The formal proof encodes zero density and asymptotic additive-basis coverage. It applies the Plünnecke–Ruzsa inequality to control truncated sumsets.
evidence.unknown: This result concerns the density-zero two-sum variant. The originally posed bounded-limsup question in Erdős 337 is different and already has a counterexample.
evidence.ai_role: The h1 harness used GPT-5.6 Sol to generate a proof script with feedback from the Lean 4 checker.

title: Coding agents and maintainers surfaced different types of software defects
summary: Across 20 open-source repositories, arithmetic and comparison errors made up 18.5% of agent reports and 9.9% of historical maintainer fixes. Missing branches for supported inputs made up 7.7% of agent reports and 18.0% of the fixes. The study compared 14 agent configurations with 2,457 fixes from 18 months of repository history.
ai_technology: Frontier coding agents including GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash
organization: LogicStar.ai; ETH Zurich

source_review.scope: §§2–4, Table 4 and taxonomy Appendix D aggregate methods

evidence.tested: The study categorized agent reports from historical snapshots and same-repository fixes using a shared bug taxonomy. Agent percentages were averages across configurations.
evidence.unknown: The comparison contrasts reported findings with fixes that maintainers chose to complete. Some reports may be invalid, and unreported or unfixed historical bugs are outside the reference set.
evidence.ai_role: Coding agents generated bug reports for historical snapshots. Additional learned classification and matching helped construct and categorize the analysis set.

title: Silicon simulations found opposite temperature trends across harmonic orders
summary: Simulations of bulk silicon from 100 to 300 K predicted stronger third and fifth optical harmonics at higher temperatures and weaker ninth and higher harmonics. The calculations linked the lower-order increase to stronger local orbital coupling and the higher-order decrease to thermally induced disorder.
ai_technology: DeePTB learned tight-binding Hamiltonians; NEP89 learned interatomic potential
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

source_review.scope: §§II–III.4, Figures 7–12 and front matter

evidence.tested: A 216-atom simulation sampled five configurations per temperature. The authors checked smaller-cell electronic structure and spectra against prior calculations and compared thermal trends qualitatively with published experiments.
evidence.unknown: The trends and proposed mechanisms come from modeled thermal configurations and a specific optical excitation. The study performed no new optical measurements.
evidence.ai_role: NEP89 generated thermal configurations in molecular dynamics; DeePTB estimated their electronic Hamiltonians, which were used to calculate the optical spectra.

title: A retrospective study evaluated MedJev for in-hospital mortality prediction
summary: Using records available 24 hours after admission, MedJev ranked eventual in-hospital deaths with an AUROC of 0.926 (95% confidence interval 0.881 to 0.960). The supervised XGBoost comparison scored 0.902, with a paired interval that included no difference. MedJev’s unadjusted risk estimates were substantially miscalibrated.
ai_technology: MedJev, based on Qwen3.5-9B; Platt scaling
organization: University of California, Los Angeles

source_review.scope: §§3.1–3.4 and 4.2–4.3, Tables 1 and 3–4 and front matter

evidence.tested: Adult patients still hospitalized at 24 hours were eligible. Evaluation examples and supervised-model/recalibration fitting used the source-described patient-disjoint MIMIC-IV MEDS partitions. Recalibration used separately partitioned labeled records and improved calibration without changing AUROC.
evidence.unknown: The retrospective single-center data do not establish external performance or patient benefit. MedJev was first adapted on MIMIC-IV Note, but the primary Methods do not explicitly establish that this adaptation excluded the evaluated patients or their later notes. The described MEDS evaluation split therefore does not authenticate checkpoint-level patient independence or absence of note-derived outcome exposure. The discrimination comparison was against supervised models at the tested local-label budget, not unlimited supervised training.
evidence.ai_role: MedJev converted patient-history events available at the prediction time into outcome-token probabilities, which were evaluated against recorded deaths.

title: Changing where memory updates occurred shifted model retrieval accuracy
summary: Across 24 update schedules with the same number of updates, a 760-million-parameter language model’s retrieval accuracy ranged from 19.7% to 34.2% on the same 6,000 prompts. The test varied which layer groups updated most often while holding the checkpoint and evaluated prompts fixed.
ai_technology: Memory-as-Context MAC-760M; scheduled learned memory updates
organization: Meta AI

source_review.scope: §§3–4, Figure 2 and Table 1

evidence.tested: The authors enumerated assignments of four update periods to four fixed layer bands and compared accuracy on each of the same exact-retrieval items.
evidence.unknown: The response range applies to one checkpoint and one retrieval task. The best and worst schedules were identified retrospectively; the ranking need not transfer.
evidence.ai_role: The learned model updated its persistent memory during the task. Controlled placement and frequency changes tested the effects of the same update count on retrieval.

title: ESMFold’s pair representation carried more readable geometric information
summary: A readout study found that ESMFold’s intermediate representations added up to 0.32 AUROC for recovering relationships within folded structures over the upstream ESM-2 representation. Single-position attributes were already largely recoverable upstream. The result distinguishes two kinds of information in the model.
ai_technology: ESMFold; ESM-2; fitted sparse autoencoders
organization: University of Virginia

source_review.scope: §§3–4, readout and circuit-attribution checks; PDF front matter

evidence.tested: Learned dictionary readouts were compared with features from the upstream sequence model. The authors also checked whether changing interpretation prompts shifted the apparent division between representation types.
evidence.unknown: The finding concerns information recoverable from one trained folding model. It does not establish that the attributed directions are causal or describe how a protein folds in a cell.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted sparse dictionaries exposed features from the trained folding network. Comparative readouts assessed where geometry-related information became more accessible.

title: Activation directions shifted both image and text generation
summary: In UniAR, Emu3.5 and Liquid, some activation directions derived from text also changed image outputs, and some image-derived directions changed text. Emotion transferred in both directions more consistently than size or left–right relations. Transfer also depended on model and layer.
ai_technology: UniAR, Emu3.5 and Liquid; activation interventions
organization: Mila and McGill University; Carnegie Mellon University; MIT CSAIL; Northeastern University

source_review.scope: §§3.1–4 and Appendix A.8, including held-out blinded human ratings

evidence.tested: The study perturbed the shared model representations and compared outputs with unperturbed controls for eight concepts. Three reviewers each rated 320 separate randomized output pairs; their majority labels and the automated judge had agreement of κ=0.62.
evidence.unknown: The concept sets include generated examples. The response varies by model, concept and intervention strength, and transferring a direction does not establish that the underlying computations are identical.
evidence.ai_role: Activation directions derived from learned image or text representations were applied to generation in the other modality to measure how it changed.

title: A mine-cavity study found that geometric prediction accuracy varied by ground history
summary: On held-out cavity scans from one mine, a 3D U-Net achieved a mean overlap score of 0.601 versus 0.491 for the planning baseline. The ranking reversed in previously unexcavated ground: 0.525 for the learned model versus 0.592 for the baseline.
ai_technology: Ensemble of fitted three-dimensional U-Nets
organization: University of Waterloo; Cameco

source_review.scope: §4.1, Tables 2–4 and aggregate test-split provenance

evidence.tested: The study randomly held out historical cavities and compared volume overlap against surveyed boundaries and the site’s geometric baseline.
evidence.unknown: The data came from one mine and roughly 90% of training-domain examples involved neighboring filled excavations. The subgroup scores do not establish prospective or cross-site reliability.
evidence.ai_role: The U-Net ensemble used recorded field inputs to estimate cavity geometry. Its predictions were compared with recorded cavity scans.

title: Obsolete evidence reduced correct answers even when the latest fact was present
summary: In a paired experiment on 74 questions, replacing one unrelated statement with an obsolete version of the answer reduced accuracy from 100% to 44.6% for Qwen2.5-7B and to 87.8% for Qwen3-14B. The newest statement remained present in both conditions.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; Qwen3-14B; paired evidence interventions
organization: Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg; University of Kerala; Technical University of Munich

source_review.scope: Paired design, frozen conditions, Table 16 and limitations

evidence.tested: The experiment held the four-statement evidence size and prompt fixed. Under the official normalized-substring metric, all 50 harmful flips across the two models were classified as using outdated information. A later manual audit found mixed latest/stale strings in two Qwen2.5 outputs; a stricter score gave 98.6% versus 43.2%, retaining the same paired discordance.
evidence.unknown: The same 74 questions informed prompt development, so this is a within-cohort contrast and generalization remains open. The study concerns synthetic single-hop updates and two Qwen models. Obsolete values often match familiar real-world knowledge while the synthetic newest statements contradict it; the experiment does not isolate temporal obsolescence from pretrained-prior conflict. Output scoring and the measured behavioral effect do not establish attention or other internal mechanisms.
evidence.ai_role: The two learned language models composed answers from matched evidence sets, enabling a direct test of which retrieved version they used.

title: A policy exploration reset helped a robot controller adapt in simulation
summary: In 30 simulation seeds, restoring an exploration parameter helped pretrained PPO controllers adapt to a reaching task after a robot joint was locked. A physical deployment also favored the reset condition for the single simulation-selected policy tested per method.
ai_technology: Proximal Policy Optimization with Gaussian policies
organization: Politecnico di Torino; Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia

source_review.scope: §§3 and 4.3, Figure 6, Table 1 and hardware sampling protocol

evidence.tested: The simulation compared continued training with a one-time exploration reset and different entropy penalties. Each physical policy was tested against the same 50 target points.
evidence.unknown: The physical experiment used a single simulation-selected seed per method and consecutive target points. The result is specific to the studied Gaussian policy parameterization and adaptation task.
evidence.ai_role: PPO-trained policies were tested with an intervention on their exploration distribution, showing a change in adaptation after the simulated task shifted.

title: Coding agents continued editing after repeated refactoring requests
summary: Across 3,000 refactoring turns on 60 Java codebases, coding agents made edits on 2,546 turns even though each follow-up supplied no new requirement. Some runs resumed editing after a no-change turn. The study observed this behavior in Codex and Claude Code across five models.
ai_technology: Codex with GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4-mini or GPT-5.5; Claude Code with Opus 4.8 or Sonnet 4.6
organization: University of Southern California; OpenSciLab

source_review.scope: §§II–V, experimental protocol and Figures 3–4

evidence.tested: Each agent received up to ten nonspecific refactoring requests in a persistent session. The study measured diffs over 50 compact reference implementations and 10 highly graded object-oriented assignments.
evidence.unknown: The starting projects were selected for quality, but not every individual edit was independently evaluated for usefulness. The finding measures continued modification under repeated requests, not code degradation in production.
evidence.ai_role: The trained coding agents decided whether to edit after repeated nonspecific developer prompts, yielding directly observable behavior across sessions.

title: Acquisition year matched breast-thermography model discrimination
summary: On a held-out set of 52 patients, acquisition year alone separated normal and sick labels with an AUROC of 0.974, within the range of the trained imaging models. On a separate 24-patient test set, confidence intervals for benign-versus-malignant classification all included chance.
ai_technology: BiomedCLIP, general CLIP variants and ViT-B/16; federated training simulation
organization: Southern Illinois University; Loyola University Chicago; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

source_review.scope: §§3–4.4, patient partitions, Tables 1–2, acquisition-period control

evidence.tested: The authors separated patients across splits, tested acquisition year as a metadata-only score and compared it with the image-model outputs.
evidence.unknown: Only two acquisition years included both normal and sick labels. These data cannot separate acquisition effects from pathology, and the small malignancy test does not establish clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: The learned thermography classifiers supplied the scores audited against acquisition dates and evaluated on the pathology distinction.

title: Random-split rankings poorly predicted microfluidic surrogate rankings under shift
summary: Across 107 held-out groups from six published tables, a random-split ranking of six learned prediction models showed little agreement with their rankings in a simulated adaptive evaluation. Mean Kendall correlation was 0.08, with a reported interval from −0.04 to 0.19.
ai_technology: XGBoost, random and quantile forests, Gaussian processes and neural surrogate models
organization: Zhiyuan Zhang, independent researcher

source_review.scope: Primary §6.4.3 and Table 20, frozen protocols and v1 front matter

evidence.tested: The analysis compared rankings from random-split error with rankings from held-out group performance under the same offline simulated evaluation, using previously published measurements.
evidence.unknown: The comparisons reused finite public tables and modeled lab activity offline. The study did not perform a new laboratory experiment, and the interval does not rule out modest agreement.
evidence.ai_role: Six fitted surrogates made predictions for previously recorded measurements. Comparing their errors under different evaluation procedures quantified how poorly random-split standings carried across the tested settings.

title: Submerged oil droplets shifted from two size peaks to one
summary: In a lab experiment with a submerged silicone-oil jet, image measurements showed two peaks in the volume-weighted droplet-size distribution in transitional flow. At higher Reynolds numbers the distribution shifted toward one peak with smaller characteristic droplets.
ai_technology: U-Net convolutional image segmentation
organization: Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad; Lehigh University

source_review.scope: §§3.5.1 and 4–5; measured droplet distributions and separate physical-model comparisons

evidence.tested: The analysis used fluorescence images from the controlled oil–water analogue and a U-Net trained on 200 manually annotated images. The source compared measurements with a physical population model.
evidence.unknown: The result describes a lab fluid pair and the tested flow regimes. The proposed breakup interpretation is supported by the accompanying flow analysis rather than independently established for all fluids.
evidence.ai_role: A trained segmentation network separated visible droplets from image artifacts so their detected sizes could be used to measure the distributions.

title: Rolling ridge forecasts failed to beat zero in an ETF return backtest
summary: In a 2005–2025 ETF study, a rolling ridge model using past return features produced negative mean out-of-sample R² at every tested regularization level against a zero-return forecast. Scores approached zero as stronger regularization shrank the predictions.
ai_technology: Ridge regression with rolling retraining
organization: KTH Royal Institute of Technology; Stanford University

source_review.scope: §§2, 5.3 and 6.3, Figure 25 and the disclosed universe selection

evidence.tested: The model was repeatedly fitted on trailing observations and scored on the following period. The paper compared multiple regularization levels with a zero forecast.
evidence.unknown: The ETFs were selected from ones still trading at study time, producing survivorship bias. The result concerns the chosen predictors, horizons and historical universe.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted regression generated return forecasts from past observations, enabling a retrospective comparison of predictive signal against the zero baseline.

title: A microscopy analysis inferred changing diffusion during nanoparticle assembly
summary: A model fitted to electron-microscopy video inferred a positive effective coefficient for density diffusion that increased in the mobile phase and decreased as crystalline clusters consolidated. The fitted coefficients for orientational order had the opposite sign over the analyzed trajectory.
ai_technology: Fitted time-varying sparse autoregressive dynamics
organization: University of Michigan; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; University of Southern California

source_review.scope: §§II.1–II.4, Figure 5 and the discussion of the continuum approximation

evidence.tested: The authors fit local evolution rules to density and orientational fields extracted from video, then computed spatially averaged coefficients from the learned operators.
evidence.unknown: The coefficients are effective estimates under locality and smoothness assumptions, not directly measured material constants. The plotted time course represents one experimental trajectory.
evidence.ai_role: Training sparse time-varying operators on successive microscopy frames converted image observations into inferred evolution equations for density and order.

title: Attention heads selected on symbols also affected evidence judgments in text
summary: Ablating eight Pythia-410M attention heads chosen using symbolic prompts reduced accuracy on a natural-language evidence task by 8.2 percentage points. Ablating random sets matched by layer and size reduced it by 0.8 points. A separate full-precision analysis showed an effect in the same direction.
ai_technology: Pythia-410M; attention-head ablation; related native full-precision models
organization: University of California, Irvine

source_review.scope: §§3–5.6, Tables 5–6 and native precision controls

evidence.tested: The study selected the eight heads without natural-language prompts, then compared ablation on held-out domains and paraphrases. The original comparison averaged five seeds.
evidence.unknown: The task asks which state has more supporting reports. The result establishes influence under intervention in these models, not a general account of reasoning or identical head functions across models.
evidence.ai_role: The learned attention heads were selected using controlled changes in symbolic evidence and then intervened on during a separate natural-language evidence comparison.

title: An AI-written attention kernel accelerated prefill on an AMD GPU
summary: A Claude Opus 5.5 team wrote a Kimi Delta Attention prefill kernel with fused input preparation and recurrent updates. Across 10 tested workloads on an AMD MI350X, it was 3.01 times as fast as the vLLM HIP kernel used for comparison.
ai_technology: Claude Opus 5.5; Evolving Agent Teams
organization: University of California, Berkeley

source_review.scope: §4.7 and Appendix C, MI350X construction, test definition and correctness gates

evidence.tested: The source reports five timing re-measurements and checks of outputs and final states under a numerical tolerance. The team added a slow-decay test after finding that earlier checks could miss state-handoff errors.
evidence.unknown: The reported speedup is an arithmetic mean for the tested hardware and workloads. The result concerns a single constructed kernel and tolerance-based validation, not universal throughput or exact equivalence.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Opus 5.5 agents developed the fused implementation and tested its scheduled state handoffs, starting from a port of the vLLM baseline.

title: AlphaEarth crop embeddings transferred less well between the United States and India
summary: In a satellite crop-classification study, a classifier trained on US data scored 0.326 macro F1 in Northern India using AlphaEarth embeddings, versus 0.493 using seasonal harmonic features. The ranking also favored harmonic features in the reverse direction, even though embeddings performed better in held-out US county comparisons.
ai_technology: AlphaEarth Foundations geospatial embeddings; supervised crop classifiers
organization: Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur; Indian Institute of Technology Delhi; Tata Consultancy Services Research

evidence.tested: The study compared satellite representations on crops represented in US field-scale data from 2017–2023 and Northern India data from 2021, with spatial validation and cross-region transfer.
evidence.unknown: The geographies differ in seasons, sample selection and field structure. The results do not establish transferability to other regions or to all crops.
evidence.ai_role: Learned AlphaEarth embeddings encoded satellite imagery for the classifiers. Comparing those embeddings with engineered seasonal features quantified the regional transfer deficit.

title: Verifier feedback raised both correct and incorrect model verdicts
summary: On 32 software verification tasks, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B averaged 22.0 correct verdicts with verifier feedback versus 12.7 without it. Incorrect verdicts also rose from one to seven. A deterministic validation baseline returned 26 correct verdicts and left six unresolved.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct; verifier output interpretation
organization: The University of Manchester; University of Rajshahi; Varendra University

source_review.scope: §§III–IV, E3 frozen-subset design, Figure 3 and interpretation limits

evidence.tested: The fixed assertion set was evaluated with and without feedback for three seeds. Correct, incorrect and unresolved decisions were counted separately.
evidence.unknown: The subset was small and selected from one verification benchmark. The deterministic baseline included an additional validation step and is not an equivalent raw-feedback condition.
evidence.ai_role: The trained coding model interpreted formal-verification evidence, allowing a direct comparison of verdicts under controlled feedback conditions.

title: AlphaCNOT exposed a shorter construction for remote qubit swaps
summary: Researchers found a recurring circuit in AlphaCNOT outputs and proved that two qubits at graph distance d greater than one can be swapped using at most 6d−4 CNOT gates. The corresponding construction that chains adjacent SWAPs uses 6d−3.
ai_technology: AlphaCNOT learned policy and value networks with Monte Carlo tree search
organization: University of Udine; University of Catania; University of Naples Federico II; National Institute for Astrophysics

source_review.scope: §§2–3, AlphaCNOT method and constructive theorem, primary PDF front matter

evidence.tested: AlphaCNOT revealed the pattern over multiple test topologies. The authors gave a constructive proof along a shortest path, valid for any distance in the stated coupling model.
evidence.unknown: The comparison is against the adjacent-SWAP construction. The bound does not establish CNOT optimality or measured hardware performance.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaCNOT’s learned policy and value networks guided a constrained circuit search. The authors recognized a recurring pattern and proved its general gate bound.

title: A model-screened copper pattern was lowest in a MoS₂ structure search
summary: In a search of 14,715 intercalated structures, a fine-tuned model identified a dice-like arrangement of copper between molybdenum disulfide layers at about 11 atomic% copper. Density-functional calculations confirmed that this candidate was the lowest-energy arrangement among the checked structures, with a binding energy of −0.21 eV per copper atom.
ai_technology: MatterSim v1.0.0-5M fine-tuned atomistic force field; DFT checks
organization: University of Oulu

source_review.scope: §§II.1–II.3, Figure 2 and field-driven model limitations

evidence.tested: The learned force field screened and relaxed enumerated structures. Density-functional calculations reevaluated selected low-energy configurations that were outside the model’s training data.
evidence.unknown: The finding is computational and constrained to the searched cells and compositions. The predicted arrangement was not directly observed in a functioning device. The paper defines this copper concentration as Cu atoms divided by all atoms; its MoS₂Cu₀.₁₁ shorthand is not a conventional Cu-per-Mo stoichiometric coefficient.
evidence.ai_role: A fine-tuned MatterSim force field made it feasible to relax and rank the enumerated configurations before DFT was applied to the leading candidates.

title: Two GPT-2 circuits showed different preservation after distillation
summary: On tested prompts, DistilGPT-2 retained 87.3% accuracy on a number-comparison task versus GPT-2’s 94.0%, but fell to 35.2% on an indirect-object task where GPT-2 achieved 94.8%. Activation interventions found evidence for retained early comparison components and little recovery from the tested indirect-object heads.
ai_technology: GPT-2; DistilGPT-2; causal activation interventions
organization: Informatics Institute of Technology, Sri Lanka

source_review.scope: §§3–6, Tables 4–6 and the single model-pair limitation

evidence.tested: The study compared behavior, activation readouts and matched discovery/evaluation head tests across two previously characterized circuits, and reported activation patching results.
evidence.unknown: One teacher–student pair and two tasks are represented. The result does not rule out alternate indirect-object mechanisms or establish what caused differences during the original training.
evidence.ai_role: Interventions on the learned activations of two language models exposed different functional preservation across the tested circuits.

title: Unchanged agent instructions could appear to improve during skill selection
summary: Across 16 tuned instruction sets, held-out task success averaged only 0.1 percentage points above the starting instructions. In replay tests, the same acceptance logic often selected apparent improvements even when every candidate kept the original instructions.
ai_technology: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GPT-6 Luna; model-driven skill optimizers
organization: Shanghai AI Laboratory; Fudan University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; University of Science and Technology of China; Tsinghua University

source_review.scope: §§4–6, Table 1 and no-change replay protocol and Appendix C.3

evidence.tested: The authors tested three optimizers on three benchmarks. Their no-change replay draws task-success probabilities from a fitted beta-binomial posterior, simulates each candidate as another run of the seed instructions, and applies the original acceptance rule. Small development sets had at most 30 tasks.
evidence.unknown: The no-change result concerns the studied acceptance rules and resampling design. An aggregate near-zero test result does not establish equivalence of every skill or model. The null replay assumes episodes are independent conditional on each task’s success probability; its prior is fitted using seed development and test episodes, so the replay is a model-based diagnostic rather than a newly executed unchanged-instruction optimization trial.
evidence.ai_role: Learned agents performed each task under original and edited natural-language instructions. Their repeated scores supplied the null replay and the held-out comparison.

title: A perfect Hausa safety proxy masked low-quality responses in one model assessment
summary: In a 500-prompt Hausa safety evaluation, Gemini classified every base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct response as safe—the paper’s refusal-rate proxy—but rated 96.2% low quality. Model variants changed benign-request over-refusal and judged linguistic quality by different amounts.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct variants; Gemini evaluator
organization: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences; Bayero University Kano; University of Hamburg; Imperial College London

source_review.scope: §§4–6, evaluation conditions, Table 3 and single-judge limits

evidence.tested: Five model variants answered 500 harmful and 200 benign Hausa prompts. One Gemini judge rated safety, helpfulness and linguistic quality using a structured rubric.
evidence.unknown: Many prompts were translated, and the ratings did not receive independent native-speaker validation. The results concern this benchmark and its one automated judge. The harmful-prompt judge returns SAFE/UNSAFE; its reported refusal-rate proxy does not independently authenticate a coherent Hausa refusal.
evidence.ai_role: The tested learned models produced Hausa responses; the learned judge supplied separate safety and language-quality ratings rather than using refusal counts alone.

title: Distilled language models retained a watermark-linked weight signal
summary: In controlled comparisons of models trained on matching clean or watermarked examples, researchers measured a watermark-linked component in the distilled models’ parameter changes. Its detectable signature persisted across some later model modifications tested in the study.
ai_technology: Fine-tuned Qwen language models; learned Qwen2.5-3B measurement probe
organization: FAIR, Meta Superintelligence Labs

source_review.scope: §§2.2 and 3.1–3.3, matched-model geometry and aggregate validation limits

evidence.tested: The main comparison held the training task, prompts, initialization and recipe fixed between the clean and watermarked models. The authors measured changes in weights separately from output-level detections.
evidence.unknown: The represented observation is limited to tested models, watermark schemes and math distillation settings. The measured component is defined relative to a paired task-only change.
evidence.ai_role: Matched learned student models allowed the authors to isolate a component of weight change associated with the watermark without changing the training task.

title: Seller message framing tracked purchases in live persuasion games
summary: A retrospective analysis of 9,337 classifiable messages from one AI seller in 725 GLEE persuasion games found that buyers purchased after 65.8% of loyalty-framed messages and 30.9% of care-framed messages. The association persisted when the study adjusted for product quality and game round.
ai_technology: Online Thompson sampling bandit; language-model message generation
organization: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

source_review.scope: Versioned primary arXiv HTML front matter, §§3.3, 4 and 6, Appendix D Tables 7, 8 and 12

evidence.tested: Among 9,337 lexicon-classifiable outgoing messages in 725 live persuasion competition games, buyer response was 65.8% for loyalty-framed versus 30.9% for care-framed messages. Game-clustered, quality- and round-adjusted odds ratio was 3.98 (95% CI 3.31–4.79), or 2.18 (1.78–2.67) for pitches only.
evidence.unknown: The agent chose framing adaptively and labels came from a lexicon. Opponents included humans and AI agents, and the aggregate does not identify a human-only effect. Repeat opponents could not be accounted for, and framing was not randomized. About half of care-labelled messages were honest recommendations not to buy, compared with 6–17% for other frames, so the raw purchase-rate contrast also reflects message intent. The pitches-only restriction reduces this difference but is itself a lexical approximation.
evidence.ai_role: An online Thompson sampling bandit fitted framing success probabilities during play and supplied the framing for the language model that wrote the analyzed seller messages.

title: A hidden Gemma arithmetic state steered the next answer digit
summary: In Gemma 4 12B-IT, a learned activation subspace carried arithmetic results across text and image tasks apart from the directions used to read the current digit. With the same first digit supplied, changing the remaining numerical state made the counterfactual units digit the top prediction in 77.6% of 1,536 interventions.
ai_technology: Gemma 4 12B-IT; Distributed Alignment Search; activation interchange
organization: Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona; Apple

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 primary HTML §§3–6, Appendix D.1–D.2, E.1–E.2 and F

evidence.tested: Across four text/image and addition/subtraction conditions, the 13-dimensional component orthogonal to the current digit readout showed 75.5% numerical retrieval across conditions among 20 values excluded from alignment fitting. In 1,536 cache tests with the same first digit supplied, the counterfactual units digit was the top prediction in 77.6% of cases.
evidence.unknown: The experiments used controlled arithmetic prompts and fitted subspaces. Numerical values held out for cross-condition alignment could still occur during earlier subspace training. A second model was tested in the same study.
evidence.ai_role: Distributed Alignment Search learns activation subspaces in Gemma 4 from paired arithmetic instances. Component-specific activation swaps isolate a part orthogonal to the current digit readout and test its downstream effect.

title: Paper trading agents echoed peer wording without a detectable immediate trade shift
summary: In a seven-day paper trading study with 200 agents across four model families, later-starting board agents reused peers' phrases 6.8 percentage points more often when they could see a fresh post. A timing-based comparison found no detectable same-morning shift in matching trades, with an estimate of 2.4 points and a 95% interval of −4.1 to 9.3.
ai_technology: Opus 5.5; GPT-6.1 Sol; Grok 4.6; DeepSeek V4 Pro
organization: Infinite Ascent

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 primary HTML §§1–2.3, 4, 5.1 and 8.2, Appendix A and C.4

evidence.tested: Timing-based comparisons found 6.8 percentage points more same-morning eight-word phrase reuse for pairs with an opportunity to read a recent peer post (95% interval 1.7–11.8, 68 board group mornings). In a separate comparison subtracting timing differences in isolated groups, same-direction orders in the same stock differed by 2.4 points (95% interval −4.1 to 9.3).
evidence.unknown: The study used one group per communication regime and model family, with only seven trading days and simulated fills at live prices. Timing was not randomized. The interval leaves room for some short-run effects and says nothing about market impact.
evidence.ai_role: Four learned model families ran separate paper trading accounts and produced peer messages while retaining independent decisions. Frozen views and time-stamped paper orders made phrase and order comparisons possible.

title: ASKAP survey identifies 148 stronger extreme scattering candidates
summary: A learned light-curve filter helped astronomers identify 72 gold and 76 silver extreme scattering candidates in ASKAP's VAST survey, plus 88 less certain cases. For the gold and silver candidates above 5 mJy at 888 MHz, the study estimated 0.012 events per square degree per year. Candidates were more common toward the Galactic center.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process light-curve regression; XGBoost classifier
organization: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; Stanford University; Manly Astrophysics; University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee; University of Sydney; University of California, Santa Cruz; University of Toronto; CSIRO

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 primary HTML §§II.2, III.1 Table 1, IV, V.6, VI and Appendix A

evidence.tested: The learned filter reduced 24,590 bright isolated radio sources to 4,446 for review. Researchers reported 72 gold and 76 silver extreme scattering candidates plus 88 bronze candidates. The gold and silver sample gave 0.012 candidate events per square degree per year above 5 mJy at 888 MHz in the study's survey estimate.
evidence.unknown: Candidate grading prioritizes reliability over completeness and the rate is direction-dependent. Sparse sampling and competing explanations leave some events uncertain. The screening classifier was assessed on simulations.
evidence.ai_role: Gaussian-process regression fitted individual light curves and extracted features. An XGBoost classifier trained on simulated light curves discarded likely stochastic variability from real ASKAP VAST data before visual and multi-frequency review.

title: Coherent microlens motion led to smaller quasar disk estimates in simulations
summary: Ridge models trained on light curves that omitted relative microlens motion underestimated accretion-disk half-light radii by about 6% to 28% when tested on more detailed simulations. The comparison covered three quadruply lensed quasar configurations and used information from all four images jointly.
ai_technology: Ridge regression of simulated light-curve statistics
organization: Stony Brook University; City University of New York; American Museum of Natural History; University of Toronto; Université de Montréal; Mila

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§III, IV.2, IV.4 Table 2 and V.3

evidence.tested: Joint fits for three quadruply lensed quasar configurations and populations of 128 matched quads underestimated radii by 27.8%, 20.9% and 5.6% when training omitted relative motions. Matched-physics controls showed median biases between −0.003 and −0.001 dex.

evidence.ai_role: Fitted ridge regression maps simulated multiband light-curve statistics to logarithmic half-light radii. Models trained under simplified assumptions were applied to a separately partitioned target with independent lens motions and a lens mass distribution.

title: Learned simulations mapped a shallow free-energy landscape for acridine

organization: New York University; NYU Shanghai; Flatiron Institute

evidence.tested: At 300 K the estimated Gibbs free energies of four metastable acridine forms were 2.27–2.83 kJ/mol above Form II. evidence.unknown: The absolute free-energy differences are computational estimates. The comparison is with observed phase transformations, and Form IV was omitted from the anharmonic calculation. The main text discusses a value near 350 K, while the supporting protocol lists temperature propagation over 280–340 K; that endpoint is not promoted here. Laboratory transitions only partly match: the calculation leaves Form III more stable throughout, unlike the observed Form VIII–III crossover.
evidence.ai_role: A MACE-MH1 interatomic model fine-tuned on electronic-structure configurations supplied energies and forces for anharmonic thermodynamic integration.

organization: Apple

evidence.unknown: The full fit was validated within the SynthAPI pipeline, and the second dataset checked one app-diversity trend. Both used synthetic environments. App coverage and benchmark weighting can affect the fitted relationship.

title: Language-model credence updates moved outside the starting opinion range

organization: Arizona State University

organization: Boston Children’s Hospital; Harvard Medical School; New Jersey Institute of Technology

summary: Neural variational Monte Carlo wave functions, benchmarked against multiband exact diagonalization on small systems, were used to map phases in the Aharonov–Casher continuum model up to 36 electrons. This is retrospective prediction in an imbalanced observational cohort, not evidence of causation or clinical utility.

evidence.unknown: The retrospective cohort is imbalanced and the review found no independent prospective validation or evidence of clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: A GAN synthesizes minority-class examples for training a metabolomics-plus-clinical risk prediction model.

summary: A fine-tuned ResNet-50 computer-aided diagnosis system classified deeply invasive T1b colorectal cancer from non-magnified endoscopic images. In a third-hospital test set of 44 lesions, it outperformed novice readers on specificity but was slightly below expert readers. The authors did not test real-time colonoscopy.
ai_technology: A pretrained ResNet-50 CNN is fine-tuned to estimate the probability that an endoscopic image depicts deeply invasive T1b colorectal cancer.
organization: University of Tokyo; National Cancer Center Hospital East

evidence.tested: Third-hospital lesion-level evaluation reported AUC 0.888; at the study threshold, specificity was 87%, sensitivity 81% and accuracy 84%. The cohort contained 44 lesions.
evidence.unknown: Small retrospective test set; performance was below experts and no real-time or clinical-outcome evaluation was performed.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained ResNet-50 CNN is fine-tuned to estimate the probability that an endoscopic image depicts deeply invasive T1b colorectal cancer.

title: Peripheral serum metabolomic profiles inform central cognitive impairment
summary: Seven serum metabolites associated with cognitive impairment were identified; in baseline cognitively normal participants, the model predicted later conversion to MCI/AD (AUC 0.804; sensitivity 0.722; specificity 0.749). title: An electronic nose and neural network classified berry ripeness grades
summary: An electronic nose and a three-layer neural network classified five expert-assigned ripeness grades in whiteberries and blackberries. The paper reports 100% correct classification for blackberries and 88.3% for whiteberries, with overlap between the last two whiteberry grades. The result comes from a small internal sample and does not establish performance across harvests or sites.

organization: Razi University; University of Tehran; Agricultural Science and Natural Resources University of Khuzestan

evidence.tested: The study used 120 fruits and a 75/25 training/test split.

title: Distinguishing vigilance decrement and low task demands from mind-wandering: A machine learning analysis of EEG.
summary: Across-task EEG classification found mind-wandering was separable from low vigilance and low task demand; the self-report-trained classifier predicted mind-wandering while classifiers trained on vigilance or task-demand labels did not, with source-localized features differing among states. Thirty participants; 10-fold and leave-one-participant-out cross-validation plus across-task testing against intermittent self-reports. Exploratory evidence with limited sample size and self-report labels.
ai_technology: SVM classifiers use EEG features to test whether mind-wandering shares neural patterns with low vigilance or low task demand; dipole fitting localizes significant classifier features.
organization: Bernoulli Institute for Mathematics, Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, University of Groningen, Groningen, The Netherlands

evidence.ai_role: SVM classifiers use EEG features to test whether mind-wandering shares neural patterns with low vigilance or low task demand; dipole fitting localizes significant classifier features.
evidence.tested: Across-task EEG classification found mind-wandering was separable from low vigilance and low task demand; the self-report-trained classifier predicted mind-wandering while classifiers trained on vigilance or task-demand labels did not, with source-localized features differing among states.

source_review.scope: Read the primary article’s Methods and Results. SVM classifiers trained on EEG from 30 participants distinguished conditions of vigilance and task demand and were tested across tasks against probe-reported mind-wandering. The vigilance- and task-demand-trained classifiers did not predict mind-wandering above chance, whereas the self-report-trained classifier did; source localization associated the states with distinct neural correlates. PubMed and the primary paper identify electronic publication on 2020-06-28; a targeted title/DOI search found no earlier preprint/version. Searches of both supplied active and archived snapshots found no same mind-wandering result. The result is exploratory: small sample, self-report labels, and source-localization interpretation.

title: A Shallow Convolutional Neural Network Predicts Prognosis of Lung Cancer Patients in Multi-Institutional CT-Image Data
summary: LungNet uses pretreatment CT images to predict non-small-cell lung cancer survival across four medical-center cohorts, with concordance indices of 0.58–0.62. Transfer learning improved nodule-classification AUC from 0.82 to 0.85; these retrospective predictions do not demonstrate improved clinical outcomes.
ai_technology: LungNet, a shallow three-dimensional convolutional neural network with transfer learning
organization: Stanford University; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Moffitt Cancer Center; Stanford University Medical Center

evidence.tested: Four independent NSCLC survival cohorts (n=129, 185, 311, 84) had C-indices 0.62, 0.62, 0.62, and 0.58; transfer learning reached AUC 0.85 for nodule malignancy classification versus 0.82 from scratch.
evidence.unknown: All evidence is retrospective prediction; the study does not show improved patient outcomes or clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: A shallow 3D CNN extracts prognostic features from pretreatment CT scans and predicts survival; transfer learning applies the model to nodule malignancy classification.

title: Development and evaluation of machine learning models for voxel dose predictions in online adaptive magnetic resonance guided radiation therapy
summary: Artificial neural networks predicted patient-specific three-dimensional dose distributions from target and organ-at-risk structures for online adaptive MR-guided radiotherapy. Cross-validation on plans from 53 patients showed agreement with selected dose metrics and flagged 25 plans as potentially inferior. The retrospective planning analysis did not test effects on treatment decisions or patient outcomes.
ai_technology: Artificial neural networks predict patient-specific three-dimensional dose distributions from anatomical structures
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: Cross-validation on more than 300 abdominal-cancer treatment plans reported R² values of 0.97, 0.95 and 0.95 for V95, V100 and D95; prediction intervals identified about 10% (25) of plans as lower quality.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective plan analysis; clinical integration and improved patient outcomes were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Artificial neural networks predict patient-specific three-dimensional dose distributions from anatomical structures

title: Predicting Short-term Survival after Liver Transplantation using Machine Learning
summary: Magnesium appeared among the leading selected features alongside INR, lymphocytes, platelets, WBC, sodium, age and BMI. The random-forest model achieved temporal-validation AUC 0.771, specificity 0.815 and sensitivity 0.50, outperforming the compared models by AUC. Derivation: 480 patients from 2004–2012 with 10-fold cross-validation. Temporal validation: 58 patients from 2013, including four deaths. This is existing-data temporal validation, not external validation; the small event count and lack of external testing limit generalizability. title: Longitudinal records supported forecasts of multiple sclerosis progression
summary: The study used routine records from 1,624 people with multiple sclerosis to forecast transition from relapsing-remitting to secondary-progressive disease at 180, 360 and 720 days. Visit-based models had 70–100% recall but 5–10% precision without confidence filtering; the history model reached 67% recall and 42% precision at 720 days. Few transitions and false positives limit treatment use; the study does not show clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Recurrent neural network (LSTM); random forest, SVM, KNN and AdaBoost
organization: Sapienza University of Rome; IRCCS Istituto Neurologico Mediterraneo Neuromed

evidence.tested: A single-center retrospective cohort of 18,574 visits from 1,624 patients. Visit models used patient-wise leave-one-group-out evaluation; the history model used a train/test split because leave-one-group-out training was computationally infeasible.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.

title: A Deep Learning System to Screen Novel Coronavirus Disease 2019 Pneumonia.
summary: The study distinguished COVID-19 from influenza-A viral pneumonia and healthy cases; overall accuracy was 86.7% on a held-out set of 90 CT cases (30 per category). The source reports 618 CT samples from three hospitals; 528 samples were used for training/validation and 90 were held out from patients not included in training. The test is an internal held-out sample, not an independent external cohort. Published abstract/full text do not establish clinical benefit or prospective utility.
ai_technology: A 3D deep-learning model segmented candidate infection regions; a location-attention classifier categorized CT regions and a Noisy-or Bayesian function combined confidence into a case-level prediction.
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine

evidence.ai_role: A 3D deep-learning model segmented candidate infection regions; a location-attention classifier categorized CT regions and a Noisy-or Bayesian function combined confidence into a case-level prediction.
evidence.tested: The study distinguished COVID-19 from influenza-A viral pneumonia and healthy cases; overall accuracy was 86.7% on a held-out set of 90 CT cases (30 per category).

The original full-text study is a specific retrospective diagnostic-validation question, eligible under the project criteria. Active/archived catalog searches found no same-cohort record; the active Mount Sinai COVID-CT entry is a different model, input set and cohort. A later Applied Intelligence article was retracted for reusing this study’s data/text and is treated as the same underlying work, not a separate discovery.

title: BADGR: The Berkeley Autonomous Driving Ground Robot
summary: A learned predictive model supports self-supervised robot navigation without human-labeled data. The primary v1 reports repeated indoor and off-road goal-reaching trials after about 42 hours of robot experience; results are limited to the reported platform and routes.

organization: Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Research (BAIR), University of California, Berkeley

evidence.tested: The primary v1 reports repeated navigation trials on indoor and off-road routes after about 42 hours of robot experience.
evidence.unknown: No independent replication; results are limited to the reported robot and routes.
