title: Quantification of Retinal Nerve Fibre Layer Thickness on Optical Coherence Tomography with a Deep Learning Segmentation-Free Approach
summary: A ResNet34 model predicted retinal nerve fibre layer thickness directly from unsegmented OCT scans. In three held-out sets, predictions tracked conventional measurements on clean scans and more closely matched same-day good-quality references on scans with segmentation errors or other artefacts. This retrospective proof of concept did not test patient outcomes.
ai_technology: ResNet34 deep-learning model predicting retinal nerve fibre layer thickness from unsegmented optical coherence tomography scans
organization: University of Pittsburgh; UPMC

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: The full study evaluated 25,285 B-scans from 1,338 eyes of 706 subjects in three test sets. Correlations with reference measurements were 0.983 on clean scans, 0.972 versus 0.829 for conventional segmentation on scans with segmentation errors, and 0.940 versus 0.640 on scans with other artefacts.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective test; references were conventional measurements or same-day good-quality scans. No downstream patient benefit was evaluated.

title: Deep learning, computer-aided radiography reading for tuberculosis: a diagnostic accuracy study from a tertiary hospital in India
summary: Against microbiological confirmation, qXR reached AUC 0.81, 71% sensitivity and 80% specificity; radiologist sensitivity was 56% with 80% specificity. title: Machine learning predicts early diabetic kidney disease in a retrospective hospital cohort
summary: Researchers evaluated six survival models in 1,006 patients with type 2 diabetes from one hospital. XGBoost using nine predictors, including the atherogenic index of plasma, achieved one-, three- and five-year AUCs of 0.784, 0.761 and 0.752 in 302 randomly held-out patients. This was internal retrospective validation. Missing values were imputed before splitting, creating possible leakage; clinical benefit was not tested.
ai_technology: XGBoost survival prediction; Boruta and LASSO feature selection
organization: Lanzhou University Second Hospital; Lanzhou University

evidence.tested: Six survival algorithms were compared using 704 training and 302 validation patients; 404 kidney-disease events occurred.
evidence.unknown: External transport, prospective performance and clinical benefit remain unestablished. Pre-split imputation can bias evaluation; the separate AIP association does not establish causation.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost learned risk from nine baseline predictors; AIP feature importance was assessed using Boruta.

source_review.scope: Publisher Methods, Results, limitations and publication history; supplement and underlying patient data not reviewed.

title: Learned prognostic screening links miR-130b-3p and NR3C2 to a putative kidney-cancer relationship
summary: An integrative analysis of clear-cell renal cell carcinoma used learned prognostic models and co-expression/target-gene intersections to prioritize NR3C2 and examine its relationship with miR-130b-3p. In 786-O cells, inhibiting miR-130b-3p increased NR3C2 mRNA and reduced proliferation, migration and invasion. The authors present the combined relationship as an extension of earlier work on each marker. Direct binding and NR3C2-dependent mediation were not established; the assays used one cell line. Prognostic evaluation was retrospective and subject to model-selection and feature-screening optimism, and it does not establish clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Integrative learned survival models; StepCox forward selection and LASSO-Cox modeling
organization: Southern Medical University; Hong Kong Baptist University; General Hospital of Southern Theater Command

evidence.tested: TCGA-KIRC model development used 516 patients/171 deaths and 99 candidate model combinations; the selected model retained 41 genes. Integrating its genes with co-expression modules and predicted targets identified NR3C2. Cell experiments in 786-O cells linked miR-130b-3p inhibition to increased NR3C2 mRNA and reduced proliferation, migration and invasion.
evidence.unknown: Direct miRNA binding and NR3C2 mediation remain untested. The authors identify prior work on both markers. GSE40914 performance helped select the model, so it is not fully independent validation; feature screening was not nested, and the model had about 4.2 events per retained variable. Generalization and therapeutic benefit are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Learned survival-model comparison and selection supplied a prognostic gene signature intersected with co-expression and predicted target-gene sets to prioritize NR3C2; LASSO-Cox modeling combined the two markers.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full-text sections 2.1–2.6, 3.5–3.7, Discussion and Conclusions; complete abstract, article date/affiliations and source-reported cell-assay results. Publisher-deposited Crossref metadata. No independent experiment or supplement review.

title: Elastic-net analysis identifies an exploratory seven-protein anti-TNF response signature in Crohn’s disease
summary: Elastic-net logistic models helped derive a seven-protein candidate signature associated with anti-TNF treatment outcomes in a cohort of 80 children and young adults with Crohn’s disease. A separate analysis fitted models to expression of the corresponding genes in 324 PANTS participants, reporting mean AUPRCs of 0.704 at baseline and 0.76 at week 14. This is exploratory, retrospective model evaluation on prospectively collected observational cohorts, not a locked-model prospective trial. The second analysis refitted transcriptomic models and does not independently validate plasma protein measurements. Modest cohort size, missing follow-up, non-standardized treatment and 90% White enrollment in the discovery cohort limit interpretation.
ai_technology: Elastic-net-regularized logistic regression
organization: Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center; University of Cincinnati College of Medicine; Connecticut Children’s Medical Center; Nationwide Children’s Hospital; Medical College of Wisconsin

evidence.tested: Discovery cohort: 80 participants; candidate proteins selected using outcome associations and regularized predictive models. Independent PANTS cohort analysis used 814 RNA-seq samples from 324 participants and separately trained/tested gene-expression models.
evidence.unknown: No orthogonal protein-level validation; refitted cross-omic models are not an external frozen protein-panel validation. Feature/outcome exploration and observational treatment variation limit generalization; no causal or treatment-selection benefit established.
evidence.ai_role: Elastic-net logistic regression evaluated candidate protein/outcome relationships and selected a seven-protein panel; corresponding gene-expression models were refitted and tested in PANTS.

source_review.scope: Original44-page medRxiv v1 PDF: relevant Materials and Methods(pp6–11), candidate-panel/cross-omic Results(pp12–15), Discussion and limitations(pp16–20); primary API abstract/version date. No supplement or independent experiment review.

title: MedNeXt localizes mandibular cancer invasion in a small retrospective CT cohort
summary: A single-center study trained a 3D MedNeXt model within nnU-Net on 30 CT examinations and evaluated it on 20 held-out patients with histopathologically confirmed mandibular invasion by oral squamous cell carcinoma. Predicted invasion overlapped expert-reviewed CT references in 18 of 20 examinations; mean invasion Dice was 0.553 and recall 0.483, with two cases missed. Among 18 evaluable cases, median absolute longitudinal invasion-span difference was 7.01 mm. This is a retrospective localization/segmentation study among invasion-positive patients, not an assessment of specificity, surgical outcomes or clinical benefit. Larger multicenter and prospective planning studies remain necessary.
ai_technology: 3D MedNeXt convolutional network in nnU-Net v2; TotalSegmentator preprocessing
organization: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich; University of Freiburg

evidence.tested: 50 positive-patient CT examinations, 30 development and 20 single-center held-out tests; expert-reviewed radiological references. Invasion overlapped 18/20, mean Dice 0.553, precision 0.742 and recall 0.483.
evidence.unknown: No invasion-negative controls, histological voxel-level boundary reference, external-center or prospective surgical/planning outcome validation. All test patients had confirmed invasion; localization overlap does not establish diagnostic specificity or resection safety.
evidence.ai_role: MedNeXt learned image-to-mask segmentation from expert-reviewed CTimages and estimated invasion location/extent; TotalSegmentator supplied initial mandibular cropping.

source_review.scope: Primary full publisher Methods/data partitioning/model training, Results, Discussion/limitations and publication metadata; abstract. No supplement review or independent image adjudication.

title: LASSO identifies a three-gene signature associated with colorectal-cancer prognosis
summary: LASSO selection of dephosphorylation-related candidates from TCGA colorectal-cancer data produced a SNAI1/TCF7L1/TIMP1 survival-risk signature. Prognostic analysis used 524 TCGA cases and 55 GSE17537 cases; reported 1-, 2- and 3-year AUCs were 0.604/0.626/0.658 in training and 0.687/0.764/0.652 in validation. New expression measurements in five paired tumors/adjacent tissues supported higher tumor SNAI1 and higher adjacent-tissue TCF7L1; TIMP1 did not differ significantly. These measurements do not validate survival prediction. The preprint reports retrospective associations and computational treatment-response estimates; phosphatase-dependent mechanisms, clinical utility and observed treatment benefit remain unestablished.
ai_technology: LASSO-regularized Cox prognostic modeling
organization: The Third Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University

evidence.tested: 524 survival-annotated TCGA colorectal tumors and 55 GSE17537 cases evaluated the three-gene signature. RT-qPCR in five paired clinical tissues assessed expression, not prognostic validity.
evidence.unknown: Associational retrospective result; no causal phosphatase mechanism, prospective survival model validation or confirmed treatment-response prediction. Small external cohort and selected cutoff limit transfer.
evidence.ai_role: After differential-expression and Cox/proportional-hazards screening, LASSO with 10-fold cross-validation selected nonzero prognostic features for a Cox risk signature.

source_review.scope: Research Square v1 full 41-page PDF: data collection/feature-selection/evaluation Methods, model and expression Results, Discussion/limitations; cover posting date 2026-11-20. No supplement or independent validation.

title: Machine-learning analysis identifies an ANAPC-related prognostic signature in hepatocellular carcinoma
summary: An analysis of TCGA liver-cancer transcriptomic and clinical data used consensus clustering and LASSO-Cox modeling to derive an ANAPC-related three-gene survival-risk signature: SPP1, CDCA8 and CFHR4. The study initially clustered 371 cases and excluded six without survival information from survival analysis. Reported 1-, 3- and 5-year survival AUCs were 0.768, 0.683 and 0.668 within the source cohort. The signature was built and assessed only in TCGA-LIHC, without external validation. Drug-sensitivity and immunotherapy-response estimates were computational. Separate CDC27 cell experiments did not validate the signature. This is an exploratory retrospective association, without established clinical utility.
ai_technology: Machine learning (consensus clustering and LASSO-Cox prognostic modeling)
organization: The Second Affiliated Hospital, Guangzhou Medical University; Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center; Guangdong Medical University

evidence.tested: ANAPC clustering initially included 371 TCGA cases; six cases without survival information were excluded from survival analysis. A three-gene signature stratified survival within the source cohort, with no external validation. Separate Huh-7 CDC27 knockdown experiments did not validate the signature.
evidence.unknown: No independent external cohort or prospective clinical validation; no observed drug-treatment response data.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning analyses of TCGA expression and survival data (ANAPC consensus clustering and LASSO/multivariable Cox modeling) derived a three-gene risk signature for overall-survival stratification.

source_review.scope: Independently downloaded/read publisher 22-page Article in Press PDF: data-processing/model/validation Methods, signature Results and Discussion/limitations; primary publisher article abstract/date/affiliations. No supplement or independent validation.

title: VIPcell prioritizes immune regulators associated with cardiac recovery in mouse heart failure
summary: VIPcell combined learned partial-least-squares models and causal-graph inference with single-nucleus data to prioritize immune regulators associated with response to neonatal stromal cells or their secretome in mouse heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. The study measured treatment-associated functional improvement in two mouse models, cardiac regulatory-T-cell expansion, and loss of functional benefit after fingolimod treatment. Fingolimod sequesters lymphocytes broadly; these experiments support immune involvement without uniquely establishing a Treg-specific mechanism or individual predicted genes as causal. Modeling used four sequencing datasets with synthetic augmentation and internal cross-validation, not independent biological replication. Results are preclinical. This entry represents the January 2026 preprint; the later journal DOI is the same study, with online date and final-version changes unassessed.
ai_technology: VIPcell machine-learning framework (data augmentation, partial least-squares regression and causal-structure inference)
organization: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago; Northwestern University; Georgia Institute of Technology; Emory University; University of Macau; Stony Brook University; University of Maryland; University of Nevada Las Vegas

evidence.tested: Treatment outcomes in two mouse models; immune-cell measurements and fingolimod perturbation within the discovery study.
evidence.unknown: No human efficacy or independent-team confirmation. Four sequencing datasets with synthetic augmentation do not provide independent replication. Fingolimod affects lymphocyte trafficking broadly, limiting Treg-specific causal interpretation. Later journal full-text changes not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: VIPcell learned PLS associations to cardiac E/e′ values and used DAS causal-graph inference to prioritize regulator hypotheses; subsequent experiments tested immune involvement, not every predicted causal edge.

source_review.scope: Independent full 48-page bioRxiv v1 PDF: Abstract, VIPcell model/causal-inference Methods(pp29–31), corresponding Results(pp12–15), immune-perturbation Results(pp17–18) and Discussion/limitations(pp20–21), source-header posting date 2026-01-30. No journal full-text/supplement review.

title: AI reconstructs maxillary denture bases from intraoral scans in a clinical feasibility study
summary: A PointNet++ model learned to reconstruct maxillary denture-base geometry from paired scans of 79 patients’ edentulous maxillae and existing dentures, using 57 training, seven validation and 15 test cases. Three randomly selected test outputs were manufactured and tried in patients; whole-surface registration RMSE ranged from 0.4 to 0.6 mm. Existing conventional dentures were subjectively more retentive than the newly printed AI bases. These descriptive, non-standardized try-ins do not establish clinical benefit, retention equivalence or border-specific reconstruction accuracy. Comparisons differed in material, manufacturing, prior wear and complete-denture versus base-only configuration. No objective retention or external validation was performed.
ai_technology: Enhanced PointNet++ deep-learning model with spatial border-attention and weighted loss
organization: University of Freiburg; Boston University; Loma Linda University

evidence.tested: 79 single-center patient pairs; 57 training, 7 validation and 15 held-out test cases. AI-generated denture bases for three randomly selected held-out cases underwent additive manufacturing and exploratory, non-standardized clinical try-in. The three existing conventional dentures were subjectively described as more retentive.
evidence.unknown: No external/multicenter validation; no objective retention-force or validated adaptation/stability measure; no border-specific quantitative accuracy test. Three try-ins were descriptive and comparators differed in age, material, manufacturing and prosthesis configuration. Clinical benefit is not established.
evidence.ai_role: PointNet++ learned a mapping from edentulous maxillary intraoral scans to corresponding clinically acceptable denture-base geometry. A spatial border-attention mechanism and weighted loss emphasized peripheral points during training, but quantitative evaluation used whole-surface metrics.

source_review.scope: Independently read primary 11-page publisher PDF: model/data partition/try-in Methods, Results and Discussion/limitations; original publisher HTML date and abstract. Three try-ins are descriptive; no supplement or independent patient assessment.

title: Learned ASD subgroups show exploratory associations with disrupted biological processes
summary: Clustering of clinical measures from 2,446 Autism Genome Project cases identified two ASD subgroups differing in severity, adaptive behavior, intellectual ability and verbal status. Analysis of copy-number variants and brain-gene functions linked the groups to disrupted biological processes. Random-forest importance analysis and a Naive Bayes classifier evaluated these relationships; in a higher-information subset, cluster prediction reached precision 0.82 but recall 0.39. These are exploratory genotype–phenotype associations, without experimental demonstration of causal mechanisms, a validated clinical biomarker or independent cohort confirmation. Missing clinical and functional-annotation information constrained prediction.
ai_technology: Clinical hierarchical clustering; random-forest feature importance; Naive Bayes classification
organization: Instituto Nacional de Saúde Doutor Ricardo Jorge; University of Lisbon; University of Coimbra

evidence.tested: 2,446 ASD cases supplied clinical clustering data; functional enrichment and cross-validated learned analyses evaluated genotype–phenotype associations, with limited recall in the information-rich subgroup.
evidence.unknown: Missing data and incomplete functional annotations constrain the usable subset. Mechanistic causation, diagnostic utility and transfer to independent cohorts are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Clustering learned phenotypic groups; random forests ranked disrupted processes, and five-fold Naive Bayes classification assessed prediction of the groups from those processes.

source_review.scope: Independent primary publisher full-text abstract, clinical/model Methods, feature-importance/classifier cross-validation, relevant Results and Discussion limitations; publisher date/affiliations. No supplement review.

title: Temporal neural networks predict three acute critical illnesses in retrospective Danish hospital records
summary: An explainable early-warning system combined a temporal convolutional network with deep Taylor decomposition to predict sepsis, acute kidney injury and acute lung injury from routine hospital records. Evaluation included 163,050 admissions from 66,288 adults in the Danish CROSS-TRACKS cohort. Patient-separated five-fold testing assessed prediction up to 24 hours before onset and supplied variable/time explanations for clinicians to inspect. The study used retrospective data without influencing care. It does not establish deployed performance, improved patient outcomes or transfer outside the represented hospital population.
ai_technology: xAI-EWS: temporal convolutional network with deep Taylor decomposition
organization: Enversion A/S; Aarhus University; Aalborg University; Aarhus University Hospital; Horsens Regional Hospital

evidence.tested: Retrospective hospital admissions from 2012–2017; 163,050 admissions/66,288 adults. Patient-separated train/validation/test assignments in five-fold evaluation; outcomes were sepsis, acute kidney injury and acute lung injury.
evidence.unknown: No prospective or treatment-impact evaluation. Clinical explanation review does not establish model causal reasoning, calibrated deployment or safety in new populations.
evidence.ai_role: A temporal convolutional network learned risk from longitudinal laboratory/vital-sign data; deep Taylor decomposition attributed predictions to input variables and times.

source_review.scope: Independent primary publisher full-text Abstract, model/result description, data/evaluation Methods and retrospective governance statement; publisher date/affiliations. No supplement review.

title: Learned selection yields a five-gene panel associated with early endometrial-cancer nodal status
summary: A study of early endometrial endometrioid carcinoma used random forests, sequential minimal optimization, J48 and Naive Bayes to develop a nodal-status panel from tumor sequencing and clinical data. Discovery used 24 hospital tumors and 289 TCGA cases; a separate 72-patient tissue cohort supported a five-gene PCR model. The reported combined panel AUC was 0.898, with sensitivity 88.9% and specificity 84.1%. The PCR cohort was also used for model construction/evaluation, so it is not a frozen-model prospective validation. Surgical-decision benefit and causal roles of the selected genes remain unestablished.
ai_technology: Random forest; sequential minimal optimization; J48; Naive Bayes
organization: National Chiao Tung University; Cathay General Hospital; Fu Jen Catholic University; Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen; Taipei Medical University

evidence.tested: 24 hospital tumors and 289 TCGA cases; new PCR measurements in 72 additional patients informed model construction/evaluation of a five-gene panel associated with lymph-node status.
evidence.unknown: No prospective frozen-model validation or demonstrated reduction in unnecessary surgery. Additional cohort measurements do not establish independent replication of a fixed diagnostic rule.
evidence.ai_role: Four learned classifiers selected and evaluated sequencing/PCR feature combinations linking tumor expression and clinical variables to observed nodal status.

source_review.scope: Independent complete primary Abstract; sequencing/model-selection and PCR-model Methods; relevant Results; visible publication/accepted dates and affiliations. No supplement review.

title: Deep learning stratifies postoperative cholangiocarcinoma recurrence risk in a multicenter cohort
summary: A neural classifier used 12 clinical factors to stratify postoperative intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma into higher- and lower-recurrence-risk groups. Development pooled 1,421 patients from three centers, with evaluation in 234 patients from another center; the source reports AUC 0.78 for the framework versus 0.60 for AJCC staging and 0.70 for a Cox model. Retrospective subgroup analyses also associated adjuvant treatment with better outcomes in the higher-risk group. Treatment was not randomized, so these comparisons do not demonstrate a causal treatment-selection benefit or justify clinical deployment.
ai_technology: Fully connected neural network with Cox-screened clinical features
organization: Renji Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Second Military Medical University; Fudan University; Fujian Medical University

evidence.tested: Retrospective derivation 1,421 patients/three centers and 234 patients/fourth center. Model recurrence-risk groups differed in survival; observational treatment subgroup comparisons remained nonrandomized.
evidence.unknown: External retrospective cohort is not independent-team replication or prospective use. Treatment associations can be confounded; outcomes after algorithm-guided treatment were not evaluated.
evidence.ai_role: A learned neural network mapped 12 Cox-screened clinical factors to recurrence-risk classes, enabling disease-specific prognostic stratification.

source_review.scope: Independent primary full Abstract, patient/network/prognostic-subtype Methods, relevant Results and Discussion; visible publication/accepted dates and affiliations. No supplement review.

title: Learned five-gene panel discriminates Alzheimer’s tissue samples in retrospective datasets
summary: LASSO, support-vector recursive feature elimination and random forests selected five Alzheimer’s-associated genes after expression, co-expression and disease-pathway screening. A five-gene nomogram had reported AUCs of 0.907 in a 195-sample dataset and 0.776 in a separate 100-sample dataset; PLCB1 also correlated with pathology-stage and neuronal measures. These retrospective tissue associations do not establish a clinical diagnostic workflow, a causal disease mechanism or effective treatment. The selected genes were screened within an already annotated Alzheimer’s pathway; no first identification of these genes or experimental validation of proposed drugs is claimed.
ai_technology: LASSO; SVM-RFE; random forest; gene-expression nomogram
organization: Affiliated Hospital of Guangdong Medical University; Guangdong Medical University

evidence.tested: Training expression dataset: 97 Alzheimer’s/98 control samples. Separate dataset: 56 Alzheimer’s/44 control samples. Five-gene nomogram AUC 0.907/0.776; additional stage and single-cell analyses provided biological context.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective tissue datasets, not clinical diagnostic utility or causal/therapeutic confirmation. Pathway-restricted screening can recover known biology; proposed drugs remain hypotheses.
evidence.ai_role: Three learned feature-selection methods intersected expression/pathway candidates to construct a disease-specific five-gene panel and evaluate observed tissue-label discrimination.

source_review.scope: Independent publisher full text: data processing, learned hub-gene selection, nomogram evaluation, Results and Discussion; visible date/affiliations. No supplement or new experiment review.

title: Neural MRI models classify liver tumors in a retrospective temporal validation cohort
summary: Inception-ResNet V2 networks were trained on MRI images from 1,210 patients to classify liver lesions, with evaluation in 201 later patients from the same hospital. Unenhanced MRI distinguished malignant from benign lesions with reported AUC 0.946; adding clinical data supported classification among malignant tumor types. The authors describe the later cohort as external, but their Methods identify a single-center temporal split. Malignancies required pathology, whereas some benign reference labels came from imaging reports. This supports retrospective diagnostic evaluation without establishing reduced contrast-agent harm, cost savings or benefit after clinical deployment.
ai_technology: Inception-ResNet V2 convolutional networks with clinical-data fusion
organization: Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, Zhejiang University; Zhejiang University; Hwa Mei Hospital, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: Development: 1,210 patients/31,608images; later same-center evaluation: 201 patients/6,816images. Seven lesion classes and malignancy tasks were compared with radiologist assessments.
evidence.unknown: Single-center retrospective study and mixed reference standards. The later cohort is temporally separate, not another center or independent-team replication. Prospective clinical outcomes and contrast avoidance benefit were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Fine-tuned Inception-ResNet V2 learned MRI lesion features; convolutional features and clinical variables were combined for subtype classification.

source_review.scope: Independent primary full Abstract, CNN/model and training/temporal-validation Methods, Results and limitations; source dates/affiliations. Corrected abstract external-cohort wording against single-center Methods.

title: Learned MRI brain-age gap associates with cognition and disability in geriatric depression
summary: A pretrained convolutional brain-age estimator was applied without retuning to midlife and older-adult cohorts totaling 170 and 154 participants, respectively. Older depressed adults had a higher estimated-minus-chronological age gap than older controls, with associations to poorer episodic memory and greater disability. Comparable diagnosis and cognition associations were not observed in the midlife cohort. This cross-sectional, exploratory analysis estimates an MRI-derived age difference; it does not measure an individual’s longitudinal aging rate or demonstrate that depression causes accelerated aging. Differences between cohort protocols and the need for replication constrain interpretation.
ai_technology: Pretrained deep convolutional BrainAGE regression
organization: Vanderbilt University Medical Center; Vanderbilt University; Veterans Affairs Tennessee Valley Health System

evidence.tested: MRI-derived brain-age estimates in 170 midlife and 154 older participants; cognitive associations in both cohorts and disability assessment in the older group. Model pretrained on over 5,000 healthy controls.
evidence.unknown: Cross-sectional associations, separate cohort protocols and exploratory subgroup tests. No causal aging trajectory, clinical predictive utility or independent confirmation established.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained convolutional regression model converted MRI/anatomical features into estimated brain age, enabling comparison of age-gap relationships across depression/age cohorts.

source_review.scope: Independent full primary Abstract, participants, brain-age inference and analytic Methods, Results and Discussion limitations; actual publisher date/affiliations. No supplement review.

title: Learned screening prioritizes FOS in human renal reperfusion data
summary: Researchers applied LASSO, random forest and support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination to renal transcriptomic data and converged on FOS and FOSB as candidates after kidney reperfusion. Both were elevated across 41 matched pre/post-reperfusion biopsy pairs, and an exploratory two-gene model reached an AUC of 0.922 on that discovery cohort; FOS alone performed similarly. In a separate dataset of 28 acute kidney injury biopsies and 11 stable controls, FOS remained elevated but FOSB did not. This is retrospective candidate evidence: the external dataset did not validate the combined diagnostic model, and the authors describe their analysis as exploratory rather than clinical model validation.
ai_technology: LASSO regression, random forest and support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination
organization: Renmin Hospital of Wuhan University; Wuhan University

evidence.tested: Three learned feature-selection approaches converged on FOS and FOSB in GSE126805, comprising 42 kidney-transplant recipients sampled at four time points; the paper excluded one unmatched post-reperfusion sample and analyzed 41 matched pre/post pairs. The exploratory two-gene ROC AUC of 0.922 and similar FOS-alone performance were estimated in this same discovery dataset, with no held-out evaluation reported. In the independent GSE30718 series (28 AKI biopsies and 11 stable controls), FOS remained elevated but FOSB did not. The authors explicitly characterize this as candidate-feature robustness assessment, not clinical validation of a diagnostic model.
evidence.unknown: The combined model was not independently evaluated; FOSB did not replicate in GSE30718, and FOS alone performed comparably in the discovery cohort. The study does not establish clinical utility, prospective performance, or a causal role for FOS/FOSB in lung-to-kidney signaling.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO, random forest and SVM-RFE feature selection identified FOS and FOSB from renal transcriptomic candidates; FOS was the more reproducible injury-associated candidate in the separate AKI cohort.

source_review.scope: Source-provenanced publisher JATS abstract, ML methods, paired-cohort analysis, results 3.3 and limitations; primary GEO metadata for GSE126805 and GSE30718. The represented claim is retrospective renal candidate evidence, not a validated diagnostic model or causal cross-organ mechanism.

title: A CT-based deep-learning system stratifies postoperative pancreatic cancer prognosis
summary: A retrospective three-hospital study of 592 surgically treated pancreatic cancer patients evaluated a CT-based Swin Transformer classifier. Its disease-free-survival C-index was 0.807–0.844, versus 0.631–0.656 for clinicopathological predictors; their integrated model reached 0.836–0.871. A 41-patient molecular subset linked predicted risk with tumor microenvironment features. These are retrospective prognostic and molecular associations; treatment benefit and prospective clinical utility were not established.
ai_technology: Multi-planar Swin Transformer-assisted deep-learning classifier for CT radiomics
organization: Suzhou Ninth Hospital Affiliated to Soochow University; Suzhou Municipal Hospital, The Affiliated Suzhou Hospital of Nanjing Medical University; The First Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University; Renji Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Derivation: 308 patients; internal test: 78; separate external test: 206. A 41-patient derivation subset supported exploratory radiogenomic associations. Reported C-index ranges include derivation and test cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective selection, semiautomatic segmentation and treatment differences limit inference. Molecular patterns need larger independent validation; model-guided patient benefit was not tested.
evidence.ai_role: A multi-planar Swin Transformer learned CT prognostic features; IPSS-PDAC combined its risk output with clinicopathological factors.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher abstract, cohorts, CT preprocessing and Swin framework, radiogenomic methods, results/discussion/limitations, affiliations and online date; supplementary methods were not assessed.

title: MicroRNA classifiers show weak separation of sepsis from non-infectious inflammation
summary: In 299 public whole-blood samples, learned classifiers evaluated literature-curated microRNAs for sepsis discrimination. The selected miR-150-5p/miR-486-5p pair had ROC-AUC 0.95 against healthy controls and 0.64 against non-infectious inflammation; adding the second marker gave no significant improvement. This is retrospective, cross-validated evidence from one cohort. Healthy controls differed demographically; an interstitial-fluid device was proposed but not built or validated.
ai_technology: Standardized logistic-regression screening; SVM, multilayer perceptron, random forest and XGBoost evaluation
organization: University of Patras; Hellenic Pasteur Institute; Vin University; United Arab Emirates University

evidence.tested: 158 sepsis cases, 82 healthy controls and 59 non-infectious inflammation controls; 263 candidate miRNAs. The paired marker gave nested-CV pooled AUC 0.83 (95% CI 0.78–0.88), with no independent cohort. Against non-infectious controls, no tested panel exceeded 0.64.
evidence.unknown: Clinical utility, prospective performance and interstitial-fluid transfer are unestablished. Whole-blood cell composition and unmeasured clinical covariates may confound associations; no causal role is established.
evidence.ai_role: Fixed logistic regression screened literature-curated single miRNAs and pairs under 10-fold cross-validation; further classifier families were compared under 5-fold cross-validation.

source_review.scope: Source-provenanced publisher JATS abstract, exhaustive miRNA screening, classifier comparison and limitations, plus affiliations and publication metadata. The represented result is retrospective host-biomarker discrimination; the proposed device and preliminary bench proof are not treated as clinical or AI validation.

title: AI-optimized magnetic nanobiocatalyst enables recyclable citrulline production
summary: A neural-network-assisted optimization selected a magnetic-nanoparticle formulation of arginine deiminase for citrulline production. The prepared catalyst achieved 70.0% activity recovery, near the predicted 71.18%, and 81.4% immobilization efficiency. It retained approximately 64% activity after 40 days at 4 °C, exceeded 74% after seven reuse cycles, and converted 99.1% of arginine to citrulline. These are laboratory formulation results; model training used only 30 observations and industrial or continuous-flow performance remains untested.
ai_technology: Hybrid Whale Optimization–artificial neural network (WO-ANN) for immobilization-condition optimization
organization: Maharshi Dayanand University

evidence.tested: Thirty designed experiments informed WO-ANN optimization; the selected conditions were experimentally tested (70.0% activity recovery vs predicted 71.18%, 81.4% immobilization efficiency). The immobilized enzyme retained about 64% activity after 40 days at 4 °C, was reused for seven cycles and achieved 99.1% L-arginine to L-citrulline conversion.
evidence.unknown: Continuous-flow performance, process scale-up and industrial operating outcomes are not established. The ANN was trained on only 30 design observations (21/4/5 train/validation/test); generalization beyond the tested factor ranges remains uncertain.
evidence.ai_role: A feed-forward neural network predicts activity recovery from four formulation variables; Whale Optimization uses the model to select immobilization conditions, which are then tested experimentally.

source_review.scope: Source-provenanced primary publisher HTML abstract, WO-ANN methods, optimized formulation tests, stability/reuse/conversion results, prior-formulation comparison, affiliations and publication history. Full PDF was available but independent reading used HTML.

title: Machine learning combines plasma spectroscopy and protein profiles for exploratory endometriosis classification
summary: A single-center study collected plasma from 37 participants with endometriosis and 45 with other benign gynecological disorders. Seventy had paired infrared-spectroscopy and HPLC protein-profile measurements. Feature selection and a shallow neural-network classifier using mid-level data fusion achieved reported sensitivity of 80% and ROC AUC of 0.80 in repeated held-out splits with nested tuning. In a separate protein-profile analysis, K-nearest-neighbor classification and SHAP prioritized a plasma fraction for mass spectrometry, identifying five candidate proteins. This is exploratory retrospective diagnostic evidence: the cohort was small, participant ages differed between groups, there was no independent external validation, and the proteins require orthogonal validation before being considered reliable biomarkers. The work does not establish a clinically validated diagnostic test or improved patient outcomes.
ai_technology: SVM, K-nearest neighbors and shallow neural networks; genetic-algorithm, VIP and random-forest feature selection; SHAP
organization: Manipal Academy of Higher Education

evidence.tested: Single-center plasma classification in 82 participants: 37 with endometriosis and 45 benign gynecological controls; 70 paired samples (32 endometriosis/38 controls) used for data fusion. Authors report stratified 80/20 splits with inner 10-fold tuning, repeated five times, and fusion sensitivity 80%/AUC 0.80. SHAP-guided fraction selection was followed by exploratory mass spectrometry.
evidence.unknown: No independent external cohort or prospective evaluation of a frozen classifier; age imbalance may limit interpretation. Protein candidates require orthogonal validation and are not established clinical biomarkers. No evidence of diagnostic deployment or patient benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Learned feature-selection/classification models distinguish endometriosis from benign controls; SHAP contributions from a KNN model prioritize a chromatographic fraction for candidate-protein analysis.

source_review.scope: Primary abstract, relevant Methods, Results and Discussion, affiliations and publication metadata in full publisher HTML; no independent reanalysis or supplement verification.

title: Transfer learning grades oral epithelial dysplasia in patient-level held-out histology images
summary: A retrospective study compared learned classifiers for four-grade oral epithelial dysplasia assessment using 3,777 histopathology tissue strips from 94 patients. Images were divided into 15,108 patches after patient-level partitioning. Xception with ReLU achieved reported patch-level test accuracy of 85.19% and weighted F1 of 85.36%; several alternative configurations performed worse or failed to train. The result is limited to this institutional dataset and 128-by-128-pixel patches carrying labels inherited from their parent images. It does not establish whole-slide grading, prospective performance or clinical diagnostic utility.
ai_technology: ImageNet-pretrained CNN transfer learning, including Xception and DenseNet201; ViT comparison
organization: Institute of Advanced Study in Science and Technology; Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research; Arya Wellness Centre; North East Cancer Hospital and Research Institute

evidence.tested: On 3,777 H&E tissue strips from 94 patients, patient-level splits were used; best Xception/ReLU reached 85.19% test accuracy and 85.36% weighted F1 at patch level.
evidence.unknown: Institutional dataset; patch-level evaluation with inherited image labels and possible local label noise; no independently external institution, whole-slide aggregation or prospective clinical validation established.
evidence.ai_role: Transfer-learned image classifiers evaluated four-grade histopathology classification on held-out patients; AI provided the classifier performance and training-convergence findings.

source_review.scope: Publisher abstract, relevant dataset/partitioning, model-training and evaluation Methods, Results and limitation sections independently read in full publisher HTML; no independent reanalysis.

title: Elastic-net analysis finds limited genomic separation of malaria infections in two connected Amazonian communities
summary: An exploratory preprint applied elastic-net logistic regression to existing genomic data from 47 Plasmodium vivax infections detected in two neighboring Peruvian Amazon communities, including 12 people reporting recent local travel. Repeated nested cross-validation yielded an AUC of 0.625 (95% bootstrap interval 0.522–0.724), versus 0.529 (0.402–0.657) after restricting the sample to non-travelers. This supports a bounded finding that fine-scale assignment was weak and sensitive to sample composition in this dataset. The analyses used different, overlapping infection sets, so their comparison does not isolate a causal effect of travel. Self-reported travel did not establish infection origin; intervals were conditional on saved predictions, and no independent cohort or operational surveillance benefit was tested.
ai_technology: Elastic-net logistic regression with nested cross-validation and K-nearest-neighbor imputation
organization: University of Antwerp; University of Liège; KU Leuven; Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia; Yale University

evidence.tested: Retrospective analysis of 47 infections from two communities; elastic-net classifier evaluated by 20 repetitions of five-fold outer cross-validation with inner tuning. Reported AUC 0.625 overall and 0.529 in a non-traveler subset; infection-level bootstrap intervals retained repeated predictions together.
evidence.unknown: Small and overlapping sample sets; no independent cohort or intervention. Travel was self-reported and did not determine acquisition location. Bootstrap intervals condition on existing predictions without refitting models, and the comparison does not isolate travel as a cause.
evidence.ai_role: A learned penalized classifier measures how much genomic variation distinguishes the two detection communities and how this assignment changes with the analyzed sample composition.

source_review.scope: Research Square v1 full PDF: primary abstract, study setting, modeling, validation and relevant results; no independent reanalysis or experimental pathogen work.

title: A finger-cuff waveform CNN screens for aortic stenosis in a multicenter cohort
summary: A one-dimensional convolutional model learned to identify at least moderate aortic stenosis from noninvasive finger-cuff arterial pressure waveforms, using echocardiography as reference. Development included 3,634 participants and evaluation used a temporally distinct multicenter cohort of 1,336 participants. In that cohort, significant stenosis screening had AUC 0.893, sensitivity 92.5%, specificity 64.5% and positive predictive value 36.4%. These are cohort diagnostic results, not evidence of improved patient outcomes. Prospective participant recruitment alone does not establish a frozen-model prospective evaluation; model-selection timing and full Methods were not assessed in the abstract review.
ai_technology: One-dimensional convolutional neural network for arterial pressure waveforms
organization: Cleveland Clinic Foundation; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center; Edwards Lifesciences; Hospital Reina Sofia de Cordoba; Amsterdam UMC, University of Amsterdam

evidence.tested: Development cohort: 3,634 participants, 307 with significant stenosis; validation cohort: 1,336 participants, 241 with significant stenosis. Echo-referenced validation AUC 0.893, sensitivity 92.5%, specificity 64.5%, PPV 36.4%.
evidence.unknown: Full manuscript Methods, prespecification and locked-model timing not assessed. Low positive predictive value implies confirmatory testing remains relevant; outcome benefit and deployment effectiveness not established.
evidence.ai_role: A 1D convolutional network maps pressure waveforms to significant-stenosis classification; echocardiography supplied the diagnostic reference.

source_review.scope: Independent reading of original NCBI PubMed XML for the primary JACC article: complete structured Background/Objectives/Methods/Results/Conclusions, electronic publication date and author affiliations. Publisher DOI route was a redirect placeholder; no full manuscript/supplement read.

title: Hybrid NMR structure maps H-NS contacts with AT-rich DNA
summary: A solution NMR structure of an E. coli H-NS domain bound to AT-rich DNA revealed auxiliary linker contacts beside its established AT-hook-like recognition motif. Mutational and NMR analyses supported their cooperative contribution to DNA binding. TALOS-N neural-network predictions supplied protein dihedral restraints alongside experimental NMR/NOE measurements and structural refinement. This is a hybrid experimental/computational result; the study did not isolate the learned component’s contribution or establish independent replication.
ai_technology: TALOS-N neural-network-based protein torsion-angle prediction
organization: Peking University; Soochow University

evidence.tested: The solution structure calculation used experimentally measured NOE restraints and TALOS-N-derived protein dihedral restraints; 20 lowest-energy conformers were selected. Mutational and NMR titration analyses tested the proposed H-NS/DNA contact contributions.
evidence.unknown: The learned component was not isolated by ablation. An isolated domain/DNA complex does not establish the behavior of full-length oligomeric H-NS in cells; independent replication was not established.
evidence.ai_role: TALOS-N, an artificial-neural-network-based hybrid predictor, supplied protein dihedral-angle restraints used in the H-NS85–137/AT-rich-DNA solution structure calculation. The structural interpretation also depends on NMR/NOE measurements, mutational/NMR analyses and other structure-refinement steps.

source_review.scope: Source-provenanced publisher PDF abstract, solution-structure Methods2.4, structural result and discussion, bounded mutational/NMR result summary, affiliations and publication date; original NIH TALOS-N developer documentation for its ANN operation. No experimental reproduction.

title: Machine learning shows hepatocyte-like cell lines poorly reproduce primary liver enhancer activity
summary: The authors compared four immortalized hepatocyte-like cell lines with primary liver tissue using chromatin-accessibility assays, motif analysis and a previously trained multi-species liver-enhancer classifier. Classifier sensitivity was below 60% on the cell-line enhancers; only HepG2 exceeded 50%, supporting the bounded finding that these lines incompletely reproduce native liver regulatory landscapes. Modifying AML12 culture conditions did not substantially improve similarity. The first preprint version already reports this result on 9 June 2026; a later version was posted 22 November. The result concerns selected cell lines and enhancer datasets, not every liver experiment, and classifier output is an indirect readout of regulatory similarity rather than direct proof of enhancer function.
ai_technology: Published multi-species liver-enhancer activity classifier trained on primary-liver sequences
organization: Carnegie Mellon University

evidence.tested: The previously trained classifier was evaluated on held-out enhancer chromosomes; it had <60% sensitivity on HLC enhancers and >50% only on HepG2. Wet-lab RT-qPCR, flow cytometry and ATAC-seq characterized cell lines; four cell lines were compared with primary tissue.
evidence.unknown: Preprint, selected cell lines and accessibility datasets; classifier sensitivity is an indirect sequence-pattern readout, not a direct functional assay of every enhancer. Architecture is not specified in the reviewed current paper. No universal suitability or clinical benefit is established.
evidence.ai_role: A learned enhancer classifier trained on primary liver data was applied as a quantitative readout of liver-like enhancer activity across cell lines, helping identify their divergence from primary liver and HepG2 as closest among those tested.

source_review.scope: First-version primary PDF header, relevant model-evaluation Methods and comparative Results, plus matching later-version Methods/Results independently read. Architecture of prior classifier not authenticated; no independent reanalysis.

title: AlphaFold3-aided cryo-EM resolves native Anopheles salivary protein complexes
summary: Biochemical and mass-spectrometry analyses identified native interactions among Anopheles mosquito salivary proteins, including Saglin and SGS4/SGS5. AlphaFold predictions helped identify subunits, and AlphaFold3 models supplied initial structures for fitting into cryo-electron-microscopy density, followed by manual model building and refinement. The resulting Saglin–SGS4 structure and related complexes reveal native protein organization and partner-dependent conformations. AI assisted structural assignment; experimental maps and biochemical observations provide the direct evidence. The proposed relevance to malaria transmission remains a hypothesis: the study does not demonstrate parasite-invasion, transmission-blocking or clinical outcomes.
ai_technology: AlphaFold and AlphaFold 3 protein-structure prediction, used to guide subunit identification and cryo-EM model building
organization: University of California, Los Angeles; National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases

evidence.tested: Mass spectrometry and biochemical analyses of native mosquito salivary-gland extracts/saliva established SGS4/SGS5 association with Saglin and other SG1 proteins; cryo-EM structures were fit and manually adjusted against experimental density. AlphaFold3 predictions supplied initial structural models and supported protein identification/model construction.
evidence.unknown: No in vivo parasite-invasion, infection, or transmission-blocking assay is reported in this paper; the proposed role of the complexes in transmission is not established by these structural studies. AI-predicted structures were fitted into cryo-EM maps and are not alone the experimental finding.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold predictions, including AlphaFold3 models, were used to help identify Saglin and build protein models into cryo-EM density, contributing to structural assignment of the newly characterized native protein complexes.

source_review.scope: Primary open-access article abstract, relevant native-complex Results, AlphaFold3/cryo-EM model-building Methods, affiliation/date metadata and functional-limitation context independently read; no pathogen experiments or independent reanalysis.

title: Survival-model screening prioritizes KIAA0408 for ovarian-cancer B-cell experiments
summary: A preprint compared 101survival-model combinations across three public ovarian-cancer cohorts (107, 80 and 101 participants), selecting a five-gene model in which KIAA0408 had the largest coefficient. This prioritized KIAA0408 for experiments in isolated B cells. Overexpression reduced a B-cell-receptor subunit and AKT signaling, altered cell-cycle distribution, and produced conditioned medium that increased SKOV3 ovarian-cancer-cell colony growth. These are in-vitro findings, not proof of an in-vivo tumor mechanism or clinical benefit. The cohorts also contributed to model selection, so their reported performance is not untouched external validation. The later accepted journal abstract describes independent validation as pending; its full final Methods were not reviewed. The entry represents the result-bearing May 2026 preprint with this version difference preserved.
ai_technology: StepCox-forward plus partial least squares Cox (plsRcox), selected from 101 survival-model combinations including LASSO, Ridge, elastic net, random survival forest, CoxBoost, GBM, SuperPC and survival-SVM
organization: Nanchang University; Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University

evidence.tested: Five-gene survival model developed from GSE26193 (n=107) and retrospectively assessed on GSE14764 (n=80) and GSE63885 (n=101); model-based KIAA0408 nomination followed by B-cell overexpression assays, pathway/cell-cycle measurements, SC79 rescue, and ovarian-cancer-cell conditioned-medium assay.
evidence.unknown: All functional experiments reviewed are in vitro. The three cohorts contribute to choosing the highest mean-C-index model, limiting independence of the reported validation. No prospective outcome, in-vivo tumor mechanism, independently replicated biology or clinical efficacy is established. The later accepted journal abstract says independent validation is pending; its final Methods/body were not available in the reviewed page.
evidence.ai_role: A screen of 101 survival-model combinations selected a StepCox-forward/partial-least-squares-Cox signature; KIAA0408 had the highest coefficient, explicitly motivating subsequent B-cell functional experiments.

source_review.scope: Primary Research Square v1 PDF header, relevant cohort/model-selection Methods, cell-assay Results and limitations independently read; later accepted journal abstract only. Represents preprint-version claims, not unreviewed final Methods.

follow_up.note: A peer-reviewed accepted-version abstract reports the KIAA0408-associated five-gene model and cell findings, while describing independent validation as pending. The final article Methods/body were not available in the reviewed page; preprint cohort details are not silently treated as final-version claims.

title: Sequence-diverse training improves retrospective brain-metastasis MRI segmentation across protocols
summary: A single-center retrospective study analyzed 925 contrast-enhanced MRI studies from 720 patients using 3D Attention U-Net and DUCK-Net 3D. Testing on 36 patient-independent studies across three MRI sequence cohorts found more consistent cross-sequence performance with DUCK-Net 3D and multi-sequence training. Accuracy declined for lesions smaller than 0.4 mL, and resampling removed 14 of 547 reference test lesions, all in this size group. External multicenter validation, prospective performance and patient benefit were not established.
ai_technology: 3D Attention U-Net and DUCK-Net 3D segmentation models
organization: Gachon University Gil Medical Center; Gachon University

evidence.tested: Patient-separated retrospective development and testing at one center: 889 development studies with grouped five-fold cross-validation and 36 held-out studies across three MRI sequence cohorts; comparison of two learned segmentation architectures and six training configurations.
evidence.unknown: No external multicenter validation was performed; prospective performance and clinical benefit remain unestablished. Small-lesion performance was limited, including loss of 14 reference lesions after resampling.
evidence.ai_role: The learned segmentation networks are directly evaluated to establish how MRI protocol heterogeneity and sequence-diverse training affect cross-cohort clinical image segmentation performance.

source_review.scope: Publisher full text: abstract, patient selection, architecture/training and patient-separated splits, results, affiliations, dates and limitations.

title: Plasma metabolite classifiers distinguish psychiatric diagnoses in internal cohort testing
summary: A study of 1,609 adults with bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, schizophrenia or healthy-control status identified 297 metabolites associated across diagnostic comparisons after age/sex adjustment and false-discovery correction. Classifiers including random forest and XGBoost evaluated diagnostic separation using randomly selected metabolite subsets in internal train/test splits. This is retrospective model evaluation of a single Han Chinese cohort whose samples were collected during 2018–2024; it does not establish causal mechanisms or clinical benefit. Medication effects were not explicitly assessed, and targeted metabolomics plus external multicenter validation are needed before diagnostic application.
ai_technology: Logistic regression, LASSO, random forest and XGBoost classifiers
organization: Suzhou Guangji Hospital; Soochow University; The University of Melbourne

evidence.tested: Internal diagnostic discrimination in a 70/30 train/test split and 10-fold training cross-validation across 1,609 participants; age/sex adjusted; random subsets of associated metabolites.
evidence.unknown: Medication effects were not explicitly assessed; lifestyle and illness-duration confounding, causal mechanisms, external multicenter performance and clinical utility remain unresolved.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised classifiers evaluated whether plasma metabolite subsets predict diagnostic groups; mutual-information feature associations are statistical screening, not AI.

source_review.scope: Publisher article-in-press full text: cohort, Methods, data split, mutual-information feature screen, model evaluation, Results, limitations and publication history.

title: Machine-learned density functional theory reveals molecular control of electrolyte screening
summary: Machine-learned neural classical density functional theory trained on grand-canonical Monte Carlo data enabled calculations of asymptotic screening behavior across increasingly molecularly detailed electrolyte models. The authors report that solvent attraction creates a monotonic decay mode, solvent polarity produces re-entrant behavior, and ionic architecture changes screening-length exponents, challenging a single universal scaling law. These are computational predictions for modelled systems; the reviewed paper reports no experimental validation of the new predictions.
ai_technology: Neural classical density functional theory
organization: University of Cambridge; Durham University; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Computed decay lengths across primitive and molecular electrolyte models; neural cDFT approach compared against known primitive-model behavior.
evidence.unknown: No experimental validation of the new molecular-structure predictions is reported in the reviewed paper.
evidence.ai_role: Neural cDFT trained on grand-canonical Monte Carlo samples supplies direct correlation functions and enables efficient screening-pole analysis across electrolyte models.

source_review.scope: Full arXiv v1 HTML Results, Conclusions and Methods; official abstract page and submission history.

title: Deep learning reveals 21 previously uncataloged slow-slip events at Parkfield
summary: An unsupervised neural autoencoder and clustering helped identify 21 short slow-slip events absent from a manual catalog of historical borehole strain records on the San Andreas Fault near Parkfield. Nearby creepmeters recorded corresponding slip for 14 of the new events. In the retrospective study, nearby low-frequency earthquakes were more frequent around slow-slip events, with enhanced activity immediately following slow-slip onset. The association does not establish a causal link or prospective earthquake forecasting. A preprint reported the main findings on 14 August 2025.
ai_technology: AutoencoderZ and K-means clustering
organization: GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences; RWTH Aachen University; EarthScope Consortium; Stanford University

evidence.tested: In 2009–2016 data, the method recovered 64 of 71 manual-catalog events at the reference station and identified 21 additional events after screening. Creepmeters corroborated 14 new detections. Figure 3 shows a new event across three borehole strainmeters and a surface creepmeter. Figure 5 compares nearby low-frequency earthquake activity with randomly selected non-event windows.
evidence.unknown: Sparse station coverage limits source depth and geometry estimates. The slip–seismicity association is retrospective, and causal and prospective predictive performance remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: AutoencoderZ learned features from daily strain wavelet representations. Two stages of K-means identified candidate slow-slip events for visual and instrument-based checks.

source_review.scope: Full publisher article, including Methods, Results and figure captions; official preprint landing-page abstract and posting date. Figure images and supplements were not independently inspected.

title: Deep clustering reveals weak tremor three days before the 2021 Geldingadalir eruption
summary: Unsupervised deep clustering of historical seismic recordings revealed a weak tremor beginning around midday on 16 March 2021, roughly three days before the Geldingadalir eruption in Iceland. Harmonic–percussive signal separation on the same recordings supported the timing. The analysis covered one eruption and relied on one seismic station. Prospective eruption forecasting remains untested. The finding was reported in a preprint on 5 May 2023 and published in Communications Earth & Environment on 2 January 2024.
ai_technology: Deep embedded clustering with a convolutional autoencoder
organization: GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences; University of Potsdam; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Figure 3 shows the tremor after harmonic–percussive separation. A reanalysis restricted to 12–19 March recovered a similar cluster across several cluster counts, with some misassigned windows. Both checks use the same historical station records.
evidence.unknown: Recurrence across eruptions, discrimination from non-eruptive unrest, and prospective alert performance remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: A convolutional autoencoder and deep embedded clustering grouped one-hour seismic spectrograms by learned features. The continuous-tremor cluster directed the authors to check the pre-eruptive interval.

source_review.scope: Full publisher article, including Methods, Results and figure captions; primary preprint Crossref abstract and posting metadata. Figure images and the linked GFZ PDF were not independently inspected.

title: Deep survival model stratifies cancer incidence risk using metabolic disease and protein profiles
summary: A DeepSurv neural survival model combined endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease subtypes with clinical and molecular features to stratify cancer incidence in UK Biobank. The prediction analysis used 13,438 training and 5,758 randomly held-out participants, rather than all 405,023 people in the broader epidemiological study. The authors report time-dependent AUCs of 0.80–0.90 and improved discrimination over their Cox models. This is retrospective model evaluation within one cohort; observational protein mediation does not establish biological causation or clinical screening benefit.
ai_technology: DeepSurv neural survival model; elastic-net Cox feature selection
organization: Wuhan University; Hubei Provincial Research Center for Precision Medicine of Cancer; Fudan University; Huazhong University of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: A random training/held-out split of 13,438/5,758 UK Biobank participants supported cancer-free survival prediction. Figure 7 reports better time-dependent discrimination and risk-group separation than the compared Cox models. The broader 405,023-person association analysis is a different analysis population.
evidence.unknown: External population transportability and prospective clinical utility were not established in this study. Mediation estimates rely on observational assumptions and do not prove that the prioritized proteins cause cancer.
evidence.ai_role: Elastic-net Cox models selected biochemical and blood-count features. DeepSurv learned nonlinear survival risk from clinical variables, ENM subtype and prioritized molecular mediators.

source_review.scope: Independently read complete source-provenanced publisher text, including Methods, Results, limitations and affiliation/publication sections. Supplement files and underlying data were not independently reanalyzed.

title: Machine learning helps prioritize a pathway for moslosooflavone wound repair in diabetic mice
summary: Consensus machine learning on public diabetic-foot-ulcer expression data helped prioritize candidate targets for moslosooflavone, including NTRK2/TrkB. Follow-up macrophage assays and topical-hydrogel experiments in diabetic mice linked improved wound closure and macrophage polarization to TrkB/PI3K-Akt signaling. The mouse study reports three animals per group in each endpoint cohort. Pharmacological inhibition supports pathway involvement, but off-target effects, an absent osmotic control and missing NTRK2 genetic tests limit mechanistic specificity. Docking does not establish direct binding, and human efficacy remains untested.
ai_technology: XGBoost; random forest; LASSO; Boruta feature selection; TargetNet
organization: Chongqing Medical University; Chongqing University; Army Medical University

evidence.tested: Four learned feature-selection approaches prioritized five genes from two merged public transcriptomic datasets. High-glucose macrophage assays, TrkB/PI3K inhibitor experiments and a diabetic-mouse wound model tested the proposed intervention. Six groups were reported with n=3 per group and separate day-7 tissue and day-14 closure endpoint cohorts.
evidence.unknown: The internally evaluated signature lacks fully external validation. The source reports no mannitol osmotic control and no NTRK2 genetic loss-of-function test; inhibitor off-target effects remain possible. Human benefit and direct biochemical target binding are not established by these assays or docking simulations.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost, random forest, LASSO and Boruta selected consensus DFU-associated genes, intersected with predicted compound targets to prioritize CYP1A1, MAOB and NTRK2 for subsequent pathway and functional experiments.

source_review.scope: Independently read complete source-provenanced publisher text, including Methods, Results, limitations and affiliation/publication sections. Supplement files and underlying data were not independently reanalyzed.

title: Random forest guides experimentally checked rare-earth disilicate phase design
summary: A random-forest classifier trained on 114 curated multicomponent rare-earth disilicate compositions identified cation-radius descriptors associated with retained high-temperature phases. Six new compositions were synthesized and characterized by X-ray diffraction and microscopy, supporting the predicted phase assignments and composition rules within two related material systems. The study establishes a specific phase-design result, not demonstrated coating service performance. The training corpus and experimental sample are small; seven withheld composition checks do not establish broad extrapolation across ceramics.
ai_technology: Random forest phase classifier; SVM and artificial neural network comparators
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Science and Technology of China; Liaoning Academy of Materials; AECC Shenyang Liming AERO-ENGINE Science and Technology Co., Ltd.

evidence.tested: A 114-composition training corpus and repeated random splits supported model selection. Six compositions absent from that corpus were synthesized and their phase assignments checked by XRD and microscopy; a seven-sample leave-one-combination-out check was also reported.
evidence.unknown: Small curated corpus, imbalanced phase categories and limited independent compositions restrict extrapolation. Coating lifetime, corrosion performance and operational engine outcomes were not established by these phase-characterization experiments.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest learned phase categories from seven composition descriptors, prioritized mean cation radius and its dispersion, and predicted composition-dependent phases for subsequent synthesis and characterization.

source_review.scope: Independently read source-provenanced full publisher 45-page Just Accepted PDF Methods, Results, validation, affiliation and date sections; original SciOpen HTML publication history.

title: AlphaFold-assisted study links WFS1 dysfunction to GnRH-neuron developmental defects
summary: An integrated human-genetics, structural-modeling and experimental study identified WFS1 as a candidate modifier of congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. AlphaFold 3 models supported simulations of rare WFS1 variants, including altered protein motions that were not captured by a simple benign/damaging prediction. Cell assays found impaired protein behavior and ER-stress activation; zebrafish knockdown disrupted GnRH-neuron architecture and reduced isl1a expression, with partial pharmacological rescue. These results support a developmental mechanism in model systems, not proof that WFS1 alone causes the human disorder or that a treatment benefits patients.
ai_technology: AlphaFold 3 structural modeling; PolyPhen-2 variant prediction
organization: University of Milan; IRCCS Istituto Auxologico Italiano

evidence.tested: Two rare heterozygous WFS1 variants in two families were examined using predicted structural models, replicated molecular-dynamics simulations and cell assays. Embryonic expression studies and zebrafish wfs1b knockdown/rescue experiments assessed GnRH-neuron development and ER-stress/isl1a changes.
evidence.unknown: Oligogenic inheritance and model-system results do not establish WFS1 as a sufficient human disease cause. Pharmacological rescue is partial and includes pleiotropic effects. Predicted structure/dynamics are not experimental structural confirmation; the model contribution was not isolated by ablation.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold 3 supplied monomeric and tetrameric WFS1 models for variant-specific membrane simulations and structural interpretation. PolyPhen-2 assisted variant assessment; experimental genetics and functional assays supplied the biological evidence. AI did not independently identify the gene from the exomes.

source_review.scope: Independently read source-provenanced full publisher article text including variant-modeling Methods, structural Results, cell and developmental-model findings, limitations, affiliations and dates. Figure images and supplementary data not independently reanalyzed.

title: Macrophage-derived features predict thyroid cancer lymph-node status in retrospective cohorts
summary: Machine-learning combinations using SPP1-positive macrophage-derived molecular features classified lymph-node status in papillary thyroid cancer cohorts. The selected glmBoost/random-forest model had AUC 0.998 in training, 0.706 in held-out TCGA data and 0.657 in a combined GEO cohort. Those latter cohorts contributed to model prioritization, so the results are cross-cohort assessments rather than untouched external validation. Single-cell discovery involved three patients. Separate cell and small mouse experiments supported SPP1 as a therapeutic candidate; they do not validate clinical prediction or establish a human treatment benefit.
ai_technology: glmBoost and random forest; 111 combinations of 12 learned model strategies
organization: Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine; Lanzhou University; Central South University; Zhengzhou University; Soochow University; Medical University of Graz; German Cancer Research Center; Nanjing Medical University; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Chongqing University; Chongqing Medical University

evidence.tested: Patient-level 70/30 TCGA partition; features selected in training and 111 model combinations compared. Selected model AUCs were 0.998/0.706/0.657 across training, held-out TCGA and Meta-PTC. Meta-PTC includes 21 pN0 and 50 pN1 tumors; model prioritization used held-out/meta-cohort performance.
evidence.unknown: The three-patient single-cell discovery cohort and model-selection use of evaluation cohorts limit generalization. Prospective clinical benefit is unestablished. Separate SPP1-inhibitor cell and mouse experiments are ancillary preclinical evidence, not validation of a frozen clinical predictor.
evidence.ai_role: Learned model combinations use macrophage-associated expression features to classify nodal status; glmBoost/random forest was selected through cross-cohort comparison. The represented claim is this clinical cohort result, not an autonomous AI discovery of SPP1 biology.

source_review.scope: Full source-provenanced publisher HTML text independently read: study data/cohorts, learned-model Methods, relevant Results, experimental limits, affiliation and publication metadata. No underlying data reanalysis or supplementary-figure validation.

title: Machine-learning feature selection prioritizes CD101 in endometrial cancer expression data
summary: LASSO, SVM-RFE, random forest and XGBoost converged on CXCL12, LAYN and CD101 in an integrated endometrial-cancer transcriptomic study. The three-gene classifier separated tumor and nonmalignant tissues with reported AUCs 0.888, 0.837 and 0.848 across three public datasets. High CD101 expression was associated with poorer survival in an unadjusted 415-person TCGA subset. Single-cell discovery used only two tumors; the smallest bulk dataset contained seven cancers and five controls. Cell assays confirmed expression direction and successful CD101 mRNA knockdown, without demonstrating a downstream tumor function or clinical utility.
ai_technology: LASSO; SVM-RFE; random forest; XGBoost
organization: Ningxia Medical University

evidence.tested: Three-gene tissue discrimination in TCGA-UCEC, GSE17025 and GSE63678: AUC 0.888/0.837/0.848. The TCGA survival analysis used 415 cases and dataset-specific cutoffs without adjusted prognostic effects. qRT-PCR in Normal-EEC/Ishikawa cells reproduced expression direction; two siRNAs reduced CD101 mRNA.
evidence.unknown: Two-tumor single-cell discovery and small bulk comparisons limit generalization. Normal-only spatial references cannot establish tumor-specific localization. Protein localization, downstream function, causal immune regulation and clinical performance remain unestablished. Cell mRNA experiments do not convert the represented retrospective diagnostic/prognostic association into prospective validation.
evidence.ai_role: Four learned feature-selection approaches reduce eight intersecting transcriptomic candidates to a common three-gene set, which is assessed for tissue-class discrimination and exploratory outcome association.

source_review.scope: Full source-provenanced publisher HTML text independently read: study data/cohorts, learned-model Methods, relevant Results, experimental limits, affiliation and publication metadata. No underlying data reanalysis or supplementary-figure validation.

title: Two-stage learned model forecasts hydrogen dispersion from early sensor observations
summary: An MLP ensemble estimated leak rate from early sensor readings, then a sparse Gaussian-process model predicted hydrogen concentration in a confined-channel dataset. The dataset combined 22 physical release tests and 10 CFD cases, representing 26 unique scenarios. Reported leak-rate MAE was 0.052 g/s; the selected dispersion model had concentration-volume-fraction MAE 0.0176 and RMSE 0.0226 on four test experiments. Candidate models were compared on that test set before final selection. This retrospective proof of concept does not establish ship-compartment transfer, operational safety benefit or prospective performance.
ai_technology: MLP ensemble; sparse variational Gaussian process with Beta likelihood
organization: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: Existing channel-release sensor/CFD data were used for scenario-based training and evaluation. Seven MLPs estimated leak rate; the final SVGP model had MAE 0.0176/RMSE 0.0226 in concentration volume-fraction units. Four held-out test experiments also supported uncertainty-coverage analysis, but their performance influenced final model selection.
evidence.unknown: One simplified channel geometry and few scenarios; high-flow cases had larger errors. No deployed ship-compartment or prospective safety benefit was demonstrated. Test-set candidate selection limits the interpretation as an untouched final performance estimate. A later journal DOI has January 2027 issue metadata; its online version date was not established here.
evidence.ai_role: A learned MLP ensemble maps early sensor history to unknown release rate; a learned Gaussian-process regressor uses that estimate, position and time to predict concentration and uncertainty.

source_review.scope: Independent primary 21-page arXiv v1 PDF text review, including model/data/split Methods, Results tables, calibration, limitations, affiliations and v1 date footer. Page 11 recovered separately with pdfplumber after pypdf extraction limit. Journal identity/issue metadata checked in original Crossref record.

title: GPT-5 scoring links feedback monitoring reports with waking hippocampal ripple rates
summary: In a nine-participant intracranial EEG neurofeedback study, GPT-5 scored participants’ free-text reports on ten cognitive dimensions. Higher GPT-5-scored feedback monitoring was associated with lower hippocampal ripple rate (β=−2.71 events/min per SD, 95% CI −4.21 to −1.21; FDR q=.0108) across up to 27 participant-condition observations after adjustment for condition.
